children.translated_text: Seated on the summit of <s>Kailāsa</s>, destroyer of Time and Kāma,
gracious, supreme lord, cause of the world's bliss,
<s>Bhairavī</s>, having bowed with supreme devotion, extended a hymn of praise:
"O god of gods, great god, destroyer of the poverty bound up with birth,
be gracious, embodiment of compassion, gracious supreme lord.
By your grace, O body of auspicious Māyā, I know
the secrets of the divine Āgamas, including the kula and kaula teachings.
O lord of all, I wish to hear your divine rasāyana (elixir-science),
which destroys old age, birth, and disease, and grants siddhis such as sky-going,
which calms poverty and suffering and bestows boons such as brahmanhood."
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
"Good, good, greatly fortunate one, benefactress of all worlds.
All that arises from <s>sūta</s> (mercury), O beloved of my pure self and life-breath.
For the benefit of all worlds, O worshipped by the gods,
I shall fully explain that beneficial secret, most secret of the secret: the origin and marks of <s>rasendra</s> (lord mercury).
Listen now, <s>Bhairavī</s>; I shall tell all of it.
By divine Indras, sages, gandharvas, serpents, and kinnaras,
and by you, I was entreated by those who desired the birth of <s>Kumāra</s>,
for the destruction of the demon <s>Tāraka</s> and for the protection of the worlds.
Then, beloved, in a cave of the <s>Himālaya</s> mountain,
a long time passed for us, playing together in desire for a son.
To make us abandon that lovemaking, which shook the three worlds, the gods sent <s>Vahni</s> (Fire).
Taking the form of a pigeon, Fire entered through the window.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā lajjayā devi visṛṣṭaṃ surataṃ mayā
children.translated_text: Seeing him, goddess, through shame I broke off the union,
and the brilliant energy of us two was placed in Fire's mouth.
Being burned by that, <s>Agni</s> plunged it into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: tena gaṅgāpi saṃtaptā tadbahir visasarja ca ||
children.translated_text: Burned by it as well, <s>Gaṅgā</s> cast it outside.
On reaching outside it became twofold: one portion was for the birth of <s>Skanda</s>,
and the other became pure rasa, <s>pārada</s> (mercury), which carries one across the ocean of calamity.
It remained in five wells, each a hundred yojanas deep.

children.text: tanmalā dhātavo jātā maṇayo divyavastu ca ||
children.translated_text: From its impurities arose the metals, gems, and divine substances.
According to the distinctions of each particular field,
this <s>rasendra</s>, breaker of the poverty of birth, obtained different names, colors, and qualities.

children.text: te kūpāḥ pralaye pañca saṃjñā jātādi vai mukhāḥ
children.translated_text: Those five wells, at the dissolution, came to have their several designations and beginnings, it is said,
and, as the colors were withdrawn, they were deposited there for myriads of years.
O goddess of gods, they have five colors and are joined with all substances.
In the east, <s>pārada</s> is white, with many-colored forms, and removes diseases.
In the south, the restless <s>rasendra</s> is blue in color,
free from faults, very dry, and especially mobile, beloved.
From it arose the great serpents, free from the defects of old age, birth, and disease.
In the west, what is called <s>sūta</s> is yellow in color and very dry.
It is possessed of all faults, but when purified by the eighteen operations,
it grants all siddhis, goddess, and gives accomplishment of the body, metals, and the rest.
In the northern direction it is red and entirely free from all faults.
By that very rasāyana the gods became free from birth and old age.
In the middle it should be known as mixed, endowed with all colors.
Externally the rasa has the luster of moon and sun, but is accompanied by faults.
Purified by the eighteen saṃskāras (operations), it becomes a bestower of siddhi.

children.text: amarāṇāṃ svarūpaṃ tu rasendro hi maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Indeed <s>rasendra</s>, O great lord, is the very form of the immortals.
Those two filled it only slightly, for they are exceedingly difficult to obtain.
In all other undertakings too, it bestows success through the proper rites.
When utterly purified by the eighteen operations, it quickly grants siddhi.

children.text: rasāvatāraṃ yo vetti sa tu dhārmikasattamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the descent of rasa is the best of righteous people.
He obtains long life, happiness, offspring, wealth, and health.
From the ocean of birth, disease, old age, death, and poverty,
it carries one across to the far shore; therefore it is called <s>pārada</s>.
Because it acts upon rasa, subsidiary minerals, metals, and the rest, it is <s>rasendraka</s>.
Because it is the seed from every limb of mine, it is called <s>sūta</s>.
Because it gives birth to every siddhi, it is remembered as <s>sūta</s>.
Because it is the rasa of my body, it is therefore proclaimed as <s>rasa</s>.
It is praised for the destruction of old age, death, poverty, and disease.
Therefore it is called rasa; and because it is a metal, fair-faced one,
it brings all metals into the state of rasa; therefore too it is named rasa.
Because it is friendly and of like color, it grants every siddhi.
As <s>pārada</s> it destroys diseases; in rasa-work it is <s>rasendra</s>.
In operations on metals it is <s>sūta</s>; in the practice of rasa it is <s>rasendra</s>.
Because it is fit for every operation and complete in every respect, beloved,
this mixed form, goddess, is said to bestow every siddhi.
Seeing that unfailing, stainless rasa, giver of every siddhi,
all the gods, led by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
petitioned me with various hymns, beloved:
"By the mere sight of <s>rasendra</s>, humans, birds, beasts, and others
attain many kinds of siddhi. Restrain that, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>."
Therefore it was yoked with three coverings and with faults.
From then onward, when freed from the faults and coverings,
<s>sūta</s>, purified by the eighteen saṃskāras, becomes a giver of siddhi.
Smoke, the crackling sound, the frog-leap,
trembling and violent trembling: these are the five states of rasa.
The motions of rasa are five; in water its motion is like water.
In smoke, <s>sūta</s> (mercury) has a smoke-like motion; in <s>staraṇa</s> it moves like a swan.
In dross, O <s>Devī</s>, it is dross-like; the fifth motion is like that of a living being.

children.text: catasro gatayo dṛśyāḥ adṛśyā paṃcamī gatiḥ
children.translated_text: Four motions are visible; the fifth motion is invisible.
The four motions, dear one, are to be restrained by apparatuses, medicines, and the like.
And the fifth motion is to be restrained by meditation, mantras, medicines, and the like.
There are the earthy one, likewise the fiery one, and also the airy one.
There is the aerial one, the one called elephant-hide, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, and the one that causes erysipelas.
There is the yellow one, the one called red-hide, the orange one, and the red-spotted one.
The intolerably fiery one, the frog-like one, and the impurities are regarded as natural.
<s>Kālikā</s>, <s>Malinī</s>, <s>Kapotī</s>, and the red-coated one,

children.text: salomī girijā caiva piṅgalī sapta kañcukāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Salomī</s>, <s>Girijā</s>, and <s>Piṅgalī</s>: these are the seven coatings.

children.text: aupādhikā imā jñeyāḥ pārade kīrtitāḥ priye ||
children.translated_text: These should be known as adventitious conditions in mercury, dear one.

children.text: viṣaṃ nāgaśca vaṅgaśca yaugikaśca trayaḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Poison, lead, and tin are remembered as the three combined defects.
The earthy one causes skin disease and also produces an aggravation of the humors.
The fiery one causes burning; the airy one becomes a maker of colic pain.
Deafness is the aerial defect; elephant-skin and elephant-hide make such a skin condition.
<s>Puṇḍarīka</s> causes ringworm, and the erysipelas defect causes erysipelas.
The yellow defect is said to cause pallor; the red-hide defect brings redness of the eyes.
The orange one causes an <s>udumbara</s>-type skin disease; the red-seeded one causes smallpox-like eruptions.
The intolerably fiery one causes bewilderment; the frog-like one causes skin tags.
The impurity, O <s>Devī</s>, causes fainting; thus the defects arising from blemishes are known.
<s>Kālikā</s> produces a black color, and <s>Malinī</s> causes the grasping or retention of impurity.
<s>Kapotī</s> causes loss of voice, and the red coating causes blisters.
<s>Salomī</s> causes vomiting, and <s>Girijā</s> causes dullness.
<s>Piṅgalī</s> destroys the eyes; these are remembered as defects born from the coatings.
Poison gives death; lead, O worshiped by the gods, gives dullness.
Tin produces foul odor; these diseases arise from the combined defects.
A maiden who has bathed after her first menstruation, beautiful and marked with auspicious signs,
wearing clean garments, anointed with garlands and perfumes, and well adorned,
mounted on an excellent horse and free from sexual union,

children.text: abhyarcya gaṇanāthaṃ ca bhairavaṃ ca guruṃ purā
children.translated_text: should first worship <s>Gaṇanātha</s>, <s>Bhairava</s>, and the guru.
Having meditated on <s>Rasendra Bhairava</s>, dear one, she should look at the mercury placed in the well.

children.text: paśyecchīghraṃ tato gacchet na punaḥ pṛṣṭhamīkṣayet
children.translated_text: Then she should go quickly and should not look back again.
This is the maiden's horse-sādhana, extending for the measure of a yojana.
At that moment he should take it, with the intention of seizing the maiden.
Leaping up from the middle of the well, it runs after her.
After coming as far as a yojana, it instantly enters the well again.

children.text: paritaḥ kṛtagarteṣu teṣu teṣu ca saṃsthitam ||
children.translated_text: When it has settled in the pits made all around, in each of them,
the teacher of <s>rasa</s>, having become pure, should take that <s>Rasendra</s> (lordly mercury).
Having fallen, because of its heaviness, from <s>Agnivadana</s> into the region called <s>Darada</s>,

children.text: deśe sa sūto bhūlīnaḥ tantrajñai rasakovidaḥ
children.translated_text: that <s>sūta</s> lies hidden in the earth, as the knowers of tantra and experts in <s>rasa</s> say.
When it is placed in an earthen apparatus called <s>pātana</s>, it comes forth.
Mercury is obtained, O <s>Devī</s>; that is said to be free from defects.
In this very way, here and there, always deposited by perfected beings and vidyādharas,
the lord of mercury exists, O <s>Devī</s>, bestowing accomplishment.
<s>Śrī Bhairavī</s> said:
I ask about the giver of instruction in <s>rasa</s>, about his pupil, and about the kākinī woman,

children.text: rasapūjāṃ tu pṛcchāmi yathāvat kathayasva me ||
children.translated_text: and about the worship of <s>rasa</s>; tell it to me just as it is.
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said:
Listen, O <s>Bhairavī</s>; I shall tell you all that unprecedented teaching.
The ācārya should be knowledgeable, competent, well conducted, virtuous, and pure.
He should know <s>dharma</s> (normative order), keep true to his word, and be skilled in the science of <s>rasa</s>.
He should know the truth of the <s>Veda</s> and <s>Vedānta</s>, be stainless, and be devoted to <s>Śiva</s>.
He should be a devotee of the goddess, always peaceful, and expert in the <s>rasa</s>-pavilion.
He should be accomplished in mantra, a great hero, and intent on the worship of the deity.
He should know the procedure of <s>rasa</s>-initiation, the mantras, medicines, and great rasas.
He should know the enumeration of colorings, the seed preparations, the joining of pairs, and <s>biḍa</s>.

children.text: rañjanaṃ sāraṇāṃ tailaṃ dalāni krāmaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: He should know coloring, sāraṇā, oils, leaves, and the krāmaṇa processes.
He should know the improvement of color, softness, and the digestion of both young and old metals.

children.text: khecarīṃ bhūcarīṃ caiva yo vetti sa gururbhavet
children.translated_text: He who knows <s>khecarī</s> and <s>bhūcarī</s> as well may be a guru.
A pupil should be devoted to the guru, of good conduct, and free from greed and deceit.
He should be without craving, without ego, truthful in speech, and established in discipline.
He should be free from laziness, know his own <s>dharma</s>, be engaged in the six rites, and be wise.
He should be free from hypocrisy, violence, and the like, and initiated into the practices of <s>Śiva</s>.
He should be an intense practitioner, peaceful, and intent on the performance of mantra rites.

children.text: dāntaḥ śiṣyaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ śaktimān gatamatsaraḥ
children.translated_text: Restrained and powerful, free from envy, such a person should be known as a pupil.
She has curled, glossy hair and eyes elongated like lotus petals.
She has a long, high nose, beautiful hair, and lips shining like coral.
Her teeth are like pomegranate seeds; her neck is like a conch, and her breasts are raised.
She is adorned with arm-bands as soft as garlands of śirīṣa flowers.
Her chest is close-set, her navel is deep, and her limbs are slender and restless.
She has a flat belly, adorned with a line of hair and three folds.
She has broad hips, thighs like plantain trunks, is fortunate, and is beloved.
Her shanks are like plantain stems, and her lotus feet are rosy.
She has red, stainless nails and an auspicious gait like a royal swan.
She is charming, with a sweet throat and a voice like the note of a cuckoo.
She is adorned with the temple of love, resembling a peepal leaf.
She is young, dark-complexioned, glossy, beautiful, and marked with auspicious signs.
She is skilled in kissing, touching, embracing, and the acts of love.

children.text: bahule yā puṣpavatī pakṣe sā kākinī smṛtā
children.translated_text: She who becomes menstruant in the dark fortnight is remembered as a kākinī.
One born in one's own <s>varṇa</s> may be taken, or one born in another <s>varṇa</s> as well.
In mercury-work, in initiation, in practical operation, and in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative alchemy),
if there is no <s>Kākinī</s>, there should be a young, beautiful woman, or another suitable woman.
Sulfur mixed with cow's ghee, one <s>niṣka</s> in measure, for three times seven days,
should be given in the morning; then that woman becomes like a <s>Kākinī</s>.
He should be righteous, afraid of sin, strong, and foremost in the wealth of knowledge,
eminent in justice, impartial toward all, and skilled in the scriptures of alchemy.
The king, and also his minister, should be skilled in all śāstras,
devoted to all dharmas, excellent, and promoters of the path of justice.
O fair-faced one, I shall describe the <s>rasaśālā</s> (alchemical laboratory) of <s>Rasendra</s>.
One should choose it in a land free from disease and free from disturbance,
dear to believers and living beings, filled with wealth and grain,
in a well-ruled kingdom, complete in prosperity, without danger, and blameless.
It should be in a city rich in all social classes and surrounded by great devotees of <s>Maheśvara</s>;

children.text: tatrāpi vijaye sthāne pavitre ca surakṣite ||
children.translated_text: there also, in a victorious place, pure and well protected.
It should be free from crowding by snakes, beasts, birds, and the like,
on level ground, adorned with walls, bars, and bolts.
It should be filled with the fruits of orange, pomegranate, ḍaha, and citron,
with palmyra, hintāla palm, bakula, coconut, āmla, and pāṭala trees,
adorned with aśoka, jambu, jackfruit, śāla, and puṃnāga trees,
with kapittha, areca, sarala, deodar, and fine bilva trees,
adorned with dhātrī, banyan, varaṇa, madhūka, mango, and āmrāta trees,
joined with ketakī, jasmine, jāti, yūthikā, and mālatī flowers,
with māgadhī, kunda, kurava, tilaka, and hundred-petalled roses,
and with water lilies, blue lotuses, kalhāra lilies, white lotuses, and lotuses.
It should be made splendid by swans, cranes, kāraṇḍava ducks, and cakravāka birds,
and surrounded on every side by ponds with cool water.
In a lovely, variegated garden, adorned with charming blossoms shaken by cool breezes,
one should construct the <s>rasaśālā</s>, exceedingly beautiful.
It should be beautiful with sixteen pillars, square, and well extended,
charming, O <s>Devadeveśī</s>, and furnished with protective parapets.
It should be provided with windows and protected by doors and bolts,
joined with chambers and banners, and shining with every implement.
The guardians of the directions should be properly painted there, and <s>Vināyaka</s> should be worshipped.
<s>Umā-Māheśa</s> should be installed, and it should be guarded by door-keepers.
It should resound with divine instruments such as drums, kettledrums, and bells.
One should construct the <s>rasaśālā</s> furnished with the marks prescribed by <s>vāstu</s>.
In the hall a platform should be made, very firm and like a mirror,
inlaid with bricks, beautiful, provided with steps, and possessing the proper marks.
It should be plastered with the dung of a tawny cow and surrounded by golden pitchers.
On the platform one should prepare a <s>bhadrapīṭha</s> (auspicious seat) for <s>Rasendra</s>.
On the <s>bhadrapīṭha</s> one should correctly draw with vermilion, two cubits across,
a hexagon, an eight-leaved figure, and outside that an eight-petalled figure.
There should be a lotus, a square, and it should be adorned with four doors.
One should place the <s>rasaliṅga</s> in the <s>yantra</s> and worship it with flowers and the rest.
Now I shall describe the twilight rite that grants the fruit of alchemical work.
Having bathed, purified himself, and been anointed, he should enter the <s>rasaśālā</s>.
He should wear white garlands and garments, be self-controlled, and have conquered his senses.
He should restrain his speech, be devoted to his guru, speak truth, and be firm in his vow.
Seated on a soft, variegated blanket, he should perform the ritual sipping of water.
The water, joined with <s>Vāc</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, and <s>Śrī</s>, is of the nature of self, knowledge, and <s>Śiva</s>.
Saying, 'I purify the principle,' he should drink it three times according to rule.
He should meditate on the boon-giving <s>Gāyatrī</s> and recite it three times, dear one.
Hear the <s>Rasabhairava Gāyatrī</s> according to the truth, O <s>Bhairavī</s>:
'Aiṃ. May we know <s>Raseśvara</s>; may we meditate on <s>Rasāṅkuśa</s>.
May that <s>Sūta</s> impel us.'
He shines like ten million suns and resembles ten million moons.
He is bright, five-faced, divine, three-eyed, and crested with the moon.
He has eighteen arms, is peaceful, and is devoted to the five cosmic acts.
He wears white garlands and garments and has a serpent as his sacred thread.
He is like crystal, mounted on a corpse: <s>Raseśvara</s>.
He is blue-throated, all-knowing, and adorned with every ornament.

children.text: varadaṃ rasaśāstraṃ ca pāradaṃ bhujaṅgaṃ sudhām ||
children.translated_text: In his hands are boon-giving, the rasaśāstra, mercury, a serpent, and nectar,
a conch, medicine, a bow, a trident, a skull-staff, and an arrow,
a ḍamaru drum, a sword, a mace, and fire, O <s>Īśvarī</s>.

children.text: ārogyaṃ divyamālāṃ ca hyabhayaṃ dvinavaiḥ karaiḥ
children.translated_text: With his eighteen hands he also bears health, a divine garland, and fearlessness.
He bears <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s> on his own lap and has the bull as his vehicle.
He is <s>Śiva</s>, beautiful with a mass of matted hair and a gently smiling face.
Having contemplated <s>Rasabhairava</s>, and <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s> in his lap,
holding a goad and a rosary in her right hands,
and bearing a noose and the gesture of fearlessness in her other hands,
four-armed, red in color, three-eyed, and crested with the moon,
the goddess wearing red garments, with a conch-like neck and full of compassion,
beautiful with jewel ornaments and radiant with a gentle smile,
one should meditate on the auspicious goddess <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>, facing the god.
Then, taking up ash, he should hold it with his left hand.
The wise man should take cow dung that has not fallen downward, catching it in a vessel.
Having dried it, he should burn it in a fire-pit and hold it in due sequence, dear one.
Its taking up again should be done with the mantras beginning with <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
Inspection, sprinkling, striking, and further sprinkling should also be performed.
Having consecrated it again with the mantras beginning with <s>Sadyojāta</s>,

children.text: mūrdhni vaktre ca hṛdaye guhye caraṇayoḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: he should apply it in order to the head, face, heart, private parts, and feet.
With the five mantras beginning with <s>Īśāna</s>, he should place them in their respective locations.
He should rub all his limbs with ash, together with those five [mantras].
The <s>rasācārya</s> (alchemical preceptor), as <s>Maheśvara</s>, should perform the saṃkalpa according to rule.
Having performed three prāṇāyāmas with the <s>mūlamantra</s> (root mantra), O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
he should sprinkle the consecrated water, held in the left hand, upon his head.
Having sipped water, and again [taking] water consecrated with the <s>mūlamantra</s>,
he should then drink the ācamana three times from the right hand.

children.text: arghyaṃ mūlena dattvā triḥ punarācamya pārvati
children.translated_text: Having offered arghya three times with the root mantra, and having again sipped, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
the noble-minded one, after reciting the <s>mūlamantra</s> one hundred and eight times,
should offer this <s>rasa-sandhyā</s> (alchemical twilight rite) to <s>sūta</s> (mercury), O <s>Īśvarī</s>.
In this way he should perform the sandhyā at the three times of day, destroying all sins.
I shall explain the procedure for deriving the <s>mūlamantra</s>; listen, dear one.
The syllable of speech, <s>Kamalā</s>, and then <s>Raseśvara</s> with the dative ending:
after that the word <s>Mahākāla</s>, then the word <s>Mahābala</s>,
then the word <s>Aghorabhairava</s>, then the word <s>Vajravīra</s>,
and the word <s>Krodhakāla</s>: all this is joined in the form of direct address.
Joined with the final letter of the sixth class beginning with ka and ṣa, ending in dha, with u and a bindu,
this is the five-syllabled <s>kūṭa</s> (mantra cluster); then it is joined with karṣaṇa.
With a visarga too, this <s>kūṭa</s>, dear one, consists of four phonemes.
This is the thirty-two-syllabled mantra of <s>Rasendrabhairava</s>.
It is hidden in all tantras, secret, and exceedingly difficult to obtain.
I shall explain the <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s> mantra; listen, O <s>Bhairavī</s>.
The syllable of speech, <s>Bhuvaneśī</s>, <s>Ramā</s>, and <s>Makaraketana</s>,
and <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s> in the dative, ending with namaḥ, form the twelve-syllabled mantra.
The mantra of <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s>, your goddess, has thus been proclaimed.
The metre of <s>Rasabhairava</s> is declared to be anuṣṭubh.
<s>Nandikeśa</s> is said to be the seer; the deity is glorious <s>Rasabhairava</s>.

children.text: raṃ bījaṃ laṃ bhavet kīlam antyārṇaḥ śaktirīritaḥ
children.translated_text: Raṃ is the <s>bīja</s> (seed syllable), laṃ is the <s>kīla</s> (pin), and the final phoneme is taught as the śakti.
For <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s>, Skanda's ardraṃ is the <s>bīja</s>, and <s>rasa</s> is the <s>kīlaka</s> (pin).
Namaḥ is known as the śakti; this is the supreme secret mantra.
I shall explain the worship of the <s>rasaliṅga</s> (mercurial liṅga); listen truly, O <s>Bhairavī</s>.
Putting the left foot forward, he should enter the sacrificial house.
Seated on a soft seat, pure and with mind restrained,
having controlled the breaths and made the resolve, he should [visualize] the glorious guru established on his head,
shining like pure crystal, peaceful, granting boons and fearlessness.
He should first remember that name and then obtain that guru's permission.

children.text: divi sthitāśca ye bhūtā bhūmisthā vighnakāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those beings who are in the sky, and those standing on the earth who create obstacles,

children.text: pātāle ye mahābhūtāḥ te naśyantu śivājñayā
children.translated_text: and those great beings who are in the underworld: let them perish by <s>Śiva</s>'s command.

children.text: anenaiva ca mantreṇa digvidikṣv akṣatān kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: With this very mantra he should cast unbroken grains of rice into the cardinal and intermediate directions.
He should cast a flower into the atmosphere with the formula 'to the weapon, phaṭ.'
Saying also 'crusher of all enemies,' he should use the right heel.
He should strike the ground three times; then there should again be prāṇāyāma.
To the south of the auspicious seat of <s>Rasendra</s>,
he should make a beautiful square maṇḍala, measuring one and a half hastas.
It should have, in sequence, a triangle, a circle, a hexagon, and a square.
He should worship the world-protectors beginning with <s>Indra</s>, preceded by their respective names,
with formulas beginning with praṇava and ending with namaḥ, using flowers and unbroken rice.
With the seed syllables of the syllable of speech and of <s>Kamalā</s>, he should worship the heart and the other limbs.
In the east and south, and then in the west and north, O <s>Śivā</s>,
he should worship the eyes in the <s>Īśāna</s> and other corner-directions.
In all directions he should worship the weapon, with the dative ending and ending in phaṭ.
He should show eight snaps of the fingers; afterward he should bring the support.
There itself he should invoke the fire-maṇḍala, rooted in the seed syllable.
There the ten kalās of fire are to be worshipped in order with fragrances and unbroken rice.
Then, taking up the vessel, he should visualize the solar orb.
There the twelve kalās of <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s> should be worshipped with sandal paste and unbroken rice.
He should fill the arghya-vessel with water endowed with the finest fragrance.
He should contemplate the lunar disk and worship those [kalās] there.
Drawing a triangle in the middle, he should inscribe the śakti-bīja.

children.text: tatra kṣipet gandhapuṣpaṃ mūlamantraṃ tridhā japet
children.translated_text: There he should place fragrance and a flower, and recite the <s>mūlamantra</s> three times.
In the four directions beginning with the east, he should set down four vessels.
He should fill them as before and worship with fragrance, flowers, and unbroken rice.
With the <s>mūlamantra</s> and with the water from the central vessel,
he should sprinkle the vessels, his own limbs, and all the materials for worship.
For the welcoming rite he should arrange a square maṇḍala.
As before, he should fill five vessels with pure water.
He should place <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in the middle, and place a jewel in the southern one.

children.text: svarṇaṃ tadvāmapātre ca tatsamīpe kuśaṃ nyaset
children.translated_text: He should place gold in the vessel to its left, and set kuśa grass near it.
In the vessel situated near the jewel-vessel there should be <s>aṣṭagandhaka</s> (the eight fragrant substances).
On each vessel he should draw a triangle, furnished with the Māyā seed syllable.
He should place fragrance, unbroken rice, and a flower, and consecrate it three times with the root mantra.
He should consecrate the mercury-vessel seven times with the <s>mūlamantra</s>.
With the water from the mercury-vessel he should sprinkle the worship materials and himself,
his body and head, as well as the seat and lamp.
For the seat, the seer is <s>Meru</s>, and the metre is said to be <s>Sutala</s>.
The blessed one in tortoise form is proclaimed as the deity.

children.text: pṛthvi tvayā dhṛtā lokā devi tvaṃ viṣṇunā dhṛtā
children.translated_text: O goddess Earth, the worlds are supported by you; you are supported by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ ca dhāraya māṃ devi pavitraṃ kuru cāsanam
children.translated_text: And you, O goddess, support me; purify the seat.

children.text: anenaiva tu mantreṇa cāsane kusumaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: With this very mantra he should place a flower upon the seat.
I shall explain <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s> (purification of the elements): earth is yellow and furnished with a vajra,
hard, joined with the seed-syllable <s>laṃ</s>, extending from the knees to the roots of the big toes.
It should be meditated upon from the knees up to the waist; above it is the crescent moon,
white, accompanied by the seed-syllable <s>vaṃ</s>, to be conceived as liquid in form.
From the waist to the heart one should meditate externally on the triangular form,
with the seed-syllable <s>raṃ</s>, red in color and adorned with a svastika.
From the heart up to the throat, the wind should be remembered, dark as collyrium,
accompanied by the seed-syllable <s>yaṃ</s>, O goddess, and adorned with six dots.
O sovereign lady, from the region of the ears up to the <s>brahmarandhra</s>,
one should remember space as circular, accompanied by the seed-syllable <s>haṃ</s>, and very black.

children.text: pṛthivīm apsu ca tāstvagnau sa ca vāyau sa so'mbare
children.translated_text: One should merge earth into the waters, those into fire, that into wind, and that into space,
and, after merging them, establish them at the <s>dvādaśānta</s>, O supreme goddess.
With the seed-syllable <s>yaṃ</s> he should dry up his own body from the <s>mūlādhāra</s>,
piercing the six supports as far as the aperture of <s>Brahmā</s>, O dear one.
With the seed-syllable <s>raṃ</s> he should burn the body; then he should flood it all
with the seed-syllable <s>vaṃ</s>, liquefied from the lunar disk at the <s>brahmarandhra</s>.
With that flowing nectar alone he should flood the body, O <s>Śivā</s>.
From space he should take up wind; from that he should collect fire.
From fire the waters are to be drawn; from them he should gather earth.

children.text: evaṃ pañca ca bhūtāni svasvasthāne niyojayet ||
children.translated_text: In this way he should assign the five elements to their own respective places.
He should meditate on the sinful person situated in the left belly, black in form,
and on him as having gone out, O goddess, bearing a sword and shield.
Having performed <s>nyāsa</s> with the <s>rasāṅkuśa</s> on the fingers, heart, and the rest,

children.text: aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kṣmauṃ kṣmaṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ phaṭ raseśvarāya mahākālabhairavāya śikhāyai vaṣaṭ
children.translated_text: <s>Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kṣmauṃ kṣmaṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ phaṭ</s>: to <s>Raseśvara</s>, to <s>Mahākālabhairava</s>, for the topknot, <s>vaṣaṭ</s>.

children.text: raudrarūpāya kṛṣṇapiṅgalalocanāya avatara 2 avatāraya 2 jalpaya 2 śubhāśubhaṃ kathaya 2 kathāpaya 2 mama mahārakṣāṃ kuru kuru mama rasasiddhiṃ dehi
children.translated_text: To the fierce-formed one, whose eyes are black and tawny: descend, descend; cause descent, cause descent; speak, speak; tell the auspicious and inauspicious, tell it; make it be told; protect me greatly, protect me; grant me <s>rasasiddhi</s>.
To <s>Mahākālabhairava</s>, for the heart, <s>namaḥ</s>.
As before, to <s>Mahābalabhairava</s>, for the head, <s>svāhā</s>.
As before, to <s>Aghorabhairava</s>, for the topknot, <s>vaṣaṭ</s>.
As before, to <s>Vajravīrabhairava</s>, for the armor, <s>huṃ</s>.
As before, to <s>Krodhabhairava</s>, for the three eyes, <s>vauṣaṭ</s>.
As before, to <s>Kālabhairava</s>, for the missile, <s>phaṭ</s>.
Thus is the finger-<s>nyāsa</s>.
Having uttered it together with the corresponding seed-syllables, and the <s>rasāṅkuśa</s> as the fourth,
he should place the five seed-syllables in the five places beginning with the heart.
Then, saying 'for the missile, <s>phaṭ</s>,' he should show the finger-snap in the directions.

children.text: mātṛkāṃ ca kalānyāsaṃ pājyonyāsaṃ ca kolakam
children.translated_text: He should perform the <s>mātṛkā</s>, the <s>kalānyāsa</s>, the <s>pājyonyāsa</s>, and the <s>kolaka</s>.
Then, O goddess, he should carry out the inner worship.
By breath retention he causes the lotus of the heart to become fully blossomed.
In the pericarp of the heart-lotus he should contemplate the form of <s>rasa</s>.
With mental offerings such as fragrances and flowers, he should worship it.
He should adorn his own body with fragrances, flowers, and the like, as he pleases.
Thus is the inner worship; then he should perform the outer worship.

children.text: astreṇa liṅgaṃ samprokṣya liṅgaśuddhiṃ vidhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: After sprinkling the <s>liṅga</s> with the missile mantra and carrying out the purification of the <s>liṅga</s>,
he should set a <s>vardhanī</s> vessel, filled with water and covered with cloth, O dear one,
on the right side, and worship it according to rule.
On the seat he should make a square with vermilion powder.
Within it he should draw a hexagon with a straight golden stylus.
He should make an eight-petalled lotus and a four-gated enclosing square,
and in the outer square he should worship the guardians of the directions, O dear one.

children.text: nandinaṃ ca mahākālaṃ bhṛṅgiṃ riṭiṃ mahābalam
children.translated_text: He should place <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgin</s>, <s>Riṭi</s>, and <s>Mahābala</s>,

children.text: kumbhakarṇaṃ ca sugrīvaṃ bhṛṅgakaṃ ca dṛḍhāyudham ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgaka</s>, and <s>Dṛḍhāyudha</s>.

children.text: caturdvāre tu vinyasya dvau dvau prāgādipūjitau
children.translated_text: At the four gates he should install them two by two, worshipped beginning in the east.
Gold, silver, copper, lead, tin, magnetic iron, <s>śaṭha</s>, and iron
he should worship at the gates beginning in the east, two by two in order, O great goddess.
Inside the enclosing square, in the east, he should worship <s>Śukra</s>; in the fire-corner, <s>Graha</s>.
In the south he should worship <s>Rudra</s>; in the demonic quarter, <s>Samīraṇa</s>.

children.text: paścimasyāṃ śivaṃ vahniṃ vāyavyām uttare hyumām ||
children.translated_text: In the west he should worship <s>Śiva</s>; in the northwest, <s>Vahni</s>; and in the north, <s>Umā</s>.
He should worship <s>Pāvaka</s> in the northeast; then, on the tips of the eight petals,

children.text: prāgādau gandhakaṃ tālaṃ kāsīsaṃ ca manaḥśilām ||
children.translated_text: beginning in the east, sulfur, orpiment, green vitriol, and realgar,

children.text: kaṃkuṣṭhaṃ mākṣikaṃ caiva nṛpāvartaṃ ca gairikam
children.translated_text: as well as <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, pyrite, <s>nṛpāvarta</s>, and red ochre.

children.text: lepikā kṣepikā caiva krāmikā rañjikā tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lepikā</s>, <s>Kṣepikā</s>, <s>Krāmikā</s>, and <s>Rañjikā</s>,
<s>Lohaṭī</s>, <s>Bandhakārī</s>, <s>Bhūcarī</s>, and <s>Mṛtyunāśinī</s>,

children.text: vibhūtiḥ khecarī caiva daśa dūtyaḥ krameṇa ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhūti</s> and <s>Khecarī</s> are the ten messengers in sequence.
They are to be worshipped on the eight-petalled lotus, on the petals above and below.
Rubies, pearls, beryls, sapphires, emeralds, and corals,
together with hessonite and topaz, are jewels that grant every siddhi.
He should worship them on the petal-tips of the second eight-petalled lotus.
The <s>Rudras</s> have eighteen arms, five faces, and three eyes;
their crowns shine with the half-moon, their throats are blue, and their banner bears the bull.
All bear their own respective colors; these are the eight <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>.
They are to be worshipped, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, in the second eight-petalled lotus.
<s>Rasaka</s>, <s>vimala</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>capala</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, and collyrium
should be the companions at the petal-tips of the hexagon, bestowing every siddhi.
Diamond, <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>vajrābhra</s>, <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
and <s>bhūnāga</s>: these powers should be worshipped in the six corners.
Cinnabar, <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>śilājatu</s>, and <s>agnijāra</s>
are, in that pericarp beginning from the east, the four higher powers.

children.text: hiṃgulaṃ mālinī śaktiḥ parā śaktiśca sasyakam
children.translated_text: Cinnabar is the power <s>Mālinī</s>; <s>sasyaka</s> is the higher power.
<s>Śilājatu</s> is the higher power, and <s>agnijāra</s> is the higher-and-lower power.
With mantras beginning with the praṇava and ending in namaḥ, preceded by each one's name,
and with the dative ending, he should worship these powers established in the enclosure of mercury.
But in the middle of the divine powers he should worship <s>Rasabhairava</s>.
In twenty-seven niṣkas of purified gold that has been melted,
he should place nine niṣkas of the king <s>sūta</s> (mercury), with his mind fixed on one point,
in a well-marked yantra made of beeswax, having the form of a liṅga.
When the gold has been fully heated, O <s>Śivā</s>, he should cast the mercury into it while it is red-hot.
After a muhūrta, when that <s>rasaliṅga</s> has cooled of itself, he should put it in milk.
Then, taking it up again, he should remove the impurity on the surface.
Having rubbed it and made the liṅga even, he should then sprinkle it.
In this way, with metals such as silver, either separately or all together,
or with the essences of mica and the like, he should make the liṅga according to his capacity.

children.text: rasaliṅgaṃ dvidhā proktaṃ sakalaṃ niṣkalaṃ priye
children.translated_text: The <s>rasaliṅga</s> is said to be of two kinds, formed and formless, dear one.

children.text: pūrvoktaṃ sakalaṃ liṅgaṃ niṣkalaṃ kevalo rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The liṅga described before is the formed liṅga; the formless one is mercury alone.
For those who desire enjoyment the formed one is suitable, and for those who seek liberation the formless one.
A <s>rasaliṅga</s> bound with gold was worshipped by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, and <s>Vahni</s>.
One bound with silver was worshipped by <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, and <s>Nandin</s>.
A <s>rasaliṅga</s> joined with the essence of mica was worshipped by you.
One bound with copper was worshipped by <s>Ramā</s>, <s>Vāṇī</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the lord of waters.
One bound with lodestone was worshipped by <s>Yama</s>, <s>Marut</s>, and <s>Nairṛta</s>.
One bound with tin was worshipped by siddhas, sādhyas, vidyādharas, and great seers.
One bound with lead was worshipped by nāgas, vasus, gandharvas, uragas, and kinnaras.
One bound with sharp iron was worshipped by <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, yakṣas, bhūtas, and piśācas.
And one bound with <s>muṇḍa</s> was worshipped by mother <s>Durgā</s>, and by apsarases, guhyakas, and asuras.
But the formless <s>rasaliṅga</s> was worshipped by yogins beginning with <s>Bhṛṅgin</s>.
These <s>rasaliṅgas</s> have been described; human beings who desire results
should worship them carefully every day for the accomplishment of all aims.
Now hear the establishment of life in the <s>rasaliṅgas</s> that have been described.
Having restrained the breaths according to rule, O <s>Śivā</s>, he should remember the life-power:
the supreme one seated on a red lotus in the middle of an ocean of blood,
wearing red garments, red in color, crowned with many jewels,
with a mass of hair adorned by a pure digit of the moon, and with the sun, fire, and moon as her eyes,
her cheeks reddened by the rays of her ear-ornaments,
beautiful with a nose-ridge shaped like a flower of <s>śrīparṇī</s>,
with bimba lips shining like coral and ruby,
splendid with smooth teeth shaped like petals of the kuruvinda,
with a lovely conch-like neck adorned by a pearl necklace,
adorned with rings, armlets, bracelets, and the like,
granting fearlessness while holding a noose, goad, sugarcane bow, and flower-arrows,
her lotus-hand shining with a vessel filled with blood,
ornamented with a necklace and saffron shining on the slopes of her full breasts,
adorned with a girdle, anklets, bracelets, and toe-rings.
With mind one-pointed, he should perform the prāṇapratiṣṭhā of the liṅga.

children.text: sṛṇiṃ mañca pāśaśca haṃsaḥ so'hamiti priye
children.translated_text: The hook, the couch, the noose, and the haṃsa: 'so'ham,' dear one.
'The breath of this liṅga is breath here.
The living soul of this liṅga is established here.

children.text: amuṣya liṅgasya sarvendriyāṇi vāṅmanaścakṣuḥśrotrajihvāghrāṇā ihāgatya sukhaṃ ciraṃ tiṣṭhantu so'haṃ haṃsaḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: May all the senses of this liṅga, speech, mind, sight, hearing, tongue, and smell, come here and remain happily for a long time. So'ham, haṃsaḥ, svāhā.'
Ya ra la va śa ṣa sa ha oṃ.
Kroṃ hrīṃ āṃ.
Having uttered this mantra, he should invite the breaths, dear one.
Of this glorious prāṇapratiṣṭhā mantra, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s> are the seers.
The Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman are the metres.
Glorious <s>Parāśakti</s> is the deity.
Āṃ is the seed.
Hrīṃ is the power; kroṃ is the pin.
Its application is for the prāṇapratiṣṭhā of this liṅga.
First he should worship the seat with perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice, and the like.
Hāṃ, homage to the support-power.
Hrīṃ, homage to <s>Kūrma</s>.
Hrūṃ, homage to <s>Ananta</s>.
Hraiṃ, homage to the earth.
Hrauṃ, homage to the bulb.

children.text: aṅkurāya nālāya karṇikebhyaḥ dalebhyaḥ kesarebhyaḥ karṇikāyai tanmadhye dharmāya jñānāya vairāgyāya aiśvaryāya adharmāya ajñānāya avairāgyāya anaiśvaryāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the sprout, to the stalk, to the pericarps, to the petals, to the filaments, to the central pericarp, and in its middle to dharma, knowledge, dispassion, sovereignty, non-dharma, ignorance, non-dispassion, and non-sovereignty.
O <s>Maheśvarī</s>, he should invoke the god who is situated in the lotus of the heart, together with the goddess,
complete with his enclosure and endowed with the powers of his own limbs.
He should install the liṅga on the pīṭha and offer arghya with kuśa-water by means of the root mantra.
He should give water for the feet with scented waters, and rinsing should be with gold.
The bath should be with jewel-water; everything is done with the root mantra, O <s>Śāmbhavī</s>.
With the elevenfold <s>Rudra</s>, with the <s>Pavamāna</s>, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
with the <s>Camaka</s>s and the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>s, and also with fruits and the five nectars,
with coconut water, sugarcane juice, and fragrant water,

children.text: saṃsnāpya ca tato liṅgaṃ pīṭhe saṃsthāpayecchive
children.translated_text: having bathed the liṅga, he should then install it on the pīṭha, O <s>Śivā</s>.

children.text: liṅgasya paritaḥ oṃ vāmadevāya namaḥ jyeṣṭhāya rudrāya kālāya kalavikaraṇāya balāya balavikaraṇāya balapramathanāya sarvabhūtadamanāya ityaṣṭāsu dikṣu manonmanāya iti śivasannidhau puṣpairabhyarcya
children.translated_text: Around the liṅga, in the eight directions, after worshipping with flowers in the presence of <s>Śiva</s>, saying, 'Oṃ, homage to <s>Vāmadeva</s>; to the eldest, to <s>Rudra</s>, to Time, to the transformer of time, to strength, to the transformer of strength, to the crusher of strength, to the subduer of all beings,' and then, 'to <s>Manonmanā</s>,'
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the heart.
Oṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Oṃ hrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the topknot.
Oṃ hraiṃ, huṃ to the armor.
Oṃ hrauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes.
Oṃ hraḥ, phaṭ to the missile.
Hrāṃ, homage to <s>Īśāna</s>.
Hrīṃ, homage to <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>.
Hrūṃ, homage to <s>Aghora</s>.
Hraiṃ, homage to <s>Vāmadeva</s>.
Hrauṃ, homage to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
With the root mantra one should give a handful of flowers to the god, dear one.
And with the root mantra and the six limbs one should perform the <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) of <s>Śiva</s>.
On the southern side of the liṅga, the Vedas beginning with the <s>Ṛgveda</s> should also be worshipped,

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ pṛthivīṃ toyaṃ viṣṇuṃ rudraṃ hutāśanam
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Brahmā</s>, earth, water, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and fire,
<s>Īśvara</s>, wind, space, and <s>Sadāśiva</s> in this way,
<s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, the moon, <s>Bhairava</s>, and the sun likewise,
the supreme <s>Śiva</s> and the supreme self; the wise man should worship them in order.

children.text: liṅgasya vāmapārśve tu brāhmyādīḥ sapta mātaraḥ
children.translated_text: On the left side of the liṅga are the seven Mothers beginning with <s>Brāhmī</s>,
<s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, <s>Mahākālī</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, and <s>Vināyaka</s>;
the Yoginīs, the field-guardians, the Śaktis, and the original seats,

children.text: oḍyāṇaśaktir jālaṃdhrī tathā pūrṇā giriḥ priye ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Oḍyāṇa</s> Śakti, <s>Jālaṃdhrī</s>, and also <s>Pūrṇagiri</s>, dear one,
and <s>Kāmeśvarī</s>, the <s>Rudraśakti</s>, should be worshipped, O you honored by the gods.
<s>Lopāmudrā</s>, <s>Kubjikā</s>, and <s>Kālasaṃkarṣaṇī</s> likewise,
the tastes beginning with sweetness, the fragrances, all grains, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
divine herbs, nectar, liquor, poison, and bodily constituents such as skin,
the senses, mind, intellect, ego, and consciousness,

children.text: śabdādyā viṣayāḥ pūjyā dehāṅgāni ca śāmbhavi ||
children.translated_text: the objects beginning with sound, and the limbs of the body should be worshipped, O <s>Śāmbhavī</s>.

children.text: liṅgasya paścime bhāge samudrāḥ sarito nadāḥ
children.translated_text: On the western side of the liṅga are the oceans, streams, and rivers,
mountains, with <s>Meru</s> foremost, and the nine planets beginning with the sun,
the circle of the stars, <s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Śiśumāra</s>, and <s>Prajāpati</s>,

children.text: kalāḥ kāṣṭhāśca ghaṭikā muhūrtāḥ praharā dinam ||
children.translated_text: kalās, kāṣṭhās, ghaṭikās, muhūrtas, watches, the day,
night, fortnight, month, seasons, times, and solstitial courses,
years, ages, kalpas, directions, stars, and lunar days, O <s>Śivā</s>,
the netherworlds, the serpent-lords, and the <s>Kālāgnirudras</s>,
yakṣas, piśācas, bhūtas, rākṣasas, and danujas likewise,
guhyakas, harmful vetālas, and diseases beginning with consumption,

children.text: mantrāḥ śastrāṇi cāstrāṇi sampūjya kramaśaḥ priye ||
children.translated_text: mantras, weapons, and missiles; one should worship them successively, dear one.
On the eastern side of the liṅga, the lines of gurus should be worshipped,
along with siddhas, sādhyas, sages, yogins, and expounders of <s>Brahman</s>,
vidyādharas, kinnaras, gandharvas, and the two <s>Aśvins</s> likewise,
the <s>Vasus</s>, the foremost of the apsarases, and the nine aesthetic moods beginning with erotic love,
song, dances and their varieties, and the ten beginning with <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
the <s>Rudras</s> together with the <s>Manus</s>, the suns, and the three fires,
the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the ancestors, the mothers, and the ancestral deities,
family teachers, teachers of rasa, former teachers, and worshippers of <s>Śiva</s>,
the ten incarnations beginning with the fish, the <s>Jina</s>, and the materialist doctrine as well,
all worlds beginning with the hells, <s>Garuḍas</s>, and the eggs of <s>Garuḍa</s>,
world-eggs, all beings who move in the sky, those who move on land, and those who move in water.
Having worshipped all the deities with mantras beginning with oṃ and ending in namaḥ,
with each of their respective names in the dative ending, with flowers, fragrance, and unbroken rice, dear one,
one should offer to the god a pair of garments and likewise two sacred threads,
madhuparka, divine fragrance, unbroken rice, and flowers,
always excluding ketaka blossoms, and also divine leaves,
those flowers: kahlāra, lotus, blue lotus, and white water-lily,
jasmine, campaka, punnāga, areca, and orange blossoms,
māgadhī, mādhavī, mallī, yūthikā, and others,
damanī and maruvaka too; he should offer them to <s>Rasendra</s>.
He should present incense made of the ten ingredients, a lamp, cakes, cooked rice, and ghee-rice pudding,
vegetables containing the six tastes and furnished with pure, excellent fragrance,
and food offerings such as what is to be licked and sucked to the lord <s>Pārada</s>.
O goddess, he should give water for washing the hands, together with scented water.
He should offer well-scented areca nuts, joined with camphor,
and white, pointed betel leaves,
powder produced from pearls, and betel.

children.text: darpaṇaṃ cāmaradvandvaṃ chatraṃ nṛttaṃ ca gītakam ||
children.translated_text: He should also offer a mirror, a pair of fly-whisks, an umbrella, dance, and song.
Among all the services he should give water for sipping, dear one.
He should offer all services with the root mantra and recite a hymn, O <s>Śivā</s>.
Having meditated on the god <s>Rasendrabhairava</s> and the goddess <s>Rasāṃkuśā</s>,
he should worship the <s>Māheśvaras</s> and the bowing goddess with fragrances, flowers, and the like.
With the thumb and ring finger he should offer what is endowed with the finest fragrance,
using the bindu-root mantra, to the god, to the goddess, and to the line of gurus.
Then, in sequence, he should also satisfy with libations the goddesses who stand in the enclosures.
Hrīṃ, I worship the form of <s>Ānandaśiva</s>.
Hrīṃ, I worship the form of <s>Parānandaśiva</s>.
Hrīṃ, I worship the form of <s>Parāparānandaśiva</s>.
Hrīṃ, I worship the form of <s>Ānandasiddha</s>.
Hrīṃ, I worship the form of <s>Parānandasiddha</s>.
Hrīṃ, I worship the form of <s>Parāparānandasiddha</s>.
Klīṃ, I worship the form of <s>Ānandaguru</s>.
Klīṃ, I worship the form of <s>Parānandaguru</s>.
Klīṃ. I worship the form of the guru who is the bliss of the supreme and the non-supreme.

children.text: tebhyo dattvā prasādaṃ ca tairanujñāpitaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: Having given prasāda to them, and having himself been permitted by them,

children.text: kuṇḍalyām ātmatattvaṃ ca vidyātattvaṃ ca nābhigam
children.translated_text: he should know the <s>ātmatattva</s> in <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>, and the <s>vidyātattva</s> at the navel,

children.text: hṛdaye śivatattvaṃ ca sarvatattvaṃ hi tālugam ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>śivatattva</s> in the heart; indeed all the <s>tattvas</s> are located in the palate.

children.text: tritattvam evaṃ saṃcintya prasādaṃ ca samantrakam
children.translated_text: Having thus contemplated the three <s>tattvas</s>, and the prasāda accompanied by mantra,
then, dear one, having remembered the blazing light contained within,
he should take the prasāda as he wishes, O you who are served by the gods.
The ancestors are pleased with joy, and all the deities through <s>mūrchā</s>.

children.text: ajñānā vaprītiḥ sa evāhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: From ignorance there is non-delight; he indeed is I, without doubt.
The finest fragrance, cooked rice, pure blood, ghee, and honey,

children.text: saṃyojya pañcakhaṇḍaṃ ca kṛtvā dadyātkrameṇa ca
children.translated_text: having combined them and made the five portions, he should offer them in sequence,
to the south, north, east, west, and middle.
Uttering the appropriate mantras, a man should then give the bali.

children.text: praṇavaṃ māyāṃ kamalāṃ devīṃ putrapradaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>praṇava</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Kamalā</s>, the Goddess, and then the giver of sons:

children.text: tato vaṭukanāthākhyaṃ kapilaṃ jaṭābhārabhāsuraṃ ca tataḥ piṅgala triṇetra imāṃ baliṃ pūjāṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa svāhā
children.translated_text: Then: 'To the one called <s>Vaṭukanātha</s>, tawny, resplendent with a mass of matted hair; then, O <s>Piṅgala</s>, three-eyed one, accept, accept this bali and worship. Svāhā.'

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ siddhayoginībhyaḥ sarvamātṛbhyo namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the perfected yoginīs and to all the Mothers.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sarvabhūtebhyaḥ sarvabhūtapatibhyo namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to all beings and to the lords of all beings.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sthānakṣetrapāla imāṃ baliṃ pūjāṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, O <s>Sthānakṣetrapāla</s>, accept, accept this bali and worship. Svāhā.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ rasendra kṣetrapāla rājarājeśvara imāṃ baliṃ pūjāṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, O <s>Rasendra Kṣetrapāla Rājarājeśvara</s>, accept, accept this bali and worship. Svāhā.
Thus, O <s>Śivā</s>, the bali should be given for the pacification of all obstacles.
Then he should recite the root mantra one hundred and eight times before the <s>rasa</s>.
Then, O <s>Devī</s>, he should recite the hymn for the satisfaction of <s>Rasabhairava</s>.

children.text: saṃtuṣṭāḥ sarvadevāḥ syuḥ tuṣṭe tu rasabhairave ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Rasabhairava</s> is satisfied, all the gods become satisfied.
This procedure of daily worship has been taught; it is hard to find anywhere.

children.text: viddhi māṃ pāradaṃ devi tatsmartā matsamaḥ priye ||
children.translated_text: Know me to be <s>pārada</s>, O <s>Devī</s>; one who remembers it is equal to me, dear one.
But <s>pārada</s> is greater than I, because it belongs to me and because of its essence.

children.text: rasasya smaraṇaṃ puṇyaṃ darśanaṃ sparśanaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Remembering <s>rasa</s> is meritorious, and so are seeing and touching it.
Worshipping, eating, and giving it are proclaimed to be the sixfold merit.

children.text: sāttvikaṃ rājasaṃ caiva tāmasaṃ trividhaṃ vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its body is threefold: sāttvika, rājasa, and tāmasa.
The sāttvika form, white and liberation-giving, is childlike and adorned with two arms,
holding a full vessel and a fine staff, two-eyed, with a garland of tinkling bells.
The rājasa form, red and enjoyment-giving, bears a crown and a moon crest.
It is four-armed, youthful, blue-throated, and three-eyed.
One should meditate on it as granting all lordly powers, with trident, vessel, boon, and fearlessness.
The tāmasa form is black in color, with hair blazing upward.
One should contemplate the <s>rasa</s> as previously described, eighteen-armed and three-eyed.
It grants all siddhis, O <s>Devī</s>, and grants the fruits of every desire.
Remembering <s>Rasarāja</s> destroys every misfortune.
One should meditate on him situated in the heart-lotus; sins perish, O <s>Bhairavī</s>.
The sight of <s>Pāradendra</s> destroys sin born in the three times.
In seeing the multitude of divine liṅgas extending from <s>Setu</s> to <s>Kedāra</s>,
whatever merit a mortal obtains becomes multiplied ten million times.
By seeing, bathing, drinking, and the like at all the sacred fords on earth, up to the oceans,
the merit gained thereby becomes multiplied ten million times.
Tens of thousands of cow-killings, O <s>Devī</s>, and hundreds of embryo-killings,
and thousands of brahmin-killings perish through the sight of <s>rasa</s>.
By the gift of ten million cows and a hundred crores of gold,
and by a thousand <s>Aśvamedhas</s>, whatever merit there is comes also from seeing it.
Touching <s>rasa</s> destroys intercourse with one who should not be approached, dear one,
the theft of another's property, and sin acquired by killing living beings.

children.text: saptadvīpe dharaṇyāṃ ca pātāle gagane divi ||
children.translated_text: On the earth with its seven continents, in the netherworld, in the sky, and in heaven,
whatever liṅgas one worships, that merit is obtained by worshipping <s>rasa</s>.
By performing worship among self-born divine liṅgas,
whatever merit there is, that result comes from worship of the <s>rasaliṅga</s>.
The state that yogins devoted to the eight limbs and proclaimers of <s>Brahman</s> attain,
that state one obtains through worship of the <s>rasaliṅga</s>.
<s>Rasa</s> placed together with saffron, agaru, musk, and camphor,
processed by <s>mūrchā</s>, should be offered to the <s>rasaliṅga</s> for the accomplishment of desired aims.
By consuming <s>Rasarāja</s>, all sin is destroyed.
It dries up the self polluted by beginningless <s>māyā</s>.
It quickly removes the disease of worldly existence and destroys the three pains.
By giving <s>Rasarāja</s>, one obtains the fruit of giving the earth bounded by the four oceans,

children.text: mahāmerusamaṃ svarṇaṃ dattvā yattat phalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and of giving gold equal to great <s>Meru</s>.
Pure <s>rasa</s> is <s>Brahmā</s> in form; when processed by <s>mūrchā</s>, it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> in form.
When reduced to ash it is <s>Rudra</s> in form; when bound, <s>sūta</s> is always <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
When leech-like it has the form of desire; when faulty it has the form of Time.
Processed by <s>mūrchā</s>, calcined, and bound, <s>Pāradendra</s>, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>,
this compassionate one removes disease, death, and poverty.
O <s>Rasendra</s>, you quickly grant through sound, touch, and smoke,
gold up to hundreds of millions; protect me, giver of <s>khecara-siddhi</s>.
Homage to you, O <s>Kālakāla</s>; homage to the self of all qualities.
Homage to the destroyer of wrinkles and grey hair, to the giver of great virility.
Homage to the destroyer of weapons and missiles, O <s>Pārada</s>, ocean of <s>māyā</s>.
O <s>Pāradendra</s>, homage to you, <s>Manmatha</s> in the play of women.
Being of nectar, destroyer of the three <s>doṣas</s>, homage to you whose nature is the six tastes.
Because of your solidity you have the form of earth; because of your fluidity, the form of water.
Because of your abundance of fire you are fiery; because of your restlessness, you have the form of wind.
Because of your subtlety, homage to you whose form is <s>rasa</s> (mercurial essence), whose form is the elements.
Homage to you who are fit for alchemical yoga; be gracious, you who are worshipped by the immortals.
Through injury to the Veda, cows, twice-borns, kings, teachers, heroes, and the like,
diseases such as consumption and leprosy arise; you remove them, O purifier.
O <s>Pārada</s>, you are the savior of the ignorant, of those whose senses and objects have been lost.
You are greater even than all medicines through the use of merely an atom-sized dose.
Even alone you destroy every <s>doṣa</s>; remover of loss of taste, homage to you.

children.text: tvayā sṛṣṭā mahendrādyāḥ surā brahmādayaḥ kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By you were created the gods beginning with <s>Mahendra</s>, the deities beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, and the arts,
the moon, sun, planets, constellations, and the powers of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Bhairava</s>,
knowledge and ignorance, the qualities, the worlds, gandharvas, serpents, and rākṣasas,
and all divine herbs, even those that bestow every perfection.

children.text: sūtendra bhavataḥ śrīman kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūtendra</s>, O glorious one, they are not worth even a sixteenth part of you.
O manifest <s>Śambhu</s>, O <s>Sūtendra</s>, what is the use of others when you are present?
You are endowed with powers such as <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and bestow many kinds of perfection.
Through service to you, yogins always obtain inexhaustible metals, with gold foremost,
and they obtain immortality. Who there is more brilliant?
A man who does not know you, whose form is visible and invisible, supreme and bestowing enjoyment and liberation,

children.text: yo na jānāti sūtendra sa māṃ vetti kathaṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūtendra</s>, how could he know me?

children.text: gururmātā pitā bhrātā dhanaṃ vidyā gatiḥ suhṛt
children.translated_text: Teacher, mother, father, brother, wealth, knowledge, refuge, and friend:

children.text: rasa tvameva bhūtānāṃ tvattaḥ ko'nyo hitaṃkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Rasa</s>, you alone are these for beings. Who other than you is a benefactor?

children.text: rasendra tava yoge ca śāstre stotre rasāyane
children.translated_text: O <s>Rasendra</s>, in your yoga, śāstra, hymn, and rasāyana,

children.text: yastu bhaktiyuto loke sa evāhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whoever in the world is endowed with devotion is indeed I; there is no doubt.
Even if one is deeply versed in knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, if he reviles you, O <s>Pārada</s>,
he should be abandoned in all worlds; I am not able to protect him.

children.text: yastvāṃ nāstīti ca vadet tasya siddhirna kutracit
children.translated_text: Whoever says, 'You do not exist,' has no perfection anywhere.
But whoever says, 'You exist,' always obtains perfection.
Whoever in this world, whether of noble birth or of low lineage, takes up <s>Rasendra</s>,
and prepares you, O <s>Sūta</s>, by the eighteen operations,

children.text: sa puṇyaḥ sa vratī dhanyaḥ sa ślāghyaḥ sa ca buddhimān
children.translated_text: he is meritorious, he is observant, he is blessed, he is praiseworthy, and he is wise.

children.text: sa pumānsa ca sarvajñaḥ sa siddhaḥ sa ca daivatam ||
children.translated_text: He is a true man, he is all-knowing, he is accomplished, and he is a deity.

children.text: tatkulaṃ pāvanaṃ bhūmiḥ puṇyā rājā jayānvitaḥ
children.translated_text: His family is purifying, the earth is holy, and the king is endowed with victory.

children.text: tatpuraṃ sotsavaṃ nityaṃ kṛtārthā ca tadambikā ||
children.translated_text: His city is always festive, and his mother is fulfilled.

children.text: tasya saṃdarśanaṃ puṇyaṃ sparśanaṃ bhāṣaṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Seeing him is meritorious, and so too are touching him and speaking with him.
By direct perception and the other means of knowledge, O <s>Pārada</s>, you are <s>Sadāśiva</s>.

children.text: tvatto dehādi lohāni vajratvaṃ yānti hematām
children.translated_text: From you, bodies and metals attain adamantine strength and golden nature.
O <s>Rasendra</s>, by your favor proud, doe-eyed women
shine with lofty, full, round breasts like cakravāka birds.
They become lively, intent on love, and beautiful with coral lips.
They have curved, sharp nail-sprouts resembling parrots' beaks.
Their lovely arms are like garlands of śirīṣa, and their radiance is like garlands of campaka.
They are adorned with a line of hair rising from a deep navel.

children.text: sarvāṅgasauṣṭhavāḥ kāntāḥ snigdhā vaśyā bhavanti ca ||
children.translated_text: They are lovely in the grace of every limb, affectionate, and compliant.
O <s>Sūtendra</s>, just as fire burns a heap of dry wood,
so too it burns away poverty from birth, death, sorrow, and great diseases.
For however many days one keeps you in the middle of fire for the purpose of <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestive calcination),
for that many thousands of kalpas he dwells happily in the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
If a person spends even a little wealth on your rites, O <s>Sūtendra</s>,
you give them that wealth increased many crores upon crores of times.
The supreme <s>Pāradī</s> science is hard to obtain in all worlds.
It is holy, grants enjoyment and liberation, and increases sons and health.
Those who revile you, O <s>Sūtendra</s>, become cats, donkeys, crows,
jackals, bulls, dogs, impotent men, blind men, deaf men, and dullards,

children.text: mūkāḥ kubjāḥ paṅgavaśca vyaṅgā vandhyāśca rogiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: mute, hunchbacked, lame, deformed, barren, and diseased,
and fishermen and evil-doers through many births.
Whoever, together with those who revile you, mixes cooked food in a vessel,
or shares a seat, bed, meal, conversation, or association with them,
becomes most sinful, to be abandoned and excluded from all dharmas.

children.text: iti stotraṃ mayā proktaṃ pāradendrasya bhairavi ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Bhairavī</s>, I have spoken the hymn of <s>Pāradendra</s>.
Whoever recites or hears it with devotion at the three junctions of the day for success in <s>rasa</s>,
from sins such as killing a Brahmin, from major sins and minor sins,
and from the defilements of the three acts and of the Kali age, O goddess, is freed; there is no doubt.
In a terrible battle, in a great forest, in confusion of direction, or in danger from enemies,
when crossing a river, O goddess, or in danger from thieves, tigers, and the like,
one should recite this hymn, O goddess, after meditating on glorious <s>Rasabhairava</s>.

children.text: iti stutvā sūtarājaṃ sarvaṃ karma samarpayet
children.translated_text: Having thus praised <s>Sūtarāja</s>, he should dedicate every rite.

children.text: raso dātā raso bhoktā rasaḥ kartā ca kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> is the giver, <s>Rasa</s> is the enjoyer, <s>Rasa</s> is the doer and the cause.

children.text: raso hotā ca havyaṃ ca sarvavyāpī rasaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> is the hotṛ priest and the oblation; <s>Rasa</s> is always all-pervading.
With this very mantra he should dedicate it to <s>Rasendra</s>.

children.text: tato nyāsaṃ ca mūlena kuryāddhyātvā ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Then he should perform <s>nyāsa</s> with the root mantra, meditating as before.
Then, having made the <s>saṃhāramudrā</s>, he should carry <s>Raseśvara</s> to the river.
He should install the god, together with his limbs, enclosure, and powers, in the lotus of the heart.
The <s>rasa</s> preceptor should contemplate the true conviction, 'I am <s>Śiva</s>.'
Having swept the place of worship, he should sprinkle it with water.

children.text: tato homālayaṃ prāpya samācamya ca deśikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having gone to the fire sanctuary, the preceptor should sip water in purification.
In the ritual hall, in the quarter of <s>Agni</s>, in a yoni-shaped fire-pit with three girdles,
properly strewn around with darbha grasses whose tips face east and north,

children.text: nyāsaṃ mūlena saṃkalpya prāṇāyāmaṃ vidhāya ca
children.translated_text: having undertaken <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual installation) with the root mantra and performed <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control),

children.text: pañcabhūsaṃskṛtaṃ kṛtvā svastriyā vā dvijena vā ||
children.translated_text: and having made it purified by the five <s>bhūsaṃskāras</s>, either with his own wife or with a twice-born assistant,
he should bring the fire, place it in the pit, and then kindle it.
He should meditate on Fire as wearing a mass of tawny matted hair, three-eyed, and clothed in white,
as a god standing on a red lotus, adorned with garlands and ornaments,
with seven hands, four horns, two heads, and three feet,
bound in three ways, bull-like, and holding weapons beginning with the spear,
and he should perform for him all services beginning with <s>arghya</s> and water for the feet.
With perfumes, unbroken rice, and fine flowers he should worship <s>Jātavedas</s>.
In that fire he should invoke the deity, visualizing <s>Rasabhairava</s>.
He should perform the deity's <s>nyāsa</s> and make oblations with the root mantra.
With sesame, ghee, and rice-grains, dear one, he should offer the mantra one hundred and eight times,
or he may do twenty-eight; from the root mantra he should pour the preliminary oblation.

children.text: prāṇāyāmaṃ tato nyāsaṃ kṛtvā ca hṛdi dhāraṇam
children.translated_text: Then, having performed <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, <s>nyāsa</s>, and concentration in the heart,
thus the rule of daily worship has been taught to you, O one worshiped by the gods.
Now I shall proclaim <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), which bestows all accomplishments.
It is said to be fivefold because of distinctions beginning with <s>samayā</s>.
The first initiation is <s>samayā</s>; the second is called <s>sādhakā</s>.
The third is called <s>nirvāṇā</s>, and the fourth is named <s>ācāryā</s>.

children.text: pañcamī siddhasaṃjñā ca prāyaśo durlabhā nṛṇām
children.translated_text: The fifth is named <s>siddhā</s> and is generally difficult for men to obtain.
A disciple endowed with the characteristics described before, bowed down in devotion and pure,

children.text: guruṃ praṇamya cāṣṭāṅgaṃ stutvā ca bahudhā tataḥ
children.translated_text: having bowed to the guru with the eight limbs and then praised him in many ways,
should petition the guru, saying, 'Favor me with initiation.'
And after obtaining initiation according to rule, the disciple becomes a seer of all aims.
The asterisms <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, and <s>Punarvasu</s>,
<s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Maitra</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, and the three <s>Uttarās</s>,
and <s>Maghā</s> and <s>Aśvinī</s> are the most excellent stars for the act of initiation.

children.text: tṛtīyā pañcamī caiva saptamī ca caturdaśī
children.translated_text: The third, fifth, seventh, and fourteenth lunar days,

children.text: aṣṭamī paurṇamāsī ca daśamī ca trayodaśī ||
children.translated_text: the eighth, full-moon day, tenth, and thirteenth,
these lunar days are principal; on the weekdays of Mercury, the Moon, Jupiter, Venus,
and the Sun, <s>rasadīkṣā</s> is very auspicious.
In the bright fortnight, under a good yoga, with the Viṣṭi karaṇa avoided,
at an equinox, solstice, or solar ingress endowed with the strength of the moon and stars,
at an eclipse, on <s>Śivarātri</s>, in the birth-asterism, at a good <s>muhūrta</s>,
under an auspicious planet and a siddhi-yoga, the best guru should give initiation.
Then, entering the <s>rasaśālā</s> (alchemical ritual hall), resplendent with all implements,
strewn with flower garlands and furnished with archways and banners,
having done the daily worship and the fire rite, he should undertake the sequence of initiation.

children.text: devasya dakṣiṇe pārśve vistare taṇḍulān śritān ||
children.translated_text: On the right side of the deity, on a spread laid over rice-grains,
he should make a square and place a <s>prastha</s> of fine rice in its center.
Above that he should set a jar wrapped with white thread,
covered with two cloths, furnished with mercury and the five jewels,
filled with water purified by the five earths, shoots, and barks,
and supplied with <s>dūrvā</s> grass, perfume, excellent sesame, gold, darbha, and unbroken rice.
He should contemplate this jar, called <s>Śiva</s>, as having the form of <s>Śiva</s>.
Having placed on its left side a pot called the <s>vardhanī</s>,
in the form of <s>Śakti</s> and furnished with all the previously mentioned substances,
around it he should draw a <s>sarvatobhadra</s> and a <s>śrīgaurītilaka</s>,
and a <s>nandyāvarta</s> and svastika, shining with five colors.

children.text: prakṣālya pādau pāṇī ca samācamya gurūttamaḥ
children.translated_text: The best guru, having washed his feet and hands and sipped water,
having taken his own seat and likewise performed three breath-controls,
should make a solemn intention for the increase of the disciple's life, health, prosperity, and offspring,
and for liberation and the eight accomplishments, and should worship <s>Śiva</s>.
With perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice, incenses, lamps, food-offerings, and showings,
he should worship the <s>Śiva</s>-jar and the <s>vardhanī</s> with full services.
He should recite the root mantra, <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>, one thousand times,
and should offer one-tenth of that in the triangular pit endowed with the proper marks.
Then he should prepare fruit mixed with the three sweet substances and furnished with excellent fragrance;
then, in order, for the deities of the enclosure, using each one's own name in the dative case,
with <s>svāhā</s> at the end and <s>oṃ</s> at the beginning, he should pronounce it and offer the oblation.

children.text: śivatrayaṃ purā devi tataḥ siddhatrayaṃ yajet ||
children.translated_text: First, O <s>Devī</s>, he should worship the three <s>Śivas</s>, and then the three <s>Siddhas</s>.
Then, O <s>Devī</s>, the best guru should worship the three gurus and the elders of the lineage;
and after worshiping the <s>Yoginī</s>, the guru, having received permission, then says:
'I worship the form of <s>Ānandaśiva</s> together with <s>Śakti</s>,
and likewise I worship the form of <s>Parānandaśiva</s>.'
Thus he should worship the three <s>Siddha</s> forms together with the <s>śrībīja</s>.
Thus he should worship the three guru forms joined with the <s>mārabīja</s>.
Taking the three <s>tattvas</s>, he should again perform <s>nyāsa</s>.
Having himself become the body of <s>Śiva</s>, he should contemplate, 'I am <s>Śiva</s>.'
The guru who sees <s>Śiva</s> should look upon the joyful disciple joined with <s>Śakti</s>,
place him at his own left side, and put upon his head
ash consecrated with the root mantra, after covering his eyes with a cloth;
then, having sprinkled his head with water from the <s>Śiva</s>-<s>vardhanī</s>,

children.text: tridhā svadakṣiṇe haste śivaṃ sāvaraṇaṃ yajet
children.translated_text: three times on his own right hand he should worship <s>Śiva</s> together with his enclosure.
This should be known as the <s>Śiva</s>-hand, cutting the bonds of worldly existence.
And he should recite the root mantra of <s>Aṅkuśī</s> three times.
He should give the mantra instruction into the disciple's right ear.
First he should recite the mantra of <s>Gaṇapati</s>, and then the mantra of <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>.
The seer is <s>Gaṇaka</s>, and the meter is remembered as nicṛd-gāyatrī.
The deity should be known as <s>Gaṇapati</s>; the nyāsa (ritual placement) is with the seed-syllable.
He should utter the mantra made from the third letter of the first class, furnished with the half-moon, and called gaṇa,
joined with pati in the dative case and ending with namaḥ.
He should meditate on him as bearing a noose, goad, sweetmeat, and his own broken tusk,
elephant-faced, coral-red, wearing a crown with the crescent moon,

children.text: tundilaṃ gaṇanāthaṃ ca dhyātvā lakṣaṃ japenmanum ||
children.translated_text: pot-bellied, lord of the hosts; then he should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ tarpaṇaṃ homaṃ saguḍaṃ satilaṃ hunet
children.translated_text: For one tenth of that, he should perform tarpaṇa (libation) and homa (fire offering), offering oblations with jaggery and sesame.
He should utter the mantra of <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>, with kṣa joined to the bindu and with the dative ending,
ending in namaḥ, and perform the nyāsa (ritual placement) with the seed-syllable.
The meter should be known as paṅkti, the sage as <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and the deity as <s>Bhairava</s>.
He should meditate on him as four-armed, adorned with trident, bowl, boon-granting, and protection gestures,
like a dark rain-cloud, ornamented with serpents, with a garland of small bells,

children.text: trinetraṃ vakradaṃṣṭraṃ ca dhyātvā lakṣaṃ japenmanum
children.translated_text: three-eyed and having curved fangs; then he should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
For one tenth of that he should perform tarpaṇa and homa, offering milk-rice soaked in the three sweet substances.
Having thus instructed, 'He should make the offering,' he should take up samayācāra (the pledged discipline).

children.text: devatāparicaryāṃ ca śuśrūṣāṃ ca guroḥ kuru ||
children.translated_text: Perform attendance on the deities and service to the guru.
Without laziness he should perform japa (recitation) and listen to scripture with reverence.
Remain constantly devoted to the path of conduct taught before.
Bowing, with joined palms, the disciple should say, 'I shall do so, lord.
I am blessed; by your favor, revered master, I have accomplished what was to be done.'
Thus the disciple, strengthened by the pledged discipline, should make his submission.
Rising very early in the morning, he should remember the gurus on his head.
Having performed the necessary acts and bathed, he should carry out the twilight worship.

children.text: nadyāstīrthe taṭāke vā puṣkariṇyāṃ śucau jale ||
children.translated_text: In pure water at a river, a sacred ford, a tank, or a lotus-pond,
he should sip water, make his resolve, and perform the regular tarpaṇa.
First he should name the three <s>Śivas</s>, <s>Vighnanātha</s>, the lord of the field, <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ bhāskarādīṃśca grahān durgāṃ ca mātṛkāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, the planets beginning with <s>Bhāskara</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, and the Mothers,
the <s>Bhairavas</s> beginning with <s>Asitāṅga</s>, and then the triad of siddhas.
He should satisfy <s>Ādinātha</s>, <s>Mīnanātha</s>, <s>Gorakṣa</s>, <s>Koṅkaṇeśvara</s>,
<s>Jālandhreśa</s>, <s>Kandhanīśa</s>, <s>Oḍḍīśa</s>, and <s>Ciñciṇīśvara</s>,
and <s>Cauraṅgi</s>; these are the nine called <s>Nāthas</s>.
Then he should satisfy <s>Cauraṅgi</s>, <s>Carpaṭi</s>, <s>Ghoḍācūli</s>, the two <s>Rāmas</s>,
the siddha <s>Bholagovinda</s>, <s>Vyāḍi</s>, and <s>Nāgārjuna</s>,

children.text: koraṇḍaṃ śūrpakarṇaṃ ca muktāyīṃ revaṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Koraṇḍa</s>, <s>Śūrpakarṇa</s>, <s>Muktāyī</s>, and <s>Revaṇa</s>,
the siddha <s>Kukkurapāda</s>, <s>Śūrpapāda</s>, and <s>Kaṇairika</s>,

children.text: siddhaṃ kiṅkiṇikākhyaṃ ca siddhān ṣoḍaśa tarpayet ||
children.translated_text: and the siddha called <s>Kiṅkiṇika</s>; he should satisfy these sixteen siddhas.

children.text: tato gurutrayaṃ tarpya mātaraṃ pitaraṃ gurum
children.translated_text: Then, after satisfying the three gurus, he should satisfy his mother, father, guru,
teacher, brother, friend, and the others born in his family.
Having satisfied them according to rule and sipped water, he should then worship the deity.

children.text: nadyāstīre taṭāke vā goṣṭhe devālaye tathā ||
children.translated_text: On a river bank, at a tank, in a cow-pen, in a temple,
or in a pure place, he should spread sand in a circular form.
He should invoke the lord of the day, red in color and of the form of <s>Śiva</s>,
supreme, two-eyed, two-armed, and holding a pair of lotuses.
Having meditated on him as resplendent on a lotus seat, with red garland, garment, unguent, ornaments,
he should worship him with red flowers; then he should meditate on <s>Vighneśa</s> and <s>Bhairava</s>,
those two as described before, and worship them with red flowers.
He should make the eight-limbed staff-like prostration twelve times.
Then he should install the deity again in his own heart and go to serve his own guru.
Thus samaya initiation has been stated; now the sādhaka initiation is described.
The guru should initiate a true disciple who is devoted to samayācāra and whose mind is mature,
on a good day and under an auspicious ascendant, with the initiation called sādhaka.
The guru should perform an occasional worship and summon the disciple.
Himself having the body of <s>Śiva</s>, he should think of the disciple as placed in <s>Gaurī</s>'s womb.
He should spread sacred ash on the ground and draw a triangle upon it.
After seating the disciple there and binding his eyes,
he should ritually arrange conception, the male-generating rite, then the parting of the hair,

children.text: jātakarma ca dīkṣāṅgaṃ nāmadheyaṃ ca kalpayet
children.translated_text: birth-rite, and name-giving as limbs of the initiation.
At the vow rite he should sprinkle him with ash by means of the root mantra.
Having imagined him as the son of <s>Gaurī</s>, he should perform his initiation.
Looking upon him with the gaze of <s>Śiva</s>, he should place <s>Śiva</s>'s ash on his head,
and he should worship the root mantra ten times.
Into his right ear he should impart the ten-syllabled
<s>Rasendrabhairava</s> mantra and the gāyatrī called <s>Rasā</s>.
It has the fire seed with bindu, followed by the word rasendrasya,

children.text: bhairavaṃ ca caturthyantaṃ karmāstraṃ ca daśāṃśakam
children.translated_text: then bhairava in the dative ending, and the karmāstra as its tenth part.
He should perform the hand-nyāsa with the fire seed joined to a long vowel.
The seer is called <s>Aghora</s>, the meter is virāj, and the deity is <s>Maheśvara</s>.
For the preliminary service, the japa is one hundred thousand recitations, and the homa and tarpaṇa are one tenth of that.
With a steady mind he should perform the homa with sesame, ghee, and rice.
He should recite the previously stated <s>Rasagāyatrī</s> one hundred thousand times and perform tarpaṇa.
He should offer one tenth as oblations with ghee together with sesame and rice, dear one.
He should give the disciple a rosary, a rasa-liṅga, and the rasa-āgama.
Having become one who observes the conduct stated before, he should worship the <s>rasa-liṅga</s>.
He should gain understanding of the meaning of his own śāstra and perform the consecration of <s>Sūtendra</s>.
