Then he should command the disciple who is constantly devoted to service of the guru.
The disciple, with joined palms and bowed down, says, "I shall carry out your command."
When this has been said, the sādhaka's <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) called nirvāṇa is praised.
Having first performed his daily rite and having carried out the occasional worship,
as before he should set up, in order, the <s>Śiva</s>-jar and the vardhanī vessel and the rest.

children.text: svavāme bhasma saṃstīrya ṣaṭkoṇaṃ bhūgṛhaṃ likhet ||
children.translated_text: On his own left he should spread ash and draw a six-cornered bhūgṛha diagram.
The guru should seat the disciple there and sprinkle him with the water from the jars.
He should place ash, empowered with the root mantra, on his head.
He should give fragrance, flowers, and unbroken rice, and should tie on the right hand
a bracelet made of thread measuring from the big toe to the <s>Brahmarandhra</s>.
That thread, perfumed and consecrated with the root mantra,
the excellent guru should place on his head as the hand of <s>Śiva</s>.
After teaching the supreme twelve-syllabled mantra of <s>Rasāṃkuśā</s>,
the teacher should give it to the disciple, with <s>Rasabhairava</s> as its deity.
The seer, meter, deity, and <s>nyāsa</s> are as stated before, dear one.

children.text: tarpaṇaṃ cātha homaṃ ca dhyānaṃ kuryācca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: He should perform the libation, the <s>homa</s>, and the meditation as before.

children.text: utthāya ca guruṃ natvā bahuśaḥ stotramuccaret
children.translated_text: Then, rising and bowing to the guru, he should recite a hymn many times.

children.text: guruḥ śiṣyāya vai dadyādvyāghracarmāsanaṃ ca yatra ||
children.translated_text: The guru should indeed give the disciple a seat of tiger skin there.
He should give a bellows filled with cloth, a medicinal bellows,
and, having had him study the <s>Rasāgama</s>, should say, "Become, O disciple, a physician."
"You have been born in the form of <s>Rudra</s>; be one who benefits all beings."
Thus the guru should instruct the disciple, and the disciple, delighted in mind,
should declare, "I have done what had to be done; I am purified; I have crossed the ocean of saṃsāra."

children.text: iti vijñāpayecchiṣyaḥ stutvā ca bahudhā gurum ||
children.translated_text: So the disciple should announce, after praising the guru in many ways.
This nirvāṇa-dīkṣā has been taught; now comes the consecration as an ācārya.
For this great-souled disciple who has received nirvāṇa-dīkṣā,
the excellent guru should duly perform the ācārya-dīkṣā also.
He should arrange everything just as in the nirvāṇa-dīkṣā.
In particular, he should place a jar in front of the <s>Śiva</s> and vardhanī vessels,
containing silver, fragrant substances, metals, grains, and groups of divine herbs.
He should put everything else into it just as in the <s>Śiva</s>-jar.
Touching the guru-jar, he should recite the root mantra one hundred and eight times.
Know this to be the guru-jar; he should worship it with the guru-mantra,
with the sixteen services beginning with invocation, seat, and arghya.
There itself he should worship the line of <s>Śiva</s> and the others, together with the guru.
He should seat the disciple as before, with mind concentrated.
As before, he should sprinkle him with the water from the <s>Śiva</s> and vardhanī vessels.
As before, he should perform the <s>Śiva</s>-hand and the teaching of the root mantra,

children.text: kṛtvā taduttamāṅge ca gurupaṅktiṃ guruṃ tathā
children.translated_text: placing it on the crown of his head; then he should worship the guru-line and the guru,
with offerings beginning with invocation, and with fragrances, garlands, and lamps.
He should worship in order with food offerings furnished with fruits and excellent fragrance.
With the jar waters, the guru should perform sprinkling with five leafy shoots,
one hundred times with the root mantra, and twenty-one times with the line of <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: tathaiva siddhapaṅktyā ca gurupaṅktyā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: and likewise with the line of siddhas and likewise with the line of gurus.
To the disciple who is devoted to the guru, endowed with power, and intelligent,
he should give necklaces, armlets, bracelets, rings, and crowns,
vehicles, seats, a fine parasol, yak-tail fly-whisks, and fans,
a pair of jeweled earrings and an inexhaustible vessel rich in sacred ash,
a helmet together with a turban, and an excellent silk bodice,
a yoga-band, a yoga-staff, and likewise an uḍḍiyāṇa binding.
He should also give him the command, "You are now an ācārya."
"You are a lord today; you are blessed. Become the teacher of all."
"Become the expounder of the divine <s>Rasāgamas</s>, a knower of reality."
Thus the guru should instruct the disciple, who is bowed down and affectionate toward the guru.
And this is the ācārya-dīkṣā; now the siddha-dīkṣā is described.
For nine nights, or seven nights, or five nights, or three nights,
twenty-one vīras endowed with śakti should be worshipped each day,

children.text: tatsaṃkhyā yoginaḥ pūjyāḥ kumārāḥ kanyakāḥ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the same number of yogins should be worshipped, along with boys, maidens, and women.
With fragrances, flowers, unbroken rice, flowers again, fruits, and excellent fragrant offerings,
having satisfied them, he should give garments, ornaments, and honoraria.
Then, touching with both hands the head of the disciple, who is seated on the seat, devoted and pure,

children.text: spṛṣṭvā karābhyāṃ tacchīrṣaṃ dakṣiṇe śravaṇe manum ||
children.translated_text: he should initiate him in the mantra at his right ear.

children.text: vahniṃ sabījaṃ śītāṃśuṃ savisargaṃ ca dīkṣayet
children.translated_text: He should initiate him into the fire together with the seed, and the moon together with the visarga.
He should contemplate the syllable repha arising from the <s>Mūlādhāra</s>, like a flame of fire,
crossing the lotuses of the six supports and reaching up to the <s>Brahmarandhra</s>.
From the <s>Brahmarandhra</s>, the melted syllable sa, having the form of the moon,
floods the whole body: the siddha should visualize the mantra in this way.
It arises from exhalation and inhalation and is the cause of dissolution and maintenance.
Knowing it thus in the mind, always and constantly as the essence of all mantras,
as consisting of all gods, meritorious, and bestowing all siddhis,
as granting liberation while living, pure, supreme, and consisting of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>,
know this rasa-mantra and practice it as having the nature of fire and moon.
Its number is twenty-one thousand six hundred,
set in motion by day and night; place your mind there.
The seer of this mantra is <s>Jīva</s>; its metre and the rest are declared as stated.

children.text: raso devastu raṃ bījaṃ saṃ śaktistu prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> is the deity; <s>raṃ</s> is proclaimed as the seed, and <s>saṃ</s> as the śakti.
One should form it joined with the long repha, and should perform the hand-and-limb nyāsa.
O <s>Devi</s>, one should meditate in the lotus of the heart on it, resembling ten million suns and moons,
on <s>rasa</s>, shining like pure crystal and carrying one across saṃsāra.

children.text: evaṃ niṣkalarūpaṃ taṃ dhyātvā tanmayatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated on him in his partless form, one should enter into identity with him.

children.text: tvaṃ rasastvaṃ śivastvaṃ hi śaktistvaṃ bhairaveśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: You are <s>rasa</s>; you are <s>Śiva</s>; indeed you are <s>Śakti</s>; you are <s>Bhairaveśvara</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ brahmā tvaṃ hi rudraśca sūryastvaṃ śītadīdhitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are <s>Brahmā</s>; you are <s>Rudra</s>; you are the sun; you are the cool-rayed moon.

children.text: tvaṃ bhūstvaṃ salilastvaṃ ca vahnistvaṃ ca sadāgatiḥ
children.translated_text: You are earth; you are water; you are fire; you are the ever-moving wind.

children.text: tvaṃ vyoma tvaṃ parākāśaḥ tvaṃ jīvastvaṃ parā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are space; you are the supreme ether; you are the living self; you are the supreme goal.

children.text: tvaṃ siddhastvaṃ prabuddhastvaṃ sugandhastvaṃ ca manmathaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the siddha; you are the awakened one; you are fragrance; and you are <s>Manmatha</s>.
You are the guardians of the worlds; you are <s>Tārā</s>; you are the mother-syllables; you are <s>Gajānana</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ skandastvaṃ gurustvaṃ ca tvaṃ sarvajanakaḥ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: You are <s>Skanda</s>; you are the guru; you are the pure progenitor of all.

children.text: tvaṃ yajvā tvaṃ haristvaṃ ca tretāgnistvaṃ ca ṛtvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are the sacrificer; you are <s>Hari</s>; you are the three sacred fires and the priests.
By whomever you are worshipped, all the deities have thereby been worshipped.
When you are pleased, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s> are pleased.
By drinking the water from your feet, one obtains the fruit of all sacred bathing places.

children.text: yastvāṃ paśyati sadbhaktyā tam ālokayate śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever sees you with true devotion is beheld by <s>Śiva</s>.
For one who praises you, the fruit of all mantras comes to be.

children.text: yatra tvaṃ kṣaṇamātre ca puṇyakṣetraṃ taducyate ||
children.translated_text: Wherever you are even for a single moment, that is called a holy field.

children.text: tvaṃ yaṃ paśyati siddhendra sa brahmā viṣṇurīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Whomever you behold, O lord of siddhas, he is <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Īśvara</s>.
Where you eat a morsel of food, there indeed the three worlds are present.

children.text: yena tvaṃ dhriyase nātha tvayāyaṃ striyatekṣaṇam
children.translated_text: By whomever you are borne, O lord, this world is sustained by you even for a moment.

children.text: sa eva citsadānandaḥ paramātmā dhruvaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: He alone surely becomes consciousness, being, and bliss, the supreme self.
For you, a siddha and yogin whose mind is thus resolved,
there are no rules of proper conduct for class and life-stage, nor any distinction of what should and should not be done.

children.text: pāpaṃ puṇyaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ śītamuṣṇaṃ priyāpriye
children.translated_text: Sin and merit, pleasure and pain, cold and heat, pleasant and unpleasant,
bathing and not bathing, loss and increase, purity and impurity, fear and fearlessness,

children.text: grāhyāgrāhyaṃ kṣudhā tṛṣṇā na kiṃcid iha vidyate
children.translated_text: what is acceptable and unacceptable, hunger and thirst: none of these exists here.
With food and movement according to his own will, he is happy, his mind delighted,
free from possessiveness in all affairs, toward wife and others and toward kinsmen.
Having thus accepted the teacher's instruction, the initiated one is told:

children.text: adya prabhṛti vandyastvaṃ mā kuru praṇatiṃ kvacit
children.translated_text: 'From today onward you are worthy of veneration; do not bow down anywhere.
You are equal to me; you are accomplished; you are now liberated while living.'
Having spoken thus, the excellent teacher too embraces the siddha for a moment.
This siddha-dīkṣā has been taught, bestowing union with <s>Śiva</s>.
It is hard to obtain in all tantras; out of affection for you it has been revealed.
O <s>Devi</s>, it should be understood in exactly this way, and it is rare among the traditions.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s>:
O lord, tell me properly the processing of <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Śrībhairava</s>:
There are eighteen saṃskāras of <s>rasa</s>, O supreme lady.
O you who are worshipped by siddhas and sādhakas, I shall tell them to you properly.

children.text: athādau svedanaṃ karma dvitīyaṃ mardanaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: First, then, is the operation of steaming; second, O beloved, is grinding.
Mūrchā is third, utthāna fourth, and pātana fifth, O <s>Śive</s>.

children.text: pañcamaṃ rodhanaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ niyāmaṃ saptamaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Rodhana is sixth, and niyāma is remembered as seventh.
Dīpana is eighth, O <s>Devi</s>, and anuvāsana is ninth.
Cāraṇa is tenth, O <s>Devi</s>, and jāraṇa has the number of <s>Rudra</s>, eleven.
Garbhadruti is twelfth, and external druti is thirteenth.
The fourteenth is called rāga, and sāraṇā is the fifteenth.
Anusāraṇā is famous as the sixteenth, and pratisāraṇā as the seventeenth.
The eighteenth is vedhana, piercing of the body and of metals.
Now, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, I shall explain the saṃskāras of the king of rasas.
On the southern side of the liṅga one should draw, in a hexagonal maṇḍala,
and outside that an eight-petalled lotus and a square,
adorned with gates in the directions; in its pericarp, O <s>Śive</s>, one should place

children.text: tāmrajaṃ kāntajaṃ vāpi khalvaṃ tu svarṇarekhitam
children.translated_text: a mortar made of copper or of magnetic stone, marked with golden lines.
In its middle one should place the king of rasas, to the amount of one hundred palas,

children.text: tadardhaṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā kṣiptvā bhaktyā prapūjayet
children.translated_text: or half of that, or half of that again, and worship it with devotion.
Then the sādhaka should perform the saṃskāra of the king of rasas.
With barley, wheat, rice, black gram, mung bean, chickpea, and the like,
and with śyāmāka, kodrava, and other various grains stripped of husk,
one should place the grain in a clay pot with four times as much water, O beloved,
and should carefully preserve it until it reaches sourness.
Into that one should put haṃsapādī, mīnākṣī, the two punarnavās,
citraka, bhṛṅgarāja, viṣṇukrāntā, and śatāvarī,

children.text: sarpākṣīṃ girikarṇīṃ ca muṇḍīṃ ca sahadevikām
children.translated_text: sarpākṣī, girikarṇī, muṇḍī, and sahadevikā,
and triphalā, cut into pieces; all these should be added.
This excellent dhānyāmla, in the measure of a fourth part of the grain,
is especially prescribed for the operations on pārada beginning with steaming.
One should place the king of rasas in a heated mortar of magnetic stone,

children.text: cūrṇaṃ ca gṛhadhūmaṃ ca citrakaṃ triphalāṃ guḍam ||
children.translated_text: together with powder, house-soot, citraka, triphalā, and jaggery,
burnt wool, brick, kanyā, salt, and the two bṛhatīs,

children.text: māgadhīṃ rājikāṃ caiva vandhyāṃ karkoṭakīṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māgadhī</s>, rājikā, vandhyā, and karkoṭakī as well.
Having put these into it in sixteenth parts of the sūta, one should triturate them,
repeatedly adding dhānyāmla; having done this, one continues for three days.
One should wash the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) properly with warm <s>āranāla</s>, beloved.

children.text: paṭuṃ rājīṃ trikaṭukaṃ mūlakaṃ citrakaṃ varām ||
children.translated_text: Salt, mustard, the three pungents, radish, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>varā</s>,
<s>punarnavā</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>meghanāda</s>, <s>durālabhā</s>,
fresh ginger, turmeric, <s>nāgabalā</s>, and <s>navasāraka</s>:

children.text: samaṃ dhānyāmlakaiḥ piṣṭvā ślakṣṇaṃ vastre pralepayet
children.translated_text: grinding these in equal quantity with sour grain-liquid into a smooth paste, one should smear it on cloth.
It should be as thick as a finger; into it one should place the previously treated <s>rasa</s>.
Having bound that up, one should put it into a copper vessel filled with sour grain-liquid.
Then, in a pot and in the apparatus called the <s>dolāyantra</s>, he should steam it for a full day and night.
Taking it out, one should again, with warm <s>āranāla</s> in a saucer,
wash the king of <s>sūta</s> (mercury). One should do this twenty-one times.
Then, beloved, one should thoroughly grind the king of <s>sūta</s> that has been steamed.

children.text: athāto mardanaṃ karma vakṣyāmi śṛṇu bhairavi ||
children.translated_text: Now I shall explain the operation of grinding; listen, <s>Bhairavī</s>.
The substances beginning with powders, as before, together with <s>viśālā</s> and <s>rājavṛkṣaka</s>,

children.text: aṅkolaṃ kṛṣṇadhuttūraṃ trikaṭuṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: <s>aṅkola</s>, black <s>dhuttūra</s>, and the three pungents, all in equal quantity:

children.text: sarvaṃ sūtakalāṃśaṃ ca taptakhalve rasaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: all of these should be one sixteenth part of the <s>sūta</s>; one should put the <s>rasa</s> into a heated mortar.
He should grind it with the aforesaid sour grain-liquid for a day and night, and then again
wash it in an earthen vessel with warm <s>āranāla</s>.
Grinding and washing are to be done in this way for twenty-one days.
Taking up the <s>sūta</s> that has been well ground in this way, one should then bring it to <s>mūrchana</s>.
Even <s>sūta</s> digested with mica or digested with seed-metal is to be ground.
With the powders and other substances mentioned before, it takes on metallic colors and becomes stainless.

children.text: atha mūrchāṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu tvaṃ sāvadhānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now I shall explain <s>mūrchā</s>; listen with attention.

children.text: rājikā meṣaśṛṅgī ca citrakaṃ ca phalatrayam
children.translated_text: Mustard, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and the three fruits,
<s>kṣīrakanda</s>, elephant-foot yam, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and <s>kākamācikā</s>,
blue <s>vacā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>kanyā</s>, black <s>unmatta</s>, and <s>ākulī</s>,
white <s>aparājitā</s>, <s>aṅkola</s>, <s>gojihvā</s>, and <s>garuḍī</s>:
with the expressed juices of these, and with the milk of <s>ravi</s>, the <s>pārada</s> (mercury) is to be ground.
For one day he should grind it with the juices of these plants, either individually or all together.

children.text: mardayettaptakhalve ca mūṣāyāṃ taṃ rasaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: He should grind it in a heated mortar and put that <s>rasa</s> into a crucible.

children.text: nirudhya bhūdhare yantre vipacettaṃ punaḥ priye ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, beloved, he should cook it again in the <s>bhūdhara yantra</s>.
With juices produced from the herbs beginning with mustard, for twenty-one days
he should perform grinding and cooking in the <s>bhūdhara</s>; the <s>rasa</s> becomes fully brought to <s>mūrchana</s>.
Then, worshipped by the gods, he should carry out the method for raising it.
The <s>sūta</s> brought to <s>mūrchana</s> in this way should be washed with sour gruel.
Or, beloved, one may raise the <s>sūta</s> with warm water.
Alternatively, by the application of a <s>pātana</s> apparatus, the raising of the <s>rasa</s> takes place.
The <s>pātana</s> of the king of <s>rasa</s>, <s>Pārvatī</s>, is said to be threefold:
upward <s>pātana</s>, downward <s>pātana</s>, and transverse <s>pātana</s>.

children.text: rasasya pātanaṃ vakṣye pāṭhā brāhmī ca citrakam
children.translated_text: I shall explain the <s>pātana</s> of <s>rasa</s>: <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
<s>śāṅgerī</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>maṇḍūkī</s>, and <s>girikarṇikā</s>,

children.text: kumārī ca jayā bhṛṅgī gojihvā śaṅkhapuṣpikā
children.translated_text: <s>kumārī</s>, <s>jayā</s>, <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>gojihvā</s>, and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpikā</s>,
<s>bhūpāṭalī</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>kākajaṅghā</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,

children.text: ārdrakaṃ devadālī ca tilaparṇī ca nīlikā
children.translated_text: fresh ginger, <s>devadālī</s>, <s>tilaparṇī</s>, and <s>nīlikā</s>,
<s>āragvadha</s>, <s>kṣīrakanda</s>, <s>aṅkola</s>, and <s>devadāru</s>:

children.text: eṣāṃ rasaiḥ samastānāṃ vyastānāṃ vā dinaṃ rasam
children.translated_text: with the juices of these, either all together or separately, one should grind the <s>rasa</s> for a day
in a heated mortar; then copper, one fourth as much as the <s>sūta</s>, should be added.
Having ground it, he should make it undergo <s>pātana</s> for a day in an upward-<s>pātana</s> apparatus.
Taking the purified <s>rasa</s> that has adhered above, he should then grind it.
With the previously stated herbal juices and joined with copper as before,
he should cause it to undergo <s>pātana</s> and grind it in this way seven times again and again.
The <s>pārada</s> purified by upward <s>pātana</s> should next be subjected to downward <s>pātana</s>.
Now I shall explain downward <s>pātana</s>: the three pungents, salt, <s>varā</s>,

children.text: citrakaṃ rājikāṃ śigruṃ sarvaṃ sūtasamaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: <s>citraka</s>, mustard, and <s>śigru</s> should all be added in an amount equal to the <s>sūta</s>.
He should grind the <s>rasa</s> in a heated mortar with sour grain-liquid.
With that paste he should smear the upper vessel and seal it properly.
Then on the back of the upper vessel he should apply a light heating.
Thus one should perform downward <s>pātana</s> seven times again and again.
For what has been purified by downward <s>pātana</s>, one should carry out transverse <s>pātana</s>.
I shall explain transverse <s>pātana</s>: <s>sūta</s> and <s>dhānyābhraka</s> are to be equal.
One should grind them for one watch with sour grain-liquid in a transverse-<s>pātana</s> apparatus.
He should cook it with fierce fire in this way seven times again and again.

children.text: evaṃ tridhā pātitaṃ ca tataḥ sūtaṃ nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>sūta</s> has thus undergone the threefold <s>pātana</s>, one should then confine it.

children.text: abhrakaṃ vātha gandhaṃ vā mākṣikaṃ vimalāmapi
children.translated_text: Mica, or else sulphur, <s>mākṣika</s>, or even <s>vimalā</s>,

children.text: svarṇaṃ vā rajataṃ vāpi kāntaṃ vā tīkṣṇameva vā ||
children.translated_text: gold or silver, or else magnetite, or indeed sharp iron,
each purified separately, should be given, as with copper, in a quarter measure.
With the juices beginning with <s>pāṭhā</s> one should perform grinding and <s>pātana</s> in sequence.
Whatever substance the <s>sūta</s> is joined with, it grants the qualities of that substance.
Through <s>pātana</s> with copper, the <s>rasa</s> abandons lead and tin.
Or else, when subjected to <s>pātana</s> in a lamp-apparatus, the <s>rasa</s> becomes purified.
The <s>sūta</s> has been worked over by the five operations beginning with steaming.
For the purpose of nourishing the <s>sūta</s>, one should perform the operation of confinement.
Now for the operation called confinement: one should grind salt with water.

children.text: sthālīmadhye rasaṃ kṣiptvā tadūrdhvaṃ lavaṇaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Having put the <s>rasa</s> in the middle of a dish, one should put the salt above it.

children.text: kiṃcij jalaṃ ca nivapettaṃ śarāveṇa rodhayet ||
children.translated_text: He should sprinkle on a little water and cover it with a saucer.
He should make a proper sealing paste at the joint, and above it he should give a light heating.
Thus, beloved, one should perform the operation of nirodhana (restraining) in seven ways.
By this the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) becomes nourished and free from inertness.
When this restraining operation has succeeded, it is vigorous and is well brought under control.
Now, fair-faced one, I shall tell the operation of niyāmana (regulating).
Yavaciñcā, kṣīrakanda, sarpākṣī, paṭu, and bhṛṅgarāṭ,
vandhyā, karkoṭakī, and nimba, all ground with sour grain-water,
should be made into a mixture with āranāla; with their liquids one should steam it for a day.

children.text: yantre niyāmake saptavāsaraṃ taṃ ca dīpayet
children.translated_text: In the niyāmaka apparatus one should heat it for seven days.

children.text: athāto dīpanaṃ karma vadāmi tava pārvati ||
children.translated_text: Now then, <s>Pārvatī</s>, I shall describe the operation of dīpana (kindling).
Svarṇapuṣpī, marīca, the three alkalis, pañcapuṣpikā,
bhūkhaga, the five salts, rājikā, śigrumūlaka,
kāsīsa, vijayā, kanyā, pātālagaruḍī, and kaṇā,

children.text: kṣīrakandaṃ ca karkoṭī girikarṇī jayā madhu ||
children.translated_text: kṣīrakanda, karkoṭī, girikarṇī, jayā, honey,
citraka, and kākajaṅghā: all this should be made into a paste with the group of acids.
With that one should triturate <s>pārada</s> (mercury), and also grind it with their juices.
One should cook it in a ḍolā-yantra for one day; in this way, seven times,

children.text: mardanaṃ pācanaṃ kuryāt grāsārthī dīpito rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should perform grinding and cooking. The rasa (mercurial substance), kindled, seeks its grāsa (food to be assimilated).
After the <s>sūta</s> has thus been kindled and purified, one should then condition it.
Now the operation of anuvāsana (conditioning): placing the kindled rasa in an earthen vessel,
one should condition it in strong heat with the juices of jambīra citron.
One should do this for seven days, and afterward undertake cāraṇa (assimilation).
By the nine operations beginning with steaming, beloved, it becomes purified.
<s>Pārada</s>, destroyer of all diseases, is freed from the seven coverings.
The venerable <s>Bhairavī</s> said:
The operations beginning with steaming have been heard. Speak, <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
By your grace I listen without doubt to cāraṇa and the rest.
The venerable <s>Bhairava</s> said:
Well asked, greatly fortunate one. Listen to that cāraṇa and the rest.
Now, supreme goddess, I shall explain the operation of abhra-cāraṇa (assimilation of mica).

children.text: samukhe vā nirmukhe vā rase vā vāsanāmukhe
children.translated_text: Whether in samukha, nirmukha, rasa, or vāsanāmukha form,
one should make gagana (mica) undergo cāraṇa step by step through the methods of embryo, piṣṭi, and grāsa.

children.text: atrādau kathyate devi samukhaṃ cāraṇaṃ sphuṭam
children.translated_text: Here first, goddess, the samukha cāraṇa is clearly described.
The samukha form consumes the grāsa; the nirmukha form is unable to consume it.
Therefore one should next carry out the mukhīkaraṇa (making a mouth) of <s>rasendra</s>.
In the middle part of a brick one should make a deep, round, even hollow.
Into it one should place the conditioned <s>sūta</s>.
One should cover it with a clean cloth, and take one-tenth part of gandha (sulfur) relative to the rasa.
Placing that gandha above it, one should seal it with a dish.

children.text: tatpṛṣṭhe'lpapuṭaṃ dadyāt gandhe jīrṇe punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On its back one should give a small puṭa heating; when the gandha is digested, again and again,
adding it repeatedly, one should make it assimilate a hundredfold and then cause it to fall down.
Through a dense cloth folded four times one should filter that <s>raseśvara</s>.
Putting it into bamboo, sealing its mouth, one should cook it in a vessel filled with cow urine
for twenty-one days; then again in a heated mortar
it should be ground for three days with jambīra, mātuluṅga, sour vetasa, and bhūkhaga substances,
and for three days with bhūnāga. Afterward, in the cavity of a brick,
one should take, for each hollow, dhānyābhra and likewise gandhaka,
ten niṣkas of each, ground for a yāma with jambīra.
With this one should smear two hollows in the two bricks.

children.text: garte kṣiptvātha taṃ taṃ viṃśanniṣkaṃ tadūrdhvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, placing into the hollow twenty niṣkas of that same rasa, above it
one should set another brick, and with saline clay
firmly plaster its joint; then one should cook it over a lamp-flame for seven days.
When that brick has cooled by itself, one should take out the rasa.
Free from dross, one should do it again in this way three times.
When this has been done, <s>rasendra</s> easily becomes what is called divine.
Again I shall proclaim another excellent mukhīkaraṇa.
One should thoroughly grind <s>rasendra</s> for three days with an equal quantity of jīvi-bhūnāga.
One should place it in a crucible smeared with bhūlatā and set it there.
Above it one should put bhūlatā paste, seal it, and dry it.
Smeared with wet cow dung, it should be set with one quarter sunk down.
In that pit a puṭa should be given with fire of husks and dried cow dung.
At the end of the day, taking it out, one should grind and cook it as before.
One should do this again thirty times; in this way the rasa becomes fire-mouthed.
This secret <s>sūta</s> consumes, and becomes the giver of all siddhis.
Again I shall proclaim another excellent mukhīkaraṇa.
In a vessel filled with cow urine, one should cook the rasa in a ḍolā-yantra.
Properly, three times seven times, in a perforated bamboo tube,
the <s>sūta</s> obtains a mouth fit for cāraṇa, fair-faced one.
Between two bricks there should be a hollow four aṅgulas deep.
Ten niṣkas of purified gandha and ten niṣkas of dhānyābhra,

children.text: jambīranīraiḥ saṃmardya yāmaṃ kalkena tena ca
children.translated_text: ground for a yāma with jambīra water, should be made into a paste; with that paste
one should smear the two hollows in equal portions and place it in the hollow.
That conditioned <s>rasarāja</s>, twenty niṣkas, should be placed above it.
Setting another brick on top, one should seal it firmly with fine clay and salts.
Then one should plaster it and light a lamp-flame beneath it, beloved.
Heated continuously for seven nights, it should be taken out after cooling by itself.

children.text: kiṭṭaṃ vihāya taṃ sūtaṃ pūrvavacca trivārakam
children.translated_text: Discarding the dross, one should treat that <s>sūta</s> again as before three times.

children.text: kuryādevaṃ hi sūtasya mukhaṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed a fine mouth is produced for the <s>sūta</s>.
Through the power of divine herbs, the rasa moves even while nirmukha.
Or, through contact with <s>vajra</s> (diamond) and <s>vaikrānta</s>, he should make it assimilate abhra and the other substances.
There should be sixty-four <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>pārada</s> (mercury), and ash of <s>vaikrānta</s>,
four <s>niṣkas</s>, and one <s>niṣka</s> of diamond ash, together with the juices of divine herbs.

children.text: sarvaṃ saptadinaṃ mardya sa raso'bhrādikaṃ caret
children.translated_text: After grinding all this for seven days, that <s>rasa</s> (mercury) assimilates abhra and the rest.
One should make sulfur undergo digestion in <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in the apparatus called the <s>dolā</s>, described before.
In that apparatus, when it is sixteenfold, the <s>rasa</s> becomes one whose mouth is prepared by conditioning.
I shall tell you the consecration of abhraka that is fit for cāraṇa (assimilation).

children.text: mṛtamabhraṃ tu rudhiraiḥ kṣārair jalakaṇair api
children.translated_text: Incinerated abhra should be ground with bloods, with alkalis, and also with drops of water,
with the three sṛṣṭis, with tumburu, and with the sour group.
For seven days <s>sūta</s> (mercury) should assimilate that, whether furnished with a mouth or without a mouth.

children.text: mṛtamabhraṃ ca kadalī mūlakaṃ ca śatāvarī ||
children.translated_text: Incinerated abhra, kadalī, mūlaka, and śatāvarī,
punarnavā, meghanāda, yavaciñcā, and śigru,
and sūraṇa: with the juices of these one should grind and impregnate it, dear one.
For seven days <s>sūta</s> should assimilate that, whether furnished with a mouth or without a mouth.
In a copper vessel, one should place salt, sarjikā, ṭaṅkaṇa, and bhūkhaga,
and make sour gruel stand there for three days until it is stale.
In that, dear one, one should melt nāga (lead) and pour it one hundred times.
For the operation concerning silver and vaṅga (tin), one should impregnate ghana (mica) with those liquids.
For seven days <s>sūta</s> should assimilate that, whether furnished with a mouth or without a mouth.
One should grind dhānyābhra with the milk of arka for one full day.
After sealing it in a covered vessel, one should cook it again in the heating called kapota.
In this way one should heat it four times, and then grind it again in the same manner.
It should be ground three times with the juices of rambhā and three times with the juices of mūlaka.
Kākamācī, meghanāda, matsyākṣī, and punarnavā,
apāmārga, citraka, vidārī, bhṛṅgarāj, and muni:
in this way one should cook it four times, and then grind it again in the same manner.
With each of these individually it should be ground, and the heating by puṭa should be done separately.
That abhraka should also be impregnated with musalī and yavaciñcikā,
taṇḍulī, kadalī, śigru, varī, arka, and punarnavā.
With the juice of each one separately it should be impregnated for one day each.
That abhraka, O worshipped by the gods, the lord <s>pārada</s> certainly assimilates.
One should grind dhānyābhra with the milk of ravi for the measure of one yāma.
Having sealed that abhra in a covered vessel, one should cook it in the heating called kapota.
When this has been done fourteen times, then rambhā, arka, and pīluka,

children.text: nāgavallī ca musalī kuberākṣī ca śigrukaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nāgavallī, musalī, kuberākṣī, and śigruka,
tumbī, tumburu, aṅkola, balā, and apāmārga, dear one:
taking one juice from these, together with vyoṣa and kāñjika,
one should place it in a vessel and cook it in the <s>dolāyantra</s> for three days.
Then, taking the previously prepared abhra out of that, one should process it further.

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tuvarī sindhukāsīsaṃ ca samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Ṭaṅkaṇa, tuvarī, sindhu, and kāsīsa should be in equal quantities.
All this, one tenth the amount of the abhraka, should be thoroughly ground.
The <s>sūta</s> then assimilates that abhraka, whether furnished with a mouth or without a mouth.

children.text: muṇḍīdrave tu śatadhā drutaṃ nāgaṃ praḍhālayet ||
children.translated_text: Into the juice of muṇḍī one should pour melted nāga one hundred times.
With that liquid one should grind dhānyābhra and place it in a covered vessel.

children.text: ruddhvā pacetkapotākhye puṭe caivaṃ tu saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, one should cook it in the heating called kapota; thus it is done seven times.
In the same way, seven times with the juices of ārdraka and seven times with the juices of citraka,

children.text: tatsamaṃ gandhakaṃ dattvā mardayed bhāvayet kramāt ||
children.translated_text: one should add sulfur equal to it and grind and impregnate it in sequence.
With the previously mentioned fresh juices of muṇḍī and with the juice of bījapūra,
it should be impregnated for one day with breast milk; <s>rasa</s> (mercury) then assimilates that abhra.

children.text: evaṃ sarvāṇi bījāni sattvaṃ cābhrakasya ca
children.translated_text: In this way all bījas, and the essence of abhraka,
all metals beginning with gold, and the various metallic essences,
paired substances and all gems, whatever may be fit for cāraṇa,

children.text: tat tat piṣṭvābhravat kāryaṃ tattaccarati pāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: each of those, after being pulverized, should be processed like abhra; <s>pārada</s> assimilates each of them.
Having ground dhānyābhra with the juices of tilaparṇī, one should heat it by puṭa three times.
By grinding, one should impregnate it seven times; then <s>pārada</s>,

children.text: piṣṭatāṃ yāti sahasā gaganaṃ carati kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: quickly becomes a paste and in an instant assimilates gagana (mica).
The three alkalis, the five salts, kāṅkṣī, kāsīsa, and ṭaṅkaṇa,
bhūkhaga, hemamākṣika, saurāṣṭrī, and vatsanābha,
tuvarī and vetasāmla: all these should be in equal portions.
Dhānyābhra equal in quantity to them should be ground for a day with sour grain liquids.
Milk of arka, bhṛṅgarāja, meghanāda, punarnavā,
mūlaka, citraka, rambhā, kākamācī, and śatāvarī,
apāmārga, tālamūlī, vidārī, taṇḍulī, and muni,
mīnākṣī, śigru, bṛhatī, kumārī, and yavaciñcikā,
balā, tumbī, kuberākṣī, vyoṣa, tumburu, and pīlunī,
aṅkola and phaṇivallī: all this should be in equal portions.
After pulverizing it, O goddess, one should make a paste with four times as much sour grain liquid.
One should repeatedly put melted nāga into it one hundred times.
With the liquid from that paste one should firmly grind the previously prepared abhra for one yāma.
It should be cooked in the heating called kapota; this is to be done twenty times.
Having added an equal amount of sulfur, with the previously mentioned herbal juices,
with breast milk, and with the liquids produced from bījapūra, it should be impregnated for three days.

children.text: etadabhraṃ tu sūtasya cāraṇe paramaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: This abhra is supremely beneficial for the cāraṇa of <s>sūta</s> (mercury).

children.text: dvaṃdvitaṃ vyomasatvaṃ ca bījāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Paired vyomasattva and various bījas,
all metals beginning with gold, and various gems,
and paired diamond-bīja are prescribed for cāraṇa.
He should have all this carried out exactly in the manner stated before.
Then <s>rasendra</s> (lord mercury) moves; all of that is suitable for cāraṇa.
In a vessel, he should put kāsīsa, kāṅkṣī, mākṣika, and sulfur,
the three alkalis and the five salts, mixed with sour substances, for a moment.
According to the procedure of the divine consecration, he should pour the mercury a hundred times.
Or with this he should treat tin and the substances fit for cāraṇa.
Varī, punarnavā, raṃbhā, gavākṣī, and yavaciñcikā,
śigrukā and meghanāda: with the juices of these he should thoroughly imbue it.
He should treat vajrābhraka in due order for seven days, O revered by the gods.
That mica may be treated with nāgavallī, koberī, or śigruka,
or with bāṇa, aṅkola, balā, raṃbhā, sphoṭā, or pīluka,
or also with alambuṣā, himarucā, musalī, and tumburu,
or with kharamañjarī or tiktaśāka, dear one.
With the juice of any one of these, combined with vyoṣa and mustard,
he should steam it for three days; into it he should put ṭaṅkaṇa and rock salt,
kāsīsa and tuvarī, according to the previous procedure of steeping.
Mercury, whether samukha or nirmukha, should consume this mica.
By the power of that mica, the pill becomes a giver of siddhi.
He should steam mica for a day with grain-sour liquid and the group of acidic substances.

children.text: tataḥ snukkṣīrato mardyaṃ kapotākhye puṭe dahet
children.translated_text: Then it should be ground with snuhī milk and burned in the puṭa called kapota.
Munitraya, meghanāda, raṃbhā bulb, and radish,
matsyākṣī, ginger, kākamācī, and punarnavā,

children.text: apāmārgas tv arūpūgaścaiteṣāṃ tu rasena ca ||
children.translated_text: and apāmārga and arūpūga: with the juice of these,
using each one separately, he should again treat each portion of the previously prepared mica.
In a ḍolā apparatus he should cook it for one day, combined with snuhī milk.
Then, when this solid substance has dried in the shade, he should add avasāraka to it,

children.text: nimbaṃ vacāṃ ca kāsīsaṃ caṇakāmlaṃ pṛthakpṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and nimba, vacā, kāsīsa, and sour chickpea liquid, each separately.
He should place one sixteenth part of the mica in a copper vessel,
grind it, and mercury should consume that through the use of an iron vessel.
He should grind dhānyābhra firmly for a day with water of somavallī.

children.text: puṭedevaṃ tridhā paścāt somavallyā rasena ca ||
children.translated_text: Then he should calcine it in this way three times; afterward, with somavallī juice,
he should imbue it seven times, O goddess; then mercury consumes that dense mica.

children.text: sāranāle tu śatadhā niṣicya tamanena ca ||
children.translated_text: In a sāranāla, after pouring this on it a hundred times,
he should flood the mica a hundred times together with a copper impregnation.
In a mortar mercury should consume it; no hesitation is needed here.
Hear, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, the impregnation of the sulfur intended for cāraṇa.

children.text: saurāṣṭraṃ cājamodaṃ ca sarjīṃ sīsameva ca ||
children.translated_text: Saurāṣṭra, ajamodā, sarjī, and lead:
he should grind them with śigru water and impregnate sulfur with that.
Having ground the sulfur for seven days, he should make mercury consume it.
It gives color to <s>rasendra</s> in the cooking and digestion of the metallic seeds.
For cutting the wings of <s>rasendra</s>, it is best in every operation.
With the fresh juices of palāśa flowers and the liquids from leaves of śāka trees,
and with the liquids of viṣṇukrāntā, he should impregnate sulfur for seven days.
He should make mercury consume that sulfur by means of the brick apparatus.
Now I shall tell you the divine roots that are best for mica-cāraṇa.
Vajrī, raṃbhā, haṃsapadī, ciñcikā, vyāghrapādikā,

children.text: maṇḍūkī bṛhatī puṅkhā kumārī lāṅgalī tathā ||
children.translated_text: maṇḍūkī, bṛhatī, puṅkhā, kumārī, and lāṅgalī,
sarpākṣī, agnidhamanī, śaṅkhapuṣpī, and indravāruṇī,
ṣaṇḍajārī and karkoṭī are famed as divine roots.
Now therefore I shall state the cāraṇa operation in brief.

children.text: dhānyābhrakaṃ drute gandhe samaṃ kṣiptvā niyojayet ||
children.translated_text: He should put dhānyābhraka in equal measure into melted sulfur and apply it.
This is known as the gandhābhra procedure, excellent in the operation of cāraṇa.
Mercury, whether samukha or nirmukha, should measure ten niṣkas.
With two niṣkas of the gandhābhra procedure, he should make a piṣṭi as prescribed.
Then he should wrap that piṣṭi evenly with a nāga-piṣṭi.
In work for gold, he should use a piṣṭi of tin; in work for silver,
he should wrap it with a copper piṣṭi for perfection of the body, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
He should cook that piṣṭi in melted sulfur for three days.
He should cook that piṣṭi in a dīpikā apparatus and make it descend below.
He should make that mercury into a piṣṭi as before, but without wrapping it.
He should cook it in melted sulfur for three days and make it descend below.

children.text: taṃ rasaṃ taptakhalve tu catuḥṣaṣṭiguṇaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: He should place that mercury, sixty-fourfold, in a heated mortar.
One part of consecrated mica should be ground for a day with divine herbs.
He should put that into a cāraṇa apparatus together with lemon juice.
It should be set in fierce sunshine for a day; then mercury consumes that dense mica.
Thus, again and again, according to the sequence of womb-piṣṭis and morsels,
the cāraṇa of leaf-mica has been taught; the cāraṇa of essence-mica is the same.
Thus he should perform cāraṇa as far as he is able, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
First he should make mercury consume mica in a sixty-fourth part,
then a thirty-second part, then this same thing as a sixteenth part,
an eighth part, a fourth part, a half part, and an equal part, in order.
Then twice as much, four times as much, eight times as much, and sixteen times as much,
and thus thirty-two times and sixty-four times as much, in order.
From the cāraṇa of mica arise wing-cutting, freedom from defect, lightness, and fitness to take morsels,
mukhitā, endurance of fire, pervasiveness, and absence of motion,
and the instability of <s>rasendra</s> also comes about through mica-cāraṇa.
For the one in whose digestion of <s>sūtendra</s> I myself would be pleased,
There should be conviction; there is no doubt that <s>jāraṇā</s> grants both enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: durlabhā jāraṇā devi vinā bhāgyaṃ na labhyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jāraṇā</s> is difficult to obtain, O goddess; without fortune it is not obtained.
<s>Jāraṇā</s> is of two kinds: juvenile <s>jāraṇā</s> and mature <s>jāraṇā</s>.
First one should assimilate gagana, and after that all the sattvas.
The paired substances, all metals, the ripened bījas, O <s>Bhairavī</s>,
and gems beginning with padmarāga should also be assimilated in due order.
The vyoma-sattva fit for the <s>jāraṇā</s> of the king of rasa will now be described.
One should duly calcine dhānyābhraka, known as vajra.

children.text: abhiṣekaṃ pūrvavat syāt tasmin tāpyaṃ daśāṃśakam
children.translated_text: The sprinkling should be as before; in it there should be tāpya in a tenth part.
With the five products of buffalo and cow it should be ground into pieces like a karṣa in weight.
One should make pellets and cause the sattva to fall in a koṣṭhī-yantra.

children.text: satvasya ca caturthāṃśaṃ tāpye mūṣāgataṃ dhamet ||
children.translated_text: With a fourth part of the sattva, one should blow it in a crucible containing tāpya.
Having done this four times, that sattva is fit for the <s>jāraṇā</s> of rasa,
and it is excellent in rasāyana, in medicine, and in every operation.
Dead abhra, a fourth part of that; nāga, a quarter of that; and mākṣika,
should be made to yield a bright sattva with the five buffalo and cow products.
That sattva, a fourth part of it as mākṣika, and śilā equal to that,
should be blown in a coated crucible; the sattva becomes like gold.
One should do this four times; rasa consumes that sattva.
Dead abhraka in a sixteenth part, and trapu in a fourth part of that,
with tālaka equal to it added, by means of the five buffalo and cow products,
one should cause the sattva to fall; and a fourth part of that is haritāla.

children.text: kṣiptvā kṣiptvā caturvāraṃ tatsatvaṃ grasate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: Adding it again and again four times, rasa consumes that sattva.
Having placed it in a vajra crucible, together with an equal amount of dense sattva,

children.text: kacaṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kṣiptvā ruddhvā tīvrāgninā dhamet
children.translated_text: one should add kāca and ṭaṅkaṇa, seal it, and blow it with intense fire.
Then one should add it with the sour group, ciñcā seed, and snuhī leaf.
After grinding these, one should again, in the same way, use kāca and ṭaṅkaṇa with it.

children.text: dhamedevaṃ saptavāraṃ secanaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should blow it thus seven times, with repeated sprinkling again and again.
That abhra-sattva becomes white, soft, and suitable for cāraṇa.
Rasendra, ṭaṅkaṇa, and tāpya should each be one part separately.
Purified nāga should be three parts, and dead abhra ten parts.

children.text: yavakṣāraṃ ca dagdhorṇāṃ sarjakṣāraṃ ca guggulum ||
children.translated_text: Yavakṣāra, burnt wool, sarjakṣāra, and guggulu,
combined with the five parts of a goat and joined with groups of sour liquids and urine,
should be ground as before; one should extract a soft, stainless sattva.
I shall explain the crucible coating for combining dvandvas, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: meṣaśṛṅgaṃ khuraṃ guñjā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ ca viṣaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Ram's horn, hoof, guñjā, ṭaṅkaṇa, and poison, in equal portions,
should be ground with the fat of a large frog, and the crucible should be coated with it.
All sattvas, when powdered in the crucible, unite there.
Guggulu, dhātakī flowers, jaggery, and the three alkalis, in equal portions,
ground with breast milk, make a crucible coating for the union of dvandvas.

children.text: aśmabhedī lāṅgalī ca bhūlatā ca marīcakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Aśmabhedī, lāṅgalī, bhūlatā, and marīcaka,
the fruit of cotton and śakragopa: these should be ground together.
With woman's breast milk, one should coat the inside of the crucible with that very mixture.

children.text: tasyāṃ milanti satvāni sarvāṇi ca mahārasāḥ
children.translated_text: In it all sattvas and all great rasas unite,
as do metals headed by gold, when blown with fierce fire.

children.text: cucundaryāśca piśitaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ ca viṣaṃ samam
children.translated_text: The flesh of the cucundarī, ṭaṅkaṇa, and poison, in equal portions,
should be ground and coated inside the crucible; then one should place the material there.
Whatever is fit for pairing, all of that unites through blowing.
Apāmārga, reduced to ash and ground with kaṅguṇī oil,
should be smeared in the crucible with that; the dvandva substances should be placed inside.
They unite through blowing with intense fire and through the casting in of the respective killing agents.
Therefore I shall now explain the combining of dvandvas; listen.
Varṣābhū, plantain root, kākamācī, and punarnavā,
gold, a human skull, guñjā, ṭaṅkaṇa, and abhraka:

children.text: satvaṃ mūṣāgataṃ dhmātaṃ hemābhraṃ milati kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: when the sattva placed in a crucible is blown, hema-abhra unites at once.
But abhraka, having been powdered and soaked with the juice of kākamācī,
combined with kapittha water and joined with sūta and ṭaṅkaṇa,
when placed between sheets of vaṅga and blown, becomes united as vaṅga-abhra.
After revolving it with pungent oil, one should add ash produced from apāmārga.
Hema-abhra unites by nāga-tāpya, and tāra-abhra by haritāla.
Śulva-abhra unites by sulfur, and tīkṣṇa-abhra by sindhu and hiṅgula.
Vaṅga-abhra unites by haritāla, and nāga-abhra by śilā.
Lāṅgalī, camarī hairs, cotton seed, and kulatthaka,
bhūlatā, aśmadamanī, woman's breast milk, and suragopaka,
when used for a dvandva in a coated crucible and well blown with intense fire,
make kānta-abhra, śaila, and vimalā all unite in an instant.
Next, the flesh of the cucchundarī, combined with poison and ṭaṅkaṇa,
when used as a crucible coating, brings about union in all dvandvas.
The horn of a black bee and the fat and flesh of a frog,
with a coating of guñjā and ṭaṅkaṇa, bring union in all sattvas.
With ṭaṅkaṇa, wool, mountain bitumen, karṇākṣī, and alakarkaṭa,
all substances unite when they are ground with woman's breast milk.
With dhātakī, guggulu, jaggery, sarja, yavaka, and ṭaṅkaṇa,
ground with woman's breast milk, the dvandva becomes suitable for rasāyana.

children.text: sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu yat kiṃcit pūrvakalkena saṃyutam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever has been made into a fine powder and combined with the preceding paste,
when placed in a blind crucible and blown, unites as a mixture at once.
Having been sown or infused with tāpya, rasaka, sasyaka, and darada,

children.text: sa satvaṃ syād anibiḍaṃ dṛḍhaṃ dhmātaṃ milettataḥ
children.translated_text: that essence should become loose-textured yet firm; when blown in the fire, it will then fuse.
One should bring together all the rasas, uparasas, and metals in one place.

children.text: anyonyaṃ dvaṃdvatāṃ yānti dravanti salilaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: They enter into mutual pairing and melt like water.
The powder of the essence of vajrābhra and whatever metal powder there may be:
the two should be equal; into them one should put an enemy group equal to them.
In a crucible for fusing pairs, fusion takes place through blowing in the fire.
One should grind <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> with water from the bulb of rambhā and smear it on.
A crucible, white abhraka, and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) fuse through blowing, dear one.
Wild śigru, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, guñjā, and a human skull,
having ground them with the water of women's breast milk, one should coat the crucible with that.
After powdering <s>vaṅga</s> and the essence of white abhra, one should put them in and blow.
Without doubt they certainly fuse; this is excellent in work with silver.
Having pulverized the essence of white abhra, and <s>pārada</s> one fourth its amount,
and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> equal to the mercury, one should grind them with liquids born from kākamācī.
Having made that into a pellet, one should wrap it in a leaf of <s>vaṅga</s>.
One should blow it when placed in a crucible smeared with an equal amount of white abhra essence.
There will be proper fusion; it is foremost in work with silver.
Now, therefore, comes the smearing for the fusion of the pair, diamond and gold.
Guñjā and kāntamukha in equal quantities, and bali twice the quantity of the pair,
having ground them with women's breast milk, likewise inside the crucible,
one should fuse them. This fusion of diamond has been taught by me.
Śilādhātu, kāntamukha, hare's teeth, and sulfur,
with amlavetasa in equal quantity, should be ground, and the crucible should be coated.
Gold and diamond certainly fuse in the crucible; there is no doubt about this.
Crab bone, śilādhātu, and the eye-filth of a buffalo cow,
all equal to <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and wool, should be ground with a beloved woman's breast milk.
With this one should coat the crucible; gold and diamond fuse completely.
A beloved woman's mouth-fluid, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, the dung of a young calf, and bee bone,
and human hair and bones should be thoroughly ground with women's breast milk.
In a crucible smeared with this, gold and diamond will certainly fuse.
Tāpya, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, bhūnāga, kānta, glass, and honey,
crab bone, snuhī milk, and arka milk, each in equal quantity,
should all be ground with breast milk, and one should make a coating for the crucible.
This becomes a crucible coating that fuses diamond and hāṭaka (gold).
With those substances by which diamond becomes ash, one should smear the inside of the crucible.
One should blow with an intense fire; fusion of gold and diamond will occur.
Now I shall explain the fusion of diamond and gold, O queen of the gods.
Gold should be twelve parts; half of that should be purified <s>pārada</s>.
Half as much as the lord of rasa should be ash of <s>nāga</s> (lead), and half as much as the lead should be dead diamond.
These four should be ground with sour liquids in a heated mortar.
Having taken it out, one should confine it in a crucible for fusing pairs and blow.
By force this fuses; no deliberation is to be made about this.
One should impregnate dead diamond in the milk of śārivā for a day; then
one should grind it, make it into a pellet, and leave one part of it.
There should be three parts <s>rasarāja</s> (mercury) and four parts gold.
One should grind it with sour liquid, make a paste, and form that into a pellet.
Having ground that, one should wrap it; and it should be wrapped in birch bark.
One should place it for a fortnight in a heap of grain; having taken it out again and again,
one should blow it forcibly. It certainly fuses; no deliberation is to be made about this.
One should wrap diamond, in a sixteenth part, with a leaf of gold.
One should put that into a smeared crucible, along with a gold portion and powder made from white glass,

children.text: cūrṇaṃ vā nṛkapālaṃ vā cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: or else a human skull, having powdered it, one should put it in.
After sealing it, one should blow intensely; in this way one should do it again and again.
Putting in white glass again and again, or else a human skull,
in this way it certainly fuses after seven times; then the same procedure is performed again.

children.text: asya hemnaḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ mṛtaṃ vajraṃ vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Into this gold one should put dead diamond in a sixteenth part.
As before, in a smeared crucible, glass or a human skull
should be put in again and again, and one should blow intensely; after seven times it fuses completely.
Thus one should do it a third time, and thus a fourth time.
Now, therefore, I shall explain the ablution of paired substances.
Kāsīsa, the five salts, mākṣīka, and sulfur,
kāṅkṣī and the three alkalis, in equal quantities, should be ground with āranāla.
That paste should be placed in a copper vessel in the sun for three days.
Into it one should pour melted <s>nāga</s> a hundred times, while it is melted, again and again.
One should impregnate it a hundred times with sauvīra kept in a copper vessel.
That paired substance is acted on by <s>sūta</s> (mercury), whatever may be fit for assimilation.
In work with silver it should be <s>vaṅga</s> (tin); in work with gold it should be <s>nāga</s> (lead).
Now, O worshipped by the gods, I shall explain prepared bīja.

children.text: suvarṇe vidrute tulyaṃ nāgābhraṃ dvaṃdvitaṃ priye
children.translated_text: When gold has been melted, an equal amount of paired <s>nāga</s> and abhra, dear one,
should be made to flow in twelvefold quantity, so that, when blown, only gold remains.
This is known as prepared bīja; it should be assimilated into <s>pārada</s> in due order.

children.text: pītābhrasatvaṃ svarṇaṃ ca samāṃśaṃ dvaṃdvitaṃ dhamet ||
children.translated_text: The essence of yellow abhra and gold, in equal parts and paired, should be blown.
One should make it flow in twelvefold quantity, so that, when blown, only gold remains.
Again one should slowly make the essence of yellow abhra flow in tenfold quantity,

children.text: svarṇaśeṣaṃ bhaved yāvat pakvabījam idaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: until only gold remains; this becomes prepared bīja.
Lead, copper, mica, and <s>rasaka</s> should be in four, three, two, and one parts.
He should pulverize them, seal them in a coated crucible, and blow strongly.

children.text: mākṣikeṇa ca tatkhoṭaṃ saṃpeṣyāmlaiḥ puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: Then he should grind that ingot with <s>mākṣika</s> and sour liquids and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Again, after grinding it with an equal amount of <s>mākṣika</s> and sour liquids, he should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ pañcapuṭaṃ dattvā taddrute hemni vāhayet ||
children.translated_text: After giving it five <s>puṭas</s> in this way, he should introduce it into melted gold.
He should blow until it has become tenfold; then it is a cooked seed.
Now therefore I shall explain the four seeds, O beautiful-faced one.
Gold, silver, lead, and tin are truly these seeds.
The gold-seed and the lead-seed are recommended in work involving gold.
The silver-seed and the tin-seed are taught in work involving silver.
The gold-seed and the silver-seed are suitable in <s>rasāyana</s>.
The lead-seed and the tin-seed are not for <s>rasāyana</s> work.
These four seeds are to be used for the pacification of diseases.
Otherwise these seeds should never be applied, O <s>Śāmbhavi</s>.

children.text: gandhakaṃ sasyakaṃ vāpi mākṣīkaṃ vātha tālakam ||
children.translated_text: Sulfur, <s>sasyaka</s>, or else <s>mākṣīka</s>, or <s>tālaka</s>,

children.text: śilāṃ ca vimalāṃ vāpi vaikrāntaṃ vāñjanaṃ ca vā
children.translated_text: or <s>śilā</s>, <s>vimalā</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, or <s>añjana</s>,

children.text: kharparaṃ vā kāntamukhaṃ vā cūrṇayitvā samāṃśakam ||
children.translated_text: or <s>kharpara</s>, or <s>kāntamukha</s>: having pulverized any of these in equal portions,
he should introduce it again and again a hundred times into melted gold.
Mercury, <s>hiṅgula</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, iron <s>parpaṭikā</s>, and mica,
calcined copper, <s>mākṣīka</s>, <s>śilā</s>, and <s>vimalā</s>, in equal portions:
these, together with portions of lead, he should grind with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, O dear one.
With that he should smear sheets of purified lead.
He should calcine it with thirty-two <s>puṭas</s>; the lead becomes ash. He should introduce that

children.text: samaṃ samaṃ ca śatadhā vidrute pūrvavāhite
children.translated_text: in equal measure, a hundred times, into what has first been introduced in molten form.
Likewise in gold too, he should blow strongly until only gold remains.
Or he should calcine tin with <s>tāla</s>, conch, mica, and mercury,
ground with tamarind alkalis and equal tin, with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>.
He should cook that with sixteen <s>puṭas</s> and introduce it a hundred times into gold.
Or he should kill copper by placing an equal amount of sulfur above and below.

children.text: kṣiptvā puṭed aṣṭavāraṃ tattāmraṃ hemni vāhayet
children.translated_text: He should calcine it eight times; then he should introduce that copper into gold.
Or he should kill <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron together with <s>hiṅgula</s> equal to the <s>tīkṣṇa</s>.
After grinding it with woman's breast milk, he should then calcine a one-sixteenth part.

children.text: tīkṣṇasya hiṃgulaṃ dattvā mardayet puṭayet kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Having added <s>hiṅgula</s> to the <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, he should grind and calcine it in sequence.

children.text: evaṃ tat ṣoḍaśapuṭaiḥ tattīkṣṇaṃ hemni vāhayet
children.translated_text: In this way, with sixteen <s>puṭas</s>, he should introduce that <s>tīkṣṇa</s> into gold.

children.text: śatadhā hema tadiśaṃ vidrute hemni vāhayet ||
children.translated_text: He should introduce that gold, a hundred times, into melted gold.
Twice as much <s>tāpya</s> should be filled into that gold, and he should blow it strongly.
He should pulverize it; when killed with two, three, or five <s>puṭas</s>, it becomes complete.
He should introduce it tenfold into melted gold, blowing again and again.
That very thing becomes divine and bestows every accomplishment.
This is known as gold-seed and is useful for the digestion of mercury.
He should pulverize <s>sasyaka</s>, mica, <s>vaikrānta</s> essence, gold, lead, copper, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron.
He should blow them in a coated crucible, sealed shut.
Again he should blow them in an open crucible; when it has melted,

children.text: mākṣikaṃ nikṣipet kiṃcit kiṃcid dattvā punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: he should cast in a little <s>mākṣika</s>, adding it little by little again and again,
until only gold remains; then into that he should put

children.text: svarṇaṃ nāgaṃ raviṃ tīkṣṇaṃ pūrvavacca dhametkramāt
children.translated_text: gold, lead, copper, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, and blow them in order as before.
He should introduce <s>mākṣika</s> in the same way and blow until only gold remains.
This is known as gold-seed and is useful for the digestion of mercury.
He should pulverize equal portions of mica, essence, and good coppery material.
With washed <s>tāpya</s> twice the amount of the mica, he should blow everything forcefully.
In a crucible coated with <s>dvandva</s>, he should then pulverize that ingot.
After grinding it with the juices of divine herbs, he should enclose it firmly in a sealed capsule.
He should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; likewise he should pulverize it, grind it, and calcine it.
When cooked in this way with five <s>puṭas</s>, he should introduce it into melted gold.
Until it is tenfold, he should blow it in an open crucible.
Then, casting purified <s>tāpya</s> into that again and again, he should blow and blow.
Until only gold remains: this is gold-seed, O dear one.
The ashes of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, copper, and lead, and <s>tāpya</s> powder, should all be equal.
He should introduce this into melted gold until it becomes tenfold.
Until only gold remains: this is gold-seed, O dear one.
Calcined silver, copper, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron should all be equal; he should blow strongly.
In a crucible coated with <s>dvandva</s>, he should then pulverize that ingot.

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ drāvite svarṇe vāhayecca śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should introduce that powder slowly into melted gold.
After it is tenfold, casting in <s>tāpya</s> powder again and again,
he should blow until only gold remains. This is gold-seed, O dear one.
One part lead, four parts copper, and essence produced from <s>rasaka</s>:
all of it should be blown in a crucible coated with <s>dvandva</s> and pulverized.
He should introduce that powder slowly, sixfold, into melted gold.

children.text: svarṇaśeṣaṃ bhaved yāvat tāvat syāt svarṇabījakam ||
children.translated_text: Until only gold remains: then it is gold-seed.
He should kill copper with <s>tāpya</s> and introduce that slowly into lead.
Until the <s>tāpya</s> powder is hundredfold, he should cast it in and blow and blow.
He should introduce that and blow it into gold in sequence, thirty-two times.
Until only gold remains: then it is gold-seed.
One part essence of <s>kharparī</s>, two parts mica essence,
and three parts copper powder should be placed in a coated crucible and blown.
He should pulverize that metallic lump, add an equal quantity of tāpya, and triturate it with sour liquids.
He should put it into a covered vessel, seal it, and again roast it in a small puṭa.
When it has been cooked in this way by five puṭas, he should introduce that powder into the molten metal,
a thousandfold, into gold, until only gold remains.
For as long as needed, he should introduce tāpya by the proper method; this becomes a hema-bīja, a gold seed.
One part should be essence of abhra and two parts purified copper.
He should pulverize them, put them into a coated crucible, seal it, and blow the fire strongly.
Then he should grind that lump, add equal tāpya, and triturate it with sour liquid.
After sealing it in a covered vessel, he should cook it in a puṭa and pulverize it again.
As before, having placed it in mākṣika, he should triturate it and make it descend, O beloved.
In this way five puṭas should be performed; he should introduce that powder, O beloved,
a hundredfold into gold, until it becomes a hema-bīja.
Mākṣika, gandha-pāṣāṇa, haritāla, manaḥśilā,
vaikrāntaka, kānta, sasyaka, vimalā, and añjana,
and also rasaka, pulverized a hundred times, should be introduced into gold.
With lohaparpaṭikā, tāpya, kaṅkuṣṭha, vimalā, and abhra,
with killed copper, śilā, sūta, the milks of snuhī and arka, and hiṅgula,

children.text: nāgo nirjīvatāṃ yāti yogaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: lead becomes lifeless through these procedures again and again.
Likewise tin, with rasa, tālaka, purified tamarind, and alkalis,

children.text: mṛtaṃ nāgaṃ mṛtaṃ vaṅgaṃ śulbaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca vā mṛtam ||
children.translated_text: or killed lead, killed tin, copper, and killed tīkṣṇa,
each one separately should be introduced into excellent gold, O you revered by the gods.
When the serpent-metal has been confined in gold and drawn out a hundredfold,
lead digested in it is yellow like rocanā, greenish, and carried into copper;
tīkṣṇa digested in it is like the sun, and tin digested in it has the color of the japā flower.

children.text: śvetābhrasatvaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca tāpyaṃ ca vimalāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: White essence of abhra, tīkṣṇa, tāpya, and likewise vimalā,

children.text: kharparaṃ ca samaṃ sarvaṃ kuṭilaṃ ca caturguṇam ||
children.translated_text: and kharpara, all in equal parts, with kuṭila in fourfold quantity:
he should blow the fire on all of it, pulverize it, and calcine it with five puṭas.

children.text: tāre drute śataguṇaṃ vāhayecca śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should introduce it a hundredfold into molten silver, slowly and gradually.

children.text: tārabījam idaṃ khyātaṃ jāraṇe paramaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: This is known as tāra-bīja, silver seed, and is supremely beneficial in digestion.

children.text: yathā tāpyena kuṭilaṃ tathā tāpyena mārayet ||
children.translated_text: As kuṭila is killed by tāpya, so he should kill it with tāpya.

children.text: tadbhāgaṃ ca samaṃ tālaṃ tatsamaṃ rajate drute
children.translated_text: He should take that part, and an equal amount of tāla; an equal amount of that should go into molten silver.

children.text: triṃśadguṇaṃ bhaved yāvat tāvad vāhyaṃ krameṇa ca ||
children.translated_text: It should be introduced successively until it becomes thirtyfold.
This is known as tāra-bīja, and he should digest it in mercury.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca vimalāṃ samāṃśaṃ cūrṇayetpriye ||
children.translated_text: Tīkṣṇa, tin, and vimalā in equal shares should be pulverized, O beloved.
He should heat it in a crucible smeared with dvandva-mela, and it will become a metallic lump.
He should pulverize that lump, triturate it with sour liquids, and roast it in a puṭa.
He should do this five times; that ash is produced, O beloved.

children.text: tadbhasma vidrute tāre vāhayecca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: He should introduce that ash, in equal portions, into molten silver.

children.text: dhaman dhaman daśaguṇaṃ yāvad bhavati bhairavi
children.translated_text: Heating and heating, O <s>Bhairavī</s>, until it becomes tenfold,
this is the best tāra-bīja for the digestion of the king of rasa.
White essence of abhra, kuṭila, and essence of tāra-mākṣika:
he should pulverize these three in equal parts and heat them after placing them in a coated crucible.
He should introduce that powder into silver, adding it in an amount equal to the silver.
This should continue up to tenfold by the addition of tāra-mākṣika.

children.text: tārabījam idaṃ proktaṃ jāraṇe paramaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: This is taught as tāra-bīja, supremely beneficial in digestion.
O <s>Deveśī</s>, in order, take tīkṣṇa, tāla, and amla in portions of three, two, and one.
Having pulverized them and placed them in a coated crucible, he should heat them with an intense fire.
He should pulverize that metallic lump, triturate it with sour liquids, and roast it in a puṭa.

children.text: saptadhā taddrute tāre vāhyaṃ daśaguṇaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: After doing this seven times, it should then be introduced tenfold into molten silver.

children.text: kṣiptvā kṣiptvā tālacūrṇaṃ tāraśeṣaṃ yathā dhamet ||
children.translated_text: Adding tāla powder again and again, he should heat it until only silver remains.
This excellent tāra-bīja is supremely beneficial in digestion.
Kharparī, tāla, white essence of abhra, and tāra-mākṣika,

children.text: tulyaṃ sarvasamaṃ vaṅgaṃ sarvaṃ mūṣāgataṃ dhamet
children.translated_text: all equal, with tin equal to the whole: he should heat everything placed in a crucible.
He should pulverize it, triturate it with sour liquids, and roast it in a puṭa in this way seven times.
He should introduce that powder tenfold into molten silver while heating it.

children.text: tāraśeṣaṃ bhaved yāvat tāvat syāt tārabījakam ||
children.translated_text: Until only silver remains, it will become tāra-bījaka.

children.text: śvetābhrasatvaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca dvandvaṃ kuryācca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: White essence of abhra and tin should be made into a dvandva compound as before.
After adding one quarter of tālaka to that powder, he should triturate it with sour liquids.
He should roast it in a puṭa, add tāla to it, and repeat the trituration and puṭa as before.
In this way he should perform five puṭas; he should introduce that powder into the molten metal.
When it is twelvefold in silver, that becomes tāra-bījaka.
White essence of abhra and tin, with tīkṣṇa powder equal to half the tin,
and vimalā of the measure of the tīkṣṇa, should all be heated after being put into a crucible.
Then he should pulverize it, grind it with sour liquids, seal it, and cook it in a puṭa.
Having done this five times, he should again introduce it into molten silver.
Until it is a hundredfold, he should add tālaka and heat it.
Until only silver remains, so long it becomes tāra-bījaka.
Now I shall explain tāmra-bīja, copper seed, for the sake of mercury's digestion.

children.text: svarṇaṃ tāmraṃ samaṃ devi tayostulyaṃ ca mākṣikam
children.translated_text: Gold and copper in equal parts, O goddess, and mākṣika equal to those two:
he should place it above and below in a coated crucible and heat it strongly.

children.text: dhamedevaṃ ca daśadhā dattvā dattvātha mākṣikam
children.translated_text: He should heat it in this way ten times, adding mākṣika again and again.
This is known as tāmra-bīja, resembling shining rays.
Abhraka and rasaka in equal parts, with lead ash fourfold:
he should heat that and pulverize it, and kill it with mākṣika.
Then he should combine an equal amount of śilā powder with this and cast it in.
He should heat that in similar melted gold a hundred times, O dear one.
This is called <s>nāga-bīja</s> (lead-seed); he should make <s>sūta</s> (mercury) digest it.
I shall teach the <s>nāga-bīja</s>, which is excellent for the digestion of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
Then he should heat mercury, mica, copper, and lead, increasing the proportions part by part.
That, killed with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), should be carried through as the seed, O dear one.
Tin, killed with <s>tāpya</s> (copper pyrite), should be introduced into gold in the proportion of one thirty-second part.
Realgar is to be added thirtyfold; this is taught as <s>nāga-bīja</s>.

children.text: bījaṃ pravakṣyāmi vaṅgaṃ tālaṃ ca tāpyakam
children.translated_text: I shall teach a seed: tin, <s>tāla</s> (orpiment), and <s>tāpya</s>.
He should heat them in equal quantity and pulverize them, together with an equal amount of <s>tāpya</s> and <s>tāla</s>.
He should grind and calcine them with sour liquids; after sixteen calcinations they become ash.
Into melted silver he should introduce tin ash a hundredfold.
Into that silver, O goddess, he should introduce <s>tālaka</s> thirty-twofold.
This is to be known as <s>vaṅga-bīja</s> (tin-seed); he should make <s>sūta</s> digest it.
I shall teach the combinations of <s>biḍa</s> that are suitable for digestion, O worshiped by the gods.
Sauvīra, sulfur, alum, green vitriol, the three pungents, and rock salt,
sauvarcala salt, sarjikā alkali, and what is produced on the banks of the Mālatī:
he should steep all of this for seven days with the juices of śigru roots.

children.text: biḍo'yaṃ jāraṇe śreṣṭho nāmnā ca vaḍabānalaḥ
children.translated_text: This <s>biḍa</s> is best for digestion and is named <s>Vaḍabānala</s>.
He should steep and calcine burnt conch-shell with the milks of arka, O dear one.

children.text: śatadhāyaṃ viḍaḥ prokto nāmnā vaiśvānaro mahān
children.translated_text: This <s>biḍa</s>, prepared a hundred times, is called the great <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text: gandhakaṃ śaṅkhacūrṇaṃ ca saindhavaṃ ca viṣaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: Sulfur, conch-shell powder, rock salt, and poison, in equal measure,
steeped a hundred times with cow urine and likewise with śigru-root juices:

children.text: bhāvito 'yaṃ biḍaḥ prokto nāmnā jvālāmukhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this is taught as the <s>biḍa</s> named <s>Jvālāmukha</s>.
Borax should be steeped a hundred times with the juices of palāśa, O dear one.
This <s>biḍa</s>, named <s>Agnijihvaka</s>, is best for the digestion of metals.
Magnetite, sulfur, and cūlī, each separately, are digesters of metal.
Cūlī, sulfur, sindhūttha, tāla, bhūkhaga, and borax,
should be cooked with alkali and urine; this is named <s>Vaḍabāmukha</s>.

children.text: devadāliṃ mokṣakaṃ ca niculaṃ ca punarnavām ||
children.translated_text: Devadālī, mokṣaka, nicula, and punarnavā,
palāśa, kāñcana, vāsā, castor, vāstuka, sesame,
and also the whole banana plant should be cut up and not dried too much.
After that, he should put it into the class of urines, eight times as much.

children.text: samūlaṃ mūlakaṃ dagdhvā tilakāṇḍaṃ ca tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: Having burnt radish with its root and an equal amount of sesame stalk,

children.text: kṣāradvayaṃ pūrvarase kṣiptvā sthāpyaṃ tryahaṃ khare
children.translated_text: he should put the two alkalis into the earlier liquid and leave it in sharp sunlight for three days.
Filtered through cloth, that liquid should be cooked in an iron vessel.

children.text: bahavo budbudā bāṣpā udbhavanti yadā yadā
children.translated_text: Whenever many bubbles and vapors arise,
he should add the three alkalis, the three pungents, sulfur, green vitriol, and the five salts,

children.text: saurāṣṭrīṃ rāmaṭhaṃ cūliṃ samaṃ cūrṇīkṛtaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: together with saurāṣṭrī, rāmaṭha, and cūlī, all powdered in equal quantity.
He should stir it with an iron ladle until it becomes like a cooking of jaggery.
Having taken it down, he should place it in an iron capsule for seven days.
He should keep it buried in the earth and in a heap of grain for another seven days.
He should keep it in the heat for seven days; this is the <s>biḍa</s> called <s>Mahāvaiśvānara</s>.
He should steep sulfur a hundred times with sour lemon juice and with the juice of wild śigru.
This <s>biḍa</s> is called <s>Vahni</s>.

children.text: navasāro'pi ca tathā gandhavatsa biḍo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Similarly, navasāra too becomes a <s>biḍa</s> when treated like sulfur.
Sulfur, nicula alkali, guñjā seeds, and borax,

children.text: mūlabījaṃ devadālyāḥ samaṃ sarvaṃ ca bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: together with the root and seed of devadālī, should all be steeped in equal quantity.
With the waters of bitter kośātakī and likewise with the sour group, seven times,
this becomes the <s>biḍa</s> called <s>Citrabhānu</s>, foremost for the digestion of gold.

children.text: mūlakaṃ śṛṅgiveraṃ ca vahniṃ dagdhvā trayaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Radish, ginger, and vahni, the three in equal quantity, should be burnt.
He should put that into cow urine and have it filtered through cloth.
Sulfur steeped with this a hundred times becomes a great <s>biḍa</s>.

children.text: tālaṃ śilā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ ca śaṅkhaṃ lavaṇaśuktike ||
children.translated_text: Tāla, realgar, borax, conch-shell, salt, and oyster shell
should be cooked gently with urines and sour liquids over fire; this is a great <s>biḍa</s>.
Then he should steep burnt conch-shell a hundred times with the milks of arka.
Having ground it with the sour group, he should seal it and cook it with five calcinations.
Then he should add an equal amount of borax and alkali, steeped in the sour group.

children.text: kṛtvā manaḥśilāṃ gandhaṃ daradaṃ vidrumaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: After making realgar, sulfur, cinnabar, and coral,

children.text: nṛpāvartaṃ tu pañcānāṃ śaṃkhacūrṇaṃ samaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: and nṛpāvarta, with conch-shell powder equal to the five, O dear one,
he should steep it for three days with the sour group; it becomes a great <s>biḍa</s>.

children.text: nāmnā vajrānalaḥ proktaḥ khoṭaḥ sūtasya jāraṇe ||
children.translated_text: It is called <s>Vajrānala</s>, a lump for the digestion of <s>sūta</s>.
He should always employ it in sāraṇa in the crucible for joining pairs.
Mercury at once digests even diamond and the rest.
Burnt conch-shell powder, soaked a hundred times in the milk of arka,

children.text: puṭitaṃ bahuśo devi praśasto jāraṇe biḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and calcined many times, O goddess, is praised as a <s>biḍa</s> for digestion.

children.text: śataśo vā plutaṃ cūrṇaṃ gandhakasya gavāṃ jalaiḥ
children.translated_text: Or sulfur powder, soaked a hundred times with cow waters,
together with burnt conch-shell powder steeped in śigru-root water,
and combined a hundred times with poison and sindhūttha, is <s>Vaḍabāmukha</s>.
He should steep sulfur with liquids produced from kanyā, dhuttūra, and karavīra.
A hundred times in the heat, this <s>biḍa</s> digests everything.
He should flood sulfur and rock salt with the juices of copper-vine leaves.
In seven days it becomes ready; he should employ it for the digestion of gold.

children.text: saindhavaṃ kunaṭī gandhaṃ pratyekaṃ ca palaṃ palam ||
children.translated_text: Rock salt, kunaṭī, and sulfur, each one pala,
and three palas of bhūlatā: he should grind all of this, dry it, and cook it.
He should do this eight times; this is remembered as the perfected <s>biḍa</s>.
Now I shall teach the operation for digesting mica; listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
In a heated mortar, well-prepared <s>sūta</s> (mercury) of sixty-four niṣkas should be used.

children.text: bhāvitaṃ gaganaṃ caikaṃ niṣkaṃ tatra vinikṣipet
children.translated_text: And one niṣka of prepared <s>gagana</s> (mica) should be put there.
The three alkalis, the five salts, bhūkhaga, sour javetasa,
in sixteenth parts of <s>rasendra</s> (mercury), should be added with citron juice.
One should grind it for a yāma in the tortoise apparatus, furnished with viḍa.
Having put it in, one should cook it for a day; the <s>rasa</s> then becomes one whose morsel has been digested.
Having placed this <s>sūta</s> in a heated mortar, along with rājī, jaggery, wool,

children.text: iṣṭikāṃ gṛhadhūmaṃ ca saindhavaṃ pāradasya tu
children.translated_text: brick, house-soot, and rock salt, each in relation to the <s>pārada</s>,
all this, in a sixteenth part, should be ground for a day with the group of sour liquids.
Having formed it into a ball in the fierce sun, one should bind it in that <s>rasa</s> as a bundle.
In a swing apparatus filled with the sour class of liquids, one should cook it for a day.
At each morsel one should do this; it then requires another morsel.
If a morsel is undigested, it should be cooked in the tortoise apparatus.
Thus, by the sequence of morsels alone, one should cause it to digest <s>gagana</s> and the rest,
beginning with a sixty-fourth part, up to sixty-fourfold quantity.
Into <s>rasendra</s> one should cause the morsel to be digested, giving it again and again.
