When <s>sūta</s> has digested mica-essence in a sixty-fourth part,
it is staff-bearing and leech-like; at a thirty-second part it is this.
At a sixteenth part it is like a crow's dung; at an eighth part,
O <s>Devi</s>, it is like the watery part of curds when it has been digested to a quarter part.
At a half part it is like fresh butter; when digested, it becomes ball-like.
When an equal amount of <s>abhraka</s> (mica) has been digested, the <s>rasa</s> has the power of piercing a hundredfold.
When twice as much dense mica is digested, it pierces by a thousandth part.
When fourfold mica has been digested, O dear one, it gives a lifespan of ten thousand years.
When eightfold <s>gagana</s> has been digested, it gives the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s> and pierces a hundred thousandfold.
When sixteenfold mica has been digested, it gives the lifespan of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and pierces ten millionfold.
When thirty-twofold has been digested, it gives the lifespan of <s>Rudra</s> and pierces by ten crores.
When sixty-fourfold has been digested, it gives eternal life and pierces by a hundred crores.
When an equal amount of mica has been digested, <s>rasa</s> casts off its defects.
It abandons all those inherent in itself and consumes all metals.
It does not fall downward from the apparatus, nor does it fly upward.

children.text: nodgārī kapilo varṇe vahnau tiṣṭhati niścalaḥ
children.translated_text: It does not belch out; it is tawny in color and remains motionless in fire.
O <s>Devi</s>, it releases drops; the <s>rasa</s> becomes one whose wings are cut.
When an equal amount has been digested it is a child; when fourfold has been digested it is young.
When sixfold <s>vyoma</s> (mica) has been digested, the <s>rasa</s> is called old.
As a child it pierces by a paste; as young, by smearing a sheet.
But this digested <s>rasendra</s>, when old, pierces metals.

children.text: bālaḥ sūto rujaṃ hanti na samartho rasāyane
children.translated_text: Child <s>sūta</s> removes disease, but is not capable in rejuvenation.
When young it is skilled in rejuvenation; when old it acts on both body and metals.
In the absence of dense mica-essence, kānta-essence is to be supplied.
In its absence, tīkṣṇa is used; in this way one should digest the paired substances.
After the <s>sūta</s> has digested dense mica, one should then digest the paired substances.
<s>Rasendra</s> should not operate on mica-essence devoid of a paired substance.
Therefore mica joined with gold and the other metals should certainly be made to operate.

children.text: nāgābhraṃ vāpi vaṅgābhraṃ tāmrābhraṃ vā surārcite ||
children.translated_text: One should digest lead-mica, tin-mica, or copper-mica, O you worshipped by the gods,

children.text: tārābhraṃ vāpi hemābhraṃ tāpyābhraṃ vāpi jārayet
children.translated_text: or silver-mica, gold-mica, or tāpya-mica.

children.text: ghanasatvaṃ yathā jīrṇaṃ tathā dvandvāni jārayet ||
children.translated_text: Just as dense mica-essence is digested, so one should digest the paired substances.
Then, after the <s>rasa</s> of paired bīja, one should digest the prepared bījas.

children.text: khalvaṃ tu pīṭhikā devi rasendro liṅga ucyate ||
children.translated_text: The mortar is the pedestal, O <s>Devi</s>; <s>rasendra</s> is said to be the liṅga.

children.text: mardanaṃ candanaṃ tasya grāsaḥ pūjā vidhīyate
children.translated_text: Its grinding is sandal-paste, and the morsel is prescribed as worship.
When the mass of sins is being destroyed, the digestion of <s>rasa</s> becomes easy.

children.text: jāraṇāyāṃ ca labdhāyāṃ jñānaṃ kaivalyadaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: And when digestion is obtained, knowledge that grants isolation-liberation arises.

children.text: tāvanmuktiḥ kutaḥ kānte yāvanno vetti jāraṇām ||
children.translated_text: How can there be liberation, O beloved, so long as one does not know digestion?
Digestion makes liberation manifest for the foremost practitioner, O dear one.

children.text: jāraṇārthaṃ raso yāvaddinaṃ vahnau tu dhāryate ||
children.translated_text: For as many days as <s>rasa</s> is kept in fire for the sake of digestion,
for that many thousands of kalpas he enjoys happiness in <s>Śiva</s>'s world.
Whoever keeps <s>rasa</s> in fire for one day, or for half of that,
his sins, accumulated through many births, are destroyed.
<s>Rasa</s> is the friend of gold-seeded one and likewise has a golden body.
There is incompatibility between <s>sūta</s> and fire; from gold there is friendship with water.
Pressed through a fourfold cloth, it is clean,
when, by the filtering operation, the morsel has gone out without remainder.
Then that <s>rasa</s> becomes staff-bearing, with the morsel digested.

children.text: hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ phaṭ raseśvarāya sarvasattvopahārāya grāsaṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hrīṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hraḥ phaṭ: O lord of <s>rasa</s>, for the offering of all beings, take the morsel, take the morsel; hrīṃ svāhā.
I shall explain the embryonic liquefaction of the digested <s>rasa</s>.
Listen, O <s>Bhairavī</s>, to the bījas fit for melting within the embryo.

children.text: nāgabhasma ca mākṣīkaṃ gandhakaṃ ca samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Lead ash, mākṣīka, and sulfur, each in equal quantity,
should be powdered and made to flow into melted gold in threefold quantity, while blowing.
This is putrid bīja; it melts instantly in the womb of <s>sūta</s>.
Having combined lead with gold, one should add powdered śilā again and again.
When the lead is exhausted, one should give lead again and again three times.
Until only gold remains, it should be blown again and again.
This bīja certainly melts within the womb of <s>rasa</s> through grinding.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ tāpyasatvaṃ tu samaṃ mūṣāgataṃ dhamet ||
children.translated_text: Gold and tāpya-essence, equal in amount, placed in a crucible, should be blown.
When that has melted, one should add equal amounts of tāpya powder again and again.
Mākṣīka-essence, threefold, should thus be caused to flow again and again.
This <s>bīja</s> (seed) melts in the womb of <s>rasendra</s> through grinding;
then he should melt the essence of tāpya in equal quantity with gold.
He should make leaves thin enough to be pierced by a thorn and smear them
with salt ground in sour liquid, equal to sulfur, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
He should cook those leaves in a closed heating until only gold remains.
This <s>bīja</s> melts in the womb of <s>rasendra</s> through grinding.
He should grind sindhūttha equal to tāpya with sour liquid,

children.text: tatsaṃpuṭe puṭe pacyāt punaḥ saṃmardayet puṭet ||
children.translated_text: cook it in a sealed capsule in a heating, and again grind it and heat it.
Again and again, twelve times, he should grind with sour liquids
an equal amount of ash born of lead; with this he treats the little gold leaf.
Having smeared it again and again, he should blow it seven times and then cause it to flow.
When molten, he should first quench it seven times with the prepared pastes.
This <s>bīja</s> melts in the womb of <s>rasendra</s> through grinding.

children.text: kāsīsaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ gandhaṃ tāpyaṃ sauvarcalaṃ śilām ||
children.translated_text: Green vitriol, borax, sulfur, tāpya, sauvarcala salt, and śilā,
all in equal quantities, he should grind with sour chickpea liquid for a whole day.
This <s>bīja</s> melts in the womb of <s>rasendra</s> through grinding.

children.text: suvarcalaṃ ca kāsīsaṃ yavakṣāraṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇam
children.translated_text: Sauvarcala salt, green vitriol, yavakṣāra, and borax,

children.text: mākṣikaṃ saindhavaṃ cullī sāmudraṃ rājikā tathā ||
children.translated_text: mākṣika, rock salt, cullī, sea salt, and mustard,
together with kāṅkṣī and camphor in equal quantity, ground with the milks of arka and snuk,
with this <s>biḍa</s> he should smear the crucible to a thickness of a finger.
This crucible apparatus is best for the operation of melting within the womb.

children.text: svarṇaṃ tāmraṃ mṛtaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ rañjitaṃ pakvabījakam ||
children.translated_text: Gold, copper, calcined tīkṣṇa iron, colored and cooked <s>bīja</s>,
and the <s>garbha-drāvaṇa-bīja</s>: he should melt all of them thoroughly.
When this is molten, he should add tāpya powder again and again, blowing steadily,
until the copper and tīkṣṇa iron have been exhausted, O queen of the gods.
This <s>bīja</s> melts in the womb of <s>rasendra</s> through grinding.
Gold, and lead struck by sulfur, are the means for preparing the cooked <s>bīja</s>.
He should put those two into the smeared crucible, close it, and blow strongly.
That powder, when sprinkled, melts completely in the womb of mercury.

children.text: suvarṇe vidrute śulbaṃ mṛtaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the gold is melted, he should gradually cause calcined copper and tīkṣṇa iron
to flow in, up to six times as much, until it melts in that mercury, O dear one.
The mahārasas, the subsidiary rasas, and the exhausted metals, inexhaustibly,
in equal parts, by the addition of equal mākṣika and sulfur,
he should cause this to flow hundreds of times, until only the inexhaustible portion remains.
It certainly melts in the womb of <s>rasarāja</s> in an equal portion.
He should place the sixty-fourth part of digested <s>rasendra</s>,
and the <s>garbha-drāvaṇa-bīja</s>, in a heated mortar.
With śilā, rucaka, mākṣika, sulfur, green vitriol, and borax,
he should grind all this with sour chickpea liquid for a whole day.
After giving this as a sixteenth part of the mercury, he should also add the <s>bīja</s>.

children.text: mucyate yatra yatraiva tat tad dravati tatkṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Wherever and wherever it is released, that very thing melts at once.
He should collect ash-alkali produced from apāmārga and palāśa,
borax with yavakṣāra, green vitriol, and sauvarcala salt,
sea salt, rock salt, mustard, mākṣika, and navasāra,
camphor and mākṣika in equal quantity, ground with the milks of snuhī and arka.
Having made a coating for the crucible with just this, he should also make one with <s>biḍa</s>.
With a coating of a finger's measure, he should put the previously prepared mercury in it.

children.text: ruddhvā svedyaṃ dinaikaṃ tu karīṣāgnau dravatyalam ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, it should be steamed for one day; in a dung-fire it melts completely.

children.text: ityevaṃ drāvitaṃ jāryaṃ yāvad bījaṃ tu ṣaḍguṇam
children.translated_text: The substance melted in this way should be digested until the <s>bīja</s> is six times as much.
O <s>Śivā</s>, I shall tell you the external liquefaction procedure in order.
Listen to the means by which the <s>druti</s> (liquefaction) of mica and the others comes about.
Now I shall teach the liquefaction of mica, and also the kañcukī tuber.

children.text: kapitindau keśataile pratyekaṃ tu tridhā vapet
children.translated_text: He should quench it three times each in kapitindau and in hair-oil.
Having melted that essence of mica in a crucible, it becomes a <s>druti</s>.
The dust of the fruit of devadālī, śakagopa, and horse saliva,
together with borax, he should steep many times with jālinī waters, O dear one.

children.text: drāvayet kāñcanaṃ tatra vapet sūtasamā drutiḥ
children.translated_text: He should melt gold there and quench it; the <s>druti</s> becomes equal to mercury.
The three alkalis, sour chickpea liquid, rāmaṭha, and amlavetasa,
and also jvālāmukhī alkali, with the juice of sthalakumbhī,
having ground them with the milks of snuhī and arka, he should put a soft diamond into that ball.
Then he should place that in a citron and cook it for three days in a swing-apparatus.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte hīrakasya drutir bhavati sūtavat ||
children.translated_text: When this has been done, the diamond's <s>druti</s> becomes like mercury.
The same liquefaction occurs when applied to rubies and the other jewels.

children.text: drutīnāṃ melanaṃ vakṣye śṛṇu bhairavi tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall teach the combining of the <s>drutis</s>; listen, O <s>Bhairavī</s>, according to truth.
Black agaru, musk, brahmabīja, and mākṣika,

children.text: nārīpuṣpaṃ viṣaṃ hiṃgu laśunaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ niśā ||
children.translated_text: nārīpuṣpa, poison, asafoetida, garlic, borax, and turmeric:

children.text: etaiḥ samaṃ drutiṃ sūtaṃ taptakhalve vimardayet
children.translated_text: with these he should grind the <s>druti</s> together with mercury in a heated mortar.
Pāṭhā, vandhyā, tālamūlī, nīlī, the three kinds of citraka,
lotus rhizome, kṣīrakanda, balā, guñjā, fresh amṛtā ginger,

children.text: aśvalālā nimbapatraṃ strīstanyaṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: horse saliva, neem leaves, and woman's milk, each in equal quantity:
he should take the clear juice of these, filtered through cloth.
Having poured it again and again into mercury joined with this <s>druti</s>, he should grind it.

children.text: milanti drutayaḥ sarvāḥ pārade nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: All the <s>drutis</s> unite in mercury; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: drutayo militā yena yantraṃ tenaiva kacchapam ||
children.translated_text: With the same substance by which the <s>drutis</s> have been united, the turtle apparatus
should be smeared with the <s>biḍa</s> mixture, and he should combine and digest them in order.
In this way he should digest into <s>rasarāja</s> a <s>druti</s> six times as great.
Listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, to the coloring of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) that has digested liquefied metal.
Therefore I shall also tell you the coloring of coloring <s>bīja</s>s.
Palāśa flower, mañjiṣṭhā, red karavīra-born

children.text: puṣpaṃ ca khadiraṃ raktacandanaṃ kukkuṭī tathā ||
children.translated_text: flower, khadira, red sandalwood, and kukkuṭī,
the two niśās, sarala, devadāru, and hibiscus flower,
and other red flowers should be ground with lac-water.
Oil four times this quantity, and red-flower liquid four times the oil

children.text: dravaṃ caturguṇaṃ deyaṃ tailaśeṣaṃ yathā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: should be added, so that only the oil remains.
Into that he should pour the <s>bīja</s> twenty-one times.
Thus he should color all the cooked <s>bīja</s>s, O you worshipped by the gods.
Taking <s>nāga</s> (lead) in an earthen pan, he should kindle a fierce fire beneath it.
He should throw palāśa leaves and seeds into it and stir it.
Grinding it with a palāśa stick for four yāmas, it turns to ash.
He should grind that ash with an equal amount of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) in sour liquid for one yāma.
After sealing it, he should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; when it has cooled of itself, he should take it out.

children.text: taccaturthāṃśakaṃ gandhaṃ dattvā piṣṭvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: Adding sulfur equal to one fourth of it, he should grind it and cook it in a puṭa.
In this way, after fourteen repetitions, the <s>nāga</s> becomes red in color.
Powder of the five parts of vāśā, and powder of kakubha,
the shoots and flowers of śigru, kiṃśuka, and koraṇḍa, nāginī,

children.text: ahimāraṃ kumārīṃ ca nāgakanyāṃ ca cūrṇayet ||
children.translated_text: ahimāra, kumārī, and nāgakanyā should be powdered.
All this is one part, and <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) is two parts.

children.text: bhāṇḍe sarvaṃ vinikṣipya gavāṃ mūtre caturguṇe ||
children.translated_text: Having put everything in a vessel with cow urine four times as much,
he should cook it until one quarter remains, pouring it again and again onto the earlier <s>nāga</s>.
He should cook it on the hearth and stir it with brahmadaṇḍa sticks for seven days.
He should quench this <s>nāga</s> three times in the melted cooked <s>bīja</s>.
The <s>bīja</s> becomes colored; it is the chief means for coloring <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
He should heat equal quantities of tāpya essence and black mica essence powder.
When it is melted, he should add tāpya powder and calcined copper in sequence.
That threefold <s>bīja</s> becomes a coloring agent, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
He should grind equal quantities of kunaṭī, mākṣika, sulfur, and cinnabar.
In the juice of the red group that has been ground in cow urine, O dear one,
he should grind it, dry it seven times, powder it, and add it.

children.text: dvaṃdvite tīkṣṇatāmre ca tulyaṃ kṣiptvā dhameddṛḍham
children.translated_text: Having thrown an equal amount into paired sharp iron and copper, he should heat it strongly.
He should quench it in the red group mixed with jyotiṣmatī oil.

children.text: punaśca pūrvacūrṇaṃ tu tulyaṃ kṣiptvā dhamet priye
children.translated_text: Again, O dear one, he should add an equal amount of the previous powder and heat it.
He should sprinkle it seven times in just this way; the <s>bīja</s> becomes a colorer of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: tāraṃ ca vimalāsattvaṃ samāṃśaṃ drāvayet tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then he should melt equal parts of <s>tāra</s> (silver) and vimala essence.
Cinnabar steeped three times in cow urine with the red group

children.text: tattulyaṃ nikṣipet tasmin dhamed evaṃ tu saptadhā
children.translated_text: should be added to it in an equal amount; he should heat it in this way seven times.

children.text: kṣiptvā kṣiptvā ca daradaṃ syādbījaṃ rasarañjakam ||
children.translated_text: Adding cinnabar again and again, the <s>bīja</s> becomes a colorer of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: ghanasattvam ahiṃ svarṇaṃ samāṃśaṃ dvaṃdvitaṃ dhamet
children.translated_text: He should heat paired equal portions of ghana essence, ahi, and gold.

children.text: kharpare raktavargaṃ ca mākṣikaṃ gairikaṃ śilām ||
children.translated_text: In an earthen pan, he should powder equally the red group, mākṣika, red ochre, and realgar.

children.text: samaṃ saṃcūrṇayet tasmin vāpayecca samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Into that he should make equal sprinklings, each in the same amount.
After ten repetitions, this becomes a <s>bīja</s> that colors lord <s>sūta</s>.
Red <s>manaḥśilā</s> should be steeped in the juices of barley and tamarind
twenty times with care; with that paste he should coat
a sheet of <s>nāga</s> and cook it in a puṭa until it has become powder.

children.text: rasakasya tu bhāgāṃstrīn bhāgaikaṃ daradasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Three parts of rasaka and one part of cinnabar,
and one part each of the three, realgar, sulfur, and poison,
he should sprinkle with sour citron juices; with that paste he should coat it.
He should put each such earlier <s>nāga</s> in the womb of a crucible and then heat it.

children.text: drutaṃ yāvat samuddhṛtya liptvā mūṣāṃ punar dhamet ||
children.translated_text: When it is melted, he should take it out, coat the crucible, and heat it again.

children.text: ityevaṃ saptadhā dhāmyaṃ nāgaṃ svarṇanibhaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>nāga</s> should be heated seven times; it becomes like gold.

children.text: pītābhrakasya satvaṃ tu pūrvanāgaṃ ca tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: The essence of yellow mica and the earlier <s>nāga</s>, equal to it,
should be paired by the previous procedure and made sprinkled.

children.text: anena dvandvayogena vāpo deyo drutasya ca ||
children.translated_text: By this pairing procedure, sprinkling should be given to the melted
cooked <s>bīja</s> three times; that <s>bīja</s> is well colored and auspicious.
Now therefore listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, to the coloring of silver <s>bīja</s>s.
O dear one, in the juice of white flowers produced from various trees,
he should add one part of kaṅguṇī oil to four parts.
He should cook it down until only the oil remains; the silver <s>bīja</s>s are placed there.
Having melted them again and again, he should quench them twenty-one times.
Thus the <s>bīja</s>s become colored for the coloring of <s>rasa</s>.
In this same way he should color the <s>bīja</s>s of <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
For <s>sūta</s> that has digested liquefied metal, a sixty-fourth part
of coloring <s>bīja</s> should be placed in a heated mortar for a day.
He should grind it in the heated mortar and cook it in a <s>kacchapa-yantra</s>.
Thus, by the sequence of mouthfuls, he should digest six times its amount, O dear one.
I shall teach the three <s>sāraṇā</s>s of colored <s>rasendra</s>.
The <s>bīja</s>s suitable for <s>sāraṇā</s> are divine, O you worshipped by the gods.
Gold should be twelve parts, and pure mercury half of that.
Lead ash should be half of the <s>rasendra</s>, and calcined diamond four parts.
These four should be ground with sour liquids in a heated mortar.
After taking it out, he should seal it in a paired-mixing crucible and heat it.
It certainly fuses forcibly; this is the diamond <s>bīja</s>, O dear one.
Then he should steep calcined diamond for a day with the milks of śāribā.
He should grind it, make it into a pellet, and dry it, using one part,
three parts of <s>rasarāja</s> (mercury), and four parts of gold.
He should grind the paste with an acidic liquid and make that diamond pellet.
He should wrap it with that paste, and wrap it with birch bark.

children.text: pakṣaṃ nyased dhānyarāśau tad uddhṛtya punaḥ priye
children.translated_text: He should place it for a fortnight in a heap of grain; then, having taken it out again, O dear one,
he should blow it forcefully. It will indeed fuse; this becomes <s>vajrabīja</s> (diamond seed).
He should wrap it with gold leaf measuring one-sixteenth of the diamond,
put it into a coated crucible, and add a gold portion and powder made from white glass.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ vā nṛkapālaṃ vā cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā vinikṣipet
children.translated_text: Or he may make powder from a human skull and put that in.

children.text: nirudhya ca dhamet tīvram evaṃ kuryāt punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, he should blow it intensely; he should do this again and again.
Putting in white glass again and again, or else a human skull,
in this way, after seven times, it fuses completely; this becomes <s>vajrabīja</s>.
After this, for <s>sāraṇā</s> I shall teach the preparation of oil:
oil produced from <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>karañja</s>, <s>akṣa</s>, and bitter gourd,
and oil produced from turtle, boar, and the like, from ram and fish.
Fat derived from leech and frog should also be taken according to rule.
The red group and the yellow group should be decocted with four times as much milk.
He should extract the liquid of many red and yellow flowers,
and also the liquids produced from <s>pāṭalīkā</s>, <s>katuṇḍī</s>, and <s>mahārāṣṭrī</s>.
There should be one part oil, one part fat, and four parts decoction,
two parts of flower liquids, and two parts of the liquids beginning with <s>pāṭalī</s>.

children.text: sarvaṃ tāmramaye pātre mṛdunā vahninā pacet ||
children.translated_text: He should cook everything in a copper vessel over a gentle fire.
Into it he should put a sixteenth part of <s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>amalatāpya</s>,
the famous <s>sāraṇātaila</s> (sāraṇā oil), for the digestion of <s>rasarāja</s>.
Colored <s>rasarāja</s>, combined with <s>sāraṇā</s> oil,
should be put into the <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus, into the tube-crucible when it has become molten.
He should pour the seed into the <s>sūta</s> (mercury), as the sixty-fourth part.
Taking it out, he should grind it for a day in a heated mortar with salts and acidic liquids.

children.text: tataḥ kacchapayantre tu savivye pācayed dinam
children.translated_text: Then he should cook it for a day in the tortoise apparatus, together with <s>savivya</s>.

children.text: ityevaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ sāryaṃ sārito jāyate rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus it should be carried through <s>sāraṇā</s> six times; the mercury becomes <s>sārita</s>.
When this has been done a second time, the <s>sūta</s> is <s>anusārita</s>.

children.text: tathā tṛtīyavāre tu rasaḥ syāt pratisāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, on the third time, the mercury is <s>pratisārita</s>.
For <s>rasendra</s> that has undergone <s>sāraṇā</s>, there should be an equal part of orpiment.
He should grind it with oils of <s>dhūrta</s> and with liquids of divine herbs for a day.
Then, having removed it, he should place it in a diamond crucible and cook it for a day.

children.text: karīṣāgnāviti punar mardyaṃ pācyaṃ tridhā priye ||
children.translated_text: This is to be done in a cow-dung fire; it should again be ground and cooked three times, O dear one.

children.text: anena karmaṇā devi sūto baddhamukho bhavet
children.translated_text: By this procedure, O goddess, the <s>sūta</s> becomes closed-mouthed.
Of the closed-mouthed <s>sūta</s>, O you who are honored by the gods, one part,
and one part of the powders of silver, copper, and iron
should all be thoroughly ground with the waters of <s>devadālī</s> for a day. Then,

children.text: madhvājyaiśca dinaṃ mardyaṃ tena kuryāt sugolakam
children.translated_text: after grinding for a day with honey and ghee, he should make from it a good pellet.
He should put it into a diamond crucible, seal it, and blow it with intense fire.

children.text: sa rasaḥ khoṭabaddhaḥ syāt tatkhoṭaṃ kācaṭaṅkaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: That mercury becomes bound as a <s>khoṭa</s> lump; that <s>khoṭa</s>, with glass and borax,

children.text: tejaḥpuñjo bhavedyāvat tāvat kuryād dhaman dhaman ||
children.translated_text: should be blown again and again until it becomes a mass of brilliance.

children.text: taṃ rasaṃ yojayed dehe lohe roge ca pārvati
children.translated_text: He should apply that mercury in the body, in metals, and in disease, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
I shall teach <s>dehavedha</s> (penetration of the body); listen attentively, O dear one.
Through digestion, oleation, sweating, vomiting, and purging, in order,
he should purify the body, avoiding salt, alkali, sour substances, and the like.
Then he should consume <s>āroṭaka</s> mercury, O supreme goddess.

children.text: kṣetraṃ kṛtvā śarīraṃ tu tataḥ siddharasaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having made the body a prepared field, he should then introduce the perfected mercury.
First the mercury that penetrates a hundred times, then that which penetrates a thousand times,
then the ten-thousandfold penetrating mercury and the mercury that effects a hundred-thousandfold penetration,
then the one that penetrates ten lakhs, and the crore-penetrating mercury, O you honored by the gods,
the <s>sūta</s> joined with sulfur, should be used by this sequence, O fair-vowed one.

children.text: sa rasaḥ kramate dehe siddhayaḥ sambhavanti hi
children.translated_text: That mercury passes through the body, and perfections indeed arise.

children.text: rasāyane tu yāḥ proktā mūlikā dehasiddhidāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those roots and herbs that are taught in <s>rasāyana</s> as giving bodily perfection
are joined with <s>rasendra</s>; then it enters the body, O dear one.

children.text: krāmati tanau hi sūto janayati putrāṃścadevatāgarbhān ||
children.translated_text: When <s>sūta</s> moves through the body, it produces sons who are like embryos of gods.

children.text: khe gamanena ca nityaṃ saṃcaraṇaṃ sakalabhuvaneṣu
children.translated_text: By going in the sky, there is constant wandering through all the worlds.
In the three worlds he is like <s>Brahmā</s>, the creator, the primal maker, the womb of creation.
For preservation he is like <s>Viṣṇu</s>; for destruction, in due form, like the god <s>Rudra</s>.
I shall teach the <s>krāmaṇa</s> for piercing metals; listen, O <s>Bhairavī</s>.

children.text: daradaṃ mākṣikaṃ kāntaṃ śilāṃ gandhaṃ viṣaṃ ghanam
children.translated_text: <s>Darada</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, magnetic iron, <s>śilā</s>, sulfur, poison, and <s>ghana</s>,

children.text: rasakaṃ bhūlatāṃ hiṅgu kāntāsyaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: <s>rasaka</s>, <s>bhūlatā</s>, asafoetida, <s>kāntāsya</s>, and borax, O dear one,

children.text: gandhakena hataṃ tāmraṃ bhujaṅgaṃ śilayā hatam
children.translated_text: copper killed by sulfur, lead killed by <s>śilā</s>,
iron killed by <s>darada</s>, and the substance produced from buffalo ear,
impurity, crow droppings, and blood from the first menstrual flow:
with this he should wrap perfected <s>sūta</s> and project it into metals.
There are ninety-eight parts of silver-dross, one part of gold, and likewise mercury.
This is known as the hundredfold penetrator; in this way it becomes the thousandfold penetrator.
It may penetrate ten thousand, a lakh, a crore, and even an arbuda.
As much power as there is in its digestion, to that extent he should project it into metals.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ bhūlatāṃ sūtaṃ kunaṭīṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>, <s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>sūta</s>, <s>kunaṭī</s>, and borax,
ground together with woman's breast milk and blood, are the <s>krāmaṇa</s> for casting and smearing.

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ rasakaṃ kāntam indragopaṃ viṣaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgula</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, magnetic iron, <s>indragopa</s>, and poison likewise
One should grind it with oil and blood; this is a <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetrating agent) for sprinkling and smearing.
The impurity produced from the mouth of a poisonous frog and from the eye of a buffalo,
combined with blood, is useful for making <s>rasa</s> (mercury) penetrate.

children.text: rocanaṃ gugguluṃ stanyam indragopaṃ viṣaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Rocana</s>, guggulu, breast milk, indragopa insects, and also poison:
one should grind all of this together, O goddess; it is useful for making <s>rasa</s> penetrate.
<s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, beeswax, and the ear-filth of a buffalo,
<s>bhūlatā</s>, crow-dung, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and dust from a biped,
human blood, <s>brahmasomā</s>, <s>surasā</s>, and a mountain-born substance, O dear one,

children.text: śṛṅgī ca lakṣmaṇā gṛdhrakarṇī ca krāmaṇaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>lakṣmaṇā</s>, and <s>gṛdhrakarṇī</s>: this is the supreme <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
With <s>śrīveṣṭa</s>, neem exudation, woman's breast milk, poison, and borax,
and combined with cow ghee, <s>rasa</s> passes into metal.

children.text: paramaṃ krāmaṇaṃ vaṅgaṃ mṛganābhaṃ ca pārvati
children.translated_text: Tin is the highest <s>krāmaṇa</s>, together with musk, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
<s>mātṛvāha</s>, crab, and the impurity produced inside a conch shell.
Likewise the exudation of kapittha is the supreme means for making <s>rasa</s> penetrate.
At the time of piercing, one should apply the <s>krāmaṇa</s> of the king of <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s> said:
The general <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion process) was explained by you before, O <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
Tell me the special <s>jāraṇa</s>, lord, so that I may know it.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu devi vakṣyāmi bhūcarākhyaṃ tu jāraṇam
children.translated_text: Listen, O goddess; I shall explain the <s>jāraṇa</s> called <s>Bhūcara</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ pītaṃ tathā raktaṃ śulbe tīkṣṇe ca melayet ||
children.translated_text: One should mix the black, the yellow, and the red with copper and sharp iron.

children.text: śulbaṃ śuddhaṃ yadā jīrṇaṃ dvāviṃśatiguṇaṃ mate
children.translated_text: When the purified copper has been digested, to twenty-two times its measure,

children.text: gandhanāgaṃ tato'rdhaṃ tu krameṇaiva tu melayet ||
children.translated_text: then one should gradually mix in half as much <s>gandhanāga</s>.

children.text: hemnā tu saha dātavyaṃ sūtakaikena ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: It should be given together with gold, in a proportion of sixteen to one of <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury).

children.text: gandhanāgaṃ yadā jīrṇaṃ tadā baddho bhaved rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>gandhanāga</s> has been digested, then the <s>rasa</s> becomes bound.
When the gold has been digested, one should color it with half as much killed metal.
Copper killed with sulfur, together with pyrite, cinnabar, and iron,
should be killed by a <s>puṭa</s> (closed heating); purified gold should be added sixfold.

children.text: sūtake hemabījaṃ ca yadā jīrṇaṃ caturguṇam ||
children.translated_text: When the gold-seed in the <s>sūtaka</s> has been digested fourfold,
one should know that it has fixed its color; the <s>rasa</s> becomes gold-like.
Placed in the middle of the <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus, it should be made to undergo <s>sāraṇā</s> with that very substance.
Having made one third undergo <s>sāraṇā</s>, one should digest it again in that same place.
Digested and made to undergo <s>sāraṇā</s>, and again digested and made to undergo <s>sāraṇā</s>,
through the application of seven chains, the <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of piercing ten millionfold.

children.text: bhūcarī jāraṇā proktā khecarīṃ jāraṇāṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhūcarī</s> <s>jāraṇā</s> has been explained; now hear the <s>Khecarī</s> <s>jāraṇā</s>.
One should make gems of deficient color into residues of <s>rasa</s>.
The seeds of bitter gourd should be added in half that quantity.
The skilled practitioner should make a paste combined with <s>mahājāra</s>.
At the mouth of a diamond-crucible, he should place the <s>rasa</s> in its middle.
He should grind <s>kataka</s> and gold together into one mass in this way.

children.text: padmarāgapralepaṃ tu rase grāsaṃ tu dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: A coating of ruby should be applied, and a morsel should be given to the <s>rasa</s>.
It should be eaten carefully, after bowing to the guru and the deities.
Having saluted all the siddhas, and the deities in particular,
stupor and burning of the limbs then arise; there is no doubt about this.
One sees oneself raised up, possessing a divine body and great strength.
With the sound of conches and trumpets, together with siddhas and vidyādharas,
one may wander through the worlds at will, assuming whatever form one desires and traveling by aerial vehicle.

children.text: devā vai yatra līyante siddhastatraiva līyate
children.translated_text: Where the gods themselves dissolve, the siddha dissolves there as well.
Again I shall proclaim another excellent <s>jāraṇā</s> method.
The <s>sūta</s>, well triturated, sublimed, and then freed from all defects,
with the essence of vegetable shoots and with the juice of <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>,
and an equal amount of sulfur steeped in water of palāśa flowers,

children.text: samaṃ kṛṣṇābhrasatvaṃ ca rasakaṃ cāṣṭakaṃ guṇam ||
children.translated_text: together with an equal amount of black mica essence and eight times as much <s>rasaka</s>,
should be digested with sharp iron, copper, and <s>nāga</s> in the tortoise apparatus.
Afterwards he should digest gold by means of the <s>biḍa</s> formula, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: tataḥ siddhaṃ vijānīyād dvaidhaṃ śulvasya dāpayet
children.translated_text: Then he should know it to be accomplished; he should supply copper in a twofold manner.
According to the measure of the number of operations, <s>nāga</s> becomes gold.
From here onward I shall explain the excellent sequence of <s>jāraṇā</s>.
Having steeped the seed-powders again and again with oil,
he should slowly grind that morsel, in a sixteenth part, with his finger.
Then, through the formula beginning with ginger, it should be given in a sixteenth part.

children.text: bhūrje dattvā tato deyaṃ ḍolāyantre vinikṣipet
children.translated_text: After placing it on birch bark, it should then be put into the <s>ḍolāyantra</s>.
In a day and a night, O dear one, the <s>sūtaka</s> consumes that seed.

children.text: samuddhṛtya rasaṃ devi khalve saṃmardayet tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having taken out the <s>rasa</s>, O goddess, he should then grind it in a mortar.
Then, after putting it in the apparatus, he should heat it day and night with a strong fire.
When it has been heated and removed from the apparatus, he should grind it in a heated mortar.
After grinding it, he should put it into a lump of ginger and then burn it with three <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: tato garbhe patatyāśu jarate tatsukhena tu
children.translated_text: Then it quickly falls into the womb and digests it with ease.
Then he should place it in the <s>ḍolāyantra</s>, joined with a moist lump.
On the third day the <s>sūta</s> digests it and then consumes it.
The skilled practitioner should keep it in the <s>ḍolāyantra</s> until it is evenly digested.
Afterwards, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, it should be evenly digested with the tortoise apparatus.
He should digest it in the tortoise apparatus with a twelfth part of copper.

children.text: prāgvad ārdrakayogaṃ ca garbhadrāvaṇam eva ca
children.translated_text: As before, there is the ginger formula and also the melting within the womb.

children.text: paścāt taṃ devi nikṣipya puṭaṃ dadyād vicakṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After placing it there, O goddess, the skilled practitioner should give it a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: aṣṭāṃśena tato grāsaṃ garbhadrāvaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Then, in an eighth part, the morsel and the womb-melting are as before.
He should place that <s>sūtaka</s> inside the corm of a sūraṇa plant.
The practitioner should heat it with <s>puṭa</s> until the corm is not burnt away.

children.text: pādāṃśena tu mūṣāyāṃ grāsaḥ sūte vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: A morsel of one quarter part is prescribed for the <s>sūta</s> in the crucible.
And as before he should add <s>biḍa</s> and also <s>garbhadrāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ caturguṇe jīrṇe sūtako balavān bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When four times the amount has been digested in this way, <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) becomes powerful.
Then <s>rasa</s> (mercury), standing in the fire, consumes the morsel with a rod.
After that the gems are to be digested according to the sequence that will be explained.

children.text: abhrakaṃ bhrāmakaṃ caiva śaṅkhanābhiṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Mica, <s>bhrāmaka</s>, and likewise conch-navel,
having added the <s>rasa</s>s and subsidiary <s>rasa</s>s, together with the great digestive agent,
the vajra-tuber creeper, <s>brāhmī</s>, goat's-horn herb, <s>amṛtā</s>, and iron,
the seeds of bitter gourd, and calcined metals: he should cook them.
All should be in equal parts, ground with peacock's blood.
The wise man should grind it for so long that the operation becomes firm.
A crucible shaped like a cup should be made, together with covers.
He should place the <s>sūta</s> in the middle of it and blow it with a downward draft.
At the beginning, diamond coated with the medicines should be prepared in just this way.
It is absorbed there without doubt, as in an intensely blazing fire.

children.text: kuliśādi bhaved dagdhaṃ karīṣā tena mardayet
children.translated_text: When the diamond and the rest have been burnt, he should grind them with cow-dung ash.
The learned man should digest the diamond until it reaches eleven times the amount.
Burnt conch-navel, soaked in citron juice,

children.text: muktāphalaṃ tato deyaṃ vajrajīrṇe tu sūtake ||
children.translated_text: and then pearl should be added when the diamond has been digested in the <s>sūta</s>.
By this ordered procedure it becomes elevenfold.
Only peacock bile, mixed with the extract of <s>nīlī</s>,
and blue lotuses smeared with it should be cast into the <s>sūta</s>.
The <s>rasa</s> drinks in the strong colors and rejects the weak colors.
The gems, peacock bile, and the great jewels,
he should smear a fine gem with that and cast it into the middle of the <s>rasa</s>.
Turmeric and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, infused with <s>brahma-niryāsa</s>,
should be used with that very substance for the digestion of topaz.
When many gems have been digested with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, O <s>Suvratā</s>,
behold <s>rasendra</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, with a blue, yellow, and red radiance.
He should smear purified gold leaves with a hundredth part.
He should calcine this with a <s>puṭa</s> heating; it becomes like an indragopa insect.

children.text: saṃsparśād vedhayet sarvam idaṃ hema mṛtaṃ priye
children.translated_text: By touch this calcined gold pierces everything, O dear one.
He should combine three parts of the lordly <s>sūta</s> together with that very substance.
When it is placed in the middle of a crucible, he should digest it again with that very substance.
It becomes smoke-piercing, O <s>Devī</s>, when it has been extended again and again.
If, by this ordered procedure, the threefold chain has been digested,
it pierces mountains, stones, and the surface of the earth; there is no doubt here.

children.text: pārśve jyotiḥ pradṛśyeta ūrdhvaṃ dṛśyeta tena vai
children.translated_text: A light is seen at its side, and above it is seen by means of that.

children.text: bhūcaraṃ taṃ vijānīyād rasendraṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Know that <s>rasendra</s> to be earth-roaming; there is no doubt here.
By means of it, O <s>Devī</s>, one would travel a hundred <s>yojana</s>s without fatigue.
He would have divine brilliance, a great body, divine sight, and great strength.
Freed from all diseases, he would live as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
His urine and feces pierce all metals.

children.text: samajīrṇena vajreṇa hemnā ca sahitena ca
children.translated_text: With diamond that has been digested in equal measure, and together with gold,
he should digest the metals while it is in the fire; the <s>sūtaka</s> comes to fixation.
He should perform <s>sāraṇa</s> with that <s>bīja</s>; it pierces even a thousandfold.
After it has been subjected to <s>sāraṇa</s>, he should digest it afterward; it is to be smeared and projected a thousandfold.
He should perform <s>sāraṇa</s> with that <s>bīja</s>; he obtains hundred-thousandfold piercing.
By this ordered procedure the <s>rasa</s> becomes crore-piercing.

children.text: kevalaṃ tu yadā vajraṃ samajīrṇaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: But when he causes only diamond to be digested in equal measure,
then the <s>sūta</s> should be known as bound, motionless, and free from disturbance.

children.text: agnistho jāyate sūtaḥ śalākāṃ grasate kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Placed in the fire, the <s>sūta</s> arises and swallows a rod in an instant.
Blown by a forced fire, it consumes everything with eagerness.
It consumes and digests; the <s>sūta</s> bestows longevity and substances.

children.text: mūṣāsthaṃ dhamayet sūtaṃ haṭhāgnau naiva kampayet ||
children.translated_text: He should blow the <s>sūta</s> in the crucible in a forced fire; it does not tremble.
He should digest all the gems; when bound, it leads to sky-going power.
When the eight metals, multiplied eightfold, have been digested, fixation of <s>rasa</s> occurs.
All the metals should be threefold, and gold likewise threefold.
At the sight of smoke it is piercing, and it becomes sky-like, giving liberation.
At first, eight times the essence of mica should be digested in the great <s>rasa</s>.
Together with gold equal to a tenth part, he should digest diamond and gems.

children.text: samaṃ ca jārayed vajraṃ tadāsau khecaro rasaḥ
children.translated_text: And he should digest diamond in equal amount; then that <s>rasa</s> is sky-going.
In sequence it becomes right-turning and crore-piercing.

children.text: same tu pannage jīrṇe daśavedhī bhavedrasaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>pannaga</s> (lead) equal in amount has been digested, the <s>rasa</s> becomes ten-piercing.

children.text: dviguṇe śatavedhī syāt sahasraṃ triguṇe bhavet ||
children.translated_text: With double the amount it becomes hundred-piercing; with triple it becomes thousand-piercing.
With quadruple it becomes ten-thousand-piercing, O <s>Devī</s>; he should increase it by this sequence.
By successive increase he should digest the <s>pannaga</s> there.
Crooked <s>pannaga</s> should be digested according to the sequence of nine numbers.
Having added it in sequence, O <s>Deveśī</s>, the <s>rasa</s> becomes crore-piercing.
When sulfur and the first mineral substances have reached digestion at sixfold amount,

children.text: rogahartā rasaḥ syāttu samukhe tavadā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the <s>rasa</s> becomes a remover of disease, and then it becomes possessed of a mouth.
When a hundredfold amount has been digested in it, it removes disease, old age, and death.
It consumes essences of mica and the other minerals equal to itself.

children.text: rugjarā maraṇaṃ jitvā śatavedhī raso bhavet
children.translated_text: Having conquered disease, old age, and death, the <s>rasa</s> becomes hundred-piercing.
When double the amount has been digested, the <s>sūta</s> grants a hundred-year life and becomes thousand-piercing.
At fourfold amount, <s>pārada</s> (mercury) gives a thousand-year life and becomes ten-thousand-piercing.
When the <s>rasa</s> has digested eightfold amount, it gives a hundred-thousand-year life and becomes hundred-thousand-piercing.
At sixteenfold amount it gives the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s> and becomes crore-piercing.
When thirty-twofold amount has been digested, it grants sky-going power and the other siddhis.
<s>Pārada</s>, piercing by touch, gives the lifespan and strength of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
When it has digested sixty-four times its amount, it is called <s>Śivāyuḥ</s>, piercing even by sound.
All the defects of <s>rasa</s>, however,

children.text: jīrṇena nāśam āyānti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: are destroyed by mica that has been digested sixfold; no deliberation is needed here.

children.text: tadā grasati lohāni tyajecca gatim ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then it consumes metals and gives up its own mobility.
Smoke, a crackling sound, and a frog-like leap,
trembling and violent shaking: these are the five states of <s>rasa</s>.
When equally digested it is a child; when fourfold, it stands in youth.
When digested sixfold it is old, auspicious, and able to perform every operation.
First he should digest sulfur, and after that all the essences.

children.text: tataḥ sarvāṇi lohāni dvandvāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Then he should digest all metals, various paired substances,
cooked <s>bīja</s>s, jewels, and liquefied essences.
The first is at a sixty-fourth part, the second at a thirty-second part,
the third at a sixteenth part, and the fourth at an eighth part.
Then the fifth is declared at a quarter part, and the sixth at a half part.

children.text: śatāṃśe saptamo jñeyo grāsamānaṃ rasasya tu ||
children.translated_text: The seventh is to be known at a hundredth part: this is the measure of the mouthful for <s>rasa</s>.
With a mouthful of a sixty-fourth part, the <s>rasa</s> becomes staff-bearing.
In the second application of the mouthful, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>, it has the appearance of a leech.

children.text: grāse rasāt tṛtīye ca kākaviṣṭhāsamo bhavet
children.translated_text: At the third mouthful from the <s>rasa</s>, it becomes like crow droppings.
The fourth is spherical in form; at the fifth it has the radiance of fire.
At the sixth, <s>sūta</s> has the radiance of the sun, and at the seventh it is a mass of brilliance.
O goddess, these are the signs, in order, of the digested king of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: samāṃśaṃ dviguṇaṃ grāsaṃ tataḥ sūte caturguṇam
children.translated_text: He should digest in <s>sūta</s> an equal mouthful, then a double one, and then a fourfold one,
and likewise, O goddess, an eightfold one and a sixteenfold one.
O goddess, then thirty-twofold and sixty-fourfold in sequence.

children.text: tīvratvaṃ janayet svedād amalatvaṃ ca mardanāt ||
children.translated_text: Through sweating he produces sharpness, and through grinding, stainlessness.
Through stupefaction comes freedom from defects; through raising, the destruction of foulness.
Through distillation it becomes a <s>rasāyana</s>; through restraint there is replenishment.
Through regulation comes steadiness; through kindling it burns with its mouth open.
Through impregnation comes suitability for compounding; through moving it gains strength and activity.
Through digestion comes proper fixation, and through the two liquefactions, unity.
Through coloring it becomes red, and through the three <s>sāraṇā</s>s, pervasive.
Through penetration it gains penetrating power, even into bodies and metals by piercing.
Having bowed her head to <s>Śambhu</s>, the daughter of <s>Girijā</s> asked:
Śrī <s>Bhairavī</s> said:
Lord, earlier you briefly taught bodily piercing.

children.text: taṃ dehavedham ācakṣva samyak jānāmyahaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Teach that bodily piercing so that I may know it completely.
Śrī <s>Bhairava</s> said:
O goddess, I shall teach what is difficult even for the gods to obtain:
bodily piercing for yogins endowed with enjoyment, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
He should carry out cooking and the rest according to the prescription of the five procedures.
He should purify, in sequence, the defects aggravated by salt and the like.

children.text: tato jīrṇarasaṃ cādyāt kramād evaṃ sureśvari ||
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>, he should take digested <s>rasa</s> in just this sequence.
Keeping to light food by day, he should take kṣudra, dhānyaka, and nāgara.
These three, each measured by one <s>pala</s>, he should stir into water.
Having boiled it until an eighth remains, he should drink it every night for three days.
Immediately afterward he should drink a decoction of varā in the same way for three days.

children.text: iti pācanam ātanyād atha snehanam ācaret
children.translated_text: Thus he should extend the cooking treatment; then he should perform oleation.
By day he should eat rice with ghee and goat broth in a measured amount.

children.text: ājyānnaṃ vā mudgarasaṃ laghvāśī syāddine sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: Or the wise man should eat lightly by day, taking ghee-rice with mung-bean broth.
At night he should drink cow ghee mixed with rock salt.
The rock salt is one <s>niṣka</s>, and the ghee is four <s>niṣka</s>s.
He should anoint his whole body with bhṛṅgāmalaka oil.

children.text: evaṃ saptadinaṃ kuryāt snehanaṃ paramaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: He should do oleation in this way for seven days; it is supremely beneficial.
Fish, meat, māṣa beans, sesame, barley, goat products, amala, and parched grain,
all this should amount to one <s>prastha</s>; ekāṣṭhīlā, aguru, and balā,
rāsnā, vyāghrī, ghana-patra, kauśika, ativiṣā, and niśā,
all these should be two <s>pala</s>s each; buttermilk, milk, water, and sour gruel

children.text: dvyāḍhake nikṣipet sarvaṃ mṛtpātre kvāthayet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: should all be placed in two <s>āḍhaka</s>s, and the wise man should boil them in an earthen pot.
With its steam he should make the body sweat for the duration of two <s>ghaṭikā</s>s.

children.text: evaṃ saptadinaṃ kuryāt svedanaṃ paramaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: He should perform sweating in this way for seven days; it is supremely beneficial.

children.text: madanasya phalaṃ caikaṃ pāṭhā ṣoḍaśikaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: One fruit of madana, pāṭhā, and water in sixteenfold measure
should be boiled until a quarter remains; in that water, strained through cloth,
he should add pippalī, indrayava, yaṣṭi, and salt, each in the measure of a <s>karṣa</s>.

children.text: nikṣipecca pibet prātar vāntiḥ syāt sarvarogahā ||
children.translated_text: He should drink it in the morning; vomiting will occur, removing all disease.
<s>Sūta</s>, borax, sulfur-stone, <s>trikaṭu</s>, and <s>triphala</s>, in equal amounts,

children.text: etaiḥ samaṃ tu jepālaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ tat parimardayet ||
children.translated_text: and jayapāla equal to these, he should grind very finely.
He should eat two <s>guñjā</s>s in measure together with jaggery.
This is taught as purgation, the destroyer of all diseases.
Thus the five procedures have been explained; after purgation he should proceed in order.
He should drink ketakī-stana and jambīra, one <s>kuḍuva</s> each day,
every morning for seven days; it removes the salt defect.
Into sixteen <s>pala</s>s of water he should put one <s>pala</s> of <s>triphala</s>.

children.text: kvāthayet pādaśeṣaṃ tat tasmin śīte madhoḥ palam
children.translated_text: He should boil it until a quarter remains; when it is cool, he should add one <s>pala</s> of honey.
He should drink it in the morning for three days; it is the supreme remover of the alkali defect.
Viḍaṅga with vacā and kuṣṭha, combined with ketakī-stana,
when decocted and drunk for three days, removes the sour defect; he should drink it.
Alternatively, he may take one <s>pala</s> of tamarind-alkali water,
combine it with one <s>karṣa</s> of yavakṣāra and sugar, and drink it for three days.
This destruction of the acid disorder has been described in the <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative treatment).
One karṣa each of vacā, biḍāla, seeds of palāśa, and the worm-killing drug should be taken.

children.text: karṣaṃ guḍaṃ ca tat sarvaṃ bhakṣayed uṣṇavāri ca
children.translated_text: Together with one karṣa of jaggery, one should eat all that and drink hot water.
If one drinks it in the morning for three days, it causes the worms to fall out.
Śyāmā, vahni, viḍaṅga, vāśā, the three pungents, and the three fruits,

children.text: saindhavaṃ devadāruṃ ca mustā caitatsamaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: together with rock salt, devadāru, and mustā, should all be in equal portions.

children.text: ghṛtaiḥ karṣaṃ lihet prātaḥ saptāhāt sarvarogajit
children.translated_text: One should lick a karṣa of this with ghee in the morning; within a week it conquers every disease.
Having thus purified the body, one should eat rice of the śāli variety with milk.
When proper strength has arisen, then one should undertake the <s>rasāyana</s>.
With milk, ghee, juice of āmalaka, and honey, the oil produced from the divine tree

children.text: tailaṃ nirmathya tatsarvaṃ dvipalaṃ pratyahaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: should be churned; one should drink two palas of all that every day.

children.text: māsena kāntirmedhā ca bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a month, beauty and intelligence certainly arise; there is no doubt.
In the second month he should drink the substance just described in a dose of four palas.
By that, the doṣas and disorders arising in the eyes are pacified.
Again, in the third month, a measure of six palas should be taken.
By that he becomes one whose body is like that of an immortal, and he certainly becomes very radiant.
Now <s>āroṭa-rasa</s> should be taken in sequence, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
It is made from iron, copper, mica, and tāpya, successively sublimed and calcined.
This is <s>āroṭaka-rasa</s>, supreme and productive of perfection of the body.
The <s>rasa</s> (mercurial preparation), processed by the seven operations beginning with sweating,

children.text: mūrchito rañjito devi sūtas tvāroṭakaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: stupefied and colored, O <s>Devī</s>, is remembered as <s>sūta</s> called <s>āroṭaka</s>.
It is best in <s>rasāyana</s> and in the pacification of disease, and it bestows every virtue.
Magnetite essence, mica essence, and āroṭa, in equal quantity, measured to two guñjās,
should be used for one month together with honey, ghee, and triphalā.
Thus it should be taken gradually, in the sequence of two, three, four, five, and six,
and so, up to the end of sixteen months, in a measure of sixteen guñjās.
One should do this with <s>āroṭaka-rasa</s> in this way, O beloved of my life.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, he lives for a hundred autumns.
Magnetite essence, mica essence, and <s>rasa</s> in which gold has been digested
should all be made equal, and one should likewise use the <s>āroṭaka</s>.
This is the preparation of the field, and it brings a lifespan of a thousand years.

children.text: abhūmau yojitaḥ sūto na prarohati kutracit ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> (mercury) applied on unprepared ground never sprouts anywhere.
Therefore, if someone applies <s>sūtaka</s> without first preparing the field,
his auspicious result will not sprout, like a seed in saline soil.
I shall now explain in due order the excellent procedure for the previously described <s>sūta</s> bound as a khoṭa,
as well as the <s>krāmaṇa</s> procedure, and the prescriptions and prohibitions.
Listen carefully, O <s>Pārvatī</s>; out of love for you I shall explain it.
Magnetite, mica, gold, and diamond are the supreme <s>krāmaṇa</s> agents for <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: krāmaṇena vinā sūto na sidhyed dehalohayoḥ
children.translated_text: Without <s>krāmaṇa</s>, <s>sūta</s> is not perfected for either the body or metals.
A guñjā-measure, bound as a khoṭa and combined with the honey of <s>krāmaṇa</s>,

children.text: māsamekaṃ bhajed itthaṃ punar vidhikrameṇa vai
children.translated_text: should be taken for one month in this way, and again according to the prescribed sequence,
up to the completion of sixteen months, just like the <s>āroṭa-rasa</s>.
He attains a lifespan of a hundred years, free from all diseases.
Through use of a pala-measure, he is not overpowered by illnesses.

children.text: dvitīye śukravṛddhiḥ syāt tṛtīye balavān bhavet
children.translated_text: In the second month there is increase of semen; in the third he becomes strong.

children.text: caturthe palitaṃ hanti valiṃ jayati pañcame ||
children.translated_text: In the fourth it destroys gray hair, and in the fifth it conquers wrinkles.
In the sixth he retains what he hears and becomes eloquent; in the seventh it removes eye disease.
In the eighth he gains eagle-like sight, with the lifespan and prowess of <s>Brahmā</s>.
If he uses nine palas, he becomes one who obtains union with siddhi.
If he uses ten palas, he becomes a second <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
A man should use a māṣa-measure of <s>sūta</s> that grants a thousand-year lifespan.
He should use a barley-grain measure of <s>sūta</s> that grants a lifespan of ten thousand years, O dear one.
The wise man should use a rice-grain measure of <s>sūta</s> that grants a lifespan of a hundred thousand years.
For a ten-million-year lifespan, he should take <s>sūta</s>, eating a mung-bean measure.

children.text: etat sarvaṃ rasānāṃ tu krāmaṇaṃ pūrvavad bhavet
children.translated_text: All this, for the <s>rasas</s>, should have <s>krāmaṇa</s> as before.
<s>Sūta</s> bestowing a thousand-year life confers the state of <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> producing a ten-thousand-year lifespan also grants the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> producing a hundred-thousand-year lifespan brings about the state of <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> bestowing a ten-million-year lifespan confers the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
But <s>sūta</s> digested with mākṣīka gives the state of <s>Dhanada</s>.
That digested with vimalā gives the state of <s>Indra</s>; that digested with mica gives the state of the sun.
That digested with copper gives the state of <s>Brahmā</s>, and that digested with silver gives the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
When digested with gold there is the state of <s>Rudra</s>; when digested with diamond, the state of the Lord.
Mercury digested with liquefied essence gives the state of <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
<s>Sūtaka</s> digested with seed gives the state whose nature is being, consciousness, and bliss.
In general, with sharp iron a man attains the state of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: evaṃ yo lohajīrṇaṃ tu bhakṣayed bhasmasūtakam
children.translated_text: Thus, if one eats ash-mercury in which metal has been digested,
with water he becomes water-formed; with earth he assumes the condition of earth.
By fire he becomes fire, O <s>Devī</s>; by wind he possesses the form of wind.
He himself is directly a creator and destroyer, able to make curses and blessings.
Wherever the practitioner leaves urine and feces,

children.text: pāṣāṇaṃ mṛṇmayaṃ tatra spṛṣṭaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: stone and clay there, when touched, become gold.

children.text: prasvedāt tasya gātrasya lohānyaṣṭau ca vedhayet
children.translated_text: From the sweat of his body he can pierce the eight metals.

children.text: tatsarvaṃ kanakaṃ divyaṃ bhakṣite dvādaśe pale ||
children.translated_text: All that becomes divine gold when the twelfth pala has been consumed.
Alternatively, he should eat ash-mercury digested with silver.

children.text: śulbāraṃ vaṅgaghoṣaṃ ca tatsvedāt tāratā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Copper, bronze, tin, and bell-metal become silver through his sweat.
Alternatively, he should eat ash-mercury digested with sharp iron.

children.text: mūtreṇa tasya spṛṣṭaṃ tu vaṅgaṃ vrajati tāratām ||
children.translated_text: But tin touched by his urine goes to the state of silver.
With each sprinkling there is fixation of both lead and tin.

children.text: guñjāmātraṃ rasaṃ devi hemajīrṇaṃ tu bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: O goddess, one should eat <s>rasa</s> (mercury), digested with gold, in the measure of one <s>guñjā</s>.
Two <s>guñjās</s> of that digested with silver, and three of that digested with <s>ravi</s> (copper).
There may be one <s>māṣa</s> of that digested with sharp iron, mica, and lodestone, or else one or two <s>guñjās</s>.
But one should eat that digested with diamond and <s>vaikrānta</s> in a mustard-seed measure.
It may be combined with lead, tin, fat, insects, poisons, and secondary poisons.

children.text: mūtrayuktaṃ haṭhād baddhaṃ tyajet kalkaṃ rasāyane
children.translated_text: Mixed with urine and forcefully bound, one should avoid the paste in <s>rasāyana</s>.
That which has arisen through the entry of gold and silver and has gradually become able to withstand fire,
that bound king of <s>rasa</s> becomes a giver of bodily perfection.
Diamond, iron, lodestone, pyrite, <s>vaikrānta</s>, mica, and gold:
<s>rasa</s> digested with these, according to availability, is praised in <s>rasāyana</s>.
The six secondary minerals too are precisely for eating in <s>rasāyana</s>.
One should eat one <s>pala</s> of ash digested with sharp iron.
He lives for ten thousand years, with a body like diamond.
In this way one should eat twelve <s>palas</s> of that digested with sharp iron.
Living thus for a great aeon, he reaches <s>Śiva</s> at the end of dissolution.
With one <s>pala</s> of ash digested with copper, one obtains the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.
With two <s>palas</s> one obtains the lifespan of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and with three <s>palas</s> the lifespan of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: caturthe tu pale devi śivatvaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ
children.translated_text: With the fourth <s>pala</s>, O goddess, a man obtains the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
When three <s>palas</s> of ash-mercury digested with gold have been eaten gradually,
eighty-eight thousand <s>yoginīs</s>, intoxicated and proud,
stand as his attendants; the man becomes able to assume any form at will.

children.text: yad yad bhāvayate rūpaṃ tattadrūpadharo bhavet
children.translated_text: Whatever form he imagines, he becomes the bearer of that very form.
Wherever they dissolve, the attainment dissolves there itself.
When gold ash, measured out in twelve <s>palas</s>, has been eaten,
O mistress of gods, one should know one's own power of digestion and take only a single <s>guñjā</s> measure.

children.text: ghṛtena madhunā cādyāt tāmbūlaṃ kāminīṃ bhajet
children.translated_text: One should eat it with ghee and honey, chew betel, and enjoy a woman.

children.text: eko hi doṣaḥ sūkṣmo'pi bhakṣite bhasmasūtake ||
children.translated_text: There is indeed one fault, even though subtle, when ash-mercury is eaten:
within three weeks, O fair-hipped one, a man becomes blinded by desire.
He can excite a thousand women in the course of a day.
Through union with women, O fair-hipped one, the <s>sūtaka</s> (mercurial preparation) penetrates the body.

children.text: nārīsaṅgād vinā devi hyajīrṇaṃ tasya jīryate ||
children.translated_text: Without union with a woman, O goddess, what is undigested in him becomes digested.
If the semen is stirred by intercourse and made to descend for three weeks,
a danger to life arises; therefore he should avoid intercourse for that long.
Conversation with a young woman should be undertaken, and massage of the limbs by a young woman.
By her mere touch, the <s>rasa</s> penetrates the body.
Just as the sight of a beautiful woman gladdens him in every way,

children.text: tathā krāmati deveśi sūtako'sau tataḥ kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: so, O mistress of gods, that <s>sūtaka</s> penetrates at once.
When her receptacle is like an aśvattha leaf, even, and auspicious,

children.text: tādṛśastu bhago devi bhājane tu rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: such a vulva, O goddess, is a vessel in <s>rasāyana</s>.
But a vulva that is fleshless, long, and marked by dry veins,
as a maker of suffering and poverty, should be avoided in <s>rasāyana</s>.
In the bright fortnight, on an auspicious day, endowed with the strength of moon and stars,
at a good muhūrta, the twice-born man should contemplate <s>Śiva</s>, fire, Brahmins, and the guru.

children.text: saṃtuṣṭaḥ sumanā bhūtvā rasaṃ seveta siddhidam
children.translated_text: Satisfied and well-minded, he should consume the <s>rasa</s> that grants accomplishment.
With milk, gold, and dry ginger, nasal administration is the best <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetrative assimilation).
Collyrium made from gold and the other six metals is the supreme <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
After this I shall explain what is beneficial and harmful for the consumption of <s>rasa</s>.
Red śāli rice, wheat, cow's milk, ghee, and curds,

children.text: jāṅgalaṃ palalaṃ mudgaṃ śarkarā madhu saindhavam ||
children.translated_text: meat of wild animals, mung beans, sugar, honey, and rock salt,
<s>haṃsodaka</s> water, <s>vāstuka</s>, <s>meghanāda</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
pointed gourd, bottle gourd, banana, coriander, sugarcane, and pomegranate,
coconut water and dry ginger, and always chewing betel,
fragrant essence, saffron, and musk should be applied as ointment.
Fragrant fine flowers, a soft bed, and desired women,
discourse on the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s> and the self, gentle speech, and a comfortable seat,
divine pure garments, shade, and a little walking about,
recitation of <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s>, joy, a gentle smile, and purity,
watching dance, hearing song, and worship of <s>Śiva</s>,
saluting gods, fire, guru, and Brahmins, and observing the <s>śruti</s>,
concentration, compassion for living beings, truthful speech, and what is beneficial and pleasant,
and activity of speech, body, and mind that prevents suffering:
all this has been taught as the <s>krāmaṇa</s> of lord mercury, dear one.
I shall tell what is harmful for the consumption of <s>rasa</s>; listen, dear one.
Overeating, excessive drinking, oversleeping, and excessive waking,
eating at the wrong time, excessive association with women, and also lack of companionship,
intoxication and laughter in improper places, elation, anger, and excessive craving,
much chatter, playing in water, sorrow, and extreme brooding,

children.text: kaliṅgaṃ kāravellaṃ ca kūṣmāṇḍaḥ karkaṭī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>kaliṅga</s>, bitter gourd, ash gourd, and cucumber,

children.text: kākamācī kulatthaṃ ca kārkoṭī ca kusumbhikā ||
children.translated_text: black nightshade, horse gram, <s>kārkoṭī</s>, and <s>kusumbhikā</s>,
sesame, linseed oil, black gram, pigeon, and lentils,
rice with buttermilk, sour gruel, and what is bitter, pungent, sour, or salty,

children.text: kṣāraṃ kṣaudraṃ picchilaṃ ca pittalaṃ ca parūṣakam
children.translated_text: alkali, honey, what is slimy, what is bilious, and <s>parūṣaka</s>,
buffalo-milk products, <s>vidara</s>, and mango,
orange, bilva, breadfruit, moringa, and eating consecrated offerings,
touching fire with the feet, and striking cows or Brahmins,
and striking maidens, children, horses, animals, and the like.

children.text: pātakaṃ prāṇihiṃsā ca chedanaṃ bhūruhām api ||
children.translated_text: Sin, harming living beings, and even the cutting of trees,
the seven vices beginning with gambling, the shade of aśvattha and kapittha trees,
the <s>liṅga</s>, women, hell, cots, and likewise fear of leopards and vibhītaka trees,
passing feces and urine in a crossroads or in an excessively secluded place,
and offenses against <s>Śiva</s>, Brahmins, the guru, women, heroes, those of controlled self,
initiatory agreements, sacred tradition, bards, riverbanks, sacred waters, and men,
onions, asafoetida, garlic, mustard, and the two kinds of bṛhatī,
niṣpāva beans, overstepping restrictions, rubbing the body, night, ornaments, and pleasure,
sleep, liquor and fermented drink, the cock, and aquatic flesh,
pungent, hot, heavy, obstructive, rough, dry meat, and honey,
eating from banana leaves or bronze vessels, and exposure to heat:
these whole groups of substances are forbidden in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative alchemy).
If one should take them through negligence, derangement arises at once.

children.text: rasājīrṇe bhavetkānte śoṣo mūrcchā bhramo jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>rasa</s> is undigested, O lovely one, wasting, fainting, dizziness, and fever occur,
fatigue, trembling, retention of feces and urine, colic, and shivering,
sleeplessness, lethargy, hiccup, cough, dyspnea, and yawning,
loss of appetite and diarrhea, stiffness of the organ, and, in the eyes and belly,
in the chest, ears, abdomen, feet, penis, head, and joints,
burning, breaking pain of the limbs, and all other diseases indeed arise.
For the calming of undigested <s>rasa</s>, this formula is now told by me:
rājakośātakī, puṅkhā, garuḍī, and kāravallikā,
kārkoṭī, kākamācī, devadālī, and parājitā,
all these, one pala each, should be boiled in four palas of cow urine.
When one quarter remains, one karṣa of clear rock salt should be added.

children.text: nikṣipet tat pibet kvāthaṃ rasājīrṇe hitaṃkaram ||
children.translated_text: One should drink that decoction; it is beneficial in undigested <s>rasa</s>.
In three days one becomes well, and the <s>rasa</s> begins to move in its course.
When the <s>rasa</s> pains any particular limb, that limb should be thoroughly massaged,

children.text: vā stanena ca tanvaṅgyā nirvyathaḥ kramate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: or with the breast of a slender woman; free from pain, the <s>rasa</s> proceeds.
The piercing of the skin is first, O goddess; the piercing of blood is second.
The third is the piercing of flesh, and the fourth is the piercing of fat.
The fifth is the piercing of bone; the sixth is of the nature of marrow.
The seventh is the piercing of semen, and the piercing of the channels is likewise eighth.
The ninth is the piercing of the eye, and the tenth pierces everything.
By piercing with <s>rasa</s>, snake-metal becomes gold; by piercing blood,

children.text: trapu svarṇaṃ bhavenmāṃsavedhāt tīkṣṇaṃ ca kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: tin becomes gold, and by piercing flesh, sharp iron becomes gold.
By piercing fat, copper becomes gold, and by piercing bone,
silver becomes gold; by piercing marrow, metals become gold.
By piercing semen, even an earthen pot becomes gold, O dear one.
Mercury that has digested diamond pierces semen; mercury digested with mica and marrow,
and mercury that has digested gold pierces bone; mercury that has digested silver, O dear one,
pierces fat; mercury that has digested tāpya pierces flesh.
Mercury that has digested copper pierces blood; mercury whose nature is rasa has digested magnetite.
When bound with sharp iron it is bluish; with copper it is red and lustrous.
With silver it resembles the moon; with gold it is golden in brilliance.
Held in the mouth as one who sees smoke, within a month it leads to sky-going.
Held in the mouth, it pierces by touch and grants accomplishment in two months.
In three months it makes a hundred crores; in four, ten crores.
In five months it pierces a crore, and in eight months ten thousand.
In nine months it pierces a thousand, and in the tenth month, a hundred.
By his urine and feces, and likewise by his phlegm and bodily impurities,
through smearing, those metals on the earth come to the state of gold.
In the eleventh month it pierces to the sixty-fourth part;

children.text: dvātriṃśakavedhī tu varṣād dehaṃ tu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: after a year it pierces thirty-twofold and pierces the body.
Freed from all diseases and devoid of wrinkles and gray hair,

children.text: nāsau chidyeta śastraiśca pāvakena na dahyate ||
children.translated_text: he cannot be cut by weapons, nor is he burned by fire.
Swift as the wind, of great brilliance, like another <s>Kāmadeva</s>,
at will he becomes visible, and also becomes invisible.
By the mere touch of one whose contact turns all metals into gold,
when, in that terrible single ocean, the moving and unmoving world is destroyed,
where the gods dissolve, the siddha dissolves there alone.
Formerly, on the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, in a cavern, the Daughter of the Mountain and the Lord
remained for a long time in play, each desiring to conquer the other.
Then a great flow of seed in the form of <s>sūta</s> arose from them.
By the power of that flow, stones became pierced.
Rubies and other gems, metals such as gold,
stones such as sulfur, divine herbs, and vines,
of many colors and many kinds, became bestowers of many accomplishments.
Among all those previously mentioned, diamond is the greatest and most excellent.
Its class-characteristics, O goddess, its processing, worship, and result

children.text: kramādvakṣyāmi te devi sāvadhānaṃ śṛṇu priye ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell you in order, O goddess; listen attentively, dear one.
Brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, in order,
are white, red, yellow, black, and also of many kinds.
Female, male, and neuter diamonds should also be known in order, dear one.
Those that are white, complete in facets, luminous, and very large,
are to be recognized as male, without lines, seeds, or holes.
They are strong, endowed with substance, and causes of the movement of metals.
They quickly bring about the binding of <s>rasa</s> and bestow accomplishments upon all.
The stout ones are indeed makers of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation), bestowers of the eight <s>siddhi</s>s.
Those women, it is taught, are brilliant with six-cornered seed-lines.
They generate bodily radiance and grant enjoyment, beauty, and happiness.
The long, triangular, and slender ones should be understood as neuter.
They are weak in essence, of little potency, and suitable for <s>krāmaṇa</s>, O queen of the gods.

children.text: klībā napuṃsake strīṇāṃ striyaḥ sarvahitā narāḥ
children.translated_text: Neuter ones are for neuters, female ones for women; male ones are beneficial for all.
According to their class they produce vigor; as is their inner strength, so is their quality.
As is their brilliance, so is their character; thus do the twice-born kinds act.
The Brahmin types remove wrinkles, grey hair, and disease; the Kṣatriya types take away death.
The Vaiśya types make the body firm and effect the piercing of metals.
The Śūdra types arrest age and destroy many diseases.
Now I shall tell the purification of diamond; listen, my dear.
Śyāmā, śamī, meghanāda, varṣābhū, dhūrtakodrava,
meṣaśṛṅgī, ākhukarṇī, kuluttha, and amlavetasa,
madana, agastya, and nirguṇḍī: with the fresh juices of these
one should cook it for a day in a swing apparatus, placed inside a vyāghrī tuber.
After removing it, one should smear it with buffalo dung and burn it in a fire of dung-cakes.
At night one should burn it for four watches, and at the end of the night sprinkle it
with horse urine, snuhī latex, and kuluttha decoction likewise.
One should cook, burn, and sprinkle it in this way seven times.
Thus the varieties belonging to the twice-born classes, when purified, become bestowers of accomplishment.
I shall teach diamond ash fit for <s>rasāyana</s>, O queen of the gods.
Vaikrānta, tāpya, gandhāśma, śilā, mākṣika, and tālaka,
kānta, āsyataṅkaṇa, alkali, and crab bones should be ground.

children.text: stanyena golake kṣiptvā mūṣāyāṃ nikṣipet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: With breast milk, having put them into a pellet, one should then place it in a crucible.
First one should blow it very strongly, and afterward cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> (large pit-firing).
Taking that same diamond, in a sixteen-part measure of it,
one should add one part mercury, digested with cooked seed.

children.text: stanyena mardayettau dvau punar gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: One should grind those two with breast milk and again cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
In this way, after sixteen firings, it is joined with mercury in which the seed has been digested.
One should make that diamond firm; it becomes an ash that is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
Listen, O <s>Rudrāṇī</s>; I shall teach the divine diamond <s>rasāyana</s>.
As stated before, one should perform the procedure beginning with purification of the body.
Under an auspicious lunar mansion and good hour, when the moon and stars are strong,
one should first worship <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Agni</s>, the guru, cows, Brahmins, and the physician.
Then, fair-faced one, one should consume that ash in the measure of a barley grain.
Kānta-sattva, mica-sattva, and gold ash, each in the measure of one <s>guñjā</s>,
with <s>triphala</s>, honey, and ghee, one whose body is purified should lick in the morning.
Thus, up to the end of sixteen months, one, two, three, and four,
increasing month by month up to sixteen barley-grain measures,
and the triad of ashes beginning with kānta should likewise be increased by <s>guñjā</s> measures.
There should be two <s>niṣka</s>s of <s>triphala</s> powder, and ghee and honey as desired.
My beloved, one should perform the regimen and avoidances as previously stated.

children.text: sevitaṃ palamātraṃ tu vajrabhasma dinaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: When diamond ash has been consumed gradually to the measure of one <s>pala</s>,
it destroys wrinkles, grey hair, and disease, and grants a life of one hundred years.

children.text: dvipalaṃ ca sahasrāyur ayutaṃ tripalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Two <s>pala</s>s give a thousand-year life, and three <s>pala</s>s a life of ten thousand.
Four <s>pala</s>s give a life of one hundred thousand; the fifth gives a million.
Six <s>pala</s>s give a life of ten million years, and the seventh the lifespan of <s>Surendra</s>.
Eight <s>pala</s>s give the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>; the ninth <s>pala</s> gives the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: rudratvaṃ daśamaṃ devi īśvaratvaṃ tataḥ param
children.translated_text: The tenth gives the state of <s>Rudra</s>, O goddess, and beyond that the state of <s>Īśvara</s>.
At the twelfth, diamond ash fully grants the state of <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
It also grants omniscience, omnipresence, and wandering according to one's own will.
I shall explain <s>vajraudana</s>, supremely beneficial for <s>rasāyana</s>.
With diamond purified as before, one should undertake the softening process.
It should be set in the middle of mātṛvāhaka and wrapped in partridge meat.
Then it should be wrapped again with the juices of sharp substances, kānta, and ānana.
One should cook it separately for three days in kulattha, <s>triphala</s> water, and kodrava.
Thus cooked, that diamond should be wrapped with leaves
of betel vine grown for three years, or of the cotton plant.
Bound up and kept between the knees, the diamond becomes soft in two watches.
This is called <s>vajraudana</s>; now the liquefaction of diamond is taught.
Trikṣāra, sour chickpea preparation, rāmaṭha, and amlavetasa,
jvālāmukhī and ikṣuraka, together with the juice of sthalakumbhī,

children.text: piṣṭvā snuhyarkayoḥ kṣīrais tadgole mṛdu hīrakam
children.translated_text: should be ground with the milks of snuhī and arka; into that pellet one should put the softened diamond.
Then one should place it in a jambīra fruit and cook it for three days in a swing apparatus.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte hīrakasya drutir bhavati sūtavat
children.translated_text: When this is done, the liquefaction of diamond comes about like mercury.
When the same is done, liquefaction also comes about for gems such as padmarāga.
Mica and other stones certainly melt when this is done.
The rasa-gems melt, and so does pearl with amlavetasa.
One should steep it for seven days in the heat, and then place it in a jambīra fruit.
