Kept in a heap of grain for twenty-one days, it melts completely in a covered firing.
As with diamond ash, so too in the case of liquefaction and softening,
it becomes ash, O fair-hipped one, conquering old age, poverty, and death.
In <s>rasāyana</s>, happiness arises from ash, liquefaction, and softening.

children.text: rasāyane tu strīpuṃsau krāmaṇe tu napuṃsakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For <s>rasāyana</s> one uses the female and male; for <s>krāmaṇa</s>, the neuter.
It has the six tastes, is cooling in potency, and destroys every disease.
It pacifies all doṣas and is a <s>rasāyana</s> giving every happiness.

children.text: vidyutprabhāṃ dehadārḍhyaṃ svacchaṃ snigdhaṃ ca lekhanam
children.translated_text: It gives a lightning-like radiance, firmness of body, purity, unctuousness, and a scraping action,
beauty, strength, long life, and the destruction of planetary affliction and misfortune.
The purification, softening, liquefaction, and ash-making of <s>vaikrānta</s> are like those for diamond.
Now I shall teach the most excellent thing; listen to the gold <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: hemotpattiḥ purā proktā tathāpi trividhā bhavet
children.translated_text: The origin of gold was explained before; nevertheless it is of three kinds.
One comes from transmutation by <s>rasa</s>; another is born from a mine.
Another is produced from an alloy of metals; they are superior, middling, and inferior.

children.text: krameṇa pītarakte ca pītaraktaṃ ca varṇataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In order, by color, they are yellow, red, and yellow-red.
In rubbing on the touchstone, cutting, and burning, they appear saffron, white, and blood-red.

children.text: divyam evaṃvidhaṃ svarṇaṃ paṭṭakaṃ kaṇaśaḥ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Such divine gold should be made into plates and into small particles.
<s>Halinī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, <s>kandasnuhī</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>agni</s>, and <s>karañjaka</s>,
<s>dhūrtā</s>, <s>guñjā</s>, <s>iṅgudī</s>, <s>cīramūla</s>, <s>tāla</s>, and <s>aśvagandhikā</s>,
these roots, together with <s>indravāruṇī</s>, should be ground with churned sour milk.
He should smear the gold plates with them and heat them in the fire.
In urine, churned sour milk, oil, horse-gram water, and sour gruel,
and in lemon juice and the latex of <s>arka</s>, he should plunge them seven times in each.
He should smear, heat, and quench them again and again, seven times.
Ant-hill earth, soot essence, brick, salt, and red ochre
should be ground with lemon water; after smearing the sheet, he should enclose it for firing.
Four-colored mica, <s>tāpya</s>, cinnabar, orpiment, and <s>śilā</s>,
<s>kānta</s>, <s>kaṅku</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>vimala</s>, mercury, and <s>bhūlatā</s>,
should be ground with an acidic liquid, and he should make pills of one <s>niṣka</s> in measure, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.

children.text: palādūnaṃ na kartavyam adhikaṃ ca catuṣpalāt
children.translated_text: It should not be made less than one <s>pala</s>, nor more than four <s>pala</s>s.

children.text: puṭitaṃ hema śulbaṃ ca drāvayecca samīkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: He should melt calcined gold and copper, brought to an equal condition.
When that has melted, he should throw one pill after another into it.

children.text: svarṇād daśaguṇā vāhyā vaṭikāḥ śoṣitāḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: The dried pills are to be introduced in sequence, ten times as much as the gold.

children.text: yāvaccheṣaṃ bhavet svarṇaṃ tāvad evaṃ dhamecchanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Until only gold remains, he should thus blow gently with the bellows.
That becomes pure and divine, removing old age, death, and disease.

children.text: ciñcāpatranibhaṃ svarṇaṃ patraṃ śuddhaṃ ca pāradam
children.translated_text: Gold like a tamarind leaf, a sheet, and purified mercury

children.text: ekāntaṃ mardayed amlais tatpiṣṭim api lepayet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground together with acidic liquids, and he should also smear on that paste.
With equal sulfur and <s>tāpya</s>, he should heat the paste placed in a crucible.
He should put mercury ash, one sixteenth part, into the gold powder.

children.text: amlena mardayed gāḍhaṃ pacet tadbhūdhare puṭe
children.translated_text: He should grind it thoroughly with an acidic liquid and cook it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> sealed firing.
In this way, up to sixteen times, he should add <s>rasa</s> at each firing.
This non-revivable gold ash is produced, bestowing all accomplishments.
With the body purified by purgation, vomiting, and the like, on an auspicious day,
he should worship <s>Īśa</s>, brahmins, fire, teachers, and physicians foremost.
With a purified heart he should take the divine gold <s>rasāyana</s>.
The essence-ash of <s>kānta</s> and mica, in the measure of one <s>guñjā</s>,
and gold ash measured as one <s>māṣa</s>, he should combine with <s>varā</s>, honey, and ghee.
As previously stated, it is to continue up to sixteen months, like the diamond regimen.
The practitioner of <s>rasāyana</s> should perform the procedure as previously taught, while observing what is to be avoided.
Listen, O daughter of the mountain, to the wondrous regimen in the gold <s>rasāyana</s>.
By using one <s>pala</s>, a person becomes free from all diseases.
Then, by the use of two <s>pala</s>s, he is free from wrinkles and grey hair.
By three <s>pala</s>s, O beloved, perfection of speech and divine sight arise.
By the use of four <s>pala</s>s, there is no fear from poison, tigers, or snakes.
Likewise, by five <s>pala</s>s, divine knowledge of the self arises.
O goddess, by the application of six <s>pala</s>s, one reaches the state of the perfected and accomplishable.
Likewise, even by seven <s>pala</s>s, one reaches the state of a <s>vidyādhara</s>.
Likewise, by the use of eight <s>pala</s>s, one becomes adept at roaming at will.
By the ninth <s>pala</s> too, one is endowed with the qualities of the eight lordly powers.
Likewise, by ten <s>pala</s>s, one obtains the state of <s>Mahendra</s>.
By eleven <s>pala</s>s, O goddess, one reaches the state of <s>Brahmā</s>; there is no doubt here.

children.text: dvādaśabhiḥ palaiḥ kānte viṣṇutvaṃ samupaiti ca
children.translated_text: By twelve <s>pala</s>s, O beloved, one attains the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
By thirteen <s>pala</s>s too, one obtains the <s>Rudra</s> state.
Likewise, by fourteen <s>pala</s>s, one attains the <s>Īśvara</s> state.
By fifteen <s>pala</s>s, one reaches the supreme state of <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
Likewise, by sixteen <s>pala</s>s, one becomes an embodiment of being, consciousness, and bliss.

children.text: sarvajñaḥ sarvakartā ca hartā goptā sa sarvagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is omniscient and all-creating, the destroyer, the protector, and all-pervading.
I shall now explain gold liquefaction; listen, <s>Pārvatī</s>.
The fruit-dust of <s>devadālī</s>, <s>śakragopa</s>, and <s>aśvalālikā</s>,
and borax should be impregnated many times with the juice of <s>jālinī</s>, O beloved.
He should melt gold there and pour in a liquefaction equal to the mercury.

children.text: imāṃ drutiṃ kāñcanavad bhasma sevāṃ ca kalpayet
children.translated_text: This liquefaction should be prepared like gold, with its ash and regimen.

children.text: svādu tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ ca śītam uṣṇaṃ rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: It is sweet, bitter, astringent, cool, hot, and rejuvenating.

children.text: hṛdyaṃ kāntipradaṃ śuddhaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ guru lekhanam
children.translated_text: It is good for the heart, gives luster, is pure, benefits the eyes, is heavy, and has a scraping action.
It bestows steadiness, memory, long life, health, wisdom, and perfection of speech.
It destroys wasting disease, madness, and other illnesses, and it pacifies the doṣas.
It is unctuous and palatable; it kindles brilliance, produces virility, and increases strength.
Now, O beloved, I shall teach <s>kānta</s>, the <s>kānta</s> <s>rasāyana</s>.
Let there be divine medicines, bestowing all accomplishments.
Among them <s>kānta</s> is the most excellent, removing wrinkles, disease, and grey hair.
At the end of the age, <s>Śambhu</s> himself, together with <s>Śarvāṇī</s>,
performed a fierce <s>tāṇḍava</s> there; drops of sweat arose.
Wherever those drops went, they came to the state of lodestone.

children.text: jāṅgale bahavo jātā deśe sādhāraṇe kvacit
children.translated_text: Many arose in arid land, and some in an ordinary region.

children.text: jalaprāye'sti vā nāsti jātyā pañcavidhāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a watery place it may or may not exist; by class they are remembered as fivefold.

children.text: bhrāmakaṃ cumbakaṃ devi karṣakaṃ drāvakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: O goddess, they are <s>bhrāmaka</s>, <s>cumbaka</s>, <s>karṣaka</s>, and also <s>drāvaka</s>,
and likewise <s>romaka</s>; and they are one-faced, two-faced, three-faced, four-faced, or facing in every direction.

children.text: teṣāṃ pañcavidhānāṃ tu pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca śoṇitam
children.translated_text: Of those five kinds, there are yellow, black, and red,
and mixed ones; separately, their presiding deities are, in order,
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Bhūtātman</s>, and the <s>Mātṛkās</s>, as has been taught.
The yellow kind pierces by touch; the black kind is best in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative alchemy).
The red kind effects the binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury); the mixed kind removes all diseases.
The <s>romaka</s> destroys fear of the planets, and the <s>drāvaka</s> is the very best.

children.text: uttamaṃ madhyamaṃ nīcaṃ karṣakaṃ cumbakaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: The <s>karṣaka</s>, <s>cumbaka</s>, and <s>bhrāmaka</s> are, in order, superior, middling, and inferior.

children.text: bhrāmakaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vacmi lohaṃ tu bhrāmayettataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall state the mark of the <s>bhrāmaka</s>: it causes iron to whirl.
Therefore it is called <s>bhrāmaka</s>; the <s>cumbaka</s> is a magnet for iron.
The <s>karṣaka</s> draws iron, and the <s>drāvaka</s> is so called because it melts it.
Because it cracks open and produces hair-like filaments, that is called <s>romaka</s>.
The many-faced kind is most excellent; the four- or five-mouthed kind is excellent.
The two- or three-faced kind is middling, and the one-faced kind is inferior.
The <s>bhrāmaka</s> and <s>cumbaka</s> are beneficial for the destruction of all diseases.
The <s>karṣaka</s> and <s>drāvaka</s> are excellent in the application of <s>rasa</s> and in <s>rasāyana</s>.
This fivefold <s>kānta</s> (magnetite), dear one, is the goad for the elephant of <s>rasa</s>.
If it has been touched by wind and sunlight, it should never be taken.
Having dug down two hand-lengths, one should collect the <s>kānta</s>, O fair-faced one.

children.text: ādau sampūjya durgāṃ ca gaṇeśaṃ bhairavaṃ priye
children.translated_text: At the beginning, having worshipped <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and <s>Bhairava</s>, dear one,
one should burn the <s>kānta</s> with intense fire and sprinkle it with water of <s>triphala</s>.
One should grind that <s>kānta</s> to a fine powder with glass, sea salt, and borax,
with lac, guggulu, guñjā, wool, ghee, honey, and beeswax,
and with hare bone, small fish, bhallātaka, and sesame pastes,
with sarja-alkali, barley-alkali, rāla resin, and likewise <s>ciragula</s>,
and with equal parts of the horns of <s>nyaṅku</s> and <s>iribhada</s>.
Together with equal parts of these, one should grind that <s>kānta</s> with goat's milk.
One should mix it with the five buffalo-products, beginning with curds and ending with dung.

children.text: ślakṣṇaṃ piṣṭvā vaṭīḥ kuryāt karṣamātrāḥ sureśvari ||
children.translated_text: Having ground it smooth, one should make pills measuring one <s>karṣa</s>, O queen of gods.
In a furnace apparatus, in a curved tube, with khadira charcoal, firmly,

children.text: pañca pañca vaṭīstatra nikṣipecca śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should place five pills there, five at a time, slowly.
After three watches of agitation, pure essence falls from the <s>kānta</s>.
Having reduced all that to grains, with equal medicinal substances such as glass,
one should place it in a crucible and blow it with strong heat; thus it should be blown three times, dear one.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtaṃ tu tatkāntasatvaṃ sattvatamaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The essence of <s>kānta</s> prepared in this way becomes the very best essence.
When drops of oil are put in water held in a vessel of <s>kānta</s>-iron,

children.text: na sarpanti caṇāstvetāḥ kṛṣṇāḥ syur nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they do not spread, and these grains become black; there is no doubt about this.
Rubbed asafoetida has no smell, and a wave of milk takes the form of a crest.

children.text: na kadācid bhuvi patecchivā muñcati tiktatām ||
children.translated_text: It never falls to the ground, and <s>śivā</s> gives up its bitterness.
Hot water into which that metal has been cast becomes cool in an instant.
It should be no less than five <s>palas</s> and no more than fifteen <s>palas</s>.
There should be sixteen <s>palas</s> of <s>triphala</s> and four times that amount of water.
One should boil it until a quarter remains, and in that decoction dip the plates.
Having smeared them with hare's blood, one should again dry them in the sun.
When heated again, they should be put into buttermilk, oil, <s>sauvīra</s>, and ghee,
and also into honey, arka latex, citron juice, and horse-gram decoction.

children.text: lepanaṃ śoṣaṇaṃ dāhaṃ secanaṃ ca kramātpriye ||
children.translated_text: Smearing, drying, heating, and sprinkling should be done in order, dear one.
Each should be done seven times; the iron gives up the defects of the mountain ore.

children.text: ādau mantrastataḥ karma kartavyo mantra ucyate ||
children.translated_text: First comes the mantra, and then the operation should be performed; the mantra is now stated.
The word <s>udbhavodbhava</s> should take the dative ending after <s>amṛta</s>.
It ends with <s>svāhā</s>, with the <s>praṇava</s> at the beginning; this is the mantra prescribed for grinding.
The mantra is: <s>oṃ amṛtodbhavodbhavāya svāhā</s>.
For the protection of the metal and the man, this is the single-origin mantra.

children.text: vinā svāhāpadaṃ sthāne phaḍantaṃ yaḥ samuccaret ||
children.translated_text: Without the word <s>svāhā</s>, in its proper place, one should utter it ending in <s>phaṭ</s>.

children.text: oṃ amṛtodbhavāya phaṭ praṇavordhvaṃ namaścaṇḍavajrapāṇaya ityapi
children.translated_text: The formula is <s>oṃ amṛtodbhavāya phaṭ</s>; after the <s>praṇava</s> one also says <s>namaś caṇḍavajrapāṇaye</s>.
After that comes: homage to the great commander of the yakṣa army.
The word <s>suru</s> is repeated twice, and then come the words 'to the power of the great vidyā'.
Then comes <s>svāhā</s>; this mantra is taught for the rite of offering.

children.text: oṃ namaścaṇḍavajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenādhipataye namaḥ suru suru mahāvidyābalāya svāhā
children.translated_text: The mantra is: <s>oṃ namaś caṇḍavajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenādhipataye namaḥ suru suru mahāvidyābalāya svāhā</s>.
Then one should pound these iron plates into a fine powder.
Having placed the <s>kānta</s> powder in an iron vessel, one should sprinkle it with <s>triphala</s> juices.
Stirring it with an iron ladle, one should cook it.
When it has become a lump, one should take it and place it on a fine layer of clay.
One should put it properly in a sealed container in a pit sixteen fingers deep.
Having set cow-dung fuel around it, one should burn the cow-dung cakes.
One should do this for a day and night, protected from wind and sunlight.
Again in the morning, one should take it up and grind it with a decoction of <s>varā</s>.
Thus, in a pot and a sealed container, one should carry out the cooking and heating operations in order.
One should perform it in this way for seven days, and <s>hiṅgula</s> should be added to it.
One should add one sixteenth part, relative to the iron, and grind it with woman's breast milk.

children.text: sthālyāṃ pākaṃ saṃpuṭe ca puṭaṃ kurvīta ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: One should cook it in a dish and give it sixteen sealed heatings.
That becomes a non-revivifiable <s>bhasma</s> (ash), O goddess, suitable for use in <s>rasāyana</s>.
As much <s>triphala</s> as there is, the water should be four times that amount.
One should boil it down until one-eighth remains; the ghee should be equal to the decoction.
The ash of magnetite should be equal to the ghee, and it should be cooked in a copper vessel, O dear one.
Stirring it with an iron ladle until that liquid dries up,
it should be cooked over a gentle fire until then, and sugar equal in amount to the iron should be added.
This is called making it nectar-like; it is supreme, carrying every formulation.
I shall explain the cooking of iron; that is threefold, O dear one.
Soft, medium, and hard are taught: the soft is like a citron,
the medium is like a lump, and the hard is like sand.
Now I shall explain the administration of the <s>bhasma</s> of magnetite iron.
On a good lunar moment and an auspicious day, after <s>Īśa</s> and the other deities have been worshipped,
one should take the divine <s>rasāyana</s>, magnetite <s>bhasma</s>, which bestows accomplishment.
With the body purified by purgation and the like, O dear one, one should first take mica <s>bhasma</s>.
One should take it for one month; from that the body becomes purified.
There should be a māṣa-measure of magnetite <s>bhasma</s> and a guñjā-measure of mica <s>bhasma</s>,
with two niṣkas of <s>triphala</s> powder, mixed with honey and ghee.
A purified person should lick it in the morning, after acts such as bathing and giving gifts.

children.text: anupeyaṃ tato lohād gavyaṃ ṣaṣṭiguṇaṃ payaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, as the after-drink for the iron, there should be cow's milk sixty times its amount.

children.text: dhāroṣṇaṃ tadabhāve tu kṛtvā kṣīraṃ samāmbukam ||
children.translated_text: It should be warm from the stream of milking; if that is unavailable, milk should be prepared with an equal amount of water.
The milk should be boiled until the water has been exhausted, and then one should drink it as the after-drink, O dear one.
If that does not agree with one, use a decoction of <s>varā</s> or a decoction of <s>guḍūcī</s>.
Thus one should take it for one month, and then gradually for a second, third, and fourth course.
Each month there is an increase by a māṣa and a guñjā for the magnetite and mica <s>bhasma</s> respectively.
In this way, up to the end of sixteen months, the increase reaches sixteen measures.
Following the rule stated before, including the prescribed avoidances, one should perform it and will attain accomplishment.
By the one-year regimen of this, minor diseases are destroyed.
By the two-year regimen of this, great diseases are destroyed.
After three years it destroys gray hair; after four years it removes wrinkles.
In the fifth year it prevents untimely death; in the sixth there is a lifespan of one hundred years.
In the seventh year there is radiance like the sun, and in the tenth union with accomplishment.
In the eleventh year, O dear one, one attains the state of a <s>Vidyādhara</s>.
In the thirteenth year there is godhood, and in the fourteenth the status of <s>Indra</s>.
Likewise, in the fifteenth year one becomes beloved by all worlds.
In the sixteenth year the eight accomplishments arise; this is true, true, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>.
The liquefaction of magnetite is like the melting of gold, as before, O dear one.
Liquefied magnetite becomes <s>bhasma</s>, like the <s>bhasma</s> of magnetite iron.

children.text: kiṭṭaṃ muṇḍaṃ tathā tīkṣṇaṃ kāntaṃ pūrvottarottaram ||
children.translated_text: Kiṭṭa iron, muṇḍa iron, sharp iron, and magnetite are successively superior to one another.
They are endowed with qualities in order by ten, a hundred, a thousand, and a lakh.
Magnetite is more than a hundredfold superior, the <s>rasāyana</s> among medicines.
It pacifies the three doṣas, is divine, and removes all diseases.

children.text: kāntiṃ rucyaṃ ca cakṣuṣyaṃ hṛdyam āyuṣyadaṃ śuci ||
children.translated_text: It gives complexion, relish, benefit to the eyes, benefit to the heart, long life, and purity.

children.text: sthairyaṃ dārḍhyaṃ ca dhātūnāṃ balavacca rasāyanam
children.translated_text: It gives stability and firmness to the bodily constituents and is a powerful <s>rasāyana</s>.
Now I shall explain mica, beginning with its origin, in order.
The primordial goddess, <s>Śakti</s>, was in beautiful <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>,
together with <s>Indrāṇī</s>, <s>Kamalā</s>, <s>Vāṇī</s>, <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and the others,
and accompanied by the divine wives of sages, headed by <s>Arundhatī</s>.
<s>Mahāmāyā</s>, whose form is consciousness, being, and bliss, played there.
Many tears of joy fell from her eyes onto her linen garment.

children.text: tadā ṛtumatī jātā tataḥ svādu saritpateḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then she became menstruant; afterward, on the bank of the sweet lord of rivers,

children.text: tīre tyaktvā ca tadvastraṃ snātvā kailāsamāyayau
children.translated_text: she left that garment, bathed, and went back to <s>Kailāsa</s>.
Driven by a gust of wind, that garment then fell into the milk ocean.
From that milk ocean, while it was being churned by gods and asuras,
that menstrual garment became fourfold and was called mica.
Black mica has the appearance of collyrium; yellow came from the goddess's body-unguent.

children.text: raktaṃ tasya rajorūpaṃ kṣaumaṃ śvetam abhūditi ||
children.translated_text: Red was in the form of her menstrual blood, and the linen became white.
Seeing that fourfold substance as the cause for binding <s>rasa</s>,
as a <s>rasāyana</s>, a remover of disease, and a giver of all accomplishments,
all the gods said, 'It is directly equal to nectar.'
The white is for works involving silver; the other three are for gold.
All of them, red, yellow, white, and black, are to be applied in <s>rasāyana</s>.
Red is a hundred times better than white, and yellow is a thousand times better than red.
Black should be known as a lakh times better than yellow in iron <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: pratyekaṃ tāni jāyante caturdhā jātitaḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Each of these is produced in four kinds according to class, in order.

children.text: pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ vajraṃ ceti caturvidham
children.translated_text: They are fourfold: pināka, dardura, nāga, and vajra.
One should obtain vajra as the best; the other three should be avoided.
Pināka, when thrown into fire, releases a mass of flakes.
If taken, it binds the stool and may kill, being a cause of disease.
Dardura, when thrown into fire, makes a frog-like sound.
It produces the incurable disease called stone.
Nāga, when placed in fire, gives off a hissing sound.
Through taking it, the great leprosy called maṇḍala certainly arises.
By taking these three, an accumulation of diseases arises.
But vajra-mica, when placed in fire, never undergoes any alteration.
Therefore vajra-mica should be taken; it conquers wrinkles, gray hair, and death.
It should preferably be obtained from its mine with a pickaxe, from a royal-cubit depth.
It should be heavy, broad-layered, smooth, and easily releasing its layers.
That which resembles glass, moonstone, or slag should never be used.
Vajra-mica endowed with the characteristics stated earlier should be heated firmly,
in arka latex, sour gruel, cow urine, and <s>triphalā</s> juice.
And in <s>meghanāda</s> juice one should thus immerse it in those liquids three times.
After properly making its layers separate, with the fluids of <s>meghanāda</s> and sour gruel,

children.text: bhāvayed ātape tīvre ślakṣṇaṃ piṣṭvātha vastrake
children.translated_text: one should impregnate it in strong sunlight, grind it smooth, and then place it in a cloth.
Having placed it together with grain and tied it up, again in that sour gruel

children.text: karābhyāṃ ghaṭṭayed gāḍhaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tatkāñjike sravet
children.translated_text: one should rub it hard with both hands; its fine portion will flow into that sour gruel.

children.text: tat kuryād ātape śuṣkam etad dhānyābhrakaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: One should dry that in the sun; this is known as grain-processed mica.
For mica, the extraction of its essence should be like that for magnetite, O dear one.

children.text: hema rūpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ ca vaikrāntaṃ madhu ṭaṅkaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, honey, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,

children.text: guñjā guḍaṃ ghṛtaṃ bhallam ekaikaṃ daśaniṣkakam
children.translated_text: <s>guñjā</s>, jaggery, ghee, and <s>bhalla</s>, each in the amount of ten <s>niṣkas</s>,
should be ground with arka latex, and pills of one <s>karṣa</s> each should be made.
When this mica essence of one hundred <s>niṣkas</s> has melted, the pills should be thrown into it.
The pills should be added slowly, one by one, for the duration of one <s>ghaṭikā</s> each.

children.text: yāvat tat sattvaśeṣaṃ syāt tāvad dhāmyam atandritaiḥ
children.translated_text: Until only that essence remains, it should be heated by men who are not negligent.
This mica essence is a <s>rasāyana</s> fit for the gods.
After powdering that mica essence, <s>meghanāda</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>sūraṇa</s>, arka leaves, <s>mustā</s>, <s>jambīra</s>, and <s>tālamūlikā</s>,

children.text: triphalā vajravallī ca śāṅgerī maricaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>triphalā</s>, <s>vajravallī</s>, <s>śāṅgerī</s>, and also pepper,
the sour group, banyan aerial roots, cotton, and <s>muniśigru</s>,
<s>ekavīrā</s>, <s>kokilākṣī</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, basil, and <s>vacā</s>,

children.text: peṭārī vākucī kanyā caikaikasya rasaiḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: <s>peṭārī</s>, <s>vākucī</s>, and <s>kanyā</s>: with the juices of each separately,

children.text: mardanaṃ gharmapākaṃ ca sthālīpākaṃ puṭaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: one should perform trituration, cooking by solar heat, cooking in a pot, and <s>puṭa</s> firing, in order,
for one day each. Then, in the case of <s>darada</s> and <s>mākṣika</s>,
one sixteenth part in relation to the essence should be combined and ground with the best juices.
One should do this up to sixteen <s>puṭas</s>, O <s>Bhairavī</s>.
As stated before, the nectarization should be like that for magnetite essence.
It becomes non-revivifiable <s>bhasma</s>, giving long life and health.
Now I shall explain the regimen for the <s>rasāyana</s> of mica essence.
A person whose body has been purified by emesis and the other purifications, and who has worshipped his chosen deity,
should lick in the morning mica essence the size of a <s>guñjā</s> together with two <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>triphalā</s> powder,
with honey and ghee, for one month; thus should he practice.
In this way, up to the end of the sixteenth month, according to the order of monthly increase,
there should be an increase by one <s>guñjā</s>, O goddess; one should take the <s>rasāyana</s> in this manner.
The regimen and the rules of avoidance should be carried out as stated before, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
After one year there is purification of the body; after two years one is freed from illness.
After three years there is certainly destruction of great diseases.
After four years there is an increase of great beauty, strength, and virility.
After five years there is firmness of the body; in the sixth he attains perfection of speech.
In the seventh there is divine sight; in the eighth, destruction of poison.
In the ninth year he attains accomplished status; thereafter he becomes a <s>Vidyādhara</s>.
In the eleventh year there is the state of <s>Indra</s>; in the twelfth, the state of <s>Brahmā</s>.
In the thirteenth year there is the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and in the fourteenth the state of <s>Rudra</s>.
In the fifteenth there is lordship; in the sixteenth year he is <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
Endowed with <s>aṇimā</s> and the other powers, free in his actions, he becomes omniscient and capable of everything.
Now I shall explain the liquefaction of mica, and also the kañcukī tuber.

children.text: kapitindau keśataile pratyekaṃ tu tridhā vapet
children.translated_text: Into <s>kapitindu</s> and hair oil one should cast it three times each.
After melting it in a crucible, that becomes the liquefied form of mica essence.
One should carefully reduce the liquefaction to <s>bhasma</s>, as with mica essence.
It has the six tastes, destroys all diseases, and is an excellent pacifier of the three <s>doṣas</s>.
It increases virility, lifespan, strength, intelligence, beauty, and form.
It gives firmness and stability to the body and destroys wrinkles, gray hair, and death.

children.text: rucyo vṛṣyo laghuḥ śīto medhyaḥ snigdho rasāyanam
children.translated_text: Mica is appetizing, aphrodisiac, light, cooling, good for the intellect, unctuous, and a <s>rasāyana</s>.
It kindles digestion, is absorbent, and is the best means for binding mercury.
Mica essence reduced to <s>bhasma</s> subdues the wings of king mercury.

children.text: abhrasya patraṃ rogaghnaṃ tacca satvaṃ dṛḍhaṃkaram ||
children.translated_text: The sheet of mica removes disease, and its essence produces firmness.
Its liquefaction gently removes weakness of mind and those forms of poverty.

children.text: sūto vajraṃ suvarṇaṃ ca kāntalohaṃ tathābhrakam
children.translated_text: Mercury, diamond, gold, magnetite iron, and mica:
these five are nectars, prepared by me for human beings.
O <s>Mattakāśinī</s>, whoever knows this is himself directly <s>Maheśvara</s>.
I am <s>rasa</s>, and <s>rasa</s> is I; there is no difference between us.

children.text: tena yuktāstu vajrādyāḥ siddhidāḥ syurna saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When joined with it, diamond and the others become givers of accomplishment, without doubt.
I shall describe the man fit for the use of <s>rasa</s>; listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: strīklībabālakānāṃ ca na hi yojyaṃ rasāyanam
children.translated_text: The <s>rasāyana</s> is not to be prescribed for women, sexless persons, or children.
Those who are fifteen years old are children; those of thirty years are classed as youths.
Those near fifty years of age are called young men.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ ca sthavirāḥ bhaveyuste rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: After that they are to be considered aged for the purpose of <s>rasāyana</s>.
At the prescribed time, accomplishment arises for a boy through <s>rasāyana</s>.
For a young man, accomplishment is certainly gained in twice that time.
For an old man, in three times that time, he obtains accomplishment.
They are to be understood in order, O goddess, as highest, middling, and lowest.
First one should take mica, then the magnetite <s>rasāyana</s>.
Then, O goddess, comes magnetite and mica; afterward, the gold <s>rasāyana</s>.
Then comes mica with a gold preparation, and the magnetite-gold <s>rasāyana</s>.
Then comes the mica-magnetite-gold preparation, and after that the diamond <s>rasāyana</s>.
Then comes the use of mica and diamond, and after that magnetite and diamond.
Then there is the mica-iron-magnetite-diamond preparation and the gold-diamond preparation.
After that come the mica-gold-diamond, the magnetite-gold-diamond,
the mica-magnetite and gold-diamond preparations; then there is the consumption of <s>pārada</s> (mercury).
Likewise there is the union of mica and <s>rasa</s> (mercury); after that comes the magnetite-mercury preparation.
O goddess, there is the mica-magnetite-mercury preparation; afterward comes the gold-mercury preparation.
After that comes the mica-gold-mercury preparation, and then the magnetite-gold-mercury preparation.
Next there is mica-magnetite with gold-mercury; after that comes the diamond-mercury preparation.
O goddess, there is the mica-diamond-mercury preparation, and then the magnetite-diamond-mercury preparation.
Then there is mica-magnetite with diamond-mercury, and after that the gold-diamond-mercury preparation.
There is mica-gold-diamond-mercury, and magnetite-gold-diamond-rasa.
There is nothing beyond this mica-magnetite-gold-diamond-rasa.
All these, each succeeding the preceding, are superior in every quality.
O fair-faced one, the single-drug <s>rasāyanas</s> are five.
The <s>rasas</s> made from two drugs are ten, and those made from three drugs are ten.
Those made from four drugs are five, while one arises from five drugs.
O lovely-hipped one, these are thirty-one <s>rasāyanas</s>, my dear.
Mica, magnetite, gold, diamond, mercury, and the others
become successively superior in quality, O beloved of my life.
The <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeating activation) of <s>rasa</s> is diamond; then gold, magnetite, and mica.
For the <s>krāmaṇa</s> of diamond, O dear one, there are gold, magnetite, and mica.

children.text: hemnaḥ kāntabhavaṃ yojyaṃ kāntasya krāmaṇaṃ ghanam ||
children.translated_text: For gold one should employ what comes from magnetite; for magnetite, the <s>krāmaṇa</s> is mica.
The <s>krāmaṇa</s> of mica is mica-essence, since it grants success.
When a single medicine is used, the <s>krāmaṇa</s> should be as just stated.
When it is joined with two, three, four, or five medicines, no separate <s>krāmaṇa</s> is needed.
<s>Triphala</s>, honey, and ghee are the general <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s>:

children.text: rasāyanārhāṃ sūtasya saṃskṛtiṃ vada me vibho
children.translated_text: Lord, tell me the preparation of mercury that is fit for <s>rasāyana</s>.
<s>Śrībhairava</s>:
Listen carefully, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, to the procedure beginning with purification.
One should grind grain-processed mica and mercury in equal quantity with juices of <s>punarnavā</s>.
O goddess, after one day in a heated mortar, the mercury placed in a <s>vajramūṣā</s> crucible
should be cooked in a <s>bhūdharayantra</s> apparatus, and then it should again be triturated.
With the earlier liquids, as before, the trituration and cooking are repeated.
Having done this ten times, one should distill it in a distillation apparatus.

children.text: śuddhaḥ syātpārado devi yojyo yoge rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: O goddess, the mercury becomes purified and fit to be applied in the <s>rasāyana</s> preparation.
One should place sulfur, one tenth the quantity of mercury, into a heated mortar.
It should be thoroughly rubbed for one <s>yāma</s> with the liquids of <s>varā</s>, citron, <s>kanyā</s>, and <s>agni</s> plants.
One should distill it in a distillation apparatus, doing this seven times.

children.text: sagandhakaṃ mardanaṃ ca pātanaṃ bhavati priye ||
children.translated_text: O dear one, there is trituration and distillation together with sulfur.

children.text: śuddhaḥ syātpārado devi yogyo yoge rasāyane
children.translated_text: O goddess, the mercury becomes purified and fit for use in the <s>rasāyana</s> preparation.
With sesame oils, buffalo urines, and sour liquid, it should be rubbed.
Cinnabar should be cooked with cow flesh in an iron vessel over a gradual fire.
For seven days one should stir it repeatedly with an iron rod while it remains moist.
It should be treated for one day in the sun with fresh peacock bile.
One should cook <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) in a distillation apparatus over a fierce fire.
After four <s>yāmas</s> it becomes purified mercury suitable for <s>rasāyana</s>.
One should place an equal amount of sulfur above and below mercury digested with <s>kha</s>.
It is put in a baked crucible, in a pit, in twofold or fourfold measure.
Having added juice of <s>kākamācī</s> and sealed it, one should cook it by gradual fire,
placing the crucible in a <s>guṇḍaka</s> apparatus for four <s>yāmas</s>.
The mercury becomes reduced to ash, and one should apply it in <s>rasāyana</s>.
One should thoroughly rub digested mercury and an equal amount of sulfur with the latex of <s>snuhī</s>.

children.text: dinaṃ tato garbhayantre puṭe bhasmati pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: After one day, in a <s>garbhayantra</s> apparatus and in a sealed heating, it turns to ash as before.
Take mercury digested with <s>kha</s> in equal part, lac, wool, honey, borax,
and <s>guñjā</s>; rub everything for one day with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s>.
When sealed in a <s>vajramūṣā</s> crucible and blown upon, the mercury turns to ash.

children.text: ghanajīrṇaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ tryahaṃ tulyaṃ vimardayet ||
children.translated_text: One should rub mercury digested with mica together with an equal amount of sulfur for three days.
This may be done with juices of <s>ahimāryā</s>, or with juice of <s>ajāmāryā</s>,
or with juice of <s>kīṭamāriṇī</s>, or with juice of white <s>aṅkola</s>.
For a day and night it should be burned in a clay-covered vessel over a dung fire.
Or, by a husk fire for three days, the mercury becomes ash.

children.text: taptakhalve vajrabhasma jīrṇe sūte samaṃ tryaham
children.translated_text: In a heated mortar, diamond ash and an equal amount of digested mercury should be treated for three days.
It should be rubbed with juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s> and with seeds produced from divine herbs.
One should smear it in a <s>vajramūṣā</s> crucible and first place the mercury there.
It should be cooked for three days by a husk fire, and again with liquids of <s>haṃsapādī</s>
one should rub it firmly for three days; that ball should be cooked as before.
The lord of mercury becomes ash, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.
Now I shall explain, O goddess of gods, the killing of mercury after it has been digested.
First one should perform digestion, O queen of the gods, together with the seed-substance.
If a fool, through negligence, kills mercury that has not been digested,

children.text: mama drohī sa pāpiṣṭho mahāpātakavān bhavet ||
children.translated_text: he is most sinful, hostile to me, and possessed of a great transgression.
He is a killer of an embryo, a slayer of his teacher, a cow-killer, and a killer of women and children.
Therefore, with every effort, one should perform the killing only after digestion.
O <s>Pārvatī</s>, this is the killing of the king of <s>rasa</s>, my own seed.

children.text: dharāyāṃ gomayaṃ devi sthāpayitvā tata upari ||
children.translated_text: O goddess, having placed cow dung on the ground and then, above it,
having put it in a baked crucible, one should place in its midst oil from bitter gourd seed

children.text: tailaṃ nidhāya sūtaṃ ca nikṣipecca tata upari ||
children.translated_text: and mercury, placing it afterward on top.
O fair-faced one, juice of <s>kākamācī</s> should be added in an amount equal to the oil.

children.text: śuddhaṃ gandhaṃ vrīhimātraṃ dattvā mūṣāṃ nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: After adding pure <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) the size of a grain of rice, one should seal the crucible.
Above it one should place a <s>śrāvaka</s> vessel filled with <s>khadira</s> charcoal.
When one knows that its own body has cooled, again sulfur and oil should be applied.
After adding juice of <s>kākamācī</s>, one should apply fire in this way again and again.
Below there should be dense cow-dung fuel, and above there should be fire.
Juice of <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>sūta</s> (mercury), and oil: these three are to be equal.
One should digest six times as much sulfur; in this way <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is made receptive.
Again one should triturate that mercury with citron juice for one day.
A gold leaf, one sixty-fourth part, should be made able to pierce a thorn.
One should smear it with peacock bile and oil produced from mustard seed.
If that oil and bile are unavailable, one should use <s>cūlikā</s> salt as the substitute.
That mercury and the gold leaf should be triturated with the juices of citron.
One should cook it in the fire as before, again with the juices of citron.
One should seal a filled crucible and digest it again as before.
Then gold is to be one thirty-second part, and above that one sixteenth part.
One should triturate and digest it in this way; next comes the killing of mercury.

children.text: samūlāṃ kumbhim ādāya gavāṃ mūtreṇa peṣayet ||
children.translated_text: Taking a <s>kumbhī</s> plant together with its root, one should grind it with cow urine.
The wise practitioner should triturate mercury for one day with its juice.
Having placed it in an iron container, with restraints above and below,

children.text: cullyāṃ mṛdvagninā pācyaṃ dinaṃ bhasma bhavedrasaḥ
children.translated_text: it should be cooked on the hearth with a gentle fire for a day; the mercury becomes <s>bhasma</s> (ash).
It is inexhaustible, a destroyer of death, and a remover of old age and poverty.
One <s>karṣa</s> of conditioned mercury, eight <s>guñjās</s> of gold,
and four <s>guñjās</s> of killed diamond should be triturated with the juices of <s>haṃsapadī</s>.
In a heated mortar, after putting it into a diamond crucible, one should seal it.
One should cook it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus, and then take that mercury again.
It should be triturated with the liquids of <s>haṃsapādī</s> in a heated mortar for three days.
As before, one should cook the mercury again and again in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus.
When it has thus received one hundred <s>puṭas</s> (firings), the <s>bhasma</s> becomes red in color.
These mercury <s>bhasmas</s> are praised in <s>rasāyana</s> practice.
I shall now describe in order the <s>rasāyana</s> joined with one, two, three, four, and five combinations,
O mistress of the gods; and even there the first practice is the taking of mica.
One whose body has been purified by emesis and the other purifications, and who has given up alkaline, sour, and similar foods,
should calcine the essence of mica as before with the juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s> and <s>varā</s>.
It is to be impregnated twenty-one times; in the morning one should take two <s>guñjās</s>,

children.text: sasitaṃ tadanu kṣaudraṃ ghṛtaiḥ satriphalaṃ lihet ||
children.translated_text: with sugar, and after that one should lick honey and ghee together with <s>triphalā</s>.
The increase is up to thirty-two <s>guñjās</s>; the <s>krāmaṇa</s> measure is one <s>karṣa</s>.
By this, at the end of sixteen months, one is freed from all diseases.
Through such use of mica, one becomes fit for taking <s>kānta</s> (magnetite).
One should calcine <s>kānta</s> as before with juices produced from <s>varā</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and <s>bhṛṅga</s>.
It should be triturated and impregnated in sequence twenty-one times.
In the morning one should lick it daily with honey and ghee, measured at two <s>guñjās</s>.
Afterward the food is powder produced from <s>sinduvāra</s>, <s>varā</s>, and <s>bhṛṅga</s>.
One whose body has been purified by emesis and the other procedures should take one <s>karṣa</s> of it with honey and ghee.
An increase of thirty-two <s>guñjās</s> is the upper limit, O <s>Īśvarī</s>.
At the end of sixteen months one is free from old age and diseases.
After taking <s>kānta</s>, one becomes fit for the <s>kānta</s>-and-mica preparation.
Killed <s>kānta</s> and <s>ghana</s> are to be equal; <s>dhātrī</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>
are to be used separately for trituration with their juices; in the morning one should lick two <s>guñjās</s>.
One purified by emesis and the other procedures should take it with sugar, honey, and ghee.
Powder of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, and <s>varṣābhū</s> is the best <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
Afterward that should be licked with honey and ghee, up to thirty-two <s>guñjās</s>.
Through a sixteen-month regimen, one becomes strong and conquers wrinkles and gray hair.
By taking the essences of <s>kānta</s> and mica, one becomes fit for taking gold.
One should calcine gold as before with a decoction of the ten roots.
One should triturate and impregnate it twenty-one times, O dear one.
In the morning, the wise and purified practitioner should lick a <s>mudga</s>-measure with honey and ghee,
and afterward drink one <s>pala</s> of decoction of <s>guḍūcī</s> and <s>triphalā</s>.
The increase has a limit of eight <s>guñjās</s> over sixteen months.
One becomes radiant, strong, intelligent, clear-sighted, and free from disease.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, one becomes a conqueror of poisons in the three times.
One should kill gold as before, and mica in twice that amount.
It should be impregnated twenty-one times with decoctions of the ten roots, <s>varā</s>, and <s>bhṛṅgī</s>.
In the morning one should lick three <s>māṣas</s> with honey and ghee, and then lick the <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
After that, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, one should take a <s>pala</s> of decoction of <s>guḍūcī</s> and <s>triphalā</s>.
For him the increase should be twenty-four <s>guñjās</s>, the upper limit.
Through the sixteen-month regimen, he becomes divinely radiant and very strong.
Through the combination of <s>ghana</s> and gold, he becomes fit for the gold-and-<s>kānta</s> preparation.
One should calcine gold as before, and <s>kānta</s> in two parts relative to the gold.
One should impregnate and triturate it in sequence fourteen times with <s>dhātrī</s> fruits.
In the morning one should take three <s>māṣas</s> with sugar, and afterward drink
one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>dhātrī</s> essence, ghee, and honey, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
The increase should be twenty-four <s>guñjās</s>, the upper limit.
Through the sixteen-month regimen, one is free from wrinkles and gray hair.
He has the true luster of heated gold and is like another <s>Pañcabāṇa</s>.
By tasting the gold-and-<s>kānta</s> preparation, one becomes fit for <s>kānta</s>, mica, and gold.
One should calcine gold as before, along with the essences of <s>kānta</s> and mica.
These three, in equal quantities, should also be levigated twenty-one times.
With the liquid of muṇḍī, nirguṇḍikā, bhṛṅga, and varā, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
one should lick a dose measuring three māṣas in the morning, soaked in honey and ghee.
Afterward one should lick a karṣa-measure of muṇḍī powder with honey and ghee,
and then drink a pala-measure of cow's milk, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
The highest increase, O dear one, should be reckoned as twelve vallas.
By using it for sixteen months, a man becomes divine-bodied.
Through taking gold, mica, and magnetite, he becomes fit for consuming diamond.
One should calcine diamond as before and triturate it with dhātrī juice.
The wise man should levigate it seven times and lick a rice-grain measure, O dear one,
mixed with ghee and honey; afterward he should drink a pala of dhātrī juice.
The increase should extend up to a valla through use for sixteen months.
He becomes long-lived, diamond-bodied, divinely sighted, and very strong.
Through consuming diamond he becomes fit for consuming diamond-mica.
One should calcine mica as before, with diamond four times as much as the diamond.

children.text: ghanaṃ dhātryāḥ śatāvaryā rasair bhāvyaṃ trisaptadhā
children.translated_text: The compact substance should be levigated twenty-one times with the juices of dhātrī and śatāvarī.
He should lick a barley-grain measure in the morning, and then lick it with honey and ghee.
The drink afterward is a pala-measure of the liquid of dhātrī and śatāvarī.
The highest increase should be four guñjās after sixteen months.
There will be power of speech and divine sight, and his brilliance will be like that of a deity.
Through consuming compact diamond he becomes fit for magnetite-diamond.
One should calcine diamond as before, and magnetite four times as much as diamond.
The magnetite should be levigated twenty-one times with juices of aśvagandhā and varā.
At daybreak one should lick a barley-grain measure mixed with honey and ghee.
He should drink a karṣa of powder of aśvagandhā and varā with cow's milk.
The upper limit of increase should be known as four guñjās, the highest limit.
By using it for sixteen months, he has a radiance equal to the young sun.
Very strong and very radiant, with perfected speech, he attains accomplishment.
Through consuming diamond and magnetite he becomes fit for diamond, magnetite, and mica.
One should calcine diamond as before, along with magnetite and mica in relation to diamond.
When the magnetite-mica is fourfold, it should be treated with juices produced from varā, bhṛṅga, and kuraṇḍa.
It should be levigated twenty-one times; one should lick a barley-grain measure, O dear one,
mixed with honey and ghee, and joined with bhṛṅga, varā, kuraṇḍa, and karaja.
He should drink a pala of cow's milk; four guñjās is the highest limit.
By using it for sixteen months, he has vulture-like sight and great strength.
Steadfast, with unobstructed movement, he lives among the host of perfected beings.
Through taking magnetite-mica and diamond, he becomes fit for gold and diamond.
One should calcine diamond as before, and gold in two parts relative to diamond.
Gold-diamond should be levigated twenty-one times with juices of punarnavā.
He should lick a rice-grain measure with honey and ghee, and then take punarnavā.
A karṣa of it and a pala of cow's milk are to be drunk afterward, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
The increase should extend up to two guñjās through use for sixteen months.
He becomes long-lived for a long time, free from wrinkles and gray hair.
Through the use of diamond and gold he becomes fit for gold, mica, and diamond.
One should calcine gold, compact mica, and diamond as before, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
There should be gold twice as much as diamond, and mica in two parts relative to the gold.
It should be levigated twenty-one times with the essence of musalī tuber.
In the morning he should lick a barley-grain measure with honey and ghee, and afterward drink
a karṣa of musalī powder and a pala-measure of cow's milk.
The increase extends up to four guñjās through use for sixteen months.
He conquers death, is free from old age, diamond-bodied, and very strong.
Through consuming this he becomes fit for diamond, gold, and magnetite.
Diamond, magnetite, and gold are to be calcined as before.
Gold should be twice as much as diamond, and magnetite in two parts relative to the gold.
It should be rubbed with juices of dhātrī and bhṛṅga twenty-one times.
In the morning he should lick a barley-grain measure with honey and ghee, and afterward drink
a karṣa of powder made from dhātrī and bhṛṅga and a pala of cow's milk.
The increase is four guñjās through use for sixteen months.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, he is divinely radiant and very strong.
Through consuming this he becomes fit for magnetite, gold, diamond, and mica.
One should calcine gold, magnetite, mica, and diamond as stated.
It should be levigated with juices of jyotiṣmatī twenty-one times.
In the morning he should lick a barley-grain measure with honey and ghee, and afterward drink
a karṣa of aśvagandhā-root powder and a pala of cow's milk.
The increase of four guñjās is the highest limit, O <s>Īśvarī</s>.
By using it for sixteen months, he becomes equal to <s>Indra</s> himself.

children.text: etasya sevayā devi rasaṃ sevitum arhati ||
children.translated_text: Through consuming this, O <s>Devī</s>, he is fit to consume <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
Dhānyābhra and mercury should be triturated in a heated mortar for three days.
One should rub it with liquids produced from triphalā, āragvadha, niśā, kumārī, kṛṣṇa, and dhūrta,
and with liquids produced from punarnavā, agni, and jambīra.
One should distill it in a distillation apparatus; thus there is trituration and distillation.
One should do this three times; the mercury becomes pure and free from faults.
One should triturate it with controlling substances and make the crucible coating with controlling substances.

children.text: kṛtvā taṃ marditaṃ sūtaṃ mūṣāyāṃ nikṣipetsudhīḥ
children.translated_text: Having prepared that triturated <s>sūta</s> (mercury), the wise man should place it in a crucible.
After sealing it, it should be cooked in the apparatus called <s>Bhūdhara</s>, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
In this way one should perform trituration and puṭa-cooking seven times.
The mercury <s>bhasma</s> (ash) becomes white and should be used in a rasāyana preparation.
Now, the <s>cāroṭaka-rasa</s> is the sole cause of bodily perfection.
One should lick a black-gram measure of it in the morning with honey, ghee, and <s>triphala</s>.
After the dose, O dear one, one should drink cow's milk warm from the udder.
Increasing the dose up to eight <s>guñjā</s>s, one should do this for sixteen months.
Free from wrinkles and gray hair, one lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
By using this, O goddess, one becomes fit for mercury together with mica.
When the mercury has been made receptive, O goddess, in the amount of sixty-four <s>niṣka</s>s,
one should add one <s>niṣka</s> of mica essence with liquids produced from citron.
One should triturate it for a day in a heated mortar and then in a tortoise apparatus.
Afterward one should cook it together with <s>biḍa</s>, take it out, and triturate it.
Then, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, add two <s>niṣka</s>s of mica essence with citron acid,
and perform the cooking operation in the heated mortar and in the apparatus called tortoise.

children.text: tṛtīye ca caturniṣkaṃ caturthe pañcame kramāt
children.translated_text: In the third operation add four <s>niṣka</s>s, and in the fourth and fifth successively,
one should add eight <s>niṣka</s>s of mica essence in the fifth cooking.
In the sixth, the compact mica is sixteen <s>niṣka</s>s, and in the seventh thirty-two parts
of essence should be exactly equal, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Thus, O dear one, the digestion of mica essence in mercury takes place.
Having thus digested the lord of mercury, one should reduce it to <s>bhasma</s> as before.
Take one <s>pala</s> of this mercury <s>bhasma</s> and four <s>pala</s>s of mica essence.
It is to be triturated with juices of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> and sealed firmly in a crucible.
One should cook it in a heating called the cock, and collect it when it has cooled by itself.
One should impregnate it twenty-one times with waters from <s>triphala</s> and <s>bhṛṅga</s>.
A purified-minded person should lick a <s>guñjā</s> measure with honey and ghee in the morning.
Afterward, with controlled mind, he should drink one <s>pala</s> of <s>varā</s> decoction.
The increase is by sixteen <s>guñjā</s>s, and it is to be taken for sixteen months.
One lives as long as the moon and stars endure, free from wrinkles and gray hair.
By using this, the beloved one becomes fit for the use of magnetite-mercury.
When the king of mercury has been made receptive, as the digestion of mica took place,
in just that way, O dear one, the digestion of magnetite essence takes place.
One should kill the mercury digested with magnetite essence as before.
Again, of such mercury with its <s>bhasma</s>, there should be one part,
and four parts of magnetite <s>bhasma</s>; one should triturate them with <s>triphala</s> water.
Then one should seal it in a crucible and cook it in a cock heating.
Taking it out, one should impregnate it twenty-one times with <s>varā</s> waters.
In the morning, tireless, one should lick a <s>guñjā</s> measure with honey and ghee.
The after-drink is cow's milk, one <s>pala</s> in measure, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
The increase is by sixteen <s>guñjā</s>s, in a course of sixteen months.
One obtains divine sight, the state of a sky-goer, and the rank of <s>Indra</s>.
By using this, one becomes fit for mercury with mica and magnetite.
When the mercury has been made receptive, one should perform the digestion of mica as before.
Afterward, O queen of gods, the wise should make it equal to the mercury.
As before, the digestion of magnetite essence is equal to the king of mercury.
If mercury is digested with magnetite essence and mica essence,
that <s>rasa</s> becomes wingless, free from volatility, and auspicious.

children.text: taṃ rasaṃ pūrvavad divyair auṣadhair māritaṃ rasam
children.translated_text: That <s>rasa</s>, having been killed as before with divine medicines,
should be one <s>pala</s>; twice that amount of mica-essence <s>bhasma</s>, and an equal amount
of <s>bhasma</s> of <s>vaikrānta</s> essence are to be triturated, these three in threefold fashion,
in the juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s> and myrobalan fruit; then it should be cooked in a light heating.
One should impregnate the <s>rasa</s> in the shade with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s> and myrobalan fruit.
Afterward one should lick a <s>guñjā</s> measure with <s>triphala</s>, honey, and ghee.
Then one should drink one <s>pala</s> of cow's milk; the increase is by sixteen <s>guñjā</s>s.
By a course of sixteen months, one lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
By using this, one becomes fit for mercury treated with gold.
One should reduce the king of mercury digested with gold to <s>bhasma</s> as before.
Take one <s>pala</s> of such mercury <s>bhasma</s> and two <s>pala</s>s of gold.
One should impregnate it three times in the shade with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s> and myrobalan fruit.

children.text: ruddhvā taṃ saṃpuṭe pacyātkukkuṭākhye puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: Having enclosed it in a covered capsule, one should cook it in a heating called the cock.
Again one should impregnate it twenty-one times with waters of <s>bhṛṅga</s> and myrobalan.

children.text: māṣamātraṃ lihet prātar madhvājyābhyāṃ yutaṃ rasam
children.translated_text: In the morning one should lick a black-gram measure of the <s>rasa</s> joined with honey and ghee.
The after-drink is cow's milk, and the increase is up to sixteen black-gram measures.
By a course of sixteen months, one becomes godlike and long-lived.
Through use of gold-mercury, one becomes fit for mica-gold-mercury.
When the mercury has been made receptive, first one should digest an equal amount of mica essence.

children.text: tataḥ svarṇaṃ samaṃ jāryaṃ taṃ sūtaṃ bhasmayettataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then an equal amount of gold should be digested, and afterward that mercury should be incinerated.
As previously stated, take one <s>pala</s> of mercury <s>bhasma</s> and two <s>pala</s>s of gold.
One should combine them together with four <s>pala</s>s of mica-essence <s>bhasma</s>.
It is to be triturated for a day, O dear one, in juice of <s>nīlī</s> leaves and in <s>varā</s> decoction.
Having enclosed it in a covered capsule, one should cook it with twenty cow-dung cakes besides.
One should impregnate it twenty-one times with <s>nīlī</s> juice and <s>varā</s> decoction.
At dawn one should lick a <s>guñjā</s> measure with honey and ghee, and then drink
one <s>pala</s> of <s>varā</s> decoction; the increase is by sixteen <s>guñjā</s>s.
By a course of sixteen months, one lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
By using this, one becomes fit for magnetite-gold-mercury.
When the mercury is receptive, magnetite essence is to be digested as prescribed.

children.text: jārayecca tathā svarṇaṃ dvābhyāṃ jīrṇaṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: And gold should likewise be digested; digested by both, each in an equal amount,
one should incinerate the mercury digested with magnetite and gold according to rule.

children.text: taṃ rasaṃ palamekaṃ ca hemabhasma paladvayam
children.translated_text: Take one <s>pala</s> of that <s>rasa</s> and two <s>pala</s>s of gold <s>bhasma</s>.
One should combine mobile <s>kānta</s>-essence <s>bhasma</s> according to rule.
After triturating it for a day in excellent water of <s>śatāvarī</s>, in a covered capsule,

children.text: ruddhvā taṃ kukkuṭapuṭe pacedādāya taṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: one should seal it and cook it in a cock heating; then one should take that <s>rasa</s>.
It should be impregnated three times seven times with juices of <s>śatāvarī</s>, with excellent juices.
One should lick a <s>guñjā</s>-measure mixed with ghee and honey, and afterward drink.
<s>Śatāvarī</s> juice is to be drunk, one <s>pala</s> in measure, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
The increase is by sixteen <s>guñjā</s>s, through a course of sixteen months.
Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one lives until the cosmic dissolution.
By using this, one becomes able to consume gold, <s>kānta</s>, mica, and <s>rasa</s>.
Mica, <s>kānta</s>, and gold should each be equal, indeed.
In receptive mercury, O dear one, one should digest them successively.
The wise should incinerate the mercury digested with mica and the rest as before.
From that incinerated mercury, there should be twice as much gold <s>bhasma</s>.

children.text: hematulyaṃ mṛtaṃ kāntaṃ kāntatulyaṃ mṛtaṃ ghanam
children.translated_text: The killed <s>kānta</s> should be equal to the gold, and the killed mica equal to the <s>kānta</s>.
All this should be triturated for a day with <s>varā</s> decoction and juices of <s>muṇḍī</s> and <s>bhṛṅga</s>.
Having sealed it in a covered capsule, one should cook it in a cock-type heating.
Taking it out, one should impregnate it with waters of <s>varā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>muṇḍī</s>.
Three times seven times in the shade; in the morning one should lick a <s>guñjā</s>-measure.
The after-drink is cow's milk together with sugar, honey, and ghee.
The increase is by sixteen <s>guñjā</s>s, through a course of sixteen months.
Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
By using this, one becomes fit for the use of mercury and diamond.
With receptive mercury one should perform the digestion of diamond as before.
The <s>rasa</s> digested with diamond, O <s>Devī</s>, should be incinerated as before.
From the incinerated <s>rasa</s>, O dear one, there should be twice as much diamond <s>bhasma</s>.
It should be triturated for a day with waters of <s>kanyā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>varā</s>, in a covered capsule.
One should cook it in the heating called cock; then, after taking it out, one should impregnate it.
One should impregnate it three times seven times with waters of <s>kanyā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>varā</s>.
In the morning one should lick a barley-measure with honey and ghee, and afterward drink.
Cow's milk, one <s>pala</s> in measure, is to be drunk; the increase is four <s>guñjā</s>s.
Through a course of sixteen months one lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
By using this, one becomes fit for diamond, mercury, and mica.
The wise should incinerate the mercury digested with mica and digested with diamond.
From the incinerated <s>rasa</s>, there should be twice as much diamond and mica <s>bhasma</s>,
and four times as much of all that; having combined it into one, one should triturate it.
For a day in <s>varā</s> decoction and juices, one should cook it in a covered capsule.
After a light heating has been done, it should then be impregnated with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s> and <s>varā</s>.
Three times seven times; one should drink a black-gram measure with equal honey and ghee afterward.
One <s>pala</s> of cow's milk is to be drunk; the increase is up to eight <s>guñjā</s>s.
Thus, in sixteen months, one lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
By using this, one becomes fit for <s>kānta</s>, diamond, and mercury.

children.text: kāntaṃ vajraṃ samaṃ jāryaṃ samukhe pārade priye
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> and diamond, equal in amount, are to be digested in receptive mercury, O dear one.
The wise should incinerate that mercury digested with <s>kānta</s> and diamond.
According to the previously stated method, O <s>Kānte</s>, this mercury <s>bhasma</s>
is to be joined with twice as much diamond as mercury and four times as much <s>kānta</s> as diamond.
It should be triturated for a day with fresh juices of <s>palāśa</s> flowers, in a covered capsule.
Having sealed it in a cock-type heating, one should then take it out and impregnate it.
One should impregnate it three times seven times with water of <s>palāśa</s> flowers.
One should lick a black-gram measure with equal honey and ghee, and afterward drink milk.
The increase should be up to eight <s>guñjā</s>s over sixteen months.
Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
By using this, one becomes fit for diamond, <s>rasa</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and mica.
In receptive mercury one should digest mica, <s>kānta</s>, and diamond in order,
each equal in amount; afterward one should incinerate that digested <s>rasa</s>.
As before, from the mercury there should be an equal amount of diamond and four times as much as the diamond.
<s>Kānta</s> and an equal amount of mica essence should be triturated with these.
With juices born of <s>triphala</s> and <s>bhṛṅga</s>, having sealed it, one should cook it in a covered capsule.
With just a light fire-heating, one should then take it out and impregnate it.
With juices of <s>varā</s> and <s>bhṛṅga</s>, twenty-one times in the sun,
a person of purified mind should lick a black-gram measure with equal honey and ghee in the morning.
The after-drink is cow's milk; the increase should be eight <s>guñjā</s>s.
Through a course of sixteen months, one lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
By using this, one becomes fit for gold, diamond, and mercury.

children.text: samukhe pārade tulye hema vajraṃ ca jārayet
children.translated_text: In receptive mercury one should digest equal amounts of gold and diamond.

children.text: taṃ rasaṃ bhasmayeddevi rasaṃ vajraṃ samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: One should incinerate that <s>rasa</s>, O <s>Devī</s>; the <s>rasa</s> and diamond are equal, equal.

children.text: tayoḥ samaṃ mṛtaṃ hema varākvāthena mardayet
children.translated_text: Killed gold equal to the two should be triturated with <s>varā</s> decoction.

children.text: tatsarvaṃ saṃpuṭe kṣiptvā bhūdharākhye puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed all that in a covered capsule, one should cook it in the heating called <s>bhūdhara</s>.
Taking it out, one should impregnate it three times seven times with <s>varā</s> decoctions.
In the morning one should lick a black-gram measure joined with sesame oil, ghee, and honey.
Cow's milk should be the after-drink, with the sequence extending up to eight <s>guñjā</s>s.
Up to sixteen months, one lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
By using this, one becomes fit for mica, gold, diamond, and <s>rasa</s>.
In receptive mercury one should digest mica, gold, and diamond.
They should be equal parts to the mercury; then one should incinerate the <s>sūta</s>.

children.text: rasatulyaṃ mṛtaṃ vajraṃ tayostulyaṃ ca hāṭakam ||
children.translated_text: Killed diamond should be equal to the <s>rasa</s>, and gold equal to those two.
Mica should be equal to all; all that, together with the <s>rasa</s>, should be ground with <s>brahmabījaka</s>
oils for three days and sealed in a <s>bhūdhara</s> heating.
It is then to be given twenty-one impregnations with <s>palāśa</s> decoction.

children.text: taṃ rasaṃ māṣamātraṃ ca tailaṃ brahmadrubījakam ||
children.translated_text: And one should take a black-gram measure of that <s>rasa</s>, together with oil from the seed of <s>brahmadru</s>.
Afterward he should drink a <s>karṣa</s> measure, up to the limit of eight <s>guñjā</s>s.
By a regimen of sixteen months, he becomes permanently perfected.
Through the use of this, he becomes fit for <s>rasa</s> with magnetite, gold, and diamond.

children.text: mukhīkṛte sūtarāje kāntaṃ svarṇaṃ samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: When the king of mercury has been made receptive, magnetite and gold should each be made equal to it.
One should digest it and incinerate it, and also diamond <s>bhasma</s> equal to it.

children.text: tayostulyaṃ mṛtaṃ hema kāntaṃ sarvasamaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: Dead gold should be equal to those two, and magnetite equal to all, O dear one.
Having ground it in the juice of <s>varā</s> and <s>bhṛṅga</s>, one should cook it in a covered <s>bhūdhara</s> vessel.
Then there should be twenty-one impregnations with waters of excellent <s>bhṛṅga</s> and <s>varā</s>.
In the morning the wise man should lick a black-gram measure of the <s>rasa</s> with <s>varā</s> and honey.

children.text: gavyaṃ payaḥ palaṃ peyaṃ vṛddhiḥ ṣoḍaśamāṣikā ||
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of cow's milk is to be drunk; the increase is by sixteen black-gram measures.
By a regimen of sixteen months, he becomes a lord equal to a perfected being.
Through use of this, he becomes fit for mercury with mica, magnetite, gold, and diamond.
That self-controlled man becomes fit to consume it, a great lord.
He should digest mica, magnetite, gold, and diamond in receptive <s>rasa</s>.
Each one, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>, should be made exactly equal to the mercury.
Then one should kill it by the proper method, with dead diamond equal to the <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: tayostulyaṃ mṛtaṃ hema sarvatulyaṃ mṛtaṃ ghanam
children.translated_text: Dead gold should be equal to those two, and dead mica equal to all.
Magnetite should be equal to the mica, and the oils from <s>suradru</s> equal to all.

children.text: tailaistataḥ saṃpuṭe ca kṣiptvā bhūdharake pacet
children.translated_text: Then, placing it in a covered capsule, one should cook it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> vessel.

children.text: guñjāmātraṃ rasaṃ caitaṃ lihet prātaḥ śuciḥ sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Pure and wise, one should lick a <s>guñjā</s> measure of this <s>rasa</s> in the morning.
With a <s>karṣa</s> measure of oil from <s>devadāru</s>, O <s>Pārvati</s>,
one should then drink one <s>pala</s> of freshly warm cow's milk, O dear one.
The course extends up to sixteen <s>guñjā</s>s by the regimen of sixteen months.

children.text: ya imaṃ pāradaṃ divyaṃ sevate pathyabhuksadā ||
children.translated_text: Whoever always eats the prescribed diet and consumes this divine mercury
is free from disease, birth, old age, and death, and becomes a possessor of all siddhis.
Omniscient, all-pervading, and perfected, he creates as if he were <s>Pitāmaha</s>.
Like <s>Viṣṇu</s> he protects the universe, and he destroys as if he were <s>Hara</s> himself.
He himself grants desired objects, like another wish-fulfilling tree.

children.text: kandarpa iva kāmākṣīḥ sahasraṃ ramayet kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Like <s>Kandarpa</s>, he can delight a thousand lovely-eyed women in a moment.
The user of <s>rasa</s> certainly becomes one whose form is being, consciousness, and bliss.
This thirty-onefold rasāyana, arising from the five preparations beginning with mica,
has been taught out of affection for you; it is a secret difficult even for gods to obtain.

children.text: praṇamya parayā bhaktyā bhairavaṃ bhairavī śivam
children.translated_text: Having bowed with supreme devotion to <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, the <s>Bhairavī</s>
spoke these words humbly, desiring the welfare of the worlds.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s>:
O god of gods, embodiment of compassion, lord who bestows favor on all,
by your grace I have learned an exceedingly rare secret.
It is the rasāyana <s>bhasma</s> of magnetite, mica, gold, diamond, and mercury.
After this, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, O <s>Bhairava</s>, I wish to hear
the rasāyana of pills formed from these substances beginning with mica.
Having heard this respectful speech of <s>Bhairavī</s>, the primordial <s>Bhairava</s>
remained there and spoke these words: I shall tell that rasāyana.
<s>Śrībhairava</s>:
Listen now with care and attentiveness, O <s>Pārvati</s>.
First the digestion is to be performed, and afterward the binding of mercury.
Therefore I shall tell you the digestive seeds for substances beginning with mica.
Sulfur, orpiment, realgar, <s>tuttha</s>, <s>kharparī</s>, cinnabar, and <s>āmalā</s>,
<s>bhūnāga</s>, <s>tāpyaka</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>nṛpāvarta</s>, mica, and red ochre,
magnetite, the three alkalies, and <s>vaikrānta</s>: these are to be powdered in equal parts.
This is known as the perfected powder and is best in the work of seeds.
One should place them, O dear one, in a crucible smeared with <s>dvandvamela</s>.
One should melt black essence and mica essence, along with an equal amount of copper.
Into that, together with the five friendly substances, one should add the perfected powder again and again.
Ten times as much as the mica should be cast in, and one should blow strongly, O lovely-faced one.
It should be blown until only the mica essence remains.
In due time this mica-essence seed is to be digested in the rasāyana.
Into receptive mercury one should cast the seed in a sixty-fourth part.
In a heated mortar, one should triturate it with the acidic group for three days.

children.text: taṃ sūtaṃ kacchape yantre sabiḍe jārayetpriye
children.translated_text: One should digest that mercury in the tortoise apparatus with <s>biḍa</s>, O dear one.

children.text: tato dvātriṃśadaṃśaṃ ca ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ rasasya tu ||
children.translated_text: Then, as portions of the <s>rasa</s>, one should use one thirty-second and one sixteenth,
one eighth, one fourth, one half, and finally an equal amount.
In this way, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>, one should digest the seed into mercury in sequence.
For mercury treated in this way, the mica essence is equal to the seed, O dear one.
One should triturate it in a heated mortar with the acidic group for one day.
One should place that paste, the king of mercury, inside a citron.
In a swing apparatus containing acid, one should cook it for seven days.
Taking it out, O <s>Pārvati</s>, one should add the bolus with the perfected powder.
Then one should cook it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus with a light heating.
Until it becomes hard, this should be done again and again.
The swing-cooking, the coating with perfected powder, and the heating in the <s>bhūdhara</s> should be repeated.
The pill named <s>Mṛtasañjīvanī</s> grants all siddhis.

children.text: vaktrāntare gale mūrdhni bāhau karṇe'thavā vahet ||
children.translated_text: One may carry it in the mouth, at the throat, on the head, on the arm, or at the ear.
Properly wrapped in gold, it destroys wrinkles and grey hair.
When kept in the mouth, it removes death; within a year it destroys poison and bodily affliction.

children.text: śuddhaṃ gandhaṃ karṣamātraṃ gavyaṃ kṣīraṃ palaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: One should drink a <s>karṣa</s> measure of pure sulfur and one <s>pala</s> of cow's milk.
By this very procedure, mercury passes into the body.
Magnetite, <s>mlecchamukha</s>, and silver, equal in amount, are placed inside a smeared crucible.
After melting them, one should slowly add perfected powder, ten times as much as the magnetite.
One should melt the substance again and again, until only the magnetite remains.
This is called the magnetite-seed, excellent for being digested in <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: samukhe pārade cedaṃ bījaṃ cāryaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: With receptive <s>pārada</s> (mercury), this seed too is to be digested as before.

children.text: catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśakaṃ pūrvaṃ samāṃśaṃ taṃ krameṇa vai ||
children.translated_text: First in a sixty-fourth part, and then in an equal part, in due sequence.
This king of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and the magnetite-seed, the two in equal measure,
should be triturated in a heated mortar with the acid group for three days.
When it has become a paste, one should put it in citron, filled with the group of acids,
and cook it properly in a swing apparatus, in this way up to seven times.
Taking it, one should coat it externally with siddha-powder, O <s>Bhairavī</s>.
Then, in a covered capsule smeared with divine herbs, one should cook it in the earth-furnace.
Until it becomes hard, one should perform the procedure step by step:
swing-cooking, coating with siddha-powder, and cooking in the earth-furnace.
One should digest those two in a heating; then, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>, it has a divine name.

children.text: vaktrāntare gale mūrdhni bāhau karṇe'thavā vahet ||
children.translated_text: One may carry it inside the mouth, at the throat, on the head, on the arm, or at the ear.
Wrapped well in gold, it is to be worn; it destroys wrinkles and grey hair.
It gives results as before, is meritorious, and should be worn carefully by people.
The penetration procedure should be done as before; the <s>rasa</s> enters the body.
In receptive <s>pārada</s>, one should kill the mica-and-magnetite seed.
Each separately should be equal to the mercury, and, as before, little by little,
a sixty-fourth part is used at first, and then an equal part, gradually, in the <s>rasa</s>.
For this <s>sūta</s>, there should be an equal portion of magnetite-seed and mica-seed.
In a heated mortar one should triturate it with the acid group for three days.

children.text: piṣṭīkṛtaṃ ca jambīre kṣiptvā dolāgataṃ pacet
children.translated_text: When it has been made into a paste, one should place it in citron and cook it in the swing apparatus.
Again, taking that paste, one should coat it with siddha-powder.
In a covered capsule smeared with the group of divine herbs, one should cook it in the earth-furnace.

children.text: yadā kaṭhinatāṃ yāti dvidhā kuryātkrameṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: When it becomes hard, one should divide it in two in due sequence.
Having performed swing-sweating, powder-coating, and cooking in the earth-furnace,
the pill called <s>Kāmeśvarī</s>, kept in the mouth, grants all siddhis.
The penetration procedure should be done as before; <s>Rasendra</s> penetrates the body.
Gold, silver, <s>mlecchamukha</s>, magnetite essence, and mica essence,
should be placed in a crucible smeared with a paired amalgam mixture.
When that has melted, one should add siddha-powder ten times the amount of the gold.
One should melt it slowly until only the gold remains.
This is known as gold-seed, excellent in <s>rasa-rasāyana</s>.

children.text: samukhe pārade devi bījaṃ rasasamaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: With receptive <s>pārada</s>, O goddess, the seed should gradually be equal to the <s>rasa</s>.
One should digest it as before, O goddess, beginning with a sixty-fourth part.

children.text: etadrasaṃ hemabījaṃ samaṃ khalve ca tāpite
children.translated_text: This <s>rasa</s> and gold-seed, equal in a heated mortar,
should be triturated with the acid group; after three days the <s>rasa</s> becomes a paste.
Having made the paste with citron, in a swing apparatus filled with acid,
one should cook it for six days, O goddess, and apply a coating of siddha-powder.
Likewise one should apply the capsule-coating, and likewise perform the earth-furnace cooking.
Until it becomes hard, one should do this just as before.

children.text: iyaṃ tu ghuṭikā divyā vikhyātā hemasundarī
children.translated_text: This divine pill is famed as <s>Hemasundarī</s>.
Kept in the mouth, it grants siddhi to men and removes old age, death, and poison.

children.text: pūrvavat krāmaṇaṃ kāryaṃ sūtaḥ saṃkramate punaḥ
children.translated_text: The penetration procedure should be done as before; the <s>sūta</s> again passes through.
When the <s>rasa</s> has been made receptive, the mica-seed and the gold-seed
are to be digested in equal measure, each in order, beginning with a sixty-fourth part.
Thus the digested <s>sūta</s> is the seed of mica and gold.
It should be triturated in a heated mortar with the acid group, in an amount equal to the mercury.
After three days a paste is produced; then put it again into citron.
In a swing apparatus filled with acid, one should cook that for seven days.
There should be coating with siddha-powder, and likewise capsule-coating,
and likewise cooking in the earth-furnace, until it becomes hard.
This pill is siddhi-giving, called <s>Madanasundarī</s>.
Placed inside the mouth, it would make one possessed of all siddhis and long-lived.
It brings snakes, tigers, elephants, and the like, as well as kings and women, under control.

children.text: pūrvavat krāmaṇaṃ kāryaṃ kāyam ākrāmate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: The penetration procedure should be done as before; the <s>rasa</s> enters the body.
In receptive <s>rasa</s>, the magnetite-and-gold seed, each in equal measure,
should be digested separately, measured against the <s>rasa</s>, beginning with a sixty-fourth part.

children.text: itthaṃ jīrṇaṃ rasaṃ bījaṃ kāntahemno rasonmitam ||
children.translated_text: In this way, the digested <s>rasa</s> is measured against the seed of magnetite and gold.
