children.text: pūrvavat piṣṭikāṃ kṛtvā dolāyantre ca pācanam
children.translated_text: Having made a paste as before, one should cook it in the swing apparatus.

children.text: yāvat kaṭhinatāṃ yāti tāvat kāryaṃ muhurmuhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Until it becomes hard, this should be done again and again.
A pill is produced, called <s>Khecarī</s>, granting all siddhis.

children.text: pūrvavat krāmaṇaṃ kāryaṃ sugandhaṃ gopayaḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: The penetration procedure should be done as before; one should drink fragrant cow's milk.
By that, the <s>rasa</s> contained inside the pill enters the body.
In receptive <s>pārada</s>, the seed of mica, magnetite, and gold, each in equal measure,
should be digested separately, beginning with a sixty-fourth part.
For such a <s>sūta</s>, the three seeds beginning with mica should be equal.
One should triturate the three for three days with acid in a heated mortar.

children.text: sa sūtaḥ piṣṭim āpnoti tāṃ piṣṭiṃ pūrvavatpriye ||
children.translated_text: That <s>sūta</s> becomes a paste; that paste, O dear one, should be treated as before:
swing-cooking, coating with siddha-powder, and cooking in the earth-furnace.
Until it becomes hard, this should be done by diligent people.
The pill called <s>Vajreśvarī</s>, kept in the mouth, grants all siddhis.
The penetration procedure should be done as before; the <s>pārada</s> pervades the body.
Pure gold, diamond <s>bhasma</s>, iron powder, and mica essence,
these four in equal measure, together with lead, should be enclosed in a crucible and blown upon.
Then, O dear one, having again taken it in the vessel smeared with <s>dvandvamela</s>,

children.text: ekībhūtaṃ ca mūṣāyāṃ prakaṭaṃ ca dhametpunaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when it has become a single mass, one should expose it in a crucible and heat it again.

children.text: dhautasattvaṃ mākṣikaṃ ca svalpaṃ svalpaṃ muhuḥ kṣipet
children.translated_text: One should repeatedly add, little by little, washed essence of <s>mākṣika</s>,
until only diamond and gold remain; then one should take it out.
Into this one should put mica essence, iron powder, and lead as before,
and, having enclosed it in a vessel smeared with <s>dvandvamela</s>, one should heat it strongly.
Taking up the unified mass, one should expose it in a crucible and heat it,
until gold and diamond remain; then one should take it up again.

children.text: vyomasatvam ayaścūrṇaṃ nāgaṃ vāhyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Mica essence, iron powder, and lead are to be added externally again and again,
and, by the sequence used before, washed essence of <s>mākṣika</s> as well.

children.text: muhuḥ kṣipya dhamettaṃ tu bāhyamevaṃ tu ṣaḍguṇam
children.translated_text: Having repeatedly added them, one should heat it; the external material is thus sixfold.
This is the excellent diamond <s>bīja</s> (seed), to be digested in mercurial <s>rasāyana</s>.
When the mercury is made receptive, the diamond <s>bīja</s>, measured against the <s>rasa</s>, is to be digested,
beginning with a sixty-fourth part, and it should be made to pass over gradually, O dear one.
For the mercury digested in this way, an equal amount of diamond <s>bīja</s>
should be triturated for three days in a heated mortar with the sour group.

children.text: sa piṣṭir jāyate sūtastāṃ piṣṭīṃ ca samāharet
children.translated_text: That <s>sūta</s> becomes a paste; one should collect that paste,
and perform <s>dolāpāka</s>, coating with perfected powder, and enclosed <s>bhūdhara</s> heating.

children.text: kurvīta pūrvavat sarvaṃ yāvat kaṭhinatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: One should do everything as before, until it reaches hardness.
A <s>ghuṭikā</s> named <s>Mahāvajreśvarī</s>, bestowing accomplishment, is produced.

children.text: vaktrasthā krāmaṇaṃ kāryaṃ pūrvavat krāmate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: Placed in the mouth, <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation) should be done; the <s>rasa</s> permeates as before.
When the <s>rasa</s> has been made receptive, mica-diamond <s>bīja</s>, measured against the <s>rasa</s>,
is to be digested separately, beginning with a sixty-fourth part.
For this digested mercury, an equal amount of diamond-mica <s>bīja</s>
should be firmly triturated for three days in a heated mortar with the sour group.

children.text: sa raso jāyate piṣṭistāṃ punaḥ pūrvavatpriye ||
children.translated_text: That <s>rasa</s> becomes a paste; that paste again, as before, O dear one,
one should subject to <s>dolā</s> steaming, coating with perfected powder, and <s>bhūdhara</s> cooking,

children.text: yāvat kaṭhinatāṃ yati tāvad evaṃ muhurmuhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: until it becomes hard; thus one should act again and again.
A divine <s>ghuṭikā</s> is produced, named <s>Vajrakhecarī</s>.

children.text: vaktrasthā siddhidā nṛṇāṃ pūrvavat krāmaṇaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: Placed in the mouth, it gives accomplishment to men; the <s>krāmaṇa</s> is as before, O dear one.
When the <s>rasa</s> has been made receptive, magnetite-diamond <s>bīja</s>, measured against the <s>rasa</s>,
is to be digested separately, beginning with a sixty-fourth part.
For this digested mercury, an equal <s>bīja</s> of diamond and magnetite
should be ground for three days in a well-heated mortar with the sour group.

children.text: piṣṭir bhavatyeṣa sūtaḥ piṣṭiṃ tāṃ punarāharet
children.translated_text: This <s>sūta</s> becomes a paste; one should take up that paste again.
There should be <s>dolā</s> steaming, coating with perfected powder, and enclosed <s>bhūdhara</s> cooking,
until it becomes hard; thus one should do it again and again.
An auspicious <s>ghuṭikā</s> is produced, named <s>Kālavidhvaṃsinī</s>.

children.text: mukhasthā siddhidā divyā pūrvavat krāmaṇaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: Placed in the mouth, it is divine and bestows accomplishment; one should take the <s>krāmaṇa</s> as before.
When the kingly <s>sūta</s> has been made receptive, the <s>bīja</s> of diamond, magnetite, and mica
is to be digested separately in the kingly <s>sūta</s>, beginning with a sixty-fourth part.
Equal to that <s>rasa</s>, the diamond <s>bīja</s> and mica <s>bīja</s>
become a paste after three days through thorough trituration in a heated mortar with the sour group.
There should be <s>dolāpāka</s>, coating with perfected powder, and enclosed <s>bhūdhara</s> cooking,
until it becomes hard; one should do it again and again.
This is the <s>Gaganeśvarī</s> <s>ghuṭikā</s>, which, placed in the mouth, gives all accomplishments.

children.text: pūrvavat krāmaṇaṃ kāryaṃ dehe krāmati sūtakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Krāmaṇa</s> should be done as before; the <s>sūtaka</s> permeates the body.
When the kingly <s>sūta</s> has been made receptive, the <s>bīja</s> of diamond and gold
is to be digested separately in equal amount, beginning with a sixty-fourth part.

children.text: asya sūtasya sadṛśaṃ hemno vajrasya bījakam ||
children.translated_text: Equal to this <s>sūta</s> is the <s>bīja</s> of gold and diamond.
With the heated mortar and the sour group, after three days the <s>rasa</s> becomes a paste.
Taking that paste again, one should prepare it as before:
<s>dolāpāka</s>, coating with perfected powder, and <s>bhūdhara</s> cooking.
Until it becomes hard, one should do it again and again.
This indeed is the <s>Vajraghaṇṭeśvarī</s> <s>ghuṭikā</s>, bestowing accomplishment.

children.text: mukhasthā siddhidā divyā pūrvoktaṃ krāmaṇaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: Placed in the mouth, it is divine and gives accomplishment; one should take the previously taught <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
When the kingly <s>sūta</s> has been made receptive, the <s>bīja</s> of gold, diamond, and mica
is to be digested separately in equal amount, beginning with a sixty-fourth part.
Equal to this <s>sūta</s> is the <s>bīja</s> of gold, diamond, and mica.
One should grind it for three days with the sour group in a heated mortar.

children.text: piṣṭirbhavet punastāṃ ca samādāya tataḥ priye
children.translated_text: A paste is produced; then, O dear one, having again taken that,
one should perform <s>dolāpāka</s>, coating with perfected powder, and <s>bhūdhara</s> cooking.
Until it becomes hard, this should be done again and again.
A divine <s>ghuṭikā</s> is produced, named <s>Vajrabhairavī</s>.
Set in the mouth, it accomplishes success; the <s>krāmaṇa</s> is as before, O dear one.
When the <s>rasa</s> has been made receptive, the <s>bīja</s> of magnetite, diamond, and gold
is to be digested separately, equal to the <s>sūta</s>, beginning with a sixty-fourth part.
Equal to the digested <s>sūta</s> is the <s>bīja</s> of magnetite, diamond, and gold.
One should grind it for three days in a heated mortar with the sour group.
The mercury becomes a paste; one should collect that as before.
There should be <s>dolāpāka</s>, coating with perfected powder, and <s>bhūdhara</s> cooking,
until it becomes hard; it should be done again and again.
A divine <s>ghuṭikā</s> is produced, named <s>Tripurabhairavī</s>.

children.text: mukhasthā siddhidā hyeṣā pūrvavat krāmaṇaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: Placed in the mouth, this indeed gives accomplishment; the <s>krāmaṇa</s> is as before, O dear one.
When the <s>rasa</s> has been made receptive, the <s>bīja</s> of magnetite, diamond, mica, and gold
is to be digested separately, equal to the <s>sūta</s>, beginning with a sixty-fourth part.
For this digested <s>sūta</s>, there is an equal <s>bīja</s> beginning with mica.
One should triturate it with the acidic group in a heated mortar for three days.
The lord of mercury becomes a paste; one should again take up that paste.
One should cook it in a <s>dolā</s>-apparatus, coat it with the prepared powder, and seal it in an earthen capsule.
This should be done again and again until it attains hardness.
This pill, named Mahābhairavīya, bestows every siddhi.
One should hold it in the middle of the mouth and drink the <s>krāmaṇa</s> as before.
<s>Triphalā</s>, <s>musalī</s>, <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, and <s>vākucī</s>;
<s>nīlī</s>, <s>kanyā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>hayagandhā</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>;
<s>uttarā</s>, <s>vāruṇī</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, <s>citrā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>;
<s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, <s>rudantī</s>, and <s>gajakarṇikā</s>;
<s>bhūtāvarāta</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, <s>kākatuṇḍā</s>, and <s>amṛtālatā</s>;
<s>palāśa</s>, <s>kukkurūṭa</s>, juice of myrobalan fruit, and milk;

children.text: palāśabījakaṃ tailaṃ ghṛtaṃ madhu śivāmbu ca ||
children.translated_text: oil of <s>palāśa</s> seed, oil, ghee, honey, and <s>śivāmbu</s>;

children.text: bilvamajjā ca tailaṃ ca tailaṃ jyotiṣmatībhavam
children.translated_text: the pith of <s>bilva</s>, oil, and oil produced from <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>;
these indeed are the medicines fit for <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
And these have been stated, in practical use, for the purpose of <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
In the application of <s>rasa</s>-<s>bhasma</s> and in the elixir of pills,

children.text: priye pañcadaśānāṃ ca ghuṭikānāṃ phalaṃ śṛṇu
children.translated_text: O dear one, hear the fruit of the fifteen pills.
A pill made with the seed of mica and combined with <s>rasa</s>,
when kept in the mouth for twelve years, destroys all diseases.
That man lives a hundred years, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
A pill made with the seed of magnetite and combined with <s>rasa</s>,
when placed in the mouth for twelve years, O fair-faced one, destroys all diseases.
It produces firmness of the bodily elements and grants a thousand years of life.
An auspicious pill made with magnetite and mica seeds and joined with <s>rasa</s>,
when kept inside the mouth for twelve years, destroys old age and disease.
It is divine, grants ten thousand years of life, and greatly increases strength.
A <s>sūta</s>-pill joined with the seed of gold and held in the middle of the mouth,
for up to twelve years, removes wrinkles, gray hair, and disease from the body.
It bestows longevity, is meritorious, and grants the strength of ten thousand elephants.
A pill formed with gold and mica seeds and joined with mercury,
when held in the mouth for twelve years, grants life for one million years.
It produces divine intelligence and bestows divine vitality.
A pill made with magnetite and gold seeds together with <s>sūta</s>,
when kept in the mouth for twelve years, increases life to ten million years.
It produces great brilliance and reveals hidden treasures and the like.
A pill formed with magnetite, mica, and gold and combined with <s>rasa</s>,
when kept in the mouth for twelve years, grants life for one hundred million years.
It bestows the state of a sky-goer and a power destructive like <s>Hālāhala</s> and the cosmic dissolution.
An auspicious pill joined with <s>rasa</s> and made with purified diamond seed,
when kept in the mouth for twelve years, grants movement through all worlds.
It extends life for as long as the earth remains firm.
He is always young and passionate, capable of love-play with beloved women.
A pill made with diamond and mica seeds and filled with <s>rasa</s>,
when kept in the mouth for six years, bestows every siddhi.

children.text: brahmāyuṣyapradā puṃsāṃ jagat sṛṣṭuṃ kramāt prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: It grants men the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>; in due course he is able to create the world.
He is worshiped like <s>Brahmā</s> by the gods and is versed in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.
He is served by <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Sāvitrī</s>, and he goes through all the worlds.
He is endowed with the eight siddhis, such as aṇimā, O <s>Īśvarī</s>.
A pill made with diamond and gold seeds together with <s>sūta</s>,
when kept in the mouth for twelve years, grants men the lifespan of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: sa ca viṣṇutvamāpnoti viṣṇuvat pālituṃ kṣamaḥ
children.translated_text: He attains the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and is able to protect like <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
He is served by <s>Sanaka</s> and the others, endowed with <s>Śrī</s>, and very strong.
He moves according to his own will and is always served by deathless beings such as <s>Mahendra</s>.
A pill made with gold, mica, and diamond seeds, O dear one,
containing mercury and kept inside the mouth for twelve years, O fair-faced one,

children.text: rudrāyuṣpradā nṝṇāṃ rudratvaṃ sā dadāti hi ||
children.translated_text: grants men the lifespan of <s>Rudra</s>; indeed it gives the state of <s>Rudra</s>.
As destroyer, like <s>Rudra</s>, he is served by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the others.
He is accompanied by aṇimā and the other siddhis, all-knowing and moving through all worlds.
He is served by the foremost <s>Pramathas</s> and endowed with divine power.
Steadfast, great in brilliance and great in strength, he is meditated upon by the lords of yogins.
A pill made with the seeds of magnetite, gold, and diamond together with <s>sūta</s>,
when kept in the mouth for twelve years, bestows siddhi upon men.
The human obtains the lifespan of <s>Īśvara</s> and the state of a sky-goer.
He disappears by himself from the world, revered by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the others.
He shines like ten million suns and possesses the essence of a mighty wind.
Even at the time of the end of a great kalpa, he certainly does not go to destruction.
His self is attached to yogic play, and he is meditated upon by the best knowers of yoga.
A <s>rasa</s>-formed pill made with the seeds of magnetite, mica, gold, and diamond,
which remains in a person's mouth for twelve years, O <s>Bhairavī</s>,
makes him possess the lifespan of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, a lord who grants favor to all.
He attains the state of <s>Sadāśiva</s> and likewise becomes lord of the gods.

children.text: vahnau vahnir jale vāri mārute mārutātmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In fire he is fire; in water, water; in wind, of the nature of wind.
On earth he has the form of earth; in the void he becomes of the nature of the void.
His eyes are moon, fire, and sun, and <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the others are his servants.
<s>Nārada</s> and the others are his singers, and apsaras-women are his dancers.
By his command alone <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the others create, maintain, and destroy.
He is formed of being, consciousness, and bliss, powerful, all-pervading, all-knowing, and <s>Śiva</s>.
Joined with supreme <s>Śakti</s>, he is pure, free from māyā, partless, and supreme.

children.text: evaṃ guṇāḥ prakathitā ghuṭikānāṃ mayā priye
children.translated_text: Thus, O dear one, I have described the qualities of the pills.
And among all of these there is also the power that stops weapons.
This, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>, is the giver of accomplishment for every <s>rasāyana</s>.
This king of mantras, granting all accomplishments, will now be taught.

children.text: aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ amṛteśvarabhairava amṛtaṃ kuru amṛteśvarabhairavāya huṃ
children.translated_text: aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ, O <s>Amṛteśvarabhairava</s>, make nectar; to <s>Amṛteśvarabhairava</s>, huṃ.

children.text: sauḥ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā
children.translated_text: sauḥ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā.
sauḥ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ.
By this mantra a man quickly obtains accomplishment.
<s>Śrī Bhairavī</s>:
O god of gods, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, you have now spoken
of divine <s>rasāyanas</s> that grant accomplishments, O <s>Maheśvara</s>.
They indeed grant accomplishment of bodies and kalpas after a long time.
O god, O <s>Parameśvara</s>, tell that by which accomplishment arises at once,
even for those whose limbs are deficient, excessive, lacking, or wasted,
and for stammerers, the mute, the hunchbacked, and lepers,
for the blind, the lame, the weak, and those whose selves are broken by old age,
for those always afflicted by disease, for eunuchs, the emaciated, and the bewildered in mind,
and even for those joined with spirits, ghosts, piśācas, epilepsy, and madness,
for men who, through misfortune, have only life remaining, giving them bodily perfection.
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s>:

children.text: śrutvā tadbhairavīvākyaṃ sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā priye
children.translated_text: Having heard that speech of <s>Bhairavī</s>, he said: You have asked well, O dear one.
I shall teach such bodily perfection, O fair-faced one.
Five pills, consisting of the five elements, should be made, O dear one.
The sixth pill should be of the nature of life, joined with the body and the furnace.
When a maiden in her season has prolonged intercourse,
the blood and semen situated in her excellent organ become the essence of the ether element.

children.text: tasyāḥ sadyaḥ prasūtasya viṣṭhā putrasya mārutam
children.translated_text: The excrement of the son just born from her is the wind element.
Her menstrual blood is solely the essence whose nature is the fire element.
The blood of that child is declared to be the water element.
The whole body of that newborn is called the earth element.
And the semen of the practitioner of <s>sūta</s> becomes the life element, O dear one.
One should apply, one karṣa at a time, <s>sūta</s> capable of transmuting ten millionfold.
Among each element one should triturate them with sprinkling.
Having made balls from them, one should set the six <s>rasas</s> apart separately.
The body should be raised to the measure of a man, and its length should be half of that.
A cauldron made of copper should be six finger-breadths in thickness.
A furnace with four openings should be made, and the cauldron above it
should be held perfectly steady; inside it one should fill, O dear one,
cow's ghee and great oil, these two in equal portions.
One should worship the guardians of the ten directions, the yoginīs, and the maiden,

children.text: śrīguruṃ siddhacakraṃ ca bhairavaṃ bhairavīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: the revered guru, the circle of siddhas, <s>Bhairava</s> and <s>Bhairavī</s>,
<s>Gaṇādhipa</s>, <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>, and one's own chosen deity,
the nine planets, fire, brahmins, astrologers, and excellent physicians,
and also those who create obstacles: spirits, ghosts, and piśācas,
yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, mantra-knowers, and one's own people.
One should satisfy them with wine and meat, with garments, ornaments, and gold.
With divine things dear to each of them, one should cast bali-offerings in the directions.
With four curved tubes one should blow upon it with a khadira-wood fire.

children.text: phenahīnam adhūmaṃ ca saṃtaptaṃ ca yadā bhavet
children.translated_text: When it has become free of foam, smokeless, and thoroughly heated,
having bowed to the revered guru, one's own deity, the moon, sun, fire, and stars,
and the worlds, one should place the body in the cauldron.

children.text: jñātvā samyagdrutaṃ dehaṃ pārthivākhyaṃ rasaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Knowing that the body is fully melted, one should add the <s>rasa</s> called earth.

children.text: dhamedgāḍhaṃ prayatnena tatkalkaṃ ca yadā bhavet
children.translated_text: He should blow strongly and carefully; when that becomes a paste,
then he should add the little <s>rasa</s> called the water element and bring it to redness.
Afterward he should add the <s>rasa</s> of the fire element, and it will become flesh.
He should put in what is called the wind element; he should cast that <s>rasa</s> there.
It obtains a white color; then he should add the ether element,
and he should add the <s>rasa</s>-principle called the life element, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Then he should add <s>rasa</s>; it becomes equal to unalloyed gold.
It becomes living and perfected; he should utter the syllable huṃ three times.
Like the risen disk of the sun, he is of great intelligence and valor,
great in body, great in brilliance, and possessing the immense strength of ten thousand elephants.
Rich in beauty like <s>Manmatha</s>, in speech he is equal to <s>Vāgīśvarī</s>.
In intellect he is equal to <s>Jīva</s>; he is prosperous like <s>Viṣṇu</s> and comparable to <s>Dhanada</s>.
In generosity and in wrath he is the fire of time; in depth, the great ocean.

children.text: sraṣṭā hartā ca goptā ca sarvānugrāhakaḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is creator, destroyer, protector, lord, and giver of grace to all.
With divine sight and a diamond body, he is this <s>Bhairava</s> manifestly.
There is something half a yojana wide, adorned with golden tinkling bells,
beautiful with moving bees and adorned with many jewels,
embraced by golden garlands and delightful with the sound of bells,
filled with divine radiance, great sound, conches, and trumpets,
together with instruments such as vīṇās, flutes, mṛdaṅgas, and murajas,
crowded with many kinds of cymbals and other divine sounds,
and joined with singing kinnaras, gandharvas, and likewise kiṃpuruṣas.
Wearing shining jeweled armlets, necklaces, bracelets, and rings,
fitted with golden anklets and adorned with divine ornaments,
decorated with divine garlands and anointed with divine perfumes,
wearing divine garments, lovely in form, and bewildered by intoxicated passion,
divine women then come near him and speak as follows.

children.text: kiṃ karma siddhasaṃkhedās tvādeśo deva dīyatām ||
children.translated_text: What rite is to be done? O god, let your command be given to those weary for siddhi.
A further hundred thousand siddha-maidens attend him;

children.text: yatra yāsyati tatraiva cānuyāmo vayaṃ vṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: wherever he goes, there indeed we, chosen by him, follow.
Accepting, again and again, various divine dwellings adorned with gold and rubies,
and divine baths and drinks,
he roams at will through all the worlds, beginning with those of <s>Vajrī</s>.
He is worshiped by hosts of gods and siddhas, just as this <s>Bhairava</s> is.
Enjoying all pleasures and free from hunger and thirst,
he becomes the enjoyer of a hundred thousand yoginīs, meditating on happiness.
Even at the end of a great kalpa, when this world has wasted away, O fair-faced one,

children.text: līyate parame vyomni līyante yatra devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: he dissolves in the supreme ether, where the deities dissolve.
By the power of this rasa, it is called <s>Bhūtakālāntaka</s>,
and this is unpierceable, indivisible, and unburnable, O dear one.
O <s>Maheśvarī</s>, this grants siddhi for every rasāyana;
this king of mantras, which bestows rasa-siddhi, will now be taught.

children.text: aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ śrībhairava ||
children.translated_text: Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ, <s>Śrībhairava</s>.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s>:
At <s>Śrīśaila</s>, varied siddhi is heard to be easy,

children.text: sulabhā śrūyate deva tāṃ brūhi vividhāṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: bringing immediate proof. O god, O lord, tell me of those various powers.
<s>Śrībhairava</s>:

children.text: vakṣyāmi śṛṇu tatsarvaṃ sadyaḥ siddhikaraṃ priye
children.translated_text: I shall tell all that; listen, O dear one, for it brings siddhi at once.
More than <s>Kailāsa</s>, <s>Mandara</s>, <s>Meru</s>, <s>Vindhya</s>, and <s>Himālaya</s>,
more than <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Malaya</s>, <s>Sahya</s>, and even <s>Dṛśyagiri</s>,
divine <s>Śrīparvata</s> is supreme, served by lords of siddhas and yogins.

children.text: tatra tīrthāni sarvāṇi sarāṃsi saritaḥ priye
children.translated_text: There, O dear one, are all tīrthas, lakes, and rivers,
liṅgas that grant siddhi, and creepers, stones, and trees.
So too there are soils, bulbs, waters, leaves, flowers, and fruits,
and such things as these, all of them producers of every siddhi.
I am <s>Śrīparvata</s>, O <s>Īśānī</s>; I myself am that mountain.

children.text: sthāvaraṃ māmakaṃ rūpaṃ viddhi taṃ surasevitam ||
children.translated_text: Know that immovable form, served by the gods, to be mine.

children.text: asminyadasti nānyatra yadanyatra sthitaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: What exists here is nowhere else, and what is established elsewhere is here.
The divine liṅga, fit to be touched, is the stainless jyotirliṅga,
famed as <s>Śrīmallikārjuna</s>, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
On the left side of this liṅga stands <s>Ghaṇṭāsiddheśvara</s>.

children.text: ghaṇṭā vilambate dvāre tīrthakuṇḍaṃ ca vidyate
children.translated_text: A bell hangs at the doorway, and there is a sacred pool.
The rite should be performed by three fasting men, wakeful and untiring.
On the night of the dark fourteenth lunar day one should bathe <s>Śiva</s> continuously.
One man should bring water from the pool, O dear one,
and another should ring the bell, O dear one, until the end of the four watches.
Pleased, this <s>Ghaṇṭāsiddheśvara</s> grants even them motion through the sky.
To the south of this <s>Ghaṇṭāsiddheśvara</s>, O dear one, one should dig
there to knee-depth; then soil with the brightness of rocanā is seen.
Gathering that soil, one should drink a karṣa-measure of it, O dear one,

children.text: kṣīrayuktāṃ ca saptāhaṃ sa sākṣādamaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: mixed with milk for seven days; he becomes visibly immortal.
In front of <s>Śrīgirīśa</s> there is a great elephant-shaped rock.
Day and night it oozes divine, fragrant, fine guggulu.
One should collect that in a bottle-gourd vessel with a palāśa ladle,
add sulfur to it, and eat a karṣa-measure.
Doing this every day for a month, he then obtains siddhi.
Ever blissful, youthful, and steady, he lives as long as the moon and stars.
Into molten <s>mlecchavadana</s> one should cast that guggulu;
then copper, in a proportion of one ten-millionth, becomes divine gold.
West of the god <s>Mallikārjuna</s> is <s>Candravāpī</s>.
On the full-moon day of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, the best sādhaka should perform the rite there.
Fearless and free from doubt, staying near the water,
he should recite the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra at night, without clothing.
At midnight, when the moon-water has been touched by the moon,
he should then place his own cupped hands at the opening of that tīrtha.
When the moon touches it and passes on, then he should take that water,
and the steadfast man should drink it immediately; he lives as long as the moon and stars.
That man becomes diamond-bodied, gentle in form, and peaceful in spirit.
At the eastern gate of <s>Śrīgiri</s> stands <s>Tripurāntaka</s>.
Near the god, in the region to the north, there is a tamarind tree.

children.text: dṛśyate tatra mūle tu svayaṃ śrībhairavaḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, at its root, <s>Śrībhairava</s> himself, the lord, is seen.
One should dig the earth in front of it to the measure of a man; then there is seen
a hot pool with blue water, granting divine siddhi.
One should tie the leaves of that tamarind tree in a cloth and cast them

children.text: kuṇḍe tasmiṃstadā tāni sthūlamīnā bhavanti ca ||
children.translated_text: into that pool; then they become large fish.
Taking them, a wise man should cook them in due order with tamarind wood.
He should discard their heads, bones, cavities, and entrails.
The sādhaka, desiring siddhi, should eat all the rest.
For a moment there is fainting because of it; afterward he awakens.
He sees an opening in the earth and lives for ten thousand divine years.
Two gavyūtis west of <s>Tripurāntaka</s>,
there is a village called <s>Maṇipalli</s>; to its western side
there is a certain mountain, and west of that an <s>Ekavāṭaka</s>.
It is seen there. One should enter it, face east, and then proceed.
Afterward, facing south, he should go the distance of ten bows.
There, stones shaped like mango fruits and shining with the brilliance of fire
should be taken and tied in a cloth; that cloth will turn red.
One should place that cloth, together with the stones, in milk.

children.text: tataḥ kṣīraṃ raktavarṇaṃ syāt pibet sādhakottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the milk becomes red in color; the best <s>sādhaka</s> should drink it.
After seven days <s>siddhi</s> arises: he has an adamantine body and great strength.
He lives as long as the moon and stars, for a whole kalpa, without diminution.
To the north of <s>Tripurānta</s> is the excellent <s>Kokilābila</s>,
illumining the world. There, after performing bodily purification,
the wise <s>sādhaka</s> should enter that cave by means of vomiting and the other purifications.
For a distance of ten bows there are stones there resembling cuckoos.

children.text: santi gṛhītvā tatpṛṣṭhe tilāḥ kṣiptāḥ sphuṭanti ca
children.translated_text: When they are taken, sesame seeds thrown on their backs split open.
Having seen this proof, one should rub those stones against one another
and throw them into milk; that milk becomes black.
One should drink that milk for one month, and he will become divine-bodied.
He lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>, free from wrinkles and gray hair.
In speed he is like the wind, and he sees openings in the earth.
In the eastern direction from <s>Tripurānta</s>, at a distance of one yojana,
there is the deity <s>Svargapurīnātha</s>; one should dig in front of him.
When the earth is dug knee-deep, there, like serpent hoods,
stones known by touch come forth, O fair-faced one.
To the west of the god <s>Tripurāntaka</s>, at a quarter yojana,
there is the entrance to a divine cave; there, within three bows,
one should go. There stands a black date-palm tree bearing fruit.

children.text: tatphalānāṃ rasaṃ pītvā tena mūrcchā bhavetkṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: After drinking the juice of its fruits, fainting occurs for a moment.
When he has awakened, he becomes perfected and lives as long as the moon and sun.
At the southern gate of <s>Śrīgiri</s>, <s>Vajreśvara</s> and <s>Sureśvara</s>
stand. One should dig the ground there; there are stones resembling śrīphala fruits.
They are touch-transforming stones; they should be gathered, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
There is one called <s>Rāmeśvara</s>; one should dig near him.
There the rudrākṣa-shaped stones become touch-transformers.
At the place of <s>Jyotiḥsiddhavaṭa</s>, to the south, a single tree
stands, named <s>Āvartaka</s>; near it, to the west,
there is a mountain. There one should dig up stones resembling palmyra fruits.
One should blow strongly upon those stones; all that becomes gold.
At its own southern gate is found <s>Kuṇḍaleśvara</s>.
Near him one should dig up the earth knee-deep and take out
red-gleaming stones, shaped like śrīphala fruits and capable of touch-transmutation.
Near the god <s>Puruṣeśvara</s> there is a pond.

children.text: guñjāriḍḍhau ca vidyete vṛkṣau tatpattram aśnīyāt
children.translated_text: There are two trees, guñjā and riḍḍhi; one should eat their leaves.
After seven days he becomes perfected, free from old age and death.
There, to the south of <s>Hastiśilā</s>, one should dig to the measure of a hand.
There jambu-fruit-shaped stones should be taken; they are called touch-stones.
It is known by the name <s>Hastiśiras</s>; it is also known as <s>Hastiśilā</s>.
At a distance of one yojana to its southern side,
there is <s>Chāyāchattra</s>, a form of <s>Śiva</s>, taught by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: vartulaṃ śatahastaṃ tu chidraṃ tasyāpyadho vrajet ||
children.translated_text: It is circular and one hundred hastas across; one should enter the opening beneath it.

children.text: na kaiściddṛśyate so'pi siddho bhavati tatkṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: He is not seen by anyone, and he becomes perfected at that very moment.
Equal to <s>Rudra</s>, he plays at will throughout the three worlds.
Or he may accomplish the set of eight <s>siddhis</s>, which grants every <s>siddhi</s>.
Magnetite, mica essence, gold, and <s>sūta</s> are successively higher in quality.

children.text: amlena mardayedgāḍhaṃ golaṃ kṛtvā tu veṣṭayet
children.translated_text: One should grind them thoroughly with an acid, make a ball, and wrap it.
Having tied that ball to the tip of a long bamboo, he should recite the mantra of glorious <s>Kālikā</s>.
He should recite and place it there by means of that <s>Chāyāchattra</s>.
Inside the ball tied to the tip of the bamboo, an auspicious pill arises.
He should hold it inside his mouth; instantly he becomes a sky-goer.
Having tied the stone, of palmyra-fruit size, in cloth and fastened it to the bamboo tip,
he should place this in <s>Chāyāchattra</s> and anoint both eyes with those two substances.

children.text: nidhiṃ paśyati bhūmisthaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: He sees treasure situated in the earth; no doubt should be entertained here.
He should place a sword tied to the bamboo tip in <s>Chāyāchattra</s>.
He should empower it with the <s>Kālikā</s> mantra and hold that sword in his hand.
The steadfast man becomes conqueror of the three worlds, a hero in the three worlds.
Having tied rocana pigment to the bamboo tip, he should place it in <s>Chāyāchattra</s>.

children.text: lalāṭe tilakaṃ tena kṛtvā lokaṃ vaśaṃ nayet
children.translated_text: Making a forehead mark with it, he brings the world under his control.
In the same way he should place srotoñjana and collyrium in <s>Chāyāchattra</s>.
Anointed with that collyrium, he is not seen even by the gods.
Having bound sandals as before, he should deposit them in <s>Chāyāchattra</s>.
Having put the sandals on his feet, wherever he wishes

children.text: prayātuṃ tatra tatraiva nayatastaṃ ca pāduke ||
children.translated_text: to go, the sandals carry him there and there exactly.
As before, he should place a red cloth in <s>Chāyāchattra</s>.
He should wrap himself in that cloth, and he becomes invisible at once.
When the cloth is cast off afterward, he is seen; there is no doubt.
Having combined magnetite, mica, gold, and mercury, he should grind them together.
The wise man should make it into a ball, wrap it in cloth, and tie it to the bamboo tip.
He should place it in <s>Chāyāchattra</s> and empower it with the <s>Kālī</s> mantra.
This becomes touch-transmuting; it is true, true, O fair-faced one.
At the western gate of <s>Śrīśaila</s> stands the god <s>Brahmeśvara</s>.

children.text: durgā devī ca tatrasthā sopānaṃ navamaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: The goddess <s>Durgā</s> is also stationed there, and there is the ninth stairway.

children.text: tuṅgabhadrāyāṃ ca nadyāṃ tato brahmeśvarasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Then, at the river <s>Tuṅgabhadrā</s> and at <s>Brahmeśvara</s>,
in the region of the gate, there are these four touchstones, the color of green gram.

children.text: ciñcāvanaṃ ca nairṛtye sthitaṃ brahmeśvarasya hi ||
children.translated_text: To the southwest of <s>Brahmeśvara</s> there is indeed a tamarind grove.

children.text: kuṇḍaṃ ca vidyate tatra ciñcādhaścaṇḍikā sthitā
children.translated_text: There is a pool there, and <s>Caṇḍikā</s> stands beneath the tamarind tree.
Standing constantly on one foot, one should collect the fruit of that tamarind.
One should tie them in a cloth, cast them into the pool, and bathe.
At the end of the bath one should take them up; by then they have become fish.
One should cook them with that fuel, but discard the bones, tails, and heads.
One should give one portion to the god and a second to guests.
One should eat the third portion oneself; in a moment one becomes unconscious.

children.text: divyo bhavati siddho'yaṃ bilaṃ paśyati bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: This man becomes divine and siddha; he sees an opening in the earth.
Freed from old age and death, he is not to be slain even by the deathless gods.
North of <s>Alampura</s> there is a village called <s>Bhīmapāduka</s>.

children.text: pārśve tu tasya grāmasya hastamātraṃ dharāṃ khanet
children.translated_text: Beside that village one should dig the earth to the depth of a hand.

children.text: pāṣāṇā hi phaṇākārāḥ sparśasaṃjñā bhavanti te ||
children.translated_text: There are stones shaped like serpent hoods; they are known as touchstones.
There is a goddess named <s>Yogīśvarī</s> there, the deity of <s>Alampura</s>.
In front of her is a lovely cave; in the middle of it one should dig the ground.
Stones resembling splits should be taken with cat's dung.
Having mixed them, one should put them into molten tin; it becomes silver.
The best practitioner should drink those stones with honey and ghee.
He becomes divine and siddha, a conqueror of wrinkles, gray hair, and death.
At the northern gate of <s>Śrīparvata</s> there is a god named <s>Maheśvara</s>.
A bee-mango tree stands there; one should collect its fruit.
One should split it open, and bees come out from inside it.
They are alive; then one should remove all those bees.
One should cook those fruits in alkali and drink milk as much as possible.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ mūrcchā bhavettena mūrcchānte ca payaḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: Because of that, unconsciousness occurs for a moment; at the end of the faint, one should drink milk.
One should do this carefully for twenty-one days.
By it he obtains a diamond body, free from wrinkles and gray hair.
Knowing the truth of the Veda and Vedāṅgas, he lives as long as the sun and stars.
At once, O dear one, he becomes equal to the swift wind.
With the fruit of that mango itself, after the bees have been removed,
a thousand palas of molten tin becomes silver.
One should make a cavity in a mango fruit and remove the bee.
Inside it one should place a karṣa of mercury and essence of black mica.

children.text: nirudhya vaktraṃ samṛdā gomayena ca lepayet
children.translated_text: Having sealed the opening with good clay, one should smear it with cow dung.
One should dry it in the shade and cook it for one watch with its own wood.
After letting it cool naturally, the wise man should keep it in his mouth.
He obtains the state of a sky-goer, free from wrinkles and gray hair.
He lives until the moon and sun endure, and his eloquence equals <s>Brahmā</s>'s.
One should place mercury and essence of black mica in the mango fruit as before.
After coating it with cow dung and clay, one should heat it in a closed firing with forest cow-dung cakes.

children.text: svaśītaṃ pāradaṃ grāhyaṃ madhusarpirbhir yutaṃ lihet ||
children.translated_text: When naturally cooled, the mercury should be taken and licked with honey and ghee.

children.text: guñjāmātraṃ ca māsāntaṃ bālo bhavati mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: A man who takes a guñjā measure for a month becomes young.
In strength he is like a fresh elephant, and he lives for one day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
North of <s>Śrīgirīśa</s> there is <s>Śuklaparvata</s>.
Having worshiped with the five offerings, the practitioner becomes famous in the three worlds.
With the mantra of oṃ huṃ phaṭ, the practitioner, free from wavering thought,
should see in the western quarter a flying palace in the sky.
It is divine, beautiful in many ways, and immediately produces certainty.
Then he should go to the western quarter, after crossing the great river.
A cave is seen there; he should enter it facing west.
There he should go three yojanas, fearless, alone, and without wavering.
A plantain grove of five yojanas is seen there.
There is a lake filled with clear water, and in its middle a blessed seat.
He should see that great, divine seat, resembling crystal.
He should utter this mantra and perform a prostration like a staff.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ vidyāvāgīśvarādhipataye hrīṃ oṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the lord of knowledge and speech, hrīṃ oṃ svāhā.
Having bathed there, O fair-faced one, he should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
The practitioner may live on bulbs and roots, or as he wishes, O dear one.
In the middle of the lion-throne he should see the god, resembling crystal,
four-armed and three-eyed, bearing the pure crescent moon.
He is blue-necked, adorned with snakes, and has an axe and a deer as weapons.
He grants boons and fearlessness; he is excellent and worshiped by eminent learned gods.
One should bow to him with eight limbs, again and again, with mantras and hymns.

children.text: tataḥ prasannaḥ sa śivo varaṃ datte yathepsitam ||
children.translated_text: Then, pleased, that <s>Śiva</s> grants whatever boon is desired.
There are a hundred shrines there, and nine hundred wells.
There are just as many pleasure gardens, <s>Nandana</s> groves, and forests.

children.text: vāpyo navaśataṃ santi vivaraṃ caiva tatsamam
children.translated_text: There are nine hundred stepwells, and just as many caverns.
There are as many wish-fulfilling trees; all these grant siddhi.
There dwells a famous yakṣiṇī named <s>Mohalī</s>, who grants desired things.

children.text: brūte sā dehi me bhuktiṃ siddhiṃ tvaṃ yadi vāñchasi ||
children.translated_text: She says, “Give me enjoyment, if you desire siddhi.”
One should say to her here, “O goddess, I will give you enjoyment.”

children.text: kandamūlaṃ phalaṃ tasyai pāyasaṃ vā samarpayet ||
children.translated_text: One should offer her bulbs, roots, fruit, or milk-rice.

children.text: sā yakṣiṇī punarvakti yāvadbhuñje sutaṃ mama
children.translated_text: That <s>yakṣiṇī</s> speaks again: "As long as I eat my son,

children.text: dhārayer vakṣasā tāvadvaraṃ dāsyāmi te mahat ||
children.translated_text: hold him against your breast for that long; I shall give you a great boon.

children.text: visṛjestvaṃ yadi tadā bhavantaṃ hanmi nirdayā
children.translated_text: But if you let him go, then I shall kill you mercilessly."
If <s>Cīra</s>, freed from fear, should act in this way, he becomes a possessor of siddhi.
He should go toward the northern quarter, half a yojana from that lake.
There, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>, stands a divine sandalwood tree, full of flowers.
By merely smelling its flowers, hunger and thirst do not afflict him.
Or he may eat one of its fruits in the prescribed manner.
A man becomes diamond-bodied merely by eating it.
He should go a quarter of a yojana to the southern side of the lake.
There a <s>Nandana</s> grove is seen, thick with pomegranate trees.
Whoever eats its fruit lives for a thousand yugas.
On the eastern side of that same lake, for about half a krośa,
there is a <s>Nandana</s> forest furnished with dhātrī fruits.
The wise man should eat that fruit, and he lives through three cosmic dissolutions.

children.text: sarasastasya bhāge ca paścime yojanaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: On the western side of that lake he should go one yojana.
There is a <s>Nandana</s> forest filled with śrīphala trees.
The one by whom that fruit is eaten lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
There in that very <s>Nandana</s> forest is a dark-blue liṅga.
By the path of its northern doorway a mighty nāga enters.
There he is great, furnished with seven hoods, fierce, and terrifying.
The sādhaka, seeking siddhi, should carefully bow to such a great nāga,
repeatedly uttering the sound "huṃ huṃ."
The great nāga speaks thus: "I grant you invisibility.

children.text: yāhi svaṃ paścimadvāraṃ divyā kanyāsti tatra vai
children.translated_text: Go to your western door; there indeed is a divine maiden."
Uttering the great mantra, the sādhaka should go there itself.

children.text: dadāti hāraṃ sā kanyā praveśaṃ na dadāti ca
children.translated_text: That maiden gives a necklace, but she does not grant entrance.

children.text: hāraṃ gale dhārayettaṃ tena sārasvataṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: He should wear that necklace on his neck; by it he becomes sārasvata, endowed with eloquence and learning.
From there he should go to the southern gate, which is exceedingly terrifying.
There he should see one with loose hair, crooked eyes, and naked body,
holding a mace, dark-blue in color: <s>Śrīkṣetrapālaka</s>.
Having seen him, he should bow, reciting the mantra and hymns for the removal of obstacles.
The mantra ends with hā hā, he he, huṃ huṃ, phaṭ, huṃ, and svāhā.
By this very mantra <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> too is quickly pleased.

children.text: svāgatvaṃ vitaratyeṣa praveśaṃ na dadāti hi
children.translated_text: He grants welcome, but he does not give entrance.

children.text: atha vrajet pūrvadiśo dvāraṃ tatra gaṇādhipam ||
children.translated_text: Then he should go to the eastern gate; there he should worship <s>Gaṇādhipa</s>.
There the excellent sādhaka should worship him as he stands, and then enter.
A divine liṅga is seen, and there also a beautiful bow.
With the mantra consisting of oṃ and huṃ he should worship that <s>Īśvara</s>.
The wise man should fast there itself and recite through day and night.

children.text: pratyakṣo bhavatīśāno dadāti hi varaṃ param
children.translated_text: <s>Īśāna</s> becomes manifest and gives the supreme boon.
Such and other siddhis exist in the <s>Kadalīvana</s>.
There, on the eastern side of the lake, at a distance of one yojana,
is the cave of <s>Padmāvatī</s>, with letters written on its doorway.
The sādhaka, purified by vomiting and the other purifications, should enter there.
There he should go a hundred bow-lengths within; there is a little drum.
Having seen it, he should play it; then, on hearing that sound,

children.text: padmāvatī svayaṃ yāti hyamṛtaṃ ca dadāti ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Padmāvatī</s> herself comes and gives nectar.
By drinking it, this man becomes siddha and obtains immortality.
Then she approaches him and requests him:
"Come near me, to my divine abode filled with five hundred maidens.
Stay there and become my husband, lord, for the span of <s>Brahmā</s>'s life.

children.text: tadante śāśvataṃ sthānaṃ gamiṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: At its end you will go to an eternal place; there is no doubt."
To the southeast of that eastern tank there is
the god <s>Kadambeśvara</s>, and before him a kadamba tree.
There he should take the leaves and smear them with bitter oil.
Or the wise man should smear them with oil produced from its seeds and cook them.
With the wood of that tree they become fish; he should place them in a copper vessel.
Avoiding the bones, head, and tail, he should eat them with honey and ghee.
By consuming that, he becomes siddha, equal to <s>Rudra</s>, and very strong.
That tree is also on the riverbank near <s>Kuṇḍaleśa</s>.
By the same method as before, siddhi comes about, and not otherwise.
To the north there is <s>Puṣpagiri</s>, and <s>Kapoteśa</s> is there.
He should make circumambulation three times and ascend its summit.
That sādhaka obtains the state of a khecara, a sky-goer; there is no doubt.
To its northeast is situated the gateway called <s>Chedikīdvāraka</s>.
Facing north, he should enter there respectfully for the distance of three bow-lengths.
A man should grind a mouse-shaped stone in buttermilk and drink it.
He quickly falls into a swoon, and then lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By mere touch he pierces all metals; there is no doubt.

children.text: upoṣya ca divā naktaṃ devāgre siddhimāpnuyāt
children.translated_text: Having fasted by day and night before the deity, he obtains siddhi.
A pair of deities is found to the south of <s>Kapoteśvara</s>.
He should dig to the depth of his navel between the two deities.
There are stones there resembling gorocanā; he should take them.

children.text: piṣṭvā kṣaudraghṛtābhyāṃ ca pibedyaḥ so'maro bhavet
children.translated_text: Whoever grinds them with honey and ghee and drinks becomes immortal.
To the northwest of <s>Kapoteśa</s>, he should dig one hand-span deep.
There are pigeon-shaped stones, known by the name of touch-stones.
Having worshiped the deity, he should collect one of them.
To the northeast of <s>Śrīgirīśa</s> there is indeed <s>Bhṛgupātana</s>.
Near it is a divine pool; he should collect clay from that.
He should heat that clay, mixed with the five products of the cow, with a fire of khadira wood.
From that, blue metal falls out, when it has been heated with honey and ghee.
He should sprinkle that after it has been washed seven times, and place that ball in his mouth.
The accomplished one becomes equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, all-knowing, all-pervading, and happy.
At a krośa from the summit of the <s>Bhṛgupātana</s> mountain is <s>Dadhikavāṭaka</s>.
In front of it there always stands the mountain named <s>Acchatailagiri</s>.
To its west there is a cave, and within it, at five bow-lengths,

children.text: gate paśyettatra kuṇḍaṃ tatra lākṣāsamaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: he should see a pool there; in it is rasa like lac.
He should take it in a bottle-gourd vessel; that mercury pierces ten million times.
The enclosure of <s>Candragupta</s> is to the west of <s>Śrīgirīśa</s>.

children.text: tanmadhye vidyate veśma caityaṃ tatpūrvataḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: Within it there is a building, and a caitya stands to its east.
East of the caitya is a divine stone, like a mung bean, known as a touch-stone.
There stands the enchanting tusker; mounting it with concentration,

children.text: pṛṣṭhāttasya tṛṇaṃ grāhyaṃ tatsarvaṃ kāñcanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: one should take grass from its back; all of that becomes gold.
On the northern side of that elephant he should dig the ground knee-deep.
There are stones like jambū fruits; they are known as touch-stones.
He should dig the earth beneath the elephant to the depth of a knee; then he will obtain
a perfected, excellent triangular pill that produces piercing a hundred thousand times.
To the northwest of <s>Mallinātha</s>, after bowing, there is another <s>Devahrada</s>.
There is a tīrtha there, and stones like mung beans, known as touch-stones.

children.text: liṅgaṃ kūrmopamaṃ tatra sparśasaṃjñaṃ śubhaṃ priye
children.translated_text: There is an auspicious liṅga like a tortoise, known as a touch-stone, dear one.
On the full-moon day under Kṛttikā he should worship it and collect it.
Two gavyūtis from that is remembered the excellent <s>Nīlavanī</s>.

children.text: tasyā liṅgaṃ ca salilaṃ nīlavarṇaṃ praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: Its liṅga and its water, blue in color, are praised.
Stones resembling the aśvāmra and the crow are touch-piercing stones.
Within the temple he should dig the ground to the depth of a knee.
Mouse-shaped stones are there, known as touch-stones.
To the southwest of <s>Śrīgirīśa</s> it is famed by the name <s>Guṇḍīprabhā</s>.

children.text: tasyāgragarte pītābhāṃ mṛttikāṃ ca puṭe dahet
children.translated_text: In the pit before it he should burn yellowish clay in a covered crucible.
From that comes forth gold, supreme and fit for the pure deity.
There too stands the <s>Bhṛṅgacūta</s>, giving siddhi as before.

children.text: tathā tambīpure cāsti tīrthe ca vipule śubham ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, in <s>Tambīpura</s> and at the broad tīrtha, there is something auspicious.

children.text: sadāphalaṃ tu vikhyātaṃ tasyāḥ pūrvottare sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man should know the famed <s>Sadāphala</s> to its northeast.
In the southwestern region of <s>Śrīgiri</s> it is known as <s>Mahānanda</s>.
The wise man should go by the bell-road; to its northeast,
there stands <s>Kālakaṇṭheśa</s>, and before him a small pool.
There is a siddhi of mercury resembling the indragopa insect.

children.text: bhavanti sapta lohāni svarṇaṃ taptāni sekataḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the seven metals are heated and sprinkled, they become gold.
To the northeast of <s>Śrīgirīśa</s> there is <s>Śrīmālinīśvara</s>.
In its northern direction is the well-known mountain called <s>Tūmāparvata</s>.

children.text: tasyāgre ca triśūlābhāḥ santi darbhāḥ śubhaṅkarāḥ
children.translated_text: Before it there are auspicious darbha grasses shaped like tridents.
Beneath that he should dig to the depth of the navel and take blue clay.
He should cook it with akṣa wood, in due order, for the deity, the guest, and the fire.
He should allot one share each, and take the fourth share himself.
As a siddha, possessed of great strength and valor, he lives for ten thousand kalpas.
Near <s>Ileśvara</s> there stands <s>Koṭīśvara</s>.
Before it are flowers and leaves that produce touch-piercing.
There the god <s>Acaleśvara</s> is an excellent producer of touch-piercing.
One yojana to its south is <s>Cāmareśvara</s>.
From there there is a gold-stone, and above it human flesh.
Or the wise man should throw cow-flesh there and kindle it with jujube wood.

children.text: prātaḥ kāñcanasaṅkāśā dṛśyate sā śilā tadā ||
children.translated_text: In the morning that stone is then seen to have the appearance of gold.
A cloth infused with the menstrual fluid of a woman whose flowers have freshly appeared
should be rolled on that stone and thrown into a vessel with a little water.
By mere contact with it, the paste becomes supreme gold.
Where <s>Śrīguru</s> is, there also are stones situated in lump-like ground.
He should eat a karṣa measure of that powder together with triphalā.
Conquering wrinkles and gray hair within a month, he lives as long as the moon and stars.
To the southwest of <s>Śrīgirīndra</s> is the lord <s>Paṭāhakarṇa</s>.
In its northeastern region, at twenty-five bow-lengths,
he should dig two hands deep at a stone standing two hands high.
He should collect those stones, shaped like lidded earthen bowls.

children.text: kurvīta tān agnivarṇān siñcyāt kūṣmāṇḍajair dravaiḥ
children.translated_text: He should make them fire-colored and sprinkle them with liquids from kūṣmāṇḍa gourds.
From their midst he should give a share of fresh butter to the deity.
One share should be given to a guest, and one share he himself should lick.

children.text: divā naktaṃ bhavenmūrcchā vinidro bhavati svayam ||
children.translated_text: By day and by night there will be fainting; he himself becomes sleepless.
Free from wrinkles and gray hair, a man lives for ten thousand years.
This is the second stairway of <s>Sparśakānta</s>, dear one.
On both sides of that deity all the stones are white and yellow.

children.text: sparśāḥ sarvā bhavantyete teṣu caikaṃ samāharet ||
children.translated_text: All these are touch-stones; among them he should collect one.

children.text: prācyāṃ hi tasya devasya samīpe kūpamasti ca
children.translated_text: To the east, near that deity, there is a well.
There are stones resembling frogs, and they are known as touch-stones.
And to the north of that <s>Īśvara</s> there is a great mountain of liṅgas.
In the direction north of that there is an east-flowing river.
On the western side of the river there is indeed a tawny liṅga.
There is a pool containing the water of <s>Pūrṇaśaila</s>, an instant-piercing one.
Two yojanas south of <s>Maheśa</s> stands <s>Caṇḍikā</s>.
She is well known by the name <s>Piṇḍikā</s>; from her northwest corner
there is a cave, and in its middle are stones the color of mung beans.
Some resemble pathyā fruits; all of them are called touch-stones.
Now the procedure for all the touch-stones found here is stated.

children.text: yadi sthūlaṃ peṣayettaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ mūṣāntareṇa hi ||
children.translated_text: If it is large, one should grind it fine inside a crucible.
O dear one, one should place all metals in that and melt them.
All of that becomes gold; in this way he may make as much as he wishes.
If it is small, he should throw it among all molten metals.
By its touch all metals indeed pass into the state of gold.
In the northwest, at the tīrtha of <s>Mallinātha</s>, there is one called <s>Sarveśvara</s>.
In the southern direction from it, two yojanas along the royal road,

children.text: gate ḍoṃgalikā tatra dṛśyate tasya mūrdhani
children.translated_text: when one has gone, <s>Ḍoṃgalikā</s> is seen there; on its summit
there are fruits of black dhātrī, and one should eat them.
For seven days, to satisfaction, he becomes diamond-bodied.
Freed from old age and death, he lives for three hundred kalpas.
South of that, in the great forest of <s>Kākalārī</s>,
there is a clump of plantains; the sādhaka should enter there.
He should go just half a krośa, and a pool of rasa (mercury) is seen.
When it is placed in a gourd vessel, that rasa becomes koṭivedhin, able to transmute ten millionfold.
A peacock made of stone, blue in color, is seen there.
In front of its mouth is a pool, a handspan across and very blue.

children.text: śuṣkavaṃśaṃ ca tanmadhye kṣaṇaṃ kṣiptaṃ navaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: A dry bamboo, thrown into it for an instant, becomes fresh.

children.text: patraṃ puṣpaṃ dinaikena bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In one day it certainly produces leaves and flowers; there is no doubt.

children.text: tatra prasthaṃ rasaṃ kṣiptvā tāvanmātraṃ jalaṃ haret
children.translated_text: After putting a prastha of rasa there, he should take the same amount of water.

children.text: madhutulyaṃ pibettaṃ ca mūrcchā bhavati tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: He should drink it like honey, and fainting occurs at that very moment.
In a moment he regains consciousness and lives for a thousand yugas.
In the southeast of <s>Śrīgiri</s> is the sky-going siddha of <s>Ghaṭikā</s>.

children.text: asti tasya puro bhūmau pañcahastaṃ khanetsudhīḥ
children.translated_text: In front of it, on the ground, the wise man should dig five hastas deep.
Stones shaped like badara fruits are found there, granting motion through the sky.

children.text: ekaṃ vaktre sadā dhāryaṃ siddhaiḥ khegatilipsubhiḥ
children.translated_text: One should always hold one in the mouth, as siddhas do when they desire sky-going.
At <s>Śrīśaila</s>, the procedure for all the siddhis that have been described is now stated.
Having first performed mantra-nyāsa, he should afterwards recite the mantra one lakh times.
With the one ending in <s>Aghora</s>, he quickly obtains each particular siddhi.
oṃ hrīṃ, homage to <s>Mahāparvatavāsinī</s>, for the heart.
oṃ hrīṃ, to <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, for the head, svāhā.
oṃ hrīṃ, to <s>Raudrī</s>, for the topknot, vaṣaṭ.
oṃ hrīṃ, to <s>Kanakakuṇḍalinī</s>, for the armor, huṃ.
oṃ hrīṃ, to <s>Saṃjīvinī</s>, for the eyes, vauṣaṭ.
oṃ hrīṃ, to <s>Mālinī</s>, for the missile, phaṭ.
He should place "oṃ huṃ, homage to <s>Śiva</s>" on the two feet.
"oṃ vaṃ, homage to <s>Vāmadeva</s>" on the two shanks.
"oṃ paṃ, homage to <s>Padminī</s>" on the secret place.
"oṃ kāṃ, homage to <s>Kanyākumārī</s>" on the navel.
"oṃ glauṃ namaḥ" on the belly.

children.text: oṃ drāṃ hrīṃ durgāyai namaḥ urasi
children.translated_text: "oṃ drāṃ hrīṃ, homage to <s>Durgā</s>" on the chest.
"oṃ huṃ, homage to <s>Vindhyavāsinī</s>" at the base of the throat.
"oṃ laṃ namaḥ" on the neck.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṣṭabhujāyai namaḥ bhujayoḥ
children.translated_text: "oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to <s>Aṣṭabhujā</s>" on the arms.
"oṃ huṃ, homage to <s>Sarvatomukhinī</s>" on the face.
"oṃ, homage to <s>Prakāśikā</s>" on the eyes.
"oṃ, homage to <s>Mahiṣamardinī</s>" on the ears.

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ sarvāṅgasundaryai namaḥ mūrdhni nyaset
children.translated_text: He should place "oṃ hrāṃ, homage to <s>Sarvāṅgasundarī</s>" on the head.
Having thus made protection for the limbs, he should worship the kṣetra.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namo bhagavati sarveśvari devi namo maṇḍalavāsini krāṃ krīṃ krūṃ hana hana paca paca matha matha śīghram āveśaya śīghramāveśaya ehyehi bhuvanavandite svāhā
children.translated_text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage, O blessed <s>Sarveśvarī</s> goddess, homage, O <s>Maṇḍalavāsinī</s>; krāṃ krīṃ krūṃ, strike, strike; cook, cook; churn, churn; quickly possess, quickly possess; come, come, O <s>Bhuvanavanditā</s>, svāhā.
With this mantra he should invoke the deity.

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ tribhuvaneśvaryai namaḥ sāṃnidhyaṃ kuru kuru svāhā
children.translated_text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, homage to <s>Tribhuvaneśvarī</s>; make your presence, make your presence, svāhā.
With this mantra he should worship that kṣetra-deity.
oṃ, homage to the dark-colored <s>Aparāmukhī</s>, in the east.
oṃ, homage to <s>Sudhāvarṣiṇī</s>, in the southeast.
oṃ, homage to the mountain-like, dark-colored, fierce-faced one, in the south.
oṃ, homage to the dawn-sun-colored <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, in the southwest.
oṃ khaṃ, to the red-mountain-colored one,
homage to <s>Mahāmahiṣāsuramardinī</s>, in the west.
oṃ māṃ, homage to the all-colored <s>Huṅkāravāgdevī</s>, in the northwest.
oṃ, homage to <s>Siṃhavāhinī</s>, in the north.
oṃ, homage to <s>Śivāśivāśivā</s>, holding a trident, in the northeast.

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ klīṃ manonmanyai namaḥ ākāśe
children.translated_text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ klīṃ, homage to <s>Manonmanī</s>, in the sky.

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ mahāmohinyai namaḥ pātāle
children.translated_text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, homage to <s>Mahāmohinī</s>, in the underworld.

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraiṃ hroṃ hrauṃ hraṃ mahāvidye jambhaya jambhaya mohaya mohaya darśaya darśaya mūrchaya mūrchaya klīṃ matha matha ākarṣayākarṣaya huṃ phaṭ svāhā
children.translated_text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraiṃ hroṃ hrauṃ hraṃ, O <s>Mahāvidyā</s>, paralyze, paralyze; bewilder, bewilder; show, show; make faint, make faint; klīṃ, churn, churn; attract, attract; huṃ phaṭ svāhā.
And he should worship in the center.

children.text: evaṃ nyāsaṃ rakṣāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā tatkarmaṇi lakṣamekam aghoraṃ japet
children.translated_text: Having thus performed nyāsa, protection, and worship, he should recite the <s>Aghora</s> mantra one lakh times for that rite.
Then he obtains siddhi.
The mantra is as follows:

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hraṃ aghoratara prasphura prasphura prakaṭa prakaṭa kaha kaha śama śama jāta jāta daha daha pātaya pātaya oṃ hraiṃ hrāṃ hraṃ adhorāstrāya phaṭ
children.translated_text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hraṃ, O most terrible one, blaze forth, blaze forth; appear, appear; say, say; pacify, pacify; be born, be born; burn, burn; cast down, cast down; oṃ hraiṃ hrāṃ hraṃ, to the downward missile, phaṭ.
He should recite this mantra one hundred thousand times.

children.text: tataḥ svapne pratyakṣībhūya devatā varaṃ dadāti ||
children.translated_text: Then, becoming visible in a dream, the deity grants a boon.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s>:
Having bowed with her head to <s>Śambhu</s>, the supreme goddess praised him.
By your grace I have heard the divine <s>rasāyana</s> concerning all essences.
Now tell me, in order, the origin of <s>gandhaka</s>, its classes, and its purification,
as well as its use and the fruit of the <s>rasāyana</s>, O <s>Maheśvara</s>.
<s>Śrībhairava</s>:
Listen, goddess; I shall explain the <s>rasāyana</s> of <s>gandhaka</s>.
Long ago, O goddess, on <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, bright with wish-fulfilling creepers and trees,
strewn with clusters of many jewels and crowded with many flowers and fruits,
with women who were siddhas and vidyādharas, and with hosts of kinnarīs and apsarases,
you were sporting, exhilarated with delight, among many divine women,
with the amusement of flutes and vīṇās and with charming sounds of instruments,
with rhythms, with the sounds of jhallarī and ḍhakkā drums, and with hand-clapping.
In extreme bliss, O queen of gods, worshiped by the gods, you were dancing.

children.text: tadā ṛtumatī jātā susrāva ca rajo mahat
children.translated_text: Then you became menstruant, and a great flow of menstrual blood issued forth.
By that fragrant blood your garment became red.
Having set aside that blood-stained garment and bathed in the ocean of milk,
you went back to <s>Kailāsa</s>, surrounded by many wives of the immortals.
By the wind that blood-stained garment was cast into the ocean of milk.
There, O queen of gods, that garment sank and remained for a long time.
When the great ocean was churned, it arose together with the nectar,
gladdening the asuras and gods with its excellent natural fragrance.
Because of that very name, the foremost gods, headed by <s>Śakra</s>, said:

children.text: gandhako'yaṃ bhavatvasya nāmnā jātaṃ tu matpriye ||
children.translated_text: 'Let this be <s>gandhaka</s>; its name has arisen from this, my dear.'

children.text: caturvidhaṃ śoṇitaṃ te divyaṃ balakaraṃ param
children.translated_text: Your divine blood is fourfold, supreme and strength-giving.
This <s>gandhaka</s> is capable in the binding of mercury and in jāraṇa, digestive calcination.

children.text: rasendre ye guṇāḥ santi te guṇāḥ santi gandhake
children.translated_text: Whatever qualities exist in <s>rasendra</s>, mercury, those qualities exist in <s>gandhaka</s>.
So spoke those headed by <s>Indra</s>, delighted by the fragrance of <s>gandhaka</s>.
From then on, my dear, this <s>gandhaka</s> became famous in this world.
The red kind, resembling a hibiscus flower, is kṣatriya and the best, my dear.

children.text: pīto vaiśyo madhyamaḥ syācchveto vipro'dhamaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The yellow is vaiśya and should be middling; the white is remembered as a brahmin and inferior.
The black-colored kind is śūdra, my dear, and is the lowest of the low.
The red-colored kind pierces iron; the yellow-colored kind is for <s>rasāyana</s>.
The white-colored kind is for medicines, and the black is for applications on kuṣṭha and the like.
Now I shall explain the purification of <s>gandhaka</s>, which bestows siddhi.
There are tilaparṇī, ajamodā, brāhmī, bhṛṅgī, and dhattūra.

children.text: eteṣāṃ ca rasair bhāvyaṃ cūrṇitaṃ gandhakaṃ dinam
children.translated_text: Powdered <s>gandhaka</s> should be steeped for a day in the juices of these plants.
It should be placed in an iron vessel and cooked with an equal portion of ghee.
After cooking it over a gentle fire, he should put it into goat's milk.

children.text: gokṣīrājyaiḥ kiṃcidūnaṃ sthālyā vaktraṃ tu bandhayet ||
children.translated_text: With cow's milk and ghee, slightly less than full, he should bind the mouth of the pot.
When it has been tied with clean cloth, he should place that powder on top.
Above it he should seal a receiving vessel, and that should be set within a pit.
After giving it a gentle puṭa with forest fuel-cakes, the <s>gandhaka</s> melts.
Again he should steep it with tilaparṇī and the other juices and dry it three times.
Taking it, he should melt it seven times with fish bile.
He should steep it with powders of jālinī seeds and grind it thoroughly.
Then it should be steeped seven times in bhṛṅga juices in fierce sunlight.

children.text: jalaiḥ prakṣālya tat samyak śoṣayettatpunaḥ pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having washed it well with water, he should dry it and cook it again.

children.text: mṛdvagninā kāntapātre ghṛtākte tu kṣaṇaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: For a moment over a gentle fire, in an iron vessel smeared with ghee,
then, when it has been cast into the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, that <s>gandhaka</s> becomes purified.

children.text: rase rasāyane yoge yojyaṃ sukhakaraṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Used in <s>rasa</s>, in <s>rasāyana</s>, and in medicinal preparations, it becomes conducive to ease.
As stated before, he should perform bodily purification through vomiting and purgation.
At an auspicious moment and under an auspicious constellation, having worshiped supreme <s>Śiva</s>,
then <s>Gaṇādhipa</s>, <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>, the revered guru, and the physician, in order,
he should take one niṣka of triphalā powder and one niṣka of guggulu.
He should lick purified <s>gandhaka</s>, measured as one guñjā, with castor oil.
It should be taken every day by the very sequence of increasing by one guñjā,
up to sixteen days, reaching a measure of sixteen guñjās.
Then, at the end of the sixteenth day, it should be taken every day,
measured at sixteen guñjās, together with excellent, unsurpassed triphalā.
One who desires siddhi should not make an increase beyond this.
Thus, by a month's use, it removes the eighteen kinds of kuṣṭha.
It also removes prameha, abdominal tumors, cough, dyspnea, wasting disease, and fever,
wounds, fistulas, and other diseases, and the eighty disorders produced by vāta.
By two months' use it bestows abundant luster.
After three months, my dear, it becomes a pacifier of all diseases.
Then, by a six-month regimen, an old man obtains youth.
In this way, by a year's use, O <s>Śāmbhavī</s>, he becomes siddha.
By means of his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
The wise man should observe the procedure and the prohibitions just as stated before.
Whoever takes the meritorious and stainless <s>rasāyana</s> beginning with <s>rasa</s>,
he alone becomes one whose task is accomplished, honored even by the deities.
He has bathed at all sacred fords and is endowed with the fruit of all vows;
he obtains the fruit of all sacrifices, beginning with the horse sacrifice.
Blessed, most meritorious, excellent, and praised by wise men,
he is a knower of yoga, omniscient, a lord who bestows favor on all.
Pure, all-pervading, peaceful, heroic, shining with the quality of sattva,

children.text: tasya dehalayo nāsti hyadṛśyaḥ śivatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: there is no dissolution of his body; invisible, he goes to the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s> said:

children.text: śrutaṃ sarvaṃ mayā deva divyaṃ sarvarasāyanam
children.translated_text: O god, I have heard all this divine universal <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir practice).

children.text: viṣotpattiṃ ca jātiṃ ca sevāṃ vada ca tatphalam ||
children.translated_text: Now tell me the origin of poison, its classes, its use, and its result.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:
When the milk ocean was being churned, with <s>Mandara</s> made into the churning-stick,
by Siddhas, Kinnaras, lords of Guhyakas, Piśācas, serpents, and Rākṣasas,
by <s>Brahmā</s> and all the gods on one side, and by the chiefs of the Dānavas
and the mighty Daityas, vast in strength and prowess, on the other side,
then jewels were born, beginning with <s>Kaustubha</s>, and the wish-granting cow,
the wish-granting tree, great <s>Lakṣmī</s>, and the great elephant <s>Airāvata</s>;
also <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>, the Moon, and <s>Dhanvantari</s>, the best of physicians,
nectar, and divine creepers that bestow divine accomplishments.
Then, from the mouth of the serpent king, weary from the turning of <s>Mandara</s>,
there arose a flame of poison, fierce and terrifying to the worlds.
Again, from the excessive churning, into the ocean of milk there sank
<s>Kālakūṭa</s>, the great poison, like <s>Yama</s> at the end of an age.
Seeing it resembling the world-destroying fire, the gods were afraid then
and came into my presence, praising me with distressed minds.
"Lord, best of all, protect us, guardian of those who have sought refuge!"
In this way the gods and asuras made many hymns of praise.
With a smiling face, I then drank that <s>Kālakūṭa</s>.
What remained of it here and there became manifold upon the earth.
In some places it took the form of a root, elsewhere the form of bark, O beloved;
somewhere it took the form of leaves, and somewhere the form of water.

children.text: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ jātaṃ tatra tatra viṣaṃ gatam
children.translated_text: Thus it became of many kinds; poison went here and there.
Among them the best is <s>kandaviṣa</s> (bulb poison), O beloved, the poison of eighteen kinds.
I shall explain the varieties in order: <s>Kālakūṭa</s> and <s>Dardura</s>,
<s>Hālāhala</s>, <s>Meṣaśṛṅga</s>, <s>Mohada</s>, <s>Granthi</s>, and <s>Karkaṭa</s>;

children.text: raktaśṛṅgi haridraṃ ca kesaraṃ daśamaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>Raktaśṛṅgin</s>, <s>Haridra</s>, and <s>Kesara</s> is remembered as the tenth.

children.text: ete daśavidhāḥ kṣveḍā na prayojyā rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: These ten kinds of poison are not to be employed in <s>rasāyana</s>.
<s>Śvetaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>Vatsanābha</s>, <s>Sarṣapa</s>, <s>Śṛṅgin</s>, <s>Vāluka</s>,

children.text: mustakaṃ saktukaṃ devi cāṣṭamaṃ kardamaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mustaka</s>, <s>Saktuka</s>, O goddess, and <s>Kardama</s> as the eighth:
these eight varieties are proclaimed as suitable to be used in <s>rasāyana</s>.
<s>Kālakūṭa</s> has the color of a crow's beak and resembles a frog.
<s>Dardura</s> is blue in color, and <s>Hālāhala</s> poison is similar.

children.text: meṣaśṛṅgī tu meṣasya śṛṅgābhaṃ mohadaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s> has the appearance of a ram's horn; <s>Mohada</s>, again,
has a red-blue radiance, O goddess; <s>Granthika</s> is furnished with knots.
<s>Karkaṭa</s> has a tawny appearance, and <s>Raktaśṛṅgi</s> is a great poison.
It is black-tawny and red-shining; <s>Haridraka</s> has the appearance of turmeric.
<s>Kesara</s> has the luster of lotus filaments: thus the tenfold set.
<s>Śvetaśṛṅgī</s> has the appearance of an elephant's tusk; <s>Vatsanābha</s> is pale.
<s>Sarṣapa</s> is furnished with dots in the shape of mustard seeds.
<s>Śṛṅgī</s> should be known as horn-shaped; <s>Vāluka</s> has the form of sand.
<s>Mustaka</s> is shaped like musta; <s>Saktuka</s> is white in color.
<s>Kardama</s>, O goddess, is the best poison, having the shape of beeswax.
When pieces of poison are broken, the dots seen in them
are white, red, yellow, and black, corresponding in order to Brāhmaṇa and the other classes.
White ones are for <s>rasāyana</s>; red ones for subjugation and work with mercury.
Yellow ones are for minor rites; black-colored ones are for killing.

children.text: viṣaṃ yuktyāmṛtaṃ devi tadayuktyā viṣaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Poison, when used properly, is nectar, O goddess; when used improperly, it becomes poison.
Therefore poison should be consumed by the proper method, never improperly.
Poison is equal in potency to mercury, mica, gold, and magnetite.
One should tie the poison in cloth smeared with red mustard oil.
After three days, having taken it out, one should combine the poison with an equal amount of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax).
One should triturate it; when that is made into a fine powder, it becomes purified.
It may be used for disease and for <s>rasāyana</s>; it becomes accomplishment-bestowing, O fair-faced one.
With the body purified by purgation and the like, and while eating wholesome food, one may become a poison-eater.
It should be consumed gradually: a mustard seed, then a royal mustard seed,
a mung bean, a rice grain, barley, black gram, and up to a <s>guñjā</s> measure as the highest limit.
The poison should be consumed with sugar; then that poison becomes nectar.
Pungent, sour, and salty things are to be avoided, as are exercise, heat, sunlight, and the like.
Oil, mustard, and foods made from them are to be avoided in poison-<s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: gavyaṃ kṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ takraṃ snigdhaṃ dadhi ca śarkarā
children.translated_text: Cow's milk, ghee, buttermilk, oily food, curds, and sugar,
and sweet-tasting substances should be consumed; otherwise there is cause for disorder.

children.text: mātrayā sevitaṃ kṣvelam amṛtaṃ bhavati priye
children.translated_text: Poison consumed in the proper measure becomes nectar, O beloved.
If the measure is excessive, even nectar turns into poison.

children.text: pramādādatimātraṃ cet tadā vegā bhavanti ca
children.translated_text: If through negligence the dose is excessive, then reactions arise.
In the first reaction there is distress; in the second, trembling.

children.text: tṛtīye ca tṛṣā dāhaś caturthe gatibhañjanam
children.translated_text: In the third there is thirst and burning; in the fourth, impairment of movement.
In the fifth the mouth is foamy; in the sixth there is breaking of the neck.

children.text: saptame ca nirutthānaṃ maraṇaṃ cāṣṭame bhavet
children.translated_text: In the seventh there is inability to rise, and in the eighth death occurs.
Therefore a remedy must be undertaken quickly, O fair-faced one.
Even a dose of poison that is only slightly excessive produces many diseases.
It produces dizziness, forgetfulness, pains, vomiting, and severe diarrhea.
It also causes loss of voice, stammering, burning, and disturbance of vision,
as well as ear pain, shortness of breath, cough, and other diseases arising from <s>vāta</s>.
When, my dear, signs of over-dosing are seen in the body,

children.text: tadā tu ṭaṅkaṇaṃ niṣkam ājyaṃ cāpi caturguṇam ||
children.translated_text: then one should drink one <s>niṣka</s> of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and four times as much ghee.
To counteract it, one may also drink <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> with water,
or the marrow, or one <s>niṣka</s> of the fruit of <s>putrajīva</s> mixed with water.
Or one may take <s>tuttha</s> measured as two <s>paṇas</s>, or turmeric with human urine,

children.text: vacāṃ vā devadālīṃ vā sarpākṣīṃ vātha sārbuṇīm ||
children.translated_text: or <s>vacā</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, or <s>sārbuṇī</s>,
or <s>paṭolī</s> or <s>giriparṇī</s>, each separately with human urine; these conquer poison.

children.text: lāṃ yāṃ vāṃ hāṃ caturvarṇair gāruḍaṃ saṃpuṭīkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: With the four syllables lāṃ, yāṃ, vāṃ, and hāṃ, the <s>Gāruḍa</s> formula is enclosed.
It is for immobilizing, arresting, drawing out, and neutralizing poison.

children.text: lāṃ proṃ lāṃ anena mantreṇa stambhanam
children.translated_text: With the mantra lāṃ proṃ lāṃ, immobilization is performed.

children.text: śītajalaghaṭam abhimantrya viṣāturasya mastake jalaṃ ḍhālayet
children.translated_text: Having consecrated a pot of cold water, he should pour the water on the head of the person afflicted by poison.
The poison does not spread.

children.text: yāṃ proṃ yāṃ anena stobhanamantreṇa viṣāturasya śikhinamandhayet
children.translated_text: With the arresting mantra yāṃ proṃ yāṃ, he should bind or cover the topknot of the person afflicted by poison.

children.text: vāṃ proṃ vāṃ anena nirvāhamantreṇārkadaṇḍaṃ vā dhuttūrakāṣṭhadaṇḍaṃ vābhimantrya viṣāturasya sarvāṅgaṃ spṛṣṭvā viṣaṃ nirvāhayet
children.translated_text: With the drawing-out mantra vāṃ proṃ vāṃ, he should consecrate a staff of <s>arka</s> wood or <s>dhuttūra</s> wood, touch the poisoned person's whole body, and draw out the poison.

children.text: hāṃ proṃ hāṃ anena nirviṣīkaraṇamantreṇa nirviṣīkaraṇārthaṃ viṣāturasya sarvāṅgaṃ daṇḍenāpāmārjayet svastho bhavati
children.translated_text: With the neutralizing mantra hāṃ proṃ hāṃ, in order to neutralize the poison, he should wipe the poisoned person's whole body with the staff; the person becomes well.

children.text: jīrṇaṃ kṣvelaṃ śarīre cetpittāntaṃ vamanaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: If the poison has been digested in the body, my dear, vomiting should be induced until bile appears.
Purgation should be done until the undigested matter is cleared, and he should eat the root of <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>.
He should consume meat with ghee; it will remove the fault caused by poison.
