One who takes the previously stated dose is freed from great disease.
O <s>Devī</s>, by a six-month regimen it destroys old age and gray hair.
By using it for a year, one lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
The poison-<s>rasāyana</s> should be administered in winter, the cold season, and spring.
In summer, the rains, and autumn it should never be administered.
Those dominated by <s>vāta</s>, the elderly, pregnant women, and those oppressed by hunger, thirst, heat, or travel,
as well as impotent persons, those wasted by illness, and those with excessive <s>pitta</s> or anger,

children.text: yakṣmiṇo naiva yogyāḥ syuḥ sadā viṣarasāyane ||
children.translated_text: are never fit for the poison-<s>rasāyana</s>.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s> said:
O lord free from impurity and illusion, remover of old age, birth, and disease,
through your grace the <s>rasāyana</s> of mercury and the other substances has become known.
After this, lord and master, I wish to hear something further:
a divine-herb <s>rasāyana</s> that is easy in method and use.
Tell me that divine procedure, the giver of every <s>siddhi</s>.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:
I shall teach the divine-herb <s>rasāyana</s>, beginning with <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>.
First, <s>Devī</s>, listen to the <s>rasāyana</s> of <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>.
One should prepare the seeds of <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>, removing their husks.
After drying them in fierce sunlight, one should make them into a fine powder.
For seven days one should steep them with <s>dhātrī</s> fruit, or else with milk.
He should put them in a wheel-press and then extract their oil.
The oil prepared in this way destroys the <s>doṣas</s> and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
A <s>prastha</s> of oil born from <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s> seeds, together with an equal amount of ghee,
should be placed in an oiled vessel and set inside a heap of grain.
After a month or half a month, O lordly goddess, he should take that oil out.
With his body purified by purgation and the other rites, and having worshiped the fire, the guru, and brāhmaṇas,

children.text: dvipalaṃ ca gavāṃ kṣīraṃ tattailaṃ niṣkamātrakam
children.translated_text: he should mix two <s>palas</s> of cow's milk with one <s>niṣka</s> measure of that oil.
He should drink it in the morning, eat wholesome food, and keep his senses controlled.
On the second day too, and then in sequence at one-day intervals,
the dose should be increased by one <s>niṣka</s> until it reaches sixteen <s>niṣkas</s>.
This has been stated as the maximum dose of that oil.
As soon as it is drunk, a momentary swoon arises; one should sprinkle his face.
When he has awakened, one should give him milk-rice with ghee and sugar.
Through the use of this oil, within a month a man becomes wise.
He grasps a thing after hearing it once, becomes handsome, and remains like a sixteen-year-old.
In the second month he becomes strong as an elephant and free from all disease.
In due order, in the fourth month he becomes firm and possessed of strength like <s>Indra</s>.
In the fifth month he has a diamond body and divine sight, and becomes a <s>khecara</s>, a sky-goer.
He is endowed with qualities such as <s>aṇimā</s>, goes everywhere, and exists at all times.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe māsi svayaṃ sraṣṭā bhoktā hartā trimūrtivat ||
children.translated_text: In the sixth month he himself becomes creator, enjoyer, and destroyer, like the <s>Trimūrti</s>.
By using it for one year, O <s>Devī</s>, he becomes directly <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
For as long as he lives on the oil, he should eat milk-rice.
Having purified his body by vomiting and the other procedures, and having worshiped the physician and brāhmaṇas,
in the morning he should take a <s>kuḍuba</s> of cow's milk and oil born from <s>kiṃśuka</s> seeds.
Making a <s>kuḍuba</s> as before, he should combine the two and drink them.
As soon as it is drunk, a swoon occurs; he should make the man lie on ashes.
After seven nights he awakens, lying on the bed as if bound.
He should not move his limbs; his eyes become unsteady.

children.text: taile jīrṇe samāpanne saṃjñā bhavati bhairavi
children.translated_text: When the oil has been digested and the process is complete, consciousness returns, O <s>Bhairavī</s>.
Cow's milk should be given to him every day for ten days.

children.text: sa tvacaṃ ca tyajeddehāt kañcukaṃ bhujago yathā
children.translated_text: He sheds the skin from his body like a snake its slough.
He should always live on a milk diet for twenty-one days.
He becomes lord of speech, steadfast, and retains what he has heard in an instant.
He becomes one who hears from afar and has divine sight; the wise man lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Under an auspicious lunar asterism he should gather the leaves of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>.
They should be free from worms and insects, tender, and auspicious.
He should dry them in strong sunlight; when powdered and strained through cloth,
he should place the powder carefully in a new vessel.
His body purified by emesis and the other purifications, celibate and with senses restrained,
eating food free from alkali and sour substances, and taking milk and cooked śāli rice,

children.text: koṣṇaṃ jalaṃ pibennityaṃ nivāte śayanaṃ bhajet
children.translated_text: he should drink warm water every day and sleep in a place sheltered from wind.
He should take a <s>karṣa</s> measure for a month, mixed with cow's buttermilk.

children.text: dvitīye ca tṛtīye ca vṛddhiḥ karṣādhikā kramāt
children.translated_text: In the second and third months the increase is by one additional <s>karṣa</s> in sequence.
Thus, up to the end of sixteen months, he should drink a <s>kuḍuba</s> together with buttermilk.
The man who uses it daily in this way has curly, glossy hair,
is strong as a rutting elephant, and lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
The wise man should dry the flowers of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s> in the shade,
powder them, strain them through cloth, and deposit them in a new vessel.
Twenty <s>palas</s> of flower-powder and twenty-four <s>palas</s> of cow's ghee,
mixed together in one place, he should put into a heap of grain.
At the end of a month he should take it out and make fourteen portions.
Each one is to be consumed separately; in this way there will be a three-month course.
He should eat from a copper vessel, avoiding salt, sour substances, and the like.
Living on milk-rice, when thirsty he should drink a decoction of khadira.
After three months the body becomes like adamant; there is no doubt about this.
The steadfast man becomes as strong as ten thousand elephants and moves with the speed of the wind.
By using this for a year, even his feces and urine
can penetrate all metals and make them into gold.
He lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s> in person and rejoices together with the deities.
He should powder the seeds of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s> and place them in a jar.
Mixed with honey, ghee, and sugar, he should put them into a heap of grain.
After a month has passed, he should collect it and take a <s>karṣa</s> measure each day.
Pure in self, he should use it and then drink cow's milk.
The increase should be only until it becomes a <s>pala</s>, not beyond that.
In this way, after a year, a death-free siddhi arises.
Purified, he lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>, with strength like that of an elephant.
He should make a fine powder from the bark of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>.
He should impregnate it with cow's milk and drink a <s>pala</s> each day.

children.text: jitendriyaśca pathyāśī bhaved ā vatsaraṃ sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: With senses restrained and eating wholesome food, the wise man should continue for a year.
He certainly lives ten thousand years and becomes a siddha.

children.text: brāhmī ca madhukaṃ sājyaṃ niryāsaṃ brahmavṛkṣajam
children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmī</s>, madhuka, ghee, and the exudate born from the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>,
in equal parts, he should consume; he should drink milk after one <s>pala</s>.
By this one-year regimen, pure and of auspicious appearance,
the knower lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>, free from wrinkles and gray hair.
He should collect the five parts of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s> according to rule.
He should dry them in the shade, powder them, and purify them through cloth.
Pure, at sunrise, he should lick a <s>karṣa</s> measure with honey and ghee.
After a year the man becomes free from wrinkles and gray hair.
He should split a very stout and tall <s>brahmabhūruha</s>, a brahma-tree.

children.text: mūle trihastaśeṣaṃ ca tadagre gartam āracet ||
children.translated_text: Leaving three hastas at the root, he should make a hollow at its top.
He should fill it there with ripe dhātrī fruits, dear one.
With the remaining piece of cut wood he should close that hollow.

children.text: kuśaiḥ saṃveṣṭayetsamyag ā mūlāgraṃ ca lepayet
children.translated_text: He should wrap it properly with kuśa grass and plaster it from root to tip.
The intelligent man should plaster it with clay and cow dung, and then wrap it with cloth.
Again he should plaster it with clay and cow dung, and the wise man should dry it.

children.text: samyak śuṣke ca paritaḥ karīṣaiḥ paripūrayet ||
children.translated_text: When it is thoroughly dry, he should pack it all around with cow-dung cakes.
He should burn it; when it has cooled, he should collect those dense fruits.
He should put those dhātrī fruits into a vessel filled with honey and ghee.

children.text: bhūgṛhe vā nivāte vā pradeśe ca vasansukhī
children.translated_text: Living happily in an underground chamber or in a windless place,
he should eat as much as he wishes every day, living on milk and controlling his senses.
After six months he sees fissures and treasures in the earth.
He sheds his skin like a snake, and the man lives for a yuga of <s>Brahmā</s>.
He should powder the five parts of white palāśa and dry them, dear one.
After they have been shade-dried and strained through cloth, he should lick them with honey, dear one.
Taking a <s>karṣa</s> measure for three months, the man conquers old age and death.
After a year he has the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>, is a siddha, and becomes all-pervading.
He should gather the seeds of white palāśa one by one.
With goat's ghee, taking them day by day, in a month he conquers death and old age.
After a year he lives for a yuga of <s>Brahmā</s>, with siddhi before him.
The qualities that have been stated for the oil, bark, leaves, and so on of red palāśa
are present in white palāśa and bestow siddhi on the practitioner.
I shall declare the mantra for the kalpa-siddhi of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ amṛtaṃ kuru kuru amṛtamālinyai namaḥ
children.translated_text: oṃ hrīṃ, make it immortal, make it immortal; homage to <s>Amṛtamālinī</s>.
First he should perform a puraścaraṇa of twenty thousand recitations.
He should meditate on <s>Amṛtamālinī</s> as bearing, in her lotus hands, a nectar-pot, the boon gesture, a rosary,
the gesture of knowledge, and a pearl noose.
At an eclipse he should consume it seven times with one hundred and eight recitations.
At the times of lunar and solar eclipses and the like, he should recite it eight thousand times.
Without the mantra there would be no siddhi, even in hundreds of crores of kalpas.
With the mantra there will be swift siddhi; he should practice with the mantra going before.
Now I shall teach <s>muṇḍī</s>, which grants the desired aims of the practitioner.

children.text: caturvidhā bhavet ca raktā pītā sitāsitā
children.translated_text: It may be of four kinds: red, yellow, white, or black.

children.text: puṣyārke pūrṇamāsyāṃ vā revatyāṃ śravaṇe'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: On a Sunday under <s>Puṣya</s>, or on a full-moon day, or under <s>Revatī</s> or <s>Śravaṇa</s>,
or at the time of an eclipse and so on, or during auspicious yogas, one should gather it.
Having first performed offering and worship, one should collect that <s>kaidārī</s>, the <s>muṇḍinī</s> plant.
Having bathed, keeping silence, and reciting the mantra, he should gather it.

children.text: oṃ amṛtodbhavāya amṛtaṃ kuru kuru svāhā hrīṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, for the one born of nectar: make nectar, make nectar; <s>svāhā</s>, <s>hrīṃ</s>, <s>saḥ</s>.
He should perform the preparatory rite by reciting the mantra twelve thousand times.

children.text: mūlaṃ nālaṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ patraṃ pañcāṅgam īritam
children.translated_text: The root, stalk, fruit, flower, and leaf are said to be its five parts.

children.text: sa pañcāṅgaṃ harenmuṇḍīṃ samyak śītena vāriṇā ||
children.translated_text: He should gather <s>muṇḍī</s> with its five parts and wash it properly with cold water.
He should dry it in the shade and then powder it.
He should strain it through cloth and then place it in a new jar in due order.
With his body purified, a man should drink one <s>karṣa</s> of that powder with cow's milk.
When the medicine has been digested, he should first drink ghee.
Then he should eat food free from salt, oil, sour substances, and the like.
His food should be rice of the <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> variety, cooked with ghee, sweetened, and rich in milk.
After six months <s>siddhi</s> arises; he casts off his skin like a snake.
Freed from gray hair and the like, he has divine sight and a firm body.
He is strong as an intoxicated elephant, steadfast, youthful, and embodied pride.
After a year every <s>siddhi</s> arises, and the man has the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.
That <s>muṇḍī</s>, when used with ghee, bestows the results previously described.
Now, O <s>Devī</s>, I shall describe the <s>rasāyana</s> of <s>devadālī</s>.

children.text: śvetā kṛṣṇā ca pītā ca devadālī tridhā matā
children.translated_text: <s>Devadālī</s> is held to be of three kinds: white, black, and yellow.
The white calms disease; the black and yellow especially
give results in <s>rasāyana</s> and in operations on metals, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
At eclipses of the moon or sun, on the full-moon day, O worshiped by the gods,
on the thirteenth day of the dark fortnight, or on the fifth lunar day, according to rule,
on an auspicious day and under an auspicious constellation, one should gather it preceded by mantra.
<s>Oṃ</s>, <s>svāhā</s> to the one whose end is the host of immortals and the host of Rudras.
Having recited it one hundred and eight times, he should gather it after making an offering.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya phaṭ svāhā
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the blessed <s>Rudra</s>; <s>phaṭ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>.
This is the mantra for binding the practitioner's topknot.
A wise man should dry the five parts of <s>devadālī</s> in the shade.
He should strain it properly through cloth and consume it with cow's milk.
The wise man should cook it in an iron vessel over a gentle fire.
Purified in self, he should lick one <s>karṣa</s> with honey and ghee for seven days.
His wisdom becomes divine; by a month's use it removes disease.
By eating it for two months, he certainly sees treasures and the like.
The juice of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit, honey, <s>devadālī</s> juice, and ghee
should each be in a measure of one <s>karṣa</s>; each day he should drink it lightly.
After twenty-one days he becomes intelligent and able to retain what he has heard.
He should powder the five parts of <s>devadālī</s> and strain them through cloth.
He should always drink it with <s>śivāmbu</s> (urine), with milk, or with cow urine.
As before, it bestows <s>siddhi</s> and removes every kind of skin disease.
It destroys jaundice, spleen disease, wind pain, colic, and fistulas.
Its juice, combined with sulfur, dissolves every metal.

children.text: badhnāti ca rasaṃ samyak samaṃ mūrchati tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: It properly fixes mercury and immediately stupefies it when used in equal measure.
Likewise, the juices of <s>gandharvalajjā</s>, <s>gāndhārī</s>, and <s>devadālī</s>,
applied with sheep oil, check a blazing fire.
One should grind the seeds of <s>devadālī</s> together with jaggery.
With that he should make a wick; it removes hemorrhoids in anal growths.
A man should anoint his eyes with the juice of <s>devadālī</s>.
He sees the host of beings, and it gives him everything.
Ghee, the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit, <s>devadālī</s> juice, honey,
and the juice of <s>lakṣmaṇā</s>: he should drink all of these, one <s>pala</s> each.
For three days, at the fertile period, it gives sons to women.
One should lick <s>devadālī</s> juice and milk together with equal honey and ghee.
For men with tender seed, the seed becomes capable of producing conception.
<s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>vākucī</s>, <s>vahni</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and <s>devadālī</s>:
one should drink one <s>karṣa</s> of these daily with <s>śivāmbu</s>, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>.

children.text: dharitryāḥ paśyati chidraṃ varṣānmṛtyuṃ jarāṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: After a year he sees the openings of the earth and conquers death and old age.
He should drink one <s>pala</s> of <s>punarnavā</s> and <s>devadālī</s> together with milk.
He should drink <s>devadālī</s> with one <s>pala</s> of <s>sarpākṣī</s> in <s>śivāmbu</s>.
As before, <s>siddhi</s> arises very quickly, O fair-faced one.
He should drink one <s>pala</s> of <s>devadālī</s> and <s>nirguṇḍī</s> with <s>śivāmbu</s>.
After a year it destroys old age, and he lives as long as the moon and stars.

children.text: oṃ amṛtaṃ kuru kuru amṛteśvarāya svāhā
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, make nectar, make nectar; <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Amṛteśvara</s>.
At the beginning, when using <s>devadālī</s>, he should recite this mantra.
Now I shall teach the preparation of the root of white <s>arka</s>; listen.
Having taken the root of white <s>arka</s> under the <s>Puṣya</s> constellation on a Sunday, removing the woody part,
he should dry the clean bark in the shade, after straining it through cloth.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā karṣamekaṃ sevyaṃ gopayasā saha ||
children.translated_text: Having made it into powder, one <s>karṣa</s> should be consumed with cow's milk.
With two <s>palas</s>, after six months it removes all diseases and old age.
After a year he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>; there is no doubt.
The fresh juice of white <s>arka</s> leaves and the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, in equal measure,
should be combined and dried in the sun until it becomes a powder.
He should cook that in four times the amount of cow's milk over a gentle fire,
until it becomes a lump; that should be consumed in a measure of one <s>karṣa</s>.
A <s>pala</s> of cow's milk should be drunk; he obtains the result as before.

children.text: oṃ āṃ haṃsamālini svāhā ayaṃ bhakṣaṇamantraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, āṃ, to <s>Haṃsamālinī</s>, svāhā. This is the mantra for eating.
Then, on a thirteenth lunar day joined with Monday, he should collect it.
He should powder the leaves of <s>hastikarṇī</s> after they have been dried in the shade.

children.text: palaṃ sevyaṃ gavāṃ kṣīraṃ varṣānmṛtyuṃ jarāṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: A <s>pala</s> should be consumed with cow's milk; after a year he conquers death and old age.
A mortal lives for the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>, attended by <s>siddhas</s>, <s>sādhyas</s>, and others.
He should dry the five parts of <s>hastikarṇī</s> in the shade.
For one month he should eat a <s>karṣa</s> every day together with water,
and then with <s>sauvīra</s>, curd, milk, ghee, buttermilk, and honey, in that order.

children.text: ekaikaṃ pratimāsaṃ ca sevyaṃ varṣācca sidhyati
children.translated_text: Each one should be consumed for a month, and after a year he attains success.
Perfected, with a diamond body and great strength, he lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Oṃ</s>, to the immortal one; I receive immortality, svāhā.
This is the mantra for taking it.
For those born in the nectar-vessel, make nectar, make nectar, svāhā.
With this mantra he should worship.

children.text: oṃ amṛtodbhavāya amṛtaṃ kuru kuru nityaṃ namo namaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, to the nectar-born one; make nectar, make nectar always; homage, homage.
This is the mantra for eating.
Now I shall teach the excellent divine procedure of <s>Rudantī</s>.
It has leaves like caṇa leaves, and flowers likewise.
It is known by the name <s>Rudantī</s>, for it sheds water downward.
It is as though it weeps when it sees people dying and afflicted with disease.

children.text: caturvidhā ca sā jñeyā pītā raktā sitāsitā
children.translated_text: It should be known as fourfold: yellow, red, white, and black.
On an auspicious day in the bright fortnight, he should collect that <s>Rudantī</s>.
A wise man should dry it root and all in the shade, after sifting it through cloth.
With his body purified, he should consume an amount the size of a cat's footprint.
He should take it daily with honey and ghee; his food should be joined with milk and ghee.
When it has been digested, remaining self-controlled, after a year he is endowed with vigor and strength.
A mortal becomes extremely long-lived and free from old age and disease.
He should make oil produced from <s>kataka</s> root in a <s>pātāla</s> apparatus,
or else in a womb-apparatus; it should be washed fifty times with water.
Or he may do this with coconut water, thus carrying out the purification of the oil.
He should finely powder the five parts of <s>Rudantī</s>, dried in the shade.
He should add half that amount of <s>musalī</s> powder, and three half-<s>palas</s> of <s>musalī</s>.
Having mixed these three powders, he should lick a <s>karṣa</s> with <s>kataka</s> oil.
Purified, he should do this daily; its increase should be up to a <s>pala</s>.
After a year he has a diamond body and lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Now I shall speak the auspicious, excellent divine procedure of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
In the morning, when <s>Puṣya</s> falls on a Sunday, the bark from the root of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> should be taken.
The bark should be dried in the shade, and that powder, in a <s>karṣa</s> measure,
a purified man should drink every other day with a <s>pala</s> measure of goat's urine.
After six months he has a divine body and is endowed with the strength of a rutting elephant.
That powder, stirred with honey, ghee, and milk, should be placed in a greased vessel.

children.text: pidhāya dhānyarāśau tu māsamekaṃ tu nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: After covering it, he should set it in a heap of grain for one month.
At the end of the month, having taken it out, with his limbs purified, he should always consume two <s>palas</s>.
Continuing for a full year, he lives as long as the moon and stars.
Or else he should drink half a <s>pala</s> of that powder together with ghee.
Success arises as before, and he is free from old age and disease.
<s>Vacā</s>, <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>varā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, and <s>bhṛṅgarāj</s> should be equal.
Having combined equal parts of these with the powder of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> root,
he should lick a <s>pala</s> measure from his hand every day with honey and ghee.
His lifespan becomes three days of <s>Viriñci</s>, free from death and old age.
The powder of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> root should be equal to <s>krimighna</s> and <s>kaṭukā</s>.
A wise man, purified, should drink a <s>pala</s> measure daily with goat's milk.
After three months he becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair, and free from disease.
He should cook the juice produced from <s>nirguṇḍī</s> leaves in a vessel over a gentle fire.
When it has reached a jaggery-like consistency, he should drink it in a <s>niṣka</s> measure.
Day by day there should be an increase by a <s>niṣka</s> until it becomes two <s>palas</s>.
By this, vomiting and purgation occur; the worms come out completely,
from the lower passage, from within the body, and from the mouth, nose, eyes, and ears.
Wasting disease, skin diseases, and other illnesses are destroyed within seven days.
In three months it removes old age, and he lives for three hundred years.
The powder of the five parts of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, consumed with sesame oil,
from a <s>niṣka</s> up to a <s>pala</s>, conquers old age in three months.
Eighty diseases born of <s>vāta</s>, skin diseases, and even throat ailments,
as well as pain in the mouth, <s>upakuśa</s>, and the like, are conquered by chewing its leaves.
The powder of the five parts of <s>sindhuvāraka</s>, soaked in honey and ghee,
he should lick in a <s>pala</s> measure in the morning; then, when it has been digested, he should drink cow's milk.
He should drink according to the strength of his digestive fire, and should eat gradually when the fire is ready.
The wise man should live where there is no wind; he obtains success within a year.
For one whose body has been perfected by the preceding procedure, poison and mercury perish.
At the proper times, as available, he should take the five parts from <s>sindhuvāraka</s>.
Dried in the shade, its powder should be joined with <s>trimadhu</s> and <s>triphala</s>.
He should place it in a greased vessel in a heap of grain for three months.
Then the intelligent man should consume it from a <s>niṣka</s> up to a <s>pala</s>, in a <s>karṣa</s> dose.
He becomes free from all diseases and devoid of old age and death.
<s>Oṃ</s>, homage to <s>Māyāgaṇapati</s>, to <s>Kubera</s>, svāhā.
This is the mantra for eating.
Now I shall teach, O goddess, the procedure for <s>śunakaśālmalī</s>.
On the eighth day of the dark fortnight, having bathed at night, he should be composed.
He should wrap the <s>śunakaśālmalī</s> tree with black threads.
There the steadfast man should recite <s>Aghora</s> one thousand and eight times.
Its root-bark should be taken and then dried in the shade.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tu madhvājyaiḥ khādetprātaḥ palaṃ palam ||
children.translated_text: Having made it into powder, he should eat one <s>pala</s> measure each morning with honey and ghee.
After a year, freed from wrinkles and old age, he lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Eighteen of its flowers should be cooked in eight <s>palas</s> of cow's milk.
After removing the flowers, he should drink that alkaline preparation every day.
In a month he obtains a divine body and lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Its fruit should be cooked in cow's milk in a <s>kānta</s> vessel.
Discarding the fruit, he should drink the milk when the digestive fire is kindled, while living on milk as food.
By using it for six months a man obtains a divine body.
He lives until the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, swift as the wind and very strong.
Through his urine and feces, copper certainly becomes gold.
Now then I shall teach the incomparable regimen of <s>pathyā</s>.

children.text: yena rogā vinaśyanti sidhyanti ca manorathāḥ
children.translated_text: By it diseases perish and desires are fulfilled.
Having drunk nectar, <s>Śacīnātha</s> joyfully drank it together with <s>Śacī</s>.
Drops of nectar fell from the lotus-faces of those two, delighted as they were.

children.text: saptadhā bhuvi te jātā mahāvīryāḥ sthirāyuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those drops arose on earth in seven forms, of great potency and stable life.
They were produced in seven regions, bearing names in seven forms.
In the <s>Vindhya</s> region, in <s>Kānyakubja</s>, in <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>, and on <s>Himavadgiri</s>,
on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in <s>Kāśmīra</s>, and in the <s>Vainya</s> region, in order,
they are <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Pūtā</s>, <s>Trivṛtā</s>, and <s>Amṛtā</s>,

children.text: jīvantī tvabhayā jātā deśe deśe yathākramam
children.translated_text: and <s>Jīvantī</s> and <s>Abhayā</s> arose, each in its respective region.

children.text: uttamā madhyamā nīcāḥ svayaṃ pakvāstu śobhanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The best, middling, and inferior fruits are those that ripen on their own and are handsome.
In harītakī there are five tastes, excluding salt.
Sweet, sour, bitter, pungent, and astringent occur in sequence.
The tastes are located respectively in the pith, fibers, stalk, skin, and flesh.
Gourd-eared, round, four-angled, and thin-skinned,

children.text: pañcāsrā māṃsalā svarṇavarṇā kṛṣṇā smṛtāḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: five-cornered, fleshy, golden-colored, and black are remembered in order.

children.text: yā majjantī jale grāhyā gurvī snigdhā ghanāghanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The fruit that sinks in water should be taken: it is heavy, oily, and very dense.

children.text: dvikarṣamātrā sā śreṣṭhā karṣamātrā tu madhyamā
children.translated_text: One measuring two <s>karṣas</s> is best; one measuring a single <s>karṣa</s> is middling.
One of half a <s>karṣa</s> is inferior: thus the fruit of <s>pathyā</s> has been described.
Harītakī that is worm-eaten, burnt by fire, spoiled, or soaked with mud or water,
split, or grown in saline soil, should be avoided.
In a pure place, on an auspicious day, during an eclipse of the moon or sun,
the wise man should first worship it with perfumes and the like, pray to it, and recite.
After repeating the <s>Gāyatrī</s> one hundred times, he should gather <s>pathyā</s> in this way.
He should use auspicious <s>Śivā</s> with dry ginger, or with jaggery, or else with rock salt.
By that it acts as a kindler of digestion and destroys <s>āma</s>.

children.text: kṣaudreṇa vā guḍenāpi pippalyā nāgareṇa vā ||
children.translated_text: Or it should be used with honey, with jaggery, with long pepper, with dry ginger,
or else with rock salt, by one whose body is purified, every day.

children.text: dve dve pathye dvādaśābdaṃ tena jīvecchataṃ samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Using two <s>pathyā</s> fruits each day for twelve years, he thereby lives for a hundred years.
There should be two <s>niṣkas</s> of powdered <s>pathyā</s> and one <s>niṣka</s> of iron ash.
After mixing it with cow's ghee, he should smear it in a <s>kānta</s> vessel.
He should place the vessel upside down and leave it there day and night.
In the morning the wise man, with purified body, should lick it and thereby conquer old age and death.
First, having bored into a <s>śālmalī</s> tree, he should place <s>Śivā</s> fruits inside it.
After six months they should be taken out, one by one, each day.

children.text: seveta pathyāṃ śuddhāṅgastasya mṛtyurjarā na hi
children.translated_text: With purified body he should use <s>pathyā</s>; for him there is neither death nor old age.
Now, O <s>Deveśī</s>, I shall teach the regimen made from āmalakī.
At the beginning of <s>Caitra</s> he should gather well-ripened fruits of <s>dhātrī</s>.
They should be taken as in the case of harītakī, dried in the shade, and powdered.

children.text: karṣaṃ jalena vājyena madhunā vā phalaṃ niśi
children.translated_text: At night he should take one <s>karṣa</s> of the fruit with water, with ghee, or with honey.
It increases the gastric fire and brings clarity to the senses.
He should lick <s>dhātrī</s> powder and iron ash mixed with honey and ghee.
It destroys wrinkles, grey hair, and death; after a year the procedure is as before.
When cooked in milk and eaten, it gives accomplishment as before.
He should lick <s>dhātrī</s> powder and <s>bhṛṅga</s> powder together with honey and ghee.
After a year he is certainly freed from wrinkles and grey hair.
He should lick powder of neem and āmalakī together with honey and ghee.

children.text: pūrvavacca phalaṃ devi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: The result, O <s>Devī</s>, is as before; no deliberation is needed here.

children.text: atha bravīmi te devi triphalāyā rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: Now, O <s>Devī</s>, I shall tell you the <s>rasāyana</s> of triphalā.
One part should be harītakī and two parts vibhītaka.
Likewise, four parts should be <s>dhātrī</s>; all should be powdered together.
It may be taken with long pepper, with <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, with rock salts, or with <s>madhuka</s>,

children.text: kṣaudreṇa vā sarpiṣā vā vacayā sitayāthavā ||
children.translated_text: or with honey, with ghee, with <s>vacā</s>, or else with sugar.
Combined with gold, silver, copper, tin, lead, and iron,
triphalā, when licked, destroys old age and death.
Equal portions of triphalā should be combined, each one separately.
The measures for long pepper and the rest, and for gold ash and the other ashes, are now stated.

children.text: sauvarṇaṃ paṇamātraṃ ca dvipaṇaṃ rājataṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Gold should be one <s>paṇa</s> in measure, and silver should be two <s>paṇas</s>.
Copper powder should be half a <s>paṇa</s>, and what is made from lead and tin should be two <s>paṇas</s>.
Iron powder is prescribed in the measure of five <s>paṇas</s>.
One who uses triphalā in this way lives as long as the moon and stars endure.
Before eating in the morning, he should take one harītakī and two vibhītakas.
At night he should take four āmalakas, all cooked in ghee.
The wise man should use this for a year and become free from wrinkles and grey hair.
Having ground it together with rice-water, he should lick it at night from a <s>kānta</s> vessel.
He should lick that with honey in the morning; it increases lifespan and health.
First he should impregnate <s>triphalā</s> with a decoction of <s>khadira</s> and <s>asana</s>.
Three times for seven days, O goddess; then it should be soaked in honey and ghee.
He should take a <s>karṣa</s> of it every day; after a year he obtains the lifespan of <s>Indra</s>.
With the juices of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>khadira</s>, and <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>, each separately,
he should impregnate <s>triphalā</s> separately for seven days in the heat, dear one.
He should eat a <s>karṣa</s> with jaggery and ghee; after a year he becomes like a god.
The powder of one hundred fruits of <s>triphalā</s> should first be treated with the juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s>.
It should be impregnated for three times seven days, and he should lick it mixed with honey and ghee.
Each morning he should take half a <s>pala</s>; when it is digested, he should eat curds and rice.
After a year his sight is clear, and he lives for six hundred years.
He becomes very strong, black-haired, and endowed with memory and intelligence.

children.text: yuvā śatastrīrantā ca dhīraḥ sa subhago bhavet
children.translated_text: He becomes youthful, capable with a hundred women, steadfast, and fortunate.
Now, O <s>Girijā</s>, I shall teach the divine <s>śuṇṭhī</s> rasāyana.
Taking the best dry ginger, he should powder it and strain it through cloth.

children.text: guḍaṃ cāsya samaṃ yojyaṃ madhunā goghṛtena ca ||
children.translated_text: He should add an equal quantity of jaggery to it, together with honey and cow's ghee.
Putting it into a greased vessel, he should seal it well in a heap of grain.
After two <s>maṇḍalas</s> he should take it out on an auspicious day, his body purified.
He should lick it daily, <s>karṣa</s> by <s>karṣa</s>; after a week he is free from disease.
Using it for six months, he lives for two hundred years.
In intellect he is equal to <s>Vācaspati</s>, and he knows the <s>purāṇas</s>, <s>āgamas</s>, and <s>śāstras</s>.
This has been experienced by me, O goddess; I have told it to you out of affection.
Now, dear one, I shall explain the rasāyana of <s>pippalī</s>.
First he should purify <s>pippalī</s> with water of <s>kiṃśuka</s> alkali.

children.text: saptadhā ca tataḥ kuryāttāsāṃ ca ghṛtabharjanam
children.translated_text: He should do this seven times, and then fry them in ghee.

children.text: tataḥ seveta śuddhāṅgaḥ pañcāṣṭau daśa saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: Then, his body purified, he should take them in courses of five, eight, ten, and seven.

children.text: varṣamekaṃ tu madhvājyai rogāstasya na santi ca
children.translated_text: For one year, with honey and ghee; then he has no diseases.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, he lives for a hundred autumns.
In the morning, before food and afterward, he should eat three <s>pippalīs</s> three times.
After a year it destroys disease and old age, and he obtains a lifespan of one hundred years.
By the sequence one, two, and three, he should increase the dose for ten days.
He should decrease the <s>pippalīs</s> in the same way, decreasing and increasing again and again.
Together with cow's milk, up to a thousand <s>pippalīs</s>,
he should take them for that long; his body purified, he is free from old age and disease.
Having ground it with goat's milk, he should drink it; so prepared, it is especially strengthening.
Boiled in milk it gives a middling result; the increases and decreases are as before.
Up to two thousand, that rasāyana should be taken.
Cough, dyspnea, consumption, pallor, splenic disease, disorders of blood and wind,
urinary disease, piles, <s>grahaṇī</s>, swelling, hiccup, vomiting, and obstruction of the throat,
and irregular fevers are destroyed by the <s>pippalī</s> rasāyana.
He lives a full hundred years, free from wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: atha citrakakalpaṃ te vakṣyāmi śṛṇu pārvati ||
children.translated_text: Now I shall teach you the <s>citraka</s> preparation; listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: citrakastrividho jñeyaḥ kṛṣṇo raktaḥ sitaḥ śive
children.translated_text: <s>Citraka</s> should be known as threefold: black, red, and white, O <s>Śivā</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇo rasāyane rakto lohe roge sito bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The black is for rasāyana, the red for metals, and the white for disease.
Whether best, middling, or inferior, it should not be gathered in winter.
In spring, on the dark fifth day, wearing black garments and purified,
he should worship it with black perfumes, unbroken rice, flowers, and black threads.
Having wrapped it around on the previous day, he should offer a bali of black rice.
In the morning, silent and purified, he should dig it up and take the <s>citraka</s> with its root.

children.text: na goghrātaṃ padā spṛṣṭaṃ śucau deśe vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: It should not have been smelled by a cow or touched by a foot; he should place it in a pure spot.

children.text: kṣiptaṃ kṣīrāntare kṛṣṇaṃ vahnau kṣīraṃ tu kṛṣṇati
children.translated_text: When the black kind is put into milk and the milk is placed on the fire, it blackens the milk.
Testing the red <s>citraka</s> in this same way, the milk becomes red.
Thus, for the red <s>citraka</s>, with red flowers, unbroken rice, and the like,

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ vā lohitaṃ vāpi samūlamapi khaṇḍayet ||
children.translated_text: he should cut up the black or the red one, even together with its root.
He should impregnate it seven times with water of <s>āmalaka</s> and dry it successively.
Having powdered it, he should take equal parts of <s>tārkṣī</s>, palm bark, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>triphalā</s>.

children.text: eṣāṃ samaṃ cāgnicūrṇaṃ sarvaṃ bhāṇḍe nave kṣipet
children.translated_text: He should add an equal quantity of <s>agni</s> powder to these and put everything into a new vessel.

children.text: tataḥ śuddhaḥ śubhadine niṣkaṃ niṣkaṃ ghṛtāplutam ||
children.translated_text: Then, purified, on an auspicious day, he should eat it, <s>niṣka</s> by <s>niṣka</s>, soaked in ghee.
In only a month it cuts away ulcers, skin disease, and the like.
The teeth, hair, and nails fall out and then grow again.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, he lives for a hundred autumns.

children.text: evaṃ ca raktacitrasya yojanā ca phalaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: So too for the red <s>citraka</s>: the application and the result are the same.
Now listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>; I shall teach the <s>bhallātakī</s> preparation.

children.text: pakvaṃ navaṃ sutīkṣṇaṃ ca bhallātakaphalaṃ haret ||
children.translated_text: He should collect a ripe, fresh, and very sharp fruit of <s>bhallātaka</s>.
The wise man should boil one fruit, pierced with a needle, in cow's milk.
After discarding the fruit, he should drink the milk mixed with honey, ghee, and sugar.
In this way he should increase by the sequence one, two, and three up to twenty-one.
The fruits and the days, dear one, are twenty-one, step by step.
All diseases perish; after six months he has a divine body.
Now, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, I shall teach the preparation of <s>bhūmikadamba</s>.

children.text: trividhaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ śveto raktaśca mecakaḥ
children.translated_text: It should be known as threefold: white, red, and dark.
In the bright fortnight, under <s>Puṣya</s> and the sun, he should gather it according to rule.
He should dry it with its root in the shade, and then powder it.
His body purified, dear one, he should lick a <s>karṣa</s> of that powder with ghee.
When it has been digested, self-controlled, he should prepare milk-rice.
His wrinkles disappear after six months, and his gray hairs as well.
By using it for a year, he lives for three hundred years.
I shall teach the divine <s>punarnavā-kalpa</s>, dear <s>Pārvatī</s>; listen.
The plant called <s>punarnavā</s> is of two kinds: red and also white.

children.text: rase rasāyane śvetā roge raktā praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: For mercury and <s>rasāyana</s> the white is praised; for disease, the red.
When the sun is in <s>Puṣya</s>, the wise man should collect, together with its root, the white variety that removes swelling.
After drying it in the shade and powdering it, he should take half a <s>pala</s> with cow's milk,
or a full <s>pala</s>, in the morning, with his body purified, for the span of a year.

children.text: yuvā bhavati vṛddho'pi sa jīveccharadaḥ śatam ||
children.translated_text: Even an old man becomes young, and he lives for a hundred autumns.
With cow's milk he should cook that root until the milk is reduced, dear one.
Having powdered that root, he should mix it equally with cooked jaggery.
He should add cow's ghee there, combine it into one mass, and take it down from the fire.
He should lick a <s>pala</s> each day, living on milk-rice and controlling his senses.
By using it for a year, he is free from wrinkles and gray hair.
For one who uses it, various poisons disappear.
Skin disorders, diseases of phlegm and pallor, abdominal diseases, tumors, and anal disorders,
all diseases disappear, including those born of vomiting, hiccup, the eyes, and the ears.

children.text: puṣpitāṃ phalitāṃ pakvām ādāya ca punarnavām
children.translated_text: He should take <s>punarnavā</s> when it has flowered, fruited, and ripened.
It should be cut up, well boiled in a decoction of dry ginger, and ground with milk.
He should drink it by day after the powder, and at night eat milk and ghee.
After six months he obtains siddhi and becomes one who can delight with a hundred women.
Now, <s>Maheśvarī</s>, I shall tell the excellent kalpa of noble <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>.
He should gather it together with its root when the sun is in <s>Puṣya</s>, and then dry it.
After it has been fully dried in the shade, he should drink a <s>karṣa</s> measure in the morning, mixed with sour gruel.
With his body purified, in a month he drives away diseases.
Then, by a six-month regimen, there is cutting away of wrinkles and gray hair.
Constantly eating ghee and milk, he lives for three hundred years.
He should use the shoots of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> mixed with half as much black sesame.
For six months this cuts away wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: bhṛṅgarājaphalaṃ puṣpaṃ patraṃ mūlaṃ ca cūrṇayet
children.translated_text: He should powder the fruit, flower, leaf, and root of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>.
He should prepare an equal amount of the herbs beginning with <s>citrā</s> to match this powder:
<s>citrā</s>, dry ginger, <s>kaṇā</s>, bilva, pathyā, dhātrī, and viḍaṅga,
black pepper, vyādhighāta, and the seed of cakramarda,
lodhra, mustard, and rājī, all gathered and powdered.
Having combined them into one, he should soak them repeatedly in the juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s>.

children.text: saptadhā ca tataḥ sarvaṃ cūrṇīkṛtya punaḥ priye
children.translated_text: Then, after doing this seven times, he should powder everything again, dear one.
With his bowels purified, he should lick a <s>karṣa</s> measure together with cow's milk, dear one.
After six months siddhi arises, and he is free from wrinkles and gray hair.
The procedure for golden <s>bhṛṅga</s> has been stated as before, <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya tiṣṭha tiṣṭha saṃgṛhāṇa svāhā
children.translated_text: oṃ, homage to blessed <s>Rudra</s>; stay, stay, receive; svāhā.
This is the gathering mantra.
oṃ, homage to <s>Rudra</s>, whose nature is immortal nectar; svāhā.
This is the stirring mantra.
oṃ, arise, arise, auspicious one; svāhā.
This is the eating mantra.
Now, goddess, I shall teach the supreme <s>kumārī-kalpa</s>.
On a riverbank, or in a village, a city, or on the seashore,
the plant whose leaves are soft, ear-like, yellowish, and like snakes,
whose flowers are like coral shoots, and which is moist and hand-sized,

children.text: yasyāḥ patrāṇi tiṣṭhanti sā kumārīti kathyate
children.translated_text: whose leaves stand upright, is called <s>kumārī</s>.
Pure, fasting, on an auspicious day, he should gather the maiden plant.
After worshiping the <s>kumārī</s> that grants siddhi and giving an offering,
with his bowels purified, he should eat it at dawn to the measure of four finger-breadths.

children.text: evaṃ māsaṃ tataḥ khādyaṃ yathā vṛddhiḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: In this way it should be eaten for a month, increasing it gradually, little by little.
He should altogether avoid the middle portion; it is always the part to be eaten with caution.
It should be used according to one's own capacity, while one follows the food and conduct one desires.
The <s>kumārikā</s> should be used properly with rich meat broth and milk.
It removes all diseases, dear one, beginning with royal consumption.
He sings like the <s>kinnaras</s>, has vulture-like sight, and is very strong.
His hair is glossy, he is intelligent, and he shines like the young sun.
He is endowed with the strength of ten elephants and is like the wind in his gait.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, he becomes as if sixteen years old.
Thus, by using it for a year, he becomes endowed with these qualities.
But one who uses it until twelve years have passed becomes, by gods and demons,
and by great serpents, invulnerable, and endowed with the strength of thirty elephants.
He has peacock-like sight, is omniscient, and is skilled in all śāstras.
A mortal becomes a <s>vidyādhara</s>; there is no doubt to be entertained about this.
Having taken a leaf of <s>kumārī</s> on a successful day under the <s>Hasta</s> constellation,
pure, every morning he should taste it according to the strength of his digestion.
Or whoever licks its pulp mixed with honey, ghee, and the three pungents
and uses it regularly for a month is freed from all diseases.
Using it for six months, he becomes free from wrinkles and gray hair.
Having collected its juice and mixed it with the three pungents, honey, and ghee,
he should use it after it has been cooked over a gentle fire, living on milk and controlling his senses.
In a month diseases perish; in two months his body becomes firm.
He gains divine sight and brilliance; in two months he becomes one who destroys enemies.
By a six-month regimen, even an old man becomes young; this is true, <s>Īśvarī</s>.
By using it in this way for a year, he lives for two hundred years.
With his bowels purified, he should eat its leaf together with the paired adjuncts.
After a year there is destruction of wrinkles and gray hair; of this there is no doubt.
Now, O <s>Devī</s>, I shall teach the rasāyana of <s>mahānīlī</s>.
When the sun is in <s>Puṣya</s>, being pure, he should gather <s>mahānīlī</s> according to rule,
together with its root, flowers, and fruit, and dry it in the shade, O dear one.
There should be two <s>niṣkas</s> of finely sifted powder, and one <s>niṣka</s> of mica should be added.
He should mix all of it with honey and place it in an oiled vessel.

children.text: dhānyarāśau nyasenmāsam uddhṛtya ca tataḥ priye
children.translated_text: He should set it in a heap of grain for a month; then, O dear one, having taken it out,
with his bowels purified, he should lick it in the morning in a dose the size of a cat's paw.
After six months a mortal becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair.
He should take <s>mahānīlī</s>, black mica, <s>musalī</s>, and the <s>amṛtā</s> creeper.
Having powdered them in equal parts, he should lick a <s>karṣa</s> with honey.
By using it in this way for a year, even an old man becomes young again.
He becomes strong, intelligent, and steadfast, and lives for two hundred years.

children.text: abhrakaṃ ca kumārīṃ ca kākajaṅghāṃ śatāvarīm ||
children.translated_text: He should take mica, <s>kumārī</s>, <s>kākajaṅghā</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
with <s>mahānīlī</s> equal to these, and powder them in an oiled vessel.
Together with honey, at the end of seven nights, he should remove it.
Subsisting on milk, he should lick a <s>karṣa</s>; after a year he conquers wrinkles and old age.
Now, O <s>Deveśī</s>, I shall describe the excellent regimen of <s>musalī</s>.
It has golden flowers and leaves shining like date-palm leaves.

children.text: antaḥ śvetā ca nārācamūlā sā musalī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: It is white inside and has an arrow-like root; that is remembered as <s>musalī</s>.

children.text: tanmūlaṃ ca samuddhṛtya chāyāśuṣkaṃ ca cūrṇayet
children.translated_text: Having pulled up its root, he should dry it in the shade and powder it.
In the morning, with his body purified, he should lick a <s>karṣa</s> mixed with honey and ghee.
When it has been digested, he should eat milk-rice and avoid dry food, O dear one.
In the sixth month, even an old man becomes like a boy, strong and intelligent.
Being pure, he should drink <s>musalī</s> powder with milk, or also with curds.
After a year he obtains youth and becomes capable in intercourse with a hundred women.
Now I shall explain the regimen of <s>indravallī</s>; listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
It was taught by me for the victory of <s>Surendra</s> over the demons.

children.text: tadā prabhṛti lokeṣu khyātā sā cendravallikā
children.translated_text: From that time onward it has been known in the worlds as <s>indravallikā</s>.
For men who make use of this plant, bodily perfection surely arises.
Having pulled it up with its root, he should dry it in the shade and powder it.
There should be twelve <s>palas</s> of that powder, and the same amount of <s>vacā</s> powder.
There should be an equal portion of wound-healing powder, and six <s>palas</s> of powder made from <s>trikaṭu</s>.
Putting everything together in one place, he should place it in a vessel.
Every morning, always, he should lick one <s>karṣa</s> at a time mixed with honey.
After six months it destroys all diseases; after a year it gives bodily perfection.
Again and again, every six months, he should prepare fresh powder.
Now, O dear one, he should also gather the five parts of the <s>jyotirdruma</s>.
For three periods of seven nights, with honey, he should let them rest in a heap of grain.
He should eat them; freed from disease, radiant, he becomes a possessor of bodily perfection.
Now he should take equal parts of <s>aśvagandhā</s> root, <s>pautrī</s>, and <s>koraṇṭa</s>.
Being pure, he should lick a <s>karṣa</s> of the powder in the morning with honey and ghee.
By using it for a year, a man comes to have a lifespan of three hundred years.
Now I shall teach the regimen of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>; listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
The divine <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> vine is like molten gold.
It has many spreading shoots, is golden in appearance, has auspicious fruits and seeds, and bestows good fortune.
In <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, in the bright fortnight, under an auspicious asterism and on an auspicious day,
he should wrap that vine with a thread smeared with saffron.
Having worshiped it with red perfumes, unbroken grains, and flowers, and having bowed to it,
wearing red garlands and garments, and anointed with saffron and agaru,
chewing betel, joyful, and with his mind restrained,
he should worship it with the mantras of his chosen deity, or with the mantra of <s>Tārā</s>.
Having meditated on his chosen deity, then, facing north, O dear one,
he should gather the ripe seeds and then dry them in the sun.
Having first set aside those freed from their husks, he should powder them carefully.
Having extracted oil from them, he should add milk equal to that oil,
and combine a quarter part of honey; he should cook it slowly until only the oil remains.
Into that he should put camphor, <s>takkola</s>, cinnamon bark, and nutmeg.
A skilled man should powder these in equal parts.
There should be sixteen <s>palas</s> of that oil and one <s>pala</s> of that powder.
Having combined them and stirred them, he should place them in an oiled vessel.
He should place the vessel in a heap of grain for three times seven days.
Or for ten days, or thirty, sixty, or likewise ninety,
or longer, as appropriate; afterward he should collect the oil.
With his bowels purified, on an auspicious day, after worshiping gods and brahmins,
at sunrise the steady practitioner should drink it, O dear one, by gradually increasing the number of drops.
By means of it, as the dose reaches a <s>pala</s>, the practitioner attains insensibility.

children.text: mandaṃ mandaṃ labdhasaṃjño muhuḥ krandati nandati ||
children.translated_text: Gradually and slowly regaining consciousness, he repeatedly cries out and rejoices.
He also repeatedly weeps; with difficulty the man regains consciousness.
Afterward he should give cow's milk mixed with honey to the one whose mind is exhausted.
In this way, gradually, that practitioner becomes well; there is no doubt.

children.text: ṣaṣṭikānnaṃ sagokṣīraṃ taile jīrṇe ca bhojanam ||
children.translated_text: When the oil has been digested, his meal should be <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with cow's milk.
He should do this every day continuously for one month.
After a month he is visibly like the sun in brilliance and knows the mantra-śāstra.
Even without having studied, the man knows the śruti with its limbs and subsidiary limbs.
At midday he sees the sun like another full moon.
His sight is equal to that of <s>Vainateya</s>; by day he sees the stars.
Poison is digested like food, and even while asleep he would hear a sound.
It destroys the eighteen kinds of <s>kuṣṭha</s> and all diseases.
Hear the fruit of the second month; I shall tell it, <s>Bhairavī</s>.
The user of the oil is served by <s>gandharvas</s>, serpents, and <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Those who commit great sins and those who revile the gods and ancestors,
those who are without the observance of the pledge and conduct: they are freed from guilt.

children.text: amuṣya sevayā muktāḥ prayānti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: Released by the use of this, they go to the supreme state.
Hear the fruit of the third month, <s>Pārvatī</s>; it will be told.
The gods, the divine seers, the eight <s>Vasus</s>, and the great serpents

children.text: amuṣya sevāṃ kurvanti priyaṃ nityahitaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: perform service for him, doing what is pleasing and always beneficial.
Having filled a copper pot with his urine, he should dig into the earth.
When it has been placed properly in that pit, after six months it becomes gold.
Now hear, <s>Śarvāṇī</s>, the fruit of the fourth month.
That mortal becomes invisible, endowed with every lordly power, and strong.
He lives for ten days of <s>Brahmā</s> and is skilled in moving through all worlds.
By rubbings of his urine, feces, sweat, and water, he should make a coating on copper.
When it is heated in fire, that copper becomes gold.

children.text: atha pañcamamāse tu sadehaḥ khecaro bhavet
children.translated_text: Then, in the fifth month, he becomes a sky-goer while still embodied.

children.text: sākṣādbrahmā bhaved devi śṛṇu ṣāṇmāsikaṃ phalam ||
children.translated_text: He becomes <s>Brahmā</s> himself, goddess; hear the six-month fruit.
Surrounded by great siddhas, through all the worlds at will,
he wanders; he becomes equal to <s>Śiva</s>, of great splendor and great fame.
Now the fruit of the seventh month will be told, auspicious one.
His mind has conquered the six inner enemies, and he is devoted to the welfare of all beings.
He obtains the lifespan of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from both merit and demerit.
He wanders with great power and fortune, like another <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
I shall tell the fruit of eight months; listen, all-auspicious one.
Dear to me, with divine action and omniscient, he attains liberation.
Hear the fruit of the ninth month, beloved <s>Kātyāyanī</s>.
That hero, like a second wish-fulfilling gem, possesses any form he desires.
The sādhaka creates the forms of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the Moon.
Whatever he thinks of in his mind, he himself is able to do exactly that.
This divine <s>rasāyana</s> is easy to perform and is a means to liberation.

children.text: puṇyaṃ paramaguhyaṃ ca gopanīyaṃ tvayā priye ||
children.translated_text: It is meritorious, supremely secret, and to be kept hidden by you, beloved.
There is nothing equal to it; it is hard to obtain even for the gods.
What need is there to say much here? I have taught it for your pleasure.

children.text: rasāyanam idaṃ divyaṃ na kurvanti ca mānavāḥ
children.translated_text: Human beings do not undertake this divine <s>rasāyana</s>.
Some are overcome by ignorance, and some by the suspicion that it does not exist.
Some are hindered by obstacles, and some because they fail to obtain it.
Some are hindered by ignorance of that kalpa, and some because they lack a guru.

children.text: kecid rogākulā devi tvitthaṃ tairapi vighnitāḥ
children.translated_text: Some, goddess, are afflicted by disease; in this way even they are obstructed.

children.text: yatra jyotiṣmatī vallī sā bhūmiḥ puṇyabhūmikā ||
children.translated_text: Where the <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> vine grows, that ground is holy ground.
There alone are all sacred bathing places and the various siddhis as well.
The divine <s>rasāyana</s> produced from the fruit of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> should be used.

children.text: atha guggulukalpaṃ ca śṛṇu tvaṃ caṇḍike'dhunā
children.translated_text: Now hear also the <s>guggulu-kalpa</s>, <s>Caṇḍikā</s>.
There are four kinds of <s>guggulu</s>: <s>kumuda</s>, and likewise <s>padmaka</s>,
<s>mahiṣākṣa</s> and the kind called <s>hema</s>, each bright with its own color.
The kind called <s>hema</s> is declared to be a <s>rasāyana</s> for human beings.

children.text: kaṇaśo gugguluṃ kṛtvā goghṛtena śanaiḥ pacet
children.translated_text: Having made the <s>guggulu</s> into granules, he should cook it slowly with cow's ghee.
In a swinging apparatus, careful in method, he should cook it as if it were meat fried in ghee.
<s>Pathyā</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>dhātrī</s>, and sulfur should each be taken separately.
Having powdered them in equal parts, he should take <s>pura</s> equal to all of these together.
With his bowels purified, he should lick it in the morning with oil produced from castor.
After stirring it, the dose is a <s>niṣka</s>; the increase may extend up to a <s>karṣa</s>.
By using it in this way for a year, diseases from cold and wind, and wounds too,
boils, glandular swellings, and other great painful diseases perish.
By using it for twelve years, a man becomes adamant-bodied.

children.text: yadyaddravyaṃ ca sātmyaṃ syāt tattaddravyeṇa vā bhajet ||
children.translated_text: Whatever substance is suitable for him, with that very substance he should take it.
For whichever disease whatever medicine has been prescribed,
he should use it together with those medicines; it will remove that particular disease.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s>:
God of gods, lord of the world, honored by gods and asuras,
lord chiefly over the five acts, homage to you, who are beyond the highest.
All the medicinal preparations have been taught by you out of love for me.
They are wondrous, lord of beings, and grant siddhi at once.
Easy to use, bringing happiness, bestowing knowledge and enjoyment, and pure,
tell me, out of love, the <s>rasāyana</s> that grants union with us.
Then <s>Śaṅkara</s>, benefactor of the world, became smiling-faced.
<s>Śrībhairava</s>:
Goddess, I shall teach a kalpa desired by gods and asuras.
It is desired by siddhas, sages, women, all social classes, and yogins,
by children, old people, the sick, impotent men, and many women.
Listen with attentive mind to what arose from immortality.
My portion is fiery, beloved; your portion is gentle and lunar.
All medicine has fire and soma as its nature; the gods, in the ocean,
and the asuras threw it in and performed the churning with Mount <s>Mandara</s>.
From the very intense churning there, goddess, my fiery portion
became the blazing, terrible great poison called <s>Hālāhala</s>.
By it the gods and asuras were distressed, withered, and deprived of strength.

children.text: kṛpayā tanmayā sarvaṃ viṣaṃ ca kabalīkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Out of compassion, all that poison was swallowed by me.
Then the gods and the sons of <s>Diti</s>, delighted in mind, churned.
Then <s>Lakṣmī</s> and the others appeared, and afterward the <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality).
That which arose was supreme and divine, cutting away old age and death.
Then great <s>Viṣṇu</s> placed it in the lotus of my hand.
Three times drops were given to the supreme one, the highest Self.
Afterward, to the one joined with the supreme <s>Śakti</s>, it was given by me to you, dear one.

children.text: pītaṃ tvayā ca me dattaṃ madhusūktamudīrya ca
children.translated_text: It was drunk by you and given to me, while the honey-hymn was uttered.
And by me, beloved, the <s>amṛta</s> whose nature is consciousness and bliss was accepted.

children.text: sāndrānandena ca mayā sphūtkṛtir lajjayā kṛtā
children.translated_text: In dense bliss I made a bursting cry out of modesty.
Subtle drops fell; from them the great medicinal plant was born.
Seeing that auspicious, divine plant, they rejoiced and tended it.
It was made to grow with the nectar brought in the lotus of my hand.
Therefore it had many leaves and clusters, with leaves like a trident.
From that the great medicinal plant was born, endowed with the qualities ordained by me.
Once <s>Bhairava</s>, seeing it, was delighted and asked me for it.
I gave it to him, and <s>Bhairava</s> too presented it to the <s>Yoginīs</s>.

children.text: tāśca prītāḥ svabhaktebhyo bhaktebhyaḥ pradaduśca te
children.translated_text: They, pleased, gave it to their devotees, and those devotees
brought down to earth the divine medicinal plant that grants all siddhis.
<s>Śrī Bhairavī</s>:

children.text: kiṃnāmnī sā kathaṃvīryā sevanīyā kathaṃ prabho
children.translated_text: What is its name, what is its potency, and how is it to be used, lord?
What is its color, how many varieties does it have, and what are its form and qualities?

children.text: kathaṃ vā siddhidā sā syātkramānme brūhi vallabha
children.translated_text: And how does it become a giver of siddhi? Tell me in order, beloved.
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s>:
Now its four colors, dear one, depend upon the <s>dharma</s> of the ages.
It is white in the Kṛta age; in Tretā it has a blood-red radiance.

children.text: dvāpare pītavarṇā ca nīlavarṇā kalau yuge ||
children.translated_text: In Dvāpara it is yellow, and in the Kali age it is blue.
Single-leaved, three-leaved, five-leaved, sage-leaved,
ten-leaved, <s>Rudra</s>-leaved, provided with thirteen petals,
and nine-leaved: these are to be known as its varieties, queen of the gods.

children.text: strīrūpā saphalā vallī puṃrūpā ca drumākṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The female form is a fruitful creeper, and the male form has the shape of a tree.

children.text: saphalā tu madaṃ mūrchāṃ sukhaṃ satvaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: The fruitful one produces intoxication, faintness, pleasure, and clarity.
It is a carrier of yoga, bitter in taste, pungent, and strong-smelling.

children.text: śivamūlī ca vijayā bhaṅgī gañjā vimardinī
children.translated_text: <s>Śivamūlī</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Bhaṅgī</s>, <s>Gañjā</s>, <s>Vimardinī</s>,

children.text: divyā siddhā siddhidā ca siddhamūlī manonmanī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Divyā</s>, <s>Siddhā</s>, giver of siddhi, <s>Siddhamūlī</s>, and <s>Manonmanī</s>,
<s>Madhudravā</s>, <s>Cidāhlādā</s>, destroyer of the bonds of creatures,
destroyer of time, destroyer of all diseases: these are its names, <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Because <s>Śiva</s> is its root, it is called <s>Śivamūlī</s>.
Because it conquers the three worlds and the six inner enemies, it is named <s>Vijayā</s>.
Because it breaks the sufferings beginning with the three torments, it is remembered as <s>Bhaṅginī</s>.
It is called <s>Gañjā</s> because it intoxicates, acting in the place of liquor.

children.text: sadṛśaṃ marśanaṃ yasyāḥ saiva proktā vimarśinī
children.translated_text: Because its proper touch or handling is of this kind, it is declared to be <s>Vimarśinī</s>.
Because it gives playfulness, delight, brilliance, intoxication, and beauty, it is <s>Divyakā</s>.
Because it is naturally accomplished, it is named <s>Siddhā</s>; because it bestows the destined siddhi,
the great siddhas call it giver of siddhi, and it has been brought as <s>Siddhamūlikā</s>.
Because it accomplishes the tasks imagined by the mind, it is <s>Manonmanā</s>.
Because it gives the bliss of consciousness, it is praised as <s>Cidāhlādā</s>.
Because it causes the nectar located in the aperture of <s>Brahman</s> to flow, it is <s>Madhudravā</s>.
Because it destroys the bonds of living beings, it is the destroyer of the bonds of creatures.
Because it conquers death it is destroyer of time; its name as destroyer of diseases is meaningful.
I shall explain the method of growing it; listen, benefactress of the world.
The ground should be free from stones, clods, sand, gravel, and the like.

children.text: bhūmiḥ kṛṣṇā pāṃsulā ca mṛdulā sakarīṣakā ||
children.translated_text: The soil should be black, dusty, soft, and mixed with dung.
There one should sow the seeds together with snake flesh.

children.text: ahivaktreṣu satvañci snigdhāni ca gurūṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: In serpent mouths, they should have vitality, and be oily and heavy.
Under the Puṣya sun, or in a siddha-yoga, or under Śravaṇa, in the bright fortnight,
having bathed, anointed his body with perfumes, and performed nyāsa, recitation, and worship,

children.text: udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vā dhyātvā ca gurupādukām
children.translated_text: facing north or facing east, and meditating on the sandals of the guru,
he should sprinkle it with water mixed with milk and aṅkola oil.
When the sprout has arisen, he should sprinkle it with water mixed with ghee.

children.text: parṇe kīṭe samutpanne sāmudraṃ vāri secayet ||
children.translated_text: When an insect appears on a leaf, he should sprinkle it with sea-water.

children.text: tato'syāṃ vitatāyāṃ ca śiraśchittvā ca randhrayet
children.translated_text: Then, when it has spread out, he should cut off its top and make an opening.
There he should put in a niṣka of mercury, one niṣka in each, with care.
He should carefully close those openings with silk.
When it flowers and fruits, he should sprinkle it with wine, meat, and water.
For the duration of each fortnight he should sprinkle it with milk and the like.

children.text: asyāṃ baddhvā jaṭāmāṃsīṃ sakṣaudraṃ vāri secayet ||
children.translated_text: Having tied jaṭāmāṃsī to it, he should sprinkle it with water mixed with honey.

children.text: śeṣaṃ madyena vā vārā vardhanīyā mahauṣadhiḥ
children.translated_text: For the rest, the great medicinal plant should be grown with wine or with water.

children.text: ādau vā paramaṃ mantraṃ paścāt sevanamantrakam ||
children.translated_text: First comes the supreme mantra, and afterward the mantra for use.

children.text: oṃ kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣetrapālāya namaḥ savīryaṃ kuru kuru siddhiṃ dehi dehi svāhā
children.translated_text: oṃ kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ, homage to <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>; make it potent, make it potent; give siddhi, give siddhi; svāhā.
This is the establishment mantra.

children.text: oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ yaralavaśaṣasaha amṛteśvari amṛtaṃ kuru kuru āṃ hrāṃ kroṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ yaralavaśaṣasaha, O mistress of amṛta, make amṛta, make amṛta; āṃ hrāṃ kroṃ svāhā.
This is the use mantra.
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight in Phālguna, the practitioner,
having bathed, wearing pure garments, and adorned with perfumes, flowers, and ornaments,

children.text: arcayedbhairavaṃ tatra nandīśaṃ ca krameṇa ca
children.translated_text: should worship <s>Bhairava</s> there, and then <s>Nandīśa</s> in sequence.
With offerings of wine and meat, and with red, yellow, white, and black
threads he should wrap it, goddess; its mantra is now stated.

children.text: oṃ glauṃ sauṃ hrīṃ khecarabhūcaradivyayogini imāṃ rakṣa rakṣa sarvaśatrupramathini svāhā
children.translated_text: oṃ glauṃ sauṃ hrīṃ, O divine yoginī who moves in the sky and on the earth, protect, protect this; O crusher of all enemies, svāhā.
This is the thread-binding mantra.
The Aghora, lord of mantras, should be recited a thousand times every day.
In this way the practice should be done for seven days; on the fifth lunar day he should meditate on <s>Amṛteśvarī</s>
as resembling jasmine, the moon, and camphor, wearing white garments,
moist with white garlands and unguents, adorned with pearl ornaments,
with a rosary in her right hand and then, in her left, a pot filled with nectar.
Below that, on the right and left, she holds <s>saṃvit</s> and a book.

children.text: tatra sthitāṃ tataḥ kuryāl lavanaṃ ca samantrakam ||
children.translated_text: Having established her there, he should then prepare the salt with its mantra.
He should gather unctuous plants, together with their seeds and leaves.

children.text: oṃ klīṃ vaṃ saṃ krauṃ śivānandāmṛtodbhave tribhuvanavijaye vijayaṃ prayaccha svāhā
children.translated_text: oṃ klīṃ vaṃ saṃ krauṃ, born from the nectar of <s>Śivānanda</s>, victorious in the three worlds, grant victory, svāhā.
This is the salting mantra.
He should dry it for seven days in gentle sunlight, in a clean place.
He should place it in a new vessel and powder those leaves finely.
After first heating two dishes, he should cook it in one of them first.
Then he should cook it in the other; this should be done again and again.
The expert should continue to cook it until it becomes well cooked.
With the leaf juices of <s>guñjā</s>, <s>unmatta</s>, and the creeper, repeatedly,

children.text: sthālyau pṛthakpṛthak devi saptadhā saptadhā priye ||
children.translated_text: the two dishes should be treated separately, O goddess, seven times each, dear one.

children.text: muṇḍī brāhmī kumārī ca varī dhātrī kaṭudvayam
children.translated_text: <s>Muṇḍī</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>kumārī</s>, <s>varī</s>, <s>dhātrī</s>, and the two pungents,
and <s>sugandhikā</s> should be known in order, each in the measure of one <s>pala</s>.
These should be powdered and combined with <s>jayā</s> equal to the whole of them.

children.text: sitā sarvasamā yojyā tatsamaṃ gopayaḥ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Sugar equal to all should be added, and an equal amount of cow's milk should be poured in.
Having put the sugar into the milk, the physician should bring it to the thread stage.
Then the powder from <s>muṇḍā</s> through <s>vijayā</s> should be put into it.
After stirring it and taking it down in this way, when it is cool he should add honey, half as much as the sugar.
He should add cow's ghee equal to the honey and mix it together.
Having placed it in a heap of grain for a fortnight, he should recite every day
the great <s>Vaṭuka</s> mantra a thousand times, or according to his ability.

children.text: hrīṃ śrīṃ mahākālāgnibhairavāya sarvasiddhimātṛbrahmā liṅgitavigrahāya sarvāpadāṃ śoṣakāya huṃ phaṭ ṭhaṃ
children.translated_text: hrīṃ śrīṃ, to <s>Mahākālāgnibhairava</s>, whose form is embraced by the mother of all siddhis, the witherer of all calamities, huṃ phaṭ ṭhaṃ.
This is the fire-cooking mantra.
After a month he should take it out according to rule and eat an amount like an āmalaka fruit.
He should remain in a windless room, eat milk-rice, and control his senses.

children.text: gurūpadiṣṭadevaṃ vā tattvaṃ vā paramaṃ smaret
children.translated_text: He should remember the deity taught by the guru, or the supreme <s>tattva</s> (principle).

children.text: dvikālaṃ vā trikālaṃ vā yathā sevābalaṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: He should do so twice or three times a day, in order, according to the strength of his practice.
Thus, after three years, he is free from old age and wrinkles,
attains <s>bhūcarī-siddhi</s> (the accomplishment of moving on earth), and lives for three hundred years.
<s>Vārāhī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>aśvagandhā</s>, in sequence,
should be added in two, three, and four parts, beginning with <s>aśvagandhā</s>, in this way.
<s>Vijayā</s> equal to this should be easily stirred together with honey.
He should set it in the sun until a fortnight has passed and heat it repeatedly.
It should be taken in an amount like a <s>dhātrī</s> fruit; after eight months he becomes sun-like.
After a year the sādhaka becomes free from old age and death.
For bodily siddhi, O queen of gods, he should recite this mantra with devotion:

children.text: hrīṃ śrīṃ mahāvyomabhāskarāya dīpimātṛkāliṅgitavigrahāya tejasāṃ nidhiṃ kuru kuru ṭhaṃ
children.translated_text: hrīṃ śrīṃ, to <s>Mahāvyomabhāskara</s>, whose form is embraced by the radiant mother, make, make a storehouse of splendors, ṭhaṃ.
Thus ends the sun-cooking mantra.
Three <s>palas</s> of <s>jayā</s> and two <s>palas</s> of powdered <s>yaṣṭī</s>,
one <s>pala</s> of powdered <s>elābhadra</s>, and half a <s>pala</s> of <s>citraka</s> root,
and one <s>pala</s> of powdered <s>śrīkhaṇḍa</s>; sugar equal to all of this should be added.

children.text: svarṇacūrṇaṃ ca niṣkārdhaṃ niṣkaṃ ca himavālukam
children.translated_text: There should also be half a <s>niṣka</s> of gold powder and one <s>niṣka</s> of <s>himavāluka</s>.
The wise man should mix everything with ghee and place it in moonlight.
Beginning with the bright fifth lunar day and continuing to the end of the fortnight, there is meditation on the moon.
Having worshiped according to rule, with his bowels purified, he should lick it, dear one.
Now I shall again tell its mantra, which grants all siddhis.

children.text: hrīṃ śrīṃ mahāśaśāṅkakiraṇavisphārabhairavāya amṛteśvarī mātṛkāliṅgitavigrahāya visphuraṇaṃ kuru kuru huṃ phaṭ ṭhaṃ
children.translated_text: hrīṃ śrīṃ, to <s>Mahāśaśāṅkakiraṇavisphārabhairava</s>, whose form is embraced by Mother <s>Amṛteśvarī</s>, cause it to shine forth, cause it to shine forth, huṃ phaṭ ṭhaṃ.
Thus ends the moon-cooking mantra.
For this kind of <s>kalpa</s> (procedure), the mantra has been taught in three forms.
For each mantra he should perform a preparatory rite of ten thousand recitations.
The fire-cooking is carried out in the four months beginning with <s>Āṣāḍha</s>.
The sun-cooking should be undertaken beginning with <s>Phālguna</s>, O queen of gods.
The cooking of the moon, beginning with <s>Kārttika</s> and the following months, grants siddhi.
Together with <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, it destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease).
If joined with <s>brāhmī</s> and <s>kumārī</s>, it destroys epilepsy.
<s>Jayā</s> joined with <s>varā</s> and <s>vyoṣa</s> brings about the destruction of wasting disease.
<s>Jayā</s> joined with the leaves of cotton and <s>matsyākṣī</s> reduces pitta.
Combined with the alkaline ash of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s> leaves, it removes abdominal tumors and colic.
Joined with <s>vacā</s> and the pollen of <s>dūrvā</s>, it grants an increase of knowledge.
Combined with <s>yaṣṭī</s> and sulphur, it removes <s>kuṣṭha</s> and gives nourishment.
Combined with the pith of <s>śālmalī</s> and with sugar, it increases virility.
Joined with <s>pāṭhā</s>, bitter herbs, and the three pungents, it removes disorders of kapha.
Joined with white <s>guñjā</s>, it destroys great poison in men.
Together with powdered <s>vyāghāta</s>, it destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s> disease.
Joined with wild pepper and castor-oil plant, it destroys vāta.
These are the twelve combinations, corresponding to the twelve months.
In each month the sādhaka should recite the three mantras.
By this yoga, the practitioner becomes free from old age and death,

children.text: bhavatyeva na sandehaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ varānane ||
children.translated_text: indeed, without doubt; it is true, true, O fair-faced one.
Mercury, the three aromatics, sulphur, black mica, rudrākṣa, and gold ash
should be ground with the juice of <s>jayā</s>, and then infused for one fortnight.
He should roast it in the covered <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus and then powder it.
This, with four times as much <s>jayā</s>, should be combined with sugar and ghee.
It is to be consumed in a <s>niṣka</s> measure, either in the morning or in the evening.
And, dear one, he should recite the great <s>Vaṭuka</s> mantra up to one hundred thousand times.
In the sixth month siddhi arises, and he is free from old age and death.
After a year he has the speed of thought and the strength of ten thousand elephants.
That perfected one has a diamond body and lives as long as the moon and stars.
With powder of banyan sprouts, together with sugar, honey, and ghee,
<s>jayā</s>, consumed for three fortnights, brings all people under one's control.
<s>Jayā</s> mixed with apāmārga powder and combined with ghee
is to be used by one who constantly recites the mantra; after six months he becomes deathless.
<s>Varā</s>, sugar, <s>jayā</s>, <s>citrā</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, the three pungents, <s>vṛṣā</s>,
<s>dūrvā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, black pepper, licorice, cumin, and rock salt,

children.text: karpūraṃ ca kacoraṃ ca sarvatulyaṃ jayārajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: camphor and <s>kacora</s>, all in equal measure, with powder of <s>jayā</s>,
should be stirred with the three sweets and placed in a greased vessel.
He should consume a <s>karṣa</s> at dawn; after a <s>maṇḍala</s> he becomes a recipient of siddhi.
After a year he becomes like a god and lives for three divine days.

children.text: aśvagandhā vacā vyoṣaṃ jayācūrṇaṃ ca tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: Aśvagandhā, vacā, the three pungents, and an equal amount of <s>jayā</s> powder
should be licked with the three sweets; after three years he becomes equal to a deity.
There should be eight parts of gañjā powder and four parts of <s>muṇḍikā</s>,
two parts of brāhmī powder, and one part of vājigandhā.
There should also be two parts of the three pungents and likewise two parts of <s>varā</s>,
one part of <s>śilā</s> and one part of sulphur.
There should be one part of the king of mercury, and half that amount of gold ash.
An equal amount of pearl should be added, and coral equal to the pearl.
It should be stirred with honey and ghee and placed in a greased vessel.
After keeping it for seven nights in a heap of grain and making three hundred thousand recitations,
pills of a <s>niṣka</s> measure should be consumed by one living on milk and controlling his senses.
After a <s>maṇḍala</s> it destroys all diseases; after a year he has digestive fire like fire in bloom.
After half a year he becomes <s>Bhairava</s> and lives as long as the moon and stars.
With the three aromatics, <s>varā</s>, and the three pungents, <s>śivamūlikā</s> is used in equal parts.
Combined with honey and ghee, it is to be licked; it cures cough and increases digestive fire.
If one eats mostly sweet food, he conquers cough, dyspnea, and disease.
Together with turmeric, it destroys all urinary disorders.
Together with maṇḍūkaparṇī, or with vacā, it grants eloquence and intelligence.

children.text: drākṣā sitā vallakī ca kharjūrī dugdhapiṇḍikā ||
children.translated_text: Grapes, sugar, <s>vallakī</s>, dates, and milk solids,
combined with the juices of <s>kandalinī</s>, are remembered as the preparation called <s>Sarvasvādu</s>.
Mixed with coconut water and made fragrant with camphor,
