the perfected preparation joined with all sweet substances removes bile disorders and increases virility.
Milk four times the amount of the sweet substance should be used, so that it becomes a honey-cooked preparation.
After filtering it through cloth, he should put camphor into it,

children.text: elāṃ ca sarvamadhuraṃ jayāṃ ca pibatastataḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as cardamom, all sweet substances, and <s>jayā</s>; then, for one who drinks it,
there is strength for intercourse with a hundred women; it removes bile and increases nourishment.
Putting <s>jayā</s> seed, tied in cloth, into equal parts water and milk,
he should cook it over a gentle fire, dear one, until a fourth part remains.
Having made that into curds according to rule, he should churn it and then take out
the fresh butter; into it he should put camphor, cardamom, sugar, and honey.
It produces nourishment, long life, and radiance, and increases strength and health.
Washed a hundred times in breast milk, it is called the hundred-washed preparation.
Nāgakesara, <s>kacchūra</s>, clove, cardamom, aloe wood,
camphor, sandalwood, musk, <s>takkola</s>, and saffron,
with an equal amount of <s>jayā</s> seed, should be ground with cow's milk.
A wise man should make pills, each of a <s>niṣka</s> measure.
After making them well scented with flowers, he should put one in his mouth together with betel.
It is pure and removes salivation, bad taste in the mouth, impurity, and foul odor.
It produces fragrance and clarity and gives joy to the mind.
He should put dhātakī flowers into cow's milk with half as much water,
along with nutmeg, dry ginger, and <s>jayā</s> equal to all of that.
When only the milk remains, he should filter it through cloth, soaked with the three sweets.
This is known as the perfected yoga; it gives virility, long life, and strength.
Or, mixed with ajamodā, or else mixed with turmeric powder,
the powder, consumed in the same measure, destroys scabies and <s>kiṭibha</s>.
<s>Jayā</s> mixed with <s>tāla</s> destroys abnormal discharge and also swelling.
<s>Vijayā</s> mixed with <s>śilā</s> should be known as calming itching.
He should infuse <s>jayā</s> with oil in a pot, and afterward in treacle.
When it becomes a thick confection, the wise man should always eat it with ghee.
It is directly another <s>Madana</s>, giving pleasure with many women.
Pathyā, bhallātaka, jaggery, and sesame should be in equal parts.
With an equal amount of <s>vijayā</s>, it destroys the six kinds of hemorrhoids.
Yavānī, the two kinds of cumin, and ajamodā should be in equal parts.

children.text: etatsamā ca vijayā sarpiṣā sevyatāṃ budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: With <s>vijayā</s> equal to that, it should be consumed by the wise with ghee.
It treats joint-vāta, dizziness, vomiting, insanity, and headache.

children.text: śarkarāṃ madhu viśvaṃ ca māgadhīṃ tatsamāṃ jayām
children.translated_text: Sugar, honey, dry ginger, long pepper, and <s>jayā</s> equal to those
should be made into a pill blended with ghee; this is known as the fivefold antidote.
It cuts down heart disease, spleen disease, abdominal disorders, and fistula,
combined with <s>citraka</s>, kindling digestive fire, joined with <s>varā</s>, and breaking colic.
With <s>vyoṣa</s> it removes vāta; with sugar it pacifies pitta.
The seed of <s>śvetādrikarṇikā</s>, together with <s>vijayā</s>, should be prepared with donkey urine.
Used as a nasal medicine, it removes epilepsy and breaks the influence of bhūtas, pretas, and the like.
One should take <s>jayā</s> powder with honey and ghee, in a dose the size of an āmalaka fruit.
The excellent <s>vijayā</s> produces skill in speech and increase of virility.

children.text: madhunājyena vā dhātryā mustayā svarasena vā ||
children.translated_text: It may be used with honey and ghee, or with <s>dhātrī</s>, <s>mustā</s>, or fresh juice.
<s>Jayā</s>, used at night, brings clarity of sight for men.
It extends the firmness of youth, and the highest longevity will result.
Jaggery, <s>abhayā</s>, and <s>vijayā</s> destroy the whole class of diseases called <s>durnāma</s>.
Cleaning the teeth with a stick of <s>jayā</s> makes the teeth firm.
If the tongue is cleaned with a stick of <s>vijayā</s> smeared with oil,
it destroys foulness and impurity of the tongue, and the perception of taste becomes accurate.
One should cook <s>jayā</s> in coconut milk over a gentle fire.
One should drink it at night, anointed with the three sweets; then one may enjoy a hundred women.

children.text: śuṇṭhī harītakī tulye tatsamā ca jayā tathā
children.translated_text: Dry ginger and <s>harītakī</s> should be equal, and <s>jayā</s> should be equal to them.
Sugar equal to all should be added; this preparation enchants the three worlds.

children.text: tryūṣaṇaṃ madhukaṃ cavyaṃ cāturjātaṃ phalaṃ varā
children.translated_text: The three pungents, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>cavya</s>, the four aromatics, <s>phala</s>, and <s>varā</s>,
<s>gostanī</s> and long-pepper root should be prepared in equal parts.
The kernel of <s>priyāla</s> should be equal to those, and <s>jayā</s> should be equal to all of this.

children.text: triguṇena guḍe pakve teṣāṃ cūrṇaṃ kṣipecchive ||
children.translated_text: When jaggery three times as much has been cooked, one should throw their powder into it, O <s>Śivā</s>.
After stirring it, the desirous man should make pills called <s>Kandarpamodaka</s>.
They pacify all diseases, remove the three doṣas, and give strength.
They are aphrodisiac and nourishing; the wise man should use them at the three twilights every day.
When the bowels have been purified, he should eat them; after three years such perfection is attained.
One who uses them continually is free from old age and death.

children.text: marīcaṃ pippalī śuṇṭhī tvagelāṃ patrakaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: Black pepper, long pepper, dry ginger, cinnamon bark, cardamom, and cinnamon leaf should be equal.
With these, <s>vijayā</s> should be equal, along with an equal amount of wheat flour.
With twice as much jaggery, one should prepare pills.
Restraining his senses, one should eat a karṣa-measure every day.
After a year he is endowed with strength and nourishment and is free from wrinkles and grey hair.
With chickpeas, black gram, mung beans, <s>āḍhaka</s> beans, and sesame seeds,
and with <s>niṣpāva</s> beans and husked grains, fried in ghee and combined with jaggery,
together with the three aromatics, with <s>vyoṣa</s>, and with cumin, in equal portions,
one should combine <s>vijayā</s> and make karṣa-sized pills.
Pure in mind, one should eat one each day, in the evening and in the morning.
They remove all diseases, are aphrodisiac, and give intelligence, sense-power, and strength.
<s>Takkola</s>, sandalwood, <s>sevya</s>, camphor, <s>nāgakesara</s>,
cardamom, clove, <s>madhuka</s>, long pepper, and black pepper as well,

children.text: sarvaiḥ samāṃśā vijayā sitā sarvasamā śubhā
children.translated_text: with <s>vijayā</s> equal to all and good sugar equal to all,
make this powder called <s>Pañcabāṇa</s>, which removes every pain.
By using it for twelve years, it removes wrinkles and grey hair.
<s>Varā</s>, the three aromatics, <s>candrakhaṇḍa</s> seed, and the three pungents,

children.text: etaiḥ samā siddhamūlī sarvatulyā ca śarkarā
children.translated_text: with <s>siddhamūlī</s> equal to these and sugar equal to all,
stirred with honey and licked, kindles digestion and grants bodily perfection.
With <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>uttamā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and twice as much <s>musalī</s>,
<s>jayā</s>, with an equal amount of sugar, is aphrodisiac and gives long life and strength.
With ghee it sustains life; in the morning it is used with dry ginger and sugar.

children.text: kṣīrasiddhā jayā vṛṣyā balyā ca niśi sevitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jayā</s> cooked in milk and used at night is aphrodisiac and strengthening.

children.text: madhunā sevitā bhukteḥ pūrvaṃ sā vājigandhayā
children.translated_text: Used with honey before a meal, together with <s>vājigandhā</s>,
it is perfected as a producer of strength and nourishment; this is the supreme <s>rasāyana</s>.
Peeled <s>markaṭikā</s> seed, black-gram powder, and <s>jayā</s> should be equal.

children.text: kṣīre ca māhiṣe paktvā rātrau sevyātivṛṣyakṛt ||
children.translated_text: Cooked in buffalo milk and used at night, it is exceedingly aphrodisiac.
According to rule, with the juices of <s>śālmalīpiccha</s>, <s>varī</s>, <s>bhṛṅgā</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>,
in a good vessel, with each juice, seven times and in seven exposures to the sun,
one should perform the impregnation; afterward one should powder it with an equal amount of <s>jayā</s>.
One should lick a karṣa with honey; it destroys old age and death.
The five parts of the <s>śālmalī</s> plant should be taken, with an equal amount of <s>vijayā</s> powder.
One should lick a karṣa with honey and ghee; it cuts down wrinkles and grey hair.
Now, on a Sunday under <s>Puṣya</s>, the <s>hastikanda</s> should be gathered together with its root.
After drying it away from sunlight, one should powder it with an equal amount of <s>jayā</s>.
Afterward one should stir it with honey and put it into a greased vessel.
It should be kept in a heap of grain for twenty-one days; then it should be taken out.
One should eat one pala every day for two maṇḍalas.
For that period he should avoid pungent and sour foods and eat mild soup and rice.

children.text: madhuraṃ laghu pittaghnaṃ palalaṃ jāṅgalaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: Sweet, light, pitta-pacifying food is suitable, and meat of animals from dry land is beneficial.
He becomes like the young sun, intelligent, cuckoo-voiced, and strong.
He travels as far as a hundred yojanas in a single day.
Powder of <s>muṇḍī</s> and powder of <s>jayā</s>, equal and joined with honey and ghee,
should be licked every morning in a karṣa dose; it produces longevity and nourishment.
One should use it for twelve years and eat food combined with ghee.
Cow's milk and rice from sixty-day rice should be taken, without salt, sour substances, or alkali.
He becomes free from wrinkles and old age, handsome, and possessed of a light body.
One should gather the leaf, flower, and fruit of the white <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>.
One should dry them in the shade and make a powder, with an equal amount of <s>vijayā</s> powder.
One should lick a karṣa with honey and ghee; after a year he obtains youth.
One should also fry <s>jayā</s> seeds and sesame seeds with jaggery, dear one.
Having prepared sweet balls, in the morning he should eat them soaked in cow's ghee,
which enchant the mind and bring about union with beloved women.
He should cook <s>jayā</s> leaves together with seasonings suitable for cooking,
and fry them in cow's ghee with jaggery, cardamom, pungent spices, and cumin.
Thus prepared, this is easy to consume and is called the king of seasoning preparations.
Rice, <s>vijayā</s> seed, and hulled mung beans
should be placed inside a coconut with a good opening, and the opening should be sealed.
Smeared outside with cow dung and clay, it should be dried over a gentle fire.
He should cook what is inside the coconut and collect it together with its kernel,
and, mixed with the three sweet substances, eat it according to his strength.
This preparation is a great aphrodisiac; it gives manhood even to impotent men.
He should place <s>vijayā</s> seed tied in cloth into cow's milk.
When that milk is reduced by half and cooled by the wind of a fan,
he should add <s>vārāhī</s>, <s>markaṭī</s> seed, camphor, cardamom, and clove,
the three sweets and the three aromatics, each in equal portions.
Having mixed them into one, he should drink it at night; it is an excellent great aphrodisiac.
This is the <s>Vārāhī-yoga</s>, which cuts away impotence and the like.
That seed, boiled in milk, should be ground finely on a stone.
With the juice of an excellent young woman he should smear it on a bronze vessel.
He should keep it in fierce sunlight and then collect the oil from it.
With that, combined with another oil, he should perform nasal therapy.
It removes diseases situated above the collarbone, as well as cough, dyspnea, and the like.

children.text: yasya yasya ca rogasya vihitaṃ yadyadauṣadham
children.translated_text: For whatever disease whatever medicine has been prescribed,

children.text: tena tena yutā siddhā tattadrogaharā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: when it is prepared together with that medicine, it will remove that particular disease.

children.text: guṇā mayā ca kathyante tān śṛṇuṣva maheśvari
children.translated_text: I shall now tell the qualities; listen to them, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>.
Moistness of the tongue, happiness of mind, satisfaction, and the fulfillment of intentions arise.
There is eloquence, brightness of the face, and the body becomes fit through exercise.
He becomes intent on bathing, meditation, and worship, and eager for sweet tastes.
He eats rich food, drinks cool water, and is devoted to conversation.
He likes to look about as he wishes and is eager for union with women.
He is filled with compassion for all beings and his mind is absorbed in knowledge of reality.
He becomes wholly devoted to poetry, narration, learned explanation, and discourse.
He wins in debates, in battles, and in wrestling contests.
There are many other qualities too, which are hard to obtain elsewhere.
But when there is excessive consumption of this root of accomplishment,
disorders arise; listen to them, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
At the first stage he has reddened eyes and dry tongue, lips, mouth, and palate,
with a dry nose-tip and hot, labored breathing in the flanks.
At the second, his eyes close and his body seems covered by a film.
At the third, there is burning in the feet, hands, and eyes, and a stammering voice.
At the fourth, he is distressed by hunger and thirst, and his eyes roll with sleepiness.
At the fifth, his speech is stammering, and he immediately forgets what he himself has said.
When the sixth disorder has arisen, it causes derangement and loss of memory.
At the seventh there is weakness of the hands, and an odd relish arises in the body.

children.text: mahormaya ivollāsā jāyante ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Again and again surges arise like great waves.
At the eighth there is disorientation, stillness, frowning, and excessive weeping.
At the ninth there is roaring in the ears, fainting, and distress from loss of consciousness,
belching, cooing sounds, rolling on the ground, and piteous speech.

children.text: anyathā bhāṣaṇaṃ guhyaṃ bravansaukhyaṃ na vetti ca
children.translated_text: Speaking otherwise and uttering secrets, he does not know pleasure,
but only pain; this state is mild, dear one, and his limbs become sweaty.

children.text: anye vikārā bahavaḥ santi teṣāṃ cikitsanam
children.translated_text: There are many other disorders; their treatment is as follows.
Purgation, sour taste, then bathing the head with cool water,
and anointing with sandalwood, uśīra, camphor, and icy water should be used.
His body should be adorned with fragrant, cooling garlands,
bearing jasmine, jāti, campaka, lotus, and blue lotus flowers.
There should be a bed shining with bracelets of lotus-fiber and with banana leaves.
Camphor, cardamom, cloves, <s>takkola</s>, and <s>kaṭukī</s> fruit
he should chew together with betel, while being fanned with a palm-leaf fan.
He should wear fine astringent garments, fragrant ones,
and, looking at the moon reflected in a bracelet, remain in moonlight for two <s>muhūrtas</s>.
Intent on the tight embrace of a woman with full, high breasts,
he should lie down; sugar, milk, ghee, meat broth, and the like may be taken.

children.text: pānakaṃ mudgayūṣaṃ vā peyaṃ vā śārkaraṃ madhu
children.translated_text: A sweet drink, mung-bean soup, or a drink of sugar and honey may be drunk.
He should simply lie down, and resort to whatever is cool.
Now I shall teach, O <s>Deveśī</s>, the excellent <s>kañcukī-kalpa</s>.
It has seven or eight sheaths and tubers resembling radishes.
When accompanied by milk, even shoots arise at the sound of a ram.
Know it, dear one, as having a yellow-red stalk and a white, slender body.
It sprouts in sacred places in the months of Āṣāḍha and Kārttika.
Ground in eight palas of milk, in a quantity measuring two thumbs,
after first performing entry into a hut, he should drink it and afterward drink milk.

children.text: jīrṇe kṣīraṃ punaḥ peyaṃ peyāṃ vā snehavarjitām ||
children.translated_text: When it has digested, milk should again be drunk, or thin gruel without fat.
That gruel should be slightly warm, salty, and sour; he should not touch cold water.
Taken in this way for seven days, it destroys every kind of skin disease.
In the third seven-night period, all diseases disappear.
In the third seven-night period, like a snake its slough,
he himself casts off skin, hair, nails, and teeth in just this way.
He lives for five hundred years, endowed with beauty, intelligence, and strength.
The powdered <s>kañcukī</s> tuber is to be impregnated with its milk.

children.text: karṣaṃ gokṣīrakuḍubaiḥ piṣṭvā khaṇḍaṃ palaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: One should grind a <s>karṣa</s> with <s>kuḍubas</s> of cow's milk and add a <s>pala</s> of sugar.
By drinking it, he destroys diseases lodged in the nails, hair, bones, and teeth.
For <s>kañcukī</s>, a <s>pala</s> of powder should be infused in a <s>prastha</s> of cow's milk.
He should cook it until only the powder remains, and then fry it with cow's ghee.
He should lick it with sugar and honey, taking milk-rice until the end of a <s>maṇḍala</s>.
Endowed with the strength of a great elephant and radiant with the age of sixteen years,
he lives five hundred years, a <s>Manmatha</s> in sport with women.
Now I shall tell you, O goddess, the excellent preparation of <s>kukkuṭī</s>.
When the ocean was being churned by gods and asuras, drops of nectar
fell; from them arose <s>kukkuṭī</s>, which bestows freedom from old age.
With leaves emerald-colored and resembling date-palm fronds,
and with tubers like a cock's mouth, slightly pungent and slimy,
so marked, it should be known as <s>kukkuṭī</s>, the supreme remover of great diseases,
and especially of vāta disorders, anal growths, and poisons.
He should fry the tuber with ghee; with his bowels purified, he should enter a hut.

children.text: guñjāmātraṃ prage sevyaṃ dhāroṣṇaṃ gopayaḥ pibet
children.translated_text: Having taken a <s>guñjā</s>-measure in the morning, he should drink cow's milk warm from the udder.
When it is digested, the wise man should eat milk-rice, or rice cooked with water.
According to his strength he should increase the dose day by day until the end of a <s>maṇḍala</s>.
It removes diseases above the collarbone, jaundice and the like, and consumption, skin disease, and so on.
With firm hair, teeth, and nails, free from wrinkles and grey hair,
he lives two hundred years, endowed with intelligence, steadiness, and strength.
Beginning with the bright fortnight's first lunar day, he should eat one tuber without ghee,
and increase it until the lunar juncture, according to his strength.
Likewise from the beginning of the dark fortnight he should certainly do this day by day.
He should use it before eating; afterward he should live on milk.
He should practice this until the new moon, month after month.
After three years he obtains success and lives for thirty thousand years.
He should take powder of the <s>kukkuṭī</s> tuber with cow's milk, according to his strength.
When it is digested, he should drink gruel; after a month, success arises.
It destroys many kinds of diseases, and he lives two hundred years.
Now I shall tell the divine preparation of <s>somalatā</s>, O <s>Śaṅkarī</s>.
<s>Soma</s> himself, for the benefit of human beings, came down to the circle of the earth,

children.text: pratipede ca tannāmnā khyātā somalatā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: and by that name <s>somalatā</s> became famous on earth.
It is said to be twenty-fourfold, according to differences of place, name, and so on.
Beginning with the first day of the bright fortnight and ending with the full moon, each day
one leaf is produced; likewise, in the other fortnight,
a leaf falls away in sequence, and on the new moon one remains.
On the full moon it is always furnished with fifteen leaves.
Provided with leaves of many kinds, consisting of fifteen leaves,
and having milky vines and tubers, all are remembered as <s>somalatās</s>.
On <s>Tuṣāra</s> mountain, on <s>Arbuda</s>, and on <s>Sahya</s>, likewise on <s>Devagiri</s>,
on <s>Śrīparvata</s>, on <s>Malaya</s>, on <s>Mahendra</s>, and on <s>Pāriyātraka</s>,
on <s>Vindhya</s>, on <s>Devasaha</s> mountain, and likewise at <s>Devasūtahṛda</s>,
on the northern bank of the <s>Vitastā</s> there is a mountain named <s>Prabhāsa</s>.
There is a <s>Sindhu</s> lake in <s>Pāñcāla</s>, and <s>Candramā</s> floats there.
In that region there is also a step-well; and there are <s>Aṃśumān</s> and <s>Muñjavān</s>.
In <s>Kāśmīra</s> there is a divine lake famed as <s>Kṣudrakamānasa</s>.
<s>Auṣṇik</s>, <s>Traiṣṭubha</s>, <s>Gāyatra</s>, <s>Jāgata</s>, and also <s>Tryaiṣṭubha</s>,
and five others are found there, creepers shining like the moon.
The luckless do not see them, nor those who revile the gods, fire, and the twice-born.
For the worship of all <s>somalatās</s>, the procedure is one.
<s>Candramā</s> is golden in hue, clear, and silver-bright.
The two have tubers shaped like plantains, while <s>Candramā</s> grows in water.
<s>Muñjavān</s> is holy, with garlic-like coverings, and is called brought by <s>Garuḍa</s>.
It is pale, resembling a falcon's covering, always like a cast-off snake skin.
It hangs from the tops of trees; this is remembered as its distinctive mark.
<s>Aṃśumān</s> and <s>Candramā</s>, <s>Śonakī</s>, and <s>Karṇakopama</s>,
<s>Dūrvāsoma</s>, <s>Jāgrata</s>, <s>Kanyābhāsa</s>, and <s>Śākvara</s>,
<s>Karavīra</s>, <s>Tālavṛnta</s>, <s>Pratāna</s>, and <s>Gavīnasa</s>,
<s>Pathya</s>, <s>Somaprada</s>, and the one named <s>Garuḍāhṛta</s>,
<s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is iron-bright, and so too are <s>Aukthya</s> and <s>Revataka</s>.
<s>Aṃśumān</s> is the chief of all; they explain its service.
Accompanied by pleased experts in this <s>rasāyana</s> and by excellent knowers of mantra,
by foremost physicians and by friends, and having purified his bowels,
he should enter a secluded hut under an auspicious asterism, on an auspicious day.
On the previous day, O goddess, he should honor Brahmins, fire, <s>siddhas</s>, <s>sāmāyikas</s>, and gurus,
as well as yoginīs, maidens, children, and the offspring of <s>siddhas</s>,
with perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice, and the like, and with incense and lamps.
He should satisfy them according to rule with food and gifts of honor.
From the tuber of <s>Aṃśumān</s>, pierced with a golden needle,
he should take the milk in a golden vessel and drink a <s>kuḍuba</s> of that milk.
He should drink it all at once and throw what remains after drinking into water.
By day he should move about with friends, restrained in speech and self-controlled.
In the hut he should stay with those who know substances, the body, and instruction, and whose understanding is orthodox.
Fasting, intent on recitation, and devoted to the evening twilight worship,
he should sleep on a bed of <s>darbha</s> grass covered with a black antelope skin.
Even if thirsty, he should drink cool water only in measured amount.
In the morning, having risen and performed the earlier prescribed routine,

children.text: vinā somaṃ tathāsīta jīrṇe kṣīre saśoṇitam ||
children.translated_text: he should likewise remain without <s>soma</s>; when the milk has been digested, vomiting mixed with blood occurs,
ending in bile and containing worms, dear one.

children.text: śṛtaśītaṃ ca gokṣīraṃ sāyaṃ peyaṃ susādhakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Boiled and cooled cow's milk should be drunk in the evening by those who practice properly.
On the third day a great purgation arises for him.
By it the mortal is freed from former impure foods.
At the end of the day he should bathe, and he should drink boiled and cooled milk.
He should sleep on a bed of darbha grass, well covered with linen.
Then, on the fourth day, swelling arises in him.

children.text: aṅgebhyaḥ krimayo bahvyaḥ sūkṣmā niryānti taddine ||
children.translated_text: On that day many tiny worms come out from his limbs.
The wise man should lie on a soft, purified bed made of cow-dung ash.
If he is thirsty, he should drink boiled and cooled water.

children.text: sāyaṃ gavyaṃ śṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ pītvā śiṣyasuhṛdvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: In the evening, having drunk boiled cow's milk, surrounded by disciples and friends,
he should sleep comfortably through the fifth and sixth nights.
This daily rule is to be followed; milk should be given to him twice a day.
On the seventh day the body is left with only skin, bones, and sinews.
The drinker of <s>soma</s>, devoid of flesh and blood, remains with only life-breath left.
His body should be sprinkled with comfortably warm cow's milk.
He should be smeared with pastes of <s>śrīkhaṇḍa</s>, sesame, and <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>.

children.text: kṣīrāśī kaṭaśāyī ca kṣaumamayyāṃ śayīta saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Eating milk and lying on a mat, he should sleep on a linen bed.

children.text: aṣṭame'hni nakhaṃ śmaśru tvakkeśā radanā api
children.translated_text: On the eighth day his nails, beard, skin, hair, and teeth too
fall out, and his body becomes like that of one newly born.
On the ninth day he should live on milk and perform an anointing with subtle oil.
He should bathe with water boiled according to the <s>somalatā</s> preparation.

children.text: tatastu navame tvakca sthiratāṃ pratiyāti ca
children.translated_text: Then, on the ninth day, the skin reaches firmness.
In the same way, beginning with the eleventh day and continuing through the sixteenth day,
he should not perform oil anointing; the bath should be made from a decoction of <s>soma</s> bark.
From the seventeenth day onward, up to the twenty-fourth day,
the skin attains firmness, and the teeth become bright like diamonds.
They become stable, very firm, glossy, and arranged in even rows.
On the twenty-fifth day he should eat sixty-day rice together with cow's milk.
His nails become bright like a parrot's beak.
His skin becomes glossy, with a luster like the blue lotus,
beautifully marked, resembling flax flowers, beryl, and a raincloud.
After a month he should apply a paste made from sesame, uśīra, and sandalwood,
and afterward perform bathing with milk.
His hair grows, resembling bees and collyrium.
After a month and seven days, there is residence in the second enclosure.
Then, in the third enclosure, the perfected man should remain for a muhūrta.
He should enter the hut as before and apply <s>balā</s> oil and ghee.
For three days he should do this; after the fortieth day,
having dusted the body with cow-dung ash, he should smear it with pastes.
These are made from the bark of <s>ajaśṛṅgī</s>; he should bathe with warm water.
With his limbs smeared with sandalwood, uśīra, and camphor, and with soups of mung and dhātrī,
he should eat sixty-day rice, along with milk mixed with the three sweet substances,

children.text: ghṛtena vā dvitīye tu vasedāvaraṇe sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: or with ghee; in the second enclosure the wise man should dwell.
For five days there, the wise man should take a little wind and sunlight,

children.text: madhye madhye ca seveta tathaiva daśavāsaram ||
children.translated_text: again and again, and likewise for ten days.
Having endured wind and sunlight, he should then resort to the third enclosure.
Remaining there for twenty-one days, with his mind made steady, he is joyful.
Then, on the twenty-second day, perfection of the body arises.
At that time, having gone outside, he should first worship <s>Bhairava</s>,
delighting the minds of the guru, the sacred fire, twice-born men, and siddhas.
Everywhere, always, he should move about at his own will, free from suffering.
He bears a new, divine, beautifully lustrous body for ten thousand years.
He has the strength of thousands of elephants; there is no doubt of this.
For him there is no fear from poison, fire, water, weapons, missiles, beasts, and the like.
He always wanders at will through the worlds, including <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
In splendor he is a second moon; in beauty he is <s>Makaradhvaja</s>.
He is pleasing to all and peaceful; with the six auxiliary disciplines and the word-by-word recitation,
he knows the Vedas and the śāstras, an immortal moving on the earth.
From a short-branched, spreading <s>somavallī</s> he should collect
thirty-two stalks, according to rule, in an auspicious golden vessel.
Or it may be prepared in a silver vessel; likewise there should be two <s>palas</s> of cow's milk.
After mixing in the juice of <s>somavallī</s> in the same way, he should then drink it.
Entry into the hut and the wholesome regimen are taught as before.
The eight siddhis, beginning with <s>aṇimā</s>, arise, and he becomes visibly immortal.
Now I shall teach the <s>amṛtalatā</s> preparation; listen, O <s>Bhairavī</s>.
The <s>sudhāmṛtalatā</s> is itself nectar, removing disease, birth, and old age.
One hundred <s>palas</s> of <s>amṛtā</s> and three <s>prasthas</s> of the three sweet substances
should be powdered; he should lick a <s>karṣa</s> measure of the powder for a full year.
It pacifies all diseases, and he lives for a hundred autumns.
Now take twenty-five <s>palas</s> of powdered <s>chinnaruhā</s>, and sugar
in double that amount, together with <s>tavakṣīrī</s>, <s>ātmaguptā</s>, and <s>aśvagandhikā</s>.
Use <s>punarnavā</s> and ghee, each in ten-<s>pala</s> amounts, dear one.
Then add eight <s>palas</s> of raisins and five <s>palas</s> of <s>yaṣṭī</s> as well.
After combining all of that into one, he should place it in a greased vessel.
Having placed it in a heap of grain for one fortnight, day by day,
one should use one <s>pala</s> at a time; after a month he becomes free from disease.
After six months he has vulture-like sight; after a year he lives out a hundred years.
One hundred <s>palas</s> of powdered <s>amṛtā</s>, sixty <s>palas</s> of honey,
and forty <s>palas</s> of ghee should be kept in a heap of grain for two months.
Eating a <s>pala</s> measure every day, after a month he removes all diseases.
He gains divine sight, lives a hundred years, and has intelligence, strength, and great brilliance.

children.text: atha vakṣyāmyahaṃ devi kalpaṃ tuvarakasya ca
children.translated_text: Now, O <s>Devī</s>, I shall teach the preparation of <s>tuvaraka</s>.
The trees stand continually on the shore of the western ocean,
their young leaves moistened by spray from waves stirred by the wind.
In the rainy season one should gather their well-ripened fruits.
After drying them and grinding them to powder, one should extract oil as from sesame.
Or else one should carefully extract the oil as from castor seeds.
Then the oil should again be cooked on the fire until the water is gone.
One should set aside a <s>karṣa</s> of it for a fortnight, and then take it out carefully.
Having gone without four meals and being purified, he should drink a <s>karṣa</s>, dear one.
With the mantra, '<s>Acyuta</s>, whose hands hold conch, discus, and mace, has commanded you,'
one should take it; every disorder disappears.
It should be taken in this way for five days, and harmful foods and practices should be avoided.
For a month he should live on mung-bean broth; he becomes free from every skin disease.
Then he should lick it with honey and ghee for a period of six months.
Free from wrinkles and grey hair, he lives for two hundred years.
For fifty days the twice-born man should take that oil as nasal therapy, steadily.
He is freed from wrinkles and grey hair, retains what he has heard, and has firm limbs.
He lives for two hundred years, intelligent and vulture-eyed.
Now, O <s>Devī</s>, I shall teach the <s>somarājī</s> rasāyana.
One should gather it when <s>Puṣya</s> falls on a Sunday, and then dry it in the sun.
Powdered, it should be drunk with warm water in the morning for purification.

children.text: tridivaṃ ca tataḥ kṣaudraiḥ karṣamātraṃ lihetprage ||
children.translated_text: For three days thereafter he should lick a <s>karṣa</s> measure with honey in the morning.
In a month diseases perish; after six months he attains accomplishment.
Now I shall tell, O <s>Deveśī</s>, the preparation of <s>vṛddhadāruka</s>.
It has leaves like <s>nāgavallī</s> leaves, with milky sap and soft hairs,
and it is a spreading plant, bearing leaves and fruit, with red flowers.
It is bitter and pungent; it is remembered as <s>kāmbutā</s>, the creeper called <s>mahiṣā</s>.
One <s>tulā</s> of its root, powdered and combined with mustard,
should be placed in a heap of grain for a fortnight; after taking it out, one should measure a <s>karṣa</s>.
Cow's milk is to be drunk after it; when it has digested, the meal should be rice cooked with milk.
Even an old man becomes young; after a year he is rid of every disease.
Thus he should take it for twelve years, free from indolence.
He lives for six hundred years, free from wrinkles and grey hair.
Purified powder of <s>vṛddhadāruka</s>, measured at one hundred <s>palas</s>,
and powder of <s>vājigandhā</s> roots, three hundred <s>palas</s>, should be mixed with ghee.
He should eat a <s>karṣa</s>; he lives for a hundred autumns.
In speed he is like a horse, and in strength like a tusked elephant.
In beauty he is like the moon, and in splendor like the sun.
<s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>gokṣura</s>, and <s>vṛddhadāruka</s>,
all in equal parts and mixed with ghee, should be eaten in a <s>karṣa</s> dose.
After a week his voice is like a <s>kinnara</s>'s; after a year he becomes a sharer in accomplishment.
The root of <s>vṛddhadāruka</s>, ground with the fresh juice of <s>varī</s>,
should be drunk in a <s>karṣa</s> dose for a year; he lives a hundred autumns.
Powder of <s>vṛddhadāruka</s>, impregnated with the fresh juice of <s>dhātrī</s>,
twenty-one times, should be licked in the morning, a <s>karṣa</s> dose with honey and ghee.

children.text: lihedabdaṃ sa jīvecca varṣāṇi ca śatadvayam ||
children.translated_text: If he licks it for a year, he lives for two hundred years.
One who uses it in that way lives free from illness and becomes great.

children.text: godugdhena ca tanmūlaṃ rasaṃ dhātryāśca saṃmitam ||
children.translated_text: With cow's milk, its root and an equal measure of <s>dhātrī</s> juice,
whoever drinks it for a year lives a hundred autumns.
He should eat ghee cooked with it; he obtains the result as before.
<s>Punarnavā</s>, <s>varī</s>, dry ginger, <s>māgadhī</s>, and the two <s>rajanī</s>s,
all these in equal parts, together with <s>vṛddhadāruka</s> and sour gruel,
the wise man should drink, one <s>pala</s> in the morning, and should observe the prescribed regimen.
In a month it destroys all diseases; after a year his lifespan becomes a hundred years.

children.text: dvīpī śauṇḍī varā viśvaṃ mustamelā samāṃśakam
children.translated_text: <s>Dvīpī</s>, <s>śauṇḍī</s>, <s>varā</s>, <s>viśva</s>, <s>musta</s>, and <s>elā</s>, in equal parts,
when this is combined and prepared, that powder becomes <s>vellarika</s>.
He should eat a <s>karṣa</s> mixed with honey and ghee; in a year he succeeds.

children.text: tatphalaṃ svarasaṃ karṣaṃ ghṛtaṃ kṣaudraṃ ca tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: One <s>karṣa</s> of the fresh juice of its fruit, with ghee and honey equal to it,

children.text: pibedanu gavāṃ kṣīraṃ māhiṣaṃ vā palonmitam
children.translated_text: should be drunk, followed by cow's milk, or by buffalo milk measured at a <s>pala</s>.
In a month it destroys all diseases; after a year he lives a hundred years.
Powder of <s>vellarika</s> root and fruit arising from <s>pippalī</s>,
together with the juices produced from equal parts of <s>vellarika</s> root and fruit,
and also with fresh juice of <s>guḍūcī</s>, should be impregnated twenty-one times.

children.text: śuṣkaṃ ghṛtaplutaṃ bhāṇḍe snigdhe dhānyacaye sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When dry, soaked in ghee, in a greased vessel, and kept in a heap of grain,
after three weeks he should take it out, and a man should lick a <s>karṣa</s> in the morning.
After a year he has a lifespan of a thousand years and is free from all diseases.
Now, O <s>Devī</s>, I shall explain the <s>vajravallī</s> rasāyana.
One should pulverize <s>vajravallī</s>, roots and all, after drying it in the shade.

children.text: varā vraṇārimūlaṃ ca pratyekaṃ bhāskaraṃ palam
children.translated_text: <s>Varā</s>, the root of <s>vraṇāri</s>, and <s>bhāskara</s> should each be one <s>pala</s>.
In six months it destroys all diseases without remainder; after a year he becomes...
Bodily perfection comes in six months; then one should prepare another powder.
I shall tell the <s>tilakṣīriṇikā-kalpa</s>, O <s>Śāmbhavī</s>.
The practitioner should silently uproot the root of <s>tilakṣīriṇikā</s>,
grind it with lukewarm water, and drink it while facing east or north.
Or, having made it into a pill, the pure man should swallow it and eat milk and ghee.
He should take it for a year, gradually increasing the dose to a half, two, and three <s>niṣkas</s>; he becomes a possessor of accomplishment.
After ten days there is an increase of semen; after three months he conquers all diseases.
After six months he obtains accomplishment; no doubt should be raised about this.
Now I shall explain, O <s>Deveśī</s>, the unsurpassed <s>brāhmī-kalpa</s>.
One should pull up <s>brāhmī</s> together with its root and wash it with water.
After pounding it in a mortar, he should collect it there in a vessel.
He should make a thousand oblations with the mantras of <s>Śāradā</s> and with that juice.
After honoring gurus and Brahmins, he should consume what remains from the offering.
He should take a <s>pala</s>-measure of that juice, and when it is digested, eat milk-rice.

children.text: evaṃ saptadinaṃ sevyaṃ brahmacārī jape rataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus it should be used for seven days by a celibate man intent on recitation.
He is born intelligent, radiant with brahmanical splendor, and purified in speech.
If it is used beyond the seventh day, he fixes learning even at will,

children.text: vismṛtānapi vettyeva śrutaṃ śīghraṃ ca dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: and he knows even things forgotten and quickly retains what he has heard.
After the second seven-day period, he should drink that juice as before.
Having heard them once, he can retain a hundred verses, even a thousand.
Thus, for three seven-day periods, the pure man should drink the juice of <s>brāhmī</s>.
Misfortune leaves his body, and imperishable speech enters him.
He becomes a <s>Vāgdevī</s> in male form, knowing the meanings of all <s>śāstras</s>.
Wise and knowing the <s>Veda</s> and <s>Vedānta</s>, he lives for five hundred years.
Now I shall tell, O <s>Devī</s>, the preparation made from <s>aṅkola</s> seeds.
It is to be undertaken by four steadfast practitioners who are pure and desire purification.
Together with the foremost practitioners, he should begin it under auspicious lunar asterisms.
He should clear the root of the <s>aṅkola</s> of grass, sweep it, and purify it.

children.text: tatra liṅgaṃ ca saṃsthāpya tadagre sthāpayedghaṭam
children.translated_text: There he should install a <s>liṅga</s>, and in front of it place a pot.
He should bind the <s>liṅga</s>, the <s>aṅkola</s>, and the pot with a single thread, dear one.
He should perform worship with fragrances, flowers, and the like by means of the <s>Aghora</s> mantra.
Each month, by day and night, flowers and the like should be offered until it bears fruit.
Taking that ripe fruit, he should fill that pot with the fruits.
Then, for the pleasure of <s>Yoginī</s> and <s>Bhairavī</s>, he should perform a great worship.
Having brought that pot home, he should dry the fruit in the sun.
He should make the seeds free of husks and rub their openings.
Then, on a vessel with a broad mouth, he should apply a coating of powdered clay.
He should plant each one with its mouth upward, shaped like a serpent.
Then he should similarly smear <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) on each of their mouths.
He should set that vessel on a bronze vessel, with it facing downward.
The wise man should keep it in the sun and cover it with straw.
For five days he should collect the oil that has dripped out day by day.
He should place that oil in a glass bottle, together with the mantra.
The measure is half a part of <s>aṅkola</s> oil and twice as much sesame oil.
As a nasal medicine in the two nostrils, it destroys old age and death.
He lives for three hundred years, free from every disease.
For men whose life-breaths have departed through disease, water, noose, and the like, through stupor and the like, or through poison,
one should administer nasal medicine mixed with male semen.

children.text: mṛtasūtaṃ ca tailaṃ te jīvanti ca na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When the oil is combined with killed mercury, they come back to life; there is no doubt.
This is the science of reviving the dead, previously mentioned, that has been taught, O blameless one.
Cardamom, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, the fruit of <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>, and <s>aruṣkara</s>,
<s>sahadevī</s>, neem leaves, and the tuber of <s>lāṅgalī</s>,
in equal parts, should be dried in the subterranean apparatus, and the oil should be drawn off.
One should take that oil as nasal medicine at intervals of seven days, dear one.
When nasal therapy is performed thus for a year, a man becomes one whose life lasts a thousand years.
He should drink half a <s>pala</s> of oil combined with the root of <s>nīlikā</s>.
After a year he becomes accomplished, free from wrinkles and gray hair.
After three years he lives for a day of <s>Brahmā</s>, swift as wind and very strong.
One should prepare a <s>prastha</s> each of <s>bhṛṅgī</s> juice and black cumin,

children.text: nīlotpalaṃ ca madhukaṃ prasthārdhaṃ ca pṛthagbhavet ||
children.translated_text: and separately half a <s>prastha</s> each of blue lotus and licorice.
He should cook all together with five <s>palas</s> of sesame oil.
When only oil remains, that oil destroys old age and death.
A half <s>niṣka</s>, one <s>niṣka</s>, and one and a half <s>niṣkas</s>, in sequence,
are said to be the measures of the oil; he lives for three hundred years.
Having added a <s>pala</s> of <s>iṣṭikākṣī</s>, he should drink one <s>karṣa</s> with water.
After a year it destroys gray hair, and the man becomes one whose life lasts a thousand years.

children.text: sarpākṣī kākamācī ca sahadevī ca bhṛṅgarāṭ
children.translated_text: <s>Sarpākṣī</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, and <s>bhṛṅgarāj</s>,
the fruit of <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>, neem leaf, and <s>vākucī</s> seed,
the whole <s>devadālī</s> with its root, <s>brāhmī</s> root, and the three fruits,
the root of <s>vājigandhā</s>, and leaves of blue <s>koraṇḍa</s>,
all in equal quantities, should be impregnated with the juices of <s>kanyakā</s>.
For seven days he should dry the powder in the shade, soaked with the three sweets.

children.text: dvikarṣaṃ pratyahaṃ sevyaṃ vatsareṇa jarāṃ jayet
children.translated_text: Two <s>karṣas</s> should be taken every day; in a year he conquers old age.
Endowed with great strength, he lives happily as long as the moon and stars endure.

The compound begins with <s>cāturjātaka</s>, <s>cora</s>, sandalwood water, grapes, <s>tugā</s>, <s>reṇukā</s>, musk, <s>tagara</s>, camphor, saffron filaments, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, and <s>abdaka</s>...
<s>Kaṅkola</s>, <s>amaradāru</s>, variegated poison, the two kinds of cumin, rock salt, <s>bhārṅgī</s>, <s>gokṣura</s>, <s>devapuṣpa</s>, <s>musalī</s>, licorice, <s>balā</s>, and sea-foam;

children.text: raṃbhākandaphalatrayaṃ trikaṭukaṃ jātīphalaṃ vāśakaṃ tālīśaṃ kaṭukīphalaṃ gajakaṇā māṣāmṛtāśarkarā
children.translated_text: plantain tuber, the three fruits, the three pungents, nutmeg, <s>vāśaka</s>, <s>tālīśa</s>, <s>kaṭukī</s> fruit, <s>gajakaṇā</s>, black gram, nectar, and sugar;

children.text: picchābhṛṅgavidārikāmadanakaṃ bījaṃ ca kacchūdbhavaṃ śālmalyaṅghripunarnavāgaruśatāvaryapyatho dīpyakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Picchā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>madana</s>, and the seed produced from <s>kacchū</s>; the root of <s>śālmalī</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, aloe-wood, <s>śatāvarī</s>, and then <s>dīpyaka</s>;

children.text: pādāṃśaṃ mṛtamabhrakaṃ ca vijayā tulyauṣadhānāṃ samā sarveṣāṃ sadṛśā sitā ca madhunā cājyena saṃyojitā
children.translated_text: a quarter part of dead mica, and <s>vijayā</s>, equal to the medicines; sugar equal to all of them is to be combined with honey and ghee.

children.text: jātīcampakaketakādikusumaiḥ seveta saṃvāsitaṃ karṣārdhaṃ niśi dehasiddhidamahākāmeśvaraḥ kāmadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should consume half a <s>karṣa</s> of it at night, perfumed with jasmine, campaka, ketaka, and other flowers; it is the great <s>Kāmeśvara</s>, giver of bodily perfection and desire.

children.text: puṃsāṃ śukravivṛddhidārḍhyakaraṇe kṣīrānupānaṃ hitaṃ śālmalyaṅghrijalānupānam athavāpyanyacca yacchukralam
children.translated_text: For men, when the aim is increasing and firming semen, milk is a suitable accompanying drink, or water from the root of <s>śālmalī</s>, or whatever else promotes semen.

children.text: prauḍhānāṃ sudṛśāṃ sukhātisukhado vaśyo mahādrāvakaḥ saṅge bhaṅgurakāmakautukarasaḥ krīḍākalāmodadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For mature beautiful women it gives pleasure beyond pleasure; it makes one subject to attraction, greatly liquefying, and in intercourse its rasa is fragile erotic delight, giving joy in the arts of play.

children.text: saṃbhoge sthavirāgniyoṣiti made yūnāṃ smare darpahā nityānandanidānam ādipuruṣair apyāhitāsvādanaḥ
children.translated_text: In sexual enjoyment with an old fiery woman, amid intoxication, it breaks the pride of young men's passion; it is the source of constant bliss and has been tasted even by the primordial men.
It brings success in speech, produces excellent compositions of poetry, and joins together special happiness, health, youth, and the full equipment of the arts.

children.text: vṛddhatvaṃ harate balaṃ ca kurute mṛtyuṃ nirasyetparaṃ vyādhivrātam apākaroti kurute kāntiṃ nayatyārjavam
children.translated_text: It removes old age and gives strength; it drives death far away, removes a mass of diseases, produces beauty, and leads to straightforwardness.

children.text: yogābhyāsavidhau ratasya sulabhā siddhiṃ vidhattetarām aṃhaḥ saṃtatisaṃhṛtiṃ kalayate strīṇām apatyapradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one devoted to the discipline of yoga practice, it readily grants a further accomplishment; it brings about the destruction of a succession of sins and gives offspring to women.

children.text: rogāṇāṃ nicayaṃ kṣayaṃ kṣapayati kṣipraṃ mahārudgaṇaṃ vyāhanti śvasanaṃ layaṃ gamayate chinte ca kāsodayam
children.translated_text: It destroys the accumulation of diseases and quickly consumes a great host of major disorders; it strikes down asthma, brings wasting to an end, and in cases of anxiety and the onset of cough

children.text: durnāmāni ca ṣaḍbhinatti harate sarvārtirogolbaṇaṃ mehaughaṃ ca lunāti śoṇitadaraṃ vidhvaṃsate sevanāt ||
children.translated_text: it splits the six kinds of piles, removes all severe pains and diseases, cuts off a flood of urinary disorders, and destroys bleeding through its use.

children.text: kṣīṇe poṣamupādadhāti vipulaṃ pūrṇātijīrṇojjvalaṃ mandāgniṃ grahaṇīṃ nikṛntatitarāṃ doṣānaśeṣānapi
children.translated_text: In one who is wasted it provides abundant nourishment; it cuts down excessive fullness, over-aging, burning splendor, weak digestive fire, <s>grahaṇī</s>, and indeed all the <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: śreṣṭhaḥ sarvarasāyaneṣu viduṣāṃ bhogārthināṃ yogināṃ siddhiṃ samyagihātanoti vapuṣaḥ saṃsevanād anvaham ||
children.translated_text: By daily use it fully produces bodily accomplishment here; it is best among all <s>rasāyanas</s> for the learned, for those who desire enjoyment, and for yogins.
Among these preparations beginning with the great tree, as taught by adepts,
this common formulation should be made by those who desire accomplishment.
One should use purified mercury, or mica, in a quantity the size of a <s>guñjā</s> seed, two <s>paṇas</s>,
and likewise magnetic iron; a man should eat it.
Through the combination of mercury, mica, and iron he attains accomplishment at once.
As a body is lifeless without life, and a flower is without fragrance,
just so herbal preparations without mercury do not bestow accomplishment.
Therefore, when joined with mercury, they bestow accomplishment immediately.
A <s>prastha</s> of juice of great indigo, a <s>prastha</s> of juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, dear one,
a <s>prastha</s> of juice of emblic fruit, and that produced from the fruit of <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>;
a <s>prastha</s> of decoction from sesame, a <s>prastha</s> of oil, and cow's milk,
an <s>āḍhaka</s>; one should combine them all, with one <s>pala</s> of <s>kākatuṇḍī</s> fruit.
There should be three <s>palas</s> of emblic, and one <s>pala</s> of powder of <s>bhṛṅga</s> and indigo leaves.

children.text: piṣṭvā tasmin kṣipet sarvaṃ pacenmandāgninā priye ||
children.translated_text: Having ground everything, one should put it into that and cook it over a gentle fire, dear one.
When only the oil remains, one should finish cooking it and then purify it through a cloth.
After anointing with this oil, one should perform an anointing of the head.
One should also fill the ears every day; in this way one should make a <s>rasāyana</s> treatment.
The hairs become like bees, and the hearing gains the sharpness of the horizons.
Diseases above the collarbone disappear, and it is also beneficial for the feet.
Sandalwood, aloe-wood, camphor, musk, and saffron,
the two kinds of <s>uśīra</s>, <s>kaṅkola</s>, nutmeg, and cloves,
<s>nalikā</s>, <s>nalada</s>, <s>spṛkkā</s>, <s>turuṣka</s>, and <s>sthāṇulocana</s>,
<s>hareṇu</s>, <s>tagara</s>, lac, <s>nakha</s>, <s>sthauṇeyaka</s>, <s>murā</s>,
<s>nalada</s>, emblic, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>coraka</s>, and <s>kaṭukī</s> fruit,
<s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, date, <s>padmaka</s>, and mace,
<s>śaileya</s>, <s>dhātakī</s> flowers, <s>sarala</s>, and <s>ailavāluka</s>,
betel-nut fruit, <s>saptaparṇa</s>, and likewise <s>tāmalaka</s>, dear one:

children.text: ekaikaṃ karṣamātraṃ syātprasthaṃ tailaṃ ca gopayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: each should be in the measure of one <s>karṣa</s>; there should also be a <s>prastha</s> of oil and cow's milk,
an <s>āḍhaka</s>. One should cook all that and collect it when only the oil remains.

children.text: tasmin mṛgāṇḍaṃ kastūrīṃ karpūraṃ kuṅkumaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Into it one should put deer's musk, musk, camphor, and saffron,
one <s>karṣa</s> of each separately; a wise man should perfume it with jasmine and other flowers.
With that he should anoint the lower body, removing bad odor.
Even if he is about eighty years old, he will become like a sixteen-year-old.
He becomes the root of pride for the world of women, handsome, and possessed of increased semen.

children.text: yoṣicchataṃ ca ramate sa jīveccharadaḥ śatam
children.translated_text: He enjoys a hundred women and lives for a hundred autumns.
Now I shall explain an unguent that breaks wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhaṃ samaṃ mardyaṃ stanadugdhena yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury and sulfur should be rubbed together in equal amount with a woman's breast milk.
<s>Muṇḍikā</s>, <s>meghanāda</s>, <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, and likewise <s>muni</s>,
and <s>sarpākṣī</s>: with the juices of these one should triturate it for one day.
Alkali of sesame and barley, ten times as much as this,
all this, together with equal honey and ghee; with this he should rub the body.
There will be destruction of wrinkles and gray hair; after a year he will live three hundred years.
The practitioner, having become possessed of a divine body, will live; there is no doubt about this.
O <s>Sūta</s>, he should rub a lotus with its stalk for seven days.
Then he should massage his body with his own <s>śiva</s>-water.
After a year perfection arises; as before, he has a divine body.
And with <s>śivāmbhas</s> he should rub the lordly mercury together with the root of <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>.
He should rub it well for seven days, O goddess, and then massage himself thoroughly.
After a year perfection arises; as before, he has a divine body.
He should steep <s>surabhi</s> in pungent oil for seven days.
He should eat half a <s>pala</s> every day; after a year his body becomes adamantine.
He has a lifespan of three hundred years, is golden in color, and is free from wrinkles and gray hair.
A man should lick in the morning a <s>karṣa</s> of powdered <s>kuṣṭha</s> mixed with honey and ghee.
His limbs become fragrant like <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, and he lives without wrinkles.
He should take <s>kākatuṇḍī</s> fruit, powdered <s>kānta</s>, and <s>āmrāṇḍa</s> oil.

children.text: āloḍya bhāṇḍe nikṣipya māsaṃ dhānyamaye kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: After stirring them together and putting them in a vessel, he should place it among grain for a month.
Having taken it out, he should apply it to the head; with this, nasal treatment is performed.

children.text: tryahāt keśāḥ sunīlāḥ syuḥ ṣaṇmāsāt keśarañjanam ||
children.translated_text: After three days the hairs become very dark blue; after six months there is hair coloring.
One <s>niṣka</s> of <s>harītakī</s>, two <s>palas</s> of powdered <s>kānta</s>,
and one <s>pala</s> of powdered <s>nāga</s> should be rubbed together with sour curd.
After being anointed, he should put it on the head and rub it for half a <s>nāḍikā</s>.
He should wrap it with castor leaves and then bind it with a cloth.
He should bathe, and again for three days, as before, there is hair coloring.
<s>Nīlikā</s> and <s>bhṛṅga</s>, together with their roots, and iron powder equal to <s>varā</s>,
should be powdered and steeped for one day in ram's urine.
After doing the bathing and other acts as before, hair coloring occurs as before.
Skinless <s>guñjā</s> fruit, cardamom, deodar, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>

children.text: samaṃ cūrṇaṃ bhṛṅgarasair bhāvyam ekadinaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: should be powdered in equal amounts and steeped for one day in juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, dear one.
The wise man should cook another powder with oil over a gentle fire.
By anointing with that oil and ghee, the hair becomes like bees.
Equal parts of burnt elephant ivory and <s>rasāñjana</s>
should be ground with goat's milk; by application, there is hair coloring.
Black earth, <s>triphala</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s> juice, and iron powder in equal amounts
should be stirred together in a vessel and kept sealed for one month.
By applying that, the locks become black after five months.

children.text: dhātrīphalaṃ japāpuṣpaṃ kiṭṭaṃ piṣṭvā ca mūrdhani ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātrī</s> fruit, hibiscus flower, and dregs should be ground and placed on the head.
He should apply it for three days; through that, the hair becomes like bees.
The powder is like vermilion, and <s>sāmbraṇī</s> equal to those two is added.
After grinding it with water, by applying it as a paste there is hair coloring at once.
<s>Gorocanā</s>, black sesame seeds, <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, with <s>śivāmbu</s>,
and <s>kākamācī</s>: all this should be rubbed in an iron vessel.
With that alone, after one day, there is excellent hair coloring.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ siddhārthakaṃ sarjo yavakṣāraṃ ca kāñjikaiḥ
children.translated_text: Powdered white mustard, resin, and alkali of barley with sour gruel
should be ground with juices of <s>nāgapuṣpa</s>; the application is for hair coloring.
Powder of plantain root, together with vermilion and embers,
should be ground with lemon juices in an iron vessel, using an iron pestle.
By applying that for one day, coloring of the hair occurs.
<s>Kāsīsa</s>, leaves of <s>nīlikā</s>, curd, and <s>bhṛṅga</s> juice,
along with iron powder in equal portions: by application, there is hair coloring.
He should rub the leaves of <s>koraṇṭa</s> with a lead rod.

children.text: dinatrayaṃ ca tallepāt keśāḥ syur bhramaropamāḥ
children.translated_text: By applying that paste for three days, the hair becomes like bees.

children.text: varā bhṛṅgī cūtabījaṃ mṛṇālaṃ ca priyaṅgukam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Varā</s>, <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, mango seed, lotus fiber, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>,
<s>nīlī</s>, turmeric, iron, and lead, powdered with neem oil,
should be stirred in a <s>kānta</s> vessel and steeped for one month.

children.text: tena liptāḥ kacāḥ kṛṣṇā rañjitā bhramaropamāḥ
children.translated_text: Locks smeared with that become black, colored like bees.
Black sesame seeds and seeds of <s>kākamācī</s>, in equal parts,
should be taken from an oil apparatus; through that there is hair coloring.
For seven days he should perform nasal therapy with a <s>karṣa</s> of hibiscus juice and honey.
After that it colors the hair; this is indeed the best of all nasal treatments.
After grinding <s>triphala</s> and iron powder with juices of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>,

children.text: tailam etatsamaṃ yojyaṃ tathā bhṛṅgarasaiḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: this oil should be added in equal amount, and again with <s>bhṛṅga</s> juice.
He should cook everything over a gentle fire until only the oil remains.

children.text: snigdhabhāṇḍe ca tattailaṃ māsaṃ bhūmau vinikṣipet
children.translated_text: He should put that oil in a greased vessel and bury it in the earth for a month.
He should apply the oil to the head, first with leaves of <s>kāravallī</s>.
He should wrap it with that and with a cloth, stay in a windless place, and live on milk.
He should wash it with decoctions of <s>triphala</s> and do this for seven days, dear one.
It produces coloring of the scalp for as long as life lasts; there is no doubt.
The seeds of <s>śriyālī</s> and <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>, with juices of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>,
should be steeped with hibiscus-flower juice separately for four days.
He should draw out that oil in a subterranean apparatus; with it he should make an application.
He should apply it on the head and wrap it with <s>gandharva</s> leaves.
Then with a cloth, the wise man should remain in a place without wind.
Living on milk, he should bathe in sour gruel for seven days; such is the rule.
The hair becomes like bees for as long as life lasts; there is no doubt.
<s>Jalamaṇḍanikā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>bhṛṅga</s>, all in equal amounts,
should be ground, and he should cook an oil well; then he should apply it with oil.
He should smear the head with it for seven days; there is hair coloring.
Bathing, food, and bedding should be arranged as before.
Having ground it with the juices of <s>varā</s> and <s>bhṛṅga</s>, he should smear it in an iron vessel.
Having set it down facing downward, in the morning with the juices of royal <s>bhṛṅga</s>,
he should grind it again, lick the head, and wash it with <s>triphala</s> water.
He should do this for twenty-one days; he obtains the result as before.

children.text: garalaṃ kṛṣṇajīraṃ ca piṣṭvā ruddhvā ca tanmukham
children.translated_text: Having ground poison and black cumin, and having sealed its mouth,

children.text: gṛhāṅgaṇe paṅkile ca khanitvā sthāpayet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should dig in the muddy courtyard of the house and place it there.
After six months, when it has become liquid and black, he should carefully take it up.
He should put a <s>karṣa</s> in the middle of the head, with wrapping and the rest as before.
It colors the hair from birth onward; that is the <s>kāpāla</s> coloring.
<s>Bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>nīlī</s>, <s>varā</s>, black iron, and <s>madana</s> seed,
<s>koraṇṭa</s> flowers, and powder produced from the bark of <s>arjuna</s>,
lotus root and also <s>jambū</s>: all of this should be in equal parts.
He should put it in an iron vessel and bury it in the ground for a fortnight.
He should take out the paste contained in the vessel; from the paste, oil should be four times as much.
The juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s> should be four times as much as the oil, and the decoction of <s>varā</s> four times as much as that.
All this should be cooked over a gentle fire.
He should cook it until only the oil remains; having ground it, he should put it in an iron vessel.
And for testing it, he should smear a crow's feather.

children.text: tailena yadi kṛṣṇaṃ tadauṣadhaṃ siddhidaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: If it becomes black from the oil, that medicine is one that gives success.

children.text: sādhako māsam ekaṃ tu tasminpātre vipācitam ||
children.translated_text: The practitioner should use for one month what has been cooked in that vessel.
His hairs, anointed with it, become like bees after six months.
With the liquids of tamarind, aśvattha, palāśa, and vāsā, again and again,

children.text: drutaṃ pātragataṃ nāgaṃ cālayed bhasmatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: he should stir melted lead placed in a vessel; it becomes ash.
He should cook the lead ash so long, with one <s>pala</s> of iron powder,
two <s>palas</s> of <s>varā</s> powder, and three <s>palas</s> of pomegranate bark.
Add one <s>pala</s> of this, and sour gruel equal to all of it, in an iron vessel.
He should stir it and cook it a little, for a moment, in that iron vessel.
He should keep it in the sun, steeped in the juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s> and <s>koraṇṭa</s>.

children.text: ekaviṃśaddinaṃ bhāvyaṃ bhūyo bhūyo dravaṃ dravam
children.translated_text: It should be steeped for twenty-one days, with liquid after liquid, again and again.
Hairs anointed with just that become feather-like, resembling feathers.
In the stated and unstated procedures for coloring hair,
application at night and wrapping with castor leaves,
and bathing in the morning: this procedure is remembered as common to all.

children.text: śmaśāne salile mārge gṛhe devālaye tathā ||
children.translated_text: In a cremation ground, in water, on a road, in a house, and likewise in a temple,
in a place joined with feces and urine, in a village, in a cow pen, beneath a tree,
in shade, in a poisonous place, in bad cold, and where there is other affliction,
in places of this sort a siddha herb should not be taken.

children.text: araṇye parvate tīre nadyā tapavane śucau ||
children.translated_text: In a forest, on a mountain, on a riverbank, in a pure ascetic grove,
in a pure field joined with rock, in a siddha field, on the shore of the ocean,
on <s>Śrīparvata</s>, on the <s>Himagiri</s>, at a pond, or in a solitary lake,
he should take herbs born there, which bestow perfection of the body.
For all siddha roots, in the acts of tying protection,
digging, uprooting, and taking, in due order,
divine mantras are taught, remembered as common to all.
On the preceding day, having bathed well and cleaned his teeth,
anointed, wearing clean garments, cheerful, and with restrained mind,
silent, furnished with fragrance and unbroken rice, with a protective thread for tying,
he should go to the herb previously located, which grants his desired aim.
Having cleared away the grass all around, he should dig and sprinkle water around it.
Having performed worship with fragrance, flowers, and unbroken rice, he should bind it with the thread.
The best practitioner, with mantra, fasting, and self-controlled, should say:

children.text: atraiva tiṣṭha kalyāṇi mama kāryakarī bhava ||
children.translated_text: "Remain right here, auspicious one; become the accomplisher of my task.

children.text: mama kāryakarī siddhā tataḥ svargaṃ gamiṣyasi
children.translated_text: When, accomplished, you have done my task, then you will go to heaven.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ namaste 'mṛtasambhūte balavīryavivardhini balamāyuśca me dehi pāpaṃ me jahi dūrataḥ
children.translated_text: "Oṃ hrīṃ, reverence to you, born of nectar, increaser of strength and vigor. Give me strength and long life; drive my sin far away.
Hrīṃ phaṭ."

children.text: anenaiva tu mantreṇa tridhā sūtreṇa veṣṭitam ||
children.translated_text: With this very mantra, when it has been wrapped three times with the thread,

children.text: rakṣāṃ badhnīta tāṃ spṛṣṭvā japedaṣṭottaraṃ śatam
children.translated_text: he should tie the protection; touching it, he should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.

children.text: tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya kṛtvā nityavidhiṃ śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, rising in the morning, having performed his daily rite, pure,
he should approach that herb with fragrance, flowers, unbroken rice, and the like.
Having worshiped it with all offerings, he should give an intentional oblation.
The wise man should dig with mantra; this mantra too is taught:

children.text: yena tvāṃ khanate brahmā yena tvāṃ khanate bhṛguḥ ||
children.translated_text: "By that with which <s>Brahmā</s> digs you, by that with which <s>Bhṛgu</s> digs you,
by that with which <s>Indra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> dig you, with that I approach you.
I myself will dig you with a hand purified by mantra."
Having first entreated it in this way, afterward he should utter the mantra:

children.text: oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ taṃ amṛteśvari ehi ehi mama sakalasiddhiṃ kuru huṃ phaṭ
children.translated_text: "Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ taṃ, O <s>Amṛteśvarī</s>, come, come; accomplish all my siddhi, huṃ phaṭ."
With this very mantra he should dig up the siddhi herb.
Then, with joined palms, he should uproot it and pray as follows:

children.text: mā utpate mā nipate mā ca te cānyathā bhavet
children.translated_text: "Do not fly up, do not fall down, and do not become otherwise.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ caṇḍa huṃ phaṭ svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ caṇḍa huṃ phaṭ svāhā."
With this very mantra, O supreme goddess, he should uproot it.
Taking it with its root unbroken, wrapped in clean cloth,
placing it in a basket, and then in a pure place in his own dwelling,
he should joyfully set it down in storage; afterward comes the breaking of the fast.

children.text: oṃ namo bhairavāya mahāsiddhipradāyakāya āpaduttaraṇāya huṃ phaṭ
children.translated_text: "Oṃ, reverence to <s>Bhairava</s>, giver of great siddhi, deliverer from calamity, huṃ phaṭ."
With this very mantra, having taken it, he should bring it home.
Then the goddess <s>Parameśvarī</s>, pleased in mind, asked:
<s>Śrī Bhairavī</s>:
O primordial <s>Bhairava</s>, lord of the gods, cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution,
omniscient <s>Śiva</s>, lord of the world, through your grace, O mighty one,
I have heard many and various divine <s>rasāyanas</s> (rejuvenating elixirs).
Tell me, O god, treasure of compassion, of one that is easy to accomplish, easy to obtain, divine, and immediately produces proof of its effect,
especially suitable for children, women, eunuchs, the elderly, and those afflicted by disease,
and fit for those who are qualified for <s>rasāyana</s> treatment.
Then <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Bhava-bhairava</s>, whose lotus-face was smiling, spoke:
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s>:
Listen, goddess; I shall teach what is suitable for all and brings happiness,
purifying, easy to obtain, and destroying inner and outer sin.
From it the worlds have arisen, and even the vital breaths of living beings;
it protects the whole universe and has all the gods as its essence, dear one.
It pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s>, gives well-being, is wholesome, and surpasses all flavors,
joined with rasa and with life-giving qualities beginning with the six; it bestows strength.
The life and strength of living beings are, for the most part, rooted in digestive fire.
Water is the fuel of that fire; therefore the wise person should drink water.
There are three fires: the lightning fire, the submarine fire, and the digestive fire.
For other fires, wood and the like are indeed their fuels; without fuel they would cease.
Therefore, goddess, I tell what is auspicious: listen to the water-<s>rasāyana</s>.
In the morning one should fill a new pot with purified waters,
whether from the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, from rivers, from ponds, or from lakes,
or from wells, or even with hot-season or rain water, according to what is available.
One should place that pot on a stand, where it is touched by the rays of the divine sun,
its defects destroyed, and at night bathed in the nectar-rays of the moon.
It should be scented with cardamom, <s>uśīra</s>, camphor, and sandalwood,
and perfumed with <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>ketakī</s>, <s>jāti</s>, <s>mallikā</s>, and blue lotus.
With a fan of <s>uśīra</s> and palm leaf sprinkled with water, gently,
it is fanned again and again; this is called <s>haṃsodaka</s>.
Before the rising of <s>Anurādhā</s>, and before touching feces or urine,
one should drink the water; after that one should pass feces and urine.
Performing the twilight worship and other duties, one may then eat according to one's wish.
A child of one year should drink one <s>pala</s> of water every day,

children.text: evaṃ ṣoḍaśavarṣāntaṃ pratyabdaṃ ca palaṃ palam
children.translated_text: and in this way, up to the sixteenth year, year by year, <s>pala</s> by <s>pala</s>,
the wise person should gradually increase it up to the limit of sixteen <s>palas</s>.
After sixteen years, water measuring sixteen <s>prasṛtas</s> is to be used,
and in this way, up to the twentieth year, one should take it daily with care.

children.text: anena vyādhayaḥ sarve vinaśyanti na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: By this all diseases are destroyed; there is no doubt.
One lives a hundred years, endowed with intelligence, strength, sound senses, and happiness.
For long life one should drink one <s>prasṛta</s>, equal to eight <s>palas</s>.
According to the strength of the digestive fire, after three days or after five days,
or after a week, the wise person should gradually increase it by one <s>prasṛta</s> at a time,
and then also by a <s>kuḍava</s>, increasing it very slowly.
It should be used until it reaches sixteen <s>prasṛtas</s>; after that,
as the water is increased, so the <s>doṣa</s> becomes pacified.

children.text: ṣaṇmāsaṃ vā vatsaraṃ vā vādyantaṃ vā pibejjalam
children.translated_text: One may drink water for six months, for a year, or from beginning to end,
and as there has been increase, so there should be reduction, down to only a handful.
He should avoid fasting by day or night, and should eat wholesome food.
But when there is extreme exercise, he should drink only a handful.

children.text: pādamardhaṃ tripādaṃ vā yathā sevāñjaliṃ pibet
children.translated_text: According to practice, he may drink a quarter, a half, three quarters, or a full handful.
Mixed with any one among honey, ghee, oil, milk, ghee-water, and the like,
it quickly destroys diseases of <s>vāta</s>, or else when joined with the appropriate medicines.
Having eaten the medicine that pacifies each particular disease,

children.text: tato jalaṃ vā prapibenmuhūrte vā gate sati
children.translated_text: then one may drink water, either after a <s>muhūrta</s> has passed,

children.text: jīrṇe vā salile sevyaṃ bhojanānte'thavā niśi ||
children.translated_text: or when the water has been digested; it may be taken at the end of a meal or at night.
If fever or another disease has arisen and fasting is required,
he should drink half of the previous amount, taking light food as is comfortable.

children.text: upavāso vratārthaṃ cet tatkṣīraṃ vā palaṃ niśi
children.translated_text: If the fast is for the sake of a vow, then he may take milk, or one <s>pala</s>, at night.
When there is no eating at night, goddess, water dries up in the stomach.

children.text: ardhaṃ vā prāñjaliṃ vāri pibennityaṃ prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore he should carefully drink half, or a full cupped handful, of water every day.
In all cases the wise person should drink water in balance with food, bodily strength, and digestive fire.
If passing feces and urine occurs before the <s>brāhma muhūrta</s>,

children.text: tataḥ pītvaiva salilaṃ viṇmūtraṃ ca visarjayet ||
children.translated_text: then, only after drinking water, should he pass feces and urine.
Even purified water becomes slightly poisonous after the passing of feces and urine.
If at night, at an unknown time, he drinks water, he should drink water again in the morning.
He should drink a quarter, or a fourth part, or a handful of water.
Wheat, sixty-day rice, <s>śāli</s> rice, barley, and meat from wild animals,
cow's ghee, curd, milk, buttermilk, and fresh butter,
honey, sugarcane, pomegranate, grapes, plantain, dates, and sugar,
mango fruit, emblic myrobalan, and fresh coconut water,
pumpkin, bottle-gourd, and neem leaves and fruits,
the leaves, flowers, and fruits of <s>śigru</s>, and soups and juices made from green gram,
<s>suniṣaṇṇaka</s>, <s>goraṇṭī</s>, and the two kinds of <s>jīvantī</s>,
<s>rājavṛkṣa</s>, <s>śothaghnī</s>, <s>cillī</s>, or <s>laghucchadā</s>,

children.text: śatāvarī taṇḍulī ca matsyākṣī ca vidārikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>taṇḍulī</s>, <s>matsyākṣī</s>, and <s>vidārikā</s>,
<s>upodakī</s>, eggplant, and the fruits of bitter gourd,
small <s>kośātakī</s>, <s>lakṣmī</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, and palm-root,
the flower of the plantain, stem-fruits, and <s>kṣudradantikā</s>.

children.text: sadāphalaṃ ca matsyāṇḍī śṛṅgaveraṃ ca saindhavam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sadāphala</s>, <s>matsyāṇḍī</s>, ginger, and rock salt;
<s>phalapūra</s>, sour fruit, ripe <s>dhātrī</s> fruit, and <s>alarkaka</s>;
<s>vāyasī</s>, <s>kuntalī</s>, and likewise <s>vasukanyālikā</s>;
<s>kustumbarī</s>, <s>sarasī</s>, <s>śārṅgerī</s>, and <s>cakramardaka</s>;
<s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, leaves of <s>pālakī</s>, and likewise <s>gāṅgeruka</s>;
<s>ākhukarṇī</s>, leaves of <s>kāsamarda</s>, and likewise <s>gāṅgeruka</s>;
and, for preparation, <s>kaiḍarya</s>, rock salt, pungent substances, and digestives;
all of these are mostly sweet, pleasant and cooling, and they bring comfort.
The young fruits of <s>kataka</s> and <s>pathyā</s>, smeared with salt,
and the stalks, flowers, rhizomes, and filaments of blue lotus and lotus are also suitable.
He should resort to a bath accompanied by oil, clean and wearing white garments.
He should use an anointing with musk, sandalwood, cooling <s>hima</s>, and camphor,
a gentle breeze, flower garlands, moonlight, and ornaments of jewels.

children.text: pathyaṃ rucyaṃ jalīyaṃ ca svāduprāyaṃ ca sadravam
children.translated_text: Food should be wholesome, appetizing, watery, mostly sweet, and rich in fluid.
The water-drinker should eat cooked rice with ghee and milk.
He should chew betel with camphor and sit comfortably.
In the evening he should take coconut water, and at night milk with sugar.

children.text: śālmalī tūlaśayyā ca niśi nidrā yathāsukham
children.translated_text: At night there should be a bed of silk-cotton down and sleep as pleasantly as possible.
Deficient, excessive, obstructing, constipating, hot, and harsh things,
dry, disagreeable, stale, heavy, slimy food and food taken at an improper time,
<s>kulmāṣa</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, the two pungent substances, bottle gourd, and hard-to-digest foods,
horse-gram soup, <s>kāliṅga</s>, <s>guñjā</s>, and fruits of trees,
onion, garlic, all tubers, and mustard seed,
meat that is not from dry-land animals, fish, and even a little food of rice cooked with milk,
unprescribed vegetables, grain, fruit, and meat combined with milk,
and all dishes combined with any kind of milk, even if they are sweet,

children.text: tilatailaṃ ca tatkalkam etaiḥ saṃyuktam auṣadham ||
children.translated_text: sesame oil, its paste, and medicine combined with these are to be avoided.
Excessive talking, sunlight, shade, fatigue, worry, travel, and anger,
grief, riding in vehicles, fear, laziness, and excessive sexual intercourse,
carrying a load on the head, swimming through water, and fasting,
exercise, jealousy, sleeping by day, and keeping awake at night,
the east wind, cold, dust, and a place where wind predominates,
a smoke-filled house and a bed prepared with cotton,
fire, exertion that produces sweat, and wearing hot garments,
wearing silk, striking the thighs, and a hard seat,
a hot dwelling, alkaline or well water, and pungent and bitter tastes,
sour, astringent, and bitter tastes, <s>rāmaṭha</s>, and drying substances,

children.text: madirā ca vasā majjā mūtraṃ duṣṭajalāni ca
children.translated_text: wine, fat, marrow, urine, and bad waters,
intoxication, cold things, unhealthy food, and food without oil,
oil massage, cold sour gruel, and astringent decoction when there is no disease,
things that burn in digestion, drying things, and bathing the head even with hot water:
one should avoid anything else blameworthy that is a cause of aggravation of the <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: svasthaḥ pītvā sukhāsīnaḥ salilaṃ vāgyataḥ śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: When healthy, after drinking, he should sit comfortably, restrain his speech, and remain pure.
He should void stool and urine and avoid betel and the like.
If urine passes out in the same measure as the water he drinks,
then, when no medicine is involved, he should know that the water has been digested.
When the drunk water comes out, he is considered still healthier.
When the drunk water has gone out completely, hunger arises.
Then he should perform an oil massage and observe the prescribed wholesome regimen.
Without observance of the avoidances, diseases certainly arise.
Fatigue, exhaustion, vomiting, headache, dizziness,
stoppage and drying up of the water, congestion, and suppression of natural urges,
<s>gulma</s> and <s>udāvarta</s>, depression of the digestive fire, and breaking pain in the limbs,

children.text: todo bastau mehane ca vakṣaṇe hṛdi locane
children.translated_text: stabbing pain in the bladder, penis, groin, heart, and eyes,
cramping of the shanks, dyspnea, aversion to food, and loss of appetite,
urinary stone, nasal catarrh, cough, and diarrhea that is difficult to overcome may occur.
If the water is dried up once by dry exertional acts and the like,

children.text: sa doṣo na tu vijñeyo doṣastaṃbho'sakṛdyadi
children.translated_text: that should not be understood as a morbid <s>doṣa</s>; but if blockage occurs repeatedly, it is a <s>doṣa</s>.
When the drunk water is obstructed, the treatment for this is prescribed.
A wise man should cover the abdomen and the bladder with leaves of <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>.
For the release of the water, he should apply a paste that promotes urination.
Or he should bathe as a <s>rasāyana</s> measure, with his limbs smeared with ghee and <s>dhātrī</s>.

children.text: saguḍaṃ vā pibetkṣīraṃ takraṃ vā śarkarānvitam ||
children.translated_text: Or he should drink milk with jaggery, or buttermilk mixed with sugar.
Or he may take cucumber and <s>urvāru</s> seeds with coconut water and sugar.

children.text: kaṣṭājjīrṇaṃ jalaṃ yasya bhukteḥ prāk sarpir ādadet ||
children.translated_text: If one's water digests only with difficulty, one should take ghee before a meal.
Or he should remain for a long time in water and bathe with cool substances such as <s>dhātrī</s>.
Or, when the drunk water is obstructed, he should cleanse with sweet and cooling substances.
He should vomit with pastes of <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>madana</s>, and <s>sindhūttha</s>, mixed with honey.
Having drunk powder of <s>pathyā</s> with coconut water, he should purge.
Or, with <s>trijātaka</s>, <s>vyosa</s>, <s>krimighna</s>, <s>amalaka</s>, and <s>abdaka</s>,
<s>trivṛt</s>, equal to all of them, should be added, and sugar equal to all of this.
Having made honeyed pills, he should lick them for the release of the water.
If <s>varā</s> is taken at night, it destroys all <s>doṣas</s>.
He should place a wet cloth below the navel for only a moment.

children.text: avagāhena śītāmbho mūrdhni vā śītavāri ca ||
children.translated_text: With immersion in cold water, or else cold water on the head,
