he should apply it, or lie on a bed adorned with wet sand.
Or he should sit in a shower-house; cucumber and <s>urvāru</s> seeds

children.text: varīdrākṣāmbunā peyaṃ vā tu kāśmīrajaṃ vṛṣam
children.translated_text: should be drunk with water of <s>varī</s> and grapes, or else <s>vṛṣa</s> from Kashmir.
Or grape juice should be drunk, together with cucumber seeds.
Or <s>madhuka</s> and sugar with the water used for washing rice;
or jaggery with grapes and <s>darvi</s>, combined with rice-water.
Or <s>gostani</s>, mixed with sugar, with the juice of <s>dhatri</s> fruits;

children.text: varīṃ vā śarkarāyuktāṃ drākṣāṃ vā mastunā saha ||
children.translated_text: or <s>vari</s> with sugar, or grapes together with whey.

children.text: jalena vā guḍaṃ peyaṃ nālikerajalena vā
children.translated_text: Or jaggery should be drunk with water, or with coconut water.
Or a paste made from <s>tugaksiri</s>, or seeds of <s>karkaru</s> gourd,

children.text: kalpaṃ vā tāmalakyāśca mūlaṃ vā yaṣṭikalkakam
children.translated_text: or a preparation of <s>tamalaki</s>, or its root, or a paste of licorice,
or the ripe fruit of <s>pisacakadali</s>, mixed with honey and sugar,
or with coconut water, or with buttermilk, or with whey,
or with water from the plantain corm, or with milk, or with juices of emblic fruit,
or with juices of <s>amrta</s>, or with fresh juice of white gourd,
or with juices of pomegranate, and likewise with juices of <s>abhiru</s>,
or with juices of bottle gourd; one should drink cardamom with sugar.
Plantain corm, licorice, <s>svadamstra</s>, and <s>kaseruka</s>,
the roots of the five grasses, together with <s>sukra</s> and <s>satavari</s>:
of these, beginning with plantain corm, a decoction
should be drunk with honey or with sugar for releasing retained water.

children.text: evaṃ brāhme muhūrte yatpītaṃ vāri rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: Thus water drunk at the <s>Brahma-muhurta</s> is a <s>rasayana</s> (rejuvenating treatment).
It pacifies all <s>dosas</s> without remainder and destroys diseases too:
<s>raktavata</s>, the wind disorders, heart disease, asthma and cough,
<s>raktapitta</s>, the bile disorders, <s>grahani</s>, vomiting, and loss of appetite,
wasting, fainting, skin disease, urinary disorder, delusion, goiter, tumors, and other illnesses,
abdominal lumps, spleen disease, stones, colic, distension, indigestion, and cholera,
worms, anemia, jaundice, <s>halimaka</s>, and erysipelas,

children.text: vraṇaṃ ca śvayathuṃ śvitramagnisādaṃ tridhā viṣam
children.translated_text: wounds, swelling, vitiligo, weakness of digestive fire, and the threefold poison,
diseases above the collarbone and of the private parts, epilepsy and confusion,
fevers, abdominal bloating, dropsy, obstruction of urine, and piles.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, he lives for three hundred years.
He is firm-minded, strong, steadfast, handsome, and a source of desire in beloved women.
The man who drinks water through the nostrils in the morning,
a <s>sukti</s> measure every day, eating wholesome food and with his senses subdued,
obtains keenness of the senses and the destruction of wrinkles and gray hair.
He attains a lifespan of a hundred years; this is the nostril <s>rasayana</s>.
<s>Sribhairavi</s>:
Lord, by your grace I have heard the sequence of daily observance.
Master, I wish to hear the occasional observance; tell me.
<s>Sribhairava</s>:

children.text: tacchṛṇu tvaṃ mahādevi brūmi naimittikīṃ vidhim
children.translated_text: Listen to that, great goddess; I shall teach the occasional rule.
That rule is dependent on time, unfailing, and always immeasurable.
Time is without beginning or end, subtle and gross, all-pervading and eternal.
<s>Brahma</s> and the others, the sun and the others, and the great elements and the rest,
all follow time; in their activity they have the form of time.

children.text: kālādeva hi jāyante līyante tatra sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: From time alone they are born, and into it they always dissolve.

children.text: yaḥ kālaḥ so'hameveti tvaṃ ca kālapravartinī
children.translated_text: That time is myself, and you are the one who sets time in motion.
Therefore it is declared for the birth and death of beings who are born.
This time is indivisible; nevertheless it is divided.
The time in which a lotus leaf is pierced by a sharp needle

children.text: sa kālo lava ityuktastruṭī triṃśallavair bhavet
children.translated_text: is called a <s>lava</s>; a <s>truti</s> consists of thirty <s>lavas</s>.
That time which is a <s>truti</s>: a <s>matra</s> is furnished with two of those.

children.text: dṛkpakṣmaṇoḥ parikṣepaḥ sa tu mātrā praśasyate
children.translated_text: The movement of the eyelashes over the two eyes is praised as a <s>matra</s>.
With eighteen <s>matras</s> there is a <s>kastha</s>; a <s>kala</s> consists of thirty <s>kasthas</s>.
A <s>ksana</s> is said to consist of thirty <s>kalas</s>; a <s>nadika</s> of six <s>ksanas</s>.
Two <s>nadis</s> make a <s>muhurta</s>, and four of those make a <s>yamaka</s>.
With four <s>yamas</s> there is the day, and likewise the night, dear one.

children.text: evaṃ divāniśaṃ kiṃ tu pūrvāhṇo daśa nāḍikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus day and night are reckoned; but the forenoon is ten <s>nadikas</s>.
At midday there are ten <s>nadis</s>, and the afternoon is the same.
The early night, midnight, and likewise the latter part of the night are divided in the same way.
By fifteen days there is a fortnight called the bright one.
The second is the dark fortnight; from two fortnights a month is produced.
From two months comes what is called a season; from two seasons comes what is called a <s>kala</s>.
Three seasons make an <s>ayana</s>, and from two <s>ayanas</s> there is a year.
Therefore time is divided in eighteen ways.
The months beginning with <s>Magha</s> occur in sequence, beginning with winter.
Winter, spring, summer, the rains, autumn, and the cold season are the seasons.

children.text: ṛtavo dakṣiṇaṃ teṣāṃ kathayāmi śṛṇu priye ||
children.translated_text: I shall describe their course; listen, dear one.
There the sun and the quarters are obscured by frost,
and the wind is smoky, dust-dimmed, slow, and awakens cold.
It makes the hairs bristle; the <s>kaubera</s> and <s>lavalya</s> plants are then in flower.
Bees are scented by the flowers of <s>punnaga</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, and <s>phalini</s>.
Elephants, horses, cows, buffaloes, crows, goats, and the rest are stirred with pride.
River birds and other creatures are covered by sheets of frost.
Wells have warm, steaming water; behold the wintry season.

children.text: evaṃ hi śiśire kāle cayaṃ yāti kaphaḥ svataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in wintertime <s>kapha</s> naturally goes into accumulation.
In spring the quarters are clear, and the sun has reddish rays.
The <s>Malaya</s> breeze moves, and everything is adorned with new shoots.
Trees everywhere are flowering, rich with fresh bark and leaves,
with blossoms of mango, <s>asoka</s>, <s>bakula</s>, <s>madhavi</s>, and <s>campaka</s>,
and with flowers such as <s>palasa</s>; the woodland shines forth,
filled with the hum of wandering bees and the calls of cuckoos.
And <s>śleṣman</s> becomes aggravated; this is indeed the best of all seasons.
In summer the fierce sun, sharp-rayed and violent, is like a flax flower.
It heats the earth and the quarters, drying up all the sap of the ground.
The directions and the earth are grey, blazing excessively with forest fires.
The southwest wind is extremely fierce, and the violent storm becomes harsh and unpleasant.
By heat, sweat, and wind, living beings are as if fever-stricken.
The reservoirs are disturbed by overheated boars, buffaloes, and elephants,
with their scanty water dried by the burning rays of the fierce sun.
Ponds and the like are rippled, and their aquatic creatures are scorched.
Trees stand with old, dry, broken, and fallen leaves.
They are hot, without shade, and violently tossed by the wind.
Their leaves, creepers, and shrubs are dry, while <s>śirīṣa</s> trees shine with blossoms.
<s>Śleṣman</s> diminishes day by day; therefore <s>vāyu</s> accumulates.
In the rainy season the west wind blows, and the earth is covered with new grass.
It is entirely covered by clouds, broken and dark like collyrium.
The earth is covered with <s>śakragopa</s> insects and is charming with every crop.
It is hidden by masses of ground-creepers, wet with water, and muddy.
It is filled with the playful dancing of flocks of intoxicated peacocks, their tail-feathers spread wide.
The faces of the quarters are deafened by the terrifying cries of frogs.
It is rich with the fragrance of <s>kadamba</s>, plantain, <s>jātī</s>, and <s>kuṭaja</s>.
Lotuses are destroyed by the impact of streams of rain-bearing cloud-water.
The long tanks have their steps completely filled with abundant water.
The great waters take on a vast form, as if meeting their lord.
Rivers are full to the edges of both banks, their waters turbid.
The sky is lit by lightning flashing forth from thundering clouds.
It is frightening with the roar born from clouds striking one another.
The disks of sun and moon are covered by clouds bright with rainbows.
The forest is crowded with delighted goats, buffaloes, boars, and <s>cātaka</s> birds.
Then <s>śleṣman</s> is further diminished, <s>vāyu</s> is aggravated, and <s>pitta</s> accumulates.
In autumn the sharp rays of the sun shine out clearly.
The paths are freed by clouds that have exhausted their water and become clear.
All creatures rejoice, sprinkled with the nectar-like essence of moonlight.
The nights are lovely, scattered with glittering clusters of stars.
They are beautiful with a clear sky and give a festival for the play of desire.
The earth has dried mud and rice-fields full of grain.
The waters are adorned with blooming lotuses, white water-lilies, and blue lotuses.
Their waves are stirred by the joyful play of fish, swans, and rows of bees.
They are filled with pure water in the reservoirs and are beneficial for bathing and drinking.
The directions are beautiful, adorned with the chowries of blossoming <s>kāśa</s> grass.
They are clear and surrounded by delighted <s>krauñca</s> birds and the fragrance of jasmine.
The forest has herds of elephants made proud by contact with the pollen of <s>saptacchada</s> trees.

children.text: prakṣīyate tadā vāyuḥ pittaṃ kupyati pārvati ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>vāyu</s> subsides and <s>pitta</s> is aggravated, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
At the beginning, middle, and end of day and night, <s>śleṣman</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>samīraṇa</s> respectively
become aggravated; all the seasons proceed in order, O <s>Śivā</s>.
Day is of a fiery nature, while night is made of soma.

children.text: dvau ca pakṣau tadā devi ṛtū hemantaśaiśirau ||
children.translated_text: And the two fortnights are so, O <s>Devī</s>; the seasons are <s>hemanta</s> and <s>śiśira</s>.
Those two seasons are the cold time; <s>madhu</s> and <s>nidāgha</s> are hot.
<s>Prāvṛṣ</s> and <s>śarad</s> should be known as the rainy time; that is what it is called.
With the three seasons beginning with <s>śiśira</s>, there is the northern course of the sun.
Thus it should be known; that is <s>ādāna</s>, the taking-away period, O beloved.
The sun and wind by nature remove the earthy and soma-like sap.
But because of their course they are extremely hot, harsh, and dry.
Day by day they take away the strength and brilliance of living beings.
The bitter, astringent, and pungent tastes become progressively stronger.
With the three seasons beginning with <s>prāvṛṣ</s>, there is the southern course of the sun.
Know this as soma-natured; it is remembered as called <s>visarga</s>, the releasing period.
By nature, through cool rain, wind, soma, water, and clouds
become very strong; therefore the sun becomes weakened in radiance.
When this heat of the earth has gone away, day by day for living beings
time releases strength, and they become progressively stronger.

children.text: atrāmlalavaṇau svādū rasāḥ snigdhā bhavanti hi
children.translated_text: Here sour, salty, and sweet tastes are indeed unctuous.

children.text: hemante śiśire pūrṇaṃ madhau śaradi madhyamam ||
children.translated_text: In <s>hemanta</s> and <s>śiśira</s> strength is full; in spring and autumn it is middling.

children.text: grīṣme prāvṛṣi śītaṃ syātsarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ balam
children.translated_text: In summer and the rainy season the strength of all living beings is low.
Because the powerful rasa is enclosed by cold at the coming of winter,
and because the abdominal fire is not dispersed, since it is gathered in the stomach,

children.text: tato balīyān koṣṭhāgnis tasmin svalpāśano yadi ||
children.translated_text: therefore the digestive fire is stronger. If one eats little at that time,
the fire, kindled by <s>vāyu</s>, would digest the bodily tissues beginning with rasa.
Therefore in the cold season the sweet, salty, and sour should be used.

children.text: atha dairghyānniśānāṃ tu kṣudhā prātastarāṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Then, because the nights are long, hunger is very strong in the morning.
According to the rule of the daily regimen, after passing feces and urine,
one should perform all such acts as cleaning the teeth, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
Then one should perform oil-massage with oil suited to the head and pacifying <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: gātrābhyaṅgaṃ mardanaṃ ca yāvacchakyaṃ ca yathāsukham
children.translated_text: One should anoint the limbs and rub them as much as possible and as comfortably as possible.
Then one should practice wrestling with skilled men as much as possible.
With wheat, chickpeas, and mung beans, the oil should be removed in the prescribed manner.
Having bathed, one should put on two silk garments, red, light, warm, and very dense.
Having put on the garments, with musk and saffron,
and with black agaru and drava, one should make an anointing on the body.
One should fumigate the body and hair with incense made from black agaru.

children.text: campakaṃ bakulaṃ puṣpaṃ śatapatraṃ ca kaitakam ||
children.translated_text: There are <s>campaka</s>, <s>bakula</s>, <s>śatapatra</s>, and <s>kaitaka</s> flowers.
Having made them smeared with hibiscus and the other substances, he should wear them on his head.

children.text: guḍāsavaṃ madyamaṇḍaṃ madyaṃ māṃsaṃ ca meduram ||
children.translated_text: He should use molasses wine, the scum of liquor, liquor itself, and rich meat.
He should use unctuous meat broth, warm, and preparations made from black gram and wheat flour,
as well as products of sugarcane and milk, warm food, and food produced from sesame.

children.text: śauce sukhoṣṇaṃ salilaṃ soṣmalaṃ cāru mandiram
children.translated_text: For cleansing, he should use pleasantly warm water, and also a beautiful warm chamber.
He should use a bed gradually spread with soft, smooth deerskins and blankets,
with coverlets and fine silks, bright and splendid.
He should enjoy the rays of the sun before they have grown strong, with his back turned to them, O <s>Śāmbhavī</s>.
He should also use sweating and footwear regularly, when there is no severe burning heat.
He should live in an inner chamber, and embrace women with rounded, full, high breasts,
with hips round like wheels and adorned with thighs like plantain trunks,
intoxicated with the exhilaration of drinking wine, adorned with garments, garlands, and fragrances.
When beloved women, pleased, are embraced, no affliction born from the fault of cold occurs.
Musk, saffron, camphor, clove, and nutmeg,
each one niṣka in measure, and catechu essence,
sixteen niṣkas, should be combined; all this is to be ground with cold water.
He should make pills the size of peppercorns, removing bad odor.
This pill is declared to remove wind and phlegm and to be appetizing.
He should always chew betel together with the pill, as he wishes.
Thus is the regimen for <s>hemanta</s> (winter); in <s>śiśira</s> (late winter) too he should follow this same one.
When <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm) has accumulated greatly, he should follow the winter procedure.
At that time, because of the sun's withdrawing force, dryness occurs and the cold becomes greater.
But in late winter the accumulated <s>śleṣman</s>, melted in spring by the sun's rays,
destroys the gastric fire by its own watery nature.
It produces every disease; therefore one should quickly overcome <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: atha vāsantikāṃ caryāṃ kathayāmi mama priye ||
children.translated_text: Now, my beloved, I shall explain the spring regimen.
He should remove it with sharp collyrium, emesis, nasal therapies, exercise, and rubbing of the body,
and by massage with the feet and bathing in warm water.
He should put on garments of silk colored astringent-red and safflower-red,
and perfume his limbs with camphor and agaru smoke.
He should anoint his body with musk, saffron, cooling camphor, and sandalwood.
He should take mango blossom, campaka, punnāga, betel-nut blossom, kesara, pāṭala,
mādhavī, ketakī, jasmine, aśoka, and fresh jasmine garlands,
smeared with hibiscus and the like, and he should carry water-lilies and lotuses.
Wine is said to be of five kinds, an excellent remover of all diseases:
mādhava, ariṣṭa, mārdvīka, āsava, and śīthu, so they are named.
That which is made with honey and intoxicating substances is remembered as mādhava.
An intoxicating substance dug down and kept in the ground for a long time
is to be known as ariṣṭa; mārdvīka is born from grapes.
Āsava arises from the pressing or infusion of intoxicating substances.

children.text: śīthur ikṣurasājjātaḥ sevyāḥ pañca mayā matāḥ
children.translated_text: Śīthu is produced from sugarcane juice; these five, in my opinion, are to be used.
They are perfumed by the lotus-like faces of women and steal the mind.
They are scented with flowers and the like, pleasing to the heart, and brightened by the glances of beloved women.
When old, pungent, bitter, and astringent, they remove <s>śleṣman</s>.
He should use citron, mango, and rose-apple, together with their leaves, flowers, and fruits,
and, with friends, citron juice, moist ginger, and onion.

children.text: jāṅgalaṃ palalaṃ śūlyaṃ tadrasaṃ ca kṛtaṃ navam
children.translated_text: He should use meat from animals of dry lands, roasted on a spit, and its fresh broth.
He should use old honey, wheat, barley, sixty-day rice, and śāli rice,

children.text: bhajetkaphaghnaṃ śākaṃ ca vyañjanaṃ pānakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: as well as vegetables that destroy <s>kapha</s>, condiments, and drinks.
But one who does not drink wine should drink water with dry ginger, water with mustā, or honey-water,
or water boiled with the heartwood of khadira and asana.
In a garden, in a beautiful pavilion fit for lovemaking, adorned with pavements
whose plaster, glass, and other surfaces shine like jewels,
charming with the calls of cuckoos and bright with fragrant flowers,
where the hot rays of the sun are blocked by the deep shade of many trees,
cooled on every side by channels filled with water,
where the water of weariness is calmed by the movement of the Malaya breeze,
delighted by rows of trees beautiful with many flowers,
sprinkled with the nectar of hanging fragrant garlands,
adorned with rows of uśīra and pāṭalī and spread with lotus fibers,
strewn with flowers and bright with the breeze from slow-moving palm-leaf fans,
seated there, with beloved women skilled in affectionate conversation and eager for love,
who are the whole wealth of <s>Kandarpa</s>'s pride and wear fine, transparent garments,
he should delight young women and hold charming conversations with them.
Together with trusted friends, happy, he should pass the midday.
In spring he should avoid things that are excessively cold, heavy, unctuous, sweet, sour, or salty,
as well as products of sesame, sugarcane, and milk, sleeping by day, and excessively slimy substances.
In spring he should avoid fish, alkaline water, cakes, and whatever increases <s>śleṣman</s>.
In summer the hot sun becomes extremely sharp and dries up the juices of the earth;
it diminishes unctuous qualities as well, and therefore <s>kapha</s> goes to depletion.
Because of that, wind too becomes accumulated; one should use cool waters filled
with sandalwood, agaru, musk, saffron, and fragrant substances,
and perfumed with various blooming flowers such as jasmine.
In water reaching up to the full breasts of women, well purified,

children.text: hrade vā dīrghikāyāṃ vā saṃskṛtāyāṃ yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: whether in a lake or in a long pond, prepared according to rule,
with moon-like faces shining with eyes filled up to the ears,
with soft arms like sirīṣa flowers, bright with lotus-fiber ornaments,
radiant with camphor, pearls, flower garlands, and sandalwood,
with waists and hips bound in fine safflower-colored garments,
made charming by the cries of sārasas attracted by the sound of their anklets;
together with women very skillful in water-play,
he should sport, their faces sprinkled by water released from his hands.
With his body sprinkled by water discharged from the mouths of squirting horns,
embracing them to his chest, he should make play again and again.
Then, having come out, he should comfortably rub dry his body and hair with cloths,

children.text: svacche sūkṣme kaṣāye ca vasane dhārayettataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and afterward put on clean, fine, astringent-colored garments.
He should perfume his hair and body with the smoke of sandalwood, agaru, and camphor.
His body should be smeared with a paste of śrīkhaṇḍa sandalwood, camphor, and musk.
He should wear nepāla, mālatī, mallī, pāṭalī, and hundred-petalled lotuses,
saugandhika, maruvaka, hrīvera, and flowers scented with musk,
and flowers anointed with fragrant oils.

children.text: atra madyaṃ na peyaṃ syādathavā madyasātmyakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here wine should not be drunk; or, by those accustomed to wine,

children.text: svalpaṃ peyaṃ tu teneṣanna tṛptiścet tadā jalaiḥ
children.translated_text: a little should be drunk. If there is still no satisfaction from that, then with waters
he may drink wine mixed with many sweet things as he pleases.
Otherwise there would be wasting of the bodily elements, and he would suffer internal burning and bewilderment,
with loosened limbs and depleted breath, intelligence, and strength, dear one.

children.text: madhuraṃ śītalaṃ snigdhaṃ dravaṃ laghu hitaṃ bhajet
children.translated_text: He should resort to what is sweet, cooling, unctuous, liquid, light, and wholesome.
He should immediately lick śāleya mixed with sugar, and eat the meat of animals from dry lands.
He should drink lean meat-broth, <s>rasālā</s> (a sweet curd drink), and <s>pānaka</s> (a sweet beverage).

children.text: pañcasāraṃ ca rāgaṃ ca ṣāḍavaṃ cāthavā hitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pañcasāra</s>, <s>rāga</s>, and <s>ṣāḍava</s> are also wholesome.
Curds churned by hand together with sugar and black pepper
are known as this <s>rasālā</s>. Made with fruits born from plantain, jackfruit, and mango,
with sugar and water, and placed in a new earthen pot,
that is known as slightly sour <s>pānaka</s>, and it is beneficial.
Grapes, royal dates, dates, and madhūka flowers,
and ripe fruits of śrīparṇī, sugarcane, and small dates,
should be placed in sugared water and firmly crushed by hand.
After being set aside in a new earthen vessel, it is strained through cloth on the next day.
It is known as <s>pañcasāra</s>, pleasing to the heart and removing <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
Whatever clear fruit preparation is mixed with sugar, honey, and other sweet substances
is to be known as <s>rāga</s>, the remover of all heat.

children.text: ayameva tu sāndraś cel lehyaṃ ṣāḍava īritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If this same thing is thick, it is called a lickable <s>ṣāḍava</s>.

children.text: sa ca vastreṇa saṃśuddhaḥ peyaṣāḍava ucyate
children.translated_text: When it has been purified through cloth, it is called a drinkable <s>ṣāḍava</s>.
These five kinds of drink, scented with pāṭalī, campaka, and the like,

children.text: elayā vāsitaṃ śuddhaṃ mṛdbhāṇḍe sthāpite nave
children.translated_text: and with cardamom, should be purified and kept in a new earthen vessel,
cooled by the breeze of uśīra and palm-leaf fans,
and furnished with leaves of mocā and coca. This is the general preparation.
Then he should drink sweet, clear water filled inside a new vessel,
made fragrant with pāṭalī, ketakī flowers, and camphor,
covered with a dense cloth and well cooled by palm-leaf fans.
He should drink water among tāla, sāla, areca-nut, and date trees,
among coconut, mango, jackfruit, rose-apple, punnāga, and campaka trees,
with clusters of fruits and flowers hanging down within reach of the hand,
splendid with branches hidden by bunches of grapes,
praised by the songs of bees settled in clusters of mādhavī flowers,
where the sun's rays are warded off by various fragrant trees,
beside a lake beautiful with haṃsas, sārasas, and kāraṇḍavas,
cooled all around by the breeze from the waves of flowing channels,
filled with the dances and calls of peacocks and lovely with the notes of cuckoos,
where passionate women are enchanted by the conversation of śārikās and parrots,
in a garden enclosed by young uśīra grass and sprinkled with water,
fashioned with lotus fibers, lotuses, kalhāras, blue lotuses, and young shoots,
very cool, with fragrant flower garlands hanging down,
and with a new shaded canopy made of wet cloths.
In a charming mādhavī pavilion that removes every heat,
on a bed arranged with plantain, lotus fibers, flowers, and shoots,
with a beautiful, excellent coverlet and sprinkled with cold water,
extremely soft and removing heat and fatigue,
filled with leather bags and cloths made still colder than frost,
sprinkled with fine drops of water and accompanied by companions,
he should pass the midday in this way, or else in a shower-house.
Playing there, on a clear crystal slab, with cool young-uśīra water
falling from the breasts, hands, and mouths of beloved women made of cloth,
and rolling on a surface anointed with camphor and sandalwood, he should quiet the heat.
Women whose bodies are cooled by a fresh bath and who are adorned with pearl ornaments,
smeared with lotus fiber and sandalwood and furnished with lotus-fiber bracelets,
very lovely in transparent garments and removing heat,
he should delight with kisses, embraces, and touches, joking with them.
On a palace terrace adorned by a canopy made of flower garlands,
bright with moonstones melting at the touch of moonbeams,
shining with the radiance of moonlight and graced by a gentle breeze,
sitting there, he should eat foods called forth by the rays of the moon,
cooled by the rays of the stars and moon.
He should drink buffalo milk with sugar; it is strength-giving and wholesome.
For one whose body is afflicted by summer heat, who wears garlands and sandalwood,
whose limbs are covered with transparent cloth, and who has completed the act of love,
by the breeze from cloths wet with water and by the wind of palm-leaf fans,
with expanded lotus leaves, fans sprinkling water,
peacock-feather and palm-leaf fans, and likewise yellow sandalwood,
with camphor, jasmine, pearl garlands, and sweet things, dear one...
by the prattling of young mynahs and parrots, and by ornaments of lotus fiber,
by places shining with blooming red water lilies, lotuses, and blue lotuses,
by applications of camphor and sandalwood, and by lovely women,
the heat of this man, afflicted by the heat of the drawing season, is removed.
He should avoid roasted barley meal, pungent, sour, salty, and dry things, exertion, and sunlight.

children.text: athāto vārṣikīṃ caryāṃ śṛṇu vakṣyāmi bhairavi ||
children.translated_text: Now then, O <s>Bhairavi</s>, listen to the rainy-season regimen; I shall explain it.
For men whose <s>dhātu</s> (bodily constituents) have been depleted by the drawing season, the digestive fire,
though already weak, quickly sinks in the rainy season because of the <s>doṣa</s>s.
When the sun is hidden by masses of water-bearing clouds,
and the sky has cold, dewy gusts of wind,
<s>vāta</s> becomes greatly aggravated, because the earth has been scorched by summer heat
and then wetted by clouds and the like, with vapors arising according to the nature of the season.
Because of sour digestion and because the waters are polluted by spiders and other impurities,
<s>pitta</s> too becomes extremely aggravated; and because of the bad cloudy days,

children.text: vahniḥ sīdati tenaiva śleṣmā kupyati dustaraḥ
children.translated_text: the digestive fire sinks for that very reason, and <s>śleṣman</s> becomes hard to overcome.
Thus the <s>doṣa</s>s become mutually vitiated, and from that there is a common mixed disorder.
He should practice massage and oiling of the head with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> oils,
and after bathing with abundant warm water he should wipe his body dry.

children.text: raktaṃ cāpyathavā śuklaṃ māñjiṣṭhaṃ vātha dhārayet
children.translated_text: He should wear red or white, or else madder-colored, garments,
and he should fumigate the body with dense agaru incense, O <s>Śive</s>.
He should use musk, saffron, and fine liquid black agaru,
as well as kuṭaja, ketakī, jasmine, maruvā, and oleander.
He should use unctuous meat of dry-land animals, and their prepared broths too,
and he should drink a well-prepared soup of mudga, āḍhaka, and kulattha beans.
He should drink what is called <s>ariṣṭa</s>, or maireya, or else an old liquor,
and <s>mastu</s> (whey) mixed with sauvarcala salt and powdered <s>pañcakola</s>.
He should use everything that produces warmth, and the man should have his bowels purified.
He should also take a decoction enema, and he should eat old grain.

children.text: divyaṃ vā kaupamudakaṃ śṛtaṃ peyaṃ sukhāvaham
children.translated_text: Rainwater, or well water, boiled, should be drunk; it brings ease.
On a day of excessive wind and rain, he should generally use salty and sour things,
as well as sweet and light foods with honey, and dried, well-fried dishes,
and condiments, oil, cakes, and parpaṭas.
He should use betel as he pleases, mixed with musk and nut,
and he should put on garments fumigated with agaru incense.
With fragrant limbs he should stay in a palace free from the vapors of the ground,
delightful, free from dewy cold, and fumigated with agaru.
He should avoid sleeping by day, river water, and roasted barley meal soaked in water and ghee,
as well as exercise, the rays of the sun, and excessive sexual intercourse.

children.text: athātaḥ śāradīṃ caryāṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu vāṅmayi
children.translated_text: Now then, O mistress of speech, I shall explain the autumnal regimen; listen.
After the rainy season, because of cold and rain, and then suddenly because of the sun's rays,

children.text: taptāṅgānāṃ nṛṇāṃ pittaṃ citaṃ vṛṣṭau tu śārade
children.translated_text: the <s>pitta</s> accumulated in the rains in men whose bodies have been heated
becomes still more aggravated then; therefore, for removing <s>pitta</s>,
he should arrange an oil massage with <s>pitta</s>-destroying oil and gentle rubbing.
He should bathe with pleasantly warm water and wear white or ocher garments.
After putting them on, he should perfume his limbs with agaru and camphor smoke.
With his limbs anointed with bhadraśrī and camphor, he should carry ketakī and bhallaka flowers,
campaka and lotus petals, together with musk.
He should use purgation, bloodletting, and the tasting of bitter ghee.
He should use śāli rice, wheat, mudga beans, paṭola, honey, and sugar,

children.text: jāṅgalaṃ piśitaṃ tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhurān bhajet ||
children.translated_text: and meat of dry-land animals, and foods that are bitter, astringent, and sweet.

children.text: bubhukṣitastu laghvannaṃ dhātrīṃ śīthuṃ ghṛtaṃ payaḥ
children.translated_text: When hungry he should use light food, dhātrī, śīthu liquor, ghee, and milk,
pānaka drink, barley-water, sugarcane juice, and fresh coconut water.
He should drink <s>haṃsodaka</s>, purified by the rising of <s>Agastya</s>, free from poison, light, and cool,
cooled after being heated by the rays of the sun and moon.
At evening he should take mung soup; smeared with cool sandalwood,
happy, adorned with fragrant garlands and clean washed garments,
decorated with pearl necklaces and anointed with fragrant uśīra,
in a palace surrounded by charming gardens and made very beautiful by moonlight,
he should sit and enjoy the moonbeams, accompanied by a young woman,
chewing sweet sugarcane stalks and drinking wine that subdues <s>pitta</s>.
Drinking again and again, he should remain happily, amusing the women.
He should avoid alkalis such as yavakṣāra, cold things, and eating to complete satiety,
as well as sesame oil, the rays of the sun, sleeping by day, fat, and curds.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ madyaṃ tyajedvastu prācīvāyuṃ ca pittakṛt ||
children.translated_text: He should avoid strong liquor and anything that produces <s>pitta</s>, including the eastern wind.
Now, O <s>Śive</s>, the general regimen will be stated briefly.
At the coming of cold and rain, he should generally use sweet, sour, and salty tastes.
In spring he should especially use bitter, pungent, and astringent tastes.
In summer he should use what is predominantly sweet, and again at the end of the rains
he should use bitter, sweet, and astringent tastes; in the rainy season too he should follow the proper order.

children.text: madhau rūkṣoṣṇamaśnīyād grīṣme snigdhaṃ ca śītalam ||
children.translated_text: In spring he should eat dry and warm food; in summer, unctuous and cool food.
In the rains, late winter, and winter he should use unctuous and rather warm food.
At the end of the clouds he should, according to this rule, use dry and cool things.
Day by day he should use in abundance the tastes prescribed for each particular season,
and all the other tastes too, in small measure, according to his liking.
The last seven days of one season and the first seven days of another,
these fourteen days are remembered as the junction of the seasons.
At the season-junction he should very gradually give up the regimen of the present season
and should adopt in sequence the regimen of the coming season.
Because wholesome substances are given up, and because unwholesome substances are used,
diseases arise; therefore one should gradually proceed to abandon those habits.
Practicing the regimen of the seasons in this way, one obtains long life and health.
I shall briefly explain the process by which food is digested, O worshipped by the gods.
All food that has been eaten is carried into the bowel by the <s>prāṇa-vāyu</s> (vital wind),
and there, broken apart by the fluids, its compact mass again becomes soft.
Brought along by unctuousness, the abdominal fire in the stomach digests it,
kindled by the <s>samāna-vāyu</s> (equalizing wind), as external fire does.

children.text: sthālīsthaṃ taṇḍulaṃ toyaṃ pacedannaṃ ca pāvakaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as fire cooks rice and water placed in a pot into food,
so immediately after eating all that food, though of six tastes, becomes sweet.
As it is being digested by sweet and similar factors that produce <s>kapha</s>, foam arises.
That foam attains the nature of <s>kapha</s>, and through burning heat it also becomes sour.
When that has fallen from the stomach, it becomes clear <s>pitta</s>.
Having reached the lower intestine and been dried by the fire,
it becomes compact and fully cooked; through the great digestion it becomes pungent.
There are five heat-principles: earthy, watery, fiery, airy, and etheric.
These five fires digest foods according to the earthy and other elements,
and also the five cooked qualities of food and the qualities of the elements.

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak yathāsvaṃ ca puṣṇantyete yathāsukham
children.translated_text: Separately, each in its own way, they nourish them properly, according to their nature.
The earthy fire nourishes the earthy elements, and the others, in order, nourish the others situated in the body.
That cooked food is of two kinds, divided into waste and essence.

children.text: kiṭṭaṃ tu dvividhaṃ cācchaṃ mūtraṃ sāndraṃ śakṛdbhavet ||
children.translated_text: The waste too is twofold: the clear part becomes urine, and the dense part becomes feces.

children.text: punaḥ sāraṃ pacantyeva yathāsvaṃ sapta vahnayaḥ
children.translated_text: Again, according to their own domains, the seven fires digest the essence.
They are the fires belonging to the bodily tissues, O goddess; from <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid) comes <s>rakta</s> (blood).
From blood comes flesh; from flesh comes fat; from that bone is produced.

children.text: asthno majjā tataḥ śukraṃ śukrādgarbho bhavetpriye ||
children.translated_text: From bone comes marrow; from that semen; and from semen an embryo arises, O beloved.
I shall describe the products born from the remaining clear essence: from <s>rasa</s> comes breast milk, and from blood

children.text: sirāśca kaṇḍarā māṃsātṣaṭ tvacaśca vasā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: come veins and tendons; from flesh come the six skins and fat.

children.text: medasaḥ snāyusandhī ca śeṣaṃ naśyatyataḥ param
children.translated_text: From fat come sinews and joints; what remains after that perishes.

children.text: rasasya kiṭṭaṃ śleṣmā syādasṛjaḥ pittameva ca ||
children.translated_text: The waste of <s>rasa</s> is <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), and that of blood is precisely <s>pitta</s> (bile).

children.text: māṃsasya kiṭṭaṃ khamalā medaso gharmavāri ca
children.translated_text: The waste of flesh is the impurity of the bodily openings, and that of fat is sweat-water.
From bone come body hair and head-hair; from marrow comes the unctuousness of the skin, eyes, and feces.
And from semen comes <s>ojas</s> (vital vigor); in order, these are remembered as the wastes of the tissues.
Through the complete digestion of the tissues, waste and clear essence come into being.
The succession of the tissues and their unctuousness is sustained by their mutual support.

children.text: āhārātsādhu jīrṇādyo jātaḥ sāro raso hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: The essence produced first from properly digested food is indeed <s>rasa</s>.
Therefore <s>rasa</s> is the increaser of the tissues, blood and the rest.

children.text: narāṇāṃ dhātavaḥ sapta santi strīṇāṃ yathā tathā ||
children.translated_text: Men have seven tissues, and women likewise have the same.

children.text: puṃsāṃ śuklaṃ ca śirasi nārīṇāṃ hṛṣṭamānase
children.translated_text: In men the semen is in the head; in women it is present when the mind is delighted.
At union with the husband, that semen flows in the temple of love.

children.text: taccāmbusadṛśaṃ svacchaṃ saumyaṃ garbhāya no bhavet
children.translated_text: That, resembling water, clear and cool in nature, is not fit for conception.
Food that has been eaten, by day and night, causes the increase of semen.
After seven days the semen becomes clear, and after a month it is capable of producing an embryo.
In this very sequence of digestion the six maternal constituents arise, O <s>Ambikā</s>.
Through the power of aphrodisiac medicines, semen and the rest are produced at once.
There is always transformation among the moving substances of food and bodily tissues.
The fires are remembered as three: gastric, elemental, and tissue-related.
Among these the gastric fire is best, by which food is completely digested.

children.text: sa eva mūlaṃ sarveṣāmagnīnāṃ tatkṣaye kṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: It alone is the root of all the fires; when it declines, they decline.
When it increases, there is increase; life and strength have that as their root.
Therefore, O goddess, with beneficial and wholesome fuels called food and drink,
one should carefully protect that fire, for freedom from disease depends on it.
That same fire is fourfold: sharp, weak, balanced, and irregular.
When the equalizing wind is overcome by <s>pitta</s>, the fire is sharp.

children.text: asamyagbahu vā bhuktaṃ pacecchīghraṃ tu pittajān
children.translated_text: It quickly digests food that has been improperly eaten or eaten in excess,
but it causes disorders born of <s>pitta</s>. When the equalizing wind is afflicted by <s>kapha</s>, the fire is weak.

children.text: samyagbhuktaṃ mitaṃ vāpi hitaṃ cānnaṃ cirātpacet
children.translated_text: Even food that has been properly eaten, measured, and wholesome it digests only after a long time.
It repeatedly produces dryness of the mouth, distension, heaviness, and rumbling in the intestines,
as well as gurgling and diseases born of <s>śleṣman</s>.
When the equalizing wind remains in its own place, the fire is called balanced.
It digests properly eaten food at the right time and gives the fruit of health.
When the equalizing wind is outside its proper path, the fire is irregular; even good food
it may digest slowly, while badly eaten food it may digest quickly, producing disorders born of <s>vāta</s>.
Therefore, being vigilant, one should preserve balanced fire, O beloved.
The sharp fire digests in two watches, while the weak fire takes six watches.
Balanced fire digests food easily in four watches, without difficulty.

children.text: asamāgniḥ kadācit tu śīghraṃ vā mandameva vā
children.translated_text: Irregular fire sometimes digests quickly and sometimes slowly.
The fire of all living beings is situated in the region of the navel.
In elephants, camels, horses, and the like, the fire is the size of a thumb.
In domestic animals, humans, and wild animals, the fire is the size of a barley grain.
In vultures, owls, cranes, and the like, the gastric fire is measured as a sesame seed.
In worms, insects, and similar creatures, the fire is the size of a hair.
When the gastric fire is blazing, it first digests food; then,
in the absence of food, it digests the <s>doṣas</s>; when the <s>doṣas</s> are depleted, then it digests
the bodily tissues; and when the tissues are depleted, it finally destroys the lives of living beings.
Śrī <s>Bhairavī</s>.
O god of gods, ocean of compassion, destroyer of <s>Kāla</s> and <s>Kandarpa</s>,
O one of eight forms, O great-formed one, devoted to the five cosmic acts,
O three-eyed one, O destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>, by whom the whole universe has been manifested,
whose moon is wearied by the hissing of the lord of serpents entwined in your matted hair,
O lord, smiling five-faced one, whose eyes are the sun, moon, and fire,
whose cheeks shine with the jewels on the hoods of serpent-earrings,
beautiful with jasmine-bud teeth and tender leaf-like lips,
whose throat is darkened by the <s>hālāhala</s> poison, adorned with seven great serpents,
shining with eighteen arms raised up by great serpent bracelets,
furnished with every divine weapon, clad in an excellent tiger skin,
whose pair of feet is waved with light by the lotus-like jewels
on the crowns of the bowing lords of gods and demons, remover of birth and old age for yogins,
whose splendor is being, consciousness, and bliss, gracious ocean of compassion,
reached through <s>oṃkāra</s>, pure, beyond reasoning, inconceivable and immeasurable, O lord:

children.text: stotā stutyaḥ stutistvaṃ hi kartā kāryaṃ ca kārakaḥ
children.translated_text: you yourself are the praiser, the praised, and the praise; you are the agent, the act, and the instrument.
Indeed you yourself are everything. Be gracious, O supreme lord.

children.text: tvanmāyayā jagatsarvaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ trātaṃ hataṃ tathā
children.translated_text: By your <s>māyā</s> the whole universe is created, protected, and also destroyed.

children.text: tvaṃ bhūstvamāpastvaṃ vahnistvaṃ vāyustvaṃ nabhaḥ śaśī ||
children.translated_text: You are earth, you are the waters, you are fire, you are wind, you are the sky and the moon.
You are the sun, you are the supreme self, you are the qualities, and likewise <s>prakṛti</s>.
You are <s>puruṣa</s>, you are mind, and also intellect, consciousness, and egoity.
Command me to tell all <s>rasāyana</s> in detail,

children.text: ājñāpayāhaṃ yadi te hṛdyā prāṇapriyā vibho ||
children.translated_text: if I am pleasing to your heart, O lord, dearer than life to me.

children.text: jīvanmuktiḥ kathaṃ nātha yogarūpaṃ ca kīdṛśam
children.translated_text: How, O lord, is <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living), and what is the form of yoga?
Show favor, O lord of gods, and teach the easy means that removes worldly existence.

children.text: śrutvā stutiṃ smitamukho bhairavaḥ parayā mudā
children.translated_text: Having heard the hymn, <s>Bhairava</s>, with a smiling face and supreme joy,
spoke to the auspicious goddess, the daughter of the lord of mountains.
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s>:

children.text: sādhu sādhu mahāmāye sarvaṃ vetsi sanātane
children.translated_text: Good, good, O great <s>Māyā</s>; O eternal one, you know everything.
Yet, O <s>Īśānī</s>, you ask out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds.
I shall explain it briefly; listen attentively, my dear.
What beloved woman other than you do I have for explaining the meaning of this secret?
Listen, O goddess of gods; I shall tell the marks of one liberated while living.

children.text: kāmaṃ krodhaṃ bhayaṃ lobhaṃ madaṃ mohaṃ ca matsaram ||
children.translated_text: Desire, anger, fear, greed, intoxication, delusion, and envy,

children.text: mānaṃ lajjāṃ kulaṃ śīlaṃ kutsāṃ dambhaṃ ca vañcanām
children.translated_text: pride, shame, family, conduct, blame, hypocrisy, and deceit,
ignorance, dullness, arrogance, cold, heat, and the heat of the sun,

children.text: vātaṃ sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca pāpaṃ puṇyaṃ hitāhitam
children.translated_text: wind, pleasure and pain, evil and merit, the beneficial and the harmful,
the three afflictions, sons, friends, wife, and the rest: whoever abandons these,
is not attached to any sense-object and is devoted to contemplation of reality,
and becomes, like a lotus leaf by waters, with a heart unstained.
His mind is adorned with friendliness, compassion, indifference, and non-duality,
his understanding detached from the work of obtaining happiness in this world or the next.
He knows discrimination between the eternal and the non-eternal and restrains the inner faculty;
free from old age and death, he possesses the essence of sameness with <s>Śiva</s>.
He should be known as a <s>jīvanmukta</s>, one who has crossed the ocean of transmigration.

children.text: devadaityādibhirvandyaḥ sa sevyaḥ sa guruḥ śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Honored by gods, demons, and others, he is to be served; he is the guru; he is <s>Śiva</s>.
Just as I am worthy of worship in all the worlds, O great lady,
so he too is always worshiped in all the worlds by everyone.
The liberation that beings have at the end of the body is connected with a purpose.

children.text: dehānte dehinaḥ sarve muktiṃ yānti na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the end of the body all embodied beings go to liberation; there is no doubt.
If liberation could arise from the flowing of sexual fluid, then donkeys and the like,
birds, bulls, and rams: are they liberated, O <s>Tripurāmbikā</s>?
If liberation were to occur through service to semen, feces, and urine, my dear,

children.text: kapiśca sūkarādyāśca kathaṃ muktā bhavanti te ||
children.translated_text: then how would monkeys, pigs, and the like not become liberated?
It does not arise merely from immortality, nor likewise from becoming <s>Śiva</s>.
From the union of those two comes what is remembered as this <s>jīvanmukti</s>.
In every tradition and scripture there is liberation born at the final time,
but that <s>Śāmbhavī</s> liberation is not seen like a jewel resting in the hand.
That which is very secret, unspeakable, and difficult even for the gods to obtain,
I shall teach, O goddess of gods: the perpetual stability of the body.
It is <s>śivatva</s> (becoming Śiva), <s>khecaratva</s> (sky-going power), auspicious and bestowing all attainments.

children.text: dehaṃ vinā na kiṃcit syāddeho'yaṃ sarvasādhanam ||
children.translated_text: Without the body nothing exists; this body is the means of every accomplishment.
Therefore one should always protect the body carefully in every way.
When the body falls, <s>dharma</s> is destroyed; when <s>dharma</s> is destroyed, ritual action is lost.

children.text: kriyācyutau kuto yogo yogabhraṃśe na cidbhavet
children.translated_text: When ritual action is lost, whence is yoga? When yoga is broken, there is no consciousness.

children.text: cidabhāve kuto mokṣo mokṣe bhraṣṭe na kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: When consciousness is absent, whence is liberation? When liberation is lost, nothing remains.
Even by a hundred other means the body is not sustained forever.
<s>Pārada</s> (mercury) and <s>pavana</s> (breath) are supreme, bestowers of all attainments.
When both <s>pavana</s> and <s>pārada</s> are made senseless, killed, and bound,
in due order they always remove disease, destroy death, and grant sky-going power.

children.text: rasaḥ pūrvaṃ mayā khyāto'dhunā vāyuḥ praśasyate
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> (mercury) was taught by me before; now <s>vāyu</s> (breath) is praised.
From the retention of breath comes knowledge; from knowledge liberation is born.
For everyone the body is the root; for its stability breath is the lord.
From that supreme imperishable arose space; from that,
wind; from that, fire; from that, water; and then earth.
Of these five elements the imperishable is the supreme cause.
Space has sound as its nature; wind has sound and touch as its nature.
Fire consists of sound, touch, and form; water is said
to have sound, form, touch, and taste as its nature, while earth has them especially.
It becomes of the nature of sound, form, taste, touch, and smell, dear one.
And the deities presiding over earth, water, fire, wind, and space
are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, and <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
Earth, when destroyed, is immersed in water, and those waters are swallowed by a great fire.

children.text: sa ca caṇḍasamīreṇa śamitaḥ so'pi pārvati ||
children.translated_text: That fire is extinguished by a fierce wind, and that too, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,

children.text: vyomni līnaḥ kramāt tasmād ākāśād udbhavanti te
children.translated_text: is dissolved in space; from that space they arise again in order.
Space, present within and without, all-pervading, without support and without resting-place,
should be meditated upon with the mind; by meditating on space one cuts the bond of becoming.
Wind is made of the life-breath of the world, and water bestows consciousness and bliss.
When one makes the wind motionless by method, one becomes, like wind, a sky-goer.
One should meditate in one's own heart on fire, blazing with the light of endless suns and fires

children.text: tejo dhyātvā svahṛdaye nāgninā sa tu bādhyate
children.translated_text: and burning the three worlds; then one is not afflicted by fire.
One should contemplate in one's own heart the water-principle, flooding the earth's surface

children.text: aptattvaṃ bhāvayan svānte vāri taṃ na hi bādhate
children.translated_text: with masses of waves of nectar; water does not afflict that person.
One should constantly imagine in the heart the earth's surface, crowded with beings moving on the ground

children.text: hṛdaye bhāvayannityaṃ tasya no pārthivaṃ bhayam
children.translated_text: and filled with the flood of living beings; for such a person there is no fear from the earthly element.
Whatever one contemplates in the mind, one attains the form of that very thing,

children.text: yathāgnitvaṃ vrajet kāṣṭhaḥ kīṭo bhramaratāṃ yathā
children.translated_text: just as wood comes to be fire, and just as a worm becomes a bee.
Posture, regulation of breath, withdrawal, and concentration,

children.text: dhyānaṃ samādhiḥ ṣoḍhā syuryogāṅgāni krameṇa ca
children.translated_text: meditation and samādhi: these are the six limbs of yoga in order.
There are indeed eighty-four hundred-thousand postures,

children.text: teṣu mukhyāsane dve ca siddhapadmāsane smṛte
children.translated_text: and among them two postures are remembered as principal: siddhāsana and padmāsana.
With the root of one foot one should press one's own generative place firmly,
and place the root of the other foot above the penis.
Seated upright, with the senses brought under control, dear one,
with unmoving eyes, looking between the eyebrows, and with a motionless mind,
this should be known as siddhāsana, the giver of the path to liberation.

children.text: dakṣiṇorau padaṃ vāmaṃ vāmorau dakṣiṇaṃ padam
children.translated_text: Placing the left foot on the right thigh and the right foot on the left thigh,
and with the pair of hands brought around to the back,
in the reverse position, grasping the left big toe with the left hand
and the right one firmly with the right hand, placing the chin on one's chest,
one should meditate on the tip of the nose, with the senses restrained.
This is known as padmāsana, the remover of all diseases.
The base, in the region of the anus, is a four-petaled lotus,
furnished with the letters from va to sa and shining like the young rising sun.
The svādhiṣṭhāna is a six-petaled lotus, furnished with the letters from ba to la.
It has the brilliance of lightning; after that, O <s>Devī</s>, is the jewel-like maṇipūraka,
joined with the letters from ḍa to pha, at the navel, consisting of a hundred petals.
The anāhata is golden in appearance, a lotus in the heart with twelve petals,
bearing the letters from ka to ṭha; viśuddhi is then praised.
It is a great sixteen-spoked lotus, adorned with the sixteen vowels.
The ājñā-cakra is two-petaled and radiant like lotus hands.
It is white; thus, in order, O <s>Devī</s>, the six cakras have been taught.
Below the navel and above the penis is what is called the kanda.
It resembles a bird's egg; there the nāḍīs arise.
They are seventy-two thousand, and among them ten are remembered as chief.

children.text: iḍā ca prathamā nāḍī piṅgalā ca dvitīyakā ||
children.translated_text: The first nāḍī is iḍā, and the second is piṅgalā.

children.text: suṣumnā ca tṛtīyā syādgāndhārī ca caturthikā
children.translated_text: The third is suṣumnā, and the fourth is gāndhārī.
The fifth is hastijihvā; the sixth is pūṣā, called tarasvinī.

children.text: saptamyalambuṣā nāḍī cāṣṭamī ca kuhūḥ smṛtā
children.translated_text: The seventh nāḍī is alambuṣā, and the eighth is remembered as kuhū.

children.text: navamī śaṅkhinī caiva daśamī ca krameṇa hi ||
children.translated_text: The ninth is śaṅkhinī, and the tenth follows in order.
These are bearers of prāṇa; the vital winds are remembered as their recitation.
They are prāṇa and apāna, likewise vyāna, udāna, and samāna,
and nāga, kūrma, kṛkala, devadatta, and dhanañjaya.
The ten vital winds move in all the circles of the nāḍīs,
restless along the left and right paths, downward and upward.
Under the control of prāṇa and apāna, the living being runs about and is not seen,

children.text: hastābhyāmāhato bhūmau kanduko na sthiro yathā
children.translated_text: just as a ball, struck by the hands on the ground, does not remain still.
So too the living being, tossed by prāṇa and apāna, is not steady.
When prāṇa and apāna are drawn together, and prāṇa likewise from apāna,
it goes outward with the syllable ha and enters inward with the syllable sa.

children.text: haṃsaḥ so'haṃ manumamuṃ sadā jīvo japet priye
children.translated_text: The living being always recites this mantra, haṃsa, so'ham, dear one.
Its number is twenty-one thousand
and six hundred, O <s>Īśvarī</s>, for the haṃsa mantra throughout a day and night.
This great mantra, called haṃsa, is proclaimed as ajapā, the unrecited recitation.
This so-called japa is the Gāyatrī that grants liberation to disciplined yogins.

children.text: etatsamaṃ tapo jñānaṃ japaḥ puṇyaṃ na kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: There is no austerity, knowledge, recitation, or merit equal to this.
It is unuttered and without phonemes, arising from Kuṇḍalinī.
It moves with prāṇa; yogins should always know it.
Mother Kuṇḍalinī Śakti is established upward from the kanda.
She is coiled eightfold, in the form of a sleeping serpent.

children.text: brahmadvāramukhaṃ sā tu svamukhena pidhāya ca
children.translated_text: She covers the mouth of the brahma-door with her own mouth.
One should first awaken her by the fire-yoga, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Together with the wind and the mind she should go through the middle nāḍī, O <s>Śivā</s>.
By forceful contraction she opens the brahma-door.

children.text: yathā nayedguṇaṃ sūcī tadvad brahmabilaṃ tu sā
children.translated_text: Just as a needle leads a thread, so she leads through the brahma-aperture.
Seated comfortably in padmāsana, with both hands turned upward, dear one...
Having placed it in the middle of the lap, he should set the chin upon the chest.
He should firmly and tightly contract the anal opening, the aperture of <s>apāna</s>.
Again and again, my dear, he should quickly drive the wind upward,
releasing the <s>prāṇa</s>; by the power of <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> he enters the path born of liberation.
He attains true awakening, which is hard even for the gods to obtain,
and with the sweat produced from that he should wipe his own limbs.
Living on milk, eating moderately, he should abandon pungent, sour, and salty foods.
With the senses conquered, celibate, dwelling in a hut, and free from worldly activity,
one devoted to practice in this way obtains accomplishment within a year.
<s>Jālandhara</s>, <s>mūlabandha</s>, <s>oḍḍīyāṇa</s>, and <s>khecarī</s>,
and <s>mahāmudrā</s>: whoever performs these becomes a possessor of bodily perfection.

children.text: eṣāṃ vakṣye lakṣaṇāni gopyāni tava śāmbhavi ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell you their characteristics, which are to be kept secret, O <s>Śāmbhavī</s>.
<s>Jālandhara</s> is the binding of the group of vessels in the throat.

children.text: kṛtvādho namayitvā kaṃ tadā syandati mūrdhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made it and bent the neck downward, then the fluid streams from the head.

children.text: nabhastaḥ syandamānā ca sudhā dogdhau patenna ca
children.translated_text: The nectar flowing from the sky-region does not fall down into the two channels,
and the wind does not run there when the contraction at the ear-region is made.
It becomes supreme, destroying disorders of the ear-region and destroying death.
For <s>mūlabandha</s>, he should press the yoni-place with the heel-area.
The yogin should contract the anus and lead the <s>apāna</s> upward.
When <s>mūlabandha</s> is done in this way, the root of impurity is worn away.

children.text: prāṇāpānau ca saṃyuktau syātāṃ vṛddho'pi yauvanam
children.translated_text: The <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, joined together, make even an old man attain youth,
and through <s>mūlabandha</s> he gains freedom even from death and a radiant state.
In <s>oḍḍīyāṇa</s>, he should firmly draw the hollow of the navel upward in the belly.
Having drawn the posterior stretch inward, he should then bind the wind.
When it has come to rest, O <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, this is called <s>oḍḍīyāṇa</s>.
It is a blazing forest fire to death, a submarine fire to the ocean of old age and disease.
He should insert the tongue into the opening inside the mouth, into the aperture of the palate.
Turning it back, he should look between the eyebrows with an unmoving gaze.
This indeed is <s>khecarī mudrā</s>, to be kept secret and exceedingly hard to obtain.

children.text: jihvā tu khagatā yasmānmanaścarati khe tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the tongue has gone into the sky-space and the mind then moves in the sky,
this is renowned as <s>khecarī</s>; it removes death, disease, and old age.

children.text: nidrā kṣudhā tṛṣā nāsti khecaryā mudritasya ca ||
children.translated_text: There is no sleep, hunger, or thirst for one who is sealed by <s>khecarī</s>.

children.text: mūrcchā bhavati sādhvī ca karmabandhabhayaṃ na hi
children.translated_text: Even fainting becomes harmless, and there is no fear of bondage by action.

children.text: ramaṇyā saṃgatasyāpi reto na patati dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Even when he is united with a beautiful woman, his semen certainly does not fall.

children.text: yāvacchukraṃ sthiraṃ dehe tāvatkālabhayaṃ na hi
children.translated_text: As long as the semen remains steady in the body, there is no fear of Time.

children.text: yena baddhā nabhomudrā bījastasya na gacchati ||
children.translated_text: For one by whom the sky-seal has been bound, his seed does not depart.
If it does depart, that seed indeed goes into the fire.
That seed rises upward by itself, checked back by <s>Śakti</s>.
Being bound by <s>yonimudrā</s>, that mudrā is difficult for him to attain.

children.text: bījastu dvividhaḥ proktaḥ śukraṃ caiva mahārajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seed is declared to be twofold: <s>śukra</s> and the great <s>rajas</s>.
<s>Śukra</s> is located in the region of the head; <s>rajas</s> is located in the yoni-place.

children.text: śukraṃ tu śvetavarṇaṃ syātpravālābhaṃ rajaḥ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śukra</s> is white in color, while <s>rajas</s> is remembered as resembling coral.

children.text: śukraṃ candragataṃ nityaṃ rajaḥ sūryeṇa saṅgatam
children.translated_text: <s>Śukra</s> is always connected with the moon, and <s>rajas</s> is joined with the sun.

children.text: śukraṃ śivo rajaḥ śaktistayā yogaḥ sudurlabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śukra</s> is <s>Śiva</s>; <s>rajas</s> is <s>Śakti</s>. Union with her is very difficult.
By the movement of <s>Śakti</s> through the wind, <s>rajas</s> is led upward.

children.text: aikyaṃ tadbindunā yāti tadā divyaṃ vapurbhavet ||
children.translated_text: It reaches union with the <s>bindu</s>; then the body becomes divine.
With the root-part of the left foot he should press the yoni-place.
He should stretch out the right foot and hold it with both hands.

children.text: hanuṃ vakṣasi nikṣipya vāyunā jaṭharaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Placing the chin on the chest, he should then fill the belly with wind,
and, remaining in the bound posture, the restrained practitioner should inhale and exhale, O <s>Devī</s>.
This is known as <s>mahāmudrā</s>, excellent for purifying impurities.
It joins the sun and moon, dries the tongue, and destroys sin.
Likewise, with the right foot he should press the yoni-place,
and, stretching out the left foot, he should hold it with his hands, my dear.
He should do the remainder as previously stated, on the left and right sides.
The practice on the two sides, left and right, should be for equal time; he should avoid imbalance.

children.text: tasya pathyamapathyaṃ ca ṣaḍrasā nīrasā api
children.translated_text: For him wholesome and unwholesome foods, the six tastes and even tasteless things,
and fierce poison are digested with great ease, as if they were nectar.
Tumors, upward-moving wind disorders, skin disease, and other illnesses are destroyed without doubt.
This <s>mahāmudrā</s> bestows accomplishment; it destroys Time and the fear of old age.

children.text: na prakāśyā na deyā ca yasmai kasmaicana priye
children.translated_text: It must not be revealed or given to just anyone, my dear.
Seated in <s>muktāsana</s>, the yogin should keep body, neck, and head straight.
With his eyes on the tip of the nose, calm and dwelling in a hut, he should recite the <s>praṇava</s>.
The three worlds, the three times, the three gods, and the three lords,
the three lights beginning with the moon, the three Vedas, and the three fires,

children.text: śaktitrayaṃ tripadavī brāhmī caindrī ca vaiṣṇavī ||
children.translated_text: the three powers, the three paths, and <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Aindrī</s>, and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>,
and the three phonemes shine where that light called <s>Oṃ</s> is present.

children.text: tam oṃkāraṃ ca manasā vacasā karmaṇā tu yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever meditates on that <s>oṃkāra</s> with mind, speech, and action,
recites it and practices it, becomes freed from the bondage of becoming.
Walking, standing, reciting, or awake, whether pure or impure,

children.text: na karmaṇā ca liptaḥ syājjalenābjadalaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: he is not tainted by action, just as a lotus leaf is not tainted by water.
When the wind moves, all the senses and bodily constituents move as well.

children.text: sthite vāyau sthire sarvaṃ vapuḥprabhṛti śāmbhavi
children.translated_text: When the wind stands still, everything, beginning with the body, is steady, O <s>Śāmbhavī</s>.
Therefore one should bind the wind; when the wind is steady, the mind is steady.

children.text: sthire manasi jīvaśca sthiro bhavati bhairavi
children.translated_text: When the mind is steady, the living self too becomes steady, O <s>Bhairavī</s>.
As long as the wind is restrained and as long as the mind too is very steady...
As long as the seed-syllable is between the eyebrows, there is no fear of Time.
Then <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is declared to be constantly thirty-six finger-breadths.
Having taken his place in the bound lotus posture, with body straight and mind steady,
he should fill himself with the wind of <s>prāṇa</s> through the left nostril alone.
He should hold it for sixteen measures and twelve, my dear,
and he should exhale for ten measures through the right nostril.
Again, through the solar channel, my dear, he should inhale as before,
and, after retaining it, he should exhale through the left nostril.
The rule of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> has been taught as threefold, O honored by yogins:
inferior, middling, O goddess, and also superior, in due order.

children.text: prokto 'yam adhamas tasmād dviguṇo madhyamaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: This one is taught as the inferior; twice that is remembered as the middling,
and three times that is taught as the superior <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, O lady.
But when he inhales the lunar syllable through the left nostril,
he should meditate on it as situated in the middle of an ocean of nectar, resembling milk.
But when he inhales the solar syllable through the right nostril,
he should always contemplate it as stationed at the navel, like blazing fire.
Thus, after meditating on the pair of seed-syllables, through the two openings of the nose,
the wise man who inhales becomes intent on purification of the channels.
Through three months of practice in this way, he retains the wind at will.
The gastric fire is kindled, and manifestation of inner sound arises.
He obtains health, O goddess, through constant disciplined practice.

children.text: prathameyaṃ na dharmaḥ syāddvitīye kampate vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the first stage this is its characteristic; in the second the body trembles.
In the third, while he remains in the bound lotus posture, it rises up.
By six rounds beginning with <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses) comes about, O <s>Śivā</s>.
By twelve of those, according to rule, <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is praised.
By twelve <s>dhāraṇās</s> there is <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and that has twelve as its measure.

children.text: samādhiḥ kathyate devi tena dṛśyaṃ parātparam
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhi</s> is described, O goddess; through it one sees what is beyond the highest.
In that supreme and non-supreme abode the accumulation of karma is destroyed.
Birth and death do not occur, and old age and disease perish.
Through yoga joined with proper method, one becomes long-lived and happy.
From practice without method arise hiccup, ear disease, headache,
asthma, cough, and other illnesses; many disorders also occur.
Coming from the lunar place, one portion is consumed by the two,
and then whatever third one remains becomes free from birth and old age.
The sun, having the form of blazing fire, is stationed in the middle of the navel.
The moon shines in the middle of the palate, facing downward and raining nectar.
The sun, facing upward, swallows that nectar with the brilliance of its rays.
The practice that is the reverse of this is called <s>viparītaka</s> (the inversion).
Making the mouth like a crow's beak and drawing in the wind with a hissing sound,
he should then expel that breath through the opening of the nose.
This yoga is called <s>śītalīkaraṇa</s> (cooling); it removes fever and bile.

children.text: amṛtaṃ śītalaṃ tasya pibataśca jarā na hi ||
children.translated_text: For one who drinks its cool nectar there is no old age.

children.text: jihvayā tālumūlena prāṇaṃ yaḥ pibati priye
children.translated_text: The yogin who drinks <s>prāṇa</s> with the tongue at the root of the palate, my dear,

children.text: tasya ṣaṇmāsataḥ sarve rogā naśyanti yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has all diseases destroyed after six months.

children.text: rasanāmūrdhvataḥ kṛtvā somaṃ pibati yaḥ priye
children.translated_text: The one who, turning the tongue upward, drinks the lunar nectar, my dear,

children.text: siddhirmāsārdha āyāti rogāstasya na santi hi ||
children.translated_text: attainment comes to him in half a month, and he has no diseases.
Pressing with the tip of the tongue the great inner cavity of the tongue,
and meditating on the mother as a stream of nectar, he becomes a poet within half a year.
For the yogin whose body is flooded with nectar, after three years
the semen surely goes upward, and powers such as minuteness are accomplished.

children.text: trividhaṃ garalaṃ tasya śarīre ca na saṃkramet
children.translated_text: The threefold poison does not pass into his body.

children.text: jarā ca maraṇaṃ nāsti duṣṭasattvabhayaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: There is no old age or death, and likewise no fear from malevolent beings.
Mounted in the posture that has been taught and always devoted to <s>prāṇāyāma</s>,
being made clear by <s>pratyāhāra</s>, he should then practice <s>dhāraṇā</s>.

children.text: cetaso niścalatvaṃ yaddhāraṇā sā smṛtā śive
children.translated_text: The steadiness of mind is what is remembered as <s>dhāraṇā</s>, O <s>Śivā</s>.
There is a separate <s>dhāraṇā</s> in the heart for the five elements beginning with earth.

children.text: caturaśrā suvarṇā salakārā ca hṛdi sthitā
children.translated_text: Earth, square, golden, marked with the syllable <s>la</s>, and situated in the heart,
together with <s>Brahmā</s>, should be meditated upon for five <s>nāḍikās</s>.
He should hold the <s>prāṇa</s> there itself together with the mind, O <s>Śāṃbhavī</s>.
This is the immobilizing knowledge; one obtains mastery over earth.
Resembling a half-moon, pure as camphor and snow,
always located in the region of the throat and joined with the syllable <s>va</s> flooded with nectar,

children.text: jalatattvaṃ ca saṃyuktaṃ viṣṇunā tatra dhārayet
children.translated_text: the water element, together with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, should be held there.
The <s>prāṇa</s>, together with the mind, should be meditated upon for five <s>nāḍikās</s>.
This indeed is the <s>Vāruṇī</s> knowledge, remover of poison, bile, and fever,
devised by me myself for the swallowing of <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison.
Triangular, shining like heated gold, containing the repha-syllable, with <s>Rudra</s> as its deity,
he should meditate on the fire element, blazing with radiance, located in the palate region.

children.text: tatraiva pañcaghaṭikāḥ prāṇaṃ ca manasā saha
children.translated_text: There itself, for five <s>ghaṭikās</s>, the yogin should hold the <s>prāṇa</s>
placed together with the mind; this is the supreme <s>Vaiśvānarī</s>.
It removes fear of poison and fire and diseases such as wind and phlegm.
Round, having the appearance of a dark-blue cloud, established between the eyebrows,
the wind element, marked with the syllable <s>ya</s>, always has <s>Īśvara</s> as its deity.

children.text: tatraiva nāḍikāḥ pañca prāṇaṃ ca manasā saha ||
children.translated_text: There itself, for five <s>nāḍikās</s>, the <s>prāṇa</s> together with the mind
should be held; this is the airy knowledge, giver of movement through the sky.
Resembling the water of a mirage and furnished with the syllable <s>ha</s>,
having <s>Sadāśiva</s> and the other deities, it is always located in the aperture of <s>Brahman</s>.
The principle of space is without ordinary space, peaceful and all-pervading, my dear.

children.text: tatra prāṇaṃ ca saṃyamya manasā saha dhārayet
children.translated_text: There one should restrain the breath and hold it together with the mind
for as long as five <s>ghatikas</s>; this, O lady, is the knowledge of space.
It has been taught, O goddess, as granting liberation to yogins and removing suffering.

children.text: stambhanī pārthivī vidyā plāvanī vāruṇī matā ||
children.translated_text: The earthly knowledge is one of immobilization, and the watery one is regarded as one of floating.
Then the fiery knowledge is proclaimed as burning.
The airy one is said to be whirling, and the space-formed one is pacifying.
In due order the five knowledges should be held separately, one by one.
They give yogins a result corresponding to their own name and action.

children.text: eṣā pañcavidhā devi dhāraṇā bhuvi durlabhā
children.translated_text: This fivefold <s>dharana</s> (concentration), O goddess, is hard to obtain on earth.

children.text: tattveṣu niścalā cintā yā taddhyānaṃ prakīrtyate ||
children.translated_text: Steady thought fixed on the principles is called <s>dhyana</s> (meditation).

children.text: dhyānaṃ dvidheti vikhyātaṃ saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ priye
children.translated_text: Meditation is known to be of two kinds, qualified and unqualified, my dear.
The qualified is accompanied by color or syllable; the unqualified is devoid of color or syllable.
A hundred thousand <s>Vajapeya</s> sacrifices and a thousand <s>Asvamedha</s> sacrifices
are not worth even a sixteenth part of a single meditation in yoga.
With mind turned inward, gaze outward, upright, and seated in <s>padmasana</s>,

children.text: dhyānayogaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sadyaḥ siddhipradaḥ śubhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this should be known as the yoga of meditation, auspicious and immediately bestowing attainment.
In the <s>muladhara</s>, in this first wheel shining like gold, my dear,
having meditated on the self and fixed attention on the tip of the nose, one destroys sin.
In the <s>svadhisthana</s>, shining like jewels, one should contemplate the self.
With attention on the tip of the nose, the best of yogins is freed from sufferings.
In this <s>manipuraka</s> wheel, shining like the young red sun,
remembering the self with gaze on the nose-tip, the restrained one agitates the three worlds.
In the <s>anahata</s> wheel, in the region of the heart, resembling a garland of lightning,
when it has been accomplished in many ways through breath control, O supreme lady,
whoever contemplates the self with eyes fixed on the tip of the nose
becomes a yogin equal to <s>Brahman</s>, with mind brought under control, my dear.
In the throat-bell, called <s>visuddha</s>, resembling golden <s>campaka</s>,
having meditated on the self with gaze on the tip of the nose, one becomes filled with bliss.
In the <s>lambika</s>, full of nectar and adorned with the disk of the moon,
having meditated on the self with gaze on the tip of the nose, one becomes filled with bliss.
Between the brows, dark like collyrium, one should meditate on the self, O lady.
The yogin becomes one who has conquered breath and is filled with the bliss of yoga.

children.text: nirguṇaṃ nirapāyaṃ ca śivaṃ śāntaṃ parātparam
children.translated_text: The unqualified, imperishable, auspicious, peaceful, and higher than the highest
self, consisting of <s>Visva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s>, should be meditated upon with the eye between the brows.
The yogin becomes filled with the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>; there is no doubt.
It is known as the <s>ajna-cakra</s>, in the supreme, stainless space.
Having contemplated the self as <s>Siva</s>, one becomes knowledge-filled and self-controlled.
Having meditated on the self as shaped like the sky, stainless, like the water of a mirage,
and all-pervading, the restrained one goes to liberation.
The region of <s>apana</s>, the generative organ, the navel, the heart, and likewise the throat-bell,
the <s>lambika</s>, the space between the brows, space, and the <s>brahmarandhra</s>:

children.text: tava cakramiti khyātaṃ deyaṃ sthānaṃ ca yoginām ||
children.translated_text: this is known as your wheel and as the place to be assigned to yogins.
Concentration lasts five <s>ghatikas</s>; six <s>nadis</s> are called meditation.
<s>Samadhi</s> lasts twelve days through restraint of the breath, my dear.
Just as, through the union of water and salt, oneness comes about,

children.text: cittātmanoḥ sāmarasyaṃ samādhiḥ sa tu kathyate ||
children.translated_text: so the equal savor of mind and self is called <s>samadhi</s>.

children.text: manaḥ pralīyate cānte yadā prāṇakṣayo bhavet
children.translated_text: And when the breath is exhausted at the end, the mind dissolves.

children.text: sāmarasyaṃ tadā syācca samādhiḥ sa tu kathyate ||
children.translated_text: Then that equal savor arises, and that is called <s>samadhi</s>.
When the individual self, all whose intentions have vanished,

children.text: yadekatvaṃ bhajeddevi samādhiḥ sa tu kathyate ||
children.translated_text: attains oneness with the supreme self, O goddess, that is called <s>samadhi</s>.
When the mind, freed from dependence on anything else, moves among the senses,

children.text: yadā jīvo gataścaikyaṃ tadā naivendriyaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the living being has gone to unity, then there is neither sense faculty nor mind.

children.text: śabdaṃ sparśaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca rasaṃ gandhaṃ paraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, taste, smell, and also what is beyond,

children.text: ātmānaṃ ca sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ mānāmānaṃ priyāpriye ||
children.translated_text: self, pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor, dear and not dear,

children.text: śītāśītaṃ tathā vātamātapaṃ yo na vetti ca
children.translated_text: cold and heat, as well as wind and sunshine: the one who does not perceive them
is not afflicted by the floods of his own actions, nor is he afflicted by anything at all.
He is not harmed by weapons, nor seized by mantras, yantras, or tantras.

children.text: nāgninā na jalenāpi vāyunā na ca pīḍyate ||
children.translated_text: He is not pained by fire, nor by water, nor by wind.
He cannot be killed by any embodied beings and is worthy of honor even by the gods.

children.text: āhāre ca vihāre ca nidrāyām avabodhane ||
children.translated_text: In eating and recreation, in sleep and waking,

children.text: sarvakarmasu yuktaḥ sansa tattvaṃ vetti yogini
children.translated_text: being disciplined in all actions, he knows the principle, O yogini.
Supportless, formless, without beginning or end, without substratum,
homeless, free from manifestation, actionless, stainless, great,

children.text: niścalaṃ nirmalaṃ nityaṃ nirguṇaṃ vyoma cinmayam ||
children.translated_text: steady, stainless, eternal, without qualities, conscious space,
ever-blissful, infinite, all-pervading, mighty, and continuous:
know this, O <s>Vindhyavasini</s>, as the state of <s>Brahman</s>, the true principle.
In the diseaseless, supportless, fearless, greatly radiant,
appearance-free, supreme principle, the one joined with yoga dissolves.
Milk cast into milk, clarified butter into ghee, fire into fire, water into water,
becomes identical with that; so too one dissolves in <s>Brahman</s>.
All this has been spoken by me: the divine elixir of wind.

children.text: yaḥ seveta sa puṇyātmā kṛtakṛtyo jagattraye ||
children.translated_text: The meritorious soul who practices it has accomplished what must be done in the three worlds.
He possesses the fruit of all sacrifices; he has bathed at every sacred ford.

children.text: sa yaśasvī sa yogīndraḥ sa evāmaravanditaḥ ||
