children.translated_text: He is famous, he is lord of yogins, he alone is praised by the immortals.

children.text: sa eva siddhaḥ śuddhaśca mama tulyo varānane
children.translated_text: He alone is perfected and pure, equal to me, O beautiful-faced one.
My mind grows attached to him; his mind is my dwelling place.

children.text: saphalaṃ jīvitaṃ tasya pūtaṃ tadubhayaṃ kulam
children.translated_text: His life is fruitful, and both his families are purified.
By the mere placing of his footstep, the earth is made holy.

children.text: yatroṣitaṃ kṣaṇaṃ tena puṇyakṣetraṃ hi sā mahī
children.translated_text: Where he has stayed for even a moment, that ground is truly a sacred field.
Blessed is the woman who bore him, and meritorious is his father, dear one.
At the sight of him, even corpses impaled on stakes and the like would become alive.
By his word alone all people obtain both auspicious and inauspicious results.
By contact with his urine and feces, metals go into the state of gold.

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ kathyate devi mama tulyaparākramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What more is to be said, O <s>Devī</s>? He has valor equal to mine.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s> said:

children.text: kuṭī proktā tvayā pūrvaṃ kathaṃ kāryā ca kīdṛśī
children.translated_text: The hut was previously mentioned by you; how is it to be made, and of what kind?

children.text: tatra kālaṃ kiyacchaṃbho vastavyaṃ brūhi me prabho ||
children.translated_text: How long is one to dwell there, O <s>Śambhu</s>? Tell me, my lord.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:

children.text: vakṣyāmi tāṃ kuṭīṃ samyak śṛṇu tripurasundari
children.translated_text: I shall explain that hut correctly; listen, O <s>Tripurasundarī</s>.
Raising up the ground, dear one, and then making it level and agreeable,

children.text: staṃbhāṃśca kramaśaḥ ṣaṭ ṣaṭ paṅktiśaḥ sthāpayedṛjūn
children.translated_text: one should set up posts, six by six in order, straight, in rows.

children.text: tulā upari cāropya dārūṇi sudṛḍhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Having placed beams above, and also strong pieces of timber,
one should then set bricks in place and plaster them thickly with lime.

children.text: parito valabhiṃ kṛtvā bhittiṃ trivalayāṃ śubhām ||
children.translated_text: Making an eave all around and a beautiful wall in three circuits,
one should make the hut in the middle of that, again with a third enclosure.
One should dig a square pit measuring ten prādeśas.
It should be five prādeśas in measure downward, and likewise upward.
Thus, with ten spans, one should make it wonderful and charming.
The outer circuit should have an eastern door; in the second circuit, O <s>Śivā</s>,
a southern door is prescribed, and in the third a western door.
The measure of the doors is said to be two spans.
Each door should have a door panel, be without gaps, and be fitted with a bolt.
One should make the wall plastered with lime, and the floor very smooth.
On the south and the north inside the hut there should be two altars.
Their breadth is three and a half spans, and their length is ten.
Their height is one prādeśa, while the middle is three prādeśas.
There one should take ash produced from cow dung, strained through cloth,
and fill the wall of the hut with a picture, extensive and very large.
One should depict <s>Bhairava</s>, dark like a rain cloud, with upward-flaming hair,
with an eye on his forehead, curved fangs, and adorned with serpent earrings,
with a serpent sacred thread, and wearing a girdle of bells and a garland of skulls,
naked, his feet and hair adorned with <s>Kākoṭī</s> serpents,
ornamented with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, rings, and the like,
ten-handed, bearing a ḍamaru, goad, sword, and trident,

children.text: varadaṃ savyahastābjair nāgaṃ pāśaṃ ca ghaṇṭikām
children.translated_text: granting boons with his lotus-like right hands, and holding a serpent, noose, and bell,
a honey vessel, and the gesture dispelling fear with his left arms.
He is rich with black unguent and garlands, destroying every disease,
slaying disease, spirits, serpents, and enemies, and removing fear from poison and the like.
Then, dear one, one should draw the peaceful <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> <s>Vaṭuka</s>,
white like mercury, the moon, and snow, a child beautiful with two arms,
adorned with earrings and anklets, bound with a garland of little bells,
a child, beautifully shining with earrings, three-eyed, and naked in form,
with white garlands and ointment, and with a full vessel on his left side,
holding a staff in his right hand, destroying death.
One should first utter the <s>māyā-bīja</s> (seed syllable of illusion) and then this <s>Vaṭuka</s>.
After the words 'for rescue from calamity,' one should write the pair of five-syllabled expressions.

children.text: vaṭukāyeti māyāṃ ca vaṭukasya manuḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: With 'to <s>Vaṭuka</s>' and the <s>māyā</s>, it is remembered as <s>Vaṭuka</s>'s mantra.
This mantra for the two forms has been taught, O you honored by the gods.

children.text: mantrasyāsya ca yadyantraṃ tadyantraṃ tatra saṃlikhet
children.translated_text: Whatever yantra belongs to this mantra, one should inscribe that yantra there.

children.text: ramāṃ ca bhuvaneśīṃ ca kāmaṃ cintāmaṇiṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: One should write, in order, <s>Ramā</s>, <s>Bhuvaneśī</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, and <s>Cintāmaṇi</s>.
First, in the pericarp, one should write the desired phrase 'to <s>Vaṭuka</s>'.
In the eight petals one should write the remaining letters, each in an eight-petaled place.
Outside, in the sixteen petals, one should write the sixteen vowels.
In the thirty-two petals, one should write the thirty-two consonants from ka through sa.
In another petal one should write the hal-akṣas, and outside the bhūpura.
This yantra rescues from calamity and wards off untimely death.
It gives protection for those afflicted by planets and for all living beings as well.
It brings women under control, kings under control, men under control, and animals under control.
It always grants various siddhis and removes all disease and poison.
Bright with necklaces and armlets, it enchants the universe with its beauty.
One should visualize the god <s>Mahāmṛtyuñjaya</s>; then one becomes a conqueror of death.
Thus, from the second group, the third letter, together with the fifth,

children.text: svareṇa bindunā yuktaṃ sontaṃ sādhyapadaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: joined with a vowel and a bindu, with sa at the end, and then the name of the person to be accomplished,
then the word 'protect' twice, and again the three seed syllables before it;
after uttering them in reverse order, one should recite the <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> mantra.

children.text: tāraṃ madhye sasādhyākhyaṃ digdale bhaṃ samālikhet ||
children.translated_text: One should write the tāra in the middle, together with the name of the sādhya, and bha on the directional petals.
In the petals beginning with the southeast, one should write the final letter in sequence.
Outside, having drawn the bhūpura, one should write densely in the directions.
In the four corners one should write the syllable ṭha; this is the yantra whose nature is <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s>.
It destroys untimely death, fever, disease, poison, and delusion.
There one should draw the god <s>Cintāmaṇi</s>, who grants the objects one has thought of.
He is beautiful with blue coral, three-eyed, and lovely-faced.
In his left hands are a noose and a red lotus; in his right hands are a trident and a skull-bowl.
One should meditate on <s>Ardhāmbikeśvara</s>, wearing the moon as his crest-jewel.
Then, in order, come the fire-letter, the beginning of the first class, ṣa, ma, and the repha.
It is joined with prāṇa and with the ending called sadya, and has the sixth vowel with bindu.
This is the auspicious mantra of <s>Cintāmaṇi</s>, granting the object that is contemplated.
Enveloped by the sixteen vowels, <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> grants what is desired.
One should enclose it with the syllable ṭha; it destroys fever, epilepsy, and death.
Then one should draw the goddess <s>Śāradā</s>, the giver of siddhi.
She is white like a conch, jasmine, and the moon, and bears a crescent moon in her crown.
With her lotus hands she holds a nectar jar, the boon-giving gesture, a rosary, and the gesture of awareness.
She wears white garments and shines with pearl ornaments.
One should utter the speech-seed, <s>Bhuvaneśī</s>, and then the two words commanding speech.
One should pronounce <s>Vāgvādinī</s> in the vocative, together with the wife of fire.
This is called the glorious <s>Mātṛkā</s> mantra, which grants eloquence.
Leaving aside the first pair of seed-syllables, one should pronounce the rest as before.
The ten-syllabled <s>Śāradā</s> mantra grants the play of speech.
One should write the sky-letter and the syllable su, ending with sadya and furnished with visarga.
First one should write it in the pericarp, and the vowels also on the filaments.
On the eight petals one should place the eight letter-groups, with the three higher ones beginning with a, śa, and ha.
The eight groups are stated to consist of the five letters beginning with ka and the others in order.
One should write the ṭha-syllables in the corners of the bhūpura and set them in the directions.
This indeed is the <s>Mātṛkā</s> yantra, removing poison, death, and disease.
O goddess, one should draw <s>Aghora</s>, resembling a dark raincloud.
He has terrible fangs and three eyes, and is adorned with eight great serpents.
His body is anointed red, his garment is red, and he is adorned with a red garland.

children.text: paraśvathuṃ ca ḍamaruṃ khaḍgaṃ kheṭam iṣuṃ dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: He bears an axe, a ḍamaru drum, a sword, a shield, an arrow, and a bow,
and with his eight arms he also holds a trident and a full vessel.
One should utter <s>Bhuvaneśī</s>, the pair sphur, and then the repeated prasphur.
Then come ghora, then aghoratara, tanurūpa, and the two caṭ syllables.
Also the doubled prakaṭa, and then the pair of kaha sounds.
O goddess, next come the two vama sounds and the repeated word bandha.
O goddess, then come the two ghātaya sounds, the kavaca, and the ending phaṭ.
This <s>Aghora</s> mantra is remembered as having fifty-one phonemes.
For the purpose of subjugation, he should have the appearance of heated gold and the form described before.
For liberation and for the <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> purpose, he is white and has the previously described form.
O beloved, one should draw the peaceful <s>Aghorāstra</s>, which grants success in every aim.
The <s>Māyā</s> seed, with the name of the sādhya, should be in the middle, joined with the vowels.
Outside that, on the filaments, one should write the eight letter-groups in this way.
Then, on the eight petals, one should write the mantra letters according to their proper count.
At the petal-tips and the remaining places likewise, and in the six angles, one should write the kavaca and astra syllables.
Outside that a bhūpura should be drawn: this is the little <s>Aghora</s> yantra.
In the middle one should write the śakti-seed, enclosed by the two sphur syllables.
In the hexagon one writes the pair prasphur; then, on the eight petals in order,
with sixes, fours, the Vedas, the rasas, the vastras, and the gopadas,
one should then write these remaining mantra letters according to the seasons and the other counts.
In the hexagon, raised up with the fire-letter and the astra, it is without the outer corner.
O beloved, one should draw the <s>Aghora</s> yantra enclosed by the bhūpura.
It removes serpents, enemies, thieves, lesser spirits, epilepsy, bhūtas, and grahas.
Now one should draw <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>, resembling coral.
He has the crescent moon in his diadem, an elephant face, and three eyes.
He is pot-bellied, clothed in red, and anointed and garlanded in red.
He is handsome with the staves of ten arms, and has a woman seated on his left thigh.
He shines with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, rings, and earrings.
He holds a citron, a mace, a sugarcane bow, and a trident,
a discus, a lotus, a noose, a blue lotus, and a panicle of rice,
as well as his own tusk, while with his trunk and ten hands he bears a jeweled pitcher.
He is embraced by <s>Śrī</s>, seated on his left thigh and holding a lotus in her hand.
He is the divine wish-tree granting the aims contemplated by the world of devotees.
The praṇava, <s>Kamalā</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Kāmarāja</s>, and <s>Vasundharā</s>,
in order, form the seed of <s>Gaṇapati</s>; then comes <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>.

children.text: caturthyantaṃ sasaṃbuddhiṃ varaṃ ca varadaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: It should end in the dative and include the vocative; then come vara and also varada.

children.text: tataḥ sarvajanaṃ me ca vaśamānaya śabdakam ||
children.translated_text: Then comes the phrase, "bring all people under my control."
Having written the wife of fire, the mantra has twenty-eight syllables.
This is the mantra of <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>, destroying death and poverty.
Having written the seed in a triangle, together with Tārā, for the lord of the gaṇas,
one should write outside, in the directions, the seeds of <s>Śrī</s>, śakti, <s>Madana</s>, and bhū.
In the hexagon one should write the six seeds, and at their junctions the limb-mantras.
Then, in the middle of the eight petals, one should write the mantras group by group.
At the final syllable and on the final petal, one should write the <s>Mātṛkā</s> in forward order.
In the inscription one should write it in reverse order, and then enclose it with the goad and noose.
This is the beautiful and auspicious yantra of <s>Gaṇapati</s>, furnished with a bhūmandira.
It ends with gaja and the divine word śrī, and it increases lifespan and health.
One should draw these networks of yantras on the inner walls of the deity-shrine.
On the outer side of the hut wall one should draw <s>Bhairava</s> with the garland of letters.
In order, one should draw <s>Asitāṅga</s>, <s>Ruru</s>, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, <s>Krodha</s>, and <s>Unmattabhairava</s>,

children.text: kapālinaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ ca saṃhāraṃ bhairavaṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Kapālin</s>, <s>Bhīṣaṇa</s>, and <s>Saṃhārabhairava</s> in sequence.
On the wall inside the second enclosure, one should draw eleven in order:
the <s>Rudras</s>, three-eyed, with matted crests bearing the crescent moon.

children.text: tadbāhye nava nāthāṃśca nava siddhāṃśca ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: Outside that one should draw the nine <s>Nāthas</s> and also the sixteen <s>Siddhas</s>,
then <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sananda</s>, and the others.
On the inner wall of the third enclosure, the Mothers beginning with <s>Brāhmī</s>,
and the sixty-four <s>Yoginīs</s> should be drawn according to rule.
Outside that wall, in order, should be the guardians of the directions beginning with <s>Devendra</s>,
the planets beginning with the moon and sun, and the stars beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s>.
The zodiac signs beginning with <s>Meṣa</s> should be drawn adorned and bearing their weapons,
and on the two sides of the hut doorway one should draw <s>Gaṇeśa</s> and <s>Bhairava</s>.
Beside the doorway of the second enclosure one should draw the two, <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Padmaka</s>,
and <s>Garuḍmat</s> and <s>Hanūmat</s> at the third enclosure.
O goddess, at the two sides of its doorway one should draw those two destroyers of fear.
In whatever country the divine hut is prepared by the best of yogins,

children.text: deśo dhanyataraḥ ślāghyaḥ puṇyakṣetraṃ ca pāvanam
children.translated_text: that country is especially blessed, praiseworthy, a holy field, and purifying.
The people who live there are blessed, prosperous in wealth, and doers of meritorious acts.
The kingdom has abundant food, health, and happiness free from sickness;
it is free from calamities, supplied with rain in season, and full of grain.
It is free from danger caused by thieves, harassment, tigers, snakes, and the like.

children.text: tatra tīrthāni sarvāṇi gaṅgādīni vasanti ca ||
children.translated_text: All sacred fords, beginning with the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, dwell there.
The gods headed by <s>Indra</s> also are there, along with the planets headed by the sun and moon,
the <s>Yoginīs</s>, <s>Bhairavas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, <s>Guha</s>, and the Mothers.
For the king abiding there, victory, prosperity, and length of life arise;
universal sovereignty may occur, and the land shines constantly with festivals.
Barren women obtain the blessing of sons from seeing the hut.
It destroys leprosy, epilepsy, affliction by spirits, and other great diseases.
Those who enter the hut and practice the <s>rasāyana</s> there
easily attain a siddhi that is difficult even for the gods to obtain.

children.text: devi citraṃ pravakṣyāmi divyaṃ guhyatamaṃ śivam
children.translated_text: O goddess, I shall teach the wondrous, divine, most secret, auspicious
and stainless <s>amarī-kalpa</s>, easy to perform and produced from one's own body.
It bestows the eight powers beginning with minuteness and siddhis over the body, metals, and the rest.
With the limbs purified by vomiting and the other purifications, one should avoid salt and sour foods.
Staying in the hut, O queen of gods, the broad-minded practitioner uses <s>śivatoya</s>.
He should make a drinking vessel from the wood of a stout <s>kataka</s> tree.
Grinding <s>triphalā</s>, he should smear it inside the cup.

children.text: karṣaṃ śivāmbunā rātrau pātraṃ cādhomukhaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: At night, with a karṣa of <s>śivāmbu</s>, O dear one, he should place the vessel mouth-down.
Then in the morning he should discard the first and last portions of the stream.
He should put the middle stream in that vessel, and then add that <s>triphalā</s>.
He should stir it together with <s>amarī</s> and always drink it facing east.
Having bowed to his chosen deities, gurus, and elders, and having worshipped <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>,
he should eat moderately, act with discipline, and avoid wind and sun.
In just one maṇḍala he becomes possessed of purity both outside and within.
With the second maṇḍala, all leprosy is destroyed.
With the third maṇḍala, the four kinds of poison are removed.
With the fourth, his own water becomes like coconut water.
With the fifth, impurity and foul smell in the <s>ātmatoya</s> are destroyed.
Through the sixth maṇḍala, the bad odor of the body is destroyed.
Through the seventh maṇḍala, sharpness of the senses arises.
Then, in the eighth maṇḍala, he should add a karṣa of powdered <s>rajanī</s>,
and consume the <s>śivatoya</s> until twice seven maṇḍalas have passed.
He becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair, and rid of fear from great poison.
In the fifteenth maṇḍala he should add one karṣa each of <s>śṛṅga</s> and sulphur.
Mixed with <s>śivatoya</s>, he should drink it through the twenty-first
maṇḍala; at the end of that he becomes a sharer in siddhi over the body and metals.
In the twenty-second maṇḍala, O goddess, mica should be combined with <s>varā</s>.
Thus the restrained practitioner should take it until the twenty-eighth maṇḍala.
He is endowed with the strength of a rutting elephant, has the sight of a vulture, and is free from disease.
When the twenty-ninth maṇḍala has been reached, with <s>varā</s>
he should drink even <s>godhā</s>, purified with powdered <s>kānta</s>, O dear one.
By the end of the thirty-fifth maṇḍala, a man becomes adamant-bodied.
From the thirty-sixth maṇḍala onward, it is mixed with the powder of golden <s>dhātrī</s>.
The drink should be taken together with <s>ātmagodhā</s> until two beyond forty
maṇḍalas have passed; then, with his body, he becomes a sky-goer.
When the forty-third maṇḍala has been reached, it should be combined with mercury.
Together with <s>varā</s>, he should drink it up to the forty-ninth maṇḍala.
He becomes endowed with qualities beginning with minuteness, adamant-bodied, and moving in the sky.
Joined with the siddhas, free from distress, free from danger, and stainless,
he always roams at will through all the worlds.
Beginning with the first maṇḍala, O goddess, he should practice daily.
He should stir it with <s>ātmatoya</s> and the juice of <s>dhuttūra</s>.
With that very ash he should repeatedly rub his whole body.
The <s>ātmatoya</s> that comes at other times should especially be used
on the head, nostrils, ears, eyes, and the two feet and hands.
He should practice this constantly, O goddess; the man becomes pure-bodied.
O dear one, he should never release the <s>ātmagodhā</s> onto the ground.
For a man who consumes <s>amarī</s>, through <s>śivatoya</s> there arises
the divine transformation of every metal into gold, difficult for human beings.
Every day he should drink <s>godhā</s> together with <s>vijayā</s>.
<s>Vandāka</s> is said to be of two kinds, distinguished as male and female.
The male has leaves like date-palm leaves and bestows all siddhis.
The one called female has few virtues; it has round leaves and great potency.
<s>Vandaka</s> is a growth on a tree, also called <s>padaparuha</s>, <s>sikhari</s>, and <s>tarurohini</s>.
It is also <s>vrksadani</s>, <s>kamini</s>, and a binding growth that is a disease of trees.
<s>Vandaka</s> is bitter and astringent, and removes phlegm, bile, and fatigue.
It grants attainments such as subjugation, is aphrodisiac, destroys poison, and is a <s>rasayana</s> (rejuvenative).
Having fasted, bathed well, and put on red garlands and unguents,
with hair and garment loosened, at night, with mind restrained,
one should circumambulate the tree and worship it with sandal, flowers, unbroken rice, and the like,
with materials for worship, and should scatter an offering of curds and boiled rice.
After reciting the <s>Cintamani</s> and <s>Nrsimha</s> mantras one hundred and eight times,
one should cut off the <s>vandaka</s> with a sword and take it according to rule.
This is declared to be the rule for all <s>vandakas</s>.
In <s>Asvini</s>, a pure man should take the <s>vandaka</s> of the sacred fig according to rule.
Having ground it with milk and stirred it, he should drink it; he will become as strong as a horse.
Likewise, during an eclipse of the sun or moon, one should take the <s>vandaka</s> of the sacred fig
while reciting the <s>Nrsimha</s> mantra, cutting it with a sword.
Having rubbed it with water on the forearm and smeared it on, together with <s>gorocana</s>,
one should make a forehead mark and look; he will certainly become one to whom all are subject.
One should take the <s>vandaka</s> of the banyan in <s>Asvini</s> according to rule.
If he ties it on his hand with a thread, a man becomes invisible.
Ground with milk and drunk, it makes all subject and cures diseases.
In <s>Asvini</s>, one should take the <s>vandaka</s> of the <s>sirisa</s> according to rule.
If he ties it on his hand with a thread, retention of virility certainly results.
In <s>Asvini</s>, the wise man should take the binding growth of the <s>palasa</s>.

children.text: haste baddhvā spṛśedyastu sā nārī vaśagā bhavet
children.translated_text: Having tied it on his hand, if he touches a woman, that woman comes under his control.
Tying the binding growth of <s>ankola</s> on the hand in <s>Asvini</s>, one becomes beloved by the world.
In <s>Bharani</s>, having taken the <s>vandaka</s> of <s>kusa</s> grass under an auspicious conjunction,
he should bind it on his right hand; by it a man becomes invisible.
In <s>Bharani</s>, one should place the <s>vandaka</s> of the <s>phalgu</s> tree in a heap of grain.

children.text: tena vai dhānyavṛddhiḥ syānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: By that there is indeed an increase of grain; no doubt is to be raised here.
In <s>Bharani</s>, one should take the <s>vandaka</s> of the jujube trees according to rule.
He should bind it on the right hand; he will obtain the desired result.
In <s>Krttika</s>, one should take the <s>vandaka</s> of the <s>kataka</s> tree according to rule.

children.text: vartimadhye kṣipettaṃ ca tena saṃgṛhya kajjalam ||
children.translated_text: He should put it in the middle of a lamp-wick and collect the soot from it.
For women, by the mere application of that collyrium, the husband certainly becomes subject to them.
In <s>Krttika</s>, having become pure, one should take the <s>vandaka</s> of the rose-apple tree.
After drinking its paste ground with milk, one is freed from diseases.
In <s>Rohini</s>, one should take the <s>vandaka</s> of the tamarind tree according to rule.

children.text: baddhvā haste spṛśedyaṃ yaṃ sarvavaśyo bhavennaraḥ
children.translated_text: If, with it tied on his hand, he touches whomever he chooses, a man becomes one to whom all are subject.
It is praised for blindness and the like; even an incurable condition is helped by an ointment with ghee.
With that same substance, rubbed with honey, an eye-salve beneficial to the eyes is made.

children.text: bandhakam udumbarabhavaṃ rohiṇyāṃ gṛhya valayakaṃ kuryāt
children.translated_text: Taking a binding growth produced from the <s>udumbara</s> in <s>Rohini</s>, one should make a bracelet.
A sweet cake kept in a vessel placed upon that bracelet does not diminish.
One should take the <s>vandaka</s> of the sacred fig in <s>Rohini</s> according to rule.

children.text: gṛhe sthite ca vandāke nityaiśvaryaṃ prajāyate
children.translated_text: When that <s>vandaka</s> is kept in the house, constant prosperity arises.
One should take the <s>vandaka</s> of the <s>kataka</s> tree in <s>Rohini</s> according to rule.
When it is used as collyrium on the pair of eyes, one surely sees treasure.
If one ties that very same thing on the hand, he will certainly become one to whom all are subject.
One should take the <s>vandaka</s> of the <s>udumbara</s> in <s>Rohini</s> according to rule.

children.text: haste baddhvā nihantyāśu jvaraṃ cāturthikaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: Tied on the hand, it quickly destroys quartan fever, my dear.
In <s>Rohini</s>, one should collect the binding growth of the citron.
He should wear it on the right ear; it is a supreme means of making the world subject.
Tying the <s>vandaka</s> of the bilva on the hand in <s>Rohini</s>, one becomes beloved by the world.
In <s>Mrgasirsa</s>, the <s>vandaka</s> of the <s>sirisa</s> should be properly taken.

children.text: haste baddhvā spṛśennārīṃ naraṃ vā vaśayeddhruvam
children.translated_text: Having tied it on the hand, if one touches a woman or a man, he certainly brings that person under control.
In <s>Mrgasirsa</s>, the <s>vandaka</s> born from the tamarind tree
should be ground with milk and drunk; a man becomes invisible.
Whoever drinks it with curds in the morning becomes one who removes all diseases.
With that substance ground in buffalo buttermilk, one should make a full-body anointing.

children.text: kṛtvā vahnigato yastu vahninā ca na dahyate ||
children.translated_text: Whoever, having done so, enters fire is not burned by the fire.
In whose house the <s>vandaka</s> of the tamarind tree is installed,

children.text: tasya corabhayaṃ nāsti kare dyūtajayo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: for him there is no fear of thieves, and on his hand there will be victory in gambling.
One should collect the <s>vandaka</s> of the <s>udumbara</s> in <s>Mrgasirsa</s>.

children.text: haste baddhvā spṛśennārīṃ sā nārī vaśagā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having tied it on the hand, if he touches a woman, that woman comes under his control.
One should tie it on women's hands or place it amid food.
Then there is an increase of food; no doubt is to be raised here.
One should collect the <s>vandaka</s> of the banyan in <s>Mrgasirsa</s>.
He should bind it on the right hand; he will certainly become one to whom people are subject.
Taking the prescribed <s>vandaka</s> of <s>matarusa</s>,
and tying it on the hand, one plays with people and becomes undefeated at gambling.

children.text: ārdrāyāṃ taumburaṃ grāhyaṃ vandākaṃ vidhinā haret
children.translated_text: In <s>Ardra</s>, one should take the <s>taumbura</s> <s>vandaka</s>, collecting it according to rule.
Whoever drinks it with milk will be able to bend iron.
Or, when the sun is in <s>Ardra</s> or on a Sunday in <s>Pusya</s>, one should take the <s>vandaka</s> of <s>tumburu</s>.
He should bind it on the right hand; the stopping of arrows arises.
The bamboo <s>vandaka</s>, taken in <s>Punarvasu</s>, should be ground with milk.
Having drunk it, a barren woman and man produce many sons.
On <s>Punarvasu</s> one should again gather the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>naktamāla</s> tree.
Having ground it with milk, one should drink it; it destroys every disease.
By just a measure of its powder, planetary spirits and rākṣasas perish.
On <s>Puṣya</s>, one should take the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>bandhūka</s> tree and deposit it.
There in an enemy's field, the destruction of the crop comes about.
Under <s>Āśleṣā</s>, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>karṇikāra</s> tree should be properly gathered.

children.text: baddhvā haste dṛḍhaṃ tena spṛśan vaśati tejanāt
children.translated_text: Having tied it firmly on the hand, whoever he touches is brought under control by its power.
And one should gather the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>madhūka</s> tree under <s>Āśleṣā</s>.
One should bind it on the right hand; it destroys fear from tigers and the like.
In the <s>Maghā</s> asterisms, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>mucukunda</s> tree, gathered according to rule,
should be deposited among grain; that grain becomes inexhaustible.
The <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>vibhītaka</s> tree, gathered under the former <s>Phalgunī</s>,
should be placed in the midst of grain; that becomes inexhaustible at once.
For the other <s>Phalgunī</s> and also for <s>Hasta</s>, this same procedure is remembered.
One should gather, according to rule, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>śāka</s> tree under <s>Maghā</s>.
At the door of a store of grain, it produces an accumulation of grain, and increase of grain arises.
One should gather, according to rule, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>mauñjī</s> tree on a Sunday under <s>Maghā</s>.
One should always wear it on the head; fortune comes under his control.
But one should gather, according to rule, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>palāśa</s> tree under the asterism <s>Hasta</s>.
One should tie it on the hand or head; it removes tigers, planets, and the like.
Likewise, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>tinduka</s> tree is gathered under <s>Citrā</s>.

children.text: baddhvā haste samastānāṃ sadhvadho bhavati dviṣām ||
children.translated_text: Having tied it on the hand, he becomes impossible to strike down for all his enemies.
But one should gather, according to rule, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>kuṭaja</s> tree under <s>Citrā</s>.
One should bind it on the right hand; he obtains the desired thing, even if it is hard to obtain.
Under <s>Svāti</s>, after taking the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>likuca</s> tree, in whatever object
he deposits it, all that becomes inexhaustible; there is no doubt about this.
Under <s>Svāti</s> one should take the <s>bandhaka</s> of the <s>babbūla</s> tree, and under <s>Anurādhā</s> that of the <s>badarī</s> tree.

children.text: badhnanyo dhārayeddhaste tatspṛṣṭā strī vaśā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The one who binds and wears it on the hand will have any woman he touches become subject to him.
Having gathered, according to rule, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>dhātrī</s> tree under <s>Viśākhā</s>,
one should deposit it in the house of a hostile maker of liquor.
All the liquor becomes undrinkable; release from that occurs when it is dug up.
The <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>aindrī</s> plant, gathered according to rule under <s>Anurādhā</s>,
when thrown into the midst of grain, makes the grain inexhaustible.
Under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, after taking the <s>vandāka</s> of the mango tree, one should bury it in a courtesan's house.
She truly becomes unfortunate; when it is dug up, release is said to occur.
Under <s>Mūla</s>, having taken the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>khadira</s> tree according to rule,

children.text: baddhvā haste naraḥ kṣipraṃ durbhagaḥ subhago bhavet
children.translated_text: and having tied it on the hand, a man quickly changes from unlucky to fortunate.
The same thing, ground with milk and drunk, destroys skin disease and the like.
On a Sunday under <s>Mūla</s>, one should gather, according to rule, the <s>vandāka</s> of <s>goṭṭikā</s>.
One should bind it on the right hand; it surely makes women subject to him.
The same thing should be worn on the head; every siddhi surely arises.
The <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>karavīra</s> tree, prepared under the former <s>Āṣāḍhā</s>,
one should wear on the head in battle; he becomes unconquered.
The <s>vandāka</s> born from the <s>badarī</s> tree under the former <s>Āṣāḍhā</s>,

children.text: pibetkṣīreṇa yā vandhyā sā bahūṃśca sutāṃllabhet
children.translated_text: if a barren woman drinks it with milk, she obtains many sons.
But the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>kurava</s> tree, on a Sunday under the former <s>Āṣāḍhā</s>,
should be bound on the right hand; the man becomes invisible.
Under the <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> asterism, the <s>bandhaka</s> of the <s>mandāra</s> tree should be taken,
or else the <s>bandhaka</s> of the <s>palāśa</s> tree; tied on the hand, it brings others under control.

children.text: śravaṇe citrakodbhūtaṃ vandākaṃ prāpyate na tu ||
children.translated_text: Under <s>Śravaṇa</s>, the <s>vandāka</s> arising from the <s>citraka</s> is not obtained.
One should smear a copper plate with <s>kaṅkuṇī</s> oil rubbed upon it.
By the method of heating in a closed crucible, that surely becomes gold.
But one should gather the <s>vandāka</s> of the castor-oil plant on a Sunday under <s>Śravaṇa</s>.
One should bind it on the right hand; there will always be victory in gambling.
The <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>badarī</s> tree, gathered according to rule under <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>,

children.text: baddhvā kare spṛśedyaṃ yaṃ sa sa dāso bhaveddhruvam ||
children.translated_text: having tied it on the hand, whomever he touches, each one surely becomes his servant.
The <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>punnāga</s> tree, taken according to rule under the <s>Vāruṇa</s> asterisms,
when ground with milk and drunk, gives the strength of a great elephant.
One should gather, according to rule, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>naktamāla</s> tree on a Sunday under <s>Maghā</s>.
Having worn it on the arm according to rule, there is a vision of piśācas.
One should gather, according to rule, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>tintriṇīka</s> tree under the <s>Punarvasu</s> asterism.
One should bind it on the right hand; there will always be victory in gambling.
Under the <s>Punarvasu</s> asterism, the bamboo <s>vandāka</s> makes one invisible when worn on the hand.
But one should gather, according to rule, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>śirīṣa</s> tree under the latter asterism.
One should tie it on the hand or head; it removes tigers, planets, and the like.
Under <s>Maghā</s>, one should place in a field the <s>vandāka</s> arising from the <s>madhūka</s> tree.
The beaks of birds and mice become bound.
But one should gather, according to rule, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>palāśa</s> tree under the asterism <s>Hasta</s>.
One should make an anointing of the penis with it; retention of semen surely results.
Having stirred <s>vallīka</s> with milk and ground it with honey, one should sprinkle it.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ tu saptadhā devi tadvaṅgaṃ rajataṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: O goddess, tin becomes silver when treated seven times with that tin-preparation.
But one should gather, according to rule, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>palāśa</s> tree under the asterism <s>Hasta</s>.
Whoever drinks it with milk becomes invisible.
Likewise, the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>tinduka</s> tree is gathered under <s>Citrā</s>.
Having tied it on the hand, he becomes invulnerable to all enemies.
But the <s>vandāka</s> of the <s>harītakī</s> tree is gathered under <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>.
Having drunk it ground with milk, one should go about equal to <s>Vararuci</s>.
That <s>arka-vandāka</s> is to be taken under <s>Uttarābhādrapadā</s> in the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>.
By smearing and the like it utterly destroys poison, whether from stationary or moving beings.
Under <s>Revatī</s>, a charm made with a creeper of <s>bodhi-vandāka</s>,

children.text: vandhyāpi labhate garbhaṃ pītvā gopayasā ca tat
children.translated_text: even a barren woman obtains pregnancy when she drinks that with cow's milk.
Under <s>Revatī</s>, a <s>vaṭa-vandāka</s>, rubbed with anthill honey,
is extremely excellent for defects of the eyes, such as coverings of the eye and the like.
Taking a <s>vaṭa-vandāka</s> under <s>Revatī</s>, one should wear it on the arm.
He becomes endowed with the strength of a great serpent and also gains a great retinue.
A <s>rājavṛkṣa-vandāka</s> pulled up under <s>Viśākhā</s>
wards off the danger of fire for a householder in the house.
A <s>vaṭa-vandāka</s> under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, placed at the waist, increases virility.
A <s>vandāka</s> arising from an <s>aśvattha</s>, taken under <s>Revatī</s>, is remembered as giving pregnancy.
If a <s>vandāka</s> grown from a poison-tree is pulled up under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>,
when smeared on, it causes speech by spirits, piśācas, and the like.
One should place it inside a small hearth, together with food and a succession of drinks.
In gambling, a <s>jāmbava-vandāka</s> taken under <s>Revatī</s> brings victory.
One should make a <s>kurava-vandāka</s> held in the hand a ward against arrows.
A <s>madhūka</s>-tree <s>vandāka</s>, placed among grain, gives increase of grain.
A <s>palāśa</s>-tree <s>vandāka</s>, taken with milk, bestows eloquence.
If a <s>nimba-vandāka</s> is hidden inside the house of a courtesan,
it wondrously brings her under control until the end of life.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s>:

children.text: śrutaṃ sarvaṃ mayā deva divyaṃ sarvarasāyanam
children.translated_text: I have heard everything, O god, the divine complete <s>rasāyana</s>,
through your favor, O <s>Śambhu</s>, ocean of compassion, lord of the gods.
I shall ask about another matter that benefits all worlds:
for the old, women, children, the impotent, and also other sick people,
who are unable to undertake <s>rasāyana</s>, how might well-being arise, O lord?
O gracious benefactor of all, illustrious <s>Bhairava</s>, please teach that.
Hearing the goddess's praise, devoted to the benefit of all worlds,

children.text: śrutvā mandasmitaṃ devo jagādetthaṃ paraṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the god, with a gentle smile, spoke this supreme speech.
<s>Śrībhairava</s>:

children.text: sādhu sādhu mahābhāge lokānāṃ jananī yataḥ
children.translated_text: Well done, well done, greatly fortunate one; because you are the mother of the worlds,
you have therefore asked about the welfare of the worlds. I shall tell it, O <s>Īśvarī</s>.
I shall explain the method for processing mercury and the other substances, which removes all diseases,
in due order; listen with attention.
Mercury is called <s>Rasendra</s>, <s>Rasarāja</s>, <s>rasa</s>, <s>sūta</s>, and <s>pārada</s>,
<s>Śivabīja</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Jaitra</s>, <s>Rasaloha</s>, and <s>Mahārasa</s>.
It is <s>Rasottama</s>, <s>Mahātejas</s>, <s>Sūtarāṭ</s>, <s>Capala</s>, and <s>Amṛta</s>,
<s>Dhuttura</s>, <s>Lokanātha</s>, <s>Prabhu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and likewise <s>Bhava</s>.
It is <s>Rudratejas</s>, <s>Khecara</s>, <s>Rasadhātu</s>, and <s>Acintyaja</s>,
<s>Amara</s>, <s>Dehada</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Skandeśa</s>, and <s>Mṛtyunāśana</s>.

children.text: devo rasāyanaḥ śreṣṭho yaśodaḥ pāvanaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: It is remembered as <s>Deva</s>, <s>Rasāyana</s>, <s>Śreṣṭha</s>, <s>Yaśoda</s>, and <s>Pāvana</s>.
Thus the divine names of mercury, thirty-three in number, have been taught.
The king <s>sūta</s>, when joined with defects, is poison itself, O lovely-faced one.
Mercury free from defects is directly nectar; there is no doubt about this.
Therefore listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, to the defect-destroying processing of <s>pārada</s>.
The teacher of mercury should be the best of physicians, self-controlled, and versed in the <s>Aghora</s> mantra.
On auspicious lunar mansions, auspicious ascendants, good muhūrtas, and good weekdays,
he should first perform the worship of <s>sūta</s>, as stated before, in a clean place.
One may use one hundred palas, fifty, or again twenty-five,

children.text: daśa vā pañca vā devi naitasmādūnamiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: or ten or five, O goddess; less than this is not approved.

children.text: lohaje vā śilotthe vā khalve sūtaṃ vinikṣipet
children.translated_text: He should place the <s>sūta</s> in a mortar made of iron or of stone.
For the king <s>sūta</s>, brick powder and turmeric dust should be a sixteenth part.
Having triturated it with sour <s>jambīra</s> juice in a heated mortar for a day, dear one,
he should wash it with hot <s>sauvīra</s>; the lead defect is destroyed.
With <s>aṅkola</s> and <s>indravāruṇī</s>, the tin defect is destroyed.
With <s>āragvadha</s> impurity is removed, and with <s>citraka</s> the lead contamination.
With black <s>dhūrta</s> its fickleness is removed; with <s>triphalā</s> one should remove poison.
With <s>trikaṭu</s> one removes the mountain defect, and with <s>gokṣura</s> its intolerable fire.
For the destruction of the seven defects beginning with tin, for seven days,
using those respective powders in sixteenth parts, together with <s>kumārī</s> juice and mercury,
after triturating the mercury, he should then wash it with hot <s>kāñjika</s>.
<s>Pārada</s> is freed from all defects, from the seven sheaths.
If mercury is to be employed in the physician's work, it becomes a remover of all diseases.
With <s>devadāru</s>, <s>malayaja</s>, <s>jayā</s>, and <s>vāyasatuṇḍikā</s>,
combined with the juices of <s>kumārī</s>, <s>musalī</s>, <s>vandhyā</s>, and <s>karkoṭī</s>,
one should triturate <s>sūta</s> for a day, and then again in a sublimation apparatus.
One should sublime it and employ the purified <s>sūta</s> in the physician's work.
With calcined stone powder and with the juices of <s>niśā</s> and <s>kanyā</s>, one should work the mercury.
He should triturate it for one day and sublime it in the previous apparatus.
Thus purified by processing, it should be employed in medical work.
Dear one, <s>darada</s> should be treated for the duration of one <s>yāma</s> with liquids of <s>pāribhadra</s>,
or with juices of <s>jambīra</s>; after triturating it, one should cook it
in the sublimation apparatus, O goddess, until it is free from the sheaths of defects.
Powdered <s>dhānyābhra</s>, ground with juices of <s>punarnavā</s>, should be equal to the mercury.
Having kept the mercury in a heated mortar for a day and placed it in a diamond crucible,
he should cook it in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus and then triturate it again.
With the previous liquids, as before, trituration and cooking should be done again.
After doing this ten times, it should be sublimed in a sublimation apparatus.

children.text: śuddhaḥ syātpārado devi yojyo yoge rasāyane
children.translated_text: O goddess, mercury should become purified and fit to be used in alchemical practice and <s>rasāyana</s>.
One should put sulfur amounting to one tenth of the mercury into a heated mortar.
He should triturate it for one <s>yāma</s> with the liquids of <s>varā</s>, citron, aloe, and <s>agni</s>.
He should distill it in a distilling apparatus; thus he should do this seven times.

children.text: sagandhakaṃ mardanaṃ ca pātanaṃ bhavati priye
children.translated_text: The trituration and distillation with sulfur then takes place, my dear.
O goddess, the mercury becomes purified and fit for operations with mercury.
With sesame oil, buffalo urine, and sour wine-vinegar,
cinnabar should be cooked together with beef in an iron vessel over a graduated fire.
For seven days one should repeatedly stir that liquid with an iron rod.
While it is moist, he should process it with peacock bile in the sun for a day.
He should distill the <s>darada</s> in a distilling apparatus with a fierce fire.
In four <s>yāmas</s> it becomes purified; the mercury is a carrier of efficacy.

children.text: śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi jāraṇārhaṃ biḍaṃ priye
children.translated_text: Listen, O goddess; I shall explain, my dear, the <s>biḍa</s> suitable for digestion.
Having powdered burnt conch, processed in heat with <s>arka</s> latex,

children.text: kuryāddinaṃ tato devi dhūmasāraṃ ca bhāvayet
children.translated_text: one should treat it for a day, O goddess; then he should process it with <s>dhūmasāra</s>.
For a day, in the extremely intense sun, he should process it with citron juices.
With goat urine for four <s>yāmas</s>, <s>suvarcala</s> should be one sixteenth part.
O fair-faced one, it should be boiled until it reaches thickness.
In human urine, in sixteen parts, <s>kaṇṭakārī</s> together with its root
should be carefully boiled until it becomes thick.
<s>Tintriṇī</s> alkali, green vitriol, <s>sarja</s> alkali, and <s>śilājatu</s>,
all separately, should be processed with citron juices for four <s>yāmas</s>.
<s>Jepāla</s> stripped of its outer skin, radish alkali, rock salt,
<s>guñjā</s>, and borax should each be processed separately with the liquids of <s>śigru</s>.
The thirteen substances beginning with conch should be processed with the liquids of citrons.

children.text: sarvaṃ samāṃśaṃ ca dinamekīkṛtya tu gālitam ||
children.translated_text: All should be combined in equal parts for a day and then filtered.
It should always be kept; it is known by the name <s>Vaḍabānala</s>.
It is to be used for the digestion of gold and other metals, and also of gems,
and, with care, of mica and the other secondary minerals.
One should grind purified mercury and purified sulfur in equal quantity with cow ghee.
When it has become a lump, he should place it inside an aloe leaf.
Having wrapped it properly with thread, he should place it in a lodestone crucible.

children.text: nirudhya taṃ mṛdupuṭe tridhā pācyaṃ punaḥ priye
children.translated_text: After sealing it, my dear, he should cook it three times with a mild <s>puṭa</s>.
Taking it out, enclosing it in a firm crucible, the wise man should heat it with bellows.
The king of mercury becomes ash and is fit for alchemical practice and <s>rasāyana</s>.
One should dry vegetables and ripe fruits in the shade.
He should grind them with <s>arka</s> latex, and with that smear the inside of the crucible.
The scraped powder from the afterbirth of a cow that has first calved
should then be put in the middle of the crucible, along with mercury, sulfur, and that powder.
After putting these in, sealing, and heating, the mercury becomes ash.
<s>Vandhyā</s>, <s>kārkoṭakī</s>, <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>, <s>kaṭutumbikā</s>,
<s>kañcukī</s>, <s>nalikā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>kālamañjarī</s>,
and <s>kākajaṅghā</s>: having pounded all these, he should put them inside a crucible.
With the eight chief herbs beginning with the previously mentioned <s>vandhyā</s>, he should grind the mercury.

children.text: tadrasaṃ liptamūṣāyāṃ kṣiptvā ruddhvā ca bhūdhare
children.translated_text: Putting that mercury into a smeared crucible, closing it, and placing it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus,
he should cook it in this way eight times. Thus the smearing of the crucible,

children.text: mardanaṃ dhamanaṃ kuryād bhūyo bhūyaḥ sureśvari
children.translated_text: the grinding, and the heating should be done again and again, O queen of the gods.

children.text: mṛto bhavati sūtendro yogyo roge rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: The lord of mercury becomes dead, fit for disease-treatment and <s>rasāyana</s>.
The mercury should be firmly ground for four <s>yāmas</s> with regulating herbs.
It should be cooked slowly over a mild fire in twice its amount of sulfur oil.
He should cook the mercury in this way until it reaches the state of a solid globule.

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ saṃpuṭe lauhe kṣiptvā rundhyāddṛḍhaṃ sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise man should put that globule into an iron crucible-pair and close it tightly.
Grinding iron dross with the waters of <s>pathyā</s>, he should smear the crucible-pair.

children.text: tasyordhvaṃ śrāvake kācaṃ kṛtvā nāgaṃ vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Above it, having placed glass in a saucer, he should put in lead.
O my dear, he should heat it in this way until that lead melts.
The wise man should not heat it beyond the point before it goes to hardness.
When hardness has again been reached, he should heat it repeatedly as described before.
By heating in this way for three <s>yāmas</s>, the mercury becomes ash.
When mercury has been calcined with herbs but is devoid of digestion,

children.text: dehe lohe na yojyaḥ syādyojyo bheṣajakarmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: it should not be applied to the body or to metals; it should be used in medicinal work.

children.text: dviguṇe gandhataile ca śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ vimardayet
children.translated_text: One should grind purified mercury in twice its amount of sulfur oil.
Having ground it again for one day, he should also take <s>sarpākṣī</s> and <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>,

children.text: viṣṇukrāntā tryahaṃ caiṣāṃ rasaiḥ ślakṣṇaṃ vimardayet
children.translated_text: and <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>; with their juices he should grind it smooth for three days.
He should cook it eight times in the three-jointed apparatus, my dear.
The lord of mercury becomes ash, destroying masses of diseases.
Mercury should be ground for three days with juices from the root of white <s>aṅkola</s>.
He should place it in a crucible, seal it, and cook it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus.
Mercury goes to the state of ash, a supreme remover of all diseases.
One should grind <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s> and <s>vedikā</s> with sour gruel.
With that paste the mercury, risen after being stupefied seven times, should be ground.
Putting that mercury in a saucer, he should sprinkle it repeatedly with those juices.
He should cook it for a day with the fire of a lamp; the ash becomes like salt.
He should process <s>somarāmaṭha</s> with the latex of <s>kākoduṃbarikā</s>.
Again and again, seven times in this way, the wise man should dry and grind it.
He should put the five-limbed whole plant of <s>kākodumbara</s> into sixteen parts of water.
When one part remains, he should grind that asafoetida with it.

children.text: tadgolake rasaṃ kṣiptvā mūṣāyāṃ taṃ ca rodhayet
children.translated_text: Having put mercury into that pellet, he should enclose it in a crucible,
and then, in the <s>bhūdhara</s> heating pit, he should heat it thus eight times again and again.

children.text: puṭe puṭe ca taddhiṅgu dadyātsūto mṛto bhavet
children.translated_text: At each heating he should add that <s>hiṅgu</s>; the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) becomes dead.
He should also use seeds of <s>urubūka</s> and those born from <s>apāmārga</s>.

children.text: pūrṇayet tacca mūṣāyāṃ kṣiptvā sūtaṃ tataḥ kṣipet
children.translated_text: He should fill the crucible with that and, after putting in the <s>sūta</s>, should then put it in.
Above that he should place the former powder and properly seal the crucible.
If he cooks it with small heatings in this way, in four rounds it goes to the state of ash.
Inside the tuber of <s>kuḍuhuñcī</s>, soaked with a beloved woman's breast milk,

children.text: rasaṃ kṣiptvā mukhaṃ ruddhvā tanmajjakalkataḥ sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: the wise man should put the mercury, close the opening, and seal it with a paste of that tuber's pith.
Smearing it all over with cow dung, he should steam it with a cow-dung fire.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte saptavāraṃ raso bhasmatvam āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: When this has been done seven times, the mercury obtains the state of ash.

children.text: aṅkolasya śiphānīraiḥ sūtaṃ gandhaṃ samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: With water from the roots of <s>aṅkola</s>, he should take equal parts of <s>sūta</s> and sulfur,
grind them for one day, and seal them inside a crucible.
He should heat it in the apparatus called <s>bhūdhara</s>; at the end of the day ash is produced.
He should take equal parts of <s>sūta</s> and <s>dhānyābhraka</s> (processed mica), with fluids made from killing drugs,
grind them for one day, and with those pastes smear a cloth.

children.text: tadvastraṃ vartikāṃ kṛtvā dhṛtvā daṃśena dīpayet
children.translated_text: Having made that cloth into a wick, held with tongs, he should light it.

children.text: taddrutiṃ patitāṃ kāṃsye kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ ca tadbhavet ||
children.translated_text: The melted substance that falls into bronze becomes black in color.
Again it should be ground with killing drugs and cooked in a distillation apparatus.
In one day it becomes dead; its ash removes every disease.
Mercury should be ground with oil of black <s>dhuttūra</s>,
and then ground for one day with restraining agents in the tortoise apparatus.
He should cook it; it goes to the state of ash, becomes white, and removes all diseases.
He should grind purified sulfur, half the quantity of purified <s>sūta</s>,
with liquids made from killing drugs, and cook it for a day inside a crucible.
In the apparatus called <s>bhūdhara</s>, within one day it turns to ash.
O beloved, he should grind <s>sūta</s> and mica with banyan milk for three watches.
Placing it inside a crucible, he should cook it for a day in a cow-dung fire.
The lordly <s>sūta</s> becomes ash, white, and the destroyer of all affliction.
When mercury has been opened and impregnated, he should digest into it an equal amount of gold

children.text: jārayet pūrvayogena tato gandhaṃ samaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: by the previous method, and then add an equal amount of sulfur.
The mercury, held in a crucible, should be ground for a day with juices of divine herbs.
By day and by night he should cook it in a cow-dung fire, or heat it with a husk fire.
Having taken it out, he should steam it again with products of divine herbs.
With seeds arising from them, in equal portions, it should be thoroughly ground for four watches, O queen of the gods.
Placed in a diamond crucible, it should be blown upon; the mercury becomes ash.

children.text: tadbhasma divyaṃ yuñjīta sadā roge rasāyane
children.translated_text: One should always use that divine ash in disease and in <s>rasāyana</s> therapy.
In mercury in which gold has been digested, he should grind an equal amount of gold with an acid.
When it has become a paste, he should wash it with sour gruel, take it, and again

children.text: piṣṭyardhaṃ śuddhagandhaṃ ca tadardhaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: add half as much purified sulfur and half that amount of borax to the paste.
He should add turmeric equal to all of it and grind it for a day with the red fluid of a woman's menses.
At the end of the day he should make that into a pellet.

children.text: paced gaḍḍukayantre ca dinaṃ mandāgninā sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man should cook it in the <s>gaḍḍuka</s> apparatus for a day with gentle fire.
Taking it out and pulverizing it, he should add sulfur equal to it.
It should be cooked in the womb-apparatus for three days with a gentle husk fire.
O goddess, the mercury becomes ash; it is non-rising and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
O beloved, he should take three <s>karṣas</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> and one <s>karṣa</s> of copper powder.

children.text: amlaiḥ saṃmardayedgāḍhaṃ dinaṃ khalve tato bhavet ||
children.translated_text: He should grind it strongly with sour substances for a day in a mortar; then it becomes
a paste. He should wash it with waters, and then take the clean material.
He should take pyrite essence, all of that with juices of <s>cakramarda</s> leaves,
and grind that paste strongly for three days in a womb-apparatus.
O goddess, he should cook it with a husk fire for three days, or day and night.
In a cow-dung fire, <s>sūta</s>-ash is produced, removing disease and old age.

children.text: sūtaṃ svarṇaṃ vyomasatvaṃ samaṃ svarṇasamaṃ biḍam ||
children.translated_text: He should take equal parts of <s>sūta</s>, gold, and sky-essence, and a flux equal to the gold.
He should grind all of it in a mortar for a day with juices of plantain stalks.
Then, with seeds produced from divine herbs in equal measure, for two days
he should grind it together with plantain water in a womb-apparatus.
He should cook it by the previous procedure; good mercury-ash is produced,
destroying old age, death, and disease, and bestowing every siddhi.
He should grind <s>rasendra</s> and essence of <s>vimalā</s> in equal parts for three days
with juices of <s>sinduvāra</s> leaves. A paste is produced; he should put it
inside a glass bottle, and smear the bottle with seven layers of clay and cloth.
He should dry it and cook it for a day in a sand apparatus with gentle fire.
Divine mercury-ash is produced, removing disease, old age, and death.
He should take two <s>karṣas</s> of <s>rasendra</s> and half that amount of purified sulfur.
He should grind all of it for a day with pyrite essence in the amount of the sulfur.
And with the essential juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> leaves, O beloved, he should put that pellet
inside a crucible; then, after closing the mouth of the crucible, he should place it.
He should cook that crucible in the <s>gaḍḍuka</s> apparatus for a day with gentle fire.
Divine mercury-ash is produced, resembling vermilion in redness,
destroying old age, death, and disease, auspicious, and bestowing every siddhi.
In the belly of a baked crucible, mercury enclosed with an equal amount of sulfur
should again be given four times as much juice of <s>kākamācī</s> as those two.
Having covered it and placed that in the <s>gaḍḍuka</s> apparatus, he should cook it in due sequence.
In the fire called mild, medium, and fierce, for four watches,
then the auspicious ash of <s>rasa</s> becomes a destroyer of all diseases.
One should grind the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) for a day with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>; in its absence,

children.text: amlavallyā rasair eva taṃ rasaṃ gandhakaiḥ samam ||
children.translated_text: with the juices of <s>amlavallī</s> alone, that <s>rasa</s> together with an equal quantity of sulphur.
Having placed it in a womb-apparatus, the wise man should cook it as before.
This <s>rasa</s> becomes killed, and it becomes a remover of all diseases.
One should take <s>guñjā</s> fruit equal to the <s>rasa</s>, with honey, borax, and <s>yāvaka</s>,
combine it with the juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s> leaves, and grind it for one day.
After covering it in a diamond-crucible, one should blow upon it with a mild fire.
This <s>rasa</s>, resembling the moon, is rejuvenating and virility-giving.
One should take equal purified sulphur and <s>rasa</s>, with the liquids of <s>kīṭamāriṇikā</s>,
or with those of <s>ajamārī</s> and <s>ahimārī</s>, or with the juice of white <s>aṅkola</s>.
One should grind it for three days and then place it in an earthen sealed capsule.
One should cook it for one day in a cow-dung fire, or for three days in a husk fire.
Then <s>sūta-bhasma</s> is produced, removing disease and old age.
O dear one, the mercury purified by the method of distillation over copper and mica,
should be ground with an equal amount of diamond ash and with the liquids of <s>haṃsapādī</s>.
The inside of a diamond-crucible should be smeared with seeds produced from divine herbs.
Having placed the previous <s>rasa</s> in it, one should seal it and then cook it for three days.
After that, having removed it from the husk fire, one should add molten mercury equal to it.
One should grind everything with the juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s> for three days; then,
one should cook it as before. This <s>rasa</s> certainly becomes ash.
It destroys old age, death, and disease, is auspicious, and grants all siddhis.
One <s>karṣa</s> of prepared mercury, and eight <s>guñjās</s> of gold,
with four <s>guñjās</s> of killed diamond, should be ground with the juices of <s>haṃsapadī</s>.
Having put it in a heated mortar and placed it inside a diamond-crucible, one should seal it.

children.text: paced bhūdharayantre ca punarādāya taṃ rasam
children.translated_text: One should cook it in the <s>bhūdhara-yantra</s>, and then, taking that <s>rasa</s> out again,
it should be ground with the liquids of <s>haṃsapādī</s> in a heated mortar for three days.

children.text: pūrvavad bhūdhare yantre pacettaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: One should cook it again and again in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus as before.
When one has thus given it one hundred puṭa firings, the ash becomes red in color.
It destroys old age, death, and poverty, and it destroys worldly existence.
There should be four parts of purified <s>sūta</s> and one part of copper powder.
One should grind it for a day in a sour liquid, wash it, and take up the paste.
Ore-essence equal to the paste should be ground with the liquids of <s>cakramarda</s> leaves.
One should grind everything for three days and put the pellet in a womb-apparatus.

children.text: nikṣipya tridinaṃ pācyaṃ tuṣāgnau vā sureśvari ||
children.translated_text: Having deposited it there, it should be cooked for three days in a husk fire, O queen of the gods.
One should cook it day and night in a cow-dung fire; the <s>rasa</s> becomes ash.
Opened <s>rasa</s>, mica-essence, and gold, these three in equal quantity,
should be ground with plantain fluid for a day, with <s>biḍa</s> salt equal to all of them.
Then it should be ground for three days with the seeds of divine herbs.
Afterward one should cook it in a womb-apparatus in a cow-dung fire; it becomes killed.
Mercury that has been fully digested, together with an equal amount of <s>vimalā</s>, should be treated with the juices of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>.
After grinding it for three days, one should place it in a glass bottle.
It should be cooked in a sand apparatus for four watches; it is reduced to ash.

children.text: tāpyasatvaṃ samaṃ gandhaṃ dvābhyāṃ tulyaṃ ca jāritam
children.translated_text: Ore-essence, an equal amount of sulphur, and <s>jārita</s> mercury equal to the two,

children.text: sūtaṃ nirguṇḍikāṃ mardya dinaṃ tadgolakaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be ground with <s>nirguṇḍikā</s> for one day; then that pellet again
should be sealed in a diamond-crucible, and one should blow upon it, or cook it in the <s>gaḍḍu-yantra</s>.
When cooked it becomes red in color; that <s>rasa</s> removes all diseases.
Inexhaustibility, non-revivability, non-adhesion, and being a good ash,
as well as the power to kill metals, should be observed in <s>rasa-bhasma</s>.
Having powdered purified sulphur, one should subject it to treatment with the juice of the aforementioned leaves,

children.text: saptadhā bhāvayed gharme strīṇāṃ ca rajasā tathā ||
children.translated_text: seven times in the sun, and likewise with women's menstrual blood.
Likewise, one should agitate the sulphur again with human bile.
One should place one <s>pala</s> of purified <s>rasa</s> in a potsherd in the sunlight.
Above it, one should place the agitated sulphur and rub it with the thumb.
One should do this; the <s>sūta</s> becomes a paste that grants success in all operations.
Purified sulphur, O goddess, with the juice of sesame leaves,
should be ground seven times, dried in the shade, and then treated successively.
One should place one <s>pala</s> of purified mercury in a crucible.
Then one should place a pellet of gold weighing a <s>niṣka</s> in the crucible.
There one should add a measured quantity of a woman's menstrual blood, urine, and excrement.
One should set that crucible in the middle of a sand apparatus, O <s>Śive</s>.
Little by little, again and again, one should put in the aforementioned sulphur.
One should cook it with a mild fire until a <s>karṣa</s> of sulphur is digested.
After taking it down and letting it cool naturally, one should remove the gold pellet.
It becomes a divine gold paste, bestowing all desired things.
One should treat purified sulphur one hundred times with the waters of <s>markaṭī</s>.

children.text: chāyāyāṃ śuddhasūtaṃ ca gharme mṛtkarpare kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: In the shade, one should place purified <s>sūta</s> in a clay potsherd in the sunlight.
One should sprinkle in a little of the previous sulphur and the juice of <s>markaṭī</s>.

children.text: jīrṇe gandhe dravaṃ deyaṃ muhur gandhaṃ muhurdravam ||
children.translated_text: When the sulphur has been digested, liquid should be given; again sulphur, again liquid.

children.text: yāvatpādāṃśakaṃ jīrṇaṃ gandhaṃ ca piṣṭikā bhavet
children.translated_text: Until one quarter-part of sulphur has been digested, and a paste has formed,
that divine paste is fit for all operations and is hard to obtain even for the gods.
Having powdered purified sulphur, one should wash it three times with <s>kāñjika</s>,
three times with sour <s>jambīra</s>, and with the juice of <s>haṃsapādī</s>.
Having washed it seven times in this way, one should treat camphor separately.
with the waters of <s>śvetādrikarṇikā</s>, three times in the sunlight.
One should smear two guñjās' measure of camphor inside the apparatus.

children.text: tatra gandhaṃ sārdhaniṣkaṃ bhāvitaṃ cūrṇitaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: There one should put in one and a half niṣkas of treated, powdered <s>gandha</s> (sulfur).

children.text: tadūrdhvaṃ ca palaṃ sūtaṃ nikṣipettasya pṛṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: Above that he should place one pala of <s>sūta</s> (mercury), on top of it.
Above that should go camphor in the same measure as before, and above that one and a half niṣkas

children.text: gandhakaṃ ca punaḥ kṣiptvā tato gomūtrakena ca
children.translated_text: of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) again; then, with cow urine,
he should grind the root of <s>śvetādrikarṇikā</s>, and with that paste
cover it with that dish, seal it, and cook it gradually.
Afterward, in the <s>jālikāyantra</s> (grill apparatus), he should take out the excellent product.

children.text: evaṃ kuryāttrivāraṃ ca gandhapiṣṭir bhaved dhruvam
children.translated_text: He should do this three times, and a <s>gandhapiṣṭi</s> (sulfur paste) will surely result.
In a mortar smeared with oil he should place one pala of purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury).

children.text: karṣaṃ ca śodhitaṃ gandhaṃ devadālīdravaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: He should add one karṣa of purified <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) and the juice of <s>devadālī</s>.

children.text: karāṅgulyā khare gharme mardayet piṣṭikā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: With a finger of the hand, in strong heat, he should grind it; it will become a <s>piṣṭikā</s> (paste).

children.text: tāmrakhalve palaṃ sūtaṃ karṣārdhaṃ gandhakaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: In a copper mortar he should put one pala of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and half a karṣa of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur).
He should cook it over a gentle fire for one yāma, stirring it with the thumb.
A marvelous <s>gandhapiṣṭi</s> (sulfur paste) results, auspicious and effective for every operation.
I shall explain the <s>stambhana</s> (stabilizing) of the pastes, produced with bitter <s>kośātakī</s>.
The seed and the tuber of <s>caṇḍālinī</s>, in equal parts, with milk from a woman's breasts,

children.text: kṣīraiḥ piṣṭvā ca tāṃ piṣṭīṃ lepayedaṅgulaṃ dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: should be ground with the milk, and that paste should be coated firmly to a finger's thickness.
In a <s>vandhyākanda</s> tuber, or in a <s>kṣīrakanda</s> tuber, or in one produced from <s>sūraṇa</s>,

children.text: kande vā vajrakande vā kande vā kuḍuhuñcije ||
children.translated_text: or in a <s>vajrakanda</s> tuber, or in a <s>kuḍuhuñcī</s> tuber,
one should place that paste and seal the opening with the corresponding pith.
Having smeared that tuber with clay, he should roast it in the <s>bhūdharayantra</s> (earth-mound apparatus).
By day and night, in a dung fire, there should be turning above and below.

children.text: yathā kandaṃ tu na dahettathā pākakramaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The method of cooking is taught so that the tuber does not burn.

children.text: atha piṣṭiṃ samānīyād bhavetsā stambhitā priye
children.translated_text: Then he should bring out the paste; it becomes stabilized, dear one.

children.text: piṣṭīnāṃ stambhitānāṃ ca jāraṇā vakṣyate śive ||
children.translated_text: And now, O <s>Śive</s>, the <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) of the stabilized pastes will be taught.
In an iron <s>stanayantra</s> (breast-shaped apparatus), <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) equal to the paste
should be put above, O <s>Deveśi</s>, together with the stabilized sulfur paste.

children.text: tadūrdhvaṃ piṣṭitulyaṃ ca gandhakaṃ cūrṇitaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Above that one should put powdered <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) equal to the paste.
Having sealed it in the <s>bhūdharayantra</s> (earth-mound apparatus), he should cook it and digest it in order.
<s>Gandha</s> (sulfur) should be added again and again, in this way up to a hundredfold, dear one.
When a hundredfold amount of sulfur has been digested, he should collect the paste from the apparatus.
For all sulfur pastes this is the <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion), and also the <s>rañjana</s> (coloring).
I shall explain the <s>māraṇa</s> (calcination) procedure for the digested pastes.
Having put the digested sulfur paste into a heated mortar,
and having ground it with the juices of divine herbs, he should make a pellet for one day.
After grinding the seeds of divine herbs with fresh juices produced from divine herbs,
he should coat the earlier pellet inside a <s>vajramūṣā</s> (hard crucible).
Having placed it there and sealed the mouth of the crucible, he should cook it in the <s>bhūdharayantra</s> (earth-mound apparatus),
again turning it upward and downward for one day, dear one.
Having taken it out, as before he should grind it with the previous liquids,
and roast it by the <s>puṭa</s> method as before, O goddess, ten times in this sequence.
Without doubt the sulfur paste is calcined and becomes capable of every operation.
The <s>rasabhasma</s> (mercurial ashes) produced by the sulfur-paste procedure, O <s>Bhairavi</s>,
are foremost in all operations, especially in the work of <s>vāda</s> (transmutation).
I shall now tell the bindings of <s>rasa</s> (mercury); listen, O <s>Bhairavi</s>.
One should put ten niṣkas of purified <s>pārada</s> (mercury) into a mortar.

children.text: niṣkaikaṃ śuddhagandhaṃ ca svalpaṃ svalpaṃ vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: A single niṣka of purified <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) should be added little by little.
He should pound and grind it with a stone; within the measure of one yāma, a paste will arise.
In a <s>kṣīrakanda</s> tuber, or in a <s>vandhyākanda</s> tuber, or in <s>kuḍuhuñcī</s>,
or in a ripe, auspicious tuber, he should deposit the sulfur paste.
The wise man should place half a niṣka of <s>vaikrānta</s> ash above and below.

children.text: tatkandamajjayā vaktraṃ nirudhya ca mṛdā bahiḥ
children.translated_text: With the pith of that tuber he should seal the opening, and outside with clay
he should smear it to a finger's measure; then he should dry it on all sides.
He should cook it eight times in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus with a <s>kaukkuṭa</s> heating,
in a dung fire, again making the upper part lower, dear one.

children.text: adhobhāgaṃ tathordhvaṃ ca bhūyo bhūyaḥ pravartanam
children.translated_text: Likewise the lower part should be turned upward, with repeated turning again and again.
Thus for one day; afterward he should cook it with paired dung cakes.
The <s>pārada</s> (mercury) becomes bound, resembling ripe pomegranate seeds.
It is named <s>vaikrāntabaddha</s> (bound with vaikrānta); when powdered, it is a <s>yogavāhaka</s> (catalytic carrier).

children.text: pūrvoktāṃ gandhapiṣṭīṃ tāṃ vastre baddhvātha saṃpuṭe
children.translated_text: Having tied that previously described sulfur paste in a cloth, then in an iron
lidded vessel he should place the pouch, with equal sulfur above and below.
Having properly sealed the lidded vessel, he should cook it in the <s>bhūdharayantra</s> (earth-mound apparatus),

children.text: yathā jīrṇo bhavedgandho bhūyo bhūyastathāpi ca ||
children.translated_text: so that the sulfur becomes digested; and thus again and again.
In this way sulfur six times the amount is to be digested, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>.
This <s>gandhakabaddha</s> (sulfur-bound) <s>rasa</s> (mercury) removes all diseases.
Sixteen finger-breadths long and as broad as a citron fruit,
a fired crucible, very firm, should be set in the middle of a sand apparatus.
One should make it sunk for three parts, with a quarter part remaining outside.
Into it one should put one pala of sulfur-mercury compound, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
Above the mercury he should place two palas of purified <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur),
and seal its mouth properly; with a gentle fire
he should cook it until it is smokeless; when the smoke has gone, again
It should be filled with the juices of <s>kākamācī</s>; when digestion has taken place in that liquid,
it is to be filled again, dear one, with the juice of <s>nāgavallī</s>.
It should be filled with the juices of <s>unmattaka</s> and cooked slowly over a gentle fire.
Until the sulfur is digested by the juices beginning with <s>kākamācī</s>,
one should cook it in this way up to <s>dhattūra</s>; the mercury becomes bound.
This is called sulfur-bound; one should apply it in all formulations.
First, as before, the skilled practitioner should prepare the sulfur paste.
The mercury should be seven and a half <s>niṣkas</s>, and the purified gold one and a half.
It should be triturated with sour liquid for one <s>yāma</s>; this is known as gold paste.
Having enclosed the sulfur paste externally with an equal gold paste,
in an iron covered vessel shaped like a breast and bound with cloth,

children.text: kṛtvā tāṃ piṣṭikāṃ kṣiptvā piṣṭyūrdhvādhaśca gandhakam
children.translated_text: having made that paste and placed it inside, he should put sulfur above and below the paste.
The wise man should add an equal amount everywhere and seal the joint with sour liquid and salts.

children.text: pacedbhūdharayantre ca jīrṇe jīrṇe punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: He should cook it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus, and when it is digested, again and again,
he should add six times as much sulfur; then he should slowly remove the cloth.

children.text: samāṃśaṃ gandhakaṃ bhūyo bhūyo jāryaṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Again and again, sulfur in equal quantity should be digested slowly and gradually.
He must not remove the sulfur completely; otherwise the mercury will be lost.
When in this way one hundred times its quantity has been digested, he should collect the sulfur paste.
He should place the paste in a covered vessel made of gold equal in amount to it.
After grinding glass with the juices of <s>kanyā</s>, he should coat the outside to the thickness of one finger.
Then, having coated it with borax, and afterwards successively with clay and salts,
each coating should be made, and it should be wrapped to the measure of one finger.
Each coating should be dried, and it should be blown in the furnace apparatus.
With a crooked tube and intense fire, it should remain for one <s>prahara</s>.
It becomes a lump like the rising sun, a divine <s>rasāyana</s>.
This sulfur-gold binding destroys old age, disease, and poverty.

children.text: athavā gandhapiṣṭiṃ tāṃ vastre baddhvātha gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: Alternatively, having tied that sulfur paste in cloth, then adding sulfur

children.text: tulyaṃ dattvā nirudhyātha saṃpuṭe lohaje dṛḍham
children.translated_text: in equal amount and then sealing it firmly in an iron covered vessel,
one should heat it in that <s>bhūdhara</s> until the sulfur is digested.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punardeyaṃ yāvadgandhaṃ tu ṣaḍguṇam
children.translated_text: Thus it should be added again and again until the sulfur is sixfold.
In this way, bound in sulfur, the mercury conquers all diseases.
One should triturate mercury for a day with liquids made from the root of <s>kārkoṭī</s>.
He should place that triturated mercury in a lump made from the root of <s>markaṭī</s>.

children.text: taṃ piṇḍaṃ vajramūṣāyāṃ ruddhvā tīvrāgninā pacet
children.translated_text: Having sealed that lump in a diamond crucible, he should cook it with intense fire.
This becomes bound as a lump, auspicious and able to accomplish every work.
He should grind the root of <s>arka</s> with the milks of <s>ravi</s> and coat a crucible with it.

children.text: tanmadhye rañjitaṃ sūtaṃ kṣiptvā baddhvātha rodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed the colored mercury in the middle of it, he should bind and seal it.
He should seal that in an earthen covered vessel and in an iron covered vessel.
Afterwards he should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; the mercury obtains binding.
One should triturate mercury for three days with the juices of <s>jalakumbhī</s>.
Having made a crucible from leaves of <s>jalakumbhī</s>, he should place the mercury there.
Having sealed that in a diamond crucible and dried it in the shade, he should heat it lightly.
With cow-dung cakes, increasing one by one, he should cook it by thirty heatings.
Then it should be put in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; the mercury becomes properly bound.
Purified mercury should be triturated for a day with the liquids of <s>ekavīrā</s>.
He should coat a diamond crucible with the paste of <s>ekavīrā</s> tuber.

children.text: tasyāṃ pūrvarasaṃ kṣiptvā dhmāte baddho bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having placed the previously treated mercury in it and blown it, the mercury becomes bound.
With liquids arising from red milky tubers, combined with women's breast milk,
mercury should be triturated for three days, and for three days with the liquids of <s>vajrakanda</s>.
He should coat a diamond crucible with the paste of <s>kṣīrakanda</s>.

children.text: tatra pūrvarasaṃ baddhvā dhmāte baddho bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having bound the previously treated mercury there and blown it, the mercury becomes bound.
Having ground the root and fruit of <s>arka</s>, he should coat a crucible with it.
In the middle of it he should place a crucible made from the root of <s>puṅkhā</s>.
In the middle of that, having placed mercury, with substances arising from the root of <s>puṅkhā</s>,
he should fill the crucible with the juices and firmly seal its mouth.
Having thus made the crucible closed, he should put it in the middle of a covered vessel.
Then he should carefully coat it with salt and likewise with clay.
Then, by the application of heating, that mercury obtains binding.
Powdered with <s>citraka</s> juice and rock salt, in the amount of two <s>rājikās</s>,
and eaten in the morning, it destroys all diseases.
One should triturate mercury for one <s>yāma</s> with water from the roots of <s>kapittha</s>.
In another blind crucible, he should seal the mercury crucible.

children.text: tathā dhamettato mūṣāṃ yathā sindūravad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Then he should blow that crucible so that it becomes like vermilion.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte rasendro'sau badhyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When this is done, that lord of mercury is bound; there is no doubt about it.
This is declared to be the herbal binding of <s>rasendra</s>.
Thus these mercuries are killed, stupefied, and brought into binding.
Applied individually there with formulations, they become carriers of the preparation.
Now the method of stupefaction for purified mercury is stated.
One should triturate the mercury with <s>meghanāda</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, and garlic.

children.text: dinaṃ piṣṭaṃ tu tadgolaṃ hiṅgunā veṣṭayedbahiḥ
children.translated_text: That ball, ground for a day, should be wrapped externally with <s>hiṅgu</s>.
It should be cooked for one day in a salt apparatus with fierce fire.
One should take what has adhered above and bind it firmly with cloth.

children.text: ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ tulyaṃ dattvā somānale pacet ||
