children.translated_text: Having placed equal sulfur above and below, he should cook it in the <s>somānala</s> apparatus.

children.text: jīrṇe gandhaṃ punardeyaṃ ṣaḍbhirvāraiḥ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: When it is digested, sulfur should be added again, in six turns, equal amount by equal amount.

children.text: ṣaḍguṇe gandhake jīrṇe mūrchito rogahā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When sixfold <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) has been digested into it, the stupefied mercury becomes a remover of disease.

children.text: gandhakaṃ dhūmasāraṃ ca śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: One should take <s>gandhaka</s>, <s>dhūmasāra</s>, and purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury), each in equal measure.
He should grind them in a mortar for one <s>yāma</s> and place them in a glass bottle.
Having sealed it, he should cook it for twelve <s>yāmas</s> in a sand apparatus.
When it has cooled by itself, he should break it open and discard the sulfur that is above.
Taking the mercury that is below, he should employ it in all formulations.

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ tathā gandhaṃ sūtārdhaṃ saindhave kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: He should put purified <s>sūta</s>, likewise sulfur, and rock salt equal to half the mercury.
With the liquids of white <s>jayantī</s> he should grind it for three days.

children.text: kṛtvā golaṃ tu saṃśoṣya mūṣāyāṃ taṃ nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made a pellet and dried it, he should seal it inside a crucible.

children.text: śoṣayitvā dhamet kiṃcit sutapte'tha jale kṣipet
children.translated_text: After drying it, he should heat it a little; when it is well heated, he should throw it into water.
Extracting the mercury from that, impregnated with the juice of <s>trikanda</s>,
he should use it in all diseases, or heat it and cook it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus.

children.text: rasārdhaṃ gandhakaṃ mardyaṃ ghṛtairyuktaṃ tu golakam ||
children.translated_text: Sulfur half the amount of mercury should be ground and made into a pellet mixed with ghee.
Having made it, he should bind it in cloth and cook it placed in a <s>ḍolāyantra</s> apparatus.
It should remain there in cow urine for one <s>yāma</s>, and in human urine for three days.
He should dry it, bind it again with cloths, wrap it firmly with clay,
and, when dry, seal it in a crucible and then cook it with a husk fire.
He should turn the upper part downward and the lower part upward,
and by such repeated reversals he should steam it for three days.
Afterward, having taken out that mercury, it is a carrier for compounds and a remover of disease.
He should take the feces of a newborn child and seed of <s>palāśa</s>,
the blood of a <s>caṇḍālī</s>, mercury, and borax equal to one quarter of the mercury.
He should grind these with the liquids of <s>jayantī</s> for one day into a pellet.
Then he should coat a copper capsule with ground <s>sahadevī</s>.
Putting the pellet inside it, he should gently heat it for two <s>yāmas</s>,
within a sand apparatus; having taken it out from there, again
he should smear sulfur on the outside with <s>citraka</s> and <s>sahadevī</s>.

children.text: sampuṭaṃ bandhayedvastre mṛdā lepyaṃ ca śoṣayet
children.translated_text: He should bind the capsule in cloth, smear it with clay, and dry it.
Having sealed it in another crucible and heated it, he should retrieve the capsule.
When reduced to a fine powder, the <s>mahārasa</s> removes diseases and acts as a carrier of compounds.
The capsule should be equal in measure to the mercury, according to the procedure seen in the śāstra.
Mercury with a portion of sulfur should be ground for a day with the liquids of <s>dhuttūra</s>.
Placed in a blind crucible and heated in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus, it becomes stupefied in a day.

children.text: kṛtvā ṣaḍaṅgulāṃ mūṣāṃ supakvāṃ mṛṇmayīṃ dṛḍhām
children.translated_text: Having made a strong earthen crucible, well baked and six fingers high,
he should smear the cavity of the crucible with roots produced by round-leaved plants.

children.text: tanmadhye sūtakaṃ kṣiptvā mūṣāṃ pūryāttu taddravaiḥ
children.translated_text: Putting mercury inside it, he should fill the crucible with their liquids.

children.text: ruddhvā tāṃ vālukāyantre cullyāṃ dīpāgninā pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having sealed it, he should cook it in a sand apparatus on a stove with a lamp-flame.
At the end of seven days he should take it out and employ it as a remover of old age.
He should grind the mercury in the sun with thick juices of <s>kuraṇḍaka</s>.
With juices arising from leaves of <s>latākarañja</s>, he should grind it with his big toe.
Stupefied properly in one day, it should be used in all formulations.

children.text: kāsīsaṃ saindhavaṃ sūtaṃ tulyaṃ tulyaṃ vimardayet
children.translated_text: He should grind <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), rock salt, and mercury in equal parts.
If <s>kāsīsa</s> is unavailable, <s>phullatūrikā</s> should be supplied.
He should add it little by little in the mortar and stupefy the three together.
Each should be one hundred <s>niṣkas</s>; it should never be less or more in any case.
He should cook it for a day in a covered-pot apparatus with fierce fire.
Then he should take the auspicious white stupefied substance adhering above.
Now there is another method for purified and stupefied mercury.

children.text: sūtatulyaṃ mṛtaṃ svarṇaṃ dvābhyāṃ tulyaṃ ca gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: Dead gold equal to the mercury, and sulfur equal to the two together, should be used.
It should be ground for a day with the milk of <s>arka</s> and sealed in a <s>bhūdhara</s> heating pit.
In a single day the mercury becomes perfected, called <s>Hairaṇyagarbhaka</s>.
Mercury that is white, red, or black in color, and heavier,
but is capable of rising again, is declared to be stupefied.
<s>Śrī Bhairavī</s>:
What kind of auspicious herb, lord, produces the stupefaction of mercury?

children.text: kena vā bhasma sūtaśca kena vā khoṭabandhanam ||
children.translated_text: By what is mercury made into ash, and by what is binding into a <s>khoṭa</s> accomplished?
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s>:
Listen, <s>Bhairavī</s>, truly, to the secret binding of mercury,
which is not known by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Surendra</s>, and the others, O you revered by the gods.
Between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s> there is a <s>rākṣasa</s> named <s>Prayāga</s>.
On his seat, O fair-hipped one, mercury is bound in an instant.
The best practitioner should take the leaves of the night-roamer.

children.text: tato nipīḍyate devi raso bhavati cottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then they are pressed, O goddess, and the mercury becomes excellent.

children.text: rasaṃ saṃmardya tenaiva dināni trīṇi vārtikaḥ
children.translated_text: Having ground mercury with that very juice for three days, the practitioner
should quickly bind <s>āroṭa</s> and digest <s>gagana</s> (mica) there.
With that same leaf-juice he should again process the sulfur.
When it has been impregnated seven times with that, together with <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: yantre vidyādhare devi gaganaṃ tatra jārayet
children.translated_text: in the <s>vidyādhara</s> apparatus, O goddess, he should digest <s>gagana</s> there.

children.text: māsamātreṇa deveśi jīryate tu samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: In the space of a month, O queen of the gods, it is digested in equal measure.
When the <s>gagana</s> has been digested in equal measure, the mercury becomes capable of hundredfold penetration.
Then, O goddess, he should impregnate sulfur in the juice of the night-roamer.
He should impregnate it seven times with the juice of <s>dvipadī</s> as well.
With a coating on leaves of silver, half by half, there is excellent gold.
When sulfur has been digested equally into this, the mercury becomes capable of hundredfold penetration.
<s>Tālaka</s> should be impregnated seven times with the juices of the night-roamer.

children.text: tenaiva ghātayedvaṅgaṃ nāgaṃ tāre tu nirvahet
children.translated_text: With that one should kill tin and lead, and carry the process through on silver.
One should digest that <s>tāra</s> (silver) in <s>sūta</s> (mercury); that mercury will become bound.

children.text: catuḥ ṣaṣṭitame bhāge śulbavedhaṃ tu dāpayet
children.translated_text: At the sixty-fourth part he should cause it to penetrate <s>śulba</s> (copper).
That portion becomes excellent, granting <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation.
He should make the flowers of <s>niśācara</s> into a fine powder.
Ten palas of the powder should be impregnated with the juices of <s>dhātrī</s>.
It should be stirred with ghee and honey and placed in a new vessel.
It is to be deposited in a heap of grain for three weeks, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
By merely eating that, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair.

children.text: valkalaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu madhunā sahitaṃ lihet ||
children.translated_text: He should lick the fine powder of the bark together with honey.
Through use for half a month, a counteracting application will arise, dear one.
By his urine and feces <s>śulba</s> (copper) becomes gold.
Through use for just a month, <s>pannaga</s> (lead) becomes gold.
One should collect that fruit-oil in the apparatus called <s>Pātāla</s>.

children.text: tena tailena deveśi rasaṃ saṃkocayed budhaḥ
children.translated_text: With that oil, O <s>Deveśi</s>, the wise man should constrict <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
At that very moment, O goddess, the great <s>rasa</s> becomes a tablet-bound preparation.
An amulet and a bracelet should be made, and a <s>rasaliṅga</s>, O beautiful-faced one.
By means of that, constriction and killing are to be performed, most wondrously.
Again I shall explain another very rare binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
There is a herb, mistress of women, which is the mother of the three worlds.
By mere contact with her, <s>pārada</s> (mercury) remains bound.
When this <s>rasa</s> has been ground for seven days with the juices of that great herb,
by penetration with only a hundredth part it produces divine gold.
By grinding it for three weeks in her juice, O best-colored one,
the <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of penetrating one hundred thousand parts and directly pierces the eight metals.
In three weeks, O <s>Deveśi</s>, it penetrates ten lakhs.
And in the fourth week the <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of crore-fold penetration.
By sweating, heating, and rubbing with the juice of the great herb,
it grants the <s>khecarī</s> siddhi, whose range is unobstructed.
At the end of a day he may enjoy a thousand women.
His shadow disappears, he becomes invisible, and he wanders through the three worlds.
By the juice of the great herb alone, revival of the dead takes place.
By this one should kill <s>sūta</s> (mercury); make it have the five states, dear one.

children.text: mṛtasya dāpayennasyaṃ hastau pādau tu mardayet ||
children.translated_text: One should administer it as nasal medicine to the dead person and rub the hands and feet.
The life-breath will enter even that dead person, O beautiful-faced one.
Again I shall explain another very rare binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
By contact with <s>narasāra</s>, the <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) is bound in an instant.
Having put the juice of <s>narasāra</s> into the <s>rasa</s> together with the dust of a two-footed female,
by the end of the day it comes to binding and colors all metals.
One should impregnate <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) with the juice of <s>narasāra</s> alone.

children.text: nirgandhā jāyate sā tu ghātayettena pannagam
children.translated_text: It becomes odorless; with that he should kill <s>pannaga</s> (lead).
Together with the dust of a two-footed female, <s>pannaga</s> becomes restrained.
When sixfold <s>pannaga</s> has been digested with the juice of <s>narasāra</s> alone,

children.text: tāre tāmre'pi vā devi koṭivedhī bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in <s>tāra</s> (silver) or also in copper, O goddess, the <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of crore-fold penetration.
Separately impregnated seven times in <s>narasāra</s> juice and in breast milk,
one should give it as a morsel to <s>rasa</s> in the apparatus called <s>Vidyādhara</s>.

children.text: jīryate gaganaṃ devi nirmukhe ca varānane
children.translated_text: <s>Gagana</s> (mica) is digested, O goddess, without a mouth, O beautiful-faced one.
With the juice of <s>narasāra</s>, O <s>Īśī</s>, and with the juice of the worm-female,
one should liquefy <s>gagana</s> (mica), O goddess, and also <s>tīkṣṇaloha</s> (iron) and <s>pannaga</s> (lead).
With the juice of <s>narasāra</s>, O <s>Īśī</s>, and with the juice of <s>Hanumatī</s>,
by sprinkling, O dear one, <s>bhāskara</s> becomes divine gold.
Putting <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> and red sandalwood into the juice of <s>narasāra</s>,
and with the fresh juices of <s>madayantī</s>, O goddess, he should sprinkle <s>pannaga</s>.
Sprinkled seven times, it instantly becomes divine gold.
Gold joined with one-eighth part is the medicine for gold-making.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) should be impregnated seven times in the juice of <s>narasāra</s>.
With that alone he should kill <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron); it attains the state of ash.

children.text: tadbhasma tāmrapiṣṭe tu triguṇaṃ tena nirvahet ||
children.translated_text: He should process that ash in a copper paste, in a threefold amount, by means of it.
That <s>śulba</s> (copper) has the appearance of gold; or, joined to <s>tāra</s> (silver) in an eighth part,

children.text: tāraṃ hemasamāṃśaṃ tu dvivarṇaṃ patitaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the <s>tāra</s>, with an equal portion of gold, will fall as a two-colored metal.
<s>Rasaka</s> should be impregnated seven times in the juice of <s>narasāra</s>.
Likewise <s>rasendra</s> (mercury) should be treated seven times with the juice of <s>narasāra</s>.

children.text: taṃ rasaṃ rasakaṃ caiva tīkṣṇalohaṃ ca pannagam
children.translated_text: That <s>rasa</s>, the <s>rasaka</s>, the <s>tīkṣṇaloha</s> (iron), and <s>pannaga</s> (lead)
should be ground together in one place with the juice of <s>narasāra</s> alone.
At once there arises a binding of both the <s>rasa</s> and the <s>rasaka</s>.

children.text: tīkṣṇanāgaṃ tathā śulbaṃ rasakena tu rañjayet ||
children.translated_text: He should color <s>tīkṣṇanāga</s> and likewise <s>śulba</s> (copper) with <s>rasaka</s>.
Immediately that becomes gold, with the luster of a pumpkin flower.
Again I shall explain another very rare binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
There is a herb named <s>Kaṅkālakhecarī</s>, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
Its oil should be collected, joined with the first <s>khecarī</s>.
He should keep it for one day in a vessel made of <s>bhāskara</s>.

children.text: dvitīye vāsare prāpte vajraratnaṃ tu ghātayet ||
children.translated_text: When the second day has arrived, he should kill the diamond-jewel.
He should blow it in the fire, well heated and shining with a blazing brilliance.
A certain bush-creeper herb, with its seeds, should be taken, dear one.
The third <s>khecarī</s>, O goddess, is named <s>Mantrasiṃhāsanī</s>.
In the <s>Pātāla</s> apparatus he should collect its oil in a copper vessel.
Into the middle of that oil he should pour the <s>khecarī</s> juice.
And he should place it in the middle of the <s>Medinī</s> apparatus, O beautiful-faced one.
In the previous herb, O goddess, the <s>gagana</s> (mica) in <s>medinī</s>-water...

children.text: rase māsaṃ tato dattvā mardanād golakaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: After placing it in mercury for a month, then make a pellet by grinding.
Having tied it into a packet, with that one should digest <s>gagana</s> (mica), dear one.

children.text: same tu gagane jīrṇe baddhastiṣṭhati pāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When an equal amount of <s>gagana</s> has been digested, the mercury remains bound.
Even when it is blown with bellows, it does not perish.
If it is only half-digested, its appearance becomes like crow droppings.
When twice as much <s>gagana</s> has been digested, it overcomes the eight metals.
Again I shall teach another, very rare binding of mercury.
The herb <s>irindirī</s>, produced from the body of <s>Śiva</s>,
digests sulfur, and it also digests <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment).

children.text: kāñcanaṃ jārayetsā tu rasendraṃ sā ca bandhayet
children.translated_text: It digests gold, and it binds <s>rasendra</s> (mercury).
It melts coral, and likewise melts <s>gagana</s> (mica).

children.text: vajraṃ ca ghātayetsā tu sarvasatvaṃ ca ghātayet
children.translated_text: It breaks down diamond and also breaks down every metallic essence.
It digests all metals, and it digests the essences as well.
Having placed mercury in the juice of <s>irindirī</s>, in a cow's horn, O fair-faced one,
it should be set in a heap of grain; the mercury remains fluid.
By the very juice of the divine herb, O worshipped by the gods, <s>rasendra</s>

children.text: same tu kanake jīrṇe daśakoṭiṃ tu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: when an equal amount of gold has been digested, pierces ten crores.
At the fifth stage it pierces a lakh of crores; at the sixfold stage it transmutes by touch.
At the seventh it transmutes by fumigation, and at the eighth by being seen.

children.text: navame śabdavedhī syādata ūrdhvaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: At the ninth it transmutes by sound; beyond this there is nothing.
Foolish beasts wander about, deprived of <s>kulauṣadhi</s> (lineage herbs).
No accomplishment arises from the juices of ordinary grasses and herbs.
Therefore the <s>kulauṣadhi</s> must be known by every effort.
Sixty-four divine herbs are established within the <s>kula</s>.
Fools do not know them, deluded by the delusion of <s>Śiva</s>.
Non-divine grasses and herbs grow in mountain caves.

children.text: tṛṇauṣadhyā rase sūto naiva baddhaḥ kadācana ||
children.translated_text: Mercury is never bound at any time by the juice of ordinary herbs.
Without <s>kulauṣadhi</s>, it would not remain imperishable.
Those who make <s>gagana</s> circulate without <s>kulauṣadhi</s>,

children.text: sa rasastu varārohe vahnimadhye na tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: that mercury, O fair-hipped one, does not stand in the midst of fire.

children.text: na khoṭaṃ na ca vā bhasma naiva dravyaṃ karoti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: It makes neither a lump nor ash, nor does it make any useful substance.
They produce some small substance, but it does not remain when blown in the fire.

children.text: patre pāke kaṣe chede naiva tiṣṭhati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: In leaf, cooking, touchstone, and cutting tests, that gold does not stand.

children.text: na vedhaṃ ca śatādūrdhvaṃ karoti sa rasaḥ priye
children.translated_text: That mercury, dear one, does not effect transmutation beyond a hundredfold.

children.text: yāvanna cābdam ekaṃ tu vikrāntaṃ trapu tattu kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: And until one full year has passed, that transformed tin is only called gold.
Therefore, dear one, one should not give it for <s>dharma</s>, wealth, pleasure, or liberation.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s>:

children.text: nirjīvatvaṃ gataḥ sūtaḥ kathaṃ jīvaṃ dadāti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Mercury has become lifeless; how does it give life?

children.text: nirjīvena tu nirjīvaṃ kathaṃ jīvati śaṃkaraḥ
children.translated_text: How, O <s>Śaṃkara</s>, can the lifeless live by means of what is lifeless?
<s>Śrībhairava</s>:

children.text: divyauṣadhyā yadā devi rasendro mardito bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When, O goddess, <s>rasendra</s> has been triturated with a divine herb,
then mercury becomes free of black stain, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Mercury free of black stain takes away the death of another.

children.text: aṣṭānāṃ caiva lohānāṃ malaṃ śamayati kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: It pacifies in an instant the impurity of the eight metals.
Who would call dead a mercury that has gone into great stupefaction?
By the juice of the divine herb alone it becomes one whose ordinary consciousness is lost.
Mercury is composed of the five elements and always remains <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
Again I shall teach another binding of mercury, O mistress.
With <s>kṣmāpāla</s> one should draw out diamond, and with this also gold.
Diamond ash and gold ash should then be bound together in one place.
It should be digested in the juice of <s>niśācara</s> and digested with <s>narajīva</s>.

children.text: taṃ sūtaṃ mārayedbhadre jāgarir divya oṣadhiḥ
children.translated_text: The divine herb <s>jāgarī</s>, O blessed one, kills that mercury.

children.text: bhakṣitaḥ sa raso yena so'pi sākṣātsadāśivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever eats that mercury is himself visibly <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
When a single <s>tolaka</s> is eaten, a man becomes able to transmute by touch.
From the sweat of his body the eight metals become gold.
That supreme practitioner lives for thousands of lakhs of years.
From the sweat of his body even the king of mercury is bound.
<s>Ajāpati</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇatejas</s> bind mercury in an instant.
By the touch of <s>jāgarī</s>, O goddess, and with <s>kṣmāpāla</s>, it is bound.
<s>Gagana</s> (mica), soaked in the juice of <s>turuvallyā</s>, dear one,
should be digested in a sand apparatus; it becomes a lump at that very moment.
One <s>māṣa</s> of a molten pellet and one <s>māṣa</s> of a gold pellet
should be combined into one and triturated with sour citron for three days.
One <s>karṣa</s> of lead leaves should be coated with the mercury paste.
One should wrap it with <s>vṛścikālī</s>, and then coat that lump.
One should kill the lead, O goddess; it becomes like a red <s>śakragopa</s> insect.
One <s>karṣa</s> of silver leaves should be coated with dead lead.
One should coat it with <s>vṛścikālī</s>, and then coat that leaf.
That silver is killed, O goddess, resembling vermilion red.
With that very substance, in a thousandth part, one should cause the piercing of copper.
Divine gold is produced, an ornament fit for the adornment of the gods.
Milky, bearing many fruits, and knotted, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
the plant called <s>vartulapattrāṇi</s> is praised for the binding of mercury.
Once, with the tuber paste, mercury placed in a blind crucible
should be blown with breaths from the mouth; when bound, it is recommended for eating.
The tuber of red <s>kañcukī</s>, ground with a woman's breast milk,
by the previous procedure in a crucible, brings about the binding of mercury.
The seed of <s>vṛścikāpattrikā</s>, combined with coconut milk,
the practitioner should blow the mercury as before, for the purpose of eating.
Having taken <s>vajrakanda</s>, one should place the mercury in the middle.
One should give the heating called <s>gajendra</s> seven times and bring it to binding.
The wise man should eat that mercury; in six months he becomes deathless.
Having taken the tuber of <s>lāṅgalī</s> and also the tuber of <s>karkoṭī</s>,
one should put the mercury inside them, steam it, and grind it again.
It is killed; there is no doubt here, when it has been blown with intense fire.
One should heat the mercury placed in <s>śukacañcu</s> with a puṭa, and then blow it.
This becomes capable of hundredfold penetration and produces bodily perfection.
One should put mercury with the juice of <s>haṃsapādī</s> into the cavity of a dried tuber.
One should give a <s>gajendra</s> puṭa; it is killed, without any doubt.
It also becomes capable of thousandfold penetration; there is no doubt here.
Taking <s>haṃsāṅghri</s> and <s>śukacañcu</s>, one should grind the mercury.
Having put it into the cavity of <s>krauñcapāda</s>, one should then give three puṭas.
The great mercury is killed, without doubt, and is capable of hundred-thousandfold penetration.
Listen, dear one, to the divine herb known as <s>tṛṇajyotis</s>.

children.text: niśā tu prajvalennityaṃ nāhnā jvalati pārvati ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Pārvatī</s>, it always blazes at night; by day it does not blaze.

children.text: tasya mūle tu saṃkṣipte kṣīraṃ raktaṃ bhavetkṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: When its root is cut, its sap becomes red in an instant.
With its root juice, sulfur, and mica, ground with the sour juice of citron,
a copper sheet smeared with it becomes gold after three puṭas.
O <s>Sureśvarī</s>, the king of mercury, combined with the powder of its root,
when rubbed in citron juice, consumes mica in an instant.
Now I shall explain <s>uccāṭā</s>, dear one, which brings about the binding of mercury.
It has only one stalk, and that is enclosed by hairs.
At its tip there is a flower resembling a parrot's beak.
O goddess, its leaves too resemble a parrot's feather.
Its tuber has the form of a tortoise, and its sap resembles vermilion.
O <s>Pārvatī</s>, water oozes in beeswax; having gathered that,
one should pierce all metals, and they become gold.
One should grind mercury, orpiment, and blue vitriol with the juices of <s>uccāṭā</s>.
Heated in the sun, the mercury is killed by the power of the divine herb.
O fair-faced one, it pierces all metals at a hundred-thousandth part.
It should be repeatedly melted until it becomes equal to the sun in brilliance.
Mercury, red <s>snuhī</s> latex, <s>kunaṭī</s>, sulfur, mica,
and <s>darada</s> should pierce the metals at a thousandth part.
Having taken <s>snuhī</s> latex, one should wrap it with powder of <s>niśā</s>.
Having made it into a pill with that, it pierces lead in that very instant.
Now listen to the procedure for the divine herb <s>sthalapadminī</s>.
It is like a lotus in its leaves, and the same in its flowers.
When broken, sap flows from it; it is red in color and very beautiful.
Stepping on it with the left foot, one should look at the circle of the sky.
One sees it together with the stars, the circle of planets and constellations.
O goddess, it should be known as <s>sthalapadminī</s> from a hundred thousand yojanas away.
Having taken its five parts, together with <s>haragaurī</s>,
combined with realgar and orpiment, and together with pyrite,

children.text: mardayetsaptarātraṃ tu tena śulbaṃ ca vedhayet
children.translated_text: one should grind it for seven nights; with it he should pierce copper.
O <s>Deveśī</s>, when pierced at a thousandth part, it becomes gold.
Having taken its five parts by the method stated before, dear one,
one should make the king of mercury assimilate it, put it in a blind crucible, and blow it.
It is killed inside the crucible by contraction; there is no doubt.
With that alone one should pierce all metals at a thousandth part.
I shall tell briefly the secret of <s>citraka</s>.
<s>Citraka</s> is to be known as threefold: black and red are <s>rasāyana</s>.
The white one pacifies disease; they are superior, middling, and inferior.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ raktaṃ sitaṃ vāpi hemante noddhared budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise man should not uproot the black, red, or white in winter.
Having uprooted black <s>citraka</s>, not smelled by cows, O <s>Īśvarī</s>,
one should put it in milk; the milk becomes black in an instant.
With the powder of its five parts, one should grind mercury.
He should blow it in a blind crucible; it becomes a lump in that very instant.
Having put on red garments, red garlands, and red unguents,
on the fifth day of the dark fortnight, with a red garland and cooked rice,
one should give an offering, O great goddess, and uproot the red <s>citraka</s>.
With the powder of red <s>citraka</s>, one should treat tin with threefold liquid applications.
Freed from all defects, it attains fixation in that very instant.
Its root, mercury, and copper, through sprinkling with <s>kuṅkuṇī</s> oil,
after twenty-one applications, will become purified copper.
Smeared with red <s>citraka</s> and <s>bhallāta</s> oil, by means of a puṭa,
O <s>Deveśī</s>, the moon-sun sheet becomes divine gold.
The tuber of <s>nāginī</s>, the lord of mercury, and red <s>citraka</s> combined,
by leaf-coatings and repeated castings, make the moon-sun metal into gold.
I shall state the procedure for <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> oil; listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: jyotiṣmatī nāma latā yā ca kāñcanasannibhā
children.translated_text: There is a creeper named <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, which resembles gold,
rich in spreading vines, auspicious, and bearing gold-colored fruit.
In the bright fortnight of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, having taken its excellent seed,
one should boil or press it like sesame, whether with the hands or even the feet.
Having taken its oil, one should place it in a copper pot.
He should set the pot underground, with a husk-fire gradually above it.

children.text: ṣaṇmāse tu vyatikrānte sa ghaṭaḥ kāñcanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: When six months have passed, that pot becomes gold.
Having made copper equal to gold and mixed it with oil and <s>mākṣīka</s> (pyrite),
one should sprinkle it at each casting; then gold equal in amount to the copper results.
And thus it becomes a hundredfold-penetrating agent, an unsurpassed jewel of knowledge.
Dear one, I shall explain <s>Dagdharuhā</s>, which brings about the binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
It is to be known as <s>Sparśauṣadhī</s>, accomplishing every desired aim.

children.text: śaśvacchinnā mahādevi dagdhā sā pāvakena tu
children.translated_text: O great goddess, though constantly cut and burned by fire,

children.text: prarohati kṣaṇāddivyā dagdhā sā tu mahauṣadhī ||
children.translated_text: that divine great herb, even when burned, sprouts again in an instant.

children.text: raktaṃ pītaṃ sitaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tasyāḥ puṣpaṃ prajāyate
children.translated_text: Its flowers arise red, yellow, white, and black.
One should recognize its well-grown leaves as like those of the chickpea.
It grows on the bank of the <s>Gomatī</s>, on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and on Mount <s>Arbuda</s>.
It is also seen south of <s>Ujjayinī</s> and in forest margins.
O divine one, with the juice of its bulb combined with black mustard,
and made equal with betel, the wise man should make a pill.
When all the molten metals are in the midst of the fire,

children.text: sahasraṃ vedhayitvā tu kāñcanaṃ kurute kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: after penetrating them a thousandfold, it instantly makes gold.
Likewise <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is killed when combined with <s>kānta</s> (magnetite), gold, and mica.

children.text: kaṭutuṃbī tu vikhyātā devi divyauṣadhiṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭutuṃbī</s> is well known; O goddess, hear of the divine herb.

children.text: tasyā bījāni saṃgṛhya sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: Having gathered its seeds, one should make them into a fine powder.
It should be impregnated twenty-one times with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> (emblic myrobalan).
Together with milk, and with that same substance combined with <s>viśvabheṣaja</s>,

children.text: bījaṃ yantre vinikṣipya tailaṃ saṃgṛhya piṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should place the seed in the apparatus, collect the oil, and press it into a mass.
With that he should stupefy <s>rasa</s> (mercury), and he should grind it with <s>cakramarda</s>.
Cow bile and peacock bile, together with <s>kāṅkṣī</s> and <s>kāsīsa</s>,
these are to be equal to <s>tāra</s> (silver), and the <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) is to be equal to them all.
It should be placed in a ram's horn continuously for one month.
Sprinkled with an iron rod, it penetrates all metals.
Sulfur, treated twenty-one times with an iron rod,
joined with the class of metals and mixed with lemon juice,
together with seed and <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury), should be placed in a sealed crucible.

children.text: bhūgataṃ māsamekaṃ tu tāraṃ kāñcanatāṃ nayet
children.translated_text: When buried for one month, it brings <s>tāra</s> (silver) to the state of gold.
One should add one part of <s>dala</s> and five parts of <s>tāra</s> (silver),

children.text: śulbaṃ ca pañcabhāgaṃ ca bījasyaikaṃ ca yojayet
children.translated_text: five parts of <s>śulba</s> (copper), and one part of the seed.
These make twelve parts; one should keep all that in the earth.

children.text: sthānasyāsya niṣekaṃ tu sudaṇḍena tu kārayet
children.translated_text: The sprinkling of this place should be done with a good rod.
At the end of twenty-five days, the finest gold is produced.
I shall describe the procedure for <s>kṣīrakanda</s>, likewise productive of every accomplishment.
There the poison is four-colored; the red bulb is praised.
When it is broken, it emits a splendid milk of red color.
It is adorned by growth produced with the rumbling of clouds.
It has smooth, even leaves like those of <s>snuhī</s>, with an excellent golden luster.
It binds the king <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and brings all essences under control.

children.text: tasya kṣīraṃ tu saṃgṛhya tāraṃ nirvāhayedbudhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having collected its milk, the wise man should process <s>tāra</s> (silver).
He should blast it with intense fire; it becomes beautiful gold.
With the extract of <s>tintriṇī</s> leaves, mixed with a little copper dust,
the learned man should grind mercury; binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) will result.
When placed in water, the pill becomes like a diamond.
O queen of the gods, pressing out the excellent juice of the <s>śākavṛkṣa</s>,
combined with red sandalwood, one should digest all metals.
All metals unite and flow like water.
Sulfur, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, mercury, and red sandalwood,
combined with the juice of <s>rudantī</s>, cause <s>tāra</s> (silver) to come to gold.
The extract of the <s>śākavṛkṣa</s> should be carefully filtered.

children.text: śigrumūlasya cūrṇaṃ tu tadrasena tu mardayet ||
children.translated_text: The powder of <s>śigru</s> root should be ground with that juice.
Having smeared copper sheets, one should put them into a covered heating and cook them.
When melted, that becomes divine gold, endowed with the proper marks.
One should gather the fully ripe fruits of the <s>śākavṛkṣa</s>.

children.text: tadrasena tu samprājñaḥ saptarātraṃ tu bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: The wise man should impregnate it with that juice for seven nights.
Joined with that juice and also mixed with <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>,
he should smear silver sheets; when heated, it becomes gold.
Now I shall explain the procedure for the great herb <s>devadālī</s>.

children.text: sā śvetā vyādhiśamane kṛṣṇā pītā rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: Its white form pacifies disease; the black and yellow forms are for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation).
On the full moon, on the thirteenth lunar day, when the sun is seized by <s>Rāhu</s>,
or on the fifth day of the dark fortnight, one should pull it up according to rule.
The fruit of <s>devadālī</s>, <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, and <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury)

children.text: mūrchayed bandhayetkṣipraṃ śulbaṃ hema karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: stupefy and bind it quickly, and make <s>śulba</s> (copper) into gold.
The fruit and root of <s>devadālī</s>, together with the juice of <s>īśvarī</s>,

children.text: toyena marditaṃ kṛtvā vaṅgaṃ stambhayati kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: when ground with water, fix <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) in an instant.
Now, dear one, I shall explain the procedure for white <s>guñjā</s>.
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, or on the eighth, O one honored by the gods,
having placed clay in a skull, one should sprinkle it with water.
One should sow the seeds of white <s>guñjā</s> under the <s>Puṣya</s> conjunction.
With the formula about to be stated, one should then perform the gathering.
Oṃ, reverence to the blessed <s>Śvetavallī</s>, dweller on the white mountain.

children.text: sarvakāryāṇi kuru kuru apratihataṃ namo namaḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: Accomplish all tasks, accomplish them, without obstruction; reverence, reverence, svāhā.

children.text: śuddhaśulbaṃ tu saṃgṛhya mūṣāmadhye tu saṃsthitam ||
children.translated_text: Having taken pure <s>śulba</s> (copper), placed in the middle of a crucible,
amounting to fifteen <s>palas</s>, together with half a <s>karṣa</s> of white <s>guñjā</s>,
together in one place, it becomes <s>tāra</s> (silver), free from its odor.
Powder of <s>guñjā</s>, combined with <s>brahmarīti</s>, together as one,

children.text: devīnāṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ devi jāyate hema śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: becomes beautiful gold, O goddess, an ornament for goddesses.
Now then I shall fully explain the binding of <s>kartarīrasa</s> (cutting rasa).
When the asuras had assembled, with his mind filled by anger,
the great discus <s>Sudarśana</s> was sent forth by the enemy of <s>Mura</s>.
Then drops of sweat fell from his brow.

children.text: te bhūmau patitā divyāḥ saṃjātāḥ kartarīrasaḥ
children.translated_text: Those divine drops, fallen upon the earth, became <s>kartarīrasa</s>.

children.text: rakṣārthaṃ sthāpitaṃ tatra viṣṇunā ca sudarśanam ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Sudarśana</s> was set there by <s>Viṣṇu</s> for protection.
This whirls like the discus and cuts down weapons.
It makes a roaring sound and emits smoke and flame.
There is <s>kartarī</s> by mere sight, and likewise another, <s>śabdakartarī</s> (sound-kartarī);
for the welfare of the worlds, a terrible power is established.

children.text: rasarūpā mahāghorā sā siddhānāṃ tu vedinī
children.translated_text: In the form of <s>rasa</s>, exceedingly terrible, she is known to the siddhas.
When one goes to its field, he should then recite the <s>Aghorāstra</s>.
Again he should place the <s>Ghora</s> there; then the wise man should arrange another.
In direct and reverse order he should establish the <s>kartarī</s> in the body.
He should seal it with the mudrā, joined with the <s>Aghorāstra</s>.

children.text: dīptena rodhayettāṃ tu stambhayed dīpanena tu ||
children.translated_text: He should restrain it with the blazing one, and make it motionless by the kindling rite.

children.text: niṣṭhayā mudrayā tāṃ tu sthānayogena yojayet
children.translated_text: With firmness and the mudrā, he should yoke it through union with the place.
Now, O <s>Īśī</s>, I shall explain the binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) by <s>candrodaka</s> (moon-water).
When the mantra-practitioner sees <s>candrodaka</s>, especially on the full-moon day,
it should be collected there, carefully, on the full-moon day.

children.text: nirgacchati mahīṃ bhittvā candravṛddhyā tu vardhate
children.translated_text: It comes out by breaking through the earth and increases with the waxing of the moon.
Having first made the field-binding and worshiped the god <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
on the fourteenth lunar day the discerning man should worship that field,
and, having remained there day and night, should offer a bali there.

children.text: paurṇamāsyāṃ ca rātrau ca gatvā tasya samīpataḥ
children.translated_text: On the full-moon night, having gone near it,
he should collect the <s>candrodaka</s>, joined with mantra and well consecrated by mantra.
Having stirred it with honey and ghee, he should drink it with concentration.
As soon as it is drunk, by that very thing he becomes unconscious for a moment.
At moonrise he should rise again; then one should administer alkali to him.
By practice for seven nights he becomes stainless like the moon.
By practice for twenty-one nights he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By practice for one month, that man obtains the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: candrodakena gaganaṃ rasaṃ hema ca mardayet
children.translated_text: With <s>candrodaka</s> he should grind <s>gagana</s> (mica), <s>rasa</s> (mercury), and gold.
Heated while placed inside a crucible, it at once becomes a pill.

children.text: ayaṃ tu sparśamātreṇa lohānyaṣṭau ca vedhayet
children.translated_text: By mere contact, this penetrates the eight metals.

children.text: tadrasaṃ tu rasaṃ cānyaṃ vajreṇa samajāritam ||
children.translated_text: That <s>rasa</s>, and another <s>rasa</s> equally digested with diamond,
should penetrate, at one sixty-fourth part, a thousand with twice that amount.
Then <s>rasa</s> the size of a <s>guñjā</s>, bound with ten links,
wrapped in three metals and held in the mouth, makes one become invisible.

children.text: oṃ namo rudrāya daṃṣṭrotkaṭāya vighnaṃ nāśaya nāśaya diśo rakṣa rakṣa rudro jñāpayati huṃ phaṭ svāhā
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to <s>Rudra</s>, fierce with fangs: destroy, destroy obstruction; protect, protect the directions; <s>Rudra</s> makes known; huṃ phaṭ svāhā.
This is the mantra for binding the directions.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya triśūlahastāya amṛtodbhava rakṣa rakṣa huṃ phaṭ svāhā
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the Blessed <s>Rudra</s>, holding a trident: O one born of immortality, protect, protect; huṃ phaṭ svāhā.
This is the drinking mantra.
Now then I shall fully explain the binding of <s>rasa</s> by <s>viṣodara</s>.
There, O goddess, is the best <s>rasa</s>, rich in colors such as white and yellow.
Having gone there to the mountain region, he should remember the terrible one a thousand times.
Hairs thrown into it burst apart; one’s own shadow is not seen.

children.text: tailaṃ ca golakākāraṃ ghṛtaṃ tena visarpati ||
children.translated_text: Oil becomes globular, and ghee spreads through it.
It removes the odor of sulfur; flesh becomes salty.
Knowing this, he should put it with a <s>palāśa</s> leaf into a bitter gourd.

children.text: viṣodakaṃ gandhakaṃ ca harabījaṃ ca tatsamam
children.translated_text: Poison-water, sulfur, and <s>harabīja</s>, each in equal amount,

children.text: ajākṣīreṇa piṣṭvā tu śulbapātre tu lepayet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground with goat’s milk and smeared on a copper vessel.
Through that heating, O goddess, it becomes like red vermilion.
With only one hundredth part of it, O goddess, it penetrates all metals.

children.text: anena vidhinā devi nāgaḥ sindūratāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: By this procedure, O goddess, <s>nāga</s> (lead) becomes vermilion.
With one thousandth part of that alone, <s>tāra</s> (silver) becomes gold.
Red, yellow, and black, each later one, accomplish their respective operations.
Either in a vessel of <s>triphalā</s> and magnet, or in a vessel made of gourd,
having taken it as before, he should wrap it outside with <s>palāśa</s> leaves.
He should keep it in the middle of grain for twenty-one days.
He should prepare a single drop in buffalo’s milk.
Whoever eats rice pudding combined with milk, honey, and ghee,
as long as full strength remains, O goddess, lives according to the number of those drops.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, house-soot, vermilion, and the two <s>rajanī</s> herbs,
ram’s horn, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, black <s>unmattā</s>, and <s>aśvamāraka</s>,
together with seeded <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury), he should grind with poison-water.
The intelligent man should impregnate it seven times with poison-water.

children.text: athavā bhāvayettaṃ tu yāvaccūrṇaṃ tu mardayet tadbhavet ||
children.translated_text: Or he should impregnate it and grind it until it becomes powder.

children.text: tena nāgaṃ pratīvāpya ṣoḍaśāṃśena khaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Having cast that upon <s>nāga</s> (lead) at one sixteenth part, it becomes <s>kha</s>.

children.text: mūṣāsthaṃ veṇuyantre ca trīṇi vārāṇi bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: Standing in a crucible and in a bamboo apparatus, it should be impregnated three times.
He should avoid its smoke; it is supremely productive of disease in the limbs.
He should place that lead-vermilion in a vessel made of gourd.
With that powder, at one hundredth part, he should penetrate silver, copper, and the like.
Having taken poison-water and fine melted <s>vaṅga</s> (tin),
And, sprinkled with those waters, silver becomes gold.
One should take the poisonous water and pour it into the best <s>rasa</s> (mercurial preparation).
<s>Kunaṭī</s>, sulphur-stone, poison, borax, and <s>lāṅgalī</s>
should be made into a vanished paste in a mortar, and one should coat silver leaves with it.
When blown in a blind crucible, it becomes seedless gold.
Oṃ hrīṃ, to <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>, ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ.
One should recite this ten thousand times.
Thus ends the mantra for taking and drinking poisonous water.
Now I shall explain the procedure for revivifying water, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
O goddess, O you honored by the gods, long ago I was worshipped by <s>Śukra</s>
for the benefit of the demons who had died in battle with the gods.
By me the revivifying knowledge, taking the form of water, was given to him,

children.text: tayā saṃjīvitā daityā ye mṛtā devasaṅgare ||
children.translated_text: and by it the Daityas who had died in battle with the gods were brought back to life.

children.text: nikṣiptā martyaloke sā samyak te kathayāmyaham
children.translated_text: It has been deposited in the mortal world; I shall explain it properly to you.
There is a very holy and pure river in the southern country.

children.text: dakṣiṇe tu taṭe tasyā utpalīnagaraṃ param
children.translated_text: On its southern bank is the excellent city <s>Utpalī</s>.
To the south of it is a mountain famed in all the worlds.
It is seen under the name <s>Kṛṣṇagiri</s>, O all-auspicious one.
Near it there is a village called the well-known <s>Ambikā</s>.
There too, having found the water, one should test it, O you worshipped by the gods.
Taking a dry bamboo, one should throw it into the middle of the water.
Within a day and night it certainly becomes green and glossy.
It sends forth shoots and leaves, and appears exceedingly lovely.
Then, O goddess, one should worship with offerings of bali and flowers

children.text: kṣetrādhipaṃ gaṇeśaṃ ca candraṃ yogigaṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the lord of the field, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, <s>Candra</s>, and the host of yogins.

children.text: oṃ candrāya pinākine śūlapāṇaye oṃ diśo bandha bandhaya diśo bandha bandhaya ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ, to <s>Candra</s>, to the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>, to the trident-holder. Oṃ, bind the directions, bind the directions, ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ.
With this mantra, sesame seeds and mustard seeds, indeed mustard seeds,
having consecrated them seven times, the practitioner should cast them into the directions.
With the protection made, concentrated, he should take the water in a bitter bottle-gourd vessel,
and, having taken it carefully, should return to his own place.

children.text: oṃ namo 'mṛte amṛtarūpiṇi amṛtaṃ kuru kuru evaṃ rudra ājñāpayati svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the immortal one, O you whose form is nectar; make it immortal, make it immortal. Thus <s>Rudra</s> commands. Svāhā.
Having consecrated that water seven times with this mantra,
for one day he should triturate <s>sūta</s> (mercury) together with two <s>māṣas</s> of gold
with that water, and the wise man should drink it.
Then for twenty-one nights he should carefully live on milk as his food.
He lives for ten thousand kalpas and more, able to assume any form and very strong.
Having gone a hundred yojanas, he returns again.
He is invulnerable to all beings, eats as he wishes, and moves through the sky.

children.text: kanakaṃ pāradaṃ vyoma samam ekatra yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Gold, <s>pārada</s> (mercury), and <s>vyoma</s> (mica) should be combined together in equal measure.
One should triturate them with that water and then heat them in a steam bath for seven days.

children.text: sa rasaḥ sarvalohāni ṣaṣṭyaṃśena tu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: That <s>rasa</s> (mercurial compound) pierces all metals with a sixtieth part.

children.text: athavā taṃ rasaṃ divyaṃ madhunā saha bhakṣayet
children.translated_text: Or else one should eat that divine <s>rasa</s> together with honey.
By using it for just one month, one lives for ten thousand days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By his urine, feces, and sweat, copper becomes gold.
Taking the water in a windless place, together with <s>pārada</s> (mercury) and realgar,
one should triturate them on a mortar-stone; then it becomes a vanished paste.
One should steam it for seven nights and wrap it with the three metals.
He becomes invisible in an instant and becomes lord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>.
Surrounded by a hundred perfected maidens, he remains for fourteen kalpas.
On all those days one should give rice cooked from śāli grain, with ghee,

children.text: payasā ca samāyuktaṃ nityamevaṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: and combined with milk; one should do this every day.
I shall explain the procedure for hot water; listen with an attentive mind.
Wherever one sees hot water, one should have him dwell right there.
There, chickpeas that have stayed overnight
should be eaten day by day for one month; he lives for eight hundred years.
By his urine and feces copper becomes gold.
Hot water, green vitriol, and sulphur-stone
should be combined by adding zinc ore as a fourth part and in ten parts.

children.text: śulbaṃ ca mardayetsarvaṃ naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ kṣaṇena tu ||
children.translated_text: He should triturate all the copper; in an instant it becomes a vanished paste.
By merely being coated with that, copper becomes gold.
The wise man should sprinkle it with that water and add it at each casting.
Copper becomes gold, with the brilliance of the young sun.

children.text: tāraṃ ca tena mārgeṇa niṣiktaṃ hematāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: And silver, sprinkled by that same method, comes to the state of gold.
With hot water one should eat bhallāta and a handful of sesame.
By using this for two months, he lives for three hundred years.
<s>Rasa</s>, sulphur, stone, zinc ore, blue vitriol, cinnabar, and pyrite
should be rubbed for a watch of the day with hot water, and one should coat silver leaves with them.
Having turned them about, one should blow them in the fire, O goddess; they become fourteen-carat gold.
By this sequence, O mistress of gods, copper becomes sixteen-carat gold.
One part each of gold and silver, and two parts each of magnetic iron and mica, separately,
should be thoroughly triturated with hot water and, by blowing, brought to the state of a lump.
He should hold that in his mouth for a month; then he becomes diamond-bodied.
He should eat its powder, the measure of a barley grain, with honey and ghee.

children.text: yāvatpalaṃ tasya malaiḥ śulbaṃ bhavati kāñcanam
children.translated_text: Until a pala has been consumed, by his wastes copper becomes gold.
He should eat horse-gram cooked in hot water and become a milk-drinker.
He should bathe with hot water; after a year he becomes long-lived for a hundred years.
He should cook milk, hot water, and a decoction of triphalā,
and cook rice pudding in an iron vessel; after eating it, he becomes very long-lived.
After this I shall explain the procedure for <s>śailodaka</s> (stone-water), dear one.
It is fourfold: muddy water, earth-water, mountain-water, and rock-water.
Some are instant-piercing agents, and some are day-piercing agents.
On earth there are those that pierce after a fortnight, a month, and so on up to six months.

children.text: kṣiptaṃ jale yadā kāṣṭhaṃ śailībhūtaṃ ca dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: When wood thrown into water is seen to have become stone,
outside and inside, O <s>Deveśī</s>, that is proclaimed a <s>vedhaka</s> (penetrating transformative agent).

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ haritālaṃ ca gandhakaṃ ca manaḥśilām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment), <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), and <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar):

children.text: eṣāṃ gandhāpahāraṃ tu kurute tacca vedhakam
children.translated_text: that which removes the smell of these is a <s>vedhaka</s>.
Otherwise, O goddess, it is merely a false imitation, unacceptable and useless.
At <s>Śrīśaila</s>, near the edge of <s>Śrīvana</s>, on the rock-surface called <s>Paryaṅka</s>,
what is found there, on the bank of the river <s>Bhagavatī</s>, is instant-piercing.

children.text: ekāhe vedhakaṃ tatra gokarṇe tu dinatrayam
children.translated_text: There it pierces in a single day; at <s>Gokarṇa</s>, however, in three days.
At <s>Bhadrāṅga</s> it is day-piercing; at the end of <s>Tristhala</s> it takes three years.
At <s>Dhāreśvara</s> it takes a fortnight; at <s>Karṣāpurī</s> a single day.
At <s>Brahmeśvara</s> it is monthly; at <s>Vyāghrapurī</s>, however, one day.
At <s>Aghoreśa</s> it is monthly, and likewise again on <s>Siṃhadvīpa</s>.
One day on <s>Brahmagiri</s>; on the <s>Vindhya</s> it is instant-piercing.

children.text: vāsaraṃ mālyavante tu kṣaṇavedhī tu tatra ca
children.translated_text: At <s>Mālyavanta</s> it takes a day, and there too it is instant-piercing.
On the lovely mountain <s>Kiṣkindha</s>, on the bank of the <s>Pampā</s>, there is instant water.
Two yojanas to its west, O goddess, again,
there is an earth-mountain there; on <s>Vedaparvata</s> it pierces in three days.
Elsewhere also, wherever it has arisen from <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or <s>Śiva</s>,
there too that <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) is excellent for making one adamantine.
I shall explain its origin, so that the practitioner may know it.
From the body of <s>Varāha</s>, when he had raised up the earth,
whatever sweat fell: from that arose the supreme <s>śailodaka</s>.

children.text: taṃ mukhe kṣaṇikaṃ jātaṃ karṇadeśe tu vāsaram ||
children.translated_text: That which arose from his mouth is instant; from the region of the ear it takes one day.
From the arms it is three-day-piercing; from the flanks it is month-piercing.

children.text: ṣaṇmāsamaparāṅge ca sarvaṃ samaphalaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: From the hind part it takes six months, and all of it has the same result.

children.text: aghorāstreṇa tatkṣetre rakṣāṃ kṛtvā diśāṃ balim
children.translated_text: In that place, after making protection with the <s>Aghora</s> weapon and giving offerings to the quarters,

children.text: dattvā lakṣaṃ japitvā tu gṛhṇīyādamṛtaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: and after reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times, one should collect the supreme <s>amṛta</s>.
In autumn, summer, spring, or winter, O you who are worshiped by the gods,
in an iron vessel, a copper vessel, or one made of magnetic iron,
one should put eight palas of stone-water and one pala of milk.
After boiling it until only the milk remains, a man should drink it for twenty-one days.
He lives a thousand years, free from wrinkles and gray hair.
Or else, eight palas of milk mixed with one pala of the water:
he should consume it when it has been reduced to the milk-remnant; he obtains the result stated before.
He should cook water with eight times as much <s>kuluttha</s> until one eighth remains.
With four times that decoction he should cook ghee until only the ghee remains.
He should lick it with honey and sugar; after twenty-one days he becomes like <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Having the appearance of a sixteen-year-old, he is thousand-lived; there is no doubt.
The remaining <s>kuluttha</s>, together with a quarter-part of honey and ghee,
he should eat in the amount of one karṣa; in a month he has a lifespan of ten thousand years.
With the oil prepared from it one should perform an anointing and rubbing.
It swiftly conquers <s>pāmā</s>, <s>vicarcikā</s>, <s>dadru</s>, and <s>kuṣṭha</s> skin diseases.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, he becomes thousand-lived.
Whoever, rising in the morning, drinks a handful of stone-water with milk,
after six months becomes thousand-lived and free from wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: athavā sūtakaṃ devi vāriṇā saha mardayet
children.translated_text: Or else, O goddess, he should grind mercury together with the water.
In one month, O <s>Deveśī</s>, it will become <s>naṣṭapiṣṭi</s>.
He should eat it for just one month; he becomes free from old age and death.
Or else he should blow that mercury with gold in a <s>khadira</s>-wood fire.
The pill named <s>Sundarī</s> wards off all weapons.
As creator and destroyer, self-perfected, he would live as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
Then with that very water he should cook <s>pāyasa</s>, with half milk.
By using it for just one month, he becomes free from wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: paktvā tenāmbhasā pathyāḥ ṣaṣṭistrīṇi śatāni ca
children.translated_text: Having cooked three hundred and sixty <s>pathyā</s> fruits with that water,

children.text: madhu saṃyojya bhāṇḍasthaṃ bhūmau sarvaṃ nidhāpayet ||
children.translated_text: he should add honey, put everything in a vessel, and place it in the ground.
Day by day, rising in the morning, he should eat one of them.
Freed from wrinkles and gray hair, he lives a thousand years.
Or he should eat <s>kuluttha</s> that has become stone-like, together with honey and ghee.
Through using it for six months, he lives a thousand years.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍamāditaḥ kṛtvā yāni kāni phalāni ca
children.translated_text: Beginning with <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, whatever fruits there are,
and metals that, thrown into the water, have become stone-like, he should eat.
Keeping to a milk diet when it has been digested, a man becomes vajra-bodied.
One should grind <s>abhraka</s> (mica) with that water and decoct it, dear one.
Eating it with the three pungents, he lives a thousand years.
Or else, one karṣa of mercury ground with that water,
placed inside an <s>iṅgudī</s> fruit and set within that <s>śailodaka</s>,
after three times the period, develops hardness.

children.text: ṣaṇmāsaṃ tanmukhe dhāryaṃ vajrakāyaṃ karoti tat
children.translated_text: Held in the mouth for six months, it makes the body vajra-like.
He has strength equal to ten elephants and rejoices together with the gods.
Having taken <s>triphalā</s>, one should put it there in the stone-water.
When it becomes stone-like, one should take it and then powder it.
With magnet-digested mercury, together with that, soaked in ghee and honey,
he should eat it for one year; thereafter he should subsist on milk.
He becomes like the rising sun, intelligent, and pleasing to behold.
And with dark, curly hair he lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.

children.text: pāradaṃ haritālaṃ ca śilāṃ mākṣikameva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Pārada</s> (mercury), <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment), <s>śilā</s> (realgar), and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite),

children.text: daradaṃ ca viṣaṃ caiva sarvamekatra kārayet ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) and poison: he should make all of these into one mixture.
He should grind it on a mortar-stone with citron juice,
and, having made a ball, he should place it in water.

children.text: tena tāraṃ ca śulbaṃ ca kāṃcanaṃ bhavati dhruvam
children.translated_text: By means of that, silver and copper certainly become gold.
He should use it for one month, free from wrinkles and grey hair.
His life is a thousand years, and he is of great strength and valor.
But turmeric that has become stony, merely by the addition of its powder,
makes <s>nāga</s> (lead) attain the state of gold, with a luster like the young sun.
Having placed it in <s>śailodaka</s> (mineral water), or in earth, stone, or mud,
then, knowing the measure of time, he should bind <s>pārada</s> (mercury).
Heated with red alkali, it has the same flow as gold.
At one hundredth part it turns all metals into gold.
Having attained the second <s>sāraṇā</s> (transmissive processing), it penetrates at one thousandth part.

children.text: taṃ khoṭaṃ dhārayedvaktre divyatvaṃ labhate dhruvam
children.translated_text: He should hold that <s>khoṭa</s> (solid pellet) in the mouth; he certainly attains divine status.

children.text: nicule kakubhe caiva kiṃśuke madhuke'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: In <s>nicula</s>, <s>kakubha</s>, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, or <s>madhuka</s>,
or inside the fruit of <s>iṅgudī</s>, or in ginger for two nights,
or in <s>amṛta</s>, in a bulb, or in the aforesaid bulbous medicines,

children.text: vidhāya koṭaraṃ tatra kṣiptvā tenaiva ḍolayet
children.translated_text: having made a cavity there, he should put it in and swing it in that very substance.
He should carefully wrap it with a paste of <s>triphalā</s> and <s>vyoṣa</s>.

children.text: pādena kanakaṃ dattvā pāradaṃ tatra yojayet
children.translated_text: Having added a quarter part of gold, he should combine the <s>pārada</s> (mercury) there.
He should place it there in <s>śailodaka</s>; the pill becomes like a diamond.
The <s>sāraṇā</s> should be done as before, and it gives accomplishment as before.

children.text: dhāryamāṇā mukhe sā tu sahasrāyuṣkarī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When that is held in the mouth, it gives a lifespan of a thousand years.
Through the method of the second <s>sāraṇā</s>, it penetrates ten thousandfold.
When held in the mouth in this same way, it gives a lifespan of ten thousand years.
Through the method of the third <s>sāraṇā</s>, it becomes capable of penetrating a hundred thousand.
A man who holds that <s>khoṭa</s> (solid pellet) in his mouth gains a lifespan of a hundred thousand years.

children.text: caturthī sāraṇā devi koṭivedhī na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: The fourth <s>sāraṇā</s>, O goddess, penetrates ten million; there is no doubt.
His life is ten million years, and the state of a sky-goer is obtained.
With five, it is a hundred million; with six, it becomes a thousand million.
His life lasts as long as the moon and sun, and he has boundless strength and vigor.

children.text: dadāti saptamī cāpi sāraṇā gulikā parā
children.translated_text: The seventh <s>sāraṇā</s> also gives the supreme pill,
known by the name <s>Khecarī</s>, taught by <s>Bhairava</s>.
Whoever eats only a mustard-seed measure of that for one month
becomes an accomplished one with a diamond body, beloved by divine women.

children.text: krīḍate khecarair bhogaiḥ svecchayā śivatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: He sports with the enjoyments of the sky-goers, and at will he enters the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
There are many kinds of fruits from this pill; listen, O beautiful one.

children.text: śuddhabaddhaṃ rasendraṃ tu gandhakaṃ tatra jārayet
children.translated_text: Into purified and bound <s>rasendra</s> (mercury), he should digest sulfur.

children.text: triguṇe gandhake jīrṇe tena hema tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: When sulfur has been digested in triple quantity, by that he should make gold.

children.text: kārayedbhasma sūtaṃ tu kāñcanaṃ tena sūtakam
children.translated_text: He should make <s>sūta</s> (mercury) into ash, and gold into mercury by means of that mercury.

children.text: tadbhasma sūtake jāryaṃ rasendrasya same samam ||
children.translated_text: That ash is to be digested into <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury), equal to <s>rasendra</s>, in equal amount.
With that mercury digested in mercury, he should destroy diamond-gem.
That diamond becomes ash, resembling red vermilion.
He should digest that ash into <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in triple amount, O worshiped by the gods.

children.text: hāṭakaṃ sārayettaṃ tu ghuṭikāṃ tena kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should process gold with it, and with that he should make a pill.

children.text: trilohāveṣṭitaṃ taṃ tu mukhe prakṣipya sādhakaḥ
children.translated_text: The practitioner, having enclosed it in the three metals and placed it in his mouth,
loses his shadow and becomes invisible to gods and demons.
For hundreds of thousands of years he remains without wrinkles or grey hair.
He should bear one with a trident, joined with a spear, adorned with the qualities of gems and the like,
in the mouth and in the hand, as a warding-off of all weapons.

children.text: vyoma mākṣikasatvaṃ ca tāraṃ tāmraṃ surāyudham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vyoma</s> (mica), the essence of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), silver, copper, and <s>surāyudha</s>,
<s>sāraloha</s>, <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury), and what is adorned with the qualities of gems and the like:
that pill, O fair-hipped one, is combined with the three sweets.
When kept in the mouth, it directly destroys grey hair; there is no doubt about this.
<s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, O goddess of gods, gems and white <s>gonasā</s>,

children.text: hema tāraṃ tathā bhānuḥ samabhāgāni kārayet
children.translated_text: gold, silver, and the sun: he should make these in equal parts.
With female menstrual blood, placed in the middle of tiger-substance, he should wrap it with lotus fiber.
It should likewise be wrapped with white cloth and placed in the secret place.

children.text: raṇe rājakule dyūte divye kāme jayo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: In battle, in the royal court, in gambling, and in divine love, victory arises.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, mica, magnet, <s>sasyaka</s>, and <s>surāyudha</s>,
should be equal to the sour gruel produced from <s>vibhītaka</s> and the rest.
Having fused them together, he should then combine them with <s>sūta</s> (mercury) by the quarter-part method.
Ground with the juice of <s>kumārī</s>, this auspicious pill is made.
When held in the mouth, it destroys disease, death, and old age; there is no doubt.
Five parts silver, O fair-hipped one, and two parts <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury),
three parts <s>gagana</s> (mica), and one part each of gold and magnet,
with half a part of copper by measure: this is the immortal-beautiful pill.
By means of it, he becomes imperishable, ageless, and very strong.
One <s>pala</s> of mercury ash, and likewise one <s>pala</s> of dead magnet,

children.text: mākṣikasya palaṃ caiva śilājatu palaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: one <s>pala</s> of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), and likewise one <s>pala</s> of <s>śilājatu</s>,
one <s>pala</s> of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and likewise one <s>pala</s> of powdered <s>pathyā</s>:

children.text: ekīkṛtya tu tatsarvaṃ madhvājyena tu peṣayet
children.translated_text: having combined all that into one, he should grind it with honey and ghee.
With that he should make three hundred and sixty pills.
He should eat one each day continuously for one year.
He lives a hundred years, very strong, like <s>Rudra</s>.
After this I shall explain the <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir) made from mercury ash.
It should be known as the supreme divine medicine itself, admitting no avoidance.

children.text: āmalakyādi kāntaṃ ca pāradaṃ ca manaḥśilām
children.translated_text: <s>Āmalakī</s> and the other ingredients, <s>kānta</s> (magnetite), <s>pārada</s> (mercury), and <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar),
together with equal parts of <s>vākucī</s>, should be ground with the juice of <s>kṣīriṇī</s>.
Provided with the juice of <s>meghanāda</s>, it should be placed in a silent crucible and cooked.
Then one should eat it in order as one <s>māṣa</s>, two <s>māṣas</s>, and three times that amount.
For three years at most, O goddess, he should take it successively in measures of a quarter <s>niṣka</s> and half a <s>niṣka</s>.
For six, seven, and eight years, he should eat it successively in <s>niṣka</s> measures.
He should eat divine food, free from old age and deformity.
With a little gold mixed in, he should take a <s>niṣka</s>, or else half a <s>niṣka</s>.
Whoever eats it over three years conquers all diseases.
He has a lifespan of eight thousand years, and in the twelfth year he can penetrate a hundred thousand.

children.text: ṣoḍaśe vatsare devi divyarūpaḥ sa jāyate
children.translated_text: In the sixteenth year, O goddess, he becomes divine in form.
The best is root-binding; the middling is essence-binding.
The lowest is cooking-binding. Thus binding is threefold.
There should be one hundred <s>palas</s> of <s>abhayā</s>, and likewise of <s>akṣa</s> and <s>dhātrī</s>; they are boiled in eight equal parts of water until one eighth remains.

children.text: ghṛtamadhusitayāḍhyaṃ vyoṣacitraṃ daśaiva rasapaladaśasiddhaṃ lohajīrṇaṃ mṛtaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: It is enriched with ghee, honey, and sugar, variegated with <s>vyoṣa</s>, and prepared with ten <s>palas</s> of <s>rasa</s>, digested with iron and calcined.

children.text: giriyutasamam abhraṃ kāntabhṛṅgaṃ viḍaṅgaṃ rasasahitavibhāvyaṃ taṇḍulair bilvamajjaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Abhra</s> equal to the mountain-mixture, <s>kānta</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s> should be impregnated with <s>rasa</s>, together with rice and the pulp of <s>bilva</s>.
This excellent paste, made with the moon-cool ingredient, should be kept in an iron vessel for a month, after the body has been purified for three days.
If one licks it at bedtime, taking half the right-eye measure, he has dense, deep concentration and the pride of an intoxicated elephant.

children.text: vigatasakaladoṣaḥ sarvadṛk divyacakṣuḥ madana iva sukāntiḥ kāminīnāṃ pravīraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Free of all faults, all-seeing, divinely sighted, lovely like <s>Madana</s>, he is foremost among lovers.

children.text: jalada iva vapuṣmānkuñcitāgrāgrakeśaḥ turaga iva viśuddhaḥ satkaviścitrakārī
children.translated_text: His body is like a rain cloud, the tips of his hair are curled, he is pure like a horse, and he becomes a fine poet and a maker of wonders.

children.text: vṛṣabhagativiceṣṭo mandagambhīraghoṣaḥ suragaja iva loke candratārārkajīvī ||
children.translated_text: With the gait and movements of a bull and a slow, deep voice, he lives in the world like the elephant of the gods, as long as the moon, stars, and sun.
A ball consisting of <s>kānta</s>, gold, copper, silver, and <s>abhraka</s> is placed inside an <s>iṅgudī</s> fruit.
The ball perfected in <s>śailavāri</s> is auspicious, the beautiful one called <s>amarasa</s>.
A ball is made of <s>kānta</s>, gold, copper, silver, <s>abhraka</s>, diamond, jewel, <s>rasa</s>, and <s>mahirāja</s>.
It is cast into the hollow of <s>āmalaka</s> wood, buried in earth and mountain, and then taken out.
When it has become stone-like, it is then placed in the mouth, bringing a diamond body over the days of the procedure.
A ball of silver, gold, excellent copper, and <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) is enclosed in an apparatus of <s>varaṇa</s> wood.
With <s>śailavāri</s> and the juices of <s>sundarī</s>, the pill is called <s>khecarī</s>.
A seed of <s>palāśa</s> placed in <s>śailāmbu</s> and made stone-like should be eaten with honey and ghee.

children.text: trisaptarātraṃ dinamekamekaṃ sahasrajīvī vidito naraḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: For twenty-one nights, one each day, and the man is known to become one who lives a thousand years.
<s>Sūtaka</s> (mercury) and <s>abhraka</s>, combined with diamond and sharp iron,
and joined with gold, become the <s>khecarī</s> pill.
Mercury should be placed right there in the middle of a <s>karañja</s> fruit.
Held within <s>śailāmbu</s>, it grants a lifespan of a thousand years.
In a <s>tinduka</s> fruit it gives two thousand years of life; in a citron, three thousand.
In a <s>mātuluṅga</s> and in an orange it gives four and five thousand.
In a plantain fruit it gives six thousand; in a jackfruit, seven thousand.
And in a <s>vibhītaka</s> fruit it gives a count of ten thousand.
In a coconut, O greatly fortunate one, it gives fourteen thousand.
In <s>pathyā</s> it gives thirty thousand, and in <s>āmalaka</s> it gives a hundred thousand.
From a decoction made of sheets of <s>abhraka</s>, kept day and night in stone-water,
one binds the extracted mercury, which destroys death and poverty.
Through the method of <s>sāraṇākrama</s>, the body becomes like diamond.

children.text: rase rasāyane caiva lakṣavedhī na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In mercury and in <s>rasāyana</s>, it penetrates a hundred thousand; there is no doubt.
The mud of <s>kumārī</s>, made into a lump with its juice,
yields its essence when blown in the furnace; a man should hold it in his mouth.
By application for six months he reaches freedom from old age and death.
The essence, smelted together with <s>srotoñjana</s>, is mixed with mercury.
If he holds that pellet in his mouth, he surely becomes invisible.
Whatever procedure for the water is taught in the <s>Śivāgama</s>,
by that, after the proper period of a hundred, one should produce <s>rasāyana</s> in the body.
That earlier preparation is the inferior, immature digestion.
Now listen to the bound digestion, which is best and difficult to obtain.
Whoever tries to digest the unbound one, while being diminished, goes to destruction.

children.text: baddhasya jīryate grāso jīrṇasya ca mukhaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: The morsel of the bound one is digested, and when digested it becomes a mouth.
When furnished with a mouth it gives to the bad-mouthed; this is the mark of the ordinary and the excellent.
The ordinary one, by enduring fire, digests great jewels and the like.
First the ordinary one should be made, provided with morsels on every side.
This ordinary one, O goddess, produces a firm body.
But the bound one that lacks morsels produces divine accomplishment.
The best is root-binding; the middling is essence-binding.
The lowest is cooking-binding. Thus binding is threefold.
Root-binding is the binding in which the great root is contracted.
Essence-binding is the binding that is called impression-binding.
Binding may be produced by some root among the sixty-four roots.
The limb of living beings and of demons and others is the root-limb, filled with deities.

children.text: pāṣāṇaṃ caiva siddhānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca pūjitam
children.translated_text: And stone, belonging to the siddhas, is worshipped also by human beings.
Binding is threefold, through <s>pīṭhikā</s>, <s>druti</s>, and <s>saṃkoca</s>.
The <s>saṃkoca</s>-binding by divine herbs has been stated before.
<s>Sūta</s> (mercury) is bound by <s>drutis</s>; this is called momentary binding.
Mica, <s>harabīja</s>, and gold in a sixteenth part:
when heated in an open crucible, one should purify it with glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax).
Heated with a rightward turning, together with a mixture of <s>harabīja</s>,
the <s>rasa</s> remains, O fair-hipped one, after leaving the crucible, as though bound in the form of <s>khaga</s>.
With only half of half a <s>raktikā</s> in measure it would pierce even mountains.
By consuming it, O <s>Deveśī</s>, a man becomes equal to <s>Rudra</s>.
He sports through the seven worlds, with valor equal to <s>Śiva</s>.
<s>Vajrakanda</s> and <s>guḍūcī</s>, together with <s>uccaṭā</s> and the other substances:
mica quickly undergoes the operation; otherwise there is no union.
With black <s>agaru</s>, <s>nābhi</s>, sugar, garlic, and <s>pitarāmaṭha</s>,
together with the flower of a woman and oil of <s>palāśa</s> seeds,
all the <s>drutis</s>, ground while warm, combine in the <s>rasa</s>.
Again I shall declare another vajra-binding, O you worshiped by the gods.
A woman should consume sulfur for twenty-one days.
Her menstrual blood is useful for binding and digesting the king of <s>rasa</s>.
One part diamond ash and three parts purified mercury
are to be ground with the fluid of a woman until they become a paste.
With gold in a quarter part, one should make a coating on a sheet.
The juice of <s>somavallī</s>, magnetic iron, and well-powdered <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and <s>āla</s>
should be added as an eighth part, and one should grind carefully.

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ tadandhayitvā puṭe tataḥ
children.translated_text: When that <s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s> has dried, after sealing it in a heating-pit,
it is placed in a closed crucible and heated, together with a penetrating agent.
A <s>khoṭa</s> is produced, O goddess: a great <s>rasa</s> with hundredfold piercing power.

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā dattvā viśodhayet ||
children.translated_text: One should purify it again and again by adding <s>sauvīra</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and glass.
Unexhausted, it combines with gold, and a complete fusion takes place.
Then, increasing in a sequence of one beyond the previous, one should make it penetrate by means of the <s>saṃkalas</s>.
With an equal amount of mercury, one <s>saṅkalikā</s> is so called.
With three times as much mercury, the second <s>saṅkalā</s> is so called.

children.text: ṣaḍguṇena tu sūtena tṛtīyā saṅkalī bhavet
children.translated_text: With six times as much mercury, the third <s>saṅkalī</s> comes to be.
With ten times as much mercury, the fourth <s>saṅkalī</s> comes to be.
With fifteen times as much, O lady, the fifth <s>saṅkalī</s> comes to be.
With twenty-one times as much, O lady, the sixth <s>saṅkalikā</s> comes to be.
With twenty-eight times as much, O lady, the seventh <s>saṅkalī</s> is remembered.
Bound when multiplied thirty-sixfold, it becomes the eighth <s>saṅkalikā</s>.
At forty-five times, it is considered the ninth <s>saṅkalī</s>.
At fifty-five times, the tenth <s>saṅkalikā</s> is remembered.

children.text: evaṃ ca kramavṛddhyā tu saṃkalī daśabandhitā
children.translated_text: Thus, by gradual increase, the <s>saṅkalī</s> is bound ten times.
In the first it has tenfold piercing, and in the second hundredfold piercing.
In the third it has thousandfold piercing; in the fourth, ten-thousandfold piercing.

children.text: pañcame lakṣavedhī syād daśalakṣaṃ tu ṣaṣṭhake ||
children.translated_text: In the fifth it has hundred-thousandfold piercing, and in the sixth, a millionfold.
In the seventh it has ten-millionfold piercing, and likewise in the eighth, a hundred-millionfold.
In the ninth it is smoke-piercing; in the tenth, sound-piercing.
When bound with all the <s>saṃkalas</s>, the piercing power becomes tenfold greater.
Bound with ten <s>saṃkalikās</s>, the great <s>rasa</s> is sound-piercing.

children.text: yathā lohe tathā dehe krāmate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: As it penetrates metal, so it penetrates the body; there is no doubt here.
It pierces metals and the body according to that same measure.
One should make a divine pill, the size of a jujube stone.
After worshiping <s>Mahākālī</s>, a wise man should wear it continually.

children.text: oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kāli kāli mahākāli māṃsaśoṇitabhojani
children.translated_text: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, <s>Kāli</s>, <s>Kāli</s>, <s>Mahākāli</s>, eater of flesh and blood,

children.text: hrāṃ hrīṃ hraṃ rakṣa kṛṣṇamukhi devi rasasiddhiṃ dadasva me
children.translated_text: hrāṃ hrīṃ hraṃ, protect me, black-faced goddess; grant me success in <s>rasa</s>.
Śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ.
Then, having worshiped the goddess and especially the circle of adepts,
he should place that divine pill in the middle of the circle.

children.text: śatavedhena yā baddhā rasena ghuṭikā priye
children.translated_text: The pill, dear one, that has been bound by mercury with hundredfold piercing power:

children.text: māsamekaṃ tu vaktrasthā jīveccaiva yathā vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: when it has remained in the mouth for one month, he lives according to the prescribed rule.

children.text: tathā sahasravedhena baddhā yā ghuṭikā śubhā
children.translated_text: Likewise, the auspicious pill that has been bound with thousandfold piercing power:
when it has remained in the mouth for two months, he lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
If the pill has been bound with ten-thousandfold piercing power,
then, in three months, a lifespan equal to <s>Śakra</s> arises.
The divine pill that has been bound with hundred-thousandfold piercing power:
when it has remained in the mouth for four months, it grants the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.
The divine pill that has been bound with millionfold piercing power:

children.text: saptamāsaṃ tu vaktrasthā vaiṣṇavaṃ labhate phalam ||
children.translated_text: when it has remained in the mouth for seven months, he obtains the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> result.
The divine pill that has been bound with ten-millionfold piercing power:
when it has remained in the mouth for six months, it leads directly to <s>Rudra</s>-hood.
The divine pill produced by the hundred-millionfold distinction:

children.text: saptamāsaṃ tu vaktrasthā sa bhavedvyāpako naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: when it has remained in the mouth for seven months, that man becomes all-pervading.
He becomes creator, destroyer, enjoyer in himself, and maker of curses and favors.
He is omniscient, maker of all things, subtle in form, and stainless.
By his will he creates; by his will he withdraws the world.
Having become free-moving, the man becomes of the form of <s>Śiva</s>.
He is worshiped by all the gods, including <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Again I shall declare a very difficult vajra-binding.
