One should make gold consume an equal portion together with purified mercury.
One should grind dead diamond in a sixteenth part with the fluids of a woman.
As before, the remaining set of operations should be done, and the result will be as before.
The binding of the vajra will be accomplished, unconquerable by gods and demons.
He becomes the leader of the twenty-four siddhas, possessing every siddhi.
Mercury equal to diamond-powder should be rubbed with <s>haṃsapādī</s>.
After heating it in a <s>puṭa</s>, one should kill it there; then one should add an equal amount of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
When blown, it quickly becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> (metallic lump), purified with glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax).
Do this, dear one, until the mercury becomes like the rising planet Venus.

children.text: vajrasattvaṃ ca gaganaṃ rasaṃ hema ca melayet ||
children.translated_text: One should combine diamond-essence, <s>gagana</s> (mica), <s>rasa</s> (mercury), and gold.
Held in the mouth, O lord of gods, it obtains immortality.
After causing the mercury to digest that, one should again digest it with that same substance.

children.text: koṭivedhī na sandeho vaktrasthaṃ khecaraṃ param
children.translated_text: Held in the mouth, it is a supreme sky-going preparation, capable of piercing ten million times; there is no doubt.
By that measure it would pierce metals and also the body.
One should make a divine pill in gold with diamond perfected in vajra.
By this sequential method one should kill it as far as one is able.
That mercury-<s>bhasma</s>, O goddess, removes all diseases.

children.text: hemnā ca sārayitvā tu candrārkaṃ lepayettataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After causing it to flow with gold, one should then smear it with moon and sun.
With a thirty-second part, half the gold becomes superior for the required operation.
A learned man should make a pill the size of a jujube stone.

children.text: yathā lohe tathā dehe kramate nānyathā kvacit
children.translated_text: As it proceeds in metal, so it proceeds in the body, and never otherwise.
Gold paired with diamond, with magnetic iron, copper, and <s>kapālin</s>,
one should color that finely powdered <s>khoṭa</s> seven times.
It is to be impregnated with women's menstrual fluid and placed in birch bark.
Joined with molten mercury, it should be bound into a bundle with cloth.
One should steam it, O mistress of gods, until it becomes a ball.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>jīvanī</s>, <s>gandhārī</s>, and <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>:
one should place it in a lump of these and wrap the diamond-ball.
Having put it inside a crucible and carefully sealed it,

children.text: bhūmau mūṣāṃ vinikṣipya puṭaṃ mūrdhni pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: one should set the crucible in the ground and apply a <s>puṭa</s> from above.
By this very heat the great <s>rasa</s> enters bondage.
When, dear one, one holds the ball in the mouth for one year,
one lives for thousands of kalpas, like a mighty elephant.
In twelve years he visibly becomes a <s>rasapūruṣa</s> (mercurial man).
From the sweat of his body the eight metals become gold.
Diamond-<s>bhasma</s>, likewise mercury, combined with gold:
whoever keeps it in the mouth is free from gray hair within a year.

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya satvaṃ ca tāraṃ tāmraṃ ca hāṭakam ||
children.translated_text: The essence of black mica, silver, copper, gold,
<s>mākṣika</s>, magnetic iron, and sharp iron should be made in equal parts.
Blown inside a blind crucible, it immediately becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu drutasūtena golayet
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s>, finely powdered, should be formed into a ball with molten mercury.
There is one part of the killed essence and four parts of the ball.
One should rub it with a heated mortar; the mercury becomes <s>bhasma</s>.
One should kill it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus according to the sequence of seven chains.

children.text: guñjāmātraṃ tu tadbhasma madhvājyena tu lehayet
children.translated_text: One should lick a guñjā-measure of that <s>bhasma</s> with honey and ghee.
By using it for a year, a man becomes ten-thousand-lived.
He is freed from wrinkles and gray hair, and has great strength and valor.

children.text: tadbhasma palamekaṃ tu palaikaṃ gandhakasya ca ||
children.translated_text: One pala of that <s>bhasma</s> and one pala of sulfur:
blown inside a blind crucible, it immediately becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.
He lives for thousands of kalpas, like a mighty elephant.
By his urine and feces the eight metals become gold.
Afterward one should color that <s>khoṭa</s> with tin, mica, and <s>kapālin</s>.
One should color it seven times; it becomes like saffron.
Having melted it together with gold, and made it flow by three <s>sāraṇā</s> processes,
one should apply a hundredth part of that very substance into copper.
Divine gold is produced, fit for adorning the ornaments of the gods.
One part of bound mercury and one part of <s>kuṭila</s>,
blown inside a blind crucible until only tin remains:
by this sequential method, one should draw off tin sixfold.
By this sequential method, one should also carry lead sixfold.
Then afterward one should color it with sharp iron, copper, and <s>kapālin</s>.
One part of cooked mercury and one part of molten mercury
should be rubbed with a moderate acid; it becomes a ball at once.
There is one part of killed diamond and four parts of the ball.
One should rub it with a heated mortar; the mercury becomes <s>bhasma</s>.
One should kill it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus according to the sequence of seven chains.
Afterward one should again rub that <s>bhasma</s> with a moderate acid.
One should carefully give it three hundred and sixty <s>puṭas</s>.
That <s>bhasma</s> becomes divine, resembling vermilion-red color.
With that alone one should pierce silver into gold at a thousandth part.
One part of killed diamond and sixteen parts of mercury,
rubbed in due order with the juice of <s>devadālī</s> and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>,
should be killed in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus; it becomes <s>bhasma</s> at once.
Being blown with a thousand blasts, it does not disappear.

children.text: īdṛśaṃ bhasma sūtaṃ ca dehe lohe ca yojayet
children.translated_text: Such <s>bhasma</s> and mercury should be applied to the body and to metal.

children.text: tadbhasma palamekaṃ tu palamekaṃ ca gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: One pala of that <s>bhasma</s> and one pala of sulfur:
blown inside a blind crucible, it immediately becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.
Afterward one should color that <s>khoṭa</s> according to the <s>kapālin</s> sequence.
By the method of the three <s>sāraṇās</s>, one should cause copper-piercing to take place.
One pala of calcined <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) and one pala of <s>pannaga</s> (lead) should also be taken.
Having placed it in a <s>kānta</s> vessel, one should grind it with an iron pestle.
Then it should be cooked over a gentle fire until it unites with <s>nāga</s> (lead).
Through a <s>puṭa</s> heating it becomes <s>bhasma</s> (ash), shining with a vermilion-red radiance.

children.text: tadbhasma tu punaḥ paścādgopittena tu mardayet ||
children.translated_text: Afterward that <s>bhasma</s> should again be ground with cow bile.
It should be heated in a <s>puṭa</s> fourteen times; then one should reduce it to ash.
One part of that <s>bhasma</s> and one part of a ball of gold should be used.
After combining them, one should grind them together with a <s>krāmaṇa</s> agent.
With that same silver paste, gold is acted upon in the proportion of one thousandth part.
By this ordered procedure <s>vaṅga-bhasma</s> (tin ash) is produced.
With that same thousandth part, one should bring about penetration into <s>śulba</s> (copper).
That copper becomes <s>tāra</s> (silver), resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.

children.text: śvetābhrakaṃ ca sattvaṃ ca kāṅkṣī kāntaṃ tathāyasam ||
children.translated_text: White <s>abhraka</s> (mica), <s>sattva</s> (essence), <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and likewise iron are taken.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ kāntaṃ tāraṃ tathā śvetaṃ vaikrāntaṃ ca kadambakam
children.translated_text: Tin, <s>kānta</s>, silver, white <s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>kadambaka</s> are also taken.
Smelted in a closed crucible, it becomes an ingot resembling jasmine and the moon.

children.text: taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu drutasūtena golakam
children.translated_text: That ingot should be made into fine powder and formed into a ball with molten mercury.
There should be one part of dead diamond and four parts of the ball.
One should grind it in a heated mortar; the <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) becomes ash.
It should be killed in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by the procedure of seven <s>saṅkalikās</s>.
Then <s>bhasma</s> is produced, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.

children.text: tadbhasma palamekaṃ tu palamekaṃ tu gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: One pala of that <s>bhasma</s> and one pala of sulfur should be taken.
Smelted in a closed crucible, that <s>rasa</s> becomes an ingot.
It should be repeatedly melted with silver and made to pass through the three <s>sāraṇās</s>.
With that same thousandth part, one should bring about penetration into copper.
Eight palas of powdered <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (sharp iron or steel) and eight palas of molten mercury are taken.
One should grind them in a heated mortar with the juice of <s>ṭeṭañcilvī</s>.
At once a lump is produced, a ball together with the <s>tīkṣṇa</s>.
There should be one part of dead diamond and four parts of the ball.
One should grind it in a heated mortar; it becomes ash at once.
It should be killed in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by the procedure of seven <s>saṅkalikās</s>.
With a sixteenth part of that, one should bring about penetration into tin.

children.text: tadbhasma palamekaṃ tu palaikaṃ gandhakasya ca
children.translated_text: One pala of that <s>bhasma</s> and one pala of sulfur should be taken.
Smelted in a closed crucible, it becomes an ingot at once.

children.text: tasya khoṭasya bhāgaṃ ca tīkṣṇacūrṇaṃ ca tatsamam
children.translated_text: One part of that ingot and an equal amount of powdered <s>tīkṣṇa</s> should be taken.
Two parts of molten mercury should be added, and all should be ground together.

children.text: taptakhalve tu saṃmardya golakaṃ bhavati kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: When it is ground in a heated mortar, it becomes a ball in a moment.
It should be killed in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by the procedure of seven <s>saṅkalikās</s>.
All of that should be digested into <s>bhasma</s>, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.
That <s>bhasma</s> should be made into an ingot, alloyed together with <s>tīkṣṇa</s>.
By this ordered procedure, with the sequence of seven <s>saṅkalikās</s>,
one should afterward digest that ingot, after it has been passed through the three <s>sāraṇās</s>.
With a hundred-thousandth part of that, one should bring about penetration into tin.
One pala of calcined mercury should be taken, and purified tin should be added.

children.text: mardayedāyase pātre vaṅgaṃ tu mriyate kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: One should grind it in an iron vessel; the tin is killed in an instant.
Two palas of dead tin and two palas of silver powder should be used.
One should add two palas of sulfur and one pala of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax).
Smelted in a closed crucible, it becomes an ingot at once.
One pala of the ingot powder and one pala of molten mercury should be taken.
One should grind it with the acidic juice of citron; it becomes a ball in a moment.
With a sixteenth part of that, one should penetrate <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>.
One pala of dead tin and one pala of mercury should be taken.
One pala of the complete powder should be prepared, the three together in one place.
One should grind it with the acidic juice of citron; it becomes a ball in a moment.
There should be one part of dead diamond and four parts of the ball.
One should grind them together, O blessed lady, joined with the liquids of herbs.
It should be killed in a <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus with seven <s>puṭas</s>.
All of that becomes <s>bhasma</s> through the very power of diamond.
Three palas of sea salt, O goddess, should be added into the <s>bhasma</s>.
After combining them, one should grind them for three days in <s>vajrīkṣīra</s>.
Placed in a <s>Viśvāmitra</s> cup, it should be given a <s>puṭa</s> in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus.
All of that becomes <s>bhasma</s>, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.
With just a barley-grain measure of that, it fixes tin in an instant.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ tathā sattvaṃ samasūtena golakam ||
children.translated_text: Tin, silver, and <s>sattva</s> should be made into a ball with an equal amount of mercury.
By this ordered procedure one should kill each separately.
All of that becomes <s>bhasma</s> through the very power of diamond.
One pala of calcined mercury and two palas of tin ash should be taken.
Two palas of dead silver and two palas of essence-ash should be added.
Five palas of conch powder and eight palas of sea salt should be used.
Eight palas of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> should be taken, and all should be digested together.
After enveloping it with <s>vajrīkṣīra</s>, one should give it fourteen <s>puṭas</s>.
This is the perfected <s>rasa</s> itself, difficult even for the thirty gods to obtain.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ tu dāpayet paścādbhāṇḍe caiva tu mṛṇmaye
children.translated_text: Afterward one should add tin into an earthen vessel.
The perfected <s>bhasma</s> will result, and one should stir it with an iron rod.
One should carefully quench it until it becomes hard.
Smelted in a closed crucible, it becomes excellent silver.
If at any time the silver cracks, one should add tin again.

children.text: patre dāhe kaṣe chede tattāraṃ śāśvataṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: In the leaf test, burning, rubbing on the touchstone, and cutting, that silver becomes permanent.
One should also make a compact ball, supplied with a sixteenth part,
and one part of dead diamond should be put together in the same place.
One should grind <s>devadālī</s> and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpa</s> with its juice,

children.text: mārayed bhūdhare yantre puṭānāṃ saptakena tu ||
children.translated_text: and kill it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus with seven <s>puṭas</s>.
Afterwards that ash should again be cooked by means of the lamp-apparatus.
One pala of ash-mercury, two leaves of white <s>abhraka</s>,
one pala of powdered conch, and one pala of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
having combined all that into one, one should grind it with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>.
Afterwards, with wild cow-dung cakes, one should give fourteen <s>puṭas</s>.
This <s>rasa</s>, in a barley-grain dose, instantly stiffens tin.
One pala of black <s>abhraka</s> and two palas of <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury),
and one pala of sulphur: having combined them into one, one should grind them.
When it is being carefully ground, a ball comes into being at once.
There should be one part of dead diamond and four parts of the ball.
One should grind for one prahara; the mercury becomes ash.
With forest cow-dung alone one should give a <s>puṭa</s> in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus.
By this procedural method one should make seven repetitions.
With that very substance, at one hundredth part, one should cause penetration of lead.
Afterwards one should color that ingot with a vessel of copper and <s>abhraka</s>.
Then again one should color it afterwards with a vessel of sharp iron and copper.
Then again one should color it afterwards with a vessel of lead and <s>abhraka</s>.
After melting it together with gold, it has been made to pass through the three <s>sāraṇās</s>.
With that very substance, at one thousandth part, one should cause penetration of copper.
Divine gold is produced, fit to adorn the ornaments of the gods.
Ash of <s>vajravallī</s>, given ten <s>puṭas</s> in the milk of <s>snuhī</s>,
one should grind with an equal quantity of mercury and heat it with the juices of <s>devadālī</s>.
One should give an equal quantity of sharp iron a <s>puṭa</s> with the juice of <s>triphalā</s>.
One should give an equal quantity of lead a <s>puṭa</s> with <s>ahimārā</s> and <s>āṭarūṣaka</s>.
That indeed gives the color of gold when combined at one twentieth part.
With one sixty-fourth part this colors purified silver.
With one eighth part of that same substance one should smear sheets of lead.
One should give it <s>puṭas</s> and kill the lead until it resembles red vermilion.
One should kill an equal quantity of gold; it should be heated in the juice of <s>kāñcanāra</s>.
One should kill an equal quantity of copper with the juice of <s>gṛhakanyā</s>.
Afterwards one should heat it with sour liquid until it resembles vermilion.
With that, cooked at one hundredth part, one should color silver and gold.

children.text: sabījaṃ bījavarjaṃ vā vajreṇa saha sūtakaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury, with seed or without seed, together with diamond,
one should afterwards grind its ash with the juice of gold leaf.
With that same substance one should pierce copper; one should combine the copper with silver.
One should pair gold with diamond, and pair <s>rasa</s> (mercury) with gold.
One should pair the body with <s>rasa</s>; that body indeed is free from old age and death.
Plantain, <s>ṭaṅka</s>, and <s>sauvīra</s>, drenched with the juice of <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>,
are the activator for all metals and the blending agent in all pairings.
The five parts of <s>timira</s>, joined with seeds of <s>peṭārī</s>,
having combined and then thoroughly ground them into one, one should wrap the diamond with that.
Blown while placed in a diamond-crucible, it should make the pairing with gold.
Powder of lodestone, <s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>rāmaṭha</s>, honey,
<s>guñjā</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, glass, crab bone, and the milk of <s>snuhī</s>:

children.text: tatsarvaṃ tu samaṃ yojyaṃ strīstanyena tu mardayet
children.translated_text: all that should be combined in equal measure and ground with woman's breast milk.
The wise man makes a crucible-coating; it easily brings about the joining of diamond.
In a forced fire, by means of diamond-crucibles, diamonds join firmly,

children.text: susūkṣmā ravakā bhūtvā hyekībhāvaṃ vrajanti ca ||
children.translated_text: and, becoming very fine particles, they enter into unity.
Blown with a mixture of glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, it obtains purification.
And even with many crucibles, a mass of brilliance is produced.
One part of dead diamond and sixteen parts of gold,

children.text: śvetakācasya sūtaṃ tu bhāgaṃ ṣoḍaśa dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: and sixteen parts of mercury from white glass should be supplied.
Blown while placed in a closed crucible, one should make the diamond-pairing.
By this procedural method one should apply it seven times.

children.text: milate tatkṣaṇād vajraṃ hemnā tu salilaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: The diamond joins with the gold immediately, like water with water.
One should put dead diamond into powder of a human skull.
Blown while placed in a closed crucible, it joins with gold at once.

children.text: bhṛṅgapatraṃ nṛkeśaṃ ca mukhaṃ kāntasya ṭaṅkaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Leaves of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, human hair, the mouth of <s>kānta</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
and the excrement of a young calf should be ground with woman's breast milk.
Blown while placed in a closed crucible, diamond joins at once.
One should impregnate dead diamond with the milk of <s>utpalasāriṇī</s>.
With a paste of gold in the middle, one should place the diamond right there.
One should wrap it in birch bark and wrap the outside with cloth.
Having placed it inside grain, continuously for one fortnight,
one should carefully take it out and make the binding of the diamond.
Melted diamonds should be joined with mercury, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
That is to be known as fixation of the liquefaction, penetrating a hundred thousand.
All the liquefactions of jewels, having been joined according to rule,
penetrate a hundred thousand and bestow bodily accomplishment.
<s>Musalī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>vandhyā</s>, <s>kukkuṭīkanda</s>, and <s>padminī</s>,
<s>kañcukī</s>, <s>nīlī</s>, <s>sindūrī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, and <s>nāgabalā</s>, likewise,
along with <s>rasa</s> in a bronze vessel, and likewise the liquefactions of jewels ...

children.text: ātape dhārayitvā vai adhaḥ karṣānalaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Having kept it in the sun, with a lower fire as from husks,

children.text: oṣadhīnāṃ rasaṃ dattvā svacchaṃ kṛtvā punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having added the juice of herbs, one should make it clear again and again.

children.text: yāmamātraṃ tu gharme ca drutirmilati vai rasam
children.translated_text: For one <s>yāma</s> in the heat, the liquefaction indeed joins the <s>rasa</s> (mercurial essence).
Even with a hundred mouths, it is impossible to state their power in <s>krāmaṇa</s> (progressive penetration).
Rock salt, neem leaves, <s>vākucī</s>, and <s>dveṣiṇī</s>, O mother,
are held to be the supreme mixture with the juice of molten <s>abhraka</s> (mica).
O <s>Īśāni</s>, the diamond-pair preparations and the killing of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) with diamond,
the seeded <s>sāraṇa</s> process, and the binding into a <s>khoṭa</s> have also been taught.
Tell me that, O lady of the gods; what else should I hear?
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:
With the great minerals, the secondary minerals, and the metals, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>,
command me about the whole binding of the king <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
One part of <s>vaikrānta</s> and eight parts of <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury),
with one-seventh part of gold, <s>dvipadīrasa</s>, and borax,

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ ca dhmātaṃ khoṭo bhavetpriye
children.translated_text: when ground until disappeared, dried, and smelted, becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>, dear one.

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā dattvā tu śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: It should be purified again and again by adding <s>sauvīra</s>, borax, and glass.
After melting it together with an equal amount of gold, once it has gone into the crucible,
one should make it undergo equal-part feeding with purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
One should smelt <s>vaikrānta</s> at one-sixteenth by the preceding procedure.
Through the procedure of ten <s>saṅkalikās</s>, its penetration is ten times greater.
Again I shall teach another procedure, rare upon the earth.
The essence of <s>vaikrānta</s>, O lady of the gods, combined with mercury,
and digested with an equal amount of gold, should be placed in a stone vessel.
After remaining in the ground for a full month, it should be carefully taken out.

children.text: eṣa devi raso divyo dehadravyakaro bhavet
children.translated_text: This, O goddess, is a divine <s>rasa</s>, producing body and wealth.

children.text: vaikrāntakāstu ye kecit triphalāyā rasena ca ||
children.translated_text: Whatever pieces of <s>vaikrānta</s> there may be, with the juice of <s>triphala</s>,
each one, O goddess, should be steamed for seven days and likewise ground.
Well smelted in a sealed crucible, it becomes an imperishable <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: kāntaṃ rūpyaṃ ca kanakaṃ pāradaṃ caiva yojayet
children.translated_text: One should combine <s>kānta</s> iron, silver, gold, and mercury,
with copper as a third part, together with <s>srotoñjana</s>.
When smelted, that goes to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s> and becomes productive of body and metal.
White <s>vaikrānta</s> powder should be ground with horse urine.
Taking it at first when well steamed, one should add a hundred <s>palas</s> to a <s>pala</s> measure.
The ash of <s>tāra</s> (silver) is produced, having the appearance of pure crystal.
The wise man should mix that ash into mercury in an equal proportion.
He should make silver circulate in mercury and grind it with horse urine.
It should be cooked in a sealed crucible, gradually, with a gentle fire.
After a day and night, or after three nights, the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) becomes able to withstand fire.
By mere touch it will make all metals into silver.
The operation for the red variety, destroying old age and poverty, will be described.
One should impregnate its powder seven times with water from <s>vyāghrīkanda</s>.

children.text: palaṃ tasya palaṃ hemnaḥ palaṃ śuddharasasya ca ||
children.translated_text: There should be one <s>pala</s> of that, one <s>pala</s> of gold, and one <s>pala</s> of purified mercury.
Everything becomes a pure ash; again one should add a hundred parts of gold.
All that ash is produced with a brilliance equal to pure gold.

children.text: tadbhasma rasarāje tu punarhemnā tu melayet
children.translated_text: That ash should again be mixed with gold in the king <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
It becomes fire-resistant, O goddess; then it becomes the excellent <s>rasa</s>.
The <s>sūta</s> (mercury) becomes able to penetrate everything; the great <s>rasa</s> penetrates a crorefold.

children.text: raktavaikrāntasattvaṃ tu hemnā tu saha melayet ||
children.translated_text: The essence of red <s>vaikrānta</s> should be mixed with gold.

children.text: samaṃ tu jārayetsūte sārayitvā samena tu
children.translated_text: It should be digested equally in mercury, and then made to undergo <s>sāraṇa</s> with an equal amount.
It penetrates metals by a thousandth part; there is no doubt here.
One part of black <s>vaikrānta</s> and purified mercury in a hundredth part

children.text: ekatra mardayet khalve cūrṇaṃ bhavati taddvayam ||
children.translated_text: should be ground together in a mortar; the two become a powder.
One part of this powder and a thousand parts of gold
should be ground together until it becomes ash.
One should heat it in a sealed crucible until it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.
Its equal-part feeding should be done, and its base should be prepared.
By mere touch it penetrates all metals into the state of gold.
That powder and <s>abhraka</s> (mica) should be ground together with mercury.
One should steam it and digest it; then it becomes able to withstand fire.
And that <s>rasa</s> (mercury), when made to circulate, penetrates all metals.
For yellow <s>vaikrānta</s> also, the procedure for the red and black varieties is prescribed.
Yellow <s>vaikrānta</s> powder, joined with gold powder,
and mixed with yellow <s>abhraka</s> powder, becomes the great <s>rasa</s>.
When steamed and ground, after a month it becomes able to withstand fire.
Blue-colored <s>vaikrānta</s> is calcined when joined with mercury,
together with black <s>abhraka</s> and combined with honey and ghee.
One should eat it for a <s>maṇḍala</s>, O goddess, and he will live as long as the moon, sun, and stars.

children.text: yasya yasya hi yo yogastasya tasya prayogataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever procedure belongs to each substance, by applying that very procedure,
after mixing mercury in the measure of a <s>guñjā</s>, combined with the three sweet substances,
one should eat milk, ghee, and <s>śāli</s> rice, and avoid other food.
One should grind mercury joined with the essence of <s>vaikrānta</s> in the sour juice of citron.
It should be heated with hot water and filled with water.
When the essence and mercury are mixed and smelted, there is binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).

children.text: baddhaṃ rasaṃ mukhe kṣiptvā bhūmicchidrāṇi paśyati ||
children.translated_text: Having put the bound <s>rasa</s> in his mouth, he sees openings in the earth.
One should grind one <s>niṣka</s> of processed <s>rasa</s> with horse urine.
After this is ground for one day, O goddess, it becomes calcined.
Doing this for four days, one should bring it to equality with an equal amount of mercury.
Grinding and steaming should be done as before by one whose mind is pure.
Each one is produced from seven pairs; in the seventh it should amount to eight <s>palas</s>.
One should grind it for a day with water from the root of <s>śalyāviśalyā</s>.
Placed within a <s>bhūdharī-yantra</s>, one should give it a <s>puṭa</s> for seven days.

children.text: tadbhasma śuddhaṃ sevyaṃ syādguñjāmātraṃ tu maṇḍalam ||
children.translated_text: That ash is pure and fit to be consumed; the dose is a <s>guñjā</s>-measure for one course.
The first beginning, the fifth middle, and again the first are commended.
The binding is as before, O <s>Devī</s>; the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) becomes capable of piercing ten millionfold.
Red-colored lodestone, shining like lac-resin,
and resembling the blood of a wounded woman: that powder, combined with <s>sūta</s> (mercury),
one should grind with goat's blood. When blown in the fire, it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>, O beloved.

children.text: sa sūtaḥ śatavedhī tu sa tu vyādhiharo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: That <s>sūta</s> pierces a hundredfold, and it removes disease.
If one holds the pill in the mouth, one lives for a thousand years.
Yellow-colored lodestone, shining like split gold,

children.text: vedhayet sparśamātreṇa sa tu lohāni sundari
children.translated_text: pierces metals by mere touch, O beautiful one.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>karavīra</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>girikarṇikā</s>,
woman's breast milk, <s>ṭaṅka</s>, and <s>sauvīra</s>: one should make these into a crucible-coating.
Use twice as much <s>sūta</s> as <s>capala</s>, and twice as much gold as <s>sūta</s>.
One should make it into a lost paste, place it in a closed crucible, and blow it in the fire.

children.text: tatra sthito rasendro'yaṃ khoṭo bhavati śobhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There this <s>rasendra</s> (lord mercury), remaining inside, becomes a fine <s>khoṭa</s>.
It pierces lead at one hundredth part, and becomes the color of <s>guñjā</s>.
With that lead at one hundredth part, copper becomes red in appearance.
With that copper at one hundredth part, it pierces silver and makes it gold.

children.text: capalasya tu ṣaḍbhāgās tārabhāgāstu sapta ca ||
children.translated_text: There are six parts of <s>capala</s> and seven parts of silver,

children.text: aṣṭau kanakabhāgāstu nava bhāgā rasasya ca
children.translated_text: eight parts of gold and nine parts of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
Joined together, they become thirty parts, O you honored by the gods.

children.text: citrakaṃ kaṇavīraṃ ca lāṅgalī gṛdhraviṭ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Citraka</s>, <s>kaṇavīra</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and vulture dung likewise,
ground with the sour juice of citron: one should make these into a crucible-coating.
After sealing it closed, one should blow it in the fire, O <s>Devī</s>; a fine <s>khoṭa</s> is produced.
Lead pierced with one tenth of that <s>khoṭa</s> becomes ruddy.

children.text: tena nāgena viddhaṃ tu śulbaṃ guñjāruṇaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Copper pierced with that lead becomes <s>guñjā</s>-red.

children.text: tena śulbena tāraṃ tu viddhaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: Silver pierced with that copper becomes gold.
Gold-mica and <s>capala</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, combined with half as much mercury,
and, after giving gold to the mercury, one should grind it briefly with <s>kunaṭī</s>.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, woman's breast milk, and <s>kaṇavīra</s>,

children.text: gṛdhraviṣṭhā tathā sarvaṃ mūṣālepaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: as well as vulture dung: one should make all this into a crucible-coating.

children.text: tanmadhye tu sthitaṃ dhmātaṃ khoṭo bhavati śobhanaḥ
children.translated_text: When the substance placed in the middle of it is blown in the fire, a fine <s>khoṭa</s> is produced.
One should pierce with this as stated before; it becomes seedless gold.
Into a well-heated iron vessel one should throw powdered <s>capala</s>.

children.text: sabījaṃ pāradaṃ kṛtvā capalasya tu vāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made mercury furnished with seed, one should cast it upon the <s>capala</s>.
The lac-colored <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is bound like a great elephant by a hook.
One <s>pala</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur,
having combined them into one, one should then grind them with the juice of <s>dhuttūra</s>.
One should kill it by the <s>cakra</s> procedure; the <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) becomes ash.
Blown in the fire while placed in a closed crucible, it becomes a fine <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: sitaṃ hema ca nāgaṃ ca candrārkaṃ cāpi vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: It pierces white metal, gold, lead, and also the moon-and-sun metals.
One <s>pala</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> and one <s>karṣa</s> of sulfur,
one should grind in a smooth mortar, drenched with the juice of <s>devadālī</s>.
One should grind it with the fingers of the hand; a sulfur paste is produced.
With the juice of citron alone one should grind it for one day.
Combined with the five liquefiers, one should make a fine pellet.
One should coat that pellet with a paste of <s>palāśa</s> root.
One should blow it in the fire; through the combination of white glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.
One should purify it carefully until it reaches stainlessness.

children.text: sa khoṭo jāyate devi triguṇaṃ pannagaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s> is produced, O <s>Devī</s>; from it there is threefold <s>pannaga</s> (lead).
Afterwards one should color it hundreds of times with copper, mica, and <s>kapālin</s>.

children.text: śulbe tāre ca khoṭo'yaṃ sahasrāṃśena vedhakaḥ
children.translated_text: In copper and silver this <s>khoṭa</s> is a piercer at one thousandth part.
When the <s>sūta</s> has been killed with sulfur, one should make it carry dead metals.
Then remelt gold and perform the consumption in an equal portion.
When made to flow with copper and silver, the <s>sūtaka</s> pierces bell-metal.
Having made <s>rasa</s> equal to gold, add sulfur equal to half the paste.
Mixed with the dust of a biped and furnished with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, one should grind it.

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ ca dhmātaḥ khoṭo bhavettataḥ
children.translated_text: When the paste has disappeared and the substance is dry, blown in the fire it then becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.
Pierced with one sixteenth part of the moon-and-sun metals, it becomes gold.
That, mixed with half as much gold, reaches the condition of the matrix.
By the procedure of chaining, the piercing becomes ten times greater.

children.text: yathā hemni tathā tāre vyāṭibījena yojitam
children.translated_text: As in gold, so in silver, it is joined with the seed of <s>vyāṭi</s>.
Bound by the third chain, it pierces lead in six hundred parts.
By that same substance in fourfold strength, gold is made with one thousandth part.
If, by this ordered procedure, there are seven chains,
it turns the eight metals into divine gold, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Having powdered that again, one should give it a <s>puṭa</s>; ash is produced.
There is victory over all diseases, O <s>Devī</s>, when one <s>pala</s> is properly consumed.
With two <s>palas</s> the lifespan is that of <s>Brahmā</s>; with three it becomes that of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
With four <s>palas</s> there is the state of the Five; with five <s>palas</s> one becomes <s>Īśa</s>.
When six <s>palas</s> are consumed, O <s>Devī</s>, one has the body of <s>Sadāśiva</s> forever.
<s>Sūtaka</s> (mercury), sulfur, silver, and the fat of <s>meṣavallī</s> are equal.
One should grind them for three days and coat tin with one quarter part.
Heated in a closed crucible, it fixes the tin at once.
O <s>Devi</s>, powdered <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), infused with the juice of <s>markaṭī</s>,
should be impregnated a hundred times; then it becomes <s>jīva-bhasma</s> (living ash).
One should place it in an earthen vessel, combined together with <s>rasa</s> (mercury),
and heat it by the sun's heat, mixed with the juice of <s>markaṭī</s>.

children.text: gandhakaṃ grasate sūtaḥ piṣṭikā bhavati kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: The <s>sūta</s> (mercury) devours the <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), and a <s>piṣṭikā</s> (paste-like mass) forms at once.
Then one should impregnate the <s>gandhaka</s> with the juice of <s>tilaparṇī</s> alone,
seven times, O <s>Deveśi</s>, drying it in the shade again and again.
O beloved, one should take purified and distilled <s>sūta</s> measuring one <s>pala</s>,
place it inside a crucible, and combine it with the juice of <s>narendrī</s>.
One should digest it in a sand-bath apparatus; then the impregnated <s>gandhaka</s> again

children.text: truṭi truṭi pradātavyaṃ gandhakaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is to be added bit by bit, and the <s>gandhaka</s> again and again.
By this sequence of procedure, a <s>gandha-piṣṭikā</s> (sulfur paste) is produced.
Powder of <s>gandha-pāṣāṇa</s> (sulfur-stone) should be treated with the juice of <s>kanaka</s>,
impregnated seven times, and sevenfold with menstrual blood.
Then one should place one <s>pala</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> on a potsherd.
One should add the treated <s>gandhaka</s>, combined with human bile.
One should agitate it under the sun's heat; a <s>piṣṭikā</s> forms at once.
O <s>Pārvatī</s>, fine powder of <s>gandhaka</s> should be treated with sour chickpea gruel,
impregnated seven times, and sevenfold with woman's menstrual discharge.
Into melted <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury), one should add camphor, <s>gandhaka</s>, and <s>rasa</s>,
then place it in a cattle shed; after seven days it is a <s>gandha-piṣṭikā</s>.
Seeds of <s>kaṭukośātakī</s> and the tuber of <s>cāṇḍālī</s>,
ground together with breast milk, should be smeared on the <s>piṣṭikā</s>.
One should fire it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus; it becomes fixed, without doubt.
Then, inside a gold capsule, one should carry out a <s>samāvarta</s> (fusion).
With one eighth part of that same substance, one should apply the piercing of lead.
With one sixteenth part of that same substance, one should apply the piercing of silver.
One <s>pala</s> of <s>gandha-piṣṭi</s> and eight <s>palas</s> of lead paste
should be smeared onto lead sheets; then one should dry them in the shade.
One should smear the lead sheets with a lump of <s>āṭarūṣaka</s>,
and, O <s>Devi</s>, give three <s>puṭas</s> with forest lotuses.
That lead is killed, divine and shining with a vermilion-red radiance.
One <s>pala</s> of that lead and eight <s>palas</s> of copper powder
should be ground for one <s>prahara</s> with the juice of <s>vāsaka</s> alone.
One should kill it in the <s>pātana-yantra</s> (distillation apparatus); that copper is killed at once.
With one sixteenth part of that same substance, one should apply the piercing of silver.
Divine gold is produced, fit as the adornment of the gods' ornaments.

children.text: yā kācidgandhapiṣṭī tu ādau nāgaṃ tu mārayet
children.translated_text: Whatever the <s>gandha-piṣṭī</s> may be, first one should kill lead.

children.text: nāgena vedhayecchulbaṃ śulbe tāraṃ tu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: With the lead one should pierce copper; with the copper one should pierce silver.
Divine gold is produced; this is declared to be an accomplished procedure.
<s>Gandhaka</s> mixed with honey and ground with <s>harabīja</s>
should be kept in the ground for one month; silver turns into gold.
By rubbing with that very substance, every skin disease is destroyed.
Combined with <s>ghana</s>, it destroys diseases of wounds.
By a year's use of it, a man becomes one whose life lasts a thousand years.
One <s>pala</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> and one <s>pala</s> of <s>tālaka</s>
should be combined and then ground together with the juice of <s>unmattaka</s>.
One should kill it by means of the <s>cakra-yantra</s>; the <s>sūtaka</s> becomes ash.
Blown while placed in a closed crucible, it becomes a fine <s>khoṭa</s> mass.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ ca śulbaṃ ca kramaśo vedhayedrasaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>rasa</s> should pierce tin, silver, and copper in sequence.
One <s>pala</s> of purified tin and one <s>pala</s> of <s>sūtaka</s>,
with two <s>palas</s> of <s>tālaka</s>, should be ground with the juice of <s>unmattaka</s>.
One should kill this in the <s>pātana-yantra</s>; by blowing, one brings it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s> mass.

children.text: śvetābhrakasya sattvaṃ ca tāraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca mākṣikam
children.translated_text: The essence of white mica, silver, <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (sharp iron), and <s>mākṣika</s>
become a <s>khoṭa</s> mass at once when blown while placed in a closed crucible.
One <s>pala</s> of that <s>khoṭa</s> mass and one <s>pala</s> of <s>sūtaka</s>,
and one <s>pala</s> of <s>tālaka</s>: one should combine all this and then grind it.
One should kill it in the <s>pātana-yantra</s>; by blowing, one brings it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s> mass.
One <s>pala</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> and one <s>pala</s> of <s>pannaga</s>,
with two <s>palas</s> of <s>kunaṭī</s>, should all be ground together.
One should kill it in the <s>pātana-yantra</s>; by blowing, one brings it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s> mass.
One <s>pala</s> of gold paste and one <s>pala</s> of <s>gandhaka</s>
should be combined and then ground together with the juice of <s>dhuttūraka</s>.
One should kill it in the <s>pātana-yantra</s>; by blowing, one brings it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s> mass.

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya satvaṃ ca kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca hāṭakam ||
children.translated_text: The essence of black mica, <s>kānta</s> (lodestone), <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>hāṭaka</s>,

children.text: śuddhaṃ tāraṃ ca mākṣīkaṃ samabhāgāni kārayet
children.translated_text: together with purified silver and <s>mākṣīka</s>, should be made in equal parts.
Blown while placed in a closed crucible, it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> mass at once.
One <s>pala</s> of that <s>khoṭa</s> mass and one <s>pala</s> of <s>sūtaka</s>,
with two <s>palas</s> of <s>kunaṭī</s>, should all be ground together.
One should kill it in the <s>pātana-yantra</s>; by blowing, one brings it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s> mass.
One <s>pala</s> of black mica and one <s>pala</s> of <s>rasaka</s>, likewise,
and one <s>pala</s> of <s>sūtaka</s>: all this should be combined into one, O beloved.
One should grind it with the juice of <s>unmattaka</s> for two <s>praharas</s>,
or grind it for one day, mixed with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.
Afterwards one should make pellets and dry them in the shade.
Blown while placed in a great <s>varti</s>, the <s>sūtaka</s> becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> mass.
One should purify that <s>khoṭa</s> through a mixture of glass, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and liquid.
Having fused it together with gold, it is processed through the three <s>sāraṇās</s>.
With that very thousandth part he should cause penetration of copper.
By this sequential procedure the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) becomes capable of crore-fold penetration.
Two seeds of <s>palāśa</s> and one <s>pala</s> of <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury)
should be ground with sour citron juice and then dried in the shade.

children.text: tumbīkā meghanādī ca kākajaṅghā ca bhūlikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tumbikā</s>, <s>meghanādī</s>, <s>kākajaṅghā</s>, and <s>bhūlikā</s>,

children.text: stanyaṃ ca taiḥ praliptāyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ caiva nikṣipet
children.translated_text: and breast milk: in a crucible smeared with these, he should place it.
He should blow it with khadira charcoal; a <s>khoṭa</s> is produced and is imperishable.
It is to be ground in <s>palāśa</s> oil until it becomes a liquid paste.
When blown inside a sealed crucible, it immediately becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.
With previously purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and an equal amount of gold, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
he should make a pellet with it, after grinding it and making it firm.
Seeds of the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>, cotton seed, <s>vibhītaka</s>,

children.text: yavaciñcā ca vandhyā ca rājikā ca samanvitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>yavaciñcā</s>, <s>vandhyā</s>, and <s>rājikā</s>, all combined:

children.text: sūkṣmapiṇḍīkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ tena liptvā tu golakam
children.translated_text: all this should be made into fine pellets, and with it he should smear the pellet.
By seven <s>puṭa</s> firings, O goddess, the fixing of the <s>piṣṭikā</s> takes place.

children.text: bṛhatpuṭaṃ tato dattvā mūṣāyāṃ tu dhamettataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after giving a large <s>puṭa</s>, he should blow it in a crucible.

children.text: samāvartya tu taṃ sūtaṃ samahemnā niyojitam ||
children.translated_text: He should make that <s>sūta</s> circulate when it has been joined with an equal amount of gold.
With a hundredth part it will penetrate silver and gold, O you honored by the gods.
Again, by that same procedure, he should cause the fixing of the <s>piṣṭī</s>.
After causing it to undergo <s>sāraṇa</s>, then with gold there is a thousandfold penetration.
In this way, by the sequential procedure, it will penetrate lakhs and crores.
After making the pellet have an opening above the seven links,
in one year he will become free from wrinkles and gray hair.
With flowers of <s>cāṇḍālī</s> and <s>rākṣasī</s>, and then with honey, ghee, and borax,
one should apply that <s>abhraka</s> (mica), or else one among the eight <s>mahārasa</s> substances.
<s>Sūta</s> (mercury) equal to lead and tin, or gold and silver,
or <s>abhraka</s>, its liquefied essence: he should grind it for two watches.
Then, O dear one, the pellet dried in the shade and placed in a closed crucible,

children.text: dattvā laghupuṭaṃ dhmātaḥ khoṭo bhavati śobhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when given a light <s>puṭa</s> and blown, becomes an excellent <s>khoṭa</s>.
<s>Raṃbhā</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, <s>yavaciñcikā</s>,
<s>dīnārī</s>, <s>gorambhā</s>, <s>mīnākṣī</s>, and <s>kākamācikā</s>:
for <s>sūta</s> (mercury) ground with these, there is no rebirth.
By the sequential procedure as before, it becomes an excellent <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: viṣṇukrāntā ca vakrāṅkābalā ca tulasī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>vakrāṅkābalā</s>, and <s>tulasī</s>, likewise,
<s>mahāsomāhivallī</s> and <s>sūryāvarta</s>, O beautiful one:
<s>sūta</s> (mercury) ground with these should be brought to the state of <s>khoṭa</s> as before.

children.text: snuhīkṣīraṃ ca kāñjīraṃ bījāni kanakasya ca ||
children.translated_text: The milk of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>kāñjīra</s>, and the seeds of <s>kanaka</s>,
<s>kañcukī</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>indravāruṇī</s>, and <s>viṣamuṣṭikā</s>,
and water from the root of <s>palāśa</s>: with that he should grind the <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury).
The wise man should make a <s>piṣṭikā</s> with equal mercury in equal gold.
He should grind the <s>mahārasa</s> substances, half as much as the <s>piṣṭikā</s>, with herbal juices.
After grinding for three watches, the wise man should make a pellet.
Having bound the <s>piṣṭikā</s>, he should cook it thoroughly in sulphur oil.
He should place the pellet in a sealed crucible and dry it in the shade.

children.text: tato laghupuṭaṃ dattvā khadirāgnau tu dhāmayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after giving a light <s>puṭa</s>, he should blow it in a khadira fire.

children.text: khoṭavajjāyate devi saha hemnā tu dhāmayet
children.translated_text: It is produced like a <s>khoṭa</s>, O goddess; he should blow it together with gold.
It joins with the gold undiminished, and circulation is produced.
At that very moment a man obtains a divine body through the <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
The colored and activated <s>rasa</s> (mercury) will penetrate all metals.
For equal-part feeding of the <s>sūta</s> (mercury), he should grind it with herbal juices.

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ tu taṃ kṛtvā pūrvayogena dhāmayet ||
children.translated_text: After making it into a vanished paste, he should blow it by the previous procedure.
A divine <s>khoṭa</s> is produced, able to penetrate with a sixteenth part.
When bound by the procedure of links, it should penetrate ten times more.
Or, when bound as a powder, it should penetrate ten times more.
<s>Mṛgadūrvā</s>, <s>candravallī</s>, and ripe <s>bimbā</s> as well,

children.text: kāṅkṣīlā karavīraṃ ca bījaṃ conmattakasya ca
children.translated_text: <s>kāṅkṣīlā</s>, <s>karavīra</s>, and the seed of <s>unmattaka</s>,
combined with <s>kākāṇḍī</s> fruit: he should grind it, O beautiful goddess.
The wise man should make a <s>piṣṭikā</s> with equal mercury in equal gold.
Or, having made it undergo <s>sāraṇa</s>, he should prepare equal <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) with an equal amount.
He should grind the <s>mahārasa</s> <s>piṣṭikā</s> with herbal juices.
After grinding for three watches, the wise man should make a pellet.
He should place the pellet in a sealed crucible and dry it in the shade.

children.text: tato laghupuṭaṃ dattvā dhmātaḥ khoṭo bhavetpriye ||
children.translated_text: Then, after giving a light <s>puṭa</s>, when blown it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>, O dear one.
The <s>sāraṇa</s> of <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) is done with the juices of excellent <s>mṛgadūrvā</s> and <s>somā</s>.
It is subdued with the roots of the three <s>lāṅgalī</s> plants and with <s>rāmaṭha</s>.
The wise man should make a <s>piṣṭikā</s> joined with an equal amount of gold.
Or he should make a silver <s>piṣṭi</s> with an equal amount of <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
By the sequential procedure as before, it becomes an excellent <s>khoṭa</s>.
Placed in a sealed crucible in the ground, it should be steamed with a cultivator's fire.
After a day and night, or after three nights, powder-binding occurs from that.
That powder-binding produces penetration ten times greater.
<s>Sūta</s> (mercury) with the juice of <s>śūlinī</s>, together with <s>srotoñjana</s>,
by the <s>piṣṭikā</s> procedure as before, becomes an excellent <s>khoṭa</s>.
<s>Srotoñjana</s>, <s>satagara</s>, and <s>rasa</s> combined with the three products of creation:
the <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) quickly becomes able to withstand fire and accomplishes all operations.
Gold-mica, silver-mica, copper-mica, and mica with iron,

children.text: vaṅgābhraṃ caiva nāgābhraṃ saha sūtena bandhayet ||
children.translated_text: tin-mica and lead-mica: he should bind them together with <s>sūta</s> (mercury),
rubbed with whatever herbs are available and combined with the <s>mahārasa</s> substances.
With gold, silver, copper, iron, tin, and lead, likewise,

children.text: ebhirvyastaiḥ samastairvā piṣṭiṃ kṛtvā same samām
children.translated_text: with these separately or all together, one should make a <s>piṣṭi</s> (triturated amalgam), equal part for equal part.
One should calcine it by the previous procedure, in a womb-apparatus with a husk fire.

children.text: samāṃśaṃ sūtakaṃ dattvā vāraṃ vāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Adding mercury in an equal portion, again and again, repeatedly,
there arises a varied <s>khoṭa</s>; the great <s>rasa</s> becomes bound with <s>kānta</s> iron.
By the use of <s>saṅkalikā</s>, its penetration becomes ten times greater.
<s>Khoṭa</s>, <s>poṭa</s>, ash, and a dust-like preparation are the fifth.
Through these two operations of <s>nigala</s> (binding compound), the fruit of every binding arises.
The milk produced from <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, binding seeds, and <s>guggulu</s>,
with twice as much rock salt added: the skillful man should grind them.
Having made the binding of the <s>piṣṭikā</s> with this paste, O beautiful one,
and having made it the size of a bilva fruit, he should prepare a good, very firm crucible.

children.text: ūrdhvādho lavaṇaṃ dattvā mūṣāmadhye rasaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: After placing salt above and below, he should put the <s>rasa</s> in the middle of the crucible.
Powder of burnt conch and the like should be placed in the middle of the crucible.

children.text: mukhaṃ tasya dṛḍhaṃ baddhvā loṇamṛttikayā budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise man should bind its mouth firmly with saline clay.
He should make the sealing salt and have it dried in the shade.
This <s>nigala</s>-binding has been taught; it is not to be told even to one's son.
On the ground, with a husk-fire of a <s>karṣa</s>, he should apply gentle steaming.

children.text: ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā puṭaṃ dattvā prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Carefully applying a heating for a day and night, or for three nights,
he should make the well-smelted <s>rasendra</s> become a <s>khoṭa</s> with khadira charcoal.

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā dattvā tu śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: With <s>sauvīra</s>, borax, and glass, added again and again, he should purify it.
Unwasted, it combines with gold, and a proper fusion arises.
That equal-part feeding should be done with purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
He should blow it with the previous operation and make <s>rasendra</s> become a <s>khoṭa</s>.
By the use of <s>saṅkalikā</s>, its penetration becomes ten times greater.
The extract of palāśa seeds, <s>kokilā</s>, <s>unmatta</s>, and <s>vāruṇī</s>,
combined with the juice of <s>śūlinī</s>, should be ground together with rock salt.
Having made the wrapping of the <s>piṣṭikā</s>, one should bind it with the <s>nigala</s>.
With a leaf of mica, with vajra-arka milk, and with salt,
with <s>tāpya</s>, iron slag, sand, and clay,
the mercury-derived great <s>rasa</s>, bound in the <s>nigala</s> by these,
does not transgress its boundary, just as the great ocean does not transgress its shore.
Oil, arka milk, <s>kataka</s>, and <s>lāṅgalī</s> make an excellent <s>nigala</s>.
Crow dung, <s>brahmabīja</s> seeds, and <s>lāṅgalī</s> are another <s>nigala</s>.
<s>Vākucī</s>, <s>brahmabīja</s> seeds, and crab bones, O beautiful one,
with sea salt and <s>śāmbara</s> salt, are an excellent <s>nigala</s>.
The milk produced from <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, and <s>brahmabīja</s> seeds, should be prepared.

children.text: kanakasya ca bījāni loṇāṣṭena ca mardayet
children.translated_text: The seeds of <s>kanaka</s> too should be ground with the eight salts.
Another <s>nigala</s> is the roots of <s>gojihvā</s>; another is women's menstrual blood.
<s>Vākucī</s>, <s>brahmabīja</s> seeds, snuhī-arka milk, and rock salt,
with <s>jvālinī</s> and crow dung, are praised as an excellent <s>nigala</s>.
Salt, borax, alkali, realgar, orpiment, and sulfur,
as well as sour vetasa, <s>tāpya</s>, and cinnabar, all in equal parts,
joined with snuhī-arka milk, should be ground into an excellent <s>nigala</s>.
One should wrap the <s>piṣṭikā</s> with one of these <s>nigalas</s>.

children.text: loṇamūṣāgataṃ prāgvat khoṭaṃ kṛtvā tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: Placed in a salt crucible as before, one should make a <s>khoṭa</s> and then cause it to penetrate.
I shall describe the second pellet, the excellent fixation of the <s>piṣṭikā</s>.
With the urine and menstrual blood of a woman, rock salt, mica, and <s>guggulu</s>,

children.text: piṣṭīṃ saṃveṣṭya kalkena mṛdā tu punaraṣṭadhā ||
children.translated_text: one should wrap the <s>piṣṭi</s> with the paste and then again with clay eight times.
On the ground, with a husk-fire of a <s>karṣa</s>, he should apply gentle steaming.
For a day and night, or for three nights, he should bring it to the state of <s>khoṭa</s> as before.
<s>Vākucī</s>, <s>brahmabīja</s> seeds, mica, <s>vimala</s>, and jewel-stone,

children.text: sauvarcalaṃ saindhavaṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇaṃ gugguluṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: with black salt, rock salt, borax, and <s>guggulu</s> too,

children.text: dvipadīrajasā mūtraṃ suślakṣṇaṃ taṃ ca mardayet
children.translated_text: he should grind that very finely with a woman's menstrual blood and urine.
Having wrapped the <s>piṣṭi</s> with the paste, he should bring it to the state of <s>khoṭa</s> as before.
Now I shall explain the <s>mūrcchā</s> (stupefying fixation) of <s>rasa</s>, O supreme lady.

children.text: bāhlīkaṃ saindhavaṃ kanyā dhūśaro laśunaṃ vacā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bāhlīka</s>, rock salt, <s>kanyā</s>, <s>dhūśara</s>, garlic, and <s>vacā</s>,
<s>meghanādā</s> and <s>kākamācī</s>: he should grind the <s>rasa</s> with all these in equal parts.

children.text: ślakṣṇaṃ taṃ golakaṃ kṛtvā hiṃgunā veṣṭayedbahiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made that smooth mass into a pellet, he should wrap it outside with asafoetida.
Placing it in a salt-apparatus with an equal amount, he should cook it for a day.
With a fierce fire, once self-cooled, the <s>rasa</s> lying in the lower vessel,
having become powdered, should be taken up and tied in a dense cloth of double thickness.

children.text: baddhvā somānale yantre hyathordhvaṃ gandhakaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the <s>somānala</s> apparatus, he should place an equal amount of sulfur above.
He should cook it again with sulfur; in this way he should make it digest sulfur to six times its amount.
That <s>rasa</s>, O goddess, becomes <s>mūrchita</s> and removes all diseases.
Sulfur and sal ammoniac, each equal to the purified <s>sūta</s>,
should be ground smooth for one watch and placed in a glass bottle.
After coating the bottle with seven layers of clay and cloth, he should dry it in the heat.
He should cook the bottle in a sand-bath apparatus for twelve watches.

children.text: sa raso jāyate devi mūrchito rañjito bhavet
children.translated_text: That <s>rasa</s>, O goddess, becomes <s>mūrchita</s> and becomes colored.
Half as much sulfur as <s>rasa</s> should be ground for two watches in harsh sunlight.
Then it should be ground for three days with the juices of white <s>jayantī</s>.
After that, having made a pellet, he should confine it in a crucible.

children.text: śoṣayitvā dhamet kiṃcit saṃtaptāṃ tāṃ jale kṣipet
children.translated_text: Having dried it, he should blow it a little; when it is heated, he should throw it into water.
Taking that <s>rasendra</s>, he should impregnate it with the liquids of <s>gokṣura</s>.
The <s>sūta</s> becomes <s>mūrchita</s>, auspicious, and remover of all diseases.
It is imperishable, quick-melting, fiery, stainless, and heavy.

children.text: sphuṭanaḥ punarāvarto baddhaḥ sūtaḥ sa ucyate
children.translated_text: It breaks open and turns back again; that is called bound <s>sūta</s> (mercury).

children.text: rasasyāṣṭamabhāgaṃ tu svarṇaṃ vā nāgameva vā ||
children.translated_text: One should take gold, or else <s>nāga</s> (lead), in an eighth part of the <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
Ripe fruit of <s>śleṣmātaka</s> and seeds of <s>kokilākṣaka</s>,
together with powdered sesame oilcake, should be ground in a heated mortar.
One should put into it the five parts of <s>śālmalī</s> and the <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
It should be ground until it becomes a <s>jalūkā</s> (leech); after that one should add
camphor, oil of <s>vākucī</s>, rock salt, borax, and <s>kaṇā</s> (long pepper),
as well as the hairs of <s>kapikacchu</s>; all that should be ground with water.
This former <s>jalūkā</s> should be worked for three weeks in a heated mortar.
Through grinding, O worshipped by the gods, a divine <s>jalūkā</s> called <s>Mardanā</s> arises.
At the menstrual season of women, it is to be applied in the cavity of the vagina.
It removes their proud intoxication and makes them bewildered with passion.

children.text: bālye cāṣṭāṅgulā yojyā yauvane sā daśāṅgulā
children.translated_text: In girlhood it should be applied at eight finger-breadths; in youth it is ten finger-breadths.
For mature women the <s>jalūkā</s> should be applied at twelve finger-breadths.

children.text: yastu tāṃ dhārayenmūrdhni vīryaṃ tasya sthiraṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: If someone wears it on the head, his semen becomes stable.

children.text: rasendrasyāṣṭamaṃ bhāgaṃ svarṇaṃ vā nāgameva vā ||
children.translated_text: One should take gold, or else lead, in an eighth part of <s>rasendra</s> (mercury).
The bark of <s>śālmalī</s>, <s>hastikanda</s>, blue root, and sage's leaf:
with the liquids of these, everything should be ground tirelessly in a heated mortar.
Ripe fruit of <s>śleṣmātaka</s> and seeds of <s>kokilākṣaka</s>,
and the well-ripened pulp of <s>bilva</s> should be put into it and ground.

children.text: jalūkā jāyate yāvat karpūrādyaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Until a <s>jalūkā</s> arises, and camphor and the rest are added as before,
one should put them into it and grind for three weeks in a heated mortar.
The <s>jalūkā</s> called <s>Manmathā</s> comes into being, giving results as before.
One should take gold, or else lead, in an eighth part of <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury).

children.text: śuṇṭhī bhṛṅgī varā kṣaudrī chāgakṣīraghṛtaṃ gavām
children.translated_text: Dry ginger, <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>varā</s>, honey, goat's milk, cow's ghee,
and urine should be ground for three times seven days in a heated mortar.
Until a <s>jalūkā</s> arises, camphor and the rest are added as before.
It should be ground for twenty-one days, and an auspicious <s>jalūkā</s> comes into being.
O queen of the gods, the one called <s>Kandarpā</s> gives results as before.
One should grind four <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in a mortar for three days.
Three <s>palas</s> of mango exudation should be added little by little.
Milk of <s>mahāśamī</s> should also be supplied, sufficient for the grinding.
This <s>jalūkā</s> called <s>Madanā</s> arises, bringing benefit to men.
For passionate, proud women it acts like a liquefying fire and ghee.
By the procedure already given, it becomes a means of arresting semen.

children.text: nānāvarṇaṃ tathā svacchaṃ dhṛtaṃ yonau jalūkavat ||
children.translated_text: Variegated in color and clear, when held in the vagina like a <s>jalūkā</s>,
the <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) becomes bound; this is the sign of binding as a <s>jalūkā</s>.
I shall explain the terminology; listen attentively.

children.text: ardhaṃ siddharasaṃ devi triṣvekaṃ hemabhasma ca ||
children.translated_text: Half should be perfected <s>rasa</s>, O goddess, and one third should be ash of gold.
One quarter part should be ash of silver, and one sixth part ash of copper.
One eighth part should be magnetic mica, and one sixteenth part the nine jewels.
With <s>Raseśvara</s> in view, to an intelligent physician of <s>rasa</s>,
to an accomplished teacher of <s>rasa</s>, one should give it for the attainment of the desired aim.
<s>Rasa</s> (mercury) ground with metals and with sulphur and the like, without liquids,
smooth and resembling lampblack, is called <s>kajjalī</s>.

children.text: sadrave marditaḥ so'pi iti pākarasaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: When that same substance is ground with liquid, it is known as <s>pākarasa</s>.
From <s>rasa</s> in a twelve-part measure and sulphur equal to half a <s>niṣka</s>, added bit by bit in the mortar,
one should grind in fierce sunlight; that <s>piṣṭi</s> becomes like fresh butter.

children.text: khalve vimardya gandhena dugdhena saha pāradam ||
children.translated_text: Others hold that when mercury is ground in a mortar with sulphur and milk,

children.text: peṣaṇātpiṣṭitāṃ yāti sā piṣṭīti matā paraiḥ
children.translated_text: through grinding it reaches the state of <s>piṣṭi</s>, and that is called <s>piṣṭi</s>.
A <s>piṣṭikā</s> made from <s>rasa</s> with a quarter part of gold
is <s>pātanapiṣṭi</s>; the same is made with silver and other metals.
Silver or gold, struck down by <s>rasa</s>, sulphur, and the like,

children.text: samutthitaṃ ca bahuśaḥ sā kṛṣṭī hematārayoḥ
children.translated_text: and repeatedly brought up, is the <s>kṛṣṭi</s> of gold and silver.

children.text: kṛṣṭīṃ kṣiptvā suvarṇānte na varṇo hīyate tayā ||
children.translated_text: When <s>kṛṣṭi</s> is put into melted gold, the color is not diminished by it.
A seed made with gold <s>kṛṣṭi</s> is the coloring preparation of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
Copper mixed with <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), melted, should be thrown in repeatedly
into sulphur and the juice of <s>likuca</s>; the excellent metal that comes out
and reddens gold with it is called <s>hemaraktī</s>.
When it is cast into molten gold, it produces an excellence of color.
It is also a coloring agent for silver and produces the red color of seeds.
In just this way the pleasing <s>tāraraktī</s> should be prepared.
It is indeed the coloring agent of silver and also the coloring agent of seeds.

children.text: mṛtena vā baddharasena vānyalohena vā sādhitamanyaloham
children.translated_text: Another metal prepared with calcined <s>rasa</s>, or with bound <s>rasa</s>, or with another metal,

children.text: sitaṃ hi pītatvamupāgataṃ taddalaṃ hi candrānalayoḥ prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: when white has come to yellowness, is known as the <s>dala</s> of silver and gold.
A white metal joined with <s>rasa</s> through apparent calcination and binding,

children.text: sādhitaṃ vānyalohena sitaṃ pītaṃ hi taddalam ||
children.translated_text: or prepared with another metal, becomes yellow; that too is <s>dala</s>.
<s>Kānta</s> iron struck down with <s>tāpya</s> and brought up seven times,
that pair, whether two <s>palas</s>, and two <s>palas</s> of copper ash,
should all be placed in a crucible and blown strongly seven times.
That is called <s>ayonāga</s>, effective for the body and for metals.
A pill of that, made with <s>rasa</s> in the <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus,

children.text: sā dhṛtā vadane hanti meharogān aśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: when held in the mouth, destroys all diseases of urinary disorder.
It gives firmness to the teeth, and makes the eyes like the eyes of a vulture.
Likewise it cures other diseases arising in the generative field and diseases originating above the collarbone.
Copper struck down with <s>mākṣika</s> and brought up ten times,
and likewise thoroughly purified lead, these two together measuring four <s>palas</s>,
again struck down with blue antimony and brought up seven times,
this, when perfected, is indeed called <s>śulbanāga</s>.
By means of it, <s>sūtendra</s> (mercury) is prepared; when held in men's mouths,
within a single month it destroys the whole mass of urinary disorders.
For one who eats wholesome food, within a year it removes grey hair together with wrinkles;
he has vulture-like sight, shining vision, and is endowed with complete health.

children.text: lohaṃ lohāntare kṣiptaṃ dhmātaṃ nirvāpitaṃ drave
children.translated_text: When a metal is thrown into another metal, blown, and quenched in liquid,
and has become pale-yellow in lustre, it is called <s>piñjarī</s>.

children.text: bhāgāḥ ṣoḍaśa tārasya tathā dvādaśa bhāsvataḥ
children.translated_text: Sixteen parts of silver and likewise twelve parts of gold,
melted together in one place, are called <s>candrārka</s>.
If another metal is thrown by means of a curved tube into the metal being maintained,
that quenching is indeed called <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> by physicians.
One should cast the <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> substance into the material to be carried through, in an equal portion.

children.text: āvāpyaṃ vāpanīyaṃ ca bhāge dṛṣṭe ca dṛṣṭavat ||
children.translated_text: The substance to be added and the one to be infused are to be handled according to the observed proportion and as previously observed.

children.text: mṛtaṃ tarati yattoye lohaṃ vāritaraṃ hi tat
children.translated_text: A calcined metal that floats on water is indeed called <s>vāritara</s>.
That which, rubbed between thumb and forefinger, enters between the lines,
is designated calcined metal under the name <s>rekhāpūrṇa</s>.
When combined with jaggery, <s>guñjā</s>, pleasant-to-touch substances, honey, and ghee,
and it does not return to its original state through blowing, it is called <s>apunarbhava</s> (not reborn).

children.text: lohena saha saṃyuktaṃ dhmātaṃ rūpyeṇa cel lihet ||
children.translated_text: If, joined with metal and blown, it licks together with silver,
then that metal is said to be <s>niruttha</s>, and that is <s>apunarbhava</s>.

children.text: evaṃ rūpyaṃ satāmraṃ ceddhmātaṃ tāmre lagenna hi ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, if silver with copper, when blown, does not adhere to copper,

children.text: tadā nirutthaṃ mantavyaṃ rajataṃ ca bhiṣagvaraiḥ
children.translated_text: then that silver is to be regarded as <s>niruttha</s> by the best physicians.
When, by a special form of <s>nirvāhaṇa</s>, its color becomes similar in that way,
soft and resembling variegated color, that is called <s>bīja</s> (seed).
This very thing is indeed designated by physicians as <s>uttāraṇa</s> (raising out).
The destruction of one metal among two metals that have been mixed together,
when strongly blown through a curved tube, is stated to be <s>tāḍana</s> (striking).
Powdered mica, mixed with rice, tied in cloth and placed in sour gruel,
when it has passed out from the cloth by rubbing, is called <s>dhānyābhra</s> (grain-mica).
When, mixed with alkaline, sour, and solvent substances, it is blown in an ore furnace,
the essence that comes out from it is called <s>sattva</s>.
With furnace-pits filled up to the top and through the application of blowing with charcoal,
what reaches the ears of the crucible is considered <s>ekakolīśaka</s>.
<s>Śikhitra</s>, residues of fire, and dead coals are <s>kokila</s> charcoal;
and black-bodied <s>kokilas</s>: these are mutually synonymous terms.

children.text: drāvaṇe sattvapāte ca mādhūkāḥ khādirāḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: For melting and for the falling of <s>sattva</s>, charcoal from <s>madhūka</s> and <s>khadira</s> is good;
for things hard to melt, that born from bamboo is good, and for steaming, that from jujube is good.
The <s>rasa</s> that has been drawn out from the apparatus called <s>Vidyādhara</s>, after being rubbed with ginger juice,
is called <s>hiṅgulākṛṣṭa</s> (extracted from cinnabar).
Bronze containing a little tin, struck with a curved tube,
when freed from tin, is that copper called <s>ghoṣākṛṣṭa</s>.
Twenty <s>palas</s> of purified lead should be made into disks,
and smeared with realgar ground together with <s>rūpikā</s> milk.
After enclosing it in a covered earthen saucer, one should cook it with a <s>kroḍapuṭa</s> heating.
One should carefully cook it that many times, until ash is produced.
After grinding it with jaggery, <s>guggulu</s>, <s>guñjā</s>, ghee, and borax,
one should confine it inside a crucible and then raise it again by blowing.
Then, making a disk again with it, one should smear it with mercury measuring one <s>pala</s>,
and also smear it with realgar together with the milk of white <s>arka</s>.
In this way one should cook it with <s>gajapuṭa</s> heat for twenty times, indeed;

children.text: puṭe puṭe ca nāgasya kuryādutthāpanaṃ khalu ||
children.translated_text: and at every heating one should surely perform the raising of the lead.
One should properly pour it ten times with the liquids of <s>nīlajyotis</s>.

children.text: iti siddhaṃ hi tat sīsaṃ karṣamātrāvaśeṣitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus that lead is perfected, with only a <s>karṣa</s> measure remaining.
It is called by the name <s>guhyanāga</s>, supreme in <s>rasa</s> and <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: niṣkamātraṃ tu nāge'smin lohākhye yā drute sati ||
children.translated_text: When, in this lead called metal, there is a molten quantity of one <s>niṣka</s>,

children.text: svato lakṣaguṇāṃ haimīṃ śalākāṃ grasate dhruvam
children.translated_text: it certainly swallows by itself a golden rod a hundred-thousand times its own measure.
When heated with oil, that gold certainly adheres and is emitted again.
This <s>guhyanāga</s> is taught as powerful, self-willed <s>Bhairava</s>.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ nīlāñjanopetaṃ dhmātaṃ hi bahuśo dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: Strong metal combined with blue antimony, firmly blown many times,
soft, black, and quickly melting, is called excellent lead.
The coming forth again of what has been calcined is said to be called <s>utthāpana</s> (raising).

children.text: drutadravyasya nikṣepo drave tat ḍhālanaṃ matam
children.translated_text: The casting of a molten substance into a liquid is considered <s>ḍhālana</s> (pouring).
Thirty <s>palas</s> of lead, rubbed with the milk of <s>bhānu</s>,
should be thoroughly ground and heated until it remains only a <s>karṣa</s>.
Even by a thousand heatings it never undergoes diminution.
This, arising from lead, is designated <s>capala</s> by the practitioners.

children.text: itthaṃ hi capalaḥ kāryo vaṅgasyāpi na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In just this manner <s>capala</s> is to be made from tin also; there is no doubt.
Mercury alone is bound when touched by a hand that has been touched by it.

children.text: sa raso dhātuvādeṣu śasyate na rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: That <s>rasa</s> is praised in doctrines of metals, but not in <s>rasāyana</s>.
This has indeed been taught by <s>Lokanātha</s>, who is called <s>Karpaṇa</s>.
Fine powder of whirling stone should be combined with a fifth part.
One should grind it for one day with water from the root of <s>kumārī</s>,
or with the fresh juice of <s>śārṅgerī</s>, for one day without interruption.
And, after being washed with <s>bhūnāga</s>, one should grind it for two days.
Then, with one <s>pala</s> of lead and also with just as much tin,
together with ten <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>rasendra</s> (mercury), one should make a finely ground paste.
After combining it with the first paste, one should triturate it as before.
Then, with one <s>śāṇa</s> of <s>rasendra</s> and with the essence of <s>rasaka</s>,

children.text: piṣṭīṃ kṛtvā tu pūrveṇa pūrvakalkaiśca yojayet ||
children.translated_text: one should make a <s>piṣṭi</s> (amalgam-paste) and combine it with the previous material and the earlier pastes.
Next, after washing it with warm <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel), one should dry it.
One should take half a <s>pala</s> with purified <s>śasya</s> and eight <s>guñjās</s> of <s>rasa</s> (mercury),
grind it with <s>kāñjika</s>, and make pills the size of peppercorns.
Having enclosed it in a diamond-hard crucible and sealed the joint,
one should heat it properly with nine <s>śikhitras</s> and blow it with a pair of bellows.
Then one should take out, from every side, the essence that is in the crucible.
One should blow it in an open crucible and purify it through a bent tube.

children.text: daśaśāṇaṃ hi tatsatvaṃ bhasmanā lavaṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: That essence, measuring ten <s>śāṇas</s>, should be ground with ash, salt,
and <s>kāñjika</s>, and purified by the procedure of <s>puṭa</s> (sealed heating).
When it measures three <s>niṣkas</s>, then with the ash described earlier,
one should smelt eighty times as much lead and draw it off.
By this amount that earlier mercury is in no way diminished.
This is taught as <s>capala</s> by <s>Śambhu</s>, lord of the world.

children.text: anenāpi rasaḥ śīghraṃ pūrvavad badhyate sukham ||
children.translated_text: By this too <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is quickly and easily bound as before.
After being heated ten times with powder of <s>kāravallī</s> root,
it becomes freed from lead and consumes the whole <s>grāsa</s> (feed).
It becomes easy to work in an open crucible and exceedingly superior in quality.
This <s>rasa</s>, once its <s>grāsa</s> has been digested, becomes effective for the body and for metals.
Washed with water mixed with the dung of <s>bhūbhujaṅga</s>, its impurity is removed.
When black in color, it is called <s>dhauta</s> by the practitioners of <s>rasa</s>.
The combining of two substances by blowing or smelting is called <s>dvaṃdvāna</s> (pairing/alloying).
When there is an addition to a portion greater in silver, it is a matching or assimilating coloration.
Or, by foils, there is the <s>varṇikāgrāsa</s> (coloring feed), a breaking operation made by the adepts.
From a paste of <s>pataṅgī</s>, silverness and goldness arise in metal.

children.text: dināni katicit sthitvā yātyasau phullikā matā
children.translated_text: After remaining for some days it passes off; this is considered <s>phullikā</s>.
From metal colored with half as much <s>rasa</s>, or else after a long time,
it issues forth; this is designated by the name <s>pataṅgīrāga</s>.
What is done by casting another substance, such as metal and the like, into a molten material,
is <s>āvāpa</s>; <s>pratīvāpa</s> is considered that very same covering operation.
When metal is molten and standing in the fire, after one has waited for eight <s>nimeṣas</s>,
the sprinkling of water upon it is remembered as <s>abhiṣeka</s>.

children.text: nāgaṃ vā vaṅgaṃ vā pradrāvya niṣecayecchataṃ vārān ||
children.translated_text: One should melt lead or tin and quench it a hundred times.
In the prescribed substance, striking that molten material is indeed this <s>abhiṣeka</s>.
Casting what has been heated into water is <s>nirvāpa</s> (quenching), and the heating is <s>tapana</s>.
<s>Prativāpa</s> and the other operations should be performed on very pure molten metal.
When the fire has blazing flames and a white upward flare,
then it should be known as <s>śuddhāvarta</s>; that is the time for the emergence of essence.
When, during blowing, a flame resembling the substance being melted is seen,
that is its readiness to melt; it is called <s>rekhāvarta</s>.
That which becomes cool while still in the fire is called <s>svāṅgaśītala</s>.
That which becomes cool after being drawn away from the fire is termed <s>vahniśīta</s>.
Cooking a substance placed in a <s>ḍolāyantra</s> with alkalies, acids, or medicines
is called <s>svedana</s> (sudation), and it loosens impurities.
Together with the prescribed medicines, all sour liquids, and <s>kāñjika</s> as well,
grinding is called <s>mardana</s> (trituration), and it destroys external impurity.
By <s>mardana</s> with the desired medicines, it produces the loss of the ordinary paste-state.
That is <s>mūrcchana</s>; it destroys the watery, stony, and earthy sheaths.
What brings about the state of <s>piṣṭi</s> through the destruction of the original form
and the increase by mastered mercury is called <s>naṣṭapiṣṭi</s>.
The restoration of its own form again by procedures of sweating, heating, and the like
is called <s>utthāpana</s>; it removes the defects of <s>mūrcchā</s>.
The expulsion upward, downward, and sideways of mercury rubbed with the stated medicines and placed in an apparatus
is taught under the name <s>pātana</s>; it destroys the coating produced by contact with tin and lead.
<s>Rasa</s> (mercury) mixed with water and rock salt for three days
and left in an <s>āpyāyinī</s> pot is what is called <s>rodhana</s>.
After <s>rodhana</s>, for the mercury that has gained potency, in order to remove its fickleness,

children.text: kriyate yo ghaṭe svedaḥ proktaṃ niyamanaṃ hi tat
children.translated_text: the sweating that is performed in a vessel is indeed declared to be <s>niyamana</s>.
When it is combined with metals, minerals, roots, and the like inside a vessel,

children.text: grāsārthaṃ tridinaṃ svedo dīpanaṃ tanmataṃ budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: sweating it for three days for the sake of feeding is considered <s>dīpana</s> by the wise.
For mercury of this measure, the measure consisting of an edible substance
which is stated as 'so much' is called the <s>grāsamāna</s> (measure of feed).
The conveying of the <s>grāsa</s>, the melting within the womb, and <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion)
are taught by the best authorities as the three forms of <s>jāraṇā</s>.
<s>Grāsa</s>, <s>piṇḍa</s>, and <s>parīṇāma</s> are again three further names.

children.text: samukhā nirmukhā ceti jāraṇā dvividhā matā
children.translated_text: <s>Jāraṇā</s> is considered twofold: with a mouth and without a mouth.
The mouthless <s>jāraṇā</s> is said to occur through the addition of seed in a fractional portion.

children.text: śuddhaṃ svarṇaṃ ca rūpyaṃ ca bījamityabhidhīyate
children.translated_text: Pure gold and silver are called the <s>bīja</s> (seed).
The insertion of seed in a sixty-fourth part is called the <s>mukha</s> (mouth).

children.text: evaṃ kṛte raso grāsalolupo mukhavān bhavet
children.translated_text: When this has been done, <s>rasa</s> becomes greedy for feed and possesses a mouth.
It becomes capable of consuming even hard metals.
This is called the mouthed <s>jāraṇā</s>, the immortalizing <s>jāraṇā</s>.
Because of combination with divine medicines, it remains in the open furnaces.
That which consumes all metals and the rest is one possessed of a <s>rākṣasavaktra</s> (demonic mouth).
The casting of morsels into the belly of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is regarded as <s>cāraṇā</s>.
