The liquefaction, inside the womb, of what has been swallowed is called <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction).
But when dense essence and the like are liquefied outside
for the digestion of <s>rasendra</s> (lord mercury), that is called <s>bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction).

children.text: nirlepitvaṃ dravatvaṃ ca tejastvaṃ laghutā tathā ||
children.translated_text: Non-adhesiveness, fluidity, fiery brilliance, lightness,
and non-combination with <s>sūta</s> (mercury): these are the five marks of <s>druti</s> (liquefaction).
When, through the use of medicines, ghee, and the like, metals, minerals, and so on
always rise up in fluid form, that is called <s>druti</s>.
The maturation of a liquefied morsel, through the use of <s>biḍa</s>, apparatus, and the like,
is called <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion); its varieties exist by the tens of millions.
With alkalis, acids, sulphur and the like, urines, and also substances containing salt,
what is used for digesting a morsel of <s>rasa</s> is called <s>biḍa</s>.
Through the digestion of perfected seed, essence, and the like, in the case of <s>rasa</s>,
the production of yellow and other colors is declared to be <s>rañjana</s> (coloring).
When gold and the like are thrown into <s>sūta</s> set in an apparatus containing oil,
that process, which increases penetration in metal, is called <s>sāraṇā</s>.
When <s>rasa</s>, furnished with a penetrating medicine, is cast into a substance,

children.text: vedha ityucyate tajjñaiḥ sa cānekavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: that is called <s>vedha</s> by those who know; it is remembered as being of many kinds.
There are <s>lepa</s> (smearing), <s>kṣepa</s> (casting), <s>kunta</s> (piercing), the one called <s>śabda</s>, and the one named <s>dhūma</s>.

children.text: lepena kurute lohaṃ svarṇaṃ vā rajataṃ tathā
children.translated_text: When by smearing it makes a metal into gold or also into silver,

children.text: lepavedhaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ puṭamatra ca saukaram ||
children.translated_text: that should be known as <s>lepavedha</s>; in this case firing in a closed crucible is easy.
The casting into molten metal is the <s>vedha</s> called <s>kṣepa</s>.
When molten material is struck with <s>sūta</s> held in tongs,
producing the state of gold and the like, that is called <s>kuntavedha</s>.
When the fire is smoking, from the smoke of <s>rasa</s> cast within,
the bringing of gold and the like into metal is called <s>dhūmavedha</s>.
When <s>rasa</s> is held in the mouth and metal is blown through a tube,
the production of goldness or silverness is called <s>śabdavedha</s>.
The removal of impurity and the like from a lump-substance by means of <s>sūta</s>,
and the making manifest of its color, is called <s>utpāṭana</s>.
When, together with alkalis, acids, and medicines, it is carefully sealed in a vessel
and buried in the ground, that is declared to be <s>svedana</s> (steaming).
When <s>rasa</s> combined with medicines is carefully sealed in a vessel
and placed inside a hearth constantly joined with fire, that is called <s>saṃnyāsa</s>.
These two, <s>sveda</s> and <s>saṃnyāsa</s>, are certainly, for the king <s>rasa</s>,
producers of qualities and potency, and also causes of rapid pervasion.

children.text: raso niyantryate yena yantraṃ taditi kathyate
children.translated_text: That by which <s>rasa</s> is controlled is called a <s>yantra</s> (apparatus).
A <s>khalvayantra</s> (mortar apparatus) is said to be of two kinds for grinding and related operations.
The mortar, O goddess, may be made of metal, or else produced from stone.

children.text: khalvayogyā śilā nīlā śyāmā snigdhā dṛḍhā guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: A stone suitable for a mortar is blue-black, dark, smooth, firm, and heavy.
The <s>khalvayantra</s> is said to be of two kinds for grinding the face of <s>rasa</s> and the rest.
Sixteen fingers high, nine fingers wide,
with a rubbing pestle twenty-four fingers long and twelve fingers wide,
or else twenty fingers long and ten fingers high:
that should be known as the measure of a mortar; it is best for grinding <s>rasa</s>.
A round mortar is sixteen fingers in breadth,
four fingers deep, and made very smooth in the middle.
The grinding pestle is flattened below, easy to grasp, and peaked above.
This round mortar gives very great ease in grinding.
Such a metal mortar may also be made of iron or of magnetic iron.
Below it a basin should be made, suitable for kindling fire.

children.text: utsedhena navāṅgulaḥ khalu kalātulyāṅgulāyāmavān vistāreṇa navāṅgulo rasamitair nimnaistathaivāṅgulaiḥ
children.translated_text: It is nine fingers high, with a length of finger-measure equal to the section, nine fingers in breadth, and likewise with depressions measured by fingers of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: kaṇṭhe dvyaṅgulavistaro'timasṛṇo droṇārdhacandrākṛtir gharṣaścaiva daśāṅgulaśca tadidaṃ khalvākhyayantraṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: At the neck it is two fingers wide and very smooth; the basin is half-moon-shaped, and the rubbing pestle is ten fingers long. This is regarded as the apparatus called a mortar.
In this, five <s>palas</s> of <s>sūta</s> should be ground for purification.
According to the suitability of each case, one should purify it in other mortars as well.
In metal, the mortar is nine fingers and six fingers deep,
and the grinder is eight fingers; this is the one called the heated mortar.
Having made a hearth in the form of a mortar and filled it with coals,

children.text: tasminniveśya taṃ khalvaṃ pārśve bhastrikayā dhamet
children.translated_text: one should place that mortar in it and blow from the side with a bellows.
A <s>piṣṭi</s> (ground amalgam), ground in that and well mixed with alkalis and acids,
liquefies with very great speed when heated; there is no doubt about this.
Made of magnetic iron, this <s>rasa</s> becomes ten-million-fold in power.
In the apparatus, in an iron vessel, there are two rings on the sides.
A similar, smaller vessel has a chamber indicating the rings.
Having set it upon the former vessel, one should cast upon the small vessel
stupefied <s>rasa</s>, and fill the large vessel with <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel).
In this way one should steam it for two <s>yāmas</s> for the purpose of raising up the <s>rasa</s>.
That is the <s>khavalabhīyantra</s>, which brings about excellence in <s>rasa</s>.
In a vessel made of fine magnetic iron, the <s>rasa</s> becomes still more excellent.
Eight fingers in measure, properly round, flat at the bottom,
and provided, four fingers below the neck, with a basin
four fingers wide, deep, and firmly joined.
And such a pot should be sixteen finger-breadths wide at the base,
and furnished with an opening nine finger-breadths wide.

children.text: pūrve ghaṭe rasaṃ kṣiptvā nyubjāṃ dadyātparāṃ ghaṭīm
children.translated_text: After putting the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) in the first pot, one should place another pot upside down over it,
with its upper part depressed all around and fitted with a firm rim.
One should pour water into the rim or trough and light a fire below.
This is the upward-sublimation apparatus, as taught by <s>Nandin</s>.
Then above that vessel one should place another small vessel facing downward,
made flattened, with mercury smeared on the inside of its bottom.
After placing it in that muddy pit, one should kindle fire on the top.
This is the downward-sublimation apparatus; thus it has been described.
One should put the <s>rasa</s> in a long pot fitted with a tube bent downward,
and that tube should indeed be inserted into the cavity of another pot.
There, having properly sealed the mouths of the two pots below with clay,
one should kindle an intense fire beneath the mercury pot.
In the other pot one should pour water that is sweet and cool.
This is called transverse distillation by the specialists.
Thus the threefold set of apparatuses for the three kinds of distillation has been stated.
Without these distillations, <s>sūta</s> (mercury) becomes exceedingly defective.
Why is it not freed from faults by just three upward sublimations?
Because through cooking in two divisions, through the mutual conjunction of substances,
and through transfer into another vessel, various qualities indeed arise.
Broken grains in a mortar, with water, become rice free from water.
This very distillation is proclaimed to be the great purification called <s>taṇḍulī</s>.
One should set it in a wide-mouthed vessel filled with water.
Another broad and properly made shallow vessel should be placed in its middle.

children.text: ālavālaṃ biḍaiḥ kṛtvā tanmadhye pāradaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having made a basin there with <s>biḍa</s> salts, one should put mercury in its middle.
Putting <s>biḍa</s> above and below, and carefully closing it with a lid,
one applies a <s>puṭa</s> (closed heating) according to suitability; this is so explained.
That apparatus is named <s>kacchapa</s> and is taught for the digestion of mercury.
Having made an iron crucible with a round base,
of a span in size and fashioned from magnetic iron,
or else made from common iron, two finger-breadths below the neck,
one should set a two-finger-breadth ring in the middle region below the neck,
a bracelet-like support for the cover, as broad as a tamarind leaf.
The cover should fit inside, have a knob, and have close-fitting joints.
Having made a vessel with a pierced opening in its bottom, facing downward,
one should suspend it above by means of the apparatus, seal it, and dry it.
Then at the neck of the vessel one should arrange the holding of the <s>puṭa</s> fire.
An apparatus of this form is called the <s>āntarālika</s>.
With it one should digest sulphur and even substances that produce liquefaction within.
One should make a heating crucible of clay, firm and measuring an <s>aratni</s>,
very firm, and in its middle provided with a two-finger-breadth opening.
One should place an iron vessel made of magnetic iron above the substance,
and fill the heater on all sides with purified sand.

children.text: tāṃ ca cullyāṃ samāropya kṣepaṃ kṣepaṃ biḍadravam
children.translated_text: Then, setting it on a stove, one should repeatedly add liquid <s>biḍa</s>,
and then kindle a fire with flames the measure of a big toe.
All substances such as iron and mica should be digested above the mercury.
This is called the <s>tāpikā</s> apparatus, easy to use for mercury digestion.

children.text: sthālyāṃ vinikṣipya rasādivastu svarṇādi khoryāṃ pravidhāya bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: After placing mercury and the other substances in a bowl, and again arranging gold and the like in a crucible,

children.text: amlena cordhvaṃ lavaṇāni dattvā cullyāṃ pacettatpratigarbhayantram ||
children.translated_text: then adding acids above and salts, one should cook it on a stove; that is the internal-chamber apparatus.
Then one should seal the crucible, the lid, and the bowl with the greatest care.

children.text: sthālyāṃ mallena vā khoryāṃ kṣiptvā vastu nirudhya ca ||
children.translated_text: Or, having put the substance in the bowl with a lid, or in the crucible, and having sealed it,
and having put in cloth and the like and sealed it, the cooking becomes the <s>garbha</s> apparatus.
A round iron cup with an upward rod whose tip is bent
is the apparatus called <s>pālikā</s>, intended for the digestion of offerings.
It holds four <s>prasthas</s> of water and has an opening of four finger-breadths.
This is called the <s>ghaṭī</s> apparatus, remembered for replenishment.

children.text: vidhāya vartulaṃ gartaṃ mallamatra nidhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Having made a round pit and placed a lid there,
one should set there a fine brick with a pit in the middle.
Around the pit one should make a rim one finger-breadth high.

children.text: tatra sūtaṃ vinikṣipya gartāsye vasanaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: There one should place <s>sūta</s> (mercury), and put a cloth over the mouth of the pit.
One should put sulphur there and seal the opening with a lid.
Between the lid and the rim one should seal it properly with clay.

children.text: vanotpalaiḥ puṭaṃ deyaṃ kapotākhyaṃ na cādhikam ||
children.translated_text: A <s>kapota</s>-named <s>puṭa</s> should be given with forest cow-dung cakes, and not more.
This is the brick apparatus; by it one should digest sulphur.
Having placed one bowl upon another and sealed it properly,
one should pour water into the upper bowl and kindle fire below.
This is the <s>vidyādhara</s> apparatus, used for extracting from cinnabar.

children.text: yantraṃ sthālyupari sthālīṃ nyubjāṃ dattvā nirudhyate
children.translated_text: When, as an apparatus, an inverted bowl is placed upon a bowl and sealed,
that apparatus is called <s>ḍamaruka</s> and is useful for binding mercury.
In the middle of a lid one should make a pit; in it are mercury with sulphur.
Around the pit one should make a wall three finger-breadths high.
Then one should cover it properly with a crucible shaped like a cow's teat,
having sealed it well with water and clay, as is being properly described here.
It is to be mixed with a decoction of <s>barbūra</s>, made like a paste.
fine powder of old slag, mixed with powdered jaggery.

children.text: iyaṃ hi jalamṛtproktā durbhedyā salilaiḥ khalu
children.translated_text: This indeed is called water-clay; it is truly hard for waters to pierce.
And with chalk, salt, and slag, rubbed together with buffalo milk,
it becomes fire-clay, capable indeed of withstanding the fierce heat of fire.

children.text: etayormṛtsnayo ruddho na gantuṃ kṣamate rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is enclosed by these two clays, it cannot escape.
Then, having poured in water, one should kindle the fire below.
This is called the <s>nābhiyantra</s>, as taught by <s>Nandin</s>, the knower of reality.
By this, purified sulphur is digested in mercury without smoke.
A crucible inserted into the belly of a crucible, equally round at the beginning and end,

children.text: cipiṭā ca tale proktaṃ grastayantraṃ manīṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: and said to be flattened at the bottom, is the <s>grastayantra</s>, according to the wise.
It has been taught by the knowers of <s>rasa</s> for the binding of the lord mercury.
Two crucibles shaped like eggplants, and below the necks of those two
a straight tube, a span in measure, is attached, together with sulphur.
Into one of them one should put mercury, and into the other powdered sulphur.
Having sealed the mouths of the crucibles, one should place them in a sand apparatus.
One should kindle fire below; this is called the <s>tulāyantra</s>.
It is proclaimed for the digestion of <s>śilā</s>, <s>tālaka</s>, sulphur, and mineral stone.

children.text: sthālyāṃ tāmrādi nikṣipya mallenāsyaṃ nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: Having placed copper and the like in a pot and closed its mouth with a lid,
what is cooked while standing in the pot is remembered as the <s>sthālīyantra</s>.
Inside the belly of a large vessel one should place clean sand,
heaped to the height of a span; then one should set there
a well-fired earthen furnace, twelve finger-breadths high,
six finger-breadths wide, and made very smooth in the middle.
The lid should be five finger-breadths, sharp-pointed and made like a bud.

children.text: na nyūnaṃ nādhikaṃ koṣṭhe kaṇṭhato masṛṇā bahiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the furnace it should be neither smaller nor larger, and outside it should be smooth from the neck.
Into the furnace one should put six <s>palas</s> of sulphur, finely powdered.
Then one should set in place and stabilize an iron tripod.

children.text: tasyāṃ ca vinyasetkhorīṃ lauhīṃ vā kāntalohajām
children.translated_text: On it one should place a <s>khorī</s>, made of iron or of <s>kāntaloha</s>.
Into that one should put purified mercury, in the measure of twenty <s>palas</s>.
Borax, sulphur, and mercury should be treated with juices of garlic.
Covering it with the previously described lid, with the point turned downward,
one should make a joint-seal with lime, clay, jaggery, and the like.
When the joint-seal has dried, one should put sand above it.
Then, having sealed the mouth of the vessel, one should kindle fire below it.
In this way, for three <s>yāmas</s>, the smoke arising from the sulphur
adheres to the lid, melts, and falls down into the mercury.

children.text: evaṃ ca ṣaḍguṇaṃ gandhaṃ bhuktvā sūto 'ruṇo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after consuming six times its quantity of sulphur, the mercury becomes red.
It produces all the excellent qualities specified in the procedure.
This is the <s>koṣṭhikāyantra</s>, proclaimed by <s>Nandin</s>.
Carefully placing five <s>āḍhakas</s> of powdered sand in a vessel,
the mercury pill and the like are cooked; that is the <s>vālukāyantra</s>.
In the same way, from the placing of salt, it is called the <s>lavaṇayantraka</s>.
One should make an iron vessel eight finger-breadths across and eight finger-breadths high.

children.text: kaṇṭhādho dvyaṅgule deśe jātādhāraṃ ca tatra ca
children.translated_text: At a place two finger-breadths below the neck, with a support formed there,
one should insert an iron rod crosswise through it.
Upon that one should place thin leaves of gold.
Below the vessel one should place the fumigant that will be described here itself.
One should cover that vessel with another vessel turned upside down.

children.text: mṛdā vilipya sandhiṃ ca vahniṃ prajvālayedadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared the joint with clay, one should kindle fire below.
By that, the leaves become blackened, struck down according to the stated procedure.

children.text: rasaścarati vegena drutiṃ garbhe dravanti ca ||
children.translated_text: The mercury moves rapidly, and the liquefied substances melt within the chamber.
For sulphur, <s>ālaka</s>, and <s>śilā</s>, with <s>kajjalī</s> or with dead serpent-substance,
the fumigation of gold leaves is proclaimed as supreme.
For the sake of silver, one should fumigate silver leaves with calcined tin.
And, as appropriate, one should also fumigate with <s>rasas</s> and <s>uparasas</s>.
This is called the <s>dhūpayantra</s>, for digestion and purification of substances.

children.text: sthūlasthālyāṃ dravaṃ kṣiptvā vāso baddhvā mukhe dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: Having put liquid into a large pot and tied cloth tightly over its mouth,

children.text: tatra svedyaṃ vinikṣipya mṛdāsyaṃ prapidhāya ca
children.translated_text: one should place there what is to be steamed and cover the mouth with clay.
One should kindle fire underneath; that apparatus is called the <s>kandukayantra</s>.
Into a hole below the neck of the vessel one should insert a bamboo tube.
Having made a pair of <s>kānta</s>-bronze vessels into a sealed container filled with water,

children.text: nālāsyaṃ tatra saṃyojyaṃ dṛḍhaṃ taccāpi kārayet
children.translated_text: the mouth of the tube should be joined there, and that too should be made firm.

children.text: yuktadravyair vinikṣiptaḥ pūrvaṃ tatra puṭe rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Mercury, previously placed there in the closed chamber with suitable substances,
when heated by fire, falls down from the tube into that water.
For just as long as the whole vessel remains hot,
the joining of mercury takes place; this is the <s>ḍhekīyantra</s>.
Fire is above, water below, and the collection of mercury is in the middle.
This is called the <s>somānalayantra</s>; it digests mica and the like.
Mercury placed in an iron tube, in a vessel filled with salt,
should be sealed and cooked; this is called the <s>nālikāyantra</s>.
Having made the joints well sealed, in an excellent vessel, facing forward,
its mouth should be eight finger-breadths, and its length should be sixteen finger-breadths.
Having made the joints well sealed, there should be a coating of cloth and clay.
There, in the <s>pātālayantra</s>, one should make mercury and the like descend.
In the <s>kacchapayantra</s>, set in a lamp standing on an earthen pedestal...
The apparatus in which <s>sūta</s> falls is said to be the <s>dīpikāyantra</s>.
It is twelve fingers high and sixteen fingers long.

children.text: tāmrīyaṃ mṛṇmayaṃ vātha suślakṣṇaṃ cipiṭaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: A copper or earthen vessel, very smooth, flat, and well-made,
should have below its rim a basin only two fingers high.
In the basin one should place another vessel of the same size, well sealed,
inverted, and at the joint of the two one should make a tube resembling a cow's mouth.
The substance to be cooked, mixed with a liquid substance, is put in the lower vessel;
after placing it there and applying a clay seal, water is poured on the top of the apparatus.
Having set that apparatus on a hearth, one should kindle a fierce fire below.
From it nothing else comes out except the <s>rasa</s> (essence) dependent on each particular substance.
This is the <s>Gaṅgāsāgarayantra</s>; it is remembered as the <s>bhaṭṭiyantra</s>.
It should obtain the finest liquefied extract from jaggery, flowers, fruits, and the like.
When the belly of a vessel is half filled with a liquid substance,

children.text: mukhe tiryakkṛte daṇḍe rasaṃ sūtreṇa lambitam ||
children.translated_text: and a rod is set crosswise at the mouth, the <s>rasa</s> is hung by a thread,
and it is steamed as it reaches that lower part; this is remembered as the <s>ḍolāyantra</s>.

children.text: cullīṃ caturmukhīṃ kṛtvā tatra bhāṇḍaṃ niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made a four-mouthed hearth, one should place a vessel there.
After putting the medicine in it and sealing the mouth of that vessel,
the people there call this by the name <s>koṣṭhīyantra</s>.
A crucible three fingers in circumference and four fingers in length
should be made of clay, very firm, with a round mouth.
Twenty parts of salt and one part of <s>guggulu</s>

children.text: suślakṣṇaṃ peṣayitvā tu vāraṃ vāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be ground very finely, again and again, repeatedly.
The wise man should make a firm coating for the crucible with half as much salty clay,

children.text: kārīṣe vā tuṣāgnau vā bhūmau tu svedayenmṛdu ||
children.translated_text: and gently steam it in a dung fire, in a husk fire, or in the ground.

children.text: ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā rasendro bhasmatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: In one day and night or in three nights, <s>rasendra</s> (mercury) becomes ash.
This is called the <s>garbhayantra</s>, which makes ash from a <s>piṣṭikā</s> (ground amalgam).
Having made a potsherd full of sand, one should place another potsherd on top of it,
and there cook it slowly with a gentle fire.
Then, with the five alkalis, with urines, and with salts, the <s>biḍa</s> is produced.
This is called <s>haṃsapāka</s>; that apparatus is praised by the best authorities.
Having made two iron crucibles, each measuring twelve fingers,
one should put a tube at the mouths of the crucibles and seal it properly.
In one should be placed purified <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury), and in the other purified sulfur.

children.text: deyaṃ jalaṃ sūtakādho vahniṃ gandhopari kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Water is to be placed below the mercury, and fire should be applied above the sulfur.
By precisely this procedure one should digest sulfur in sixfold quantity.
This should be known as the <s>mūṣāyantra</s>, taught by the siddha <s>Nāgārjuna</s>.
A vessel made of magnetic iron is to be twelve fingers long,
eight fingers in length, O goddess, and below the vessel three fingers; it is excellent.

children.text: nimnaṃ pātraṃ pidhānīṃ ca lohotthāṃ cipiṭāṃ śubhām
children.translated_text: There should be a depressed vessel, and also an excellent flat lid made of iron.
This <s>stanayantra</s> is best for the digestion of mercury amalgams.
A pair of eggplant-shaped crucibles should be made from <s>padmavarta</s> iron.
Into one he should put <s>sūta</s>; into the other he should put poison.
A spout shaped like a serpent should be set at the mouth of the poison crucible,
and a spout shaped like a peacock should be set at the mouth of the mercury crucible.
The wise man should join the serpent's mouth to the peacock's mouth.
He should coat the three joints with diamond-clay so that they are firm.
Water is placed below the mercury crucible, and a charcoal fire below the poison.
This is the <s>nāgamāyūrayantra</s>, best for poison-fumigation, dear one.
A pit should be made a hand-length long and two spans deep.
In the middle of the pit there should be a furnace twelve fingers long,
and two spans high; one should fill that good furnace
with sand outside it, and with cow-dung fire in the furnace, O dear one, and with <s>rasa</s>.
This <s>cakrayantra</s> is recommended for the operation of making mercury ash.
In a good pot one should make a perforated little crucible resembling a plantain flower,
turned mouth downward, and coat it firmly with diamond-clay.
Above it another pot should be placed, mouth downward, with its joint well sealed.
In the crucible one should put <s>vatsanābha</s>, and in the upper vessel
one should smear <s>rasa</s> properly; above the apparatus is the deceptive <s>rasa</s>.
The cooking below is with a gentle fire; this is the <s>khecarayantraka</s>.
For the most part it is best in poison-fumigation for perfected <s>rasendra</s>, dear one.
Having put <s>sūta</s> and the like into a pot, together with a gold, silver, or similar shallow cup,

children.text: nyubjāṃ sandhiṃ mṛdā liptvā vālukāṃ khorikāntagām ||
children.translated_text: one should invert it, coat the joint with clay, and put sand inside the shallow cup.
Cooking it with a gentle fire is this <s>kāpāliyantraka</s>.
A glass flask, containing liquid, with its mouth concealed, and joined with clay and cloth to the breadth of a finger,
should be dried and filled to three parts.
It is set in sand inside a vessel a span deep.
One should cover it with other fillers up to the remaining part.
The mouth of the vessel should be covered with a gem-stopper; the joint should be smeared with clay and cooked.
When the grass placed on the back of the stopper does not burn in the hearth,
this is the <s>vālukāyantra</s>, and it cooks mercury pills and the like.
When salt is inserted in this same way, it is called the <s>lavaṇayantraka</s>.
For a copper vessel whose mouth has been coated inside with <s>rasa</s>,
one should smear the joint at the bottom of the vessel with clay and salt alone,
fill that vessel with salt or with alkalis, and cook it as before.
In the apparatus, a crucible containing <s>rasa</s>, with its whole body hidden by sand,
One should cover the apparatus with blazing utpala-fuel; that is called the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus.
At the side of the jar one should make a hole the size of a thumb,
and an iron tube of that thickness, or else a bamboo tube.
One should join the tube to the hole and place a small vessel at the end of the tube.
Having put sarja-resin and the like into the jar, one should seal its mouth.
One should kindle fire below it; this is called the <s>nālikāyantra</s> (tube apparatus).
With the substance enclosed inside a pair of earthen saucers, one who knows fire should heat it among cow-dung cakes.

children.text: paceta cullyāṃ yāmaṃ vā rasaṃ tatpuṭayantrakam
children.translated_text: Or one should cook the <s>rasa</s> in a hearth for a <s>yāma</s>; that is the <s>puṭayantraka</s> (covered-heating apparatus).
A wide-mouthed cooking pot should be set in a pit filled with wet cow-dung,
and another jar should be filled up to the opening.
A cooking pot furnished with five or six holes should be set in the mouth.
One should fill that jar with substances from which oil is to be extracted and seal it.
One should cover the vessel's mouth with an earthen saucer and give heat all around.
The oil that falls from the holes should be used in the respective preparations.
This is the <s>pātālayantra</s> (downward apparatus), for it makes every oil descend.
One should collect wood, bark, seeds, flesh, bone, bamboo, and the lower parts.
Having put the dung of donkeys and the like into a pot, one should set a bronze vessel at its mouth.
One should place it with water, O <s>Devī</s>, and kindle fire below.
The oil collected in the bronze vessel heals all wounds.
This <s>dhūpayantra</s> (smoke apparatus), O <s>Devī</s>, was proclaimed by <s>Nandin</s>.
A round bottle-gourd, of even thickness, with a long tube and perforated,
should be filled, my dear, with seeds and other substances from which oil is to be extracted.
One should put hair at its mouth and set it facing downward.

children.text: sacchidre ca ghaṭe nālaṃ bhāṇḍacchidre niveśayet
children.translated_text: The tube should be inserted into a perforated jar and into the hole of the vessel.
One should give a covered heating in the middle of the jar and place a small vessel beneath the tube.
This is the <s>adhaḥpātanayantra</s> (downward-dripping apparatus), excellent for extracting oil.
Inside a broad bronze vessel one should place an even support.
Above that one should set a very firm earthen vessel, four fingers in measure.
One should set another heated vessel inside the former vessel.
Having placed in it sandalwood, black agarwood, and honey-moistened material,

children.text: evaṃ dvitīyaṃ pātraṃ tu tṛtīyamapi tadvidham ||
children.translated_text: one should arrange a second vessel in this way, and a third likewise.
After setting them one above another, one should place an earthen basin above them.
One should set the basin inverted in the bronze vessel and wipe the basin with water.
The <s>adhaḥpātanayantra</s> makes fragrant oil drip down.

children.text: mūṣā hi krauñcikā proktā kumudī karahāṭikā ||
children.translated_text: Crucibles are taught as <s>krauñcikā</s>, <s>kumudī</s>, <s>karahāṭikā</s>,
<s>pācanī</s>, and <s>vahnimitrā</s> by the experts in <s>rasa</s>.
Because this crucible removes faults, it is called <s>mūṣā</s>.
Its material should be clay and also metal.
Even one <s>kākinī</s> coin that has come forth from the mouth of a crucible is preferable
to even a hundred thousand gained by bowing to base men: shame on that for men of honor.
When binding the crucible and its lid, one should thoroughly plaster the openings.
Stopping, piercing, and tightly joined sealing are the fastening of joints.
Clay that is pale, coarse, reddish-pale, and saline
and able to withstand long blowing is highly praised for crucibles.

children.text: tadabhāve ca vālmīkī kaulālī vā samīryate ||
children.translated_text: In its absence, anthill clay or potter's clay is prescribed.

children.text: yā mṛttikā dagdhatuṣaiḥ śaṇena śikhitrakairvā hayaladdinā ca
children.translated_text: The clay that has been pounded with burnt husks, hemp, peacock-feathers, and horse dung,

children.text: lohena daṇḍena ca kuṭṭitā sā sādhāraṇā syātkhalu mūṣikārtham ||
children.translated_text: and with an iron rod, is indeed the ordinary material for a crucible.
White stones, husks, burnt matter, peacock-feathers, and hemp cloth,
together with dung and slag, should be mixed with crucible clay as appropriate.
Having ground three parts clay, two parts hemp and dung, lead, burnt husk and stone,
and half a part of slag, one should make a <s>vajramūṣā</s> for extracting metallic essence.
Clay born from an anthill, mixed with burnt charcoal and husk,
joined with the respective <s>biḍa</s> and smeared with the respective <s>biḍa</s>,

children.text: tayā yā vihitā mūṣā yogamūṣeti kathyate
children.translated_text: when a crucible is made from it, is called a <s>yogamūṣā</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> (mercury) prepared with it becomes superior in quality.
With equal portions of plaster, washed earthworms, hemp, and burnt husk,
and with an equal amount of crucible clay mixed with buffalo milk,
the <s>krauñcikā</s>, now to be described, is proclaimed in many forms.
A crucible fashioned from that is useful for melting diamond.
Even after two <s>yāmas</s> of blowing, it does not melt in the fire.
Rich in sixfold burnt plaster and furnished with slag, charcoal, and hemp,
a crucible made with black clay is called a <s>gāramūṣā</s>.
Cloth, charcoal, and husk are equal, and the clay is four times that amount.
The plaster and clay are equal; made from all these,
it is designated a <s>vajramūṣā</s>, and it withstands fire for a <s>yāma</s>.
Mixed with powder of the red group and prepared with water of the red group,
it is called the excellent crucible and is also termed the gold crucible.
A crucible made of clay and smeared with <s>kṣitikhecara</s>
is called the color crucible and is employed for improving color.
In the same way, with the white group, it is called the silver crucible.
Made from clay of the respective <s>biḍa</s> and smeared with the respective <s>biḍa</s>,
it is called the <s>biḍamūṣā</s>, for operations concerning the body and metals.
It withstands fire for four <s>yāmas</s>, even while afflicted by molten material.
The reaching of a molten state by what is to be liquefied through the process of blowing in the crucible,
and the removal for a moment: that is called <s>mūṣāpyāyana</s> (refreshing the crucible).
In an eggplant-shaped crucible the tube should measure twelve fingers.
Above it should be like a <s>dhuttūra</s> flower, very firm, with tightly fitted joints.

children.text: aṣṭāṅgulaṃ ca sacchidraṃ sā syād vṛntākamūṣikā
children.translated_text: It should be eight finger-breadths and provided with a hole; that is the small <s>vṛntāka-mūṣā</s> crucible.
With this one should extract the <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) of soft substances such as <s>kharpara</s> and the like.
A crucible that is shaped like a cow's teat and has a lid furnished with a crest

children.text: sattvānāṃ drāvaṇe śuddhau mūṣā sā gostanī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: is the <s>gostanī mūṣā</s>, for melting and purifying <s>sattvas</s>.
The <s>malla-mūṣā</s> that has been specified, made from the enclosing of two <s>mallas</s>,
is proclaimed for steaming <s>parpaṭī</s> and other <s>rasas</s>.
The one that has the form of a potter's vessel, is firm, and has been thoroughly baked
is called the baked crucible, for the cooking of <s>poṭṭalī</s> and the like.
The mouthless one, spherical in shape, containing substances for <s>puṭa</s>-heating within it,
is called the <s>gola-mūṣā</s>; it restrains substances that are liable to move away.
The one that is shaped like an elbow at the bottom and gradually expands above,
large like a large eggplant, is remembered as the <s>mañju-mūṣā</s>.
It is used for the <s>puṭa</s>-heating and melting of iron, mica-essence, and the like.
The crucible that has the form of a casket and is not broad in its hollow
is a crucible measuring six finger-breadths and is known as the <s>mañjūṣā</s>.
Having buried that crucible in the ground, one should then apply a <s>puṭa</s>-heating from above.
A crucible that is flat at the base, round, and eight finger-breadths high

children.text: mūṣā sā musalākhyā ca cakribaddharase tathā ||
children.translated_text: is called the <s>musala</s> crucible, and likewise is used for mercury bound in a wheel-like form.
Six parts of burnt charcoal, red ochre, black clay,
mortar-clay, and charcoal slag: this is proclaimed as the <s>vajra-mūṣā</s>.
Mortar-clay, burnt husks, burnt matter, and ant-hill clay,

children.text: śaṇatvak ca samāyuktā mūṣā vajropamā matā ||
children.translated_text: combined with hemp fiber, form a crucible regarded as diamond-like.

children.text: prakāśā cāndhramūṣā ca mūṣā ca dvividhā smṛtā
children.translated_text: The open crucible and the <s>Andhra</s> crucible are remembered as two kinds of crucible.
The open crucible should be understood as one furnished with the shape of a shallow saucer.
It is praised by practitioners for the draining or carrying off of substances.
The <s>Andhra-mūṣā</s> should be made resembling the shape of a cow's teat.
It is furnished with a lid and has its head somewhat raised.
It is useful for coating sheets, for coloring, and for joining paired metals.
That same crucible, provided with holes and deep as the <s>nanda</s> type, is suitable for <s>sāraṇa</s>.
Sesame ash should be two parts, combined with a portion of brick.
This should be known as the ash crucible; it is useful for the purification of <s>tāra</s> (silver).

children.text: tuṣaṃ vastraṃ samaṃ dagdhaṃ mṛttikā caturaṃśikā ||
children.translated_text: Husk and cloth, burnt in equal quantity, and clay in four parts,
combined with <s>kūpī</s>-stone, are proclaimed as a <s>vajra-mūṣā</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇā raktā ca pītā ca śuklavarṇā ca mṛttikā ||
children.translated_text: Clay is black, red, yellow, and white in color.

children.text: ādyā śreṣṭhā kaniṣṭhāntyā madhyame madhyame mate
children.translated_text: The first is best, the last is worst, and the two middle ones are considered middling.
After burning the dung of elephants and horses until it has become black,

children.text: vāśā vajralatā patraṃ valmīkasya mṛdā saha
children.translated_text: one should take <s>vāśā</s>, <s>vajralatā</s> leaf, and ant-hill clay together,
and grind them with <s>vajra</s>-water until the mixture becomes white.
With that one should knead and bind the <s>vaṅka-nāla</s> and the furnace chamber.
Ant-hill clay, iron slag, and white stone, separately,

children.text: ekāṃśau dvau tu dagdhasya tuṣasya strīśiroruhām
children.translated_text: one part of each; then two parts of burnt husk and of women's hair,
all in equal portions, should be kneaded with goat's milk.

children.text: yāmadvayaṃ dṛḍhaṃ tena kuryānmūṣāṃ ca sampuṭam
children.translated_text: For two <s>yāmas</s> one should knead it firmly; with it one should make the crucible and the sealed container.

children.text: śoṣayitvā rasaṃ kṣiptvā tatra kaṃsaṃ nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having dried it and placed the <s>rasa</s> there, one should confine bronze in it.
The <s>vajra-mūṣā</s> and the rest have been taught for the proper killing of mercury.
Two parts of <s>mokṣa-kṣāra</s>, combined with a portion of brick,

children.text: yatkṛtau sā tu mūṣā syāduttamā tāraśodhane
children.translated_text: make a crucible that is excellent for the purification of <s>tāra</s> (silver).
Mixed with substances of the red group and thoroughly soaked in the red group,
coated with a coating made from the red group, it is considered suitable for work on gold.
Mixed with substances of the white group and thoroughly soaked in the white group,
coated with a coating made from the white group, it is recommended for purifications of white metals.
Mixed with substances of the <s>viḍ</s> group and thoroughly soaked with the <s>viḍ</s> group,
coated with a coating made from the <s>viḍ</s> group, the crucible is for liquefaction and digestion.
Mixed with substances of the alkali group and thoroughly soaked in the alkali group,
coated with a coating made from the alkali group, the crucible is useful for drawing off or extraction.
One should make a coating for the crucible with poison, borax, and <s>guñjā</s> seeds.
One should do this in the open crucible, or else apply a charcoal coating.
Having placed the substance in that crucible, the wise man should melt it down.
For the color of the coating in <s>puṭa</s>-heating, red clay, <s>paṭu</s>, and <s>bhūkhaga</s> are to be used.
When gold is being melted, a yellow color is used; for <s>tāra</s> (silver), a white luster.
For copper a water-like color is used; for <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), a white color is praised.
An apparatus itself is best among remedies for the restraint of mercury.
Even when these are joined with herbs, their <s>rasa</s> is bound by means of an apparatus.
For causing the <s>sattvas</s> to fall and for purifying those that have fallen,
there are furnace chambers of various forms; their characteristics are now stated.
It should rise to a royal cubit's height, and have half of that as its length and breadth.

children.text: caturaśrā ca kuḍyena veṣṭitā mṛṇmayena sā
children.translated_text: It is square and enclosed by an earthen wall.
In one wall one should make a door, furnished with the breadth of a span.

children.text: dvāraṃ sārdhavitastyā ca saṃmitaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: The door, measured at one and a half spans, should be very firm and well made.
Below it, an opening should be arranged as appropriate for blowing.
The wall of the upper section above should be measured by a <s>prādeśa</s>.
A door should also be made above, indeed measuring a <s>prādeśa</s>.
Then, having blocked it with bricks and smeared the joint of the door,
one should fill it with <s>śikhitra</s> fuel and blow it with two bellows.
Through the upper door one should put in the <s>śikhitra</s>, the material for blowing,
and the balls for precipitating <s>sattva</s>, five by five, again and again.
This is the ore-furnace for causing the <s>sattva</s> of coarse substances to fall.
On firm ground one should make a good pit, measured by a span.
It should be round; and then, in the middle of it, one should prepare another pit.
It should be furnished with a width of four finger-breadths and with depth.
From the pit up to the surface of the earth it should have lateral petals or flanges,
somewhat raised, and sloping toward the outer pit.
One should place an earthen disk, provided with five holes, over the inner pit.
Having filled the furnace-chamber with coals, one should blow it with a single bellows.
This is the <s>pātālakoṣṭhikā</s> (subterranean furnace), for extracting the essence from soft substances,
and it has been declared by <s>Nandin</s> for substances that are accomplished by blowing.
That which is twelve finger-breadths deep and likewise a span in measure,
and, above, furnished with a rim four finger-breadths high,
one should place a disk with many holes upon the rim.
Having put coals there, one should blow through a curved tube.
It should be made of crucible-clay, firm, and measuring one <s>aratni</s>.

children.text: adhomukhaṃ ca tadvaktre nālaṃ pañcāṅgulaṃ khalu ||
children.translated_text: It is turned downward, and at its mouth there is indeed a tube five finger-breadths long.
It is called the <s>vaṅkanāla</s> (curved tube), and is taught for strong blowing.
The <s>gāragoṣṭhī</s> is prescribed; it destroys or removes imperfectly formed metal.
A furnace is prescribed for preparing bound mercury and similar substances.
It is twelve finger-breadths high and four finger-breadths at the base.
The one that is blown from the side purifies soft substances.
The <s>puṭa</s> (enclosed firing) is the indication of the proper measure for cooking mercury and other substances.
Cooking that is deficient or excessive is not desired; a well-cooked medicine is beneficial.
From the <s>puṭa</s> there arise the non-reversion of metals and the like, increase of qualities, and also sharp potency,
not sinking in water, filling of the lines,

children.text: puṭādrāgo laghutvaṃ ca śīghraṃ vyāptiśca dīpanam ||
children.translated_text: color from firing, lightness, quick pervasion, and stimulation.
For metals, there is greater virtue than even from assimilated lordly mercury.
Just as fire, though standing outside, enters into stone through the application of a <s>puṭa</s>,
so, because of pulverization, the obtaining of qualities in metals is certain.
Having put the medicine to be cooked inside a sealed pair of earthen dishes,
and having closed it, the <s>garuṇḍapacana</s> firing is said to be that <s>puṭa</s>.
In a square pit two cubits in depth and breadth,
filled with a thousand forest cow-dung cakes, the medicine to be fired,
carefully sealed in a furnace, should be placed upon a layer of paste or cakes.
One should place half a thousand forest cow-dung cakes above the covering layer.
One should kindle fire there; this is remembered as the <s>mahāpuṭa</s> (great firing).
With the measure of a royal cubit, square and hollow,
and filled with pieces of dried dung up to the neck, one should then set it in place.
There one should place the lidded vessel filled with the substance to be fired.
As before, one should put in half the number of <s>garuṇḍas</s>.
This is called the <s>gajapuṭa</s> (elephant firing), producing great efficacy.
Thus, in a pit of one <s>aratni</s>, the firing is called the <s>vārāha</s> (boar) <s>puṭa</s>.
The firing on the surface of the ground, whose height is two spans,
and whose breadth at the base is the same, is the <s>kukkuṭaka</s> <s>puṭa</s> (cock firing).
The firing that is given on the ground with eight forest cow-dung cakes
is called the <s>kapotapuṭa</s> (dove firing) for calcining tender mercury.
Dry cow-dung, crushed by cows' hooves inside a cowshed and powdered,
is designated <s>gorvara</s>, the best in the preparation of mercury.
Where a firing is given with <s>gorvaras</s> or else with husks,
that is called the <s>gorvarapuṭa</s>, for the successful preparation of mercury ash.
In a large vessel filled with husks and furnished with a crucible in the middle,
when cooking is performed by fire, that is called the <s>bhāṇḍapuṭa</s> (vessel firing).
When the covering is placed below and above, indeed,
with heated sand, that apparatus is the <s>vālukāpuṭa</s> (sand firing).
In ground containing fire, one should bury it properly two finger-breadths below;
the apparatus that has the firing above is called the <s>bhūdharapuṭa</s>.
A firing above with husks or <s>gorvaras</s>, measuring sixteen units,
that apparatus is called <s>lāvakā</s>, for the easy preparation of soft substances.
When the measure of a <s>puṭa</s> has not been stated, according to the strength or weakness of the substance to be accomplished,
the firing should be determined and applied by those skilled in inference and exclusion.
Glass, iron, earthen jars, small bottles, and cups,

children.text: rūpikā kūpikā siddhā golaṃ caiva karaṇḍakam ||
children.translated_text: a <s>rūpikā</s>, a small bottle, a prepared round vessel, and a basket-vessel,

children.text: caṣakaṃ ca kaṭhorī ca vāṭikā khorikā tathā
children.translated_text: a cup, a bowl, a <s>vāṭikā</s>, and a <s>khorikā</s>,
a <s>kañcolī</s> and a <s>grāhikā</s>: these are names having a single meaning.
The fires for processing mercury, secondary minerals, and metals are threefold.
They are, separately and threefold, accomplished by <s>garuṇḍa</s>, wood, and coal.
Among these, the <s>garuṇḍa</s>-based procedures include the firing called <s>kukkuṭa</s>,
and also the firing called <s>varāha</s> and the one called <s>gaja</s>.
The best are dung-cakes produced in the forest, the middling are those produced in a cowshed,
and the lowest is artificial wood, born of <s>khadira</s> and <s>āsana</s>.
Or else wood from a heartwood tree, two spans long,
and as thick as a stout forearm, is best for cooking lordly mercury.
Wood-based firing is known as mild, medium, and fierce fire.
Coals born from <s>khadira</s> and from <s>triphala</s> trees,
and charcoal pieces born from heartwood trees, are best in the act of blowing.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s> said:
O God of gods, consciousness-bliss, giver of being, consciousness, and bliss,
by you alone I was previously instructed in the procedure concerning mercury.
Now, by your favor, O Lord, I wish to hear
the characteristics and the classes of secondary minerals beginning with sulphur, and of metals beginning with gold,
and of jewels beginning with ruby.

children.text: saṃskāraṃ ca guṇānbrūhi yathā jānāmyahaṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: Tell me also the preparation and the qualities, O lord, so that I may know them.
Śrī <s>Bhairava</s> said:
<s>Gandha</s>, <s>tāla</s>, <s>śilā</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>ghana</s>, <s>hiṅgula</s>, and <s>gairika</s>,
<s>capalā</s>, <s>aśmaja</s>, <s>bhūnāga</s>, <s>haridrāśma</s>, <s>agnijāra</s>,
<s>kharparī</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>girisindūra</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
<s>kampilla</s>, poison, <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>gaurīpāṣāṇa</s>, and <s>bhūkhaga</s>,
<s>poddāra</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>sindūra</s>, <s>tuvarī</s>, and <s>rasāñjana</s>,
<s>nīlāñjana</s>, <s>sauvīra</s>, <s>srotoñjana</s>, and <s>aphenaka</s>,
<s>puṣpāñjana</s>, conch, oyster-shell, snail-shell, and cowries,
<s>sābuṇī</s>, <s>navakṣāra</s>, <s>cīnakṣāra</s>, and <s>ākhumāraka</s>,
resin of <s>sarja</s>, guggul, lac, alkalis, and salts,
<s>gorocanā</s>, sour cane, glass, dung, and sand:
these are known as the <s>uparasas</s> (secondary mineral substances) in the work of the king of rasas.
The essences of gold, silver, copper, <s>kānta</s>, and mica, together with <s>tīkṣṇa</s> and <s>muṇḍaka</s>,

children.text: bhujaṅgaṃ trapusaṃ caiva rītiḥ kāṃsyaṃ ca vartakam
children.translated_text: <s>bhujaṅga</s>, tin, <s>rīti</s>, bronze, and <s>vartaka</s>:
these twelve are metals; <s>maṇḍūra</s> and iron slag are also counted.

children.text: māṇikyamuktāphalavidrumāṇi tārkṣyaṃ ca puṣyaṃ bhiduraṃ ca nīlam
children.translated_text: Ruby, pearl, coral, <s>tārkṣya</s>, <s>puṣya</s>, diamond, and sapphire,

children.text: gomedhakaṃ cātha viḍūrakaṃ ca krameṇa ratnāni navagrahāṇām ||
children.translated_text: then <s>gomedhaka</s> and <s>vaiḍūrya</s>: these, in order, are the gems of the nine planets.
Sun-stone, moon-stone, star-stone, and <s>kāntaka</s>,
<s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>nṛpāvarta</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, and <s>vimalā</s>,
and <s>peroja</s>: these nine should be named as the lesser gems.
Having stated the origin, characteristics, and kinds, one should next purify sulphur.

children.text: sājyaṃ bhāṇḍe payaḥ kṣiptvā mukhaṃ vastreṇa bandhayet
children.translated_text: Putting milk mixed with ghee into a vessel, one should bind its mouth with cloth.

children.text: tatpṛṣṭhe cūrṇitaṃ gandhaṃ kṣiptvā śrāveṇa rodhayet ||
children.translated_text: On the back of that cloth one should place powdered sulphur and seal it with a shallow cover.

children.text: bhāṇḍaṃ nikṣipya bhūmyantarūrdhvaṃ deyaṃ puṭaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: After setting the vessel into the earth, one should give a light heating from above.

children.text: tataḥ kṣīre drutaṃ gandhaṃ śuddhaṃ yogeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Then the sulphur, melted into the milk, is pure and should be used in preparations.
Oil of <s>kaṅguṇī</s>, mustard, or castor, or oil born from safflower,
ewe's milk, ghee, cow's milk, or sour gruel:
with one of these one should fill the inside of a vessel a little short of full.

children.text: ruddhvā vastreṇa tadvaktraṃ gandhacūrṇaṃ tata upari ||
children.translated_text: Having closed its mouth with cloth, one should then put sulphur powder above it.

children.text: lohapātreṇa ruddhvātha pṛṣṭhe sthāpya ca kharparam
children.translated_text: After covering it with an iron vessel and placing a potsherd on its back,
one should fill it with burning cow-dung cakes, melt the sulphur, and take it up.

children.text: taddhuttūradravaiḥ piṣṭvā śuṣkaṃ drāvyaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Grinding that with juices of <s>dhuttūra</s>, drying it, and melting it as before,
one should do this again and again; the sulphur becomes well purified.
For one <s>yāma</s> one should triturate sulphur with <s>bṛhatī</s> and <s>ajagandhā</s>,
or with the juices of <s>bhṛṅgī</s> and <s>dhuttūra</s>, or of <s>tilaparṇī</s>.
Taking it, one should cook it for a moment in an iron vessel with an equal amount of ghee.

children.text: baddhvāgninā drutaṃ taṃ vai hyajākṣīre vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Melted by the fixed fire, it should then be poured into goat's milk.
Doing this seven times, sulphur reaches purification.
Castor oil with <s>karañja</s> oil, and goat's milk, should be placed in a vessel.

children.text: kṣiptvā tasya mukhaṃ baddhvā svacchavastreṇa buddhimān
children.translated_text: A wise person should bind its mouth with a clean cloth.
The sulphur should be steeped for a day in juices produced from <s>dhūrtaja</s> and then dried.
That powder should be placed on the cloth over the former vessel.

children.text: ācchādya śrāvakenaiva pṛṣṭhe deyaṃ puṭaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: Covering it with a shallow cover, one should give light heating on its back.
Taking the melted sulphur, one should steep it in juices of <s>dhuttūra</s>.
In the same way it should be melted, steeped again, and then melted once more.
Taking it, one should steep it seven times in fish bile in the sunlight.
Then one should grind it together with powder of <s>kośātakī</s> seeds.
One should steep it with juices produced from <s>bhṛṅga</s> for seven days in strong sunlight.

children.text: toyena kṣālitaṃ śoṣyaṃ tato mṛdvagninā kṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Washed with water and dried, it should then be heated briefly over a gentle fire.
When melted, it should then be poured into an iron vessel smeared with ghee.
Standing within <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> juice, it becomes properly purified.
Or sulphur should be triturated for the length of one <s>yāma</s> with wine, <s>brāhmī</s>, and <s>ajagandhā</s>,
or with <s>bhṛṅga</s> and <s>dhuttūra</s>, or with the juice of <s>tilaparṇī</s>.
Taking that with ghee, one should cook it for a moment in an iron vessel.
When melted by a light fire, it should be cast into ewe's milk.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtaṃ saptavāraṃ śuddhaṃ bhavati gandhakam
children.translated_text: Done in this way seven times, sulphur becomes pure.
<s>Devadālī</s>, <s>amlaparṇī</s>, orange, or pomegranate,
or citron, according to availability: one should obtain the juice of any one of these.
For sulphur, one should take a quarter part of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> combined with the liquid.

children.text: ātape tridinaṃ śuṣkaṃ dravaṃ deyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: It should be dried in the sun for three days, and the liquid should be applied again and again.
<s>Dhuttūra</s>, basil, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, garlic, and <s>devadālikā</s>,
root of <s>śigru</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, camphor, and the two <s>śaṅkhinīs</s>,

children.text: kṛṣṇāgaru ca kastūrī vandhyā karkoṭakī samam ||
children.translated_text: black aloe-wood, musk, <s>vandhyā</s>, and <s>karkoṭakī</s>, in equal amount:
having ground these with citron juice, one should put them into castor oil.
With this, one should steep the former sulphur, placed in an iron vessel.
After three times, it becomes like honey and free from the smell of sulphur.
This is sulphur oil; one should use it in all preparations.
Alternatively, a cloth should be smeared seven times with the milks of <s>arka</s> and <s>snuhī</s>.

children.text: gandhakaṃ navanītena piṣṭvā vastraṃ lipettu tām ||
children.translated_text: Grinding sulphur with fresh butter, one should smear that cloth with it.
One should make that into a wick, light it, hold it with tongs, and turn it downward.

children.text: tailaṃ patedadho bhāṇḍe grāhyaṃ yogeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: The oil falls below into a vessel; it should be collected and used in preparations.
Sulphur, thoroughly triturated for a long time with <s>kuberākṣī</s> oil,
when blown in a firm, open crucible, releases its essence.
Or, having placed previously purified sulphur in the belly of a vessel...
Having covered it with a copper vessel, one should pour cold water into it.

children.text: mandaṃ prajvālya tadadho vahnimuṣṇaṃ jalaṃ haret
children.translated_text: Kindling a gentle fire beneath it, one should remove the water when it has become hot.
In this way, again and again, one should pour cold water above.
Through fire, the <s>sattva</s> (essence) of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur), golden in appearance, accomplishes every operation.

children.text: na cāsya sattvam ādadyāt sattvarūpo hi gandhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Yet one should not extract its <s>sattva</s>, for <s>gandhaka</s> itself is of the nature of essence.
So some other knowers of the principle of <s>gandhaka</s> declare.
Or else, sulphur that has been powdered and mixed with pungent oil
should be placed in a cloth, and that cloth should be made into a firm wick.
Then, after wrapping it with thread and soaking it thoroughly in cow's ghee,
one should hold the wick with tongs and light it from below.
The liquid product becomes the color of the juice of a ripe mango fruit.

children.text: gandhakaḥ kaṭukaḥ pāke vīryoṣṇo vimalaḥ saraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gandhaka</s> is pungent in digestion, hot in potency, pure, and flowing.
It removes <s>visarpa</s> (spreading inflammation), skin disease, itching, worms, abdominal tumors, and wasting disease.
It pacifies eye diseases, is aphrodisiac, and overcomes distress from poison and illness.
It grants all accomplishments, strengthens, destroys the three humors, and is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).
<s>Haritāla</s>, <s>godantī</s>, <s>tālaka</s>, and <s>naṭamaṇḍana</s>,
<s>girijālalita</s>, the yellow one, <s>atigandha</s>, and <s>biḍālaka</s> are its names.
<s>Haritāla</s> is said to be of two kinds: the one called leafy and the one called lump-like.

children.text: svarṇavarṇaṃ guru snigdhaṃ tanupattraṃ ca bhāsuram ||
children.translated_text: That which is gold-colored, heavy, unctuous, thin-leaved, and shining
is called leaf-<s>tālaka</s>; it has many leaves and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
That which is leafless, resembling a lump, of little essence, and also heavy
is the lump-<s>tālaka</s>; it suppresses women's menses and has few virtues.
It causes disorders of wind, phlegm, urinary disease, and the like, and it destroys life.
Unpurified <s>haritāla</s> causes burning, eruptions, and contraction of the limbs.

children.text: tālakaṃ kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā daśāṃśena tu ṭaṅkaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Having reduced <s>tālaka</s> to small particles, one should add <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) in a tenth part.
It should be washed with liquids produced from citron and then washed again with sour gruel.

children.text: vastre caturguṇe baddhvā ḍolāyantre dinaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: Tied in a fourfold cloth, it should be cooked for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus).
It should be steamed for a day with powdered sour gruel, or with juices from <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash gourd),
or with water of <s>śālmalī</s>; <s>tālaka</s> thereby obtains purification.
When a decoction made from <s>brahmamūla</s> has thickened to the consistency of honey,

children.text: trivāraṃ tālakaṃ bhāvyaṃ piṣṭvā mūtre'tha māhiṣe ||
children.translated_text: <s>tālaka</s> should be impregnated three times with it, and then ground in buffalo urine.
A firing should be given with ten <s>utpalas</s>; one should do this again and again.

children.text: evaṃ dvādaśadhā pācyaṃ śuddhaṃ yogeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Thus cooked twelve times, it is purified and should be employed in preparations.

children.text: tālakaṃ poṭṭalaṃ baddhvā sacūrṇe kāñjike pacet
children.translated_text: Having bound <s>tālaka</s> into a bundle, one should cook it in sour gruel together with powder.
It should be cooked by means of a <s>dolāyantra</s> for one watch, then in juice from <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>.
One should cook it in sesame oil for a watch and in water of <s>triphala</s> for a watch.

children.text: evaṃ yantre caturyāmaṃ pācyaṃ śudhyati tālakam ||
children.translated_text: Thus cooked in the apparatus for four watches, <s>tālaka</s> is purified.

children.text: lākṣā rājī tilāḥ śigru ṭaṅkaṇaṃ lavaṇaṃ guḍam
children.translated_text: Lac, <s>rājī</s> (mustard), sesame, <s>śigru</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), salt, and jaggery
should be ground in the measure of the <s>tālaka</s>, and a perforated crucible should be sealed.
It should be fired with the <s>pātālayantra</s> (downward apparatus); the essence certainly falls.
One should grind <s>tālaka</s> with milk or with decoctions of <s>sarpākṣī</s>.
As before, one should produce the essence, the perforated crucible having been sealed.

children.text: lākṣā rājī guḍaṃ śigru ṭaṅkaṇaṃ lavaṇaṃ tilāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Lac, <s>rājī</s>, jaggery, <s>śigru</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, salt, and sesame:
with these, in equal quantity, one should grind essence-yielding <s>tāla</s> with milk of <s>arka</s>.

children.text: dinaṃ vā vajriṇīdugdhaiḥ kūśmāṇḍasya dravaiśca vā ||
children.translated_text: Or for a day with the milk of <s>vajriṇī</s>, or with the liquids of <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>.
Having smeared the inside with that paste, one should seal the perforated crucible.
From firing or from blowing, the essence should be collected in the <s>pātālayantra</s>.
Mercury and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> should be added, each in an eighth part of the <s>tālaka</s>.
One should triturate for three days with juices of <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s> and with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>.

children.text: tadgolaṃ chidramūṣāyāṃ grāhyaṃ sattvaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: That ball should be placed in a perforated crucible, and the essence should be collected as before.
There are sixteen parts of <s>tāla</s>; poison, mercury, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>
and powders of white mica and tin should each be mixed in one part.
One should grind the equal mixture for two days with the milk of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>.
Having put that ball inside a glass bottle,
one should coat that glass bottle firmly on all sides, one finger thick, with cloth and clay.
When it is dry, one should cook it in a sand apparatus slowly, with a mild fire.
When the liquid has dried, then one should properly seal the mouth with clay and salt.
One should cook it with a fierce fire for as long as twelve watches.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take it out, break the bottle, and collect it.
The essence of <s>tāla</s> adhering above resembles crystal stone.
After it has been impregnated and sprinkled with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, with fluids of <s>snuhī</s> fourteen times,
sesame, mustard, <s>śigru</s>, and salt make up the group called <s>mitrapañcaka</s>.
With these, in equal quantity, one should grind purified <s>tāla</s> for one day.
Blown in a perforated crucible in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus, it releases its essence.
Purified <s>tālaka</s> is excellent; it removes skin disease, death, and old age.
It produces good fortune and fragrance and greatly increases lifespan.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is <s>kunaṭī</s>, <s>nāgāsyā</s>, and red sulphur.
<s>Nepālikā</s>, <s>nāgajihvā</s>, and <s>kalyāṇī</s> are the seven names.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is said to be threefold: <s>śyāmāṅgī</s>, <s>kaṇavīrakā</s>,
and the one called <s>khaṇḍā</s>; their forms are distinguished and set forth.

children.text: śyāmā raktā kharāṅgā ca bhārāḍhyā śyāmikā matā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>śyāmikā</s> is considered dark red, rough-bodied, and heavy.
The <s>kaṇavīrakā</s> is bright, light, and copper-colored.
The <s>khaṇḍapūrvikā</s> is crumbling into powder, very red-bodied, and heavy.
The last-mentioned is declared the best in qualities and abundant in essence.
Urinary stone, painful urination, weak digestive fire, and constipation...

children.text: karoti kuṣṭhaṃ tāpaṃ ca śuddhihīnā manaḥśilā
children.translated_text: Unpurified <s>manaḥśilā</s> causes skin disease and burning.
One should cook <s>manaḥśilā</s> for three days in goat's urine in a <s>dolāyantra</s> apparatus.
For purification, it should be heated seven times in the sun with curd and goat's bile.
With the juices of <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, and red <s>agastya</s>,
one should cook the <s>manaḥśilā</s> in a <s>dolāyantra</s>, for a <s>yāma</s> at a time, with he-goat urine.
One should wash it with sour gruel and employ it in all preparations.
The mineral should be levigated in the juice of <s>agastya</s>; after a week it is purified.
The extraction of <s>śilāsattva</s> and its purification are likewise as in the case of <s>tāla</s>.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> should be soaked for a day with cow-flesh and the sour juice of citron.
Then it should be levigated with the juices of red and yellow flowers, and with yellow liquids.
At the end of the day one should triturate it for a <s>yāma</s>, combined with <s>mitrapañcaka</s>.
After making a pellet and placing it inside a glass bottle, that glass bottle
should be firmly coated on all sides, to the measure of a finger's breadth, with cloth and clay.
When it is dry, one should cook it in a sand apparatus, gradually, with a mild fire.
When the liquid has dried, one should then seal the mouth properly with clay and salt.
One should cook it with a fierce fire for as long as twelve <s>yāmas</s>.
When it has cooled on its own, one should take it out, break the bottle, and collect
the <s>śilāsattva</s> adhering above, resembling the young sun.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> should be levigated for three days with waters from <s>agastya</s> and <s>śigru</s>.
By the formula for <s>tālaka</s> medicines, the essence becomes like gold.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is pungent, hot, slightly bitter, and conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
It removes itching, consumption, cough, poison, demonic affliction, and sluggish digestion.
<s>Mākṣika</s> is <s>madhudhātu</s>; it is called <s>mākṣīka</s> and <s>hemamākṣika</s>.
It is also <s>tāpya</s>, <s>tāpija</s>, and <s>tārkṣya</s>, arising in the <s>Tāpī</s> country.
<s>Mākṣīka</s> is twofold: <s>hemamākṣika</s> and <s>tāramākṣika</s>.
Of these, the first <s>mākṣika</s>, produced in <s>Kānyakubja</s>, resembles gold.
Born on the bank of the <s>Tapatī</s>, five-colored and like gold,
abundant in stone, it is said to be called <s>tāpya</s> and to possess good qualities.
Because of distinctions in gold-like form, each of these is again threefold:
<s>kādamba</s>, called <s>kāravella</s>, and named <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>.
Unpurified <s>mākṣika</s> causes obstruction of breath, weakness, decline of digestive fire, and eye disease.
Unpurified <s>mākṣika</s> indeed kills a person, O you who are worshipped by the gods.
With human urine, with decoctions derived from <s>kulattha</s>,
with <s>vetasa</s> and the class of sour substances, with borax, and with the three pungents,
it should be cooked for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s>, placed in the middle of <s>sūraṇa</s>.
It should be cooked for a day with plantain juices; when taken out, it should be ground with ghee.
Mixed with castor oil and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>, it becomes purified.

children.text: mākṣikasya trayo bhāgā bhāgaikaṃ ṭaṅkaṇasya ca ||
children.translated_text: There should be three parts of <s>mākṣika</s> and one part of borax.
It should be cooked with the juices of citron or else with juices produced from lime.
One should cook it in an iron vessel until the vessel becomes very red.
Or until it takes on a copper color; to that extent the <s>mākṣika</s> becomes purified.
One should rub <s>śigru</s> root with exudates of <s>agasti</s> flowers,
and with the liquids of <s>pāṣāṇabhedī</s>; with these the <s>mākṣika</s> should be ground.
Then its pill should be placed in a crucible and fired with ten <s>utpalas</s>.
After grinding it again and again, it is purified by six firings.
Honey, milk, and sour gruel are each to be eight parts separately.

children.text: gavyaṃ takraṃ caturbhāgaṃ bhāgaḥ kaulutthajo rasaḥ
children.translated_text: Cow's buttermilk is four parts, and the juice produced from <s>kulattha</s> is one part.

children.text: sarvaṃ sampūrayed bhāṇḍe bhāgaikaṃ mākṣikaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: One should fill all this into a vessel and cook one part of <s>mākṣika</s>.
With a <s>dolāyantra</s>, over a gentle fire, one should cook it again for the measure of a <s>yāma</s>.
After taking it out and grinding it with the sour juice of citron, with ten <s>utpalas</s>
one should perform the firing again and again in this way for twelve days.
The <s>mākṣīka</s> becomes purified and should be employed in all preparations.
Having made <s>mākṣika</s> into granules, one should place it in a lump of <s>jālinī</s> and <s>meghanāda</s>.
It should be cooked in a <s>dolāyantra</s> in a decoction of <s>kulattha</s>.
It thereby reaches purity and is excellent for the calcination of metals.

children.text: taile takre gavāṃ mūtre kaulutthe vāmlakāñjike ||
children.translated_text: In oil, buttermilk, cow's urine, <s>kulattha</s> decoction, or sour gruel,
a wise man should purify <s>mākṣika</s> for the removal of mountain-born faults.
With decoctions of <s>kulattha</s> and <s>kodrava</s>, with human urine and sour <s>vetasa</s>,
or with borax, the class of sour substances, or the three pungents,
it should be cooked for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s>, placed in the middle of a <s>sūraṇa</s> tuber.
It should be cooked for a day with plantain juices; when smelted, taken out, and ground,
with castor oil and ghee, <s>mākṣika</s> is purified by firings.
Gold-colored, stainless <s>tāpya</s>, or else that which has been made into granules,
should be placed in a paste of <s>punarnavā</s> and steamed in <s>kulattha</s> juice.
Or, joined with rock salt moistened by <s>bījapūra</s>, it should be made into a bundle.
Steamed for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s>, it certainly comes to purification.
With cow's milk, with the latex of <s>snuhī</s>, and with castor oils it should be levigated.
<s>Mākṣika</s>, rubbed for one day, should be made into pellets.
As with mica, its essence is obtained by blowing; this is also the method for <s>sasyaka</s>.
One should steam <s>mākṣika</s> for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s> with sour gruel.
Powdered and combined with honey and ghee, it should be cooked for a day in an iron vessel.
After taking it, one should levigate it in the sun with <s>vajrī</s> latex for the length of a day.
One should triturate it for a day with house soot, ghee, and honey mixed together.
When smelted in a sealed crucible, the essence becomes like a <s>guñjā</s> seed.
With water from plantain bulb, <s>mākṣika</s> is treated a hundred times in the sun.
After it has been impregnated, one should cook it for one <s>yāma</s> with ghee and oils that counteract wind.
When it is blown as before, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like an <s>indragopa</s> insect.
With the milk-sap of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, and with breast milk, <s>mākṣika</s> should be rubbed for a day.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> as well should be mixed in, each in a quarter part.
Placed in a sealed crucible and blown, it yields a <s>sattva</s> like a jewel.
With the liquids of plantain tuber, <s>tulasī</s>, and citron, in due order,
one should impregnate finely ground <s>mākṣika</s> seven times with each liquid.

children.text: ruddhvā dhmāte patet sattvaṃ śukatuṇḍanibhaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: When it is sealed and blown, an auspicious <s>sattva</s> falls, resembling a parrot's beak.
One should impregnate it for two weeks with the urine group and the sour group.
The <s>mākṣika</s> should be rubbed with sour substances for a day under intense heat.
Combined with the five <s>mitras</s>, it should be made into pellets and blown firmly.
As with <s>vyoma</s>, through a bent tube, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like copper.
The <s>mākṣika</s> should be impregnated with the milk-sap of <s>snuhī</s>, cow's milk, and castor oils.
Anointed with the five <s>mitras</s>, at the end of seven days it should be made into pellets.
By blowing it in the manner stated before, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like lac.
With breast milk, <s>kaṅkuṣṭhaka</s>, and plantain water,
and with the five <s>mitras</s> added, <s>mākṣika</s> should be treated for seven days.
Having been impregnated, it should be rubbed for a <s>yāma</s> with oils that counteract wind, for one day.
One should cook it with a gentle fire until the ball melts.
By blowing it as with <s>vyoma</s>, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like a <s>kiṃśuka</s> flower.
This is also the procedure for all the <s>vimalas</s> and for <s>sasyaka</s>.
Having powdered purified <s>mākṣika</s>, one should rub it with some sour liquid.
One should wash it with sour gruel; what remains below is like powder of gold.
Having gathered that, one should digest it and blow it; it releases the <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: yojayedvāpane cedaṃ bījānāṃ yatra yatra vai ||
children.translated_text: This should be applied in sprinkling wherever seeds are used.
One should swiftly impregnate <s>mākṣika</s> with water produced from plantain leaves.
Then, cooked for one day with castor oil, honey, and ghee,
that heated substance should be placed in a baked diamond-crucible.
An equal amount of the substance that effects the joining of metals should be put there.
It should be placed firmly in a sealed crucible within the furnace chamber.
With coals produced from <s>khadira</s>, one should blow it with two bellows.
Joined to a bent tube, the <s>sattva</s> of <s>tāpya</s> certainly falls.
One should take <s>māṇivandhya</s> and <s>vaiṣṇava</s> in equal portions.
Grinding them with citron juice, one should place them in a very firm sealed capsule.
After coating it properly, one should fire it with forest-born cow-dung cakes.
When it has come from the <s>kukkuṭa</s> firing, it should be taken out, cooled by itself, and rubbed well.
Then, after rubbing it with cooked citron juices, as before,
the skilled man should perform firing with goat-dung again and again,
until that fired paste, rubbed with sour citron,
makes a sword sharpened on a whetstone and smeared with it assume a coppery state.

children.text: itthaṃ śuddhaṃ ca garuḍaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ nīrajaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: Thus purified, <s>garuḍa</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>nīraja</s>, and mercury,

children.text: ghṛtena madhunā yuktaṃ saguḍaṃ guñjayā samam
children.translated_text: mixed with ghee and honey, with jaggery, each equal to a <s>guñjā</s>,
should be put into a crucible as before and blown with a <s>khadira</s> fire.
A soft <s>sattva</s>, equal to lead and resembling an <s>indragopa</s> insect,
certainly falls; there is no doubt. Such is the statement of the omniscient one.
When the fire is white, brilliant, and soundless,

children.text: tadā tu sattvaṃ patitaṃ jānīyānnānyathā kvacit ||
children.translated_text: then one should know that the <s>sattva</s> has fallen, and not otherwise anywhere.
The two kinds of <s>mākṣika</s> are astringent, bitter, sweet, and pungent.
They are hot, rejuvenating, and remove skin disease, consumption, hiccup, and vomiting.

children.text: mākṣīkadhātuḥ sakalāmayaghnaḥ prāṇo rasendrasya paraṃ hi vṛṣyaḥ
children.translated_text: The ore <s>mākṣika</s> destroys every disease; it is truly the life of the lord of mercury and is supremely aphrodisiac.
It joins two metals that are hard to combine, and, being superior in qualities, is foremost among the earlier rejuvenatives.
The origin and the rest of <s>ghana</s> were explained before in that rasāyana section.
Now I shall fully explain its procedures and also its qualities.
One should rub <s>dhānyābhraka</s> for a day with the liquids of <s>meghanāda</s>.

children.text: śatāṃśaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ dattvā tato gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: After adding <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> in a hundredth part, one should then cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
With the separate juices of <s>mustā</s>, <s>sūraṇa</s>, and <s>varṣābhū</s>, one should give three firings,
five with the juices of <s>kāsamarda</s>, and also with excellent cow urine.
Again it should be rubbed with decoctions of the aerial roots of the banyan and given ten firings.
Then six with citron water, and three firings with cow's milk.

children.text: peṣaṇaṃ gharmapākaṃ ca sthālīpākaṃ puṭaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: Grinding, cooking in the sun, cooking in a pot, and firing in a <s>puṭa</s>, in order,

children.text: kuryāccatvāri karmāṇi ṭaṅkaṇaṃ ca puṭe puṭe ||
children.translated_text: one should perform these four operations, adding <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> in every firing.
The <s>abhra</s> becomes free from glitter; it may be used in all compounds.
This is the general purification. The special one is now stated.
The glitterless, dead <s>vyoma</s>, purified by the general method,
should be ground with decoctions of the substances that remove the respective diseases and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.
One should do this three or seven times with apparatuses; it becomes a remover of those particular diseases.
This is the special purification, removing each respective disease.
Grinding is to be done in the forenoon, sun-cooking at midday.

children.text: sāyāhne sthālikāpākaṃ kuryād rātrau puṭaṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: In the evening one should perform pot-cooking, and at night the firing in sequence.
The purification of <s>ghana</s> has been declared to be fivefold, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>:
making <s>dhānyābhraka</s>, extracting the <s>sattva</s>, the cleansing operation,
proper calcination, and also immortalization.
For the calcination of the <s>sattva</s> of <s>ghana</s> and for the calcination of sheets of <s>ghana</s>,
<s>darada</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> are said to be respectively the very best and are praised.
One should cook <s>dhānyābhra</s> with a decoction of <s>mustā</s> in twenty-five <s>puṭa</s> heatings.
Likewise with cow urine and with decoctions of <s>triphala</s>, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>,
with liquids of <s>kāsamarda</s> once, and with cow's milk in three <s>puṭa</s> heatings.
Thus the <s>abhraka</s> becomes lusterless; one should employ it in all preparations.
When joined with a particular processing, it becomes curative of the corresponding diseases.

children.text: dhānyābhrakasya bhāgaikaṃ bhāgau dvau ṭaṅkaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: Take one part of <s>dhānyābhraka</s> and two parts of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.
Having ground them, seal them in a closed blind crucible and blow them with intense fire.
The powder, naturally cooling, should be employed in all preparations.
When joined with a particular processing, it becomes curative of the corresponding diseases.
One should triturate <s>dhānyābhra</s> with sour liquids and then set it in the heat of the sun.
Then one should perform a <s>puṭa</s>; after that, sprinkling with sour liquid and trituration are to be done again.
After twenty repetitions, the <s>abhraka</s>, made fixed by heating, should then be put in milk.
One should triturate it with milk, put it in milk, and set it in the sun.

children.text: puṭaṃ triḥ saptavārāṇi kuryādevaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: One should perform the <s>puṭa</s> three times, seven times over, again and again.
<s>Taṇḍula</s>, <s>vajravallī</s>, <s>tālamūlī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,

children.text: śārṅgerī maricaṃ caiva balā ca payasā saha
children.translated_text: <s>śārṅgerī</s>, pepper, and also <s>balā</s>, together with milk:
with these, each separately for three days at a time, one should grind the previously processed <s>abhraka</s>.
Having placed it in the sun, one should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> with each, again and again.

children.text: evaṃ niścandrakaṃ vyoma kajjalābhaṃ mṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: In this way the mica becomes lusterless, resembling collyrium, and killed.
Into dry <s>dhānyābhraka</s> one should put pepper equal to a tenth part.
One should grind it with the class of sour liquids; it should be steeped in sour liquids for three days.
When that is dry, it should be strongly blown in a covered vessel with charcoal of <s>khadira</s>.
Then, covering it with an upper vessel, one should sprinkle it with some sour liquid.
There itself, one should sprinkle that dhānya six times, again and again, with sour liquids.
With juices produced from the roots and leaves of <s>agastya</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>varṣābhū</s>,

children.text: piṣṭvābhraṃ secayettena ṣaḍdhā dhāmyaṃ ca secayet
children.translated_text: one should grind the <s>abhraka</s> and sprinkle it with that; it is to be blown and sprinkled six times.
That washed <s>abhraka</s> should be ground with sugar, honey, ghee, and cow's milk.

children.text: ruddhvā ṣaḍbhiḥ puṭaiḥ pācyaṃ piṣṭvā caiva punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: After sealing it, it should be cooked with six <s>puṭa</s> heatings, being ground again and again.
Having ground it with the liquids of <s>matsyākṣī</s> and <s>ekavīrā</s>, one should cook it three times.
Cooked thus with <s>gajapuṭa</s> heatings, <s>abhraka</s> becomes lusterless.
The red powder of leaf-mica should be employed in all preparations.
One should triturate <s>dhānyābhra</s> for one <s>yāma</s> with fresh juices of <s>matsyākṣī</s>.
