Then one should cook it with <s>gajapuṭa</s> heatings, in this way seven times with juices of basil,
seven times with juices of <s>kokilākṣa</s>, and likewise with fresh juice of <s>kumārī</s>,
similarly with juice of white <s>dūrvā</s> and with juice of the tuber of <s>vyāghrī</s>.
Seven times with juices of <s>punarnavā</s>, and then in the same way with the five nectars,
the <s>abhraka</s> becomes lusterless; one should employ it in all preparations.
<s>Dhānyābhra</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> in equal amount are to be ground with cow urine and liquids of basil,

children.text: vākucyā sūraṇairnālyā dinaṃ piṣṭvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: with <s>vākucī</s>, with <s>sūraṇa</s>, and with the stalk for a day, and then cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: dravaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ piṣṭvā dinānteṣu puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having ground it again and again with liquids, one should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> at the ends of the days.

children.text: ruddhvā ruddhvā puṭaistvevaṃ niścandraṃ cābhrakaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Thus, sealed again and again and treated with <s>puṭa</s> heatings, the <s>abhraka</s> becomes lusterless.
After grinding the bark produced from the root of <s>peṭālī</s> with sour rice-gruel,
one should triturate the <s>abhraka</s> for a day with those liquids and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ saptapuṭaṃ kāryaṃ dadhnā ca puṭasaptakam ||
children.translated_text: In this way seven <s>puṭa</s> heatings are to be done, and also seven <s>puṭa</s> heatings with curds.
In the same way, with liquids of <s>yavaciñcā</s>, the <s>abhraka</s> becomes lusterless.
One should triturate <s>dhānyābhraka</s> with milks of <s>ravi</s>, or with liquids from the root of <s>ravi</s>,

children.text: mardyaṃ mardyaṃ puṭe pacyātsaptadhā mriyate dhruvam
children.translated_text: again and again, and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>; after seven times it is certainly killed.
One should place <s>dhānyābhraka</s> for a day in sour husk-water in the sun.

children.text: yāmaṃ mardyaṃ tu tadgolaṃ ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet
children.translated_text: After triturating it for one <s>yāma</s>, one should seal that ball and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ kārpāsatoyāntaḥ sthāpyaṃ pācyaṃ puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: In this way it should be placed in cotton-water, and it should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ gokṣīramadhyasthaṃ sthāpyaṃ peṣyaṃ puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: In this way it should be placed in cow's milk, ground, and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Afterwards, with sour liquids, cow's milk, and cotton-water, again and again,

children.text: gharmapākaṃ mardanaṃ ca sthālīpākaṃ puṭaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: there are cooking in the heat of the sun, trituration, cooking in a pot, and <s>puṭa</s> heating, in sequence.
When twenty-one <s>puṭa</s> heatings have been reached, the <s>abhraka</s> becomes lusterless.
This is the procedure for nectarization of all killed <s>abhraka</s>s.
<s>Abhraka</s>, <s>gagana</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>bahuputra</s>, and <s>umābhava</s>:
the red powder of leaf-mica is nectar, supremely beneficial.
It destroys the three doṣas, gives strength, is aphrodisiac, health-giving, and pure.
It removes all diseases, is gentle, destroys poison, and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
<s>Hiṅgula</s>, <s>darada</s>, powdered mercury, and that born from rasa:
<s>rasagarbha</s>, <s>suraṅga</s>, <s>lohaghna</s>, and <s>siddhipārada</s>.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> should be known as threefold: <s>carmāra</s>, <s>śukatuṇḍaka</s>,
and <s>haṃsapāda</s>; among them, the first should be employed in operations on silver.
One should know that one to be inferior, while <s>śukatuṇḍa</s> is middling.
It should be employed on the path of operations involving gold and silver, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
<s>Haṃsapāda</s> is the very best; it performs all operations.

children.text: tasya sattvaṃ sūta eva daradasya tribhedataḥ
children.translated_text: Its essence is mercury itself, because <s>darada</s> is of three kinds.
Resembling the dross of gold, of that appearance, and a sharp killer of metals,
<s>carmāra</s> has a sharp form; <s>śukatuṇḍaka</s> is pleasing.
Like a hibiscus flower in appearance, <s>haṃsapāda</s> is the most excellent.
In <s>rasāyana</s>, in all extraction of mercury, and in all coloring,
it is the best in the killing of metals and in the operation of improving color.
Likewise, in fixing the color of <s>rasaka</s>, it is remembered as the foremost.
There is no impurity, defect, or the like; it is honored in all operations.
<s>Darada</s>, treated with ewe's milk and with the sour group,
carefully, seven times, certainly attains purification.
<s>Darada</s>, sublimed in a distillation apparatus and deposited in a water-vessel,
releases an essence resembling <s>sūtaka</s>; there is no doubt.

children.text: ye guṇāḥ pārade proktāste guṇāḥ santi hiṅgule
children.translated_text: The qualities that are declared for <s>pārada</s> are also present in <s>hiṅgula</s>.
It is said to remove the nine fevers and to destroy <s>sampāta</s> fever.
<s>Gairika</s> is <s>giridhātu</s>, red mineral, and <s>gavedhuka</s>.
<s>Gairika</s> is said to be of two kinds; of these, the first is <s>svarṇagairika</s>.
The other is <s>pāṣāṇagairika</s>; the former is the very best in qualities.

children.text: śoṇitaṃ masṛṇaṃ snigdhaṃ svādu vṛṣyaṃ himaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: Red, smooth, unctuous, sweet, aphrodisiac, cooling, and light,
beneficial for the eyes, removing <s>raktapitta</s>, poison, hiccup, and vomiting,
and removing heat and fever, red <s>gairika</s> is excellent and destroys gold.
<s>Pāṣāṇagairika</s> is said to be hard and copper-colored.
<s>Capalā</s> penetrates the body and penetrates metals; it is restless and binds mercury.
<s>Capalā</s> has many varieties, according to the nature of all the metals:
golden in substance, silvery, made of copper, leaden in essence, and bearing the form of tin,
having the form of sharp iron, having the form of bronze, red, and also poisonous.
These have the nature of essential metals; the one called poison partakes of yellow orpiment metal.

children.text: viṣākhyaṃ capalaṃ prāpya nirjīve tasya dāpayet
children.translated_text: Having obtained the poisonous <s>capalā</s>, one should put it into its lifeless form.
With a firing by forest-born cow-dung cakes, one should by all means avoid its smoke.

children.text: naśyeta tasya dhūmaṃ vai sparśanaṃ dūratastyajet
children.translated_text: Its smoke is destructive; one should avoid touching it, even from a distance.
From eating it or from contact with it, one dies immediately.
From seeing its smoke, pain in the head and fever arise.
When the firing thus given has cooled, one should then take the <s>capalā</s>.
By mere contact with it, diamond dies in an instant.
This is declared to be the nature of all kinds of <s>capalā</s>.
In fixing tin and in the king of lead, in sequence, it is considered exceedingly praiseworthy.
They turn all metals into gold and also silver.

children.text: yuktyātha śodhitaḥ sūte vinā bījaṃ ca vā tathā
children.translated_text: Then, when purified by method in mercury, with or without <s>bīja</s>,

children.text: śataṃ vāpi sahasraṃ vā lakṣaṃ koṭiṃ ca vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: it can penetrate a hundred, a thousand, a lakh, or a crore.
Supported by diamond, the king of mercury, and <s>bīja</s>,
it penetrates metals by fumigation; when digested by mercury, it melts by itself.
After effecting the body by means of that great-souled <s>capalā</s>,
<s>Aśmaja</s>, <s>girija</s>, <s>śaila</s>, <s>aśmalākṣā</s>, and <s>śilājatu</s>
are the two kinds of <s>śilādhātu</s>; the first, beginning with cow urine, is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
The other begins with camphor; of these, the first is remembered as twofold:
with essence and without essence, and of the two the former is richer in qualities.
In summer, from the feet of the snow-mountain, heated by the fierce sun,
<s>śilādhātu</s> issues from mountains whose wombs contain gold, silver, and copper.
That born from a gold-bearing mountain is like a hibiscus flower and heavy.
Possessing essence, it is supremely sweet and is the supreme <s>rasāyana</s>.
That born from a silver-bearing mountain is sweet, pale, and heavy.
This <s>śilāja</s> removes anemia and is especially victorious over bilious diseases.
That born from a copper-bearing mountain is blue in color, dense, and heavy.
This <s>śilāja</s> removes phlegm and wind, is sharp and hot, and is the best kindler of digestion.
When thrown into fire, that which becomes shaped like a liṅga and is smokeless,
and also dissolves in water, that is perfected <s>śilājatu</s>.
The best <s>śilājatu</s> smells of cow urine, is black, resembles <s>guggulu</s>, contains granular crystals and earthiness,

children.text: snigdhamanamlakaṣāyaṃ mṛdu guru ca śilājatu śreṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: is unctuous, not sour or astringent, soft, and heavy.
All of it is bitter and pungent, sweet, and neither very hot nor very cold.
It is aphrodisiac, conquers the three doṣas, is purgative, beneficial for the eyes, and a <s>rasāyana</s>.
It removes consumption, swelling, abdominal disease, and piles, and takes away urinary disease and obstruction of urine.

children.text: nūnaṃ sajvarapāṇḍuśophaśamanaṃ mehāgnimāndyāpahaṃ medaśchedakaraṃ ca yakṣmaśamanaṃ mūlāmayonmūlanam
children.translated_text: It surely calms fever, anemia, and swelling, removes urinary disease and weak digestion, cuts away fat, calms wasting disease, and uproots root-disease.

children.text: plīhavināśanaṃ jaṭharahṛcchūlaghnam āmāpahaṃ sarvatvaggadanāśanaṃ kimaparaṃ dehe ca lohe hitam ||
children.translated_text: It destroys splenic disease, removes pain of the belly and heart, dispels undigested matter, and destroys all skin disorders; what more can be said? It is beneficial for the body and for metal.
Whatever qualities exist in minerals, subordinate minerals, mercury, jewels, and metals
abide in <s>śilādhātu</s>, for the conquest of old age and death.
<s>Bhūnāga</s>, <s>kṣitināga</s>, <s>bhūlatā</s>, red creature,
earth-born, earth-creature, poison-remover, and red-beaked one are its names.

children.text: yāsāṃ chede na raktaṃ prabhavati satataṃ prāyaśo raktabhūmau
children.translated_text: Those <s>bhūlatās</s> from whose cut no blood generally flows at all, in red ground,
should be collected; in them one should make the poison-removing, wealth-bestowing essence fall.
If, by method, the lord <s>pārada</s> moves equally with that through the use of a <s>sāraṇa</s> apparatus,
then this bound substance, capable of crorefold penetration, shines like a battle-sun; or one should apply it to copper.
The essence born from <s>bhūnāga</s> conquers the death caused by poison, yakṣas, and rākṣasas.
It makes everything subject to one's will, destroys all diseases, and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
When digested in the lord of mercury by the operation of digestion, it causes crorefold penetration.
It consumes gold and other red metals in an instant.
One should wash with water the earth of <s>bhūnāga</s> born from red earth.

children.text: yāvat sattvāvaśeṣaṃ syād dhautasattvaṃ tadeva hi ||
children.translated_text: Until only the essence remains; that washed remainder is indeed the essence.
Joined with the five allies, one should blow it strongly in a crucible.

children.text: nirbhidya mūṣāṃ tatsattvaṃ gṛhītvā kiṭṭakaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Breaking the crucible, one should take that essence and again take the slag.
Thus, by blowing three times, one should collect the remaining essence.
One should place <s>bhūnāga</s> earth in a vessel together with <s>bhūnāgas</s>.
For six months, or for a full year, one should sprinkle it again and again with water.
One should extract its <s>sattva</s> by the prescribed method, as with <s>abhra-sattva</s>.
One should feed red-soil-born <s>bhūnāga</s>s to a peacock kept in a cage,
in autumn, every day, and collect that dung.
<s>Lākṣā</s>, <s>sarja-rasa</s>, <s>sarjī</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, and <s>mitrapañcaka</s>,
wool, alkalis, and salts, the blue snake and the <s>indragopa</s> insect,
fish, the blue lizard, tortoise shell, and hare bone,

children.text: mākṣīkaṃ śikhiśaṃkhatutthaṃ ca sarvāṃśaṃ barhiṇo malam ||
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣīka</s>, <s>śikhiśaṅkhatuttha</s>, and peacock dung in a quantity equal to all the rest:

children.text: sarvaṃ nikṣipya mūṣāyāṃ dhamet tīvrāgninā dṛḍham
children.translated_text: putting all this into a crucible, one should blow it firmly with a fierce fire.

children.text: nirbhidya mūṣāṃ tatsattvaṃ gṛhītvā kiṭṭakaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After breaking open the crucible, one should take that <s>sattva</s>; the slag again,
after being blown three times in this way, should have the remaining <s>sattva</s> collected.
It is called <s>haridrāśman</s>, <s>niśāgrāvan</s>, yellow-bodied, and yellow-drawing.
Its white <s>sattva</s> is gold, excellent in mercury-rasāyana.
It is remembered as <s>agnijāra</s>, <s>agniniryāsa</s>, <s>agnigarbha</s>, and <s>agnija</s>.
It should be known as <s>vaḍabāgni-mala</s>, and also as the ocean-born membrane.
The ten names are stated, including <s>agnijvāla</s>, <s>agnijāra</s>, and <s>sindhuplava</s>.
The membrane of the oceanic fire-crocodile, cast out externally,
and dried by the heat of the sun, is remembered as <s>agnijāra</s>.
Resembling lac, it burns on contact; it is sticky and floats up from the sea.
That membrane has four colors; among them the red one is the best.
<s>Agnijāra</s> is pungent and hot in potency; it destroys abdominal diseases and removes kapha and vāta.
It produces pitta and destroys blood disorders, sannipāta, colic, and other vāta diseases.
<s>Agnijāra</s> destroys the three doṣas and removes vāta disorders such as <s>dhanurvāta</s>.
It is a grinder of the strength of mercury, a kindler, and also a digestive-calcining agent.
<s>Kharparī</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, <s>kharparī</s>, and that which is born from nectar:
<s>Rasaka</s> is said to be of two kinds, <s>dardura</s> and <s>kāravellaka</s>.
The toothed one is called <s>dardura</s>; the toothless one is <s>kāravellaka</s>.
For the falling of <s>sattva</s> the first is good; the second is good in medicines and the like.
Externally, the good one resembles compact <s>sattva</s>; next it is like turmeric.
Clear, like <s>kharpara</s>, <s>tuttha</s> is best when it has a good interior.
<s>Rasaka</s> destroys all disorders and removes kapha and pitta.
It destroys eye diseases and consumption, and it colors iron and mercury.
<s>Nāgārjuna</s> taught both <s>rasaka</s>s as belonging to mercury.
They are renowned as excellent perfected minerals, supreme in effecting body and metal.
Mercury and <s>rasaka</s>, both made able to endure fire,
will grant perfection in body and metal; there is no doubt.
Powder of <s>jayantī</s> and <s>triphalā</s>, turmeric, jaggery, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>:
this, in a quarter portion of the <s>rasaka</s>, should be ground and used to coat the crucibles.
After binding a tubular sealed capsule, one should dry it in harsh sunlight.

children.text: grāhyaṃ pātālayantreṇa sattvaṃ dhmāte puṭe'tha vā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>sattva</s> should be obtained with the <s>pātāla-yantra</s>, or else after blowing it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
One should treat <s>rasaka</s> for a day with menstrual blood and urine.
With those same substances one should rub it for one day; it attains purification.

children.text: mayūratutthaṃ tutthaṃ ca nīlāśmā tāmrabhasma ca
children.translated_text: <s>Mayūra-tuttha</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, blue stone, and copper ash,
peacock-necked <s>sasyaka</s>, O beloved, is a destroyer of poison.
That which resembles a peacock's neck and, when rubbed, looks like cow's milk,
and which floats when thrown into water: this is <s>māyūra-tutthaka</s>.
Or else it resembles a parrot's feather and is marked inside with golden specks.
One should rub <s>tuttha</s> on iron together with an acid.
If it becomes like iron and copper, that is <s>māyūra-tutthaka</s>.
One should rub <s>tuttha</s> with the dung of cats and pigeons.

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ dattvā pācyaṃ mṛdupuṭe tataḥ
children.translated_text: After adding one-tenth <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, it should then be cooked in a gentle <s>puṭa</s>.
One <s>puṭa</s> with curds and one <s>puṭa</s> with honey should be given for the purification of <s>tuttha</s>.

children.text: tutthaṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇaṃ caiva tulyaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ vimardayet
children.translated_text: <s>Tuttha</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, in equal parts, should be rubbed very finely.

children.text: mūṣāyāṃ taṃ vinikṣipya ruddhvā tīvrāgninā dhamet ||
children.translated_text: Putting that into a crucible and sealing it, one should blow it with fierce fire.
A <s>sattva</s> like an <s>indragopa</s> insect certainly falls; there is no doubt.
<s>Tuttha</s> is pungent, astringent, and hot, removing skin disease and eye disease.
It is praised in all poison disorders and produces beauty.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> and <s>kākakuṣṭha</s> are purgative and color-giving.

children.text: kaṃkuṣṭhaṃ ca dvidhā proktaṃ hematārātmakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṃkuṣṭha</s> too is said to be twofold, golden and silver in nature.
It destroys wound-worms and fever, and removes colic, <s>udāvarta</s>, and abdominal tumors.
In the great mountains, the essence situated inside stone, called <s>cāllova</s>,
when dry and red, is designated by the name <s>girisindūra</s>.
It pacifies the three doṣas, is purgative, and causes the binding of mercury.
<s>Girisindūra</s> is said to act on body and metal and to be good for the eyes.
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa-kṣāra</s>, <s>rasa-kṣāra</s>, and what is superior in mercury,
a melter of metals, destructive to mercury, auspicious, and color-giving: such it is.
Born on the bank of the <s>Mālatī</s>, the best alkali, called <s>nava</s>,
destroys urinary stone and diarrhea, as well as fixed poison.
It is said by <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and those before him to bring about mercury-perfection.
It resembles powdered brick, is rich in shining luster, and is excellent.
Mined in the region of <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>, it is regarded as <s>kampillaka</s>.
It destroys bilious sores, abdominal distention, and constipation; it removes phlegm, abdominal pain, worms, and abdominal tumors.
<s>Kampillaka</s> is purgative and removes piles, āma-colic, fever, swelling, and impurities.
The rasāyana concerning poison, beginning with its origin and so on, has indeed been stated first.
<s>Vatsanābha</s> is <s>amṛta</s>, poison, fierce, and a great medicine.
It is <s>garala</s>, death, <s>nāga</s>, little in quantity, and life-taking.
It is said to cure all <s>kuṣṭha</s> and to destroy all diseases,
and to bring about the cessation of disorders beginning with <s>sannipāta</s>, O beloved.
<s>Kāsīsa</s>, <s>dhātukāsīsa</s>, <s>kesara</s>, and <s>haṃsalomaśa</s>,
<s>śodhana</s>, <s>pāṃśukāsīsa</s>, <s>śubhra</s>, and that called <s>sattva</s> are understood as names.

children.text: kāsīsaṃ trividhaṃ śubhraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ pītamiti smṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>Kāsīsa</s> is remembered as threefold: white, black, and yellow.
They are <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>puṣpakāsīsa</s>, and then <s>hīrakāsīsa</s>.

children.text: pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ sitaṃ raktaṃ caturdheti pare jaguḥ
children.translated_text: Others have said that it is fourfold: yellow, black, white, and red.
<s>Kāsīsa</s> is hot, alkaline, astringent, sour, and somewhat bitter.
It pacifies <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, benefits the eyes, and is an excellent coloring agent.
It removes urinary difficulty, stones, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, itching, wounds, and poison.
<s>Gaurīpāṣāṇaka</s> is yellow, with a distinct body, and powdery;
it fixes <s>rasa</s> (mercury), is unctuous, removes the doṣas, and gives potency to mercury.
<s>Bhūmistuvarikā</s>, <s>phullatuvarī</s>, <s>rañjikā</s>, and <s>kṣiti</s>,
<s>citrabhū</s>, <s>cīnakāra</s>, and that which gives the red dye of <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> are names.
<s>Khaga</s>, <s>phaṭakī</s>, <s>dugdhapāṣāṇa</s>, and remover of eye diseases,
the mineral called <s>karpūra</s>, and that which dyes with the red of <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> are names.
With petals and yellow color, it occurs in the region of <s>Gurjara</s>;
born on the side of Mount <s>Arjuna</s>, it is called <s>podāraśṛṅgika</s>.
The essence of lead pacifies <s>marut</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> and removes diseases of the male organ;
it is excellent for fixing mercury and best for dyeing the hair.
<s>Sindūra</s> is in the womb of lead; <s>saimantika</s>, <s>vīrapāṃsu</s>, and lead-born,

children.text: raktaṃ ca nāgareṇuḥ gaṇapatibhūṣā suraṅga ityākhyā ||
children.translated_text: red <s>nāgareṇu</s>, <s>gaṇapatibhūṣā</s>, and <s>suraṅga</s> are its names.

children.text: saubhāgyaṃ caiva śṛṅgāraṃ maṅgalyam aruṇaṃ rajaḥ
children.translated_text: Also <s>saubhāgya</s>, <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, <s>maṅgalya</s>, <s>aruṇa</s>, and <s>rajas</s>;
<s>Sindūra</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, and heals wounds.
It is excellent at pacifying <s>kilāsa</s>, poison, itching, and <s>visarpa</s>.

children.text: hiṅgule ye guṇāḥ santi te guṇāstimurau priye ||
children.translated_text: The qualities that exist in <s>hiṅgula</s> are those in <s>timura</s>, O beloved.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> is born from <s>rasa</s>, contains <s>rasa</s>, and is foremost among products of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: rītyāṃ tu dhāmyamānāyāṃ tatkiṭṭaṃ tu rasāñjanam ||
children.translated_text: When brass is being smelted, its dross is <s>rasāñjana</s>.
In its absence, one should make the kind produced from a decoction of <s>dārvī</s>.
The artificial kind, a children's medicine, is likewise produced from <s>dārvī</s> decoction.
That which is produced from <s>dārvī</s> decoction and, when placed in the eye, diffuses to the throat,
is designated <s>rasāñjana</s>; it is astringent, pungent, and bitter.

children.text: kiṃcid uṣṇaṃ kaphaharaṃ chedanaṃ lekhanaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: It is somewhat hot, removes <s>kapha</s>, cuts, scrapes, and is light.
It pacifies <s>raktapitta</s> and destroys eye diseases.
<s>Rasāñjana</s>, <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s>, and <s>varyañjana</s> should be known,
as well as <s>rasanābha</s> and <s>agnisāra</s>; it is celebrated as having twelve names.
Blue <s>nīlāñjana</s>, called <s>nīlāñjana</s> itself, benefits the eyes and is born from water.
<s>Kapotaka</s> and <s>kāpota</s> are said to be born from <s>Śakra</s>'s earth.
<s>Nīlāñjana</s> is said to be cooling, pungent, bitter, and astringent.
It benefits the eyes, destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, destroys poison, and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
<s>Sauvīramañjana</s> is unctuous when rubbed on a stone slab;
having the appearance of collyrium and the form of stone, this natural kind is the best.
<s>Sauvīramañjana</s> is also wholesome and removes <s>raktapitta</s>;
it destroys poison, hiccup, and eye disease, and cleanses and heals wounds.

children.text: srotodbhavaṃ srotanadībhavaṃ ca srotoñjanaṃ vāribhavaṃ tathānyam
children.translated_text: Born from streams, born from river-streams, <s>srotoñjana</s>, and another water-born kind,
<s>sauvīrasāra</s>, <s>kapotasāra</s>, <s>valmīkaśīrṣa</s>, and <s>munisaṃmita</s> are its names.
If it has the shape of the peak of an anthill and, when broken, the luster of a blue lotus,
and on rubbing has the hue of <s>gairika</s>, this is <s>srotoñjana</s>.
<s>Sroto'ñjana</s> is cooling, pungent, astringent, and destroys worms.
It is a <s>rasāyana</s>, suitable for use with mercury, and excellent at increasing breast milk.
<s>Sroto'ñjana</s> is cold, unctuous, sweet, thirst-removing, and scraping.
Beneficial to the eyes, it removes hiccup, vomiting, nausea, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and disorders of the blood.
From the mouth of <s>Vāsuki</s>, exhausted by the agitation of churning,
poisonous drops of sweat fell upon another island.

children.text: yatra yatra patanti sma prarūḍhā gulmarūpataḥ
children.translated_text: Wherever they fell, they grew up in the form of shrubs;

children.text: teṣu jātaṃ tu niryāsamaphenaṃ bruvate janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: people call the resin produced in them <s>aphena</s>.
<s>Aphena</s> is fourfold: <s>jāraṇa</s>, <s>māraṇa</s>,
<s>dhāraṇa</s>, and <s>sāraṇa</s>; I shall state their characteristics in order.

children.text: śvetaṃ tu jāraṇaṃ proktaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ tu māraṇam
children.translated_text: The white is called <s>jāraṇa</s>; the black-colored is <s>māraṇa</s>.

children.text: dhāraṇaṃ pītavarṇaṃ ca karburaṃ sāraṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: The yellow-colored is <s>dhāraṇa</s>, and the mottled is <s>sāraṇa</s>.
<s>Jāraṇa</s> digests food; <s>māraṇa</s> brings death.
<s>Dhāraṇa</s> arrests age, while <s>sāraṇa</s> promotes evacuation of feces.

children.text: aphenaṃ sannipātaghnaṃ vṛṣyaṃ balyaṃ ca mohadam
children.translated_text: <s>Aphena</s> destroys <s>sannipāta</s>, is aphrodisiac and strengthening, and causes stupefaction.
It destroys <s>grahaṇī</s> disease and diarrhea, and even impotence.
<s>Puṣpāñjana</s>, <s>puṣpaketu</s>, <s>kaustubha</s>, and <s>kusumāñjana</s>,
<s>rītika</s>, <s>rītikusuma</s>, <s>rītipuṣpa</s>, and <s>puṣpaka</s> are names.
<s>Puṣpāñjana</s> is said to be beneficial, removing burning from <s>pitta</s> and hiccup.
It destroys poison, cough, and pain, and removes all eye disorders.
<s>Śaṅkha</s>, ocean-born, <s>kambu</s>, water-born, and having a purifying sound,
curved, with great inner resonance, white-yellow, and good-sounding,
resonant, long-sounding, much-sounding, and dear to <s>Hara</s>,
the small one is <s>kṣullaka</s>, <s>kṣudraśaṅkha</s>, <s>śaṃbūka</s>, or <s>nakhaśaṅkhaka</s>.
<s>Śaṅkha</s> has pungent taste, is cooling, and gives nourishment, virility, and strength.
It destroys abdominal tumors, colic, <s>kapha</s>, and dyspnea, and removes poison disorders.

children.text: kṣullakaḥ kaṭukaḥ snigdhaḥ śūlahārī ca dīpanaḥ
children.translated_text: The small shell is pungent, unctuous, pain-removing, and digestive.
<s>Śukti</s> is mother of pearls, <s>mahāśukti</s>, and <s>śuktikā</s>.
She is <s>muktāsphoṭa</s>, <s>stautika</s>, and <s>mauktikaprasavā</s>, the producer of pearls.
She is also to be known as <s>mauktikasū</s> and is likewise remembered as <s>muktāmātā</s>, the mother of pearls.
<s>Muktāśukti</s> (pearl shell) is pungent and unctuous, and removes asthma and heart disease.
It calms colic, is appetizing, sweet, and an excellent kindler of digestion.
It is <s>jalaśukti</s>, <s>kṣudraśukti</s>, and also <s>krimisusphuṭikā</s>.
<s>Jalaśukti</s> (water shell) is pungent and unctuous, kindles digestion, and removes <s>gulma</s> and colic.
Likewise it counteracts poison, is appetizing, digestive, and strength-giving.
<s>Kapardaka</s> is <s>varāṭa</s>, <s>kaparda</s>, and <s>varāṭikā</s>.
It is <s>carācara</s>, <s>cara</s>, excellent, and also a child's plaything.
The <s>varāṭikā</s> is yellowish, knotted on the back, long, and round.
That is designated by physicians of <s>rasa</s> as bearing the name <s>carācara</s>.
One weighing one and a half <s>niṣkas</s> is best, while one weighing a <s>niṣka</s> is middling.
One weighing a quarter less than a <s>niṣka</s> is declared to be inferior.
It destroys <s>pariṇāma</s>-colic and the like, and eliminates <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder and wasting.
It is pungent, hot, digestive-kindling, aphrodisiac, good for the eyes, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
It is prescribed for the digestion of <s>rasendra</s> (mercury) and is praised among the <s>biḍa</s> substances.
Other male cowries are heavy and produce <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Kaparda</s> is pungent, bitter, and hot; it removes earache and wounds.
It also destroys <s>gulma</s>, colic, and disease, and cuts away defects of the eyes.
<s>Sarvakṣāra</s> is <s>bahukṣāra</s>, <s>samūhakṣāra</s>, and <s>sābuṇi</s>.
It is <s>stomakṣāra</s>, <s>mahākṣāra</s>, <s>malāri</s>, and <s>kṣāramelaka</s>.
<s>Sarvakṣāra</s>, the very strong alkali, is good for the eyes and cleanses the bladder.
It destroys <s>udāvarta</s> and worms, and, like <s>biḍa</s>, cleanses cloth.
The alkali that arises from bricks while <s>karīra</s> and <s>pīlu</s> wood are being cooked
is this <s>navasāra</s>, known by the name <s>cūlikā-lavaṇa</s>.
It digests <s>rasendra</s>, melts metals, and produces gastric fire.
It destroys <s>gulma</s>, spleen disease, and dryness of the mouth, and digests eaten meat and the like.
One should impregnate <s>saurāṣṭrī</s> a hundred times with cow bile; then,
after blowing it, one should cause the essence to fall; the <s>krāmaṇa</s> is extremely secret.
First comes the name <s>mūṣaka</s>, and then the name <s>pāṣāṇa</s>.
This, named <s>ākhupāṣāṇa</s>, causes the alloying of metals.
<s>Ākhugrāvā</s> is fluid and dry, and removes vomiting and cold fever.
It is esteemed in operations on silver and cuts away fat and bad flesh.
<s>Rāla</s> is <s>sarjarasa</s>, <s>yakṣadhūpa</s>, and beloved of fire.
It is dear to the gods, the exudation of the <s>śāla</s> tree, fragrant, and beloved as incense.

children.text: rālastu pañcadhā prokto raktaḥ pītaḥ sito'sitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāla</s> is taught as fivefold: red, yellow, white, black,
and variegated; among these, the black is to be known as superior in qualities.
<s>Rāla</s> is cooling, unctuous, astringent, and bitter in taste.
It removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and destroys eruptions, itching, and severe wounds.
Once, seeing the gods defeated by the lord of the <s>Dānavas</s>, bereft of beauty, firmness, courage, and splendor,
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is said to have created the nectar, <s>guggulu</s>, which grants strength, body, and victory.
In desert lands the <s>pura</s> trees generally grow.

children.text: bhānor mayūkhaiḥ saṃtaptā grīṣme muñcanti guggulum
children.translated_text: Scorched by the rays of the sun in summer, they emit <s>guggulu</s>.
<s>Guggulu</s> is taught as fivefold: <s>mahiṣākṣa</s>, <s>nīlaka</s>,
<s>padma</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, and <s>suvarṇa</s> as the fifth, O dear one.
<s>Mahiṣākṣa</s> and <s>nīla</s> bestow good qualities on elephants.
<s>Kumuda</s> and <s>padma</s> do so for horses, and the golden-colored kind for human beings.
In castor-seed oil, or in sesame oil, or in ghee,
one should purify good <s>guggulu</s> with decoctions boiled with the five bitters.
One should cook it in a <s>dolāyantra</s> until it becomes clear.
Thus purified, it should be collected and used in the appropriate preparations.
Pustules, scrofulous swellings, and the like perish, as do disorders of <s>marut</s>.
<s>Yavakṣāra</s> is <s>amṛta</s>, <s>pākya</s>, <s>yavaja</s>, and <s>yavaśūkaja</s>.
It is <s>yavaśūka</s>, <s>yavāhva</s>, <s>yavapākya</s>, and <s>yavāruja</s>.
<s>Yavakṣāra</s> is pungent and hot, and removes abdominal distress caused by <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
It is supreme for removing <s>āma</s>-colic, urinary stones, dysuria, poison, and disorders.
<s>Sadyaḥkṣāra</s> is <s>sarjika</s>, <s>kṣāra</s>, <s>sajjī</s>, and <s>suvarjika</s>.
<s>Sarjīka</s> is pungent, dry, and sharp, and removes afflictions of <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
It destroys <s>gulma</s>, abdominal distension, and vomiting, and removes urinary and abdominal diseases.
<s>Loṇāra</s>, <s>lavaṇottha</s>, <s>lavaṇāsura</s>, and <s>lavaṇameda</s>,

children.text: jatujaṃ lavaṇakṣāraṃ lavaṇaṃ ca kṣāralavaṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>jatuja</s>, <s>lavaṇakṣāra</s>, <s>lavaṇa</s>, and <s>kṣāralavaṇa</s> are its names.
<s>Loṇakakṣāra</s> is very hot and sharp, and causes an increase of <s>pitta</s>.
It is somewhat alkaline and saline, and removes pain from <s>vāta</s>, <s>gulma</s>, and the like.
<s>Vajraka</s>, <s>vajrakakṣāra</s>, the best alkali, and <s>vidāraka</s>,

children.text: sāraṃ candanasāraṃ ca dhūmotthaṃ dhūmajaṃ gajāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>sāra</s>, <s>candanasāra</s>, <s>dhūmottha</s>, <s>dhūmaja</s>, and <s>gaja</s> are its names.

children.text: vajrakakṣāram atyuṣṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ kṣāraṃ ca rodhanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrakakṣāra</s> is very hot, sharp, alkaline, and obstructive.
It is supreme for calming <s>gulma</s>, abdominal distress, obstruction, and colic.
<s>Sāmudraka</s> is <s>sāmudra</s>, <s>sāmudralavaṇa</s>, and <s>śiva</s>.
<s>Sāmudra</s> (sea salt) is light, pleasing to the heart, and increases fluids, blood, and <s>pitta</s>.
It is burning, destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, kindles digestion, creates appetite, and is agreeable.
<s>Saindhava</s> is <s>śītaśiva</s>, <s>nādeya</s>, <s>sindhuja</s>, and <s>śiva</s>.
It is pure, auspicious in nature, wholesome, and newly named <s>māṇimantha</s>.

children.text: saindhavaṃ lavaṇaṃ vṛṣyaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ dīpanaṃ ruci
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> salt is aphrodisiac, good for the eyes, digestive-kindling, and appetizing.
When purified, it is suitable for nasal therapy, destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>, and overcomes defects of wounds and constipation.

children.text: saindhavaṃ dvividhaṃ jñeyaṃ sitaṃ raktamiti kramāt
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> is to be known as twofold, respectively white and red.
The white, purifying kind is rich in qualities with respect to taste, potency, and post-digestive effect.
It is produced from blue glass, is <s>kācatilaka</s>, and is born from glass.
<s>Kākasauvarcala</s>, <s>kācalavaṇa</s>, and that which is born from cooking are remembered;
also glass-born, pleasant-smelling, and likewise <s>tatkālalavaṇa</s>,
<s>kuruvinda</s>, glass-impurity, and <s>katima</s>: these are fourteen names.
The salt called <s>kāca</s> is appetizing, slightly alkaline, and somewhat bilious;
it causes burning, destroys phlegm and wind, kindles digestion, and removes abdominal tumors and colic.

children.text: biḍaṃ ca biḍakaṃ khaṇḍaṃ kṛtakṣāraṃ ca āsuram
children.translated_text: <s>Biḍa</s>, <s>biḍaka</s>, <s>khaṇḍa</s>, prepared alkali, and <s>āsura</s>,

children.text: supākyaṃ lavaṇaṃ khaṇḍaṃ dhūrtaṃ kṛtrimakaṃ daśa ||
children.translated_text: well-cooked salt, <s>khaṇḍa</s>, <s>dhūrta</s>, and artificial: these ten are its names.
<s>Biḍa</s> is hot, salty, digestive, and destructive of wind;
it is appetizing and destroys pain from indigestion, abdominal tumors, and urinary disease.
<s>Sauvarcala</s>, <s>rucaka</s>, <s>tilaka</s>, pleasant-smelling,

children.text: akṣaṃ ca kṛṣṇalavaṇaṃ rucyaṃ kodravikaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>akṣa</s>, black salt, appetizing, and <s>kodravika</s> are likewise its names.
<s>Sauvarcala</s> is light, alkaline, pungent, hot, and removes abdominal tumors and colic;
it conquers upward-moving wind, pain from undigested matter, obstruction, and loss of appetite.
<s>Amla</s>, <s>amlavetasa</s>, <s>vedhin</s>, <s>rasāmla</s>, and <s>vītavetasa</s>,
<s>vetasāra</s>, <s>amlasāra</s>, <s>śaravedhin</s>, and <s>vedhaka</s>,
<s>nīla</s>, breaker, splitter, royal acid, and acid-splitter,
<s>amlāṅkuśa</s>, red-essence, fruit-acid, and chief of acids,
thousand-piercer, powerful acid, banner against abdominal tumors, and <s>dharākṣidhā</s>:
it dissolves conch, flesh, and the like; <s>amlavetasa</s> itself is twofold.
<s>Amlavetasa</s> is very sour, astringent, hot, and conquers undigested matter and wind;
it is supreme in removing phlegm, piles, disorders from undigested matter, abdominal tumors, and loss of appetite.
<s>Kāca</s>, <s>tuṣārasāra</s>, and remover of the impurities of mercury and <s>khoṭa</s>,
<s>śṛṅgārī</s> and bearer of mica: it removes all eye diseases.
<s>Piṣṭaka</s>, <s>chagaṇa</s>, <s>chāṇa</s>, <s>utpala</s>, and forest-lotus,
<s>kariṇḍopala</s>, <s>śāṭhī</s>, <s>varaṭī</s>, and that called <s>chagaṇa</s> are its names.
Its ash is famed as removing the defects of mercury and metals and as destroying impurity.
<s>Śikhitrā</s>, fire-remnants, charcoals, and <s>koliśā</s> are held to be its names;
and charcoals, also called <s>kokilā</s>, are those that have gone out without water.
Sand is produced by streams; sprinkled, it is fine powdered water-stone.
That sand removes fatigue, and by sprinkling it destroys disorders of the combined doṣas.
One should soak <s>kāsīsa</s> in the heat of the sun for a day with liquids born from citron.

children.text: śudhyate ṭaṅkaṇaṃ gairī kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ ca varāṭikā
children.translated_text: <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, red ochre, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, and cowrie

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ nīlāñjanaṃ caiva pṛthak śodhyaṃ dine dine ||
children.translated_text: and conch and blue collyrium should each be purified separately, day by day.
One should grind <s>śilājatu</s> in an iron vessel with cow's milk, decoctions of <s>triphalā</s>, and juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s>;
after one day it becomes purified.
<s>Darada</s>, treated with ewe's milk and substances of the sour group,
seven times with care, certainly attains purification.
<s>Sūryāvarta</s>, <s>vajrakanda</s>, plantain, <s>devadālikā</s>,

children.text: śigruḥ kośātakī vandhyā kākamācī ca vālukā ||
children.translated_text: <s>śigru</s>, <s>kośātakī</s>, barren <s>kākamācī</s>, and sand:
with the juice of any one of these, together with the three alkalis and salts,
and with substances of the sour group, one should soak it carefully for one day.
<s>Sauvīra</s>, lodestone, and purified earth of the <s>bhūnāga</s>,
and then all subordinate minerals should each be treated separately, day by day.

children.text: tataḥ pācyaṃ ca taddrāvairḍolāyantre dinaṃ sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: Then the wise person should cook them with those liquids in a <s>ḍolāyantra</s> for a day;

children.text: śudhyante nātra sandehaḥ sarve uparasāḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: all subordinate minerals are purified separately; there is no doubt here.
With <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>meghanāda</s>, <s>kapi-jambīra</s>, and <s>tinduka</s>,
with <s>agasti</s> flowers, white water-lily, barley, tamarind, and <s>amlavetasa</s>,
with wild elephant-foot yam, earth-emblic, <s>maṇḍūkī</s>, and oleander,
with bitter gourd, milk-tuber, red lotus, and thick juice of <s>śamī</s>,
with <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, hare fat, <s>śakravāruṇī</s>, and borax,
with oil, fish fat, the three pungents, and these liquids together with sour gruel:
with all these together or separately, in a <s>ḍolāyantra</s> for three days,
one should thoroughly cook mica sheets and the other subordinate minerals for the sake of purification.
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said:
I shall tell the sequence of the origin and so forth of gold and all metals.
<s>Svarṇa</s>, <s>suvarṇa</s>, <s>kanaka</s>, bright <s>kāñcana</s>, auspicious <s>hāṭaka</s>, <s>hiraṇya</s>, and lovely gold,
<s>gāṅgeya</s>, ocher-hued, great silver, fire-potency, <s>rukma</s>, <s>hema</s>, <s>tapanīya</s>, and shining gold,
<s>jāmbūnada</s>, <s>aṣṭāpada</s>, native gold, <s>piñjāna</s>, <s>cāmīkara</s>, and variegated gold,
<s>kārtasvara</s>, tawny-colored, very brilliant, blazing, stainless, lamp-like, and yellow gold,
auspicious, <s>saumerava</s>, <s>śātakumbha</s>, ornamental, moonlike, silver-born, and <s>jāmbava</s>,
fire-born, <s>niṣka</s>, and flame-like: thus the names of gold are traditionally determined.
Natural, innate, fire-born, and mine-born:
together with that produced by the penetration of mercury, gold is remembered as fivefold.
That by which the cosmic egg was covered, born indeed from the quality of passion,
is called natural; it is difficult even for the gods to obtain.

children.text: brahmā yenāvṛto jātaḥ suvarṇaṃ sahajaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: That by which <s>Brahmā</s> was covered when born is indeed innate gold.
The Śaiva yellow radiance, very hard to bear, emitted by fire,
became gold; that is specified as fire-born gold.
These three kinds of gold are divine and endowed with sixteen grades of color;
by merely wearing them, they make the body free from old age and disease.
That which is produced in the mines of mountains is remembered as mine-born gold;
it is rich in fourteen grades of color and, when eaten, removes every disease.
That which is produced by the penetration of the lord of mercury is called penetration-born;

children.text: rasāyanaṃ mahāśreṣṭhaṃ pavitraṃ vedhajaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: that penetration-born gold is a most excellent <s>rasāyana</s> and purifying.

children.text: raktābhaṃ pītavarṇaṃ ca dvividhaṃ kāñcanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: <s>Kāñcana</s> is of two kinds, reddish in appearance and yellow in color;

children.text: dāhe raktaṃ sitaṃ chede nikaṣe kuṅkumaprabham ||
children.translated_text: in burning it is red, in cutting it is white, and on the touchstone it has the lustre of saffron.

children.text: guru snigdhaṃ mṛdu svacchaṃ nirdalaṃ raktapītakam
children.translated_text: Gold that is heavy, unctuous, soft, clear, free from lamination, and reddish-yellow,
and that is endowed with sixteen grades of color, is praised for the body and for metals.

children.text: śvetāṅgaṃ kaṭhinaṃ rūkṣaṃ vivarṇaṃ samalaṃ dalam
children.translated_text: Gold that is white-bodied, hard, dry, discolored, impure, and laminated,

children.text: dāhe śvetāsitaṃ śvetaṃ nikaṣe laghu ca vrajet ||
children.translated_text: turns white or black in burning, white when cut, and pale on the touchstone.

children.text: na śuddhaṃ na mṛtaṃ svarṇaṃ rogavargaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: Gold that is neither purified nor killed produces a class of diseases,
and destroys happiness, virility, and strength; therefore purification is prescribed.
Anthill earth, soot, red ocher, brick, and salt:
these are the five clays; with citron juices and sour gruel,
one should grind them and smear gold leaf; covered with ash in an earthen saucer,
one should apply <s>puṭa</s>-heating until it liquefies; by that it is purified.
One should purify gold by <s>puṭa</s>-cooking with clay that has been impregnated for five days with citron acid,
together with ash and salt.
One should soak the five clays for three days with citron acid;
with rock salt and earth-ash, gold is purified as before.

children.text: taile takre gavāṃ mūtre hyāranāle kulutthake
children.translated_text: In oil, buttermilk, cow's urine, sour gruel, and horse gram,
one should quench the heated metal seven times in sequence, with each liquid.
This purification is praised for sheets of gold and other metals;
melted lead and tin likewise should be quenched for purification.
First one should cast gold in the juice arising from <s>kāñcanāra</s>;

children.text: saptavāraṃ tataḥ karmayogyaṃ hema bhaved dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: after seven times the gold certainly becomes fit for operations.
Lead powder mixed with <s>śilā</s> (realgar) and combined with the latex of <s>vajrī</s>,
should be applied to gold leaves by smearing and by the <s>puṭa</s> procedure.
One should grind killed lead with the latex of <s>snuhī</s>, or with some sour liquid,

children.text: piṣṭvā lepyaṃ svarṇapatraṃ ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: smear it on gold leaf, seal it, and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Taking killed lead, one eighth part, one should grind it in sour liquid,
seal it and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, combined with lead as before.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ pākādaṣṭadhā mriyate dhruvam
children.translated_text: By cooking again and again in this way, it is certainly killed in eight rounds.
Add sulphur equal to purified mercury, and <s>mākṣika</s> with sour substances;
with eight <s>puṭas</s> gold is killed, the procedure being as before.
One should make a pellet in a mortar from gold equal to purified mercury;

children.text: ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ dattvā sarvatulyaṃ nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: placing sulphur above and below, equal to the whole, and sealing it,
one should give fourteen <s>puṭas</s> with thirty forest-fuel cakes.

children.text: nirutthaṃ jāyate bhasma gandhaṃ deyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: A non-revivable ash is produced; sulphur should be added again and again.
After melting one <s>tola</s> of gold, one should add one <s>māṣa</s> of purified lead;
having taken that powder, into sulphur and <s>mākṣika</s> equal to it,
one should triturate it with sour liquid for a <s>yāma</s>, seal it, and cook it in a light <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: gandhaṃ punaḥ punardeyaṃ mriyate daśabhiḥ puṭaiḥ
children.translated_text: Sulphur should be added again and again; it is killed with ten <s>puṭas</s>.
One should make gold leaves and smear them with ash of mercury;
having ground it with sour liquid, one should heat the gold in a <s>puṭa</s>; it becomes lifeless.
Or, heated in a <s>puṭa</s> with <s>tāpya</s>, gold goes to the state of ash.
Or one should reduce it to ash with killed <s>kariṇa</s> and with a preparation of <s>śilā</s> (realgar);
or, smeared with a <s>yoginī</s> portion together with killed diamond,
it goes to ash by subordinate minerals, by <s>rasas</s>, and indeed by <s>mahārasas</s>.

children.text: amlapiṣṭair viliptaṃ ca puṭitaṃ yāti bhasmatām ||
children.translated_text: Smeared with substances ground in sour liquid and heated in a <s>puṭa</s>, it goes to the state of ash.
One should triturate mercury twice the amount of gold with sour liquid for a <s>yāma</s>;
after placing <s>āroṭa</s>-<s>mākṣika</s>, equal to the gold, in a crucible,
on top of that the triturated gold, and on top of that purified <s>mākṣika</s>,

children.text: deyaṃ svarṇasamaṃ tacca pṛṣṭhe gandhaṃ ca tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: also equal to the gold, should be placed; and on top, sulphur equal to that.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca cūrṇitaṃ dadyād ruddhvā mūṣāṃ dhameddṛḍham
children.translated_text: All of it, powdered, should be put in; after sealing the crucible, one should blow it strongly.
When naturally cooled, it should be taken; that ash is in five parts.
One should grind borax and white glass, one part of each;
the three, mixed with honey and ghee, are formed into a pellet.
One part of <s>dhānyābhra</s> should be placed below and above;
after sealing it, one should blow it strongly in a crucible for two <s>ghaṭikās</s>.
A non-revivable ash is produced; it should be employed in the appropriate formulations.

children.text: hemnaḥ pādaṃ mṛtaṃ sūtaṃ piṣṭamamlena kenacit ||
children.translated_text: Dead mercury, one quarter of the gold, ground with some sour liquid,
should be smeared on the leaf and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>; with eight <s>puṭas</s> it is certainly killed.
For killing all purified metals, the method is like this.
One part of purified <s>mākṣika</s> and one part of <s>āroṭa</s>-<s>mākṣika</s>,
adding two parts of mercury, one should triturate the three with sour liquid.

children.text: bhāgaikaṃ hemapatraṃ ca liptvā cāmlena mardayet
children.translated_text: Then one should smear one part of gold leaf and triturate it with sour liquid,
and cook that pellet forcefully in a <s>pātana</s> apparatus for three <s>yāmas</s>.

children.text: ityevaṃ mriyate svarṇaṃ nirutthaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: In this way gold is killed and becomes non-revivable; there is no doubt here.
With barley, tamarind, <s>rajovṛkṣa</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, and borax,

children.text: liptvā svarṇasya patrāṇi ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet
children.translated_text: having smeared the leaves of gold and sealed them, one should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: tair dravaiḥ piṣṭyā mriyate saptadhā puṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ground with their liquids, it is killed by sevenfold <s>puṭa</s>-heating.
<s>Pīluka</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>bukkāṇa</s>, and <s>sauvarcala</s>, well ground,

children.text: liptvā svarṇasya patrāṇi mriyate saptabhiḥ puṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: after smearing the leaves of gold, kill it with seven <s>puṭas</s>.
Gold is nourishing, unctuous, and sweet in taste and post-digestive effect;
cool, slightly astringent and bitter, it removes the faults of poison.

children.text: hṛdyaṃ kāntipradaṃ balyaṃ saṃrasanaṃ guru lekhanam
children.translated_text: It is good for the heart, gives complexion, gives strength, harmonizes the fluids, is heavy, and is scraping;
it produces intelligence, understanding, and memory, heals wounds, and gives purity of speech.
It pacifies consumption and madness, benefits the eyes, and is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative);
it pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s>, is mild, life-promoting, pleasing, and pure.
By wearing it, there arises sovereignty that produces insight, vigor, and good voice.
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said:
Silver is white, the best of wealth, beautiful, and moon-metal;
it is called <s>rajata</s>, heated silver, and, since it has the nature of the moon, <s>raupyaka</s>.

children.text: kaladhautaṃ ca saudhaṃ ca candrahāsaṃ ca tārakam
children.translated_text: It is also called refined silver, bright silver, moon-smile, and star-like silver.

children.text: sahajaṃ khanisaṃjātaṃ kṛtrimaṃ ca tridhā matam ||
children.translated_text: It is considered threefold: natural, mine-born, and artificial.
Of these forms of silver, each preceding kind is superior to each succeeding one by its own qualities.
Silver produced from mountains such as <s>Kailāsa</s> is natural silver.
When merely touched, it becomes a destroyer of great diseases for embodied beings.
That silver which is produced on peaks such as the <s>Himācala</s>

children.text: khanijaṃ kathyate tajjñaiḥ paramaṃ hi rasāyanam
children.translated_text: is called mine-born by those who know; it is indeed an excellent <s>rasāyana</s>.
Tin which, placed on the sandals of <s>Śrī Rāma</s>, has become silver
is called foot-silver; it is artificial and removes all diseases.

children.text: ghanaṃ snigdhaṃ guru snigdhaṃ dāhe chede sitaṃ mṛdu ||
children.translated_text: Good silver is solid, oily, heavy, oily, white when burned or cut, and soft;
rich in color, clear like the moon, and of equal brightness when burned and cut.
Silver that resembles a conch, is smooth, and is free from blisters is auspicious.

children.text: dāhe raktaṃ ca pītaṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ sphuṭaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: Silver that, when burned, is red, yellow, or black, dry, cracked, light,
large-limbed, or rough-bodied is to be rejected in eight ways.

children.text: kaṭhinaṃ kṛtrimaṃ rūkṣaṃ vivarṇaṃ samalaṃ dalam
children.translated_text: Hard, artificial, dry, discolored, impure, and flaky silver,

children.text: dāhe chede ghane naṣṭaṃ madhyamaṃ rajataṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: and that which is ruined in density when burned or cut, is considered middling silver.
Unpurified and unincinerated <s>tāra</s> (silver) produces heat, looseness of stool, and loss of semen, strength, and lifespan;

children.text: na śuddhaṃ na mṛtaṃ tāraṃ tasmācchuddhaṃ ca mārayet ||
children.translated_text: therefore one should purify and incinerate <s>tāra</s>.
Melted with lead and borax, it attains purification.
Silver, cast three times into oil made from <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>,
one should heat again and again as silver leaf and sprinkle it; it attains purification.
Or, when it is thrown into that which is produced from <s>piśāca</s>, it attains purification.
One should take silver freed from defects and taken out from lead.
One should pour it seven times into water produced from white gourd.
One should grind it thoroughly with waters produced from <s>kuraṇḍa</s> and sage-flowers.
Silver leaves smeared with these should be heated in a closed firing with wild cow-dung cakes.

children.text: mriyate nātra sandehaḥ liptaṃ vā rasabhasmanā
children.translated_text: It is incinerated; there is no doubt here. Or it may be smeared with ash of mercury.
Smeared with substances of the sour group, by the procedure of heating as before,
<s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), mercury, and tin are incinerated when ground with acid.
Having smeared silver leaves and heated them in a closed firing, one should bring them to the state of ash.
It is incinerated by treatments beginning with sulphur; by the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> method it is destroyed.
One should cook <s>tāpya</s> with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and smear the silver leaves.
Having sealed them and cooked them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, one should cook them again with the substances stated before.
In this way, with forty closed firings, one should cook the silver; it becomes incinerated.
One should take equal quantities of earth-emblic and pyrite, with long pepper, rock salt, and sour substances,

children.text: liptvā tārasya patrāṇi ruddhvā saptapuṭaiḥ pacet ||
children.translated_text: smear the leaves of silver, seal them, and cook them with seven closed firings.

children.text: dravaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ piṣṭvā mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Grinding again and again with liquids, it is incinerated; there is no doubt here.
One should prepare a paste of silver with citron juice and mercury.

children.text: ruddhvādho gandhakaṃ dattvā mūṣāgarbhe nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: Having sealed it, placing sulphur below, and enclosing it inside a crucible,
one should steam it in a sand apparatus for one day with strong fire.
When the paste has cooled by itself, it should be ground with sour <s>tāla</s>.
One should heat it twelve times in closed firings; the silver becomes ash.
Pyrite powder, ground with citron acid and heated slowly,
makes that silver, after thirty repetitions, become ash that does not rise again.

children.text: rāgaḥ syāt sarvalohānāṃ puṭādhikye na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: With an excess of closed firings, all metals acquire color; there is no doubt.
Let silver leaf be four parts and purified <s>tālaka</s> one part.
It should be ground with liquids born from citron, and the silver leaves should be smeared.
One should dry it, close it, and heat it with thirty wild cow-dung cakes.
In this way, with fourteen closed firings, it certainly becomes incinerated and unable to rise again.
Let silver leaf be four parts and incinerated tin one part.
Or else one part of sulphur should be smeared on, ground with citron.
Having sealed it, it should be cooked with three closed firings, each with twenty-five wild cow-dung cakes.

children.text: mriyate nātra sandeho gandho deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: It is incinerated; there is no doubt here. Sulphur should be added again and again.
Making mercury and sulphur equal, with the root of <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>,
one should grind them with buffalo milk and wash that paste with water.
Having put it into a ball of turmeric, one should place the ball in horse dung.
After putting it there for twenty-one days, one should take it out again from within it.
After grinding that, the silver leaves are to be smeared with some acid.

children.text: puṭair viṃśatibhir bhasma jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: With twenty closed firings it becomes ash; there is no doubt here.
One should smear a copper razor with the ash ground with acid.
When it is produced, one should know that to be incinerated ash of gold and silver.

children.text: raupyaṃ snigdhaṃ kaṣāyāmlaṃ vipāke madhuraṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: Silver is oily, astringent and sour, and sweet in post-digestive effect and taste.
It preserves age, is cooling and scraping, and conquers disorders of wind and bile.
It is aphrodisiac, pleasant to the taste, strengthening, and kindles the digestive fire.
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said:
Copper is called <s>mlecchamukha</s>, <s>śulba</s>, desired in heating, and <s>udumbara</s>;
also <s>tryambaka</s>, lovely lotus, sun-metal, and beloved of the sun.
It is red, Nepalese, red ore, and <s>karendudhā</s>.
It is of two kinds, <s>mleccha</s> and Nepalese; of those two, Nepalese is best.
That produced from a mine other than Nepal is called <s>mleccha</s>.
It is very oily, soft, red, compact under blows, durable, and heavy.
Copper that is unaltered, heavy, and excellent is called <s>Nepāla</s>.
It has a white, black, and red sheen, is difficult to split, and is hard.
When washed it becomes black again; this is <s>mlecchaka</s> copper.
Copper that is pale, black-red, light, and marked by cracking,
with a dry body and layers, is not desired in <s>rasa</s>-work.
Oozing, stupor, dizziness, burning, and piercing pains are indeed the hard-to-remove faults of copper.
Through purification, freed from its own faults, it becomes like nectar in taste, potency, and digestion.
It causes vomiting, fainting, dizziness, madness, various diseases, skin disease, and colic.
It causes the loss of lifespan, complexion, and strength, and it vitiates the bodily constituents.

children.text: nu śuddhaṃ na mṛtaṃ tāmraṃ tena saṃśodhya mārayet ||
children.translated_text: Copper that is not purified and not incinerated should therefore be purified and incinerated.
Copper joined with alkali and acid, melted, and treated with heated red ochre,
should be thrown seven times into a mass of buffalo buttermilk and goat-dung.
By the seventh repetition it becomes free from the five faults.
Having smeared thin copper sheets with citron and rock-salt,
one should heat them and cast them into <s>sauvīraka</s>; after eight repetitions it is purified.
When they have been smeared with citron-water and salt and heated eight times,
the sheets are purified by rubbing with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
A copper sheet placed inside leaves of <s>kumārī</s>,
when fired in a <s>puṭa</s>, becomes free from faults and turns pale.
Copper purified in this way is rid of all faults
and becomes supreme, producing <s>rasāyana</s> effects and perfection of the body and metals.
One should know this purification as taught by <s>Śiva</s> or <s>Nandikeśvara</s>.
Copper struck down by a strong agent and raised again seven times
becomes free from all faults and resembles nectar.
A copper sheet should be smeared with the latex of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, salt, and sour gruel,

children.text: liptvā pratāpya nirguṇḍīrasaiḥ siñcyāt punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: heated, and sprinkled again and again with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
After twelve repetitions, through smearing, heating, and sprinkling, it is purified.
One should grind chalk and salt with buttermilk and <s>āranāla</s>.

children.text: tena liptaṃ tāmrapatraṃ taptaṃ taptaṃ niṣecayet
children.translated_text: A copper sheet smeared with that should be heated repeatedly and quenched.
For purification, this is done six times in sour buttermilk and in <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
Heated copper sheets should be sprinkled with bitter plant juices.
After smearing them again and again with sour buttermilk, salt, and sour gruel,
one should sprinkle them three times while hot; they certainly attain purification.
One should cook a copper vessel in cow urine for one <s>yāma</s> with a strong fire.
It is purified, with no doubt here; now its incineration is also described.
One should smear it with sulfur equal to the copper and ground with an acid liquid.
The pierced sheet should be enclosed and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.
After removing it, one should powder it; into that one should add a quarter-part of sulfur.
With citrons, with <s>āranāla</s>, or with liquids of <s>mṛgadūrvā</s>,

children.text: piṣṭvā piṣṭvā pacedruddhaṃ sagandhaṃ ca catuṣpuṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should grind it again and again and cook it sealed, together with sulfur, through four <s>puṭas</s>.
After grinding it with citron juice, one <s>puṭa</s> should be given.
One <s>puṭa</s> should also be given with white sugar; it becomes incinerated.
With juices of <s>pāṣāṇabhedī</s> and <s>matsyākṣī</s>, sulfur in double quantity

children.text: tāmrasya lepayet piṣṭiṃ ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground into a paste with the copper; after sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Again adding sulfur in an equal part, one should stir and grind it with liquids.

children.text: evaṃ saptapuṭaiḥ pakvaṃ tāmrabhasma bhaved dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Thus cooked through seven <s>puṭas</s>, copper ash certainly comes into being.
One should triturate mercury three times the quantity of copper with the acid of citron.

children.text: ādau mūṣāntare kṣiptvā dhuttūrasya tu patrakam ||
children.translated_text: First, after placing leaves of <s>dhattūra</s> inside a crucible,

children.text: tatpṛṣṭhe tāmratulyaṃ ca gandhakaṃ cūrṇitaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: one should put on top of them powdered sulfur equal to the copper.

children.text: tatpṛṣṭhe marditaṃ tāmraṃ pūrvatulyaṃ ca gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: On top of that one should put the triturated copper and sulfur equal to the previous amount.
After covering it with leaves of <s>dhūrtā</s> and sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
When it has cooled by itself, the powder is certainly incinerated.
One should wash the copper sheet with a little sulfur or with acid.
One should smear the moist sheet with mercury equal to one quarter of the copper.
Then again, with sulfur twice the copper and ground with acid,
having smeared it, one should place well-ground sour <s>parṇikā</s> below and above.

children.text: tatpiṇḍaṃ bhāṇḍagarbhe tu ruddhvā cullyāṃ vipācayet
children.translated_text: That lump should be sealed inside a vessel and cooked on a hearth.
In one <s>yāma</s>, by the cooking of the copper, it certainly becomes ash.

children.text: sūtamekaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ yāmaṃ kanyā vimardayet
children.translated_text: One part mercury and two parts sulfur should be rubbed for one <s>yāma</s> with <s>kumārī</s>.

children.text: dvayos tulye tāmrapatre sthālyā garbhe nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: It should be enclosed inside a pot between two equal copper sheets.
The joint should be sealed well with clay and salt, and ash should be placed at the side.
One should cook it for four <s>yāmas</s> on a hearth, with cow-dung on the back of the vessel.
Water should be applied again and again; when it has cooled by itself, it should be powdered.
It is incinerated, with no doubt here, and should be used in all formulations.
Taking aged copper, one should add these to it:

children.text: vaṅgaṃ ghoṣaṃ gajaṃ tīkṣṇasāraṃ kāntaṃ ca ṣaṭ samān ||
children.translated_text: <s>vaṅga</s>, <s>ghoṣa</s>, <s>gaja</s>, <s>tīkṣṇasāra</s>, and <s>kānta</s>, the six in equal parts.
Each should be in a measure equal to the copper; one should smelt them all together.
By means of a bent tube, this is continued until only the distillate remains.
That distillate should first be poured into <s>nirguṇḍī</s> water.
Seven times one should cause its root-powder to pass into the distillate.
With that copper one should make an unbroken, auspicious pill.

children.text: dviguṇaṃ gandhakaṃ liptvā balestryaṃśaṃ ca pāradam ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared it with twice as much sulfur and a third part of mercury,
or with purified mercury born from <s>hiṅgula</s>, one should triturate it with citrons,
or with lemons or with waters of <s>likuca</s>, grinding it thoroughly.
After drying it for three days, one should then place it inside a vessel.
And above it one should place a copper vessel with its mouth turned downward.
Afterwards one should smear it firmly, and set on a small earthen bowl.

children.text: atiprayatnāllimpet tāṃ yathā vārā na bhidyate ||
children.translated_text: One should seal it with the greatest care, so that the water does not break through.
Then, having placed it on a stove and filled the lower part with water,
one should kindle the fire in sequence, mild, moderate, and strong.

children.text: dināni ṣaṭ samādāya svāṅgaśītaṃ tu pātrakam
children.translated_text: After six days have passed, when the vessel has cooled of itself,

children.text: nirbhidya śulvaṃ gṛhṇīta mṛtaṃ sūtena yatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should break it open and carefully take the copper killed with <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
Then one should pulverize this in a mortar and employ it as desired.
For purifying various kinds of killed copper, there should be five parts

children.text: bhāgaikaṃ śvetakācaṃ ca bhāgaṃ śvetaṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇam
children.translated_text: of copper, and one part of white glass and one part of white <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax).
Having mixed these and put them in a crucible, one should add one part of mica sheet above.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ dattvā nirudhyātha dhmāte grāhyaṃ suśītalam
children.translated_text: Then, after sealing it and blowing the fire, it is to be taken out when well cooled.
The copper becomes free from defect and becomes a remover of all diseases.
Or else one should grind killed copper with any one sour liquid.
Having sealed that ball inside a <s>sūraṇa</s> tuber, one should smear it on every side.
When dry, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; it becomes a remover of all defects.

children.text: vāntiṃ bhrāntiṃ virekaṃ ca na karoti kadācana ||
children.translated_text: It never causes vomiting, dizziness, or purging.
Having smeared the copper sheets with a paste of <s>gandhāśma</s> ground in the juice of <s>likuca</s>,
one should cover them, seal them inside a dish,
cook them properly for one <s>yāma</s>, draw them out when cool, and powder them.
That ash, in a dose of one <s>valla</s>, wrapped in a betel leaf,
when eaten, first makes one vomit and then purges after two <s>yāmas</s>.
It destroys fever in people when accompanied by colic and abdominal distension.

children.text: viṣaṃ garaṃ ca vegena vāmayatyeva niścitam
children.translated_text: It certainly makes one vomit up poison and artificial poison quickly.

children.text: pathyamatra pradātavyaṃ gavyaṃ takraṃ ca bhaktakam ||
children.translated_text: As regimen here one should give cow-product buttermilk and cooked rice.
In excessive purging, excessive vomiting, confusion, or an excessive dose,
one should perform a cooling countermeasure according to the appropriateness of each case.
In excessive vomiting one should take a well-cooled roasted sugarcane stalk,

children.text: yadvā bilvabhavaṃ kvāthaṃ sitayā saha pācayet ||
children.translated_text: or else cook a decoction made from <s>bilva</s> with sugar.
In purging, juice of <s>barbūra</s> bark is to be drunk mixed with buttermilk.
With <s>sūta</s> (mercury) equal to the copper, with <s>balin</s> equal to that,
with <s>tāla</s> in a half portion of that, and with <s>śilā</s> in half of that,
one should make a smooth <s>kajjalī</s>, resembling split collyrium.
Inside the belly of the <s>garbhayantra</s> described in the chapter on apparatus,
one should place the <s>kajjalī</s> and copper sheets in alternation.
One should cook it for the length of a <s>yāma</s>, let it cool by itself, and powder it.

children.text: tattadrogaharānupānasahitaṃ tāmraṃ dvivallonmitaṃ sallīḍhaṃ pariṇāmaśūlamudaraṃ śūlaṃ ca pāṇḍujvaram
children.translated_text: Copper measuring two <s>vallas</s>, licked up with the appropriate disease-removing vehicle, removes digestive colic, abdominal disease, colic, pallor, and fever.

children.text: gulmaplīhayakṛtkṣayāgnisadanaṃ mehaṃ ca mūlāmayaṃ duṣṭāṃ ca grahaṇīṃ hareddhruvamidaṃ sarvāmayadhvaṃsanam ||
children.translated_text: It surely removes abdominal tumors, spleen disease, liver wasting, weakness of digestive fire, urinary disease, piles, and bad <s>grahaṇī</s>; this destroys all illnesses.

children.text: tāmraṃ tiktakaṣāyakaṃ ca madhuraṃ pāke'tha vīryoṣṇakaṃ koṣṇaṃ pittakaphāpahaṃ jaṭhararukkuṣṭhāmajūrtyantakṛt
children.translated_text: Copper is bitter and astringent, sweet in digestion, hot in potency, and warm; it removes pitta and kapha and puts an end to abdominal pain, skin disease, <s>āma</s>, and feverish disorder.

children.text: ūrdhvādhaḥpariśodhanaṃ ca viṣahṛtsthaulyāpahaṃ kṣutkaraṃ durnāmakṣayapāṇḍurogaśamanaṃ netryaṃ paraṃ lekhanam ||
children.translated_text: It purifies upward and downward, removes poison and obesity, stimulates hunger, pacifies piles, wasting, and pallor, benefits the eyes, and is an excellent scraping agent.
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said:
Now the origin of the metals called <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍa</s> is told.
When the great ocean was being churned by the host of gods and demons,
long ago there arose in it the nectar, the life of the gods.
As the gods were drinking that, tiny drops fell from it.

children.text: jñātvā tān bhūgatān yantā gopayāmāsa dhūrjaṭiḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing that they had gone into the earth, <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> concealed them,
having made them, on the surface of the earth, into the form of metallic stones.
Those human beings who are overwhelmed by sin and disease do not worship these.

children.text: ityevaṃ śivaguptā ye sudhāyā bindavaḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: Thus, those drops of nectar that were formerly hidden by <s>Śiva</s>:

children.text: teṣāṃ mayā samāsena kathyate sādhanaṃ sphuṭam
children.translated_text: I shall briefly explain their preparation clearly,
for the destruction of diseases such as skin disease, according to my understanding.
Thus iron is threefold, called <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍa</s>.
One should know it to be a hundred times superior to all <s>rasāyanas</s>.
<s>Ayaskānta</s>, <s>kāntaloha</s>, <s>kānta</s>, black iron,
<s>kāntāyasa</s>, great iron, and black iron: <s>kāntaloha</s> is sevenfold.
When consumed, iron that has not been purified and has not been killed
causes heart pain, weakness of digestive fire, great diseases, and even death.
Therefore the purification and killing of <s>kānta</s> are prescribed.
<s>Sūta</s> (mercury) is a rut-maddened elephant; <s>kānta</s> is called its goad.
After recognizing the deposit, one should take it with very great care.
One should reject what has been exposed to wind and sun, O <s>Surasundarī</s>.
The <s>kānta</s> that lies in the earth should be impregnated with goat's blood.
One should wrap it in a hide smeared with goat's blood.
Having enclosed it in goat hide, one should place it in the ground as before.
When it has been dug up after seven months, one should put it in a water pot.
It should always be worshipped with red flowers and anointments of red perfume,
and, supplied with wine and meat, it should be used in mercury-<s>rasāyana</s>.
Processed with goat's blood, it becomes a rotator and a magnet.
By this ordered procedure, dear one, it becomes a dissolving agent.

children.text: kāntalohaṃ vinā sūto dehe na krāmati kvacit
children.translated_text: Without <s>kāntaloha</s>, <s>sūta</s> never enters the body at all.

children.text: na kāntena vinā sūtaḥ kāntaḥ sūtavivarjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor is <s>sūta</s> effective without <s>kānta</s>, nor <s>kānta</s> without <s>sūta</s>.
A procedure joined with <s>kānta</s> and <s>sūta</s> sustains the body.

children.text: purā proktaṃ mayā sarvaṃ kāntasatvaṃ yathāvidhi ||
children.translated_text: Previously I described completely, according to rule, the essence of <s>kānta</s>.
Now I shall explain the processing of <s>kānta</s> and its qualities.
A leaf of <s>kānta</s>, smeared with hare's blood and coated with lime,

children.text: trivāraṃ cāgninā devi doṣaṃ naisargikaṃ tyajet
children.translated_text: when heated three times by fire, O goddess, gives up its natural defect.
In water eight times the measure of <s>triphalā</s>, sixteen palas of <s>triphalā</s>
should be boiled to a decoction reduced to a quarter, and five palas of <s>kānta</s> are to be used.
Having made heated leaves, one should quench them seven times.
Thus the mountain-born, iron-born defect is dissolved.
One should cook powder made of <s>kānta</s> iron in eight times its measure of cow urine.
Washed again with grain-sour gruel and dried, it attains purification.
<s>Ratnamālā</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s>, <s>gojihvā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>,
<s>gopālī</s>, <s>tumburu</s>, and <s>dantī</s>: these should be ground in cow urine.

children.text: tatkalke kāntapatraṃ tu taptaṃ taptaṃ dvisaptadhā ||
children.translated_text: In that paste the <s>kānta</s> leaves, heated again and again, should be quenched fourteen times.
Indeed, one should quench the <s>kānta</s> iron for the removal of all defects.
The procedure for accomplishing <s>kānta</s> should be performed with mantra first.
The repeated word 'udbhava' should stand in the dative ending after 'amṛta'.
It ends with 'svāhā', and the praṇava is at the beginning; this is the mantra established for grinding.
For the protection of iron and mercury, this same formula has the one word 'udbhava'.
Without 'svāhā' at its end, one should add an ending in 'phaṭ', dear one.
After the praṇava come 'namaḥ', 'caṇḍa', and also 'vajrapāṣāṇa'.
After that comes 'namaḥ to the lord of the great diamond army'.
The word 'saru' should be repeated twice, and then 'to the strength of the great vidyā'.
Then comes 'tvāhā'; this mantra is honored in the rite of offering.
Having made the offering with this very mantra, one should perform the procedure as stated.
Then one should grind five palas of <s>hiṅgula</s> with breast milk.
With that very substance one should smear a leaf of <s>kānta</s> measuring five palas.
Having sealed it, it should be cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; then again with <s>triphalā</s> decoctions,
with citrons or with <s>āranāla</s>, one should use <s>hiṅgula</s> as a twentieth part.
Having ground and smeared it, and having sealed it in a closed firing, one should cook that iron again.
Sealed in a closed firing, it should be cooked at night; in the morning it should be impregnated with liquids.
One should do this for eight days; the iron of three kinds is indeed incinerated.
One should make <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍaka</s> like tamarind leaves.
Placed in an earthen vessel in the heat, it should be filled with the juices of <s>dantī</s>.
The leaf should be treated again and again, until it floats by itself.
It is incinerated by the intense heat; having powdered it, one should apply it.
The powder of <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍa</s> irons should be treated with liquids produced from <s>matsyākṣī</s>.
It should be impregnated in the sun for three days, and for three days with the juices of <s>citraka</s>.
For three days with the juices of <s>trikaṇṭaka</s>, and for one day with the liquids of <s>sahadevī</s>.
It should also be impregnated with cow urine and <s>triphalā</s> decoctions for three days each.
Then it should be ground with the stated liquids; in order, closed firing after closed firing should be given.
Having sealed it and treated it thus with <s>gajapuṭa</s> firings, when incinerated it should be used in formulations.

children.text: sthālyāṃ vā lohapātre vā lohadarvyā vicālayan
children.translated_text: In an earthen pot or in an iron vessel, stirring with an iron ladle,
one should cook the iron powder for one day with <s>triphalā</s> decoctions.

children.text: tatpiṇḍaṃ triphalātoyaiḥ piṣṭvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: Having ground that lump with <s>triphalā</s> waters, one should seal it and cook it in a closed firing.
Inside a pit sixteen finger-breadths deep, without wind, it should be cooked day and night.
Thus the pot-cooking, ending in closed firings, should be performed in three ways.
<s>Bhṛṅga</s>, fresh ginger, <s>tālamūla</s>, and the root of <s>hastikarṇī</s>,
and the roots of <s>śatāvarī</s> and <s>vidārī</s>: these should be put in <s>triphalā</s> water.

children.text: saṃpeṣya pūrvavatsthālyāṃ pācyaṃ peṣyaṃ tridhā puṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having ground them together, it should be cooked in the pot as before, ground again, and treated with three closed firings.
Then it should again be cooked with decoctions of <s>punarnavā</s> and <s>daśamūla</s>,
with a decoction of <s>bṛhatī</s> and with liquids of <s>bījapūra</s>,
with juices of <s>brahmabīja</s>, decoctions of <s>śigru</s>, and also with cow's milk.
Having first ground it separately with each, one should cook it in the former pit and closed firing.
At the end of the firing, it should be impregnated with that very liquid for the duration of one <s>yāma</s>.
Grinding it separately in this way, one should subject it to closed firing and impregnate it in sequence.

children.text: mriyate nātra sandehaḥ kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca muṇḍakam
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍaka</s> are incinerated; there is no doubt here.

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ khalve kṛtvā tu kajjalīm ||
children.translated_text: One should place purified mercury and twice as much sulphur in a mortar and make <s>kajjalī</s>.
One should add <s>kānta</s> powder equal to the two and grind it with the juices of <s>kanyakā</s>.
After two <s>yāmas</s>, one should take it out and place that ball in a copper vessel.
Covered with castor leaves, after half a <s>yāma</s> it becomes very hot.
After that one should place it in a heap of grain and take it out at the end of three days.
Having ground it and strained it through cloth, truly it becomes water-floating.

children.text: kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca muṇḍaṃ ca nirutthaṃ jāyate mṛtam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍa</s> become incinerated and unable to rise again.
One should incinerate gold and the other metals in this same way, and powder them like iron.
Now the accomplished formulation has been declared, received face to face from the siddhas.
It has been experienced by me, O goddess, and removes all diseases.

children.text: nāyaḥ pacetpañcapalapramāṇād adho na cordhvaṃ tridaśapramāṇāt ||
children.translated_text: One should cook iron in a quantity not below five palas and not above thirty palas.
The bark of <s>arjuna</s> should be ground and thoroughly stirred with <s>kāñjika</s>.
In the midst of that, one should place <s>kānta</s> powder in a bronze vessel.

children.text: dinaikaṃ dhārayedgharme dravaiḥ pūryaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: It should be kept in the heat for one day, being filled again and again with liquids.
With liquids of <s>arjuna</s>, or with <s>sāranāla</s>, one should incinerate the threefold iron.
One should grind <s>kānta</s> powder with liquids obtained from <s>kukkuṭapatra</s>.

children.text: dinaṃ ca hyātape tīvre dravairmardyaṃ trikaṇṭajaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one day in intense sunlight it should be ground with liquids produced from <s>trikaṇṭaka</s>.
Again, for one day, with <s>vandhyā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s> together with cow urine.
One should decoct <s>triphalā</s> with cow urine and impregnate it with that decoction.
For three weeks, with care, one should then grind it for one day.
After sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; for a day one should grind it with the decoction.
It should be ground by day and put into a <s>puṭa</s> at night, up to twenty-one days.
By these twenty-one <s>puṭas</s>, the three kinds of iron are indeed incinerated.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ ca śilā hyamlairharidrā maricāṅghri ca
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> and <s>śilā</s>, with acids, turmeric, and the root of pepper,

children.text: piṣṭvā lepyaṃ kāntapatraṃ taptaṃ taptaṃ niṣecayet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground; one should smear a sheet of <s>kānta</s> iron, heat it repeatedly, and quench it.
Seven times in a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>; then one should wash it again with water.
One should pound it with an iron rod and grind it in <s>triphalā</s> water.
<s>Mākṣika</s> and <s>śilā</s> should be added in a sixteenth part of the iron.
After grinding them with an acid, one should seal them and cook them in a single <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: nirutthaṃ jāyate bhasma kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca muṇḍakam
children.translated_text: The ash of <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍaka</s> iron becomes <s>niruttha</s> (non-revivable).
After smearing a sword with the pulp of <s>tindū</s> fruit in fierce sunlight,
one should keep it inside a bronze vessel; in one day it cracks sufficiently.

children.text: lepaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kuryāddinānte taṃ prapeṣayet ||
children.translated_text: One should apply the paste again and again, and at the end of the day grind it thoroughly.
Combined with <s>triphalā</s> decoction, it becomes incinerated in one day.
With water reduced to one eighth, there should be five <s>palas</s> of <s>triphalā</s>.
The ghee should be equal to the decoction, and the incinerated iron equal to the ghee.
