One should cook it in a copper vessel, stirring it with an iron ladle.
One should cook it over a gentle fire until that liquid is absorbed.
Sugar equal to the iron should be added; when it is well cooked, one should remove it.
This incinerated iron is known as a <s>yogavāha</s> (catalytic carrier), a great nectar.

children.text: itthaṃ kāntasya tīkṣṇasya muṇḍasyāpi hyayaṃ vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus this is the procedure also for <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍa</s> iron.
One should cook incinerated iron equal to the ghee in an iron vessel.
When the ghee has been absorbed, one should take it and use it in all formulations.
<s>Oṃ</s>, <s>oṃ</s>. Homage: I consume, O <s>Amṛtendra</s>.

children.text: pātre yasminpraviśati jale tailabindurna sarpet hiṅgurgandhaṃ visṛjati nijāṃ tiktatāṃ nimbakalkaḥ
children.translated_text: In the vessel into which it is placed, an oil drop does not spread on water; asafoetida gives up its own smell, and neem paste its bitterness.

children.text: pāke dugdhaṃ bhavati śikharākāratā naiva bhūmau kāntaṃ lohaṃ tadidamuditaṃ lakṣaṇoktaṃ na cānyat ||
children.translated_text: In cooking, milk does not become peak-shaped on the ground: that alone is called <s>kānta</s> iron, as defined by its marks, and no other.
The cooking of iron is said to be threefold: soft, medium, and hard.
The first is like a heap of mud; the medium is a lump-cooking.
The third is a hard cooking, like sand, O dear one.

children.text: pākaṃ varṇaṃ tathā gandhaṃ jñātvā lohasya vahnitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having known the cooking, color, and smell of the iron from the fire,
one should remove it, and then place the purified material in another iron vessel.
<s>Loha-mātaṅga-pañcāsya</s>, sulfur, <s>mākṣika</s>, and cinnabar
all this incinerated iron should be smelted with the five friendly substances.
If in this way it becomes <s>niruttha</s>, floating on water, it is fit for use and beneficial.
Iron mixed with honey and ghee and combined with silver
should be smelted in a blind crucible; one should take it when it has cooled by itself.
If the silver within the iron remains in its former measure,
then the iron is <s>niruttha</s>; otherwise one should process it again.

children.text: gandhakaṃ cotthitaṃ lohaṃ tulyaṃ khalve vimardayet
children.translated_text: Sulfur and revived iron, in equal parts, should be rubbed in a mortar.
For one day with the juices of <s>kanyā</s>, then after sealing, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Thus, for all metals, <s>nirutthi</s> should be carried out in this manner.
<s>Kānta-sindūra</s> promotes longevity and gives health, strength, and virility.
It is excellent for making the body firm and produces acuity of the senses.
It pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s> and destroys the disease of royal consumption.
It destroys fever, blood-pitta, anemia, and the like, the eight great diseases.
When joined with whatever disease-destroying formulations, it becomes a destroyer of that particular disease.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ śastrāyasaṃ śastraṃ piṇḍaṃ piṇḍāyasaṃ śaṭham
children.translated_text: <s>Tīkṣṇa</s> iron is weapon-iron: weapon, lump, lump-iron, and <s>śaṭha</s>.

children.text: āyasaṃ niśitaṃ tīvraṃ lohakhaḍgaṃ ca muṇḍajam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āyasa</s>, sharp, intense, iron-sword, and that born of <s>muṇḍa</s> are names for it.
It is called variegated iron, and also Chinese-born, in three and five varieties.
<s>Muṇḍa</s>, <s>muṇḍāyasa</s>, iron, black iron, and rock-born iron are its names.
The incineration of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> and <s>muṇḍa</s> iron is by the method for <s>kānta</s> iron.
<s>Tīkṣṇa</s> iron is astringent and sour, bitter, pungent, and light.
It is cooling, scraping, and dry, and overcomes kapha, pitta, blood disorders, and anemia.
It destroys urinary disease and every kind of colic; <s>tīkṣṇa</s> surpasses <s>muṇḍa</s> in qualities.

children.text: cakṣuṣyaṃ muṇḍalohaṃ tu kaṣāyaṃ svādu tiktakam
children.translated_text: <s>Muṇḍa</s> iron is good for the eyes, astringent, sweet, and bitter.
It is scraping, removes wind, is cooling, and drives away worms, pitta, and kapha.
It conquers swelling, abdominal disease, colic, piles, skin disease, anemia, and urinary disease.
<s>Śrībhairava</s>:
Tin is said to be twofold: <s>khuraka</s> and <s>miśraka</s>.

children.text: khuraṃ tatra guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ guṇahīnaṃ tu miśrakam ||
children.translated_text: Of these, <s>khura</s> is best in qualities, while <s>miśraka</s> is deficient in qualities.
White, soft, smooth, quickly melting, and heavy:
that is <s>khuravaṅga</s>, silent when struck; <s>miśraka</s> is dark and whitish.

children.text: trapu trapusamārūpaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca kuṭilaṃ himam
children.translated_text: <s>Trapu</s>, similar to <s>trapu</s>, <s>vaṅga</s>, crooked, and cold,
<s>kurūpya</s>, <s>viccaṭa</s>, <s>raṅga</s>, foul-smelling, and called <s>rasa</s>: these are names for tin.
Clear, unable to bear heat, cool, making fine sheets, and light:
that tin is called the best for removing disease and for making silver.
After melting it, when it is joined with turmeric and cast into juices of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>,
<s>khuravaṅga</s> is purified in three repetitions, without doubt.
Ground with sour buttermilk, <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, and salt,
the two kinds of tin, placed inside a bitter gourd, are purified.
Then, after smearing tin leaves with orpiment and the milky sap of <s>arka</s>,
one should give light <s>puṭas</s> with the alkalis of <s>bodhiciñcā</s> bark.
After triturating it, one should use the ash; that has been taught in procedures involving mercury and the rest.
One should purify <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) just like <s>nāga</s> (lead), and likewise with <s>aśvattha</s> and tamarind materials.
One should triturate that ash and <s>haritāla</s> in equal quantity with an acidic liquid,
or else with liquids produced from <s>palāśa</s>; after stirring it, one should seal it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Having taken it out, one should triturate it together with <s>tāla</s> in a tenth part.
After mixing it with the earlier liquids, one should seal it and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
By twenty-one <s>puṭas</s>, <s>vaṅga</s> becomes killed and disease-removing.
With powders of <s>śirīṣa</s> and turmeric, a pellet joined with <s>kumārī</s>,
and a sheet of <s>vaṅga</s> smeared with <s>sūta</s> (mercury), the pellet should be triturated evenly.
When sealed and cooked with light <s>puṭas</s>, it becomes killed by the previously stated number.
Having ground the sheets with the waters of <s>akṣa</s> and <s>bhallātakī</s>, one should smear them.
Then one should place them in the midst of sesame chaff, seal them, and cook them with <s>puṭas</s>.
By forty <s>gajapuṭas</s>, the <s>vaṅga</s> becomes ash.
<s>Vaṅga</s> is sharp, hot, and pungent, and it slightly aggravates <s>vāta</s>.
It destroys disorders of fat and phlegm, destroys worms, and removes urinary disease.
It is cooling, astringent and salty, removes pallor and burning, and is flowing in action.

children.text: lekhanaṃ pittalaṃ kiṃcit trapu sīsaṃ ca tadguṇam
children.translated_text: It is scraping and somewhat productive of pitta; <s>trapu</s> and <s>sīsa</s> have those same qualities.

children.text: sīsakaṃ tu jaḍaṃ śītaṃ yavaneṣṭaṃ bhujaṅgamam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sīsaka</s> is dull and cold; it is desired by the <s>Yavanas</s>, and is called <s>bhujaṅgama</s>.
<s>Yogīṣṭa</s>, <s>nāga</s>, <s>uraga</s>, <s>kuvaṅga</s>, and <s>paripiṣṭaka</s> are its names.
It is soft, a black metal, and is remembered as a purifier of the eyelashes and the pupil.

children.text: sirāvṛttaṃ ca vaṅgaṃ syāccīnapiṣṭaṃ ca ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: It is also vein-marked, and called <s>vaṅga</s> and <s>cīnapiṣṭa</s>; there are sixteen such names.
<s>Sīsa</s> is equal to <s>vaṅga</s> in taste, potency, and post-digestive effect.
When insufficiently cooked, <s>nāga</s> and <s>vaṅga</s> cause skin disease, abdominal tumors, and pain.
They are remembered as producing urinary disease, pallor, fever, phlegm, vāta, and pitta.
What melts quickly, is very heavy, black when cut, and brightly shining,
with a foul smell and black on the outside, is pure <s>sīsa</s>; anything else is otherwise.
One should smear a sheet of <s>nāga</s> with powder of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> root together with the milk of <s>arka</s>.
Then, when it is dry, one should melt it and quench it.

children.text: liptvā drāvyaṃ punaḥ secyaṃ saptavāraṃ viśuddhaye
children.translated_text: After smearing it, it should again be melted and quenched seven times for purification.
Turmeric, <s>tumburu</s> seeds, <s>kokilākṣī</s>, and <s>kuberaka</s>,

children.text: gaurīphalaṃ mallikā ca mokṣo brahmā mayūrakam
children.translated_text: <s>gaurīphala</s>, <s>mallikā</s>, <s>mokṣa</s>, <s>brahmā</s>, and <s>mayūraka</s>:
according to availability, their ashes should be impregnated with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>.

children.text: tanmadhye drāvitaṃ nāgaṃ śuddhaṃ secyaṃ tu saptadhā
children.translated_text: Into that, molten <s>nāga</s>, after being purified, should be quenched seven times.
By means of buffalo bone powder, well cooked and quenched in urine,
<s>vaṅga</s> becomes pure; likewise <s>nāga</s>, from the bone and urine of a serpent.
Ash of <s>aśvattha</s> and tamarind bark should be added as one fourth part for <s>nāga</s>.
One should cook it in a furnace over fire, stirring it with an iron ladle,
until it becomes ash; having taken it out, one should add <s>manaḥśilā</s> equal to the ash.

children.text: jambīrair āranālair vā piṣṭvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: After grinding it with citron juice or <s>āranāla</s>, one should seal it and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
When it has cooled by itself, one should grind it again with acidic <s>śilā</s> in a twentieth part.

children.text: evaṃ ṣaṣṭipuṭaiḥ paktvā nāgaḥ syāttu nirutthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Cooked in this way with sixty <s>puṭas</s>, <s>nāga</s> becomes non-revivable.
Alternatively, sheets of <s>nāga</s>, smeared with powder, should be put in a potsherd.
One should cook them on a gentle fire for a <s>yāma</s>; that ash, with juices of <s>citraka</s>,
should be roasted in an iron vessel, stirred with a <s>pārtha</s> rod.
Up to sixteen <s>yāmas</s>, liquid should be supplied again and again.
One should pound the extracted material firmly with a rod, using <s>citraka</s> liquids.
After stirring it and sealing it, it is quickly killed by six <s>puṭas</s>.
With ashes produced from tamarind, <s>akṣa</s>, sugarcane, <s>bhallāta</s>, <s>vāśā</s>, and <s>vajralatā</s>,
and with those produced from <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, and <s>aśvattha</s>,
one should roast it thoroughly in an iron vessel with a <s>palāśa</s> rod.
In seven days alone it is killed; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: piṣṭvāgastyaṃ ca bhūnāgaṃ liptvā bhāṇḍaṃ viśodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having ground <s>agastya</s> and <s>bhūnāga</s>, one should smear the vessel and purify it.
In that vessel one should melt <s>nāga</s>; when the <s>nāga</s> is molten, one should add
the alkali of <s>vāśā</s> and tamarind, and rub it with <s>vāśā</s> wood.
One should cook it on the furnace for one <s>yāma</s>, take it out, and mix it.
Having pulverized it with <s>śilā</s> and <s>tāpya</s>, together with <s>vāśaka</s> alkali,
one should cook the preceding <s>nāga</s>, four times as much, with twenty-one <s>puṭas</s>.
Two <s>puṭas</s> should be given with tamarind alkalis accompanied by <s>vāśā</s> juice.
<s>Nāga</s>, resembling vermilion in color, is killed and becomes effective for every operation.
<s>Sīsaka</s> is very hot, unctuous, bitter, and removes vāta and kapha.
It destroys urinary and fluid disorders in <s>prameha</s>, kindles digestion, and diminishes <s>āmavāta</s>.
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s>:

children.text: rītiḥ kṣudrasuvarṇaṃ sitakanakaṃ piṅgalaṃ ca pittalakam
children.translated_text: <s>Rīti</s>, petty gold, white gold, <s>piṅgala</s>, and <s>pittalaka</s>,
<s>lohitaka</s>, <s>ārakūṭa</s>, <s>piṅgalaloha</s>, and <s>pītaka</s>: it is ninefold.
<s>Rītikā</s> and <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>: <s>pittala</s> is of two kinds.

children.text: saṃtaptā kāñjike kṣiptā tāmrābhā rītikā matā ||
children.translated_text: When heated and thrown into sour gruel, the copper-colored one is considered <s>rītikā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ yā jāyate kṛṣṇā kākatuṇḍīti sā matā
children.translated_text: The one that becomes black in this way is considered <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>.

children.text: gurvī mṛdvī ca pītākapotābhā sārāṅgī tāḍanakṣamā ||
children.translated_text: Heavy, soft, yellow, dove-hued, sound, and able to bear hammering,
very unctuous and smooth-bodied: such <s>rīti</s> is auspicious.

children.text: śuddhā snigdhā mṛduḥ śītā suraṅgā sūtrapattriṇī ||
children.translated_text: Pure, unctuous, soft, cool, well-colored, and capable of being drawn into wire and sheet,
gold-like and auspicious by nature: this is proclaimed as <s>rīti</s>.

children.text: pāṇḍuḥ pītā kharā rūkṣā barbarā ghaṭṭanākṣamā ||
children.translated_text: Pale, yellow, rough, dry, coarse, and unable to bear rubbing,
foul-smelling and also light: such <s>rīti</s> is not desired in mercury and related procedures.
<s>Rīti</s> has a bitter taste, is dry, kills parasites, and diminishes bloody pitta.
The black variety removes skin disease when used in formulations; it is hot in potency and cooling.
<s>Kākatuṇḍī</s>, when treated with oil, follows the qualities of royal <s>rīti</s>.
Royal <s>rīti</s> is said to be similar to <s>rītikā</s> in its qualities.
The pair of <s>rītikās</s> is dry, somewhat bitter, salty, and flowing.
It is beneficial, removes pallor and vāta, and increases strength, virility, and lifespan.
<s>Rītikā</s> is pungent, bitter, and hot, and removes spleen disease and abdominal distension.
It is dry, and, when administered with something sweet, it destroys kapha, blood-disorder, and pitta.
<s>Rājarīti</s>, <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>, <s>rājaputrī</s>, and <s>maheśvarī</s>,
<s>brāhmaṇī</s>, <s>brahmarīti</s>, and also <s>kapilā</s> and <s>piṅgalā</s> are its names.
<s>Kāṃsya</s> is called <s>saurāṣṭrika</s>, <s>ghoṣa</s>, <s>kaṃsīya</s>, and <s>vahnilohaka</s>,
also <s>dīptaloha</s>, <s>ghoṣayuṣya</s>, and <s>dīptaka</s>; it is known by nine names.
With eight parts of copper and two parts of <s>kuṭila</s>,
when melted, <s>kāṃsya</s> is produced; that which comes from <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> is auspicious.
With a sharp sound, soft, unctuous, slightly dark and whitish,

children.text: nirmalaṃ dāharaktaṃ ca ṣoḍhā kāṃsyaṃ praśasyate
children.translated_text: clear, and red when heated: <s>kāṃsya</s> with these six qualities is praised.
White and bright, soft in lustre, rich in sound, unctuous, and spotless,
compact, fire-resistant, and fibrous in body: this is declared to be the best <s>kāṃsya</s>.

children.text: tatpītaṃ dahane tāmraṃ ghanaṃ rūkṣaṃ ghanāsaham ||
children.translated_text: That <s>kāṃsya</s> which is yellow, becomes copper-colored in fire, is dense, dry, and cannot withstand blows,
has a dull sound and has lost its lustre should be rejected as sevenfold defective.
Everything except ghee that is placed in <s>kāṃsya</s> and eaten by people
gives health and happiness, is wholesome, and also makes the food suitable to them.
<s>Kāṃsya</s> is light, bitter, and hot; it scrapes and clarifies the sight.
It removes worms and intestinal disorders, pacifies vāta and pitta, and is wholesome in food.
<s>Vartaloha</s>, <s>vartatīkṣṇa</s>, <s>vartaka</s>, and <s>lohasaṃkara</s>,
<s>nīlikā</s>, <s>nīlaloha</s>, <s>lohaka</s>, and <s>vaṭṭalohaka</s> are its names.
That which is produced from <s>kāṃsya</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>rīti</s>, iron, and <s>ahi</s> is <s>vartaloha</s>.
That very thing is called <s>pañcaloha</s> by those who know metals.
Everything prepared in vessels made from it, preceded by other condiments,
and free from sour substances, is very kindling, digestive, and auspicious.
<s>Vartaloha</s>, when melted and thrown into horse urine, is purified.
<s>Vartaloha</s> is killed when incinerated with sulfur and <s>tāla</s>.
It should be applied according to rule in each of the respective sections.

children.text: vartalohaṃ kaṭūṣṇaṃ ca tiktaṃ ca śiśiraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Vartaloha</s> is pungent and hot, bitter and also cooling.
It conquers kapha, pacifies pitta, is sweet, and removes burning and urinary disease.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ rucyaṃ kṛmighnaṃ ca netryaṃ malaviśodhanam
children.translated_text: It is dry, appetizing, worm-destroying, beneficial to the eyes, and purifies the stools.
One should levigate the three alkalis and the five salts seven times with sour liquid.
With that paste one should smear sheets of <s>kāṃsya</s>, <s>āra</s>, and <s>ghoṣa</s>.
After sealing them, one should heat them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; purification comes about in no other way.
Having performed their killing as in the case of copper, one should apply them everywhere.
Metals that have been killed become nectar-like; when properly combined they destroy great diseases.
Through repeated practice they produce the attainment of a firm body and destroy disease, birth, and old age.

children.text: nāgena svarṇaṃ rajataṃ ca tāpyaiḥ gandhena tāmraṃ śilayā ca nāgam
children.translated_text: Gold is killed with lead, silver with <s>tāpya</s>, copper with sulfur, and lead with <s>śilā</s>.

children.text: tālena vaṅgaṃ trividhaṃ tu lohaṃ nārīpayo ghnanti ca hiṅgulena ||
children.translated_text: Tin is killed with <s>tāla</s>, the three kinds of iron with woman's milk, and with cinnabar too.

children.text: tathābhrasatvaṃ balinopalohaṃ vajreṇa sūtaṃ vinihanti sadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise the essence of mica, the strong subordinate metal, and mercury are killed at once with diamond.
I shall explain the true essence of diamond-mica; listen, O <s>Bhairavī</s>.
The essence of mica is fourfold: hard, soft, fluid,
and seed; each should be known as successively more endowed with qualities.
<s>Dhānyābhraka</s> should be placed in <s>ravi</s>-latex in the heat for the length of a day.
One should grind that smooth on a slab and enclose it in a covered dish.
One should cook it properly in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, and cook it again in <s>ravi</s>-latex.

children.text: mardanaṃ puṭapākaṃ ca kuryādevaṃ tu saptadhā
children.translated_text: Pounding and cooking in a sealed crucible should be done in this way seven times.

children.text: tathā jambīranīre ca niculasya rase tathā ||
children.translated_text: So too in lemon juice and in the juice of <s>nicula</s>.
This is the best prepared dense mica, free from lustre, for extracting the essence.
With the substances that kill dense mica, either separately or all together,

children.text: piṣṭvā dhānyābhrakaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet
children.translated_text: one should grind <s>dhānyābhraka</s> smooth, seal it, and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
<s>Lākṣā</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, burnt wool, <s>sarja</s>, <s>sarjarasa</s>, salt,
hare bone, small fish, turmeric, and <s>mitrapañcaka</s>,

children.text: pañcamāhiṣakaṃ cāpi bhallātaṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: also <s>pañcamāhiṣaka</s> and <s>bhallāta</s>, each in equal amount,
and prepared dense mica equal to all of them should be ground for a day until free from lustre.
From all that, pills should be made, each measuring a <s>karṣa</s>.
In a furnace apparatus one should blow strongly with charcoal produced from <s>khadira</s>.
After just three <s>yāmas</s> of blowing, a pure essence falls.
It is hard, finely granular, and free from glass and borax.
One should do this three times with the slag in order to extract the essence.
Again I shall explain another, the soft essence, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
<s>Guggulu</s>, borax, <s>guñjā</s>, <s>sarja</s>, <s>sarjarasa</s>, and molasses,
small fish, barley-alkali, glass, oilcake, and <s>sūraṇa</s>,
<s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>vahni</s>, <s>kṣīrakanda</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>dhuttūra</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, mercury, <s>balā</s>, and <s>gandhakasevaka</s>,

children.text: gokṣīraṃ pañcalavaṇaṃ sarvaṃ ca dviguṇaṃ madhu ||
children.translated_text: cow's milk, the five salts, all of this, and honey in double quantity,
<s>ṣaḍbindu</s>, small shellfish, and the bones of a hare,
pigeon dung, <s>tryūṣa</s>, <s>indragopa</s>, together with <s>śigru</s>,
wheat, mustard, and <s>tāpya</s> should be triturated with goat's milk.

children.text: evaṃ vyastaṃ samastaṃ vā yāmamātreṇa marditam ||
children.translated_text: In this way, separately or all together, it is to be triturated for a single <s>yāma</s>.

children.text: asya piṇḍasya bhāgaikaṃ dvibhāgaṃ siddham abhrakam
children.translated_text: One part of this lump and two parts of prepared mica
together with one part of <s>pañcamāhiṣa</s> should all be stirred together in one place.
Pills weighing a <s>karṣa</s> should be made and dried a little in the shade.
One should keep throwing it into a <s>koṣṭhīyantra</s> (furnace apparatus) heated with <s>khadira</s> charcoal.
For five sets of five <s>ghuṭīs</s>, one should blow strongly through the bent tube.
A soft, bright-white <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) arises, destroying disease, old age, and death.
One should do this three times; its slag is made to yield <s>sattva</s>.
By the application of this procedure, <s>kānta</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s>,
as well as the hard secondary minerals and other purified substances, together with earth of <s>bhūnāga</s>,
release a collected molten essence and each separately takes on this form.
Taking <s>abhrasattva</s> (mica essence), along with equal parts of glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),
one should add them again and again three times and blow it in a diamond-hard crucible.
One should grind the sour group, <s>snuhī</s> leaves, and <s>bimbī</s> seeds together with the bark,
and into that mixture one should quench the heated material seven times.
Its product becomes soft and bright white, destroying disease, old age, and death.
There should be ten parts of prepared <s>abhraka</s> and three parts of the purified substance.

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ mākṣikaṃ sūtaṃ bhāgaikaṃ ca suśodhitam
children.translated_text: Purified <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and <s>sūta</s> (mercury) should each be one part,
and one part each of <s>ūrṇā</s>, <s>sarja</s>-alkali, and barley-alkali should be mixed in.
It is to be triturated for a day with urine and the sour group, as has been prescribed,
and, combined with the fivefold product of a goat, the extraction of <s>sattva</s> is performed as before.
Having done this and taken up the incinerated material, it becomes manifestly stainless and soft.
I shall explain the cooking of the seed; this is supremely beneficial for <s>ghana</s> (mica).
There should be one hundred <s>palas</s> of prepared <s>abhraka</s>, together with gold, silver, copper, and <s>kānta</s>,
as well as <s>rasa</s>, the three aromatics, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vimalā</s>, <s>bhūlatā</s>, and mountain-born mineral,

children.text: nīlāñjanaṃ ca kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ kāsīsaṃ daradaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: blue collyrium, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and <s>darada</s> too;
each should measure ten <s>niṣkas</s>; then come red ochre and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.

children.text: indragopaṃ guḍaṃ guñjā madhu sarpiśca gugguluḥ
children.translated_text: There should be <s>indragopa</s>, jaggery, <s>guñjā</s>, honey, ghee, and <s>guggulu</s>,
<s>sarja</s>-alkali, barley-alkali, and <s>matkuṇa</s> bugs, five and nine in number,
small fish, hare bones, buffalo horn, and a garland-like horn substance.
One should triturate them separately with the five roots and the five buffalo products.
Pellets are to be made from them and dried a little in the shade.
One should extract the <s>sattva</s> as before; it removes disease, old age, poverty, and death.
This seed-<s>sattva</s> is best in medical treatment, alchemical transmutation, and <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation).
I shall explain the clarification of <s>ghana-sattva</s> (mica essence), O <s>Pārvati</s>.
One should break that <s>sattva</s> into particles and combine it with the five friendly substances.
After placing it in a crucible, one should put glass below it and above it.
Having sealed it, one should blow it over a forced fire with the use of <s>khadira</s> charcoal.
In this sequence one should blow it seven times; it becomes stainless.
The purified <s>sattva</s>-bearing material should be powdered in an iron mortar.
One should triturate it with decoctions of <s>triphalā</s> for a <s>yāma</s> and dry it in the sun.

children.text: pākaṃ puṭaṃ ca vidhivatkuryādevaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Cooking and <s>puṭa</s> firing should be performed according to rule, again and again.
In this way one should perform forty <s>puṭas</s> with the liquids of <s>mārkavajra</s>.
With each of the five nectars one should give five <s>puṭas</s>, and with sugarcane juice three times.
The <s>ghana-sattva</s>, resembling the rising sun, bestows excellent accomplishment.
One should powder purified <s>abhraka</s> in an iron mortar.

children.text: niṣkāṇāṃ śatakaṃ tasmin niṣkaikaṃ gandhakaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: When there are one hundred <s>niṣkas</s> of it, one should add one <s>niṣka</s> of sulfur to it.
One should grind it for one day with the juice of <s>kumārī</s>.

children.text: yāmaṃ tattāpayed gharme tato gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: It should be heated in the sun for a <s>yāma</s>, and then cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
In this way one should perform one hundred <s>puṭas</s>, adding sulfur again and again.
The <s>abhrasattva</s> becomes the color of red vermilion, O <s>Śive</s>.
One should powder the very stainless <s>ghana-sattva</s> in an iron mortar.
When there are one hundred <s>niṣkas</s> of it, one should add a half <s>niṣka</s> of <s>mākṣika</s> to it.
Having triturated it for a day with the latex of <s>arka</s>, one should seal it and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ śatapuṭaṃ kuryānmākṣīkaṃ ca puṭe puṭe ||
children.translated_text: In this way one should perform one hundred <s>puṭas</s>, adding <s>mākṣika</s> at every <s>puṭa</s>.
This becomes <s>sattva-sindūra</s>, destroying disease, old age, and death.
A wise person, after removing the granules from that <s>sattva</s>,
should triturate it with an iron pestle, together with a decoction of <s>varā</s>.
For one <s>yāma</s> he should place it in an iron vessel in fierce sunlight.

children.text: sthālīpākaṃ kharaṃ kṛtvā rātrau gajapuṭe pacet
children.translated_text: After performing a strong pot-cooking, he should cook it at night in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
In this way he should perform seven <s>puṭas</s>, likewise with the fresh juices of <s>mārkava</s>.
Likewise with the fresh juices of <s>kumārī</s>, and likewise with juices of <s>citramūla</s>,
likewise with juices of <s>nīlī</s> leaves, and likewise with the juices of <s>punarnavā</s>.
He should give seven with the liquids of <s>meghanāda</s>, and with decoctions produced from banyan aerial roots.

children.text: evaṃ susūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu śatāṃśaṃ gandhakaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: When it is thus a very fine powder, one should add sulfur in a hundredth part.
One should triturate it with <s>āranāla</s> and cook it in a pot with <s>puṭa</s> heat in the sun.
One should do this for ten days; then it should again be heated with a hundredth part.

children.text: kṣiptvāranālaiḥ saṃmardya gharme sthālyāṃ puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: After adding <s>āranāla</s> and triturating it well, one should cook it in a pot with <s>puṭa</s> heat in the sun.
One should do this for ten days; then it should again be cooked with the five nectars.
With five sets of sugarcane juices one should perform the <s>puṭa</s> operation five times.
When the calcined <s>abhraka</s> has the appearance of vermilion, one should put in purified <s>hiṅgula</s>.
Then, as a twentieth part of the <s>ghana</s>, it should be triturated with breast milk in a covered vessel.

children.text: ruddhvātha bhūdhare yantre kṣiptvā laghupuṭaṃ vidhet ||
children.translated_text: Having sealed it and placed it in a <s>bhūdhara-yantra</s>, one should apply a light <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ viṃśatpuṭaṃ kuryād dattvā dattvātha hiṅgulam
children.translated_text: In this way one should perform twenty <s>puṭas</s>, adding <s>hiṅgula</s> again and again.
By the application of this ordered procedure, the <s>sattva</s> becomes like vermilion.
This is the general processing; the special processing is now stated.
With whatever substances remove particular diseases, it becomes a remover of those diseases.
One should powder very stainless <s>ghana-sattva</s> in an iron mortar.
It should be triturated for a day with the juice of <s>muṇḍī</s> leaves and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Thus ten <s>puṭas</s> should be performed, likewise with the fresh juices of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>,
and similarly with decoctions of banyan aerial roots and with juices produced from the root of <s>peṭārī</s>.
In the same way, with the juices of <s>kakubha</s>, and also with the fresh juice of <s>jambū</s> bark,
thus sixty <s>puṭas</s> should be performed. After that, one should put into it
<s>darada</s>, in a twentieth part, and rub it for a day with breast milk.

children.text: tatastatsampuṭe ruddhvā bhūdhare tu puṭaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: Then, having sealed that in a covered vessel, one should give it a light <s>puṭa</s> in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace.
One should do this twenty times; it will certainly become vermilion-colored.
<s>Sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooking) is declared to be threefold: soft, medium, and hard in nature.
The first is like a heap of mud; the medium is a lump-cooking.
The third is hard cooking, like sand, O dear one.

children.text: sthālīpāko rase yuktaḥ saṃyukto daradena vā
children.translated_text: <s>Sthālīpāka</s> is joined with mercury, or else combined with <s>darada</s>.
It should then be done in the <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace by the soft and medium cookings.
After placing it there, a light <s>puṭa</s> should be given, excluding mercury and cinnabar.
Hard cooking should be performed; the procedure is to cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
For all incinerated metals, and also for mica,
I shall explain the supreme secret, the process of making them nectar-like; listen.
One should take sixteen parts of the decoction produced from <s>triphalā</s>,
eight <s>palas</s> of cow's ghee, and ten <s>palas</s> of incinerated mica.
Having combined them in an iron vessel, one should cook them with a gentle fire.
When the liquid has been absorbed, one should take it and employ it in all formulations.
Even without an <s>anupāna</s> (vehicle), mica removes old age, death, and disease.
Or, when used with <s>anupānas</s>, it becomes a remover of the corresponding diseases.
The <s>sindūra</s> of hard mica-essence removes gray hair and wrinkles,
brings acuity of the senses, and also has the qualities of leaf-mica.
The <s>sindūra</s> of soft essence destroys all diseases.
It destroys wrinkles, gray hair, poverty, and death; it is a divine <s>rasāyana</s>.
It pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s>, is gentle, stimulates digestion, cooks what is eaten, and is auspicious.
It destroys the whole mass of fevers, as well as <s>grahaṇī</s> and diarrhea.
It destroys stone, difficult urination, wasting disease, anemia, and <s>halīmaka</s>,
as well as bad piles, urinary disorders, skin diseases, and diseases born of wind and of bile.
It also destroys hard-to-cure diseases born of phlegm, abscesses and other wounds,
many kinds of colic, and it breaks infertility in men and women.
With whatever disease-removing formulations it is joined, it removes that particular disease.

children.text: pārade ye guṇāḥ santi bījasatve'pi te guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The qualities that exist in mercury also exist in seed-essence.
One should heat iron slag with <s>akṣa</s> charcoal and sprinkle it with cow urine,
inside an <s>akṣa</s> vessel, six times, again and again.
This is called <s>maṇḍūra</s>; once purified and finely ground, it should be applied.
<s>Triphalā</s> should be decocted in cow urine, and with that decoction one should sprinkle slowly
the well-heated iron slag, until it crumbles apart by itself.
One should collect that crumbled material, grind it, and use it as <s>maṇḍūra</s>.

children.text: ye guṇā mārite muṇḍe te guṇā muṇḍakiṭṭake
children.translated_text: The qualities that are in incinerated <s>muṇḍa</s> iron are also in the slag of <s>muṇḍa</s> iron.
Therefore <s>maṇḍūra</s> should be used everywhere for the pacification of disease.
<s>Muṇḍa</s> iron is ten times stronger than slag; <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron is a hundred times stronger than <s>muṇḍa</s>.
<s>Kānta</s> iron, through ingestion, produces qualities a hundred thousand times greater than <s>tīkṣṇa</s>.
<s>Maṇḍūra</s> removes anemia, wasting, piles, <s>grahaṇī</s>, and jaundice.
It destroys all colic and urinary disease, stimulates digestion, and is supremely beneficial.
It is cooling, bitter, astringent, and sour, and destroys heart disease and splenic disease.
One may purify <s>rasendra</s> (mercury), O <s>Devī</s>, in the amount of two thousand <s>palas</s>,

children.text: sahasraṃ vā śataṃ vāpi pañcāśadvā tadardhakam
children.translated_text: or a thousand, or a hundred, or fifty, or half of that.
One should not perform mercury operations with less than twenty-five <s>palas</s>.
One should not have the cooking of iron performed beyond thirty <s>palas</s>.
Below five <s>palas</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, one should likewise cook mica-essence.
Gold should not be purified above five <s>palas</s>, nor below one <s>pala</s>.

children.text: tathā rūpyaṃ ca tāmraṃ ca śodhayenmārayet priye ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, O dear one, one should purify and incinerate silver and copper.
Mica-essence, like iron, and mica sheets in the same way,
one should not work below five <s>palas</s> or above twenty <s>palas</s>.
The melting, purification, O <s>Devī</s>, and incineration of lead and tin
and of diamond should not be performed, for purification or incineration, below or above a <s>niṣka</s>.
Padmarāga and the other jewels, O queen of gods, should be treated in the same way.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:
In the great ocean, in a river, on a mountain, or even in a forest,
there is a source of gems, O <s>Devī</s>, because of the excellence of the place and substratum.
Among them, gems arise that remove demons, poison, snakes, diseases, and faults,
and likewise gems that are defective.
Those born in a corrupted state, and those damaged by living creatures,
increase in defects and are diminished in the abundance of their qualities.
<s>Māṇikya</s>, red jewel, king of jewels, sun-jewel,
<s>śṛṅgāri</s>, <s>raṅgamāṇikya</s>, <s>tarala</s>, and lord of jewels;
<s>rāgadṛk</s>, <s>padmarāga</s>, jewel, and red stone,
<s>saugandhika</s>, <s>lohitaka</s>, <s>kuruvinda</s>, and <s>śarenduka</s> are names for it.
A <s>māṇikya</s> called <s>padmarāga</s>, and a second kind, <s>nīlagandhi</s>,
has the color of a lotus petal, is clear, glossy, heavy, and transparent.

children.text: vṛttāyataṃ samaṃ gātraṃ māṇikyaṃ śreṣṭham ucyate
children.translated_text: Round or elongated, with an even body: such a <s>māṇikya</s> is called the best.
For kings, gems that have been purified by examination
should always be worn by one who desires welfare, prosperity, and fame.
Therefore their examination and related procedures are now stated according to the <s>śāstra</s>.
That which is found in <s>Siṃhala</s>, <s>Kālapura</s>, <s>Andhra</s>, and located in <s>Tumburu</s>...
The field or source for the production of that <s>māṇikya</s> is fourfold.
In <s>Siṃhala</s> it becomes red, the unsurpassed <s>padmarāga</s>.
The yellow one, born in <s>Kālapura</s>, is remembered as <s>kuruvinda</s>.
The <s>Andhra</s> stone has the hue of an <s>aśoka</s> sprout and is called fragrant, my dear.
In <s>Tumbura</s> it is of a deep blue hue and is called blue-fragrant.
The middling <s>māṇikya</s> should be known as middling according to difference of source.
Four qualities of ruby have been taught by the foremost sages.
They are glossy luster, heaviness, purity, and very deep redness.
Ruby kindles digestion, is aphrodisiac, and removes consumption, pain, and disorders of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
It destroys spirits, <s>vetālas</s>, and sin, and removes diseases born of karma.
Ruby is greatly meritorious and supremely productive of great fortune.
It destroys all spirits, seizures, madness, and poison, and is supreme in conquering doṣas.

children.text: muktā saumyā mauktikaṃ śauktikeyaṃ tāraṃ tārā śauktikaṃ tārakā ca
children.translated_text: <s>Muktā</s>, <s>saumyā</s>, <s>mauktika</s>, <s>śauktikeya</s>, <s>tāra</s>, <s>tārā</s>, <s>śauktika</s>, and <s>tārakā</s> are names of pearl.

children.text: ambhaḥsāraṃ śītalaṃ nīrajaṃ ca nakṣatraṃ syād induratnaṃ valakṣam ||
children.translated_text: It is also called essence of water, cooling, water-born, star, moon-gem, and white.

children.text: muktāphalaṃ binduphalaṃ ca muktā śaukteyakaṃ śuktimaṇiḥ śaśipriyam
children.translated_text: <s>Muktāphala</s>, <s>binduphala</s>, <s>muktā</s>, <s>śaukteyaka</s>, oyster-gem, and beloved of the moon are names of pearl.

children.text: svacchaṃ himaṃ haimavataṃ ca śubhraṃ sudhāṃśuratnaṃ ca bhasaṃkhyakāhvam ||
children.translated_text: It is called clear, snowy, Himalayan, bright, moonstone, and by the name <s>bhasaṃkhyaka</s>.
The pearl-gem is clearly eightfold, arising from the heads of elephants, snakes, fish, and boars, and from bamboo, conch, cloud, and the belly of oysters.

children.text: chāyāḥ pāṭalanīlapītadhavalāstatrāpi sāmānyataḥ saptānāṃ bahuśo na labdhir itaracchaukteyakaṃ tūlvaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Their hues are generally rose, blue, yellow, and white; yet the seven kinds are often unobtainable, while the other, oyster-born kind, is common.

children.text: nakṣatrābhaṃ śuddhamatyantamuktaṃ snigdhaṃ sthūlaṃ nirmalaṃ nirvraṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: A pearl that shines like a star, is perfectly pure, glossy, large, spotless, and without wound,

children.text: yastaṃ dhatte gauravaṃ yattulāyāṃ tannirmaulyaṃ mauktikaṃ saukhyadāyi ||
children.translated_text: and that has weight when one holds it on the balance, is a priceless pearl that gives happiness.

children.text: mauktikaṃ ca madhuraṃ suśītalaṃ dṛṣṭirogaśamanaṃ viṣāpaham
children.translated_text: Pearl is sweet and very cooling; it pacifies eye disease and removes poison.
It destroys the anger of kings and yakṣas and increases nourishment, strength, and diminished virility.
Pearl is cold, unctuous, clear, and increases beauty.
It removes burning, thirst, dizziness, fainting, blood, bile, fever, and poison.

children.text: cakṣuṣyaṃ pavanāsrapittaviṣajit sarvendriyāhlādanaṃ tṛḍdāhajvaraśokamohaśamanaṃ śītaṃ śramaghnaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: It benefits the eyes, conquers <s>vāta</s>, blood, <s>pitta</s>, and poison, delights all the senses, pacifies thirst, burning, fever, grief, and delusion, is cooling, removes fatigue, and is wholesome.

children.text: dhanyaṃ maṅgalamāyuṣaḥ sthitikaraṃ saubhāgyakāntipradaṃ muktā hāravibhūṣaṇaṃ tad akhilaṃ mūlaṃ śaśī prīyate ||
children.translated_text: It is blessed, auspicious, sustains life, grants fortune and beauty; pearl is the ornament of necklaces, and the moon is pleased by all this as its root.
<s>Pravāla</s>, gem of <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, <s>vidruma</s>, and sprout of the ocean are names of coral.
It is also Mars's gem, red-bodied, and the gem of the red sprout-creeper.

children.text: setau sāgaramadhye yā jāyate vallarī śubhā ||
children.translated_text: The fine creeper that arises at the bridge, in the middle of the ocean,
is called <s>vidruma</s>; it is very red, difficult to obtain, and radiant in form.
When it is hard, it takes on the state of stone through ripening.
That red substance, named coral, bestows beauty of color and radiance.

children.text: siddhaṃ svacchaṃ snigdharūpaṃ vṛttaṃ kāntaṃ samaṃ guru ||
children.translated_text: Perfect coral is clear, glossy in form, round, lovely, even, and heavy.
Coral that has a colored body, is firm, and is compact is called the best.
Coral that resembles a ripe <s>biṃba</s> fruit and is like a hibiscus flower
and has the hue of a parrot's beak is exceedingly beautiful.

children.text: śāradābhaṃ dalaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vakraṃ rūkṣaṃ sakoṭaram ||
children.translated_text: Coral that is autumn-colored, split, thin, crooked, rough, and hollow

children.text: viddhaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ laghutamaṃ pravālaṃ doṣakṛd bhavet
children.translated_text: or pierced, black, and very light becomes productive of faults.
One should reject inauspicious coral that is pale in color and invaded by water.

children.text: pravālaṃ komalaṃ snigdhaṃ surāgaṃ vidrumaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: Coral that is soft, glossy, richly red, and called <s>vidruma</s> is beneficial.
It produces wealth and grain, promotes intelligence, and destroys fear of poison and snakes.
Coral is sweet and sour, and removes disorders beginning with <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
When worn by women, it produces virility and beauty and grants auspiciousness.
<s>Marakata</s>, <s>rauhiṇeya</s>, <s>gārutmanta</s>, and <s>harinmaṇi</s> are names of emerald.
It is also called <s>sauparṇa</s>, vomited by <s>Garuḍa</s>, Mercury's gem, and born from stone.
It is the enemy of poison, possessed of wind-power, <s>gāruḍa</s>, and comparable to <s>Rudra</s>.
In the ocean of the <s>Turuṣka</s> land, on Mount <s>Samīrārohaṇa</s>,
the region darkened with its hue became a mine of emerald.
From that special condition emerald arose, endowed with faults and qualities.
Its faults are said to be sevenfold and its qualities fivefold.
The hue of the emerald gem is eightfold.
What is unglossy is called rough; likewise blistered and pustular,

children.text: jaṭharaṃ kāntihīnaṃ ca vicchāyaṃ malinaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: dull, without brilliance, colorless, and dirty,
gritty, stony, harsh, and threaded,
or mottled and variegated in color: all these are said to bring every kind of fear.

children.text: nirmalaṃ kathitaṃ svacchaṃ guru syād gurudāyutam
children.translated_text: Spotless is called clear; heavy is joined with weight.
Glossy means free from roughness; dustless means without particles.
Deeply colored means rich in color: these are remembered as the five qualities.
An emerald endowed with these qualities is supreme, removing all sin.

children.text: marakataṃ viṣaghnaṃ ca śītalaṃ madhuraṃ rase
children.translated_text: Emerald destroys poison, is cooling, and is sweet in taste.
It removes indigestion and bile, is appetizing, gives nourishment, and destroys spirits.
A glossy, clear emerald is auspicious and removes every doṣa.
It grants beauty and fortune, promotes intelligence, and removes spirits, seizures, and poison.

children.text: pītastu puṣparāgaḥ pītasphuṭikaṃ ca pītaratnaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The yellow stone is <s>puṣparāga</s>, yellow crystal, and yellow jewel.
It is yellow stone, Jupiter's gem, yellow gem, and <s>puṣyarāga</s>.

children.text: īṣat pītaṃ pavicchāyaṃ svacchaṃ kāntyā manoharam
children.translated_text: The gem that is slightly yellow, with the hue of a thunderbolt, clear, and charming in brilliance
is known among gem examiners as <s>puṣyarāga</s>.
A <s>puṣyarāga</s> gem with a golden luster, rounded at the top, and clear like glowing light or embers,
yellow-bodied, heavy, and smooth, is praised as excellent <s>puṣyarāga</s>.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ kṣatalaghu śvetaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ gauraṃ saśarkaram
children.translated_text: A rough, damaged, light, white, black, pale, gritty,
dirty, spotted jewel is not approved as <s>puṣyarāga</s>.
<s>Puṣyarāga</s> is sour and cooling, conquers <s>vāta</s>, and is an excellent kindler of digestion.

children.text: āyuḥ śriyaṃ ca prajñāṃ ca dhāraṇātkurute nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: When worn, it produces long life, prosperity, and wisdom for people.
A good <s>puṣyarāga</s> is auspicious and intellect-promoting; it grants wealth, good fortune, and fame.
It produces eloquence, is pleasing to the heart, destroys poison, and supremely conquers the bodily faults.
<s>Vajra</s> is called the weapon of <s>Indra</s>, heroic, splitter, <s>kuliśa</s>, and <s>pavi</s>;

children.text: abhedyam asiraṃ ratnaṃ dṛḍhaṃ bhārgavakaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: it is remembered as unbreakable, hard as a sword, a jewel, firm, and <s>bhārgavaka</s>.

children.text: svacchaṃ vidyutprabhaṃ snigdhaṃ sundaraṃ laghu lekhanam
children.translated_text: Clear, lightning-bright, smooth, beautiful, light, and capable of scratching,

children.text: ṣaḍāraṃ tīkṣṇadhāraṃ ca susaumyāraṃ śriyaṃ diśet ||
children.translated_text: six-cornered and sharp-edged, with well-formed points, it should bestow prosperity.
<s>Pauṇḍra</s>, <s>Mataṅga</s>, <s>Himācala</s>, <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>, <s>Supāraka</s>, <s>Kosala</s>, and <s>Kaliṅga</s>,
together with the bank of the <s>Peṇṇā</s> river, are specified as the eight diamond deposits.
A diamond from <s>Pauṇḍra</s> is dark; one born on <s>Mataṅga</s> mountain is somewhat yellow.
One arising from <s>Himavat</s> or <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> is reddish, while that from <s>Supāraka</s> has a black sheen.
One from <s>Kosala</s> has the hue of a blossoming <s>śirīṣa</s> flower, and the <s>Kaliṅga</s> diamond has a golden luster.
A diamond born on the bank of the <s>Peṇṇā</s> river is said to resemble the moon.
The countries <s>Kaliṅga</s> and <s>Kosala</s>, <s>Mataṅga</s> mountain and the <s>Himālaya</s>,
and likewise <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>, <s>Pauṇḍra</s>, the <s>Kauvera</s> mine, and <s>Supāraka</s>,
are remembered, in the ages beginning with the <s>Kṛta</s>, as the deposits of diamonds.
In those very deposits, the source of diamonds is declared to be mine, stream, or scattered find.
The place of origin is thus set forth in three ways, O divine lady.

children.text: koṭyaḥ pārśvāni dhārāśca ṣaḍaṣṭau dvādaśaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Its points, sides, and edges are six, eight, and twelve respectively.
These clear, sharp-edged points are then said to be the qualities of diamond.

children.text: malo binduśca rekhā ca trāsaḥ kākapadaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Impurity, spot, line, fracture, and crow's-foot mark

children.text: ete doṣāḥ samākhyātāḥ pañca vajreṣu saṃsthitāḥ
children.translated_text: are proclaimed to be the five defects found in diamonds.
An unpurified diamond causes skin disease, burning, and heaviness of the limbs,
pain in the heart and sides, and pallor; therefore its purification is now taught.
After taking a white diamond, one should place it inside a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber.
One should coat it with buffalo dung and cook it in a dung fire.
After a day and night, one should take it out and sprinkle it with horse urine.
Cooked again and again in this way, it is purified after seven nights.
With substances produced from <s>meghanāda</s>, <s>āśamī</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, and <s>madanaka</s>,
and with <s>kuluttha</s>, <s>vetasa</s>, <s>agastya</s>, <s>sindhuvāra</s>, and <s>ākhukarṇikā</s>,
a decoction of these is again to be prepared with horse urine.
Having placed the <s>kuliśa</s> in a citron, one should cook it for three days with horse urine
by the procedure of the <s>ḍolāyantra</s>; then it obtains purification.
One should cook it in a <s>ḍolāyantra</s> with decoctions of <s>kuluttha</s> and <s>kodrava</s>.
A diamond placed inside a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber obtains purification after a week.
Decoction of <s>kulattha</s> and <s>kodrava</s>, horse urine, and the latex of <s>snuhī</s>
should be put into a vessel, and in that one should cook the <s>pavi</s> placed inside a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber.
After cooking it day and night in a <s>ḍolāyantra</s>, one should take it out and again put it

children.text: vajrakande mṛdā kandaṃ liptvā gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: in a <s>vajra</s> tuber; having smeared the tuber with clay, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
When thus cooked and sprinkled with digestive liquids, it obtains purification.

children.text: vyāghrīkandagataṃ vajraṃ mṛdā liptaṃ puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: A diamond placed in a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber, smeared with clay, should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>.
After a day and night, one should take it out and sprinkle it with horse urine,

children.text: vajrīkṣīreṇa vā siñcyādevaṃ śuddhaṃ tu mārayet ||
children.translated_text: or sprinkle it with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>; once purified in this way, it should then be calcined.
The calcination of purified diamond of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> type and the others will be described.
<s>Aśvattha</s>, <s>badarī</s>, <s>bhaṇḍī</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and crab bone
should be ground in equal parts with <s>snuhī</s> latex and smeared inside a crucible.
In the middle of it one should place the diamond, and then further cover it with those medicines.
Having carefully covered the diamond, one should then seal the crucible.
One should fire it with the great <s>puṭa</s> called <s>kuñjara</s>.
A diamond of the <s>vipra</s> class is perfected with a single <s>puṭa</s>.
<s>Karavīra</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>darada</s>, and <s>udumbara</s>

children.text: arkadugdhaiḥ samaṃ piṣṭvā tatkṛte golake kṣipet
children.translated_text: should be ground equally with the latex of <s>arka</s>; the diamond is to be placed in a pellet made from that.
A diamond of the <s>kṣatriya</s> class should certainly be calcined as before.
One should grind <s>sūraṇa</s>, garlic, conch shell, and <s>śilā</s> equally on a stone,
and grind <s>balā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, sulfur, and turtle bone.
With the milk of <s>uttarāvāruṇī</s>, the diamond is to be placed in a pellet made from that.
A diamond of the <s>vaiśya</s> class then becomes calcined as before.
One should grind together equal parts of <s>sūraṇa</s>, garlic, conch shell, and <s>śilā</s>.
With banyan latex, in a pellet made from that, one should cook it as before.
That diamond of the <s>śūdra</s> class thereby becomes properly calcined.
Female and male diamonds are calcined by the medicines previously stated for each of them.
In a neuter diamond, calcination is achieved only by the medicines of the four classes.
The general procedure for calcining all diamonds will now be described.
Having smeared purified diamond with the blood of bedbugs, one should heat it again.
When it is the color of fire, one should put it repeatedly into donkey urine.
Smeared and heated in the same way, this should be done twenty-one times.

children.text: tālakaṃ matkuṇaiḥ piṣṭvā tasmingole kṣipettu tam ||
children.translated_text: Having ground <s>tālaka</s> with bedbugs, one should put that diamond into the pellet.
After sealing the crucible, one should heat it intensely and plunge it into horse urine.
Having taken it out, one should repeat the same procedure; after seven times it becomes calcined.
Ram's horn, snake bone, tortoise shell, and <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch),
sulfur, magnet-stone, <s>munipuṣpa</s>, and <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment);
the three alkalis, the five salts, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s> and <s>indravāruṇī</s>,
<s>vajravallī</s>, <s>mūṣakarṇī</s>, and buds of <s>badarī</s>;
mouse dung, breast milk, the latexes of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, and bedbugs,
the whole five-part plant of <s>śarapuṅkhā</s>, and the bones of donkey and ram;
<s>peṭārī</s> seed, <s>strīpuṣpa</s> (menstrual fluid), pigeon dung, and stone,

children.text: puṣpāṇi caiva vākucyāḥ pañcāṅgaṃ timirasya ca ||
children.translated_text: also the flowers of <s>vākucī</s> and the whole five-part plant of <s>timira</s>;
the whole five-part plant of the <s>dhātrī</s> tree, <s>gorambhā</s>, and horse urine,
<s>haṃsapādī</s>, <s>vajrakanda</s>, fruit of <s>bṛhatī</s>, and <s>sūraṇa</s>;

children.text: gojihvā karkaṭaṃ māṃsaṃ mūtravargaṃ ca miśrayet
children.translated_text: <s>gojihvā</s>, crab flesh, and the group of urines should be mixed.
All these, together or separately, according to availability, should be made into a well-formed lump.
In that lump one should place the diamond, put it in a blind crucible, and heat it by <s>puṭa</s>.
One should grind horse gram and <s>kodrava</s> grain and stir them in horse urine.
Into that one should pour the hot crucible when it has come out from the crucible-heating.
Thus one should do it again and again twenty-one times.
Then, taking that diamond again, in <s>tālaka</s> ground with bedbugs,

children.text: golake nikṣiped ruddhvā mūṣāṃ tīvrānale dhamet ||
children.translated_text: one should place it in a pellet, seal the crucible, and blow it in a fierce fire.
When it has been blown seven times in this way, one should quench it in horse urine.
By this ordered procedure it certainly becomes killed.
That killed diamond should be powdered in a mortar; this is taught as an effective method.
<s>bhrāmaka</s>, killed <s>tāpya</s>, <s>peṭālī</s> seed, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),
the latex of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>, sulfur, <s>tālaka</s>, and stone,
tamarind seed, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>strīpuṣpa</s>, and <s>amlavetasa</s>,
the whole five-part plant of <s>śarapuṅkhā</s>, hare's tooth, and <s>śilājatu</s>;
all these, together or separately, according to availability, should be well powdered.
One should triturate them with the latexes of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>arka</s>, and <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>, and with breast milk.
One should place the diamond in that pellet and seal this blind crucible firmly.
<s>Guḍūcī</s>, rock salt, <s>hiṅgu</s>, with <s>mustā</s> and <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>,
having ground them with decoctions of horse gram, one should put it into that decoction.

children.text: taṃ vajraṃ pūrvavadgole kṛtvā ruddhvā dhamettathā
children.translated_text: One should make that diamond into a pellet as before, seal it, and blow it in the same way.
Then one should carry the procedure through to quenching twenty-one times.
In a combination of <s>tālaka</s> and bedbugs, one should again blow it seven times.
One should quench it with horse urine; that diamond surely dies.
Taking the root of a three-year-old cotton plant, one should grind it,
or one may grind it with the own juices of a three-year-old <s>nāgavallī</s>.
One should place the diamond in that pellet, seal it, and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Cooked thus with seven <s>puṭas</s>, each performed one by one, it becomes prepared.
<s>Tālaka</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, and the ash of <s>apāmārga</s>,
having ground them with horse-gram decoctions, one should put the well-heated diamond into that.
After three sets of seven repetitions it dies; there is no doubt about this.
Together with calcined <s>vaikrānta</s>, one should grind <s>amlavetasa</s>.
One should place the diamond in that pellet and blow it in a blind crucible.
One should quench it with horse urine and again place it in the previous pellet.

children.text: ruddhvā dhmātaḥ punaḥ secyamevaṃ kuryāt trisaptadhā
children.translated_text: Sealed and blown, it should again be quenched; one should do this three times sevenfold.
It dies, there is no doubt; it should be applied in all preparations.
With the latex of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>, one should grind for a moment the <s>mukha</s> product of magnet-stone.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ piṣṭvā tu tadgolaṃ kṣiptvā tasminpaceddinam ||
children.translated_text: Having made that into a pellet and placed the diamond in it, one should cook it for a day.
With human oil and <s>gandha</s>-oil it dies; there is no doubt about this.
Then one should grind <s>bhūnāga</s> and sulfur with a woman's breast milk.
The diamond, placed in that pellet and cooked in the preceding oil, becomes killed.
Having ground <s>vimalā</s> with the latex of <s>snuhī</s>, one should put it in that pellet.

children.text: vajraṃ nirudhya mūṣāṃ tu śuṣkāṃ tīvrāgninā dhamet
children.translated_text: After sealing the diamond and the dry crucible, one should blow it with fierce fire.

children.text: kṣiptāmaśvasya mūtre tu kṣiptvā vajraṃ samāharet ||
children.translated_text: Having plunged it into horse urine, one should recover the diamond.
When one has done this seven times, then with <s>tālaka</s> and bedbugs,
having ground a pellet, one should put the diamond in it and seal the crucible.
Blown as before and quenched, it becomes killed with seven repetitions.
One should smear the diamond with bedbug blood and put it in the sun.
When it is dry, it should be smeared again and dried again, for up to seven days.
With the liquids of <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s> and <s>peṭakārī</s>, one should sprinkle it again and again.

children.text: taptaṃ taptaṃ ca tadvajraṃ śatavārairmṛtaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: That diamond, heated repeatedly, becomes killed in one hundred repetitions.

children.text: gandhakaṃ cūrṇitaṃ bhāvyaṃ strīpuṣpeṇa tu saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: Powdered sulfur should be impregnated seven times with <s>strīpuṣpa</s>.
Then, mixed with menstrual blood, one should quench the well-heated diamond in it.
One should quench and heat it twenty-one times; it becomes killed.
Having placed the diamond in a large river oyster shell, it should be treated again and again,
in the sun with any one of the liquids of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>arka</s>, and excellent <s>kumārī</s>.
Then one should wrap it with ground black crab meat.
Properly held in the clay of <s>bhūnāga</s>, it attains the state of ash.
With the roots of <s>raktamūla</s> and the buds of <s>meghanāda</s>,
when wrapped with these ground substances and blown, the diamond fully becomes ash.
The diamond placed inside a citron should be sealed, and one should smear the outside with clay.
One should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>, take it out, and similarly cook it in one hundred <s>puṭas</s>.
Smeared with the liquids of <s>nāgaparṇī</s> and wrapped in that very leaf,

children.text: jānumadhye sthitaṃ yāmaṃ tad vajraṃ mṛdutāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: kept between the knees for a <s>yāma</s>, that diamond becomes soft.
One should place the diamond in the middle of a seed of <s>mātṛvāhaka</s>.
or inside a <s>jambīra</s> citron, and cook it for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus).
In a decoction of <s>kuluttha</s> and <s>kodrava</s>, or in a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>,
after taking it out after a day and night, one should again place it inside a <s>jambīra</s> citron.
Or, after placing it in the seed of <s>mātṛvāhaka</s>, one should cook it as before.

children.text: punaḥ kṣepyaṃ punaḥ pācyaṃ tridinānte samuddharet ||
children.translated_text: It is to be put in again and cooked again; at the end of three days one should take it out.
One should gather the sprouts of <s>badarī</s>, banyan, and neem.
After grinding them, one should place the previously cooked diamond in that pellet.
Having wrapped that pellet in an <s>aśvattha</s> leaf, one should place it between the knees,
or hold it in the armpit for a day; it certainly becomes soft.
One should triturate mercury and powdered sharp iron with a sour liquid for a day.
One should place the diamond in that pellet and wrap it outside with thread.
Wrapped also with betel leaves and placed in a heap of grain,
at the end of a month one should take it out and smear it with the juices of <s>nāgalatā</s>.
Wrapped with those leaves and placed between the knees, it attains softness.
Either lodestone, or powder produced from magnetic iron,
should be triturated with mercury and a sour mixture for one day.
One should place the diamond in that pellet; with neem, cotton, and <s>kodrava</s>
leaves ground into a paste and then with betel leaves,
wrapped and placed between the knees, it attains softness at the end of the day.
One should place the diamond in the middle of a castor tree, or in its fruit.
After taking it out after the measure of a month, and putting it between the knees as before,

children.text: komalaṃ jāyate vajraṃ dinānte nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: the diamond becomes tender at the end of the day; there is no doubt about this.
One should wrap the diamond in partridge meat and put it in the mouth
of a very large frog, and bind the mouth with thread.
One should bury it in the earth to the measure of a cubit and take it out after a month.
Having enclosed the frog in a covered vessel, one should cook it properly in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> (large heating pit).
That diamond, placed in the previous pellet and kept between the knees for a day,
becomes true <s>vajraudana</s>; afterward one should apply it as fit for ingestion.
For all preparations of <s>vajraudana</s>, the calcination is to be as before.
The three alkalis, <s>rāmaṭha</s>, sour gruel of chickpea, and <s>amlavetasa</s>,
<s>jvālāmukhī</s>, <s>ikṣuraka</s>, and the fruits of <s>sthalakumbhī</s>,
should be ground finely with the latex of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, and one should put it in that pellet.
Having tied the thoroughly purified diamond in cloth, one should cook it forcefully.
By means of a <s>dolāyantra</s>, in sour fermented grain liquid, it becomes liquid after eight months.
Or, having put the diamond inside <s>vajravallī</s> and confined it,
it should be placed in a sour vessel; after seven days it reaches liquidity.
<s>Bhasmaudana</s>, <s>druti</s>, and this are the threefold calcination of diamond.
It is said by <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and those before him to bring about the fixation of mercury.
Diamond, endowed with the six tastes, removes all diseases.
It pacifies every sin, gives happiness and firmness of body, and is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).
Diamond is the best of jewels, holy, and increases prosperity and good fortune.
It promotes longevity, is blessed, gives vigor and fame, and conquers every evil.

children.text: āyurbalaṃ dehasaukhyaṃ rūpaṃ kāntiṃ karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: It produces long life, strength, bodily comfort, beauty, and radiance.

children.text: sevitaṃ hanti rogāṃśca mṛtaṃ vajraṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When used, calcined diamond destroys diseases; there is no doubt about this.
The blue stone is the jewel of <s>Sauri</s>; it is called blue stone and blue gem.
It is called blue sapphire, grass-attractor, great blue stone, and fine blue stone.
The <s>indranīla</s> gem is fourfold there, according to difference of class.
The one with a white shade is the brahmin; the red one is of the kṣatriya class.
The yellow one is of the vaiśya class, while the one with black rays is the śūdra.
Its auspicious shades resemble the juice of <s>nīlī</s>, the flower of <s>vaiṣṇavī</s>,
the flower of <s>lavalī</s>, and the lustre of the blue lotus's essence.
They resemble the flower of flax and have a brilliance like the wing of the <s>cāṣa</s> bird.
They bear a brilliance equal to that of the black <s>trikarṇikā</s> flower.
They have the fine shade of a peacock's neck and likewise resemble the neck of <s>Śambhu</s>.
They resemble the body of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and have the lustre of a bee's wing.
These shades of the great <s>indranīla</s> gem are auspicious.
Heaviness, glossy brilliance, fine color, and coloring of the sides,
and the power of attracting grass: these five qualities are declared.

children.text: na vimlo nirmalo gātro masṛṇo gurudīptikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is not dirty, its body is clear, it is smooth, heavy, and brightly shining.
Grass-attracting, soft, blue, and endowed with the marks, it is rare.
Auspicious <s>indranīla</s> is to be praised; it removes all sin.
It grants long life, fame, strength, prosperity, and health.
The blue stone is slightly bitter and hot, and removes <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and wind.

children.text: yo dadhāti śarīre'sya saurir maṅgalado bhavet
children.translated_text: For the person who wears it on his body, the <s>Sauri</s> gem becomes a giver of auspiciousness.
The <s>gomedaka</s> is also called <s>gomeda</s>, the jewel of <s>Rāhu</s>, and the dark gem.
It is called <s>Svarbhānava</s>; this six-named gem is also called tawny crystal.

children.text: gomūtrābhaṃ yanmṛdu snigdhamuṣṇaṃ śuddhacchāyaṃ gauravaṃ yacca dhatte
children.translated_text: That which has the appearance of cow's urine, is soft, glossy, hot, of pure hue, and possesses weight,

children.text: hemāraktaṃ śrīmatāṃ yogyametat gomedākhyaṃ ratnam ākhyāti santaḥ ||
children.translated_text: golden-red and suitable for the prosperous: the good call this the jewel named <s>gomedaka</s>.
Its shade is like a drop of honey, and its lustre like cow's urine and ghee.

children.text: hemaraktaṃ guru svacchaṃ snigdhaṃ gomedakaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: Golden-red, heavy, clear, and glossy is an auspicious <s>gomedaka</s>.
One should reject a bad <s>gomedaka</s> that is white, black, colorless, or spoiled by cracks and lines,
rough, and shaped like a <s>pāṭala</s> blossom.
The <s>gomedaka</s> jewel is purifying, fame-giving, and increases prosperity.
It is auspicious, produces radiance, is glossy, and removes all poison.
<s>Gomedaka</s> is sour and hot, and conquers disorders caused by aggravated wind.
It stimulates appetite and digestion, and when worn it destroys sin.
<s>Vaiḍūrya</s>, <s>keturatna</s>, and likewise that born from the sprout of the sound <s>kha</s>,
the gem born in the land of <s>Viḍūra</s>, and <s>prāvṛṣya</s>: these are its five names.
From the roar of the lord of the sons of <s>Diti</s>, like a fire burning the ocean shaken at the time of cosmic dissolution,
there arose multicolored <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, the best of gems, lovely with its beautiful brilliance.
Not far from the lofty bank of mount <s>Viḍūra</s>,
on the border of <s>Koṅka</s> and <s>Colaka</s>, the mine of that gem is remembered.
There, in answer to the roar of the lord of demons, with the deep thunderings of clouds,
<s>vaiḍūrya</s> gems come into being at the arrival of the rainy season.
That which resembles a white cloud or smoke, slightly blackish, or else white,
is declared by examiners of gem color to be called <s>vaiḍūrya</s>.
Having a luster like bamboo leaf, a cat's eye, or a peacock's neck,
smooth-bodied, heavy, and clear: such <s>vaiḍūrya</s> is considered endowed with good qualities.
One should reject as defective <s>vaiḍūrya</s> that is split by lines, light, too obvious, like stone, charcoal, or mud,
discolored, rough, or black.
Clear and glossy <s>vaiḍūrya</s> increases affection, lifespan, and strength.
Indeed, when worn, it is auspicious and removes all planetary afflictions and poisons.
<s>Vaiḍūrya</s> is sour and hot, and destroys phlegm and wind.
It pacifies abdominal tumors and colic, and when worn as an ornament it brings good fortune.

children.text: māṇikyaṃ mauktikaṃ vajraṃ nīlaṃ marakataṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māṇikya</s>, pearl, diamond, sapphire, and emerald
are called the five gems, removing sin, misfortune, and poison.
<s>Gomedaka</s>, topaz, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and coral:
with the five gems, these should be designated the nine gems.
Next comes <s>sūryakānta</s>: <s>tapanamaṇi</s>, <s>tāpana</s>, and <s>ravikānta</s>,
<s>dīptopala</s>, <s>agnigarbha</s>, <s>jvalanāśman</s>, and <s>arkopala</s>; it has eight names.
Like white mica in color, moonlike in the <s>Himādri</s>,
spotless and endowed with radiance: such crystal is called the best.

children.text: himālaye siṃhale ca vindhye revātaṭe tathā ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Himālaya</s>, in <s>Siṃhala</s>, in the <s>Vindhya</s>, and on the bank of the <s>Revā</s>,
and in places where <s>padmarāga</s> arises, various kinds of crystal may occur.
Among them one is <s>sūryakānta</s>, and another is <s>candrakānta</s>.
By the mere touch of the sun's rays, it emits fire at once.
That crystal, penetrated by gem-quality, is known as <s>sūryakānta</s>.
<s>Sūryakānta</s> is hot, pure, and a rejuvenative.
It removes wind and phlegm, benefits the intellect, and, when worshiped, gives satisfaction to the sun.
<s>Indukānta</s>, <s>candrakānta</s>, <s>candrāśman</s>, and <s>saṃsravopala</s>,
<s>śītāśman</s>, <s>candrikādrāva</s>, and <s>śaśikānta</s>: these are the seven names.

children.text: snigdhaṃ śvetaṃ pītam atrāsamantād dhatte cittaṃ svasthatāṃ yanmunīnām
children.translated_text: Smooth, white, and yellowish, it everywhere brings the minds of sages to steadiness.

children.text: yacca drāvaṃ yāti candrāṃśusaṅge jātyaṃ ratnaṃ candrakāntākhyametat ||
children.translated_text: And that excellent gem which liquefies in contact with moonbeams is called <s>candrakānta</s>.
<s>Candrakānta</s> is cooling and glossy, and removes bile, blood disorders, and burning.
It brings pleasure to <s>Śiva</s>, is clear, and removes planetary affliction, misfortune, and poison.

children.text: sphaṭikaḥ sitopalaḥ syād amalamaṇis tārakopalaḥ svacchaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sphaṭika</s> is also called <s>sitopala</s>, spotless gem, star-stone, and clear stone.

children.text: śītoṣṇavīryam akṣṇaḥ pittaṃ vātaṃ nihanti śophaghnam ||
children.translated_text: With both cooling and heating potency, it benefits the eye, destroys bile and wind, and removes swelling.

children.text: purā proktaṃ hi kāntasya mayā te lakṣaṇādikam
children.translated_text: Previously I told you the marks and other features of <s>kānta</s>.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>vikrānta</s>, blue diamond, inferior diamond,
<s>gonāsa</s>, small thunderbolt, powdered diamond, and <s>gonasa</s> are its names.
It is white, red, yellow, blue, dove-colored,
dark, black-colored, and variegated; thus it is eightfold.
In the absence of diamond, <s>vaikrānta</s> is equal in taste, potency, and the rest.
Eight-cornered, eight-faced, six-angled, smooth, and heavy,
joined with pure or mixed colors, it is called <s>vaikrānta</s>.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, steamed in a decoction of <s>kuluttha</s>, becomes purified.
With the three alkalis, the five salts, fat, urine, sour <s>kodrava</s> gruel,
equal amounts of fish oil and ghee, <s>kuluttha</s>, and sour gruel,
one should cook it for seven days in a swinging apparatus, placed inside a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, then having the color of heat, certainly comes to purity.
While it is repeatedly heated, it should be sprinkled with horse urine fourteen times.
Then it should be put into a ball with the five parts of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>.

children.text: ruddhvā mūṣāṃ puṭe paktvā punaruddhṛtya golake ||
children.translated_text: After sealing the crucible and cooking it in a closed heating, one should take it out again and put it into a ball.

children.text: kṣiptvā ruddhvā puṭedevaṃ saptadhā bhasmatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: Sealing it and heating it in this way seven times, it becomes ash.

children.text: vaikrāntasya palaikaṃ tu palaikaṃ ṭaṅkaṇasya ca ||
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of <s>vaikrānta</s> and one <s>pala</s> of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>
should be steeped for a day in <s>ravi</s> latex, and ground for a day with the juices of <s>śigru</s>.
One should add one <s>karṣa</s> each of <s>guñjā</s>, oil-cake, and <s>vahni</s>.
Making pellets with this, one should blow them strongly in a furnace apparatus.
The essence born from <s>vaikrānta</s> becomes like conch, jasmine, and the moon.

children.text: vaikrāntaṃ vajrakandaṃ ca samaṃ snukpayasā saha
children.translated_text: Equal amounts of <s>vaikrānta</s> and <s>vajrakanda</s>, together with the milk of <s>snuk</s>,
fresh buffalo butter, and honey, should be ground for a day.
By blowing as before, the essence becomes like an <s>indragopa</s> insect.
Powder of <s>vandhyā</s> with an equal amount of <s>vaikrānta</s> should be ground in the shade
with goat urine for one day; the essence becomes like silver.
It is killed by eight closed heatings when combined with sulfur and the juice of citron.
Ground by the method for causing essence to fall, and made into pills,
<s>vaikrānta</s>, blown for a <s>ghaṭikā</s> in a crucible, releases its essence.
White-colored <s>vaikrānta</s>, steeped in <s>amlavetasa</s>...
Within a week, there is no doubt here; in intense heat it melts completely.
One should take the fresh juice of <s>ketakī</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, rock salt, <s>svarṇapuṣpikā</s>,
all combined in a measure like an <s>indragopa</s>, and put them into a vessel.
One should steam it there for seven days; <s>vaikrānta</s> then passes into liquidity.
The <s>vaikrāntaka</s> gives long life, produces strength and complexion, is exceedingly aphrodisiac, gives intelligence, and removes the intoxication of all the humors.
It kindles the digestive fire, is swift and has qualities equal to the thunderbolt; indeed <s>vaikrāntaka</s> makes the body strong as iron.
<s>Āvartamaṇi</s>, <s>āvarta</s>, <s>rājāvarta</s>, and the fire-named one are its names.
Now I shall state the characteristics of the essence of <s>rājāvarta</s>.
In color it should resemble a bee; with respect to processing it is of two kinds.
One is known as powder-shaped, and the second has the nature of a ball.
Joined with specks of gold, having a stable color, it gives stability.
It is very effective in heightening the color produced from rasa.
It is best for coloring <s>nāga</s> and for the coloring operation in <s>tāra</s>.
It is considered to bind the color of all unstable colors.
<s>Rājāvarta</s> has a radiance mixed with slight red and deep blue.
The heavy and smooth one is best; another kind is remembered as middling.
Indeed, when steamed with lemon liquids, cow urine, and alkalis,
the metals beginning with <s>rājāvarta</s> are purified in two or three treatments.
Powdered <s>rājāvarta</s>, combined with citron water and sulfur,
becomes calcined <s>rājāvarta</s> through seven calcinations.
One should cook <s>rājāvarta</s> in an iron vessel with buffalo ghee
and with milk for one day, mixed with the five allied substances.
Then, over five nights, one should make it into a solid lump.
By means of khadira charcoal in a furnace, it releases its metallic essence.
It removes urinary disease, wasting, piles, anemia, phlegm, and wind.
<s>Rājāvarta</s> is a digestive stimulant, a digestive, aphrodisiac, and a <s>rasāyana</s>.
<s>Sasyaka</s> is called <s>garuḍodgāra</s>, <s>kālajit</s>, and <s>viṣasāraka</s>.
Having drunk the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison, <s>Garuḍa</s> was unable to endure it.
Then, coming forth from his beak, that substance became manifold <s>sasyaka</s>.
<s>Sasyaka</s> is a great mineral, endowed with five appearances:
white, dark, yellow, green, and very red.
It is exceedingly stable, fiery, and assumes every form in every respect.
The white and the green are praised for operations on silver.
The red, dark, and yellow are praised for operations on gold.
<s>Sasyaka</s> destroys all diseases and removes fear of poison and death.
<s>Vimala</s> is spotless, pure, clear; <s>vimala</s> has a clear mineral nature.
Praised under five names, it is divided into two kinds, silver and gold.
<s>Vimala</s> is declared to be threefold: first the gold kind, then the silver kind,
and the third is bronze <s>vimala</s>; it is recognized there by its lustre.
It is round, furnished with angles, glossy, and provided with plates.
<s>Vimala</s> removes wind and bile, is aphrodisiac, and is an excellent <s>rasāyana</s>.
The first is said to be useful for gold operations, the second for aphrodisiac work,
and the third for medicine; among these, each preceding one is successively superior in qualities.
Steamed in the juice of <s>āṭarūṣa</s>, <s>vimala</s> becomes purified <s>vimala</s>.
First one should cook <s>vimala</s> in water from the plantain rhizome.
Then one should cook it in <s>amlavetasa</s>, sour grain gruel, and ewe's urine.
In a <s>dolāyantra</s> for four watches: this is their excellent purification.
With liquids arising from <s>kārkoṭī</s> and <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and with citron liquids, for a day,
one should impregnate it in fierce sunlight; <s>vimala</s> is certainly purified.
One should treat <s>vimala</s> with water of <s>śigru</s>, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
combined with <s>vajrakanda</s>, and impregnate it with plantain juices.
Placed in a closed crucible together with <s>mokṣaka</s> alkali, it should be blown.
Its metallic essence, shining like moon and sun, falls out; there is no doubt.
<s>Haritāśman</s>, <s>peroja</s>, enemy of poison, and green gem are its names.
In taste, potency, and post-digestive effect it follows the qualities of <s>sasyaka</s>.
<s>Śrībhairavī</s>:
What kind of auspicious herb, Lord, is effective in alchemical work?

children.text: kena vā bhasma sūtaśca kena vā khoṭabandhanam ||
children.translated_text: By what does mercury become ash, and by what is the globule-fixation made?

children.text: nirjīvatvaṃ gataḥ sūtaḥ kathaṃ jīvaṃ dadāti saḥ
children.translated_text: When mercury has become lifeless, how does it give life?

children.text: nirjīvena tu jīvatvaṃ kathaṃ jīvati śaṅkara ||
children.translated_text: And by means of what lifeless thing does it come alive, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>?

children.text: etanme saṃśayaṃ brūhi yathā jānāmyahaṃ śiva
children.translated_text: Tell me this doubt of mine, <s>Śiva</s>, so that I may know.
<s>Śrībhairava</s>:
Listen, <s>Bhairavī</s>; I shall tell you all that unprecedented matter.
It was not known by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Surendra</s>, and the others, O you honored by heroes.
They destroy wrinkles, gray hair, and disease, and break death and poverty;
the divine <s>kulauṣadhi</s> herbs, effective in alchemical work, grant excellent attainments.
Foolish, beast-like people wander about without the <s>kulauṣadhi</s> herbs.
No success at all arises from the juices of common grass-herbs.
Therefore the <s>kulauṣadhi</s> must be known with every effort.
Sixty-four divine herbs are established within the <s>kula</s>.
Fools do not know them, being deluded by <s>Śiva</s>'s delusion.
Non-divine grass-herbs are born in mountain caves.

children.text: tṛṇauṣadhyā rase sūtaṃ naiva bandhaṃ kadācana ||
children.translated_text: With the juice of grass-herbs, mercury never attains fixation.
Nor does it remain imperishable when bereft of the <s>kulauṣadhi</s>.

children.text: kulauṣadhyā vihīnāstu gaganaṃ ca na hanti te ||
children.translated_text: Those without the <s>kulauṣadhi</s> do not even kill <s>gagana</s>.

children.text: sa rasastu varārohe vahnimadhye na tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: That mercury, O beautiful-hipped one, does not remain in the midst of fire.

children.text: na khoṭo na ca vā bhasma naiva dravyaṃ karoti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: It makes neither a globule nor ash, nor any effective substance.
They produce a little substance, but when blown it does not remain.

children.text: patre pāke kaṣe chede naiva tiṣṭhati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: In the leaf-test, cooking, decoction, and cutting, the gold does not remain at all.

children.text: naiva vedhaṃ śatādūrdhvaṃ karoti sa rasaḥ priye
children.translated_text: That <s>rasa</s> (mercurial elixir), beloved, does not effect penetration beyond a hundredfold.

children.text: yāvanna cābdamekaṃ tu vikrītaṃ tattu kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: Until a full year has passed, that gold is saleable.
But it should certainly not be given, beloved, for the aims of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, or liberation.

children.text: divyauṣadhyā yadā devi rasendro mardito bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When, O goddess, <s>rasendra</s> (lord mercury) has been ground with a divine herb,
then <s>sūta</s> (mercury), free from blackening, is always produced, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
<s>Rasa</s> that is free from blackening removes the death-time of another.

children.text: aṣṭānāṃ caiva lohānāṃ malaṃ śamayati kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: It pacifies at once the impurities of the eight metals.
Who indeed would call dead the mercury that has entered a great stupor?
By the juice of a divine herb it alone becomes one whose lost consciousness has returned.
<s>Sūta</s>, made of the five elements, abides always as <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
Mercurial herbs, great herbs, perfected herbs, and others likewise,
called divine herbs: these four kinds have been stated by me.
Among them the divine herbs are declared to be the ones richer in virtues.
