They are trees, creepers, vines, shrubs, grasses, and parasitic growths.
The herbs that bind <s>rasa</s> are proclaimed to be sixfold:
<s>Somavallī</s>, <s>Mahāgulmā</s>, <s>Yakṣaśreṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Dhanurlatā</s>,
<s>Somāhvā</s>, <s>Gulmavallī</s>, <s>Yajñavallī</s>, and <s>Dvijapriyā</s>,

children.text: somakṣīrā ca somā ca yajñā divyalatā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Somakṣīrā</s>, <s>Somā</s>, <s>Yajñā</s>, and the divine creeper are remembered.
<s>Somavallī</s> is pungent, cooling, sweet, and removes burning caused by bile.
It especially calms thirst, promotes digestion, and is rejuvenative.
It has five parts, is rich in fifteen leaves, serpent-shaped, and red at the joints.
That <s>Somavallī</s>, brought on a full-moon day, performs the operation of binding <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇe pakṣe pragalati dalaṃ pratyahaṃ caikamekaṃ śukle pakṣe prabhavati punar lambamānā latā syāt
children.translated_text: In the dark fortnight one leaf drops away each day; in the bright fortnight it grows again, becoming a hanging creeper.

children.text: tasyāḥ kandaḥ kalayatitarāṃ pūrṇimāyāṃ gṛhīto baddhvā sūtaṃ kanakasahitaṃ dehalohaṃ vidhatte ||
children.translated_text: Its tuber, especially obtained on the full moon, binds mercury together with gold and produces effects on the body and metals.
This creeper, named <s>Somalatā</s>, is exceedingly hard to obtain.
By means of it, bound lordly mercury becomes capable of penetrating a hundred thousandfold.
In <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative alchemy), the marks of the twenty-four <s>somas</s> are evident.
The <s>Somavṛkṣa</s> too performs such operations as binding and killing <s>rasa</s>.
Of those two, the creeper brought on a full-moon day has superior qualities.
It is also called <s>Mahiṣavallī</s> and <s>Pratisomāntravallikā</s>.
It is described as a leafless creeper, with stem and branches, and as milky.
In taste, potency, and post-digestive effect, it is remembered as equal to <s>Somavallī</s>.
Now then, hear the rule for the divine herb <s>Sthalapadminī</s>.
It resembles a lotus in its leaves, and likewise in its flowers.
When broken, it exudes a beautiful milk of red color.
Stepping on it with the left foot, one should look at the vault of the sky.
One sees the sphere of planets and constellations, furnished with stars.
By this sign, O goddess, it should be known as <s>Sthalapadminī</s> from a distance of a hundred thousand yojanas.
It is a creeper shaped like a <s>gonasa</s> snake and adorned with variegated circles.
It pacifies old age, disease, and death, and is capable of binding and killing <s>rasa</s>.
Now I shall explain <s>Uccaṭā</s>, beloved, which brings about the binding of <s>rasa</s>.
It has just a single stalk, which is enveloped in hairs.
At its tip is a flower resembling a parrot's beak.
Its leaves too, O goddess, are like parrot feathers.
Its tuber has the shape of a tortoise, and its milk resembles vermilion.
A liquid flows in the beeswax-like part; taking that, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
one may pierce all metals, and they become gold.
There is one called <s>Īśvarī</s>, resembling <s>Īśvarī</s> in form.
It pours forth abundant milk and binds <s>rasa</s> when seed is present.
With leaves like neem leaves, it is called <s>Bhūtakeśī</s>.

children.text: na vadhyate yayā sūtaḥ sūto'sau hi nibandhakaḥ
children.translated_text: The mercury that is not killed by it is indeed a binder.
A creeper resembling split lampblack is known as <s>Kṛṣṇalatā</s>.
It binds even seedless <s>rasa</s> and removes all poisons.
Named <s>Laśunavallī</s>, it has leaves resembling those of garlic.

children.text: kṣaratkṣīrā sukandā ca rasaṃ badhnāti vegataḥ
children.translated_text: It exudes milk, has a fine tuber, and swiftly binds <s>rasa</s>.
Its leaves are like chickpea leaves, and its flowers are likewise.
It is famous by the name <s>Rudantī</s>, raining water downward.
It seems to weep on seeing people afflicted by death, poverty, and old age.

children.text: caturvidhā tu sā jñeyā pītā raktā sitāsitā
children.translated_text: It should be known as fourfold: yellow, red, white, and black.
As a rejuvenative, it kills <s>rasa</s> into which mica has been assimilated, and it also binds it.
Its tuber is like the tuber of <s>Musalī</s>, and its leaves have the form of that plant's leaves.
Milky and hairy, it is called <s>Vārāhī</s>, the binder of <s>rasa</s>.
Filled with seven shoots, it is regarded as <s>Saptapattrī</s>.
It is rejuvenative and destroys old age; mercury is bound by it.
The creeper called <s>Nāginī</s> has limbs like the coils of a serpent.
It destroys snake poison and the like, and binds clear <s>rasa</s>.
Another little creeper is <s>Sarpiṇī</s>, with a crooked stem like a serpent.
It is milky and has glossy leaves, and it binds young mercury.
The one whose stalk and leaves are like an umbrella, neither too low nor too tall,
milky and named <s>Chattriṇī</s>, is regarded as bringing about the binding of <s>rasa</s>.
Growing from stone on a mountain, it has a tuber shaped like a <s>gokanda</s>.

children.text: kṣatā muñcati sā kṣīraṃ gośṛṅgī rasabandhinī ||
children.translated_text: When cut, it releases milk; <s>Gośṛṅgī</s> is a binder of <s>rasa</s>.
The one named <s>Jyotis</s> is said to be threefold, consisting of tree, tuber, and grass forms.
On a mountain it shines at night; it binds mercury in its creeper form.
The one whose milk, leaves, and body are red, a creeper not very spreading,
is designated the divine <s>Raktavallī</s>, a binder of <s>rasa</s>.
The vine whose leaves are shaped like lotus leaves is called <s>patravallī</s> by those who know <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: sakṣīrakandā salilodbhavā ca kṣitau na tiṣṭhedrasabandhanī sā ||
children.translated_text: It has a milky tuber and is born in water; that binder of <s>rasa</s> should not remain on dry ground.
Rich in the color of large thorns, that vine is said to be <s>kākinī</s>.
This one binds <s>rasa</s> and destroys old age and death.
It is designated <s>cāṇḍālī</s>, bearing three or four leaves.

children.text: sā ca raktā kṣīrakandā tayā sūto nibadhyate ||
children.translated_text: It is red and has a milky tuber; by means of it <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is bound.
The <s>caṇḍālakanda</s> is said to have one leaf or two leaves,
or else three leaves, four leaves, and five leaves, according to its divisions.
Having copper-colored vine, leaves, flowers, and milk,
it is called <s>tāmravallikā</s> and is an effective means for <s>rasa</s>, metals, and the like.
Joined with yellow leaves, vine, flowers, and juice, and very hard to obtain,
it is called <s>pītavallikā</s> and is useful in the procedure for binding <s>rasa</s>.
With white milk, covered with leaves like those of <s>āḍhakī</s>, and not very spreading,
this plant is famed as <s>vijayā</s> and is useful in the procedure for binding <s>rasa</s>.
Endowed with a triangular tuber and covered with leaves like those of <s>citraka</s>,

children.text: mahauṣadhīti sā proktā rasabandhe paraṃ hitā ||
children.translated_text: it is called <s>mahauṣadhī</s> and is supremely useful in binding <s>rasa</s>.
Rich in leaves resembling a peacock's neck and heavy with the fragrance of sandalwood,

children.text: devadālītyasau divyā rasaṃ badhnāti sā kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: this divine plant is <s>devadālī</s>; it binds <s>rasa</s> in an instant.
Called <s>navanītakagandhī</s>, it is bitter and has the smell of unguent.

children.text: sakṣīrā raktapuṣpā ca rasendro badhyate tayā ||
children.translated_text: It has milk and red flowers; by means of it <s>rasendra</s> (mercury) is bound.
It has milk and red flowers, and leaves like jujube leaves.
It is called <s>gāruḍavallī</s> and quickly binds <s>pārada</s> (mercury).
The vine called <s>tumbinī</s> is furnished with its characteristic leaves and blossoms.
It has bitter red milk, and its fruit binds <s>rasa</s>.
The plant whose leaves are like the leaves of <s>tumbinī</s> is <s>bhūtumbinī</s>; it does not spread very far.
It is furnished with fruits like lemons, destroys every disease, and binds <s>rasa</s>.
Having leaves like castor leaves, with milk, and not very spreading,

children.text: gandharvetyuditā sā hi tayā bandhaṃ raso vrajet ||
children.translated_text: it is called <s>gandharvī</s>; by means of it <s>rasa</s> goes to fixation.
The plant whose leaves are like tiger's feet, with red flowers and milky sap,
is designated <s>vyāghrapādī</s>; it certainly binds <s>rasa</s>.
Having leaves like <s>saptacchada</s>, slender-bodied and not very spreading,

children.text: mahauṣadhītyasau proktā rasaṃ badhnāti hanti ca ||
children.translated_text: this is called <s>mahauṣadhī</s>; it binds and kills <s>rasa</s>.
The vine named <s>gomārī</s> has leaves like bamboo leaves.

children.text: tasyā mūlaṃ samāsādya śastaḥ sūto nibadhyate ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained its root, excellent <s>sūta</s> is bound.
The plant whose leaves are shaped like a trident and whose fruits are like <s>śamyāka</s> fruits
is called <s>triśūlī</s> and is famous in the binding of <s>rasa</s>.
Its leaves and fruits are like those of <s>rutasī</s>, and it has a milky tuber.
It is called the <s>rutasī</s> vine, mountain-born, and a binder of <s>rasa</s>.
With fine flowers, bearing a tilaka-mark, and furnished with red threefold fruits,
it is taught in the procedure for binding <s>rasa</s> and has been named <s>tridaṇḍī</s>.
Rich in leaves colored like a bee, milky, and yellow-flowered,
it is called <s>bhṛṅgavallī</s> and is employed in binding <s>rasa</s>.
Rich in fan-shaped leaves, furnished with milk, and bearing a moonlike mark,

children.text: latā camarikā nāma sā ca badhnāti pāradam ||
children.translated_text: the vine named <s>camarikā</s> also binds <s>pārada</s>.
A vine possessing leaves and flowers like <s>hayamāra</s>,
it is called <s>karavīralatā</s> and is especially a binder of <s>sūta</s>.
With blossoms and leaves resembling coverings of <s>koraṇḍa</s> leaves, and with a good milky tuber,

children.text: sā vajravallī kaṭutiktasārā vajrāṅkapatrā rasabandhinī ca ||
children.translated_text: that <s>vajravallī</s> has a pungent and bitter essence, diamond-marked leaves, and binds <s>rasa</s>.
Possessing red milk and leaves resembling bilva leaves,
it is <s>vāravallī</s>, a binder of <s>sūta</s> and destroyer of disease.
Having flowers and leaves shaped like hemp blossoms, ten flowers, and milk,
it is designated <s>rohiṇī</s>, a binder of the king of <s>rasa</s>.
Having leaves and foliage shaped and colored like those of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, and celebrated,
it is taught in the procedure for binding <s>rasa</s> and is called <s>bilvinī</s>.
Endowed with the brilliance of <s>gorocanā</s> and furnished with leaves and vine,
<s>gorocanalatā</s> frees beings and binds <s>rasa</s>.
Born on the summit of <s>Śrīśaila</s>, it is an herb resembling <s>mārkaṇḍī</s>.
When cut it releases red milk; <s>karīrī</s> is a binder of <s>rasa</s>.
With leaves like sheets of lead, giving fruit after three years,
it is called <s>akṣarā</s> and binds <s>rasa</s> exceedingly well.
Like <s>somavallī</s>, leafless, and endowed with a black-collyrium-like sap,
this leafless plant grows in the <s>Vindhya</s>, not very tall, and binds <s>rasa</s>.
In the first year it is sour; in the second it becomes bitter.
In the third year it comes to be furnished with sweet fruits.
It immediately removes bilious fever and has good leaves and fruits.
The vine <s>kuṭajavallī</s> has the fruits and leaves of that plant.
Sweet <s>rudhiragranthi</s> is a binder of the king <s>sūta</s>.
Famed as <s>mūlakanda</s>, it bears root-like fruits and leaves.
A vine furnished with milk certainly causes the binding of <s>sūta</s>.
The <s>pārijāta</s>-mountain-born vine is covered with leaves of a hundred flowers.
Bearing black milk and fruit, it is called <s>brāhmaṇī</s> and binds <s>rasa</s>.
Its leaves are like <s>agasti</s> leaves, and it has red flowers of that same form.
Smelling of ghee and destructive of <s>rasa</s>, it is called <s>munivallī</s>.
By its leaves, flowers, and fruits the vine resembles the neem tree.

children.text: tanmūlairbadhyate sūtaḥ sā proktā nimbakā latā
children.translated_text: By its roots <s>sūta</s> is bound; it is called <s>nimbakālatā</s>.
Famed as <s>tilakanda</s>, it bears root-like fruits and leaves.
A milky vine binds <s>sūta</s> in fierce sunlight.

children.text: atasya iva puṣpāṇi phalāni ca dalāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Its flowers, fruits, and leaves are like those of <s>atasi</s>.
That <s>atasīvallikā</s> is indeed a binder of <s>pārada</s> (mercury).
It is called <s>bodhilatā</s>, joined with the latex of the <s>bodhi</s> leaf.
It binds the king of mercury, as <s>Acyuta</s> bound the lord of the Dānavas.
Famed as <s>madyagandhā</s>, it is leafless, yet furnished with fruiting leaflike parts.

children.text: tasyāḥ kando rasaṃ śīghraṃ bandhanaṃ nayati dhruvam
children.translated_text: Its tuber quickly and certainly brings mercury to fixation.
<s>Kūrmalatā</s> is said to have a tortoise-shaped tuber and to be endowed with latex.
With leaves and blossoms resembling jasmine, it binds mercury.
Its roots are like the roots of <s>mādhavī</s>, and it has leaves like those of <s>nāgavallī</s>.
The vine called <s>mādhavī</s>: by its roots mercury is bound.
A vine with white leaves, and likewise with white flowers and fruits,
is designated <s>viśālā</s>; it too is a binder of mercury.
With a tuber like a serpent's coil and leaves resembling its hood,
this vine named <s>mahānāgā</s> binds mercury.
With a tuber shaped like a frog and leaves like frog-leaves,
this is <s>maṇḍūkalatikā</s>; by its roots mercury is bound.
With fruits shaped like <s>udumbara</s> fruits and with leaves like its leaves,
that is called <s>udumbaralatā</s>, a binder of the king of mercury.
The one with milky tubers, banyan-like leaves, variegated foliage, large fruit, and great length,
is called <s>citravallī</s>; <s>rasendra</s> (mercury) is bound when placed inside its fruit.
Thus sixty-four powerful divine herbs have been stated.
Bound by these, mercury accomplishes for human beings the purposes of the body and of metals.
The <s>somavallī</s>, the <s>somavṛkṣa</s>, then <s>sthalapadminikā</s>,

children.text: gonasā kāravallī ca uccaṭā īśvarī tataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>gonasā</s>, <s>kāravallī</s>, <s>uccaṭā</s>, and then <s>īśvarī</s>,
<s>bhūtakeśī</s>, <s>kṛṣṇalatā</s>, and what is known as <s>laśunavallarī</s>,

children.text: rudantī caiva vārāhī saptapattrī ca nāginī
children.translated_text: <s>rudantī</s>, <s>vārāhī</s>, <s>saptapattrī</s>, and <s>nāginī</s>,
<s>sarpiṇī</s> and <s>chattriṇī</s>, as well as <s>gośṛṅgī</s>, giver of all accomplishments,
<s>jyotirnāmnī</s> in three forms, <s>raktavallarī</s>, and <s>patravallarī</s>,
<s>kākinī</s>, <s>cāṇḍālī</s> vine, and <s>tāmravallarī</s>,

children.text: pītavallī ca vijayā vijñeyā ca mahauṣadhī
children.translated_text: <s>pītavallī</s> and <s>vijayā</s>; these should be known as great herbs.
<s>devadālī</s> is to be known, and there is <s>navānītagandhinī</s>,
<s>garuḍavallī</s>, <s>tumbinī</s>, and <s>bhūmituṃbinī</s> should be known,

children.text: gandharvā vyāghrapādī ca vijñeyā ca mahauṣadhī ||
children.translated_text: <s>gandharvā</s>, <s>vyāghrapādī</s>, and <s>mahauṣadhī</s> should be recognized.

children.text: gomārī ca triśūlī ca rutasī ca tridaṇḍikā
children.translated_text: <s>gomārī</s>, <s>triśūlī</s>, <s>rutasī</s>, and <s>tridaṇḍikā</s>,
<s>bhṛṅgavallī</s>, <s>camarikā</s>, then <s>karavīralatā</s>,
<s>vajravallī</s>, <s>vāravallī</s>, <s>rohiṇī</s>, and <s>bilvinī</s>,
<s>gorocanalatā</s>, <s>karīrī</s>, and <s>akṣarā</s>,

children.text: apattrī kuṭajā vallī mūlakandā ca brāhmaṇī
children.translated_text: <s>apattrī</s>, <s>kuṭajā</s> vine, <s>mūlakandā</s>, and <s>brāhmaṇī</s>,
<s>ghṛtagandhā</s>, <s>nimbavallī</s>, <s>tilakandā</s>, and <s>atasī</s>,
<s>bodhivallī</s>, <s>madyagandhā</s>, <s>kūrmavallī</s>, and <s>mādhavī</s>,
<s>viśālā</s> and <s>mahānāgā</s>; <s>maṇḍūkavallī</s> should be known,
and <s>udumbaralatā</s> and <s>citravallī</s>, O you honored by the gods.
Thus sixty-four powerful divine herbs have been stated.
<s>Śrībhairava</s>:
<s>himajā</s>, <s>kāñcanakṣīrī</s>, <s>yavaciñcā</s>, and <s>mahādrijā</s>,
<s>himāvatī</s>, <s>pītadugdhā</s>, <s>recanī</s>, and <s>paṭuparṇikā</s>,
Its latex is <s>hemakaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>pulaka</s>, and likewise <s>recana</s>.

children.text: tejovatī bahurasā kanakaprabhānyā tīkṣṇāgnigarbhā suravallarī ca ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>tejovatī</s>, rich in sap, golden in radiance, with sharp fire inside, and <s>suravallarī</s>.
<s>himajā</s> is pungent, bitter, purgative, and removes every disorder of <s>vāta</s>.
It destroys worms, wasting, and abdominal disease, and removes bilious fever.
<s>kāravī</s> and <s>kāravallī</s> are astringent, hot, and dispel <s>kapha</s>.
It removes cough and asthma, gives strength, and should be known as a regulator of mercury.
<s>kaṭutumbī</s>, <s>kaṭuphalā</s>, <s>rājaputrī</s>, and <s>mahatphalā</s>,
<s>kaṭutumbī</s> is pungent and bitter, causes vomiting, and overcomes difficult breathing and vomiting.
It destroys cough, purifies, and removes swelling, wounds, pain, and poison.
But <s>tiktatumbī</s> is bitter; it is pungent and called <s>kaṭutumbikā</s>.
<s>tumbī</s> is remembered among the synonyms such as the bitter-pungent <s>tumbī</s>.

children.text: jyotiṣmatī nāma latānalaprabhā jyotirlatā sā kaṭabhī supiṅgalā
children.translated_text: The vine named <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, with fire-like radiance, is <s>jyotirlatā</s>, <s>kaṭabhī</s>, and very tawny.

children.text: dīpyā ca medhyā matidā ca durjarā sārasvatī syādamṛtārkasaṃkhyā ||
children.translated_text: It is stimulating, intellective, gives understanding, and is hard to digest; it is called <s>sārasvatī</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, and <s>arkā</s>.
<s>liṅginī</s> is <s>bahuputrī</s>, <s>īśvarī</s>, and <s>śaivavallarī</s>.
It is <s>svayambhū</s>, born from the liṅga, <s>laiṅgī</s>, and endowed with variegated fruits.
It causes the fixing of iron, and is <s>liṅgabījā</s> and <s>śivavallarī</s>.

children.text: liṅginī kaṭurūkṣā ca durgandhā ca rasāyanī
children.translated_text: <s>liṅginī</s> is pungent and dry, foul-smelling, and rejuvenative.
Divine and bringing every siddhi, it regulates the king of mercury.
<s>pātālagaruḍī</s>, <s>tārkṣī</s>, <s>sauvarṇī</s>, and <s>garuḍī</s>,
<s>vatsādanī</s>, long-stalked, firm-stalked, and very powerful,
long-vined and firm-liana: these are its names, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
This plant brings all things under control and destroys poisons from snakes and the like.
<s>girikarṇī</s>, <s>kaṭabhī</s>, <s>gardabhī</s>, and <s>dadhipuṣpikā</s>,
<s>sitapuṣpī</s>, poison-destroying, and <s>śvetāśvakhurapuṣpikā</s>.
<s>girikarṇī</s> is cooling, bitter, and destroys disorders arising from <s>pitta</s>.
It benefits the eyes, destroys toxic defects, and pacifies the three <s>doṣa</s>s.
The blue-flowered one is <s>mahānīlā</s>, and is <s>nīlagirikarṇikā</s>.
<s>nīlādrikarṇī</s> is cooling and slightly bitter, destroying bloody diarrhea, fever, and burning,
and it removes <s>pratardikā</s>, insanity, intoxication, fatigue, pain, and distress from breathlessness; it also removes poison.
<s>ākhukarṇī</s>, ground-creeping, <s>dravantī</s>, and <s>bahupādikā</s>,
<s>sutaśreṇī</s>, <s>dravantī</s>, <s>nyagrodhā</s>, and what is called <s>mākṣikā</s>,

children.text: citrā mūṣakapucchī ca pratyakśreṇī ca śabarī ||
children.translated_text: <s>citrā</s>, <s>mūṣakapucchī</s>, <s>pratyakśreṇī</s>, and <s>śabarī</s>,
<s>sutaśreṇī</s> benefits the eyes, is pungent, and removes mouse-poison.
It removes disorders of wounds and destroys diseases of the eye.

children.text: kṛṣṇikā bahuparṇī ca pratyakśoṇī ca śabarī
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇikā</s>, <s>bahuparṇī</s>, <s>pratyakśoṇī</s>, and <s>śabarī</s>,
<s>Pūtiparṇī</s>, <s>śivā</s>, and <s>parvaśālinī</s>, shaped like a mouse's ear, are its names.
<s>Ākhukarṇī</s> is pungent and hot, removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and is flowing in action.
It is supreme for destroying abdominal distension, colic, feverish pain, and disorders of movement, and it promotes digestion.

children.text: vārāhī syāt sūkarī kroḍakanyā gṛṣṭirviṣvaksenakāntā kumārī
children.translated_text: <s>Vārāhī</s> is called <s>sūkarī</s>, <s>kroḍakanyā</s>, <s>gṛṣṭi</s>, beloved of <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, and <s>kumārī</s>;

children.text: kaumārī syād brahmapattrī trinetrā krauḍīkanyā gṛṣṭikā mādhaveṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: it is <s>kaumārī</s>, <s>brahmapattrī</s>, <s>trinetrā</s>, <s>krauḍīkanyā</s>, <s>gṛṣṭikā</s>, and beloved of <s>Mādhava</s>.
<s>Vārāhī</s> is bitter and pungent, and removes poison, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.
It removes skin disease, urinary disorder, and worms; it is aphrodisiac, strengthening, and a <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: devadālī tridhā proktā śvetā kṛṣṇā ca pītalā
children.translated_text: <s>Devadālī</s> is taught as threefold: white, black, and yellow.

children.text: sā śvetā vyādhiśamanī kṛṣṇā pītā rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: The white one pacifies disease, while the black and yellow are used in <s>rasāyana</s>.
<s>Devadālī</s> is <s>kośaphalā</s>, <s>dālī</s>, and <s>lomaśapattrikā</s>;
it is <s>kṛṣṇabījā</s>, <s>kaṭuphalā</s>, <s>vṛttakośā</s>, and <s>amlavallarī</s>.
<s>Jīmūta</s>, <s>kaṇṭakaphalā</s>, <s>veṇī</s>, and remover of mouse-poison,
<s>turaṅgikā</s>, <s>jālaphalā</s>, enemy of poison, and <s>sāramūṣikā</s> are further names.
<s>Devadālī</s> is sharp, hot, and pungent; it removes anemia and <s>kapha</s>.
It destroys piles, dyspnea, and cough, and removes jaundice and skin eruptions.
It causes the melting of all metals and removes nasal catarrh and serpent-poison.
<s>Aindrī</s>, <s>indravāruṇī</s>, <s>aruṇā</s>, <s>mṛgādinī</s>, <s>gavādanī</s>, <s>kṣudrasahā</s>, and <s>indracidbhaṭā</s>,

children.text: sūryā viṣaghnī ruṇakarṇikāmarā suparṇikā syāt phalatārakā ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>sūryā</s>, poison-destroying <s>ruṇakarṇikā</s>, <s>amarā</s>, <s>suparṇikā</s>, and <s>phalatārakā</s> are its names.
It is also <s>vṛṣabhākṣī</s>, <s>gavākṣī</s>, and the yellow-flowered <s>indravallarī</s>.
<s>Hemapuṣpī</s>, <s>kṣudraphalā</s>, <s>vāruṇī</s>, dear to children,
<s>raktorvāru</s>, poison-creeper, <s>cakravallī</s>, and poison-remover are its names.
It is also <s>amṛtā</s> and <s>viśālā</s>; it should be known as having twenty-nine names.

children.text: indravāruṇikā tiktā kaṭuḥ śītā ca recanī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indravāruṇikā</s> is bitter, pungent, cooling, and purgative.
It removes abdominal tumors, <s>pitta</s>, abdominal disease, <s>śleṣman</s>, worms, skin disease, and fever.
<s>Mahendravāruṇī</s> is charming <s>cakravallī</s> with large fruits.

children.text: sā mahendrī vṛttaphalā trapusī trapusā tathā
children.translated_text: It is <s>mahendrī</s>, round-fruited, <s>trapusī</s>, and <s>trapusā</s> as well.
It is <s>ātmarakṣā</s>, <s>viśālā</s>, long-creeper, and large-fruited.
This gentle <s>bṛhadvāruṇī</s> has fourteen names.
<s>Māhendravāruṇī</s> should be known as bearing the qualities already stated.

children.text: rase vīrye vipāke ca kiṃcideṣā guṇādhikā
children.translated_text: In taste, potency, post-digestive effect, and qualities it is somewhat superior.
<s>Gojihvā</s> is <s>kṣurapattrī</s>; it is downward-flowered and downward-facing.
<s>Gojihvā</s> is pungent, intense, cooling, and destroys <s>pitta</s>.
It pacifies wounds and removes <s>saptadanta</s> poison.
<s>Kākatuṇḍī</s>, <s>kākanāsā</s>, <s>kākasiṃhī</s>, and <s>raktalā</s>,
<s>kākadantī</s>, <s>kākapīlu</s>, and the round red-fruited one are its names.
It is <s>kākaprāṇā</s>, <s>valkaśalyā</s>, <s>kṛṣṇabījā</s>, and <s>rañjakī</s>.
<s>Kākatuṇḍī</s> is sweet, cooling, and removes <s>pitta</s>.
It is a <s>rasāyana</s>, gives firmness, and especially removes gray hair.
<s>Raktapādī</s> has leaves like those of <s>śamī</s> and is <s>khadirapattrikā</s>.
It is <s>saṃkocanī</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>namaskārī</s>, and <s>prasāraṇī</s>.
<s>Lajjālu</s>, <s>saptaparṇī</s>, <s>khadirī</s>, and <s>maṇḍamālikā</s> are its names.
It is red-rooted, copper-rooted, self-hidden, and makes a folded-hand gesture.
<s>Lajjālu</s> is pungent and cooling, and destroys <s>pitta</s> and diarrhea.
It removes swelling, burning, fever, dyspnea, wounds, skin disease, and affliction from <s>kapha</s>.
The plant called the opposite of <s>lajjālu</s> is pungent and hot, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>āma</s>.
It is extremely regulatory in alchemical rasa and produces many kinds of knowledge.

children.text: punarnavā tridhā proktā śvetā raktā ca mecakā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Punarnavā</s> is taught as threefold: white, red, and dark.
<s>Punarnavā</s> removes poison; it is <s>kaṭhillā</s> and cures diseases of the eye.
The white <s>punarnavā</s> is <s>pṛthvīkā</s>, white monsoon-earth, long-leaved, and white-bodied.
White <s>punarnavā</s> is somewhat hot, bitter, and removes <s>kapha</s> and poison.
It removes cough, heart disease, colic, blood disorders, anemia, swelling, and afflictions of wind.
Another <s>punarnavā</s>, called red, has leaves arranged in circles.
It is <s>vaiśākhī</s>, red in all its parts, swelling-destroying, and an excellent remover of poison.

children.text: punarnavo navo navyā prāvṛṣeṇyā ca sāriṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Punarnavā</s>, ever new and fresh, monsoon-born, and <s>sāriṇī</s>,
red <s>punarnavā</s> is bitter, laxative, and destroys swelling.
It removes disorders of bloody vaginal discharge and crushes anemia and <s>pitta</s>.
The one called dark is blue monsoon-earth, long-leaved <s>punarnavā</s>.

children.text: nīlā punarnavā tiktā kaṭūṣṇā ca rasāyanī
children.translated_text: Blue <s>punarnavā</s> is bitter, pungent, hot, and a <s>rasāyana</s>.
It removes heart disease, anemia, swelling, dyspnea, wind, and <s>kapha</s>.
<s>Atyamlaparṇī</s> is sharply sour, itching-producing, a creeper rich in sap.
It grows in the forest, dwells in the wilderness, is rich in tubers, and has rough leaves.
<s>Atyamlaparṇī</s>, sharply sour, destroys splenic disease and colic.
It removes wind, kindles digestion, is appetizing, and removes abdominal tumors and phlegmatic disease.
<s>Kārkoṭakī</s> is twofold: barren, and the better other kind, <s>phalamāriṇī</s>.
It is softly thorny, round-fruited, and forest-dwelling.

children.text: vandhyā devī vandhyakārkoṭakī syānnāgārātir nāgahantrī manojñā
children.translated_text: The barren one is <s>devī</s>; barren <s>kārkoṭakī</s> is enemy of snakes, snake-slayer, and lovely.

children.text: pathyā divyā putradātrī trikandā śrīkandā sā kandavallī viṣaghnī ||
children.translated_text: It is wholesome, divine, giver of sons, three-tubered, <s>śrīkandā</s>, tuber-creeper, and poison-destroying.
<s>Yogīśvarī</s>, <s>vyāghrapādī</s>, and <s>kanyā</s> are among its sixteen names.

children.text: vandhyā karkoṭakī tiktā kaṭūṣṇā ca kaphāpahā ||
children.translated_text: Barren <s>karkoṭakī</s> is bitter, pungent, hot, and removes <s>kapha</s>.
It destroys plant and other poisons, and is used in binding mercury and in <s>rasāyana</s>.
The plant named <s>śarā</s> is <s>puṅkhā</s>; it is called <s>śarapuṅkhī</s>.

children.text: śarapuṅkhī tridhā śvetā raktā kṛṣṇā ca kaṇṭakā
children.translated_text: <s>Śarapuṅkhī</s> is threefold: white, red, black, and thorny.
Of these, the white one is rich in virtues and is used in <s>rasāyana</s> practice.
Another is <s>kaṇṭapuṅkhā</s>, <s>kaṇṭasāyakapuṅkhikā</s>.
<s>Kaṇṭaspṛśā</s> and <s>kuṇḍī</s> are names; a decoction of the root of thorny <s>śarapuṅkha</s>,
quickly treats indigestion, cholera-like illness, severe wasting, and emaciation.
All kinds of <s>śarapuṅkhā</s> are pungent, hot, and remove <s>kapha</s> and wind.
They remove indigestion, colic, and worms, and are excellent for calming <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder.
<s>Mārkava</s> is <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>; it is called <s>bhṛṅga</s> and <s>keśarañjaka</s> (hair-colorer).
It is <s>pitṛpriya</s>, <s>brahmapattrī</s>, <s>keśya</s> (beneficial for hair), and <s>kuntalavardhana</s> (promoter of locks).
Another, yellow one is <s>svarṇabhṛṅgāra</s>, <s>harivāsa</s>, and <s>harapriya</s>.
